tw-book1-chapter19_Sc4.description: I became more afraid for my safety when the Cullens decided I must be moved south and then hunted James once I was clear.
tw-book1-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: "We'll lead him off, and then Jasper and Alice will run her south."

tw-book1-chapter19_Sc4.description: I felt more protected by Esme and the Cullens when Esme immediately took me in her arms and carried me upstairs.
tw-book1-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: Esme was at my side in half a heartbeat, swinging me up easily into her arms, and dashing up the stairs before I could gasp in shock.

tw-book1-chapter19_Sc5.description: I learned that Alice dressed me in her clothes to try to confuse my scent for a limited time.
tw-book1-chapter19_Sc5.source_text: Trying to confuse the smell. It won't work for long, but it might help get you out.

tw-book1-chapter19_Sc5.description: I learned that Esme and Rosalie would take my truck while Alice and Jasper would use the Mercedes and Edward and Carlisle would go in the Jeep.
tw-book1-chapter19_Sc5.source_text: "Esme and Rosalie will be taking your truck, Bella," he told me as he passed. "Alice, Jasper — take the Mercedes. You'll need the dark tint in the south." "We're taking the Jeep."

tw-book1-chapter19_Sc5.description: I felt suddenly unworthy and believed that if anything happened to them, it might be for nothing.
tw-book1-chapter19_Sc5.source_text: "I'm not," I mumbled. "If anything happens to them, it will be for nothing."

tw-book1-chapter19_Sc5.description: I felt supported and protected by Alice, Esme, and Emmett when they physically carried and comforted me during the escape.
tw-book1-chapter19_Sc5.source_text: She lifted me in her slender arms as easily as Emmett had, shielding me protectively, and then we flew out the door, leaving the lights bright behind us. "Esme touched my cheek as she passed."

tw-book1-chapter19_Sc5.description: I learned that Edward kissed me briefly and then left with the hunting party, leaving me distraught.
tw-book1-chapter19_Sc5.source_text: He caught me up in his iron grip, crushing me to him. For the shortest second, his lips were icy and hard against mine. And they were gone.

tw-book1-chapter2_Sc1.description: I learned that Charlie couldn't cook much besides fried eggs and bacon and that I requested and received kitchen duty and the keys to the banquet hall.
tw-book1-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: Last night I'd discovered that Charlie couldn't cook much besides fried eggs and bacon. So I requested that I be assigned kitchen detail for the duration of my stay. He was willing enough to hand over the keys to the banquet hall.

tw-book1-chapter2_Sc1.description: I began to feel less overwhelmed and more able to cope, like I was treading water instead of drowning.
tw-book1-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: I began to feel like I was treading water, instead of drowning in it.

tw-book1-chapter2_Sc1.description: I started to worry that I might be the reason Edward wasn't at school, even though it felt ridiculous and egotistical.
tw-book1-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: I couldn't get rid of the nagging suspicion that I was the reason he wasn't there.

tw-book1-chapter2_Sc1.description: I noticed that the Cullens and the Hale twins were dressed exceptionally well in clothes that subtly hinted at designer origins and that their looks did not necessarily buy them acceptance.
tw-book1-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: They were all dressed exceptionally well; simply, but in clothes that subtly hinted at designer origins. It didn't look as if it bought them any acceptance here.

tw-book1-chapter2_Sc1.description: I drove a loud truck that drew attention when I started it and left the school parking lot.
tw-book1-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: I gunned my deafening engine to life, ignoring the heads that turned in my direction, and backed carefully into a place in the line of cars that were waiting to exit the parking lot.

tw-book1-chapter2_Sc1.description: I recognized that Mike was overly friendly and faithful to me like a golden retriever, and I realized I was going to have to handle his attention diplomatically.
tw-book1-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: Mike, who was taking on the qualities of a golden retriever, walked faithfully by my side to class. It looked like I was going to have to do something about Mike, and it wouldn't be easy.

tw-book1-chapter2_Sc2.description: I became accustomed to the routine of my classes and to the social patterns at school.
tw-book1-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: I got used to the routine of my classes.

tw-book1-chapter2_Sc2.description: I accepted an invitation to the La Push Ocean Park trip and agreed to go more out of politeness than desire.
tw-book1-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: Mostly it centered around a trip to the La Push Ocean Park in two weeks that Mike was putting together. I was invited, and I had agreed to go, more out of politeness than desire.

tw-book1-chapter2_Sc2.description: I dislike snow and I find it inferior to rain because it is too cold and melts unpleasantly.
tw-book1-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: Ew. Snow. There went my good day.

tw-book1-chapter2_Sc2.description: I felt more comfortable in Forks than I had expected and more comfortable than I had ever expected to feel here.
tw-book1-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: All in all, I was feeling a lot more comfortable than I had thought I would feel by this point. More comfortable than I had ever expected to feel here.

tw-book1-chapter2_Sc2.description: I worried that I might be responsible for Edward's continued absence from school even though I thought that worry was ridiculous.
tw-book1-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: I tried not to think about him, but I couldn't totally suppress the worry that I was responsible for his continued absence, ridiculous as it seemed.

tw-book1-chapter2_Sc2.description: I noticed Edward and his family enjoying the snow and I perceived Edward as less pale with the circles under his eyes less noticeable.
tw-book1-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: They were laughing. Edward, Jasper, and Emmett all had their hair entirely saturated with melting snow. His skin was less pale, I decided — flushed from the snow fight maybe — the circles under his eyes much less noticeable.

tw-book1-chapter2_Sc2.description: I felt self-conscious at lunch, considered escaping to the nurse, and kept my head down to avoid attention.
tw-book1-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: I told him it was nothing, but I was wondering if I should play it up and escape to the nurse's office for the next hour.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc1.description: I woke up confused in an unfamiliar hotel room.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: When I woke up I was confused.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc1.description: I noticed hotel details like bedside lamps bolted to the tables, long drapes matching the bedspread, and generic watercolor prints on the walls.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: This room was too bland to belong anywhere but in a hotel. The bedside lamps, bolted to the tables, were a dead giveaway, as were the long drapes made from the same fabric as the bedspread, and the generic watercolor prints on the walls.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc1.description: I remembered riding in a sleek black car with windows darker than a limousine and a nearly silent engine while we raced across black freeways at more than twice the legal speed.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: I did remember the sleek black car, the glass in the windows darker than that on a limousine. The engine was almost silent, though we'd raced across the black freeways at more than twice the legal speed.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc1.description: I found that I had been crying until my tears ran dry and that Alice's thin cotton shirt was cold and damp from those tears.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: The front of her thin cotton shirt was cold, damp with the tears that streamed from my eyes until, red and sore, they ran dry.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc1.description: I realized that I could not sleep because closing my eyes made unbearably vivid images flash behind my lids.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: Sleep had evaded me; my aching eyes strained open even though the night finally ended and dawn broke over a low peak somewhere in California. But I couldn't close them; when I did, the images that flashed all too vividly, like still slides behind my lids, were unbearable.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc1.description: I felt comforted by Alice's presence and by the cool hardness of her neck when my head rested against it, and I noticed that my closeness did not bother her.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: And I remembered Alice sitting with me on the dark leather backseat. Somehow, during the long night, my head had ended up against her granite neck. My closeness didn't seem to bother her at all, and her cool, hard skin was oddly comforting to me.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc2.description: I learned that we had arrived over Phoenix and I observed the palm trees, smog, freeways, golf courses, and swimming pools.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: I stared blankly at the wide, flat expanse laid out in front of me. Phoenix — the palm trees, the scrubby creosote, the haphazard lines of the intersecting freeways, the green swaths of golf courses and turquoise splotches of swimming pools, all submerged in a thin smog and embraced by the short, rocky ridges that weren't really big enough to be called mountains.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc2.description: I realized we had made a three-day journey in one.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: I didn't have enough emotion left to be surprised that we'd made a three-day journey in one.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc2.description: I remembered beginning the loop around Sky Harbor International and I understood we were close to the airport.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: I remembered beginning the loop around Sky Harbor International… but not ending it.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc2.description: I confirmed that it was three in the morning and I saw that my room looked out on a deserted section of the freeway and the new long-term parking garage for the airport.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: The red numbers claimed it was three o'clock, but they gave no indication if it was night or day. My room looked out on a deserted section of the freeway and the new long-term parking garage for the airport.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc2.description: I noticed I was still wearing Esme's clothes and I discovered my duffel bag on top of the low dresser.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: I was still wearing Esme's clothes, and they didn't fit very well at all. I looked around the room, glad when I discovered my duffel bag on top of the low dresser.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc2.description: I felt no relief and I had no sense of homecoming despite arriving.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: I felt no relief, no sense of homecoming.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc2.description: I noticed Jasper's voice was soft and un-alarming when he asked which way to the airport and I registered that his question broke the long night's silence.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: "Which way to the airport, Bella?" Jasper had asked, and I flinched, though his voice was quite soft and un-alarming. It was the first sound, besides the purr of the car, to break the long night's silence.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc2.description: I remembered Alice physically supporting me with my arm draped over her shoulder and her arm firm around my waist as she dragged me along while I stumbled.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: I did have a vague impression of leaving the car — the sun was just falling behind the horizon — my arm draped over Alice's shoulder and her arm firm around my waist, dragging me along as I stumbled through the warm, dry shadows.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc3.description: I learned that we must stay inside as a precaution.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: "We'll need to stay inside," she told me.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc3.description: I learned that Alice ordered food for me and that Edward reminded her I have to eat more frequently than they do.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: "I ordered some food for you, it's in the front room. Edward reminded me that you have to eat a lot more frequently than we do."

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward had called before they left but had not called since.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: "He called?" "No," she said, and watched as my face fell. "It was before we left."

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc3.description: I learned that we were supposed to wait for Carlisle to call for further information.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: "What do we do now?" "We wait for Carlisle to call."

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc3.description: I observed that Alice and Jasper were staring blankly at the TV and remained unnaturally still.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: "Alice perched on the arm of the sofa and stared blankly at the TV like Jasper."

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc3.description: I felt my distrust of Alice increase because her calm words did not match her wide, honest eyes.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: "Her eyes were wide, honest… and I didn't trust them."

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc3.description: I became more alert and anxious when I realized Edward had called earlier.
I became dependent on Carlisle and Edward for updates and for decisions during this uncertain situation.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc4.description: I learned that Laurent warned that James was lethal and that this warning frightened me.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: You heard what Laurent said. "He said James was lethal."

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc4.description: I felt my guilt slowly subside after Alice's reassurance calmed me.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: My guilt slowly subsided as I looked into her dark eyes.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc4.description: I was told by Jasper that I had nothing to worry about and that I was completely safe here.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: "Bella," he said in a suspiciously soothing voice. "You have nothing to worry about. You are completely safe here."

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc4.description: I understood that the Cullen family fears losing me and that they value my presence with Edward.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc5.description: I learned that food was brought to me at regular intervals while we stayed in the room.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: At regular intervals, food was delivered for me.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc5.description: I realized that my babysitters handled the suspense better than I did, highlighting my own greater anxiety.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: My babysitters handled the suspense better than I did.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc5.description: I began to view Alice and Jasper as watchers or guardians, almost statue-like as their eyes followed me.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: they simply grew more still, two statues whose eyes followed me imperceptibly as I moved.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc5.description: I noticed that the silver phone on Alice's bag became a focus of my attention as the hours passed.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: The silver phone resting on Alice's bag seemed to grow bigger as the hours passed.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc5.description: I found that trying to sleep alone increased my panic until I surrendered to Jasper's supervision.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: I hoped that by myself in the dark, I could give in to the terrible fears that hovered on the edge of my consciousness, unable to break through under Jasper's careful supervision.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc6.description: I learned that Carlisle planned to lead the tracker far north to wait until he got close and then turn and ambush him.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: Carlisle wanted to lead the tracker as far north as possible, wait for him to get close, and then turn and ambush him.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc6.description: I learned that Esme and Rosalie were instructed to head west as long as they could keep the female behind them and to return to Forks if the female turned around in order to watch Bella's dad.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: Esme and Rosalie were supposed to head west as long as they could keep the female behind them. If she turned around, they were to head back to Forks and keep an eye on your dad.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc6.description: I learned that Alice inferred that the lack of calls meant the tracker was close enough that they did not want him to overhear.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: So I imagine things are going well if they can't call. It means the tracker is close enough that they don't want him to overhear.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc6.description: I learned that Alice said she could tell the mechanics of how to become a vampire but only as a theory because she neither remembers the process nor has she done or seen it done.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: I'll tell you the mechanics of it, but I don't remember it myself, and I've never done it or seen it done, so keep in mind that I can only tell you the theory.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc6.description: I decided that Alice's direct statement 'I will always tell you the truth' was sincere and that Bella could trust her on honesty.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: Yes. I will always tell you the truth.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc6.description: I felt that Edward's opposition to Alice telling Bella created a point of contention and that Bella became more determined to assert her right to know despite Edward's wishes.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: "Edward doesn't want me to tell you that," she said firmly, but I sensed she didn't agree. "That's not fair. I think I have a right to know."

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc7.description: I learned that vampires possess enhanced strength, speed, acute senses, some have extra senses, and they are physically attractive to their prey.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc7.source_text: "As predators, we have a glut of weapons in our physical arsenal — much, much more than really necessary. The strength, the speed, the acute senses, not to mention those of us like Edward, Jasper, and I, who have extra senses as well. And then, like a carnivorous flower, we are physically attractive to our prey."

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc7.description: I learned that vampires are venomous and that their venom incapacitates rather than kills, spreading slowly through the bloodstream and causing agonizing change until the heart stops and the conversion is finished.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc7.source_text: "We're also venomous," she said, her teeth glistening. "The venom doesn't kill — it's merely incapacitating. It works slowly, spreading through the bloodstream, so that, once bitten, our prey is in too much physical pain to escape us. Mostly superfluous, as I said. If we're that close, the prey doesn't escape. Of course, there are always exceptions. Carlisle, for example." "So… if the venom is left to spread…" I murmured. "It takes a few days for the transformation to be complete, depending on how much venom is in the bloodstream, how close the venom enters to the heart. As long as the heart keeps beating, the poison spreads, healing, changing the body as it moves through it. Eventually the heart stops, and the conversion is finished. But all that time, every minute of it, a victim would be wishing for death."

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc7.description: I learned that tasting or smelling blood triggers a nearly uncontrollable feeding frenzy in vampires, making biting someone likely to provoke blood-lust and making the act difficult for the vampire and painful for the victim.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc7.source_text: "We're also like sharks in a way. Once we taste the blood, or even smell it for that matter, it becomes very hard to keep from feeding. Sometimes impossible. So you see, to actually bite someone, to taste the blood, it would begin the frenzy. It's difficult on both sides — the blood-lust on the one hand, the awful pain on the other."

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc7.description: I remembered that Edward had demonstrated the same predatory attraction for me in the meadow, which reinforced my awareness of how perilous his nature can be.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc7.source_text: I was very still, remembering how pointedly Edward had demonstrated the same concept for me in the meadow.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc7.description: I learned that Alice does not remember being human while most vampires recall the transformation's pain as the sharpest memory of their human lives.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc7.source_text: "For everyone else, the pain of transformation is the sharpest memory they have of their human life. I remember nothing of being human."

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc8.description: I learned that the tracker's plans have changed.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc8.source_text: It means the tracker's plans have changed.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc8.description: I learned that the tracker will be in the mirror room today or maybe tomorrow.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc8.source_text: He'll be in the mirror room today, or maybe tomorrow.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc8.description: I learned that the mirror room is long with mirrors everywhere, a wooden floor, and a gold stripe across the mirrors, and that there is a black table with a big stereo and a TV.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc8.source_text: I see a room. It's long, and there are mirrors everywhere. The floor is wooden. ... There's gold… a gold stripe across the mirrors. And there's a black table with a big stereo, and a TV.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc8.description: I learned that the tracker is currently in a dark room running a VCR and touching the VCR.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc8.source_text: He's watching TV… no, he's running a VCR, in the dark, in another place. ... He's touching the VCR there, but he doesn't watch the way he does in the dark room. This is the room where he waits.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc8.description: I became convinced that the tracker will elude the hunters and will not be in the mountains north of Washington.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc8.source_text: But we do know that he won't be in the mountains north of Washington, being hunted. He'll elude them.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc8.description: I felt more reliant on Alice's visions in the moment because I jerked my head up, stared at her startled, and sat close to catch her low, quick voice.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc8.source_text: My head jerked up as I stared at her, startled. I sat close to her, leaning in to catch her low, quick voice.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc9.description: I learned that Alice told Carlisle she had just seen him in a vision and described that vision.
I learned that they lost the pursuer who kept his distance and that he appeared to have boarded a plane likely heading back to Forks.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc9.source_text: "we lost him. He seems suspicious of us — he's careful to stay just far enough away that I can't hear what he's thinking. But he's gone now — it looks like he got on a plane. We think he's heading back to Forks to start over."

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc9.description: I learned that Esme has been in town and that Esme and Rosalie are watching Charlie and the house to keep him safe.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc9.source_text: "Yes — the female has been in town. She went to the house, but while Charlie was at work. She hasn't gone near him, so don't be afraid. He's safe with Esme and Rosalie watching."

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc9.description: I felt the hovering cloud of despair lighten and drift back as I heard his voice and his reassurance.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc9.source_text: "It was so unbelievably good to hear his voice. I felt the hovering cloud of despair lighten and drift back as he spoke."

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc9.description: I learned that Edward reaffirmed his love, promised to come as soon as possible, and vowed to make me safe first.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc9.source_text: "I will make you safe first." "I love you,"

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc10.description: I recognized the sketched room as a ballet studio that looked like the place I used to go for dance lessons.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc10.source_text: "It's a ballet studio," I said, suddenly recognizing the familiar shapes.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc10.description: I remembered the studio's location as being near my mother's house in Phoenix at Fifty-eighth Street and Cactus.
I used Alice's phone to leave a voicemail asking my mom to call the number Alice provided and to wait to speak with me.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc10.source_text: "Mom," I said after the beep, "it's me. Listen, I need you to do something. It's important. As soon as you get this message, call me at this number."

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc10.description: I felt the cloud of depression creeping over me again after the phone went dead and I noticed my anxiety rising as I considered possible complications.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc10.source_text: As soon as the phone went dead, the cloud of depression began to creep over me again.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc10.description: I concluded that the room Alice drew might just be another typical dance studio and not necessarily connected to Alice or Jasper.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc10.source_text: "No, not at all — I suppose most dance studios would look the same — the mirrors, the bar."

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc10.description: I became worried about my mother's safety at home because I was thinking about something Edward had said about a red-haired female at my father's house and at the school where my records would be.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc10.source_text: I was thinking about something Edward had said, about the red-haired female at Charlie's house, at the school, where my records would be.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc11.description: I settled into the sofa, nibbling on leftover fruit and anticipating a long evening.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc11.source_text: I settled into the sofa, nibbling on a plate of leftover fruit, anticipating a long evening.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc11.description: I thought about calling Charlie and felt unsure whether I should be home by now.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc11.source_text: I thought about calling Charlie, but I wasn't sure if I should be home by now.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc11.description: I concentrated on the news and watched for stories about Florida, spring training, strikes, hurricanes, or terrorist attacks.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc11.source_text: I concentrated on the news, watching out for stories about Florida, or about spring training — strikes or hurricanes or terrorist attacks — anything that might send them home early.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc11.description: I concluded that immortality must grant endless patience.
I watched Alice sketch the vague outline of the dark room from her vision in the light from the TV.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc11.source_text: For a while, Alice sketched the vague outline of the dark room from her vision, as much as she could see in the light from the TV.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc11.description: I noticed that neither Jasper nor Alice seemed to feel the need to do anything at all, which made me perceive their calm as almost detached from my worry.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc11.source_text: Neither Jasper nor Alice seemed to feel the need to do anything at all.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc11.description: I observed that Jasper had no urge to pace, peek through the curtains, or run screaming out the door like I did.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc11.source_text: Jasper, too, seemed to have no urge to pace, or peek through the curtains, or run screaming out the door, the way I did.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc11.description: I must have fallen asleep on the couch while waiting for the phone to ring again.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc11.source_text: I must have fallen asleep on the couch, waiting for the phone to ring again.

tw-book1-chapter20_Sc11.description: I was briefly woken by the touch of Alice's cold hands as she carried me to the bed and I was unconscious again before my head hit the pillow.
tw-book1-chapter20_Sc11.source_text: The touch of Alice's cold hands woke me briefly as she carried me to the bed, but I was unconscious again before my head hit the pillow.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc1.description: I learned that I was waking too early and that my days and nights were slowly reversing.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: I could feel it was too early again when I woke, and I knew I was getting the schedule of my days and nights slowly reversed.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc1.description: I learned that Alice and Jasper were sitting together on the sofa with Alice sketching while Jasper looked over her shoulder.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: Alice and Jasper were sitting together on the sofa, Alice sketching again while Jasper looked over her shoulder.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc1.description: I learned that Alice's vision depicted a square room with dark beams across a low ceiling, wood-paneled walls, a patterned dark carpet, a large south window, an opening to the west, a tan stone fireplace between rooms, and a TV and VCR on a too-small wooden stand in the southwest corner.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: I watched as Alice drew a square room with dark beams across its low ceiling. The walls were paneled in wood, a little too dark, out of date. The floor had a dark carpet with a pattern in it. There was a large window against the south wall, and an opening through the west wall led to the living room. The focus of the room from this perspective, the TV and VCR, balanced on a too-small wooden stand, were in the southwest corner of the room.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc1.description: I felt close enough to Jasper to creep to his side, ask about Alice's vision, and accept his explanation.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: "Did she see something more?" I asked him quietly.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc1.description: I learned the intended placement of the phone in the vision when I pointed and whispered where it should go.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: "The phone goes there," I whispered, pointing.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc1.description: I was surprised that Alice and Jasper were loud enough for me to hear from my room and I found that notable.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: That they were loud enough for me to hear at all was strange.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward is coming to get me and that he, Emmett and Carlisle will take me somewhere to hide.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: Edward is coming to get you. He and Emmett and Carlisle are going to take you somewhere, to hide you for a while.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc2.description: I learned that Jasper and Alice will stay until my mother is safe.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: Jasper and I will stay till she's safe.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc2.description: I realized that Alice had a precise rendering of my mother's family room.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: I stared at the precise rendering of my mother's family room.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc2.description: I noticed that Jasper's light touch on my shoulder strengthened his calming influence on me.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: He lightly touched his hand to my shoulder, and the physical contact seemed to make his calming influence stronger.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc2.description: I felt that I couldn't win and that I couldn't guard everyone I know forever.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: I can't win, Alice. You can't guard everyone I know forever.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc2.description: I believed that seeing Edward soon was the only solace and hope I had left.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: The only solace, the only hope I had left, was knowing that I would see Edward soon.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc2.description: I trusted Alice's assurance that they would catch him while remaining deeply worried about others being harmed in the process.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: "We'll catch him, Bella," she assured me.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc3.description: I learned that an unknown man on the phone was threatening my mother and controlling what I had to say.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: Now, I don't need to hurt your mother, so please do exactly as I say, and she'll be fine.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc3.description: I learned that the kidnapper ordered me to go to my mother's house and call a specific number next to the phone before noon.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: I want you to go to your mother's house. Next to the phone there will be a number. Call it, and I'll tell you where to go from there.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc3.description: I became convinced that obedience was the only safe option to protect my mother, despite my horror.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: My joints were frozen with terror — I couldn't unbend my fingers to drop it.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc3.description: I noticed that Alice and Jasper were taking protective actions for me while simultaneously creating distance because Jasper left the room and Alice planned to relocate closer to my mother's house.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: Alice was talking as rapidly as ever, but what caught my attention was that, for the first time, Jasper was not in the room.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward's expected arrival time was nine-forty-five from Alice's update about a plane.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: "They're just boarding their plane," Alice told me. "They'll land at nine-forty-five."

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc4.description: I decided I had to go to the mirrored room and likely die to try to save my mother.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: I read: 'To plan. For I had no choices now but one: to go to the mirrored room and die.'

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc4.description: I learned that James had my mother captive and that I had to act because she was in danger.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: I read: 'He has my mom, and I have to try.'

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc4.description: I learned that Alice and Jasper were waiting nearby and that evading them was essential to my plan.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: I read: 'I had to think clearly, because Alice and Jasper were waiting for me, and evading them was absolutely essential, and absolutely impossible.'

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc4.description: I accepted that I would not see Edward again and that I could not say goodbye to him.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: I read: 'I had to accept that I wouldn't see Edward again, not even one last glimpse of his face to carry with me to the mirror room.'

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc4.description: I asked Edward to forgive me and to not come after James because I feared anyone coming after him would be hurt.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: I read: 'And please, please, don't come after him. That's what he wants. I think. I can't bear it if anyone has to be hurt because of me, especially you.'

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc4.description: I expressed gratitude toward Alice and Jasper and asked Edward to tell them thank you, asking especially that Alice be thanked.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: I read: 'Tell them thank you for me. Alice especially, please.'

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc4.description: I sealed away my heart and steeled myself emotionally to carry out the plan.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: I read: 'And then I carefully sealed away my heart.'

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc5.description: I learned that I was afraid to be in the same room with Alice and afraid to hide from her for the same reason.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: I was afraid to be in the same room with her, afraid that she would guess… and afraid to hide from her for the same reason.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc5.description: I learned that I was surprised to see Alice physically react to something by bending over the desk and gripping the edge with both hands.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: I would have thought I was far beyond the ability to be surprised, my thoughts tortured and unstable, but I was surprised when I saw Alice bent over the desk, gripping the edge with two hands.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc5.description: I learned that I instinctively hurried to Alice's side and reached out to touch her hand when I saw her distressed.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: I hurried to her side, reaching out automatically to touch her hand.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc5.description: I changed my belief to suspect that Alice had seen something concerning about my family because my thoughts flew to my mother in that moment.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: My thoughts flew to my mother. Was I already too late?

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc5.description: I grew to rely on Jasper's calming influence because I welcomed the tranquil atmosphere he created and used it to control my emotions.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: I felt a tranquil atmosphere settle around me.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc5.description: I learned that I prepared practically to leave by digging through my bag for the sock full of money and emptying it into my pocket.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: I dug through my bag until I found my sock full of money.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc5.description: I learned that I was anxious to get to the airport and that we left by seven, with me sitting alone in the back of the car.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: I was anxious to get to the airport, and glad when we left by seven.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc5.description: I updated my view of Alice to see her as desperate and secretive because I could feel her wild, well-concealed desperation to have me out of the room to be alone with Jasper.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: I could feel Alice's wild — though well-concealed — desperation to have me out of the room, to be alone with Jasper.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc6.description: I learned that I hid an unmarked letter under Alice's bag for Edward to find.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: "My letter," I said. She nodded, tucking it under the top flap. He would find it soon enough.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc6.description: I learned that the airport ladies' room I used has two exits, which I exploit to slip away.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: "I remembered the time I had gotten lost from this bathroom, because it had two exits."

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc6.description: I realized that I accepted I would never see the distant cities Alice and Jasper discussed.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: "Places I'd never seen. And would never see."

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc6.description: I noticed that I perceived Alice as watching me closely but not yet suspicious, attributing her confusion to tracker interference rather than betrayal.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: "Alice's eyes were confused, but — I saw to my relief— not suspicious. She must be attributing the change in her vision to some maneuver of the tracker's rather than a betrayal by me."

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc6.description: I discovered that my longing for Edward intensified and made my planned escape feel much harder to carry out.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: "every cell in my body seemed to know he was coming, to long for his coming."

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc7.description: I learned that I received a direct phone call from my antagonist who began with 'Hello, Bella' and commented that I had been quick.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc7.source_text: I heard 'Hello, Bella,' that easy voice answered. 'That was very quick. I'm impressed.'

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc7.description: I learned that my house was empty when I returned and that the caller reassured me that my mother was perfectly fine.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc7.source_text: I heard 'She's perfectly fine. Don't worry, Bella, I have no quarrel with her.'

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc7.description: I learned that the caller arranged for me to come to the ballet studio around the corner and that I was expected there soon.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc7.source_text: I heard 'Do you know the ballet studio just around the corner from your home?' and I heard 'Well, then, I'll see you very soon.'

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc7.description: I learned that the ballet studio was closed for spring break yet unlocked and that the east dance floor was lit while the west was dark.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc7.source_text: I saw the sign that said the dance studio was closed for spring break and I saw that 'The east dance floor, the bigger room, was lit.'

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc7.description: I changed from trying to force calm and not panic to being overwhelmed by terror and feeling literally trapped when I entered the studio.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc7.source_text: I felt 'Terror seized me so strongly that I was literally trapped by it.'

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc7.description: I updated my view to understand that the caller was my enemy who had last walked through my familiar rooms and violated my sanctuary.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc7.source_text: I noticed 'The last person to walk through those familiar rooms was my enemy.'

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc8.description: I learned that my mother was safe in Florida because she never received my message.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc8.source_text: My mother was safe. She was still in Florida. She'd never gotten my message.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc8.description: I felt immediate relief and almost giddy bravado when I believed my family would not be harmed.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc8.source_text: "Yes," I answered, my voice saturated with relief. "I felt almost giddy."

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc8.description: I knew that I had left Edward a letter asking him not to hunt James.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc8.source_text: I asked him not to. "I left him a letter."

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc8.description: I discovered that James had a running video camera and intended to leave a recorded message to provoke Edward.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc8.source_text: "Would you mind, very much, if I left a little letter of my own for your Edward?" ... "A small red light indicated that it was already running."

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc8.description: I judged James as average-looking and courteous while also seeing his eyes as thirsty and his actions as deliberately menacing.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc8.source_text: He was so very average-looking, nothing remarkable about his face or body at all. Just the white skin, the circled eyes I'd grown so used to.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc9.description: I realized I was badly injured with a broken leg and a scalp wound that bled heavily and made me lose consciousness.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc9.source_text: He was over me at once, his foot stepping down hard on my leg. I heard the sickening snap before I felt it. But then I did feel it, and I couldn't hold back my scream of agony.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc9.description: I noticed that the blood from my head was driving the hunter into an uncontrollable thirst that made him more dangerously focused on feeding.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc9.source_text: Through the nausea and dizziness I saw something that gave me a sudden, final shred of hope. His eyes, merely intent before, now burned with an uncontrollable need. The blood — spreading crimson across my white shirt, pooling rapidly on the floor — was driving him mad with thirst.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc9.description: I changed my belief that this would be a quick end when I realized there wouldn't be enough for him to feed and go and that he intended to prolong the attack.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc9.source_text: There wouldn't be enough for him to win, to feed and go. There would be no quick end like I'd been counting on.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc9.description: I viewed the hunter as a calculating predator who treated my injuries as entertainment while he circled and smiled before attacking.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc9.source_text: He stepped back, and began to circle, casually, as if he were trying to get a better view of a statue in a museum. His face was still open and friendly as he decided where to start. Then he slumped forward, into a crouch I recognized, and his pleasant smile slowly widened, grew, till it wasn't a smile at all but a contortion of teeth, exposed and glistening.

tw-book1-chapter21_Sc9.description: I wanted Edward to try to find me and I called his name in a desperate hope that he would come.
tw-book1-chapter21_Sc9.source_text: "Wouldn't you rather have Edward try to find me?" he prompted. "No!" I croaked. "No, Edward, don't—"

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc1.description: I learned that I believed I was dead while I was submerged and dreaming.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: And then I knew I was dead.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc1.description: I learned that an angelic voice called my name and called me to the only heaven I wanted.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: Because, through the heavy water, I heard the sound of an angel calling my name, calling me to the only heaven I wanted.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc1.description: I learned that the angel cried out in horror specifically saying "Oh no, Bella, no!" and begged for me.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: "Oh no, Bella, no!" the angel's voice cried in horror.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc1.description: I changed to feeling that the angel's weeping was wrong and surprising because I expected an angel not to weep.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: The angel shouldn't weep, it was wrong.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc1.description: I realized that the voice calling me was desperately attached and terrified at the thought of losing me.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: "Bella, please! Bella, listen to me, please, please, Bella, please!" he begged.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc1.description: I learned that I experienced a point of pressure and increasing pains before I cried out and broke the surface gasping.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: There was a point of pressure against my head. It hurt. Then, as that pain broke through the darkness to me, other pains came, stronger pains. I cried out, gasping, breaking through the dark pool.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc2.description: I learned I had lost some blood and that my head wound wasn't deep.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: "She's lost some blood, but the head wound isn't deep," a calm voice informed me.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc2.description: I learned that my leg was broken.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: "Watch out for her leg, it's broken."

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc2.description: I learned that I had some damaged ribs.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: "Some ribs, too, I think," the methodical voice continued.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc2.description: I learned that my hand was burning with a scalding pain that overshadowed other pains.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: There was a new pain, a scalding pain in my hand that was overshadowing everything else.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc2.description: I realized I was not in heaven because the intensity of pain made that impossible.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: This couldn't be heaven, could it? There was too much pain for that.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc2.description: I felt reassured and loved when Edward told me I was going to be fine and said he loved me.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: "Bella, you're going to be fine. Can you hear me, Bella? I love you."

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc2.description: I learned that Alice had found me and was present.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: "She's here, she knew where to find you."

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc2.description: I trusted Carlisle to give me something to stop the pain.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: "I know, Bella. Carlisle will give you something, it will stop."

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc3.description: I learned that my hand was burning from a wound.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc3.source_text: "My hand is burning!" I screamed, finally breaking through the last of the darkness, my eyes fluttering open.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc3.description: I learned that I had been bitten.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc3.source_text: "He bit her." Carlisle's voice was no longer calm, it was appalled.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc3.description: I became terrified and desperate as the pain and the image of fire overwhelmed me.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc3.source_text: "The fire! Someone stop the fire!" I screamed as it burned me.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc3.description: I felt pressure and something poking and pulling at my scalp while they examined me.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc3.source_text: As Carlisle spoke, I could feel more pressure on my head, something poking and pulling at my scalp.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc4.description: I experienced severe burning pain and writhing in my leg and hand during the attack.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: I writhed in the grip of the fiery torture, the movement making the pain in my leg flare sickeningly.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc4.description: I felt Edward physically restrain my hand and press his lips to my skin to remove the venom.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: I felt his cool, strong fingers on my burning hand, locking it in place. Then his head bent over it, and his cold lips pressed against my skin.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc4.description: I became reassured that Edward would stay with me after he promised he would.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: 'Stay, Edward, stay with me…' 'I will.' His voice was strained, but somehow triumphant.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc4.description: I realized my fear of losing Edward intensified as my consciousness slipped and I feared the darkness.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: I felt my consciousness slipping as the pain subsided. I was afraid to fall into the black waters again, afraid I would lose him in the darkness.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc5.description: I realized that the fire was gone and that my other pains had been dulled by a sleepiness seeping through my body.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: "The fire was gone, the other pains dulled by a sleepiness seeping through my body."

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc5.description: I heard Edward say that my blood tasted clean and that he could taste the morphine in it.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: "Her blood tastes clean," Edward said quietly. "I can taste the morphine."

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc5.description: I learned that the attacker had watched our videos and that he knew Alice and where she came from.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: "He tricked me, Edward. He watched our videos."

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc5.description: I noticed that I smelled gasoline even as I drifted in and out of consciousness.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: "I smell gasoline," I added, surprised through the haze in my brain.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc5.description: I felt reassured by Edward's declaration of love and by his quiet, relieved laugh after I responded that I knew he loved me.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: "I love you," he answered. "I know," I breathed, so tired. I heard my favorite sound in the world: Edward's quiet laugh, weak with relief.

tw-book1-chapter23_Sc5.description: I surrendered to sleep feeling safe when Edward offered to carry me and soothe me in his arms.
tw-book1-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: "You can sleep, sweetheart, I'll carry you," Edward soothed me. "Sleep now, Bella" were the last words I heard.

tw-book1-chapter24_Sc1.description: I woke in a white hospital room with tubes, monitors, and a nasal tape after an attack.
tw-book1-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: My eyes opened to a bright, white light. I was in an unfamiliar room, a white room.

tw-book1-chapter24_Sc1.description: I learned that I sustained severe injuries including a broken leg, four broken ribs, skull cracks, extensive bruising, and major blood loss.
tw-book1-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: You have a broken leg, four broken ribs, some cracks in your skull, bruises covering every inch of your skin, and you've lost a lot of blood.

tw-book1-chapter24_Sc1.description: I learned that Alice called my family and that Renée was at the hospital.
tw-book1-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: Alice called them. Renée is here — well, here in the hospital.

tw-book1-chapter24_Sc1.description: I felt relieved and elated to be alive and grateful for Edward's presence.
tw-book1-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: I realized again that I was alive, this time with gratitude and elation.

tw-book1-chapter24_Sc1.description: I felt guilty and apologetic for nearly taking myself away from Edward forever.
I understood that Edward, Alice, Carlisle, Emmett, and Jasper love me and acted to protect me.
tw-book1-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: They love you, too, you know.

tw-book1-chapter24_Sc3.description: I relied on Edward to support me as I limped toward the school.
tw-book1-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: He kept his arm tightly around me, supporting me as I limped toward the school.

tw-book1-chapter24_Sc3.description: I noticed the Cullen family dancing flawlessly and drawing everyone's attention.
tw-book1-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: Emmett and Jasper were intimidating and flawless in classic tuxedos.

tw-book1-chapter24_Sc3.description: I was surprised to realize that I was actually enjoying myself… a little.
tw-book1-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: I was surprised to realize that I was actually enjoying myself… a little.

tw-book1-chapter24_Sc3.description: I observed Edward become angry and possessive when Jacob arrived.
tw-book1-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: Edward was staring toward the doors, and his face was angry.

tw-book1-chapter24_Sc3.description: I accepted that Jacob still liked me after he told me I looked really pretty.
tw-book1-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: "You look really pretty, by the way," he added shyly.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.description: I noticed the morning light was clearer and that no fog veiled my window.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: I realized there was no fog veiling my window.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.description: I learned that a fine layer of snow covered the yard and that yesterday's rain had frozen into dangerous ice on the driveway.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: A fine layer of snow covered the yard, dusted the top of my truck, and whitened the road. ... All the rain from yesterday had frozen solid — coating the needles on the trees in fantastic, gorgeous patterns, and making the driveway a deadly ice slick.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.description: I learned that Charlie had left for work before I got downstairs.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: Charlie had left for work before I got downstairs.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.description: I ate a quick bowl of cereal and drank orange juice from the carton.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: I threw down a quick bowl of cereal and some orange juice from the carton.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.description: I realized I felt excited to go to school and that the excitement scared me because I was eager to see Edward Cullen.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: I felt excited to go to school, and that scared me. ... I knew I was eager to get to school because I would see Edward Cullen.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.description: I concluded it was very stupid that I wanted to see him and believed my league and his league were spheres that did not touch.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: And that was very, very stupid. ... I was well aware that my league and his league were spheres that did not touch.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.description: I became suspicious of Edward because I questioned why he should lie about his eyes.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: And I was suspicious of him; why should he lie about his eyes?

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.description: I was frightened of the hostility I sometimes felt emanating from him.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: I was still frightened of the hostility I sometimes felt emanating from him,

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.description: I found myself tongue-tied whenever I pictured his perfect face.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: and I was still tongue-tied whenever I pictured his perfect face.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.description: I almost lost my balance on the icy driveway but managed to cling to the truck's side mirror and save myself.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: I almost lost my balance when I finally got to the truck, but I managed to cling to the side mirror and save myself.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc2.description: I distracted myself from my fear of falling and from unwanted speculations about Edward Cullen by thinking about Mike and Eric.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: Driving to school, I distracted myself from my fear of falling and my unwanted speculations about Edward Cullen by thinking about Mike and Eric, and the obvious difference in how teenage boys responded to me here.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc2.description: I noticed Mike's puppy dog behavior and I noticed Eric's apparent rivalry with him as disconcerting.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: Whatever the reason, Mike's puppy dog behavior and Eric's apparent rivalry with him were disconcerting.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc2.description: My truck had thin chains crisscrossed in diamond shapes around the tires that Charlie had put on early.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: There were thin chains crisscrossed in diamond shapes around them. Charlie had gotten up who knows how early to put snow chains on my truck.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc2.description: I observed that my truck seemed to have no problem with the black ice that covered the roads even though I drove very slowly.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: My truck seemed to have no problem with the black ice that covered the roads. I drove very slowly, though, not wanting to carve a path of destruction through Main Street.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc2.description: I was surprised by Charlie's unspoken concern and I realized I was not used to being taken care of.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: My throat suddenly felt tight. I wasn't used to being taken care of, and Charlie's unspoken concern caught me by surprise.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc2.description: I heard a high-pitched screech and I saw a dark blue van skidding with locked tires, spinning wildly across the ice toward my truck while I stood between them.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: It was a high-pitched screech, and it was fast becoming painfully loud. I looked up, startled. I saw several things simultaneously. ... But of more immediate importance was the dark blue van that was skidding, tires locked and squealing against the brakes, spinning wildly across the ice of the parking lot. It was going to hit the back corner of my truck, and I was standing between them.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc2.description: I experienced an adrenaline rush that seemed to make my brain work much faster, allowing me to absorb several details at once.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: Instead, the adrenaline rush seemed to make my brain work much faster, and I was able to absorb in clear detail several things at once.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc3.description: I learned that my head struck the icy blacktop and that I felt something solid and cold pinning me to the ground.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: My head cracked against the icy blacktop, and I felt something solid and cold pinning me to the ground.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc3.description: I learned that the van curled gratingly around the end of the truck and was still spinning and sliding toward me.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: the van was still coming. It had curled gratingly around the end of the truck and, still spinning and sliding, was about to collide with me again.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc3.description: I learned that I had a throbbing ache centered above my left ear after the impact.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: I became aware of a throbbing ache centered above my left ear.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc3.description: I realized that Edward could move with astonishing speed and precision when he saved me from beneath the van.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: Then his hands moved so fast they blurred. One was suddenly gripping under the body of the van, and something was dragging me, swinging my legs around like a rag doll's, till they hit the tire of the tan car.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc3.description: I felt intensely protected and closely attended by Edward when he held me against his body in an iron grasp and asked if I was all right.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc3.source_text:
I tried to sit up, and realized he was holding me against the side of his body in an iron grasp.

"Bella? Are you all right?"

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc4.description: I was loaded into the back of the ambulance with a neck brace while Edward rode in the front.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc4.source_text: It took six EMTs and two teachers — Mr. Varner and Coach Clapp — to shift the van far enough away from us to bring the stretchers in. Edward vehemently refused his, and I tried to do the same, but the traitor told them I'd hit my head and probably had a concussion. I almost died of humiliation when they put on the neck brace. It looked like the entire school was there, watching soberly as they loaded me in the back of the ambulance. Edward got to ride in the front.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc4.description: I saw a deep dent in the tan car's bumper that matched the contours of Edward's shoulders, suggesting he had braced against the car.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc4.source_text: When they'd lifted me away from the car, I had seen the deep dent in the tan car's bumper — a very distinct dent that fit the contours of Edward's shoulders… as if he had braced himself against the car with enough force to damage the metal frame…

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc4.description: I tried to find a logical explanation that excluded the possibility that I was insane after seeing evidence that contradicted Edward's denials.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc4.source_text: I tried to think of a logical solution that could explain what I had just seen — a solution that excluded the assumption that I was insane.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc4.description: I felt humiliated and increasingly suspicious of Edward after he intervened with EMTs and refused to admit being by the car.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc4.source_text: Edward vehemently refused his, and I tried to do the same, but the traitor told them I'd hit my head and probably had a concussion. I almost died of humiliation when they put on the neck brace. It looked like the entire school was there, watching soberly as they loaded me in the back of the ambulance. Edward got to ride in the front. It was maddening.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc5.description: I learned that I was placed in the emergency room and given basic vital checks (pressure cuff and thermometer).
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: They put me in the emergency room, a long room with a line of beds separated by pastel-patterned curtains. A nurse put a pressure cuff on my arm and a thermometer under my tongue.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc5.description: I learned that I removed a neck brace because there was no privacy and I hid it under the bed.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: Since no one bothered pulling the curtain around to give me some privacy, I decided I wasn't obligated to wear the stupid-looking neck brace anymore. When the nurse walked away, I quickly unfastened the Velcro and threw it under the bed.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc5.description: I learned that Tyler Crowley was badly hurt and was brought in on a stretcher with bloodstained bandages.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: I recognized Tyler Crowley from my Government class beneath the bloodstained bandages wrapped tightly around his head.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc5.description: I learned that I was X-rayed and that I did not have a concussion.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: They wheeled me away then, to X-ray my head. I told them there was nothing wrong, and I was right. Not even a concussion.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc5.description: I realized that I was not imagining what I had seen and that my perception could not be easily explained away.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: I knew I wasn't crazy. What had happened? There was no way to explain away what I'd seen.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc5.description: I credited Edward Cullen with pulling me out of the way and saving me during Tyler's accident.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: Umm… Edward pulled me out of the way.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc6.description: I learned that my X-rays look good and that my father is in the waiting room so I can go home with him.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc6.source_text: "Your X-rays look good," he said. "Well, your father is in the waiting room — you can go home with him now. But come back if you feel dizzy or have trouble with your eyesight at all."

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc6.description: I realized that I had been extremely lucky that Edward happened to be standing next to me when I was hurt.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc6.source_text: "It sounds like you were extremely lucky," Dr. Cullen said, smiling as he signed my chart with a flourish. "Lucky Edward happened to be standing next to me," I amended with a hard glance at the subject of my statement.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc6.description: I suspected that Dr. Cullen was complicit with Edward about managing the situation.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc6.source_text: My intuition flickered; the doctor was in on it.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward appeared uninjured and that there were visible dents on the vehicles after the accident.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc7.source_text: "your hands left dents in the side of it — and you left a dent in the other car, and you're not hurt at all"

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc7.description: I became convinced that Edward may have physically lifted the van off me to save my legs.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc7.source_text: "You think I lifted a van off you?"

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc7.description: I grew more suspicious and distrustful of Edward because I realized I was lying for him without understanding why.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc7.source_text: "I want to know why I'm lying for you."

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc7.description: I decided that I was not going to tell anybody about what happened at the scene.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc8.description: I learned that Dr. Cullen examined me and said I was fine and could go home.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: Dr. Cullen saw me, and he said I was fine and I could go home.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc8.description: I became convinced that Edward's defensive behavior in the hall confirmed the bizarre things I had witnessed.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: I was positive that Edward's defensive behavior in the hall was a confirmation of the bizarre things I still could hardly believe I'd witnessed.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc8.description: I became more obsessed with Edward and less eager to escape Forks despite the danger.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: I was consumed by the mystery Edward presented. And more than a little obsessed by Edward himself. ... I wasn't as eager to escape Forks as I should be, as any normal, sane person would be.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc8.description: I noticed Charlie acted protectively but awkwardly by putting one arm behind my back, not quite touching me.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: Charlie put one arm behind my back, not quite touching me, and led me to the glass doors of the exit.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc8.description: I felt betrayed and appalled when Charlie told my mother about the incident.
I experienced a strong sense of relief once I was inside the cruiser.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: It was a huge relief— the first time I'd ever felt that way — to get into the cruiser.

tw-book1-chapter3_Sc8.description: I dreamed of Edward Cullen for the first time that night.
tw-book1-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: That was the first night I dreamed of Edward Cullen.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc1.description: I learned that I dreamed of Edward walking away and that I could not catch up to him.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: I couldn't see his face, just his back as he walked away from me, leaving me in the blackness.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc1.description: I learned that I woke in the middle of the night troubled and that I could not sleep again for a long time.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: Troubled, I woke in the middle of the night and couldn't sleep again for what seemed like a very long time.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc1.description: I became more anxious and restless because Edward began appearing in my dreams nearly every night but always remained out of reach.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: After that, he was in my dreams nearly every night, but always on the periphery, never within reach.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc2.description: I found myself the center of attention for the rest of that week after the accident.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: To my dismay, I found myself the center of attention for the rest of that week.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc2.description: I experienced Tyler Crowley following me around obsessively and trying to make amends.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: Tyler Crowley was impossible, following me around, obsessed with making amends to me somehow.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc2.description: I noticed that Tyler followed me between classes and sat at our now-crowded lunch table.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: He followed me between classes and sat at our now-crowded lunch table.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc2.description: I observed that Mike and Eric were even less friendly toward Tyler and that I feared gaining another unwelcome fan.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: Mike and Eric were even less friendly toward him than they were to each other, which made me worry that I'd gained another unwelcome fan.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc2.description: I learned that other students claimed they had not seen Edward until after the van was pulled away.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: Jessica, Mike, Eric, and everyone else always commented that they hadn't even seen him there till the van was pulled away.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc2.description: I realized with chagrin that no one else was as aware of Edward as I always was, which explained why others did not notice him.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: With chagrin, I realized the probable cause — no one else was as aware of Edward as I always was.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc2.description: I felt that the Cullens and the Hales remained aloof at their usual table and that none of them, especially Edward, glanced my way anymore.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: The Cullens and the Hales sat at the same table as always, not eating, talking only among themselves. None of them, especially Edward, glanced my way anymore.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc2.description: I concluded that Edward wished he hadn't pulled me from the path of Tyler's van.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: He wished he hadn't pulled me from the path of Tyler's van — there was no other conclusion I could come to.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc3.description: I went from furious anger at Edward for withholding the truth to feeling awed gratitude because he had saved my life.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: I still was angry that he wouldn't trust me with the truth, even though I was keeping my part of the bargain flawlessly. But he had in fact saved my life, no matter how he'd done it. And, overnight, the heat of my anger faded into awed gratitude.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc3.description: I tried to talk to Edward the day after the accident and discovered that he ignored me in Biology when I greeted him.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: I wanted very much to talk to him, and the day after the accident I tried. He turned his head a fraction toward me without meeting my gaze, nodded once, and then looked the other way.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc3.description: I watched Edward from a distance in the cafeteria and parking lot but gave him no notice in class, which left me miserable.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: I watched him sometimes, unable to stop myself— from a distance, though, in the cafeteria or parking lot. But in class I gave no more notice that he existed than he showed toward me. I was miserable.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc3.description: I lied in my emails but learned that the tenor of my messages alerted Renée to my depression and she called worried.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: Despite my outright lies, the tenor of my e-mails alerted Renée to my depression, and she called a few times, worried.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc3.description: I noticed that Mike was pleased by the obvious coolness between Edward and me and that he grew more confident around me.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: Mike, at least, was pleased by the obvious coolness between me and my lab partner. I could see he'd been worried that Edward's daring rescue might have impressed me, and he was relieved that it seemed to have the opposite effect. He grew more confident, sitting on the edge of my table to talk before Biology class started, ignoring Edward as completely as he ignored us.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.description: I learned that Jessica called on the first Tuesday of March to ask permission to invite Mike to the girls' choice spring dance in two weeks.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.source_text: Jessica made me aware of another event looming on the horizon — she called the first Tuesday of March to ask my permission to invite Mike to the girls' choice spring dance in two weeks.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.description: I learned that I told Jessica, "No, Jess, I'm not going," refusing to attend the dance.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.source_text: "No, Jess, I'm not going," I assured her.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.description: I learned that I considered dancing to be glaringly outside my range of abilities.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.source_text: Dancing was glaringly outside my range of abilities.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.description: I learned that Mike told me he had told Jessica he had to think about going to the dance.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.source_text: "I told her I had to think about it."

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.description: I learned that Mike asked me if I might be planning to ask him to the dance.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.source_text: "I was wondering if… well, if you might be planning to ask me."

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.description: I learned that I told Mike I was going to Seattle that Saturday as an excuse to avoid the dance.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.source_text: "I'm going to Seattle that Saturday," I explained.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.description: I felt a wave of guilt and pity sweep through me when Mike hesitated, which weakened my resolve to be indifferent to his feelings.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.source_text: I paused for a moment, hating the wave of guilt that swept through me.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.description: I recognized that Edward has a strong and unhealthy influence over my emotions and that I considered that level of influence to be pathetic and unhealthy.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.source_text: I couldn't allow him to have this level of influence over me. It was pathetic. More than pathetic, it was unhealthy.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.description: I suspected that Jessica enjoyed my inexplicable popularity more than my actual company, which changed my view of her motivations.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.source_text: I suspected that Jessica enjoyed my inexplicable popularity more than my actual company.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.description: I inferred that Mike might be interested in me romantically when he blushed and asked if I might be planning to ask him to the dance.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc4.source_text: His face was bright red as he looked down again.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc5.description: I learned that he believes it is better if we are not friends.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc5.source_text: I heard "It's better if we're not friends," he explained.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc5.description: I began to believe that he might regret having saved my life.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc5.source_text: I heard "For not just letting that stupid van squish me."

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc5.description: I felt our relationship cool and saw him intentionally trying to distance us.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc5.source_text: I heard "It's better if we're not friends," he explained. "Trust me."

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc5.description: I noticed that he had already stacked my books and handed them back to me with a hard face.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc5.source_text: I noticed "He was there; he'd already stacked them into a pile. He handed them to me, his face hard."

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc6.description: I learned that I was distracted during gym because my head was filled with Edward which made me clumsy and not receive passes.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc6.source_text: Today I was worse than usual because my head was so filled with Edward. My team never passed me the ball, so that was good, but I fell down a lot.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc6.description: I learned that my truck had only minimal damage from the accident and that I had replaced the taillights.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc6.source_text: The truck had suffered only minimal damage in the accident. I'd had to replace the taillights, and if I'd had a real paint job, I would have touched that up.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc6.description: I learned that Eric asked me to the spring dance and that I told him I would be in Seattle that day.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc6.source_text: "Uh, I was just wondering… if you would go to the spring dance with me?" ... "Thank you for asking me, but I'm going to be in Seattle that day."

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc6.description: I learned that Tyler also asked me to the spring dance while we were stuck in the parking aisle and then mentioned prom.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc6.source_text: "Will you ask me to the spring dance?" he continued. "I'm not going to be in town, Tyler." ... "That's cool. We still have prom."

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc6.description: I noticed my irritation toward Edward and his family escalated to the point I fantasized about bumping his car.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc6.source_text: My foot itched toward the gas pedal… one little bump wouldn't hurt any of them, just that glossy silver paint job.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc6.description: I realized I perceived Edward as amused by my discomfort after he seemed to shake with laughter while watching me.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc6.source_text: In his rearview mirror, Edward's eyes were on me. He was unquestionably shaking with laughter, as if he'd heard every word Tyler had said.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc7.description: I decided to make chicken enchiladas for dinner to keep myself occupied.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc7.source_text: When I got home, I decided to make chicken enchiladas for dinner.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc7.description: I received a phone call from Jessica who was jubilant because Mike had accepted her invitation.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc7.source_text: It was Jessica, and she was jubilant; Mike had caught her after school to accept her invitation.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc7.description: I realized that Edward's comment meant he probably wasn't interested in me and didn't want to lead me on.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc7.source_text: He must see how absorbed I was by him; he must not want to lead me on… so we couldn't even be friends… because he wasn't interested in me at all.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc7.description: I decided I would leave Edward alone and stop pursuing a relationship with him.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc7.source_text: Well, that was fine. I could leave him alone. I would leave him alone.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc7.description: I told my dad that I'm going to Seattle for the day a week from Saturday and asked if that was okay.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc7.source_text: Um, I just wanted to let you know that I'm going to Seattle for the day a week from Saturday… if that's okay?

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc8.description: I learned that Bella dropped her key into a puddle and that a hand grabbed it before she could retrieve it.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc8.source_text: I fumbled with my key and it fell into a puddle at my feet. As I bent to get it, a white hand flashed out and grabbed it before I could.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc8.description: I realized Bella's feelings toward Edward shifted from anger to a conflicted attraction when she felt a thrill at saying his name.
tw-book1-chapter4_Sc8.source_text: I felt a thrill go through me as I said his name, and I hated it.

tw-book1-chapter4_Sc8.description: I acknowledged that Bella agreed to go to Seattle with Edward when she nodded in response to his question.
