tw-book1-chapter4_Sc8.source_text: Will you go with me to Seattle? I couldn't speak yet, so I just nodded.

tw-book1-chapter5_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward is dangerous.
tw-book1-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: He was dangerous. He'd been trying to tell me that all along.

tw-book1-chapter5_Sc2.description: I realized that I did not believe Edward was bad and felt more fascinated than afraid.
tw-book1-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: No, I don't believe that you're bad.

tw-book1-chapter5_Sc2.description: I acknowledged that I felt anxious and fascinated rather than frightened when I was near him.
tw-book1-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: I just felt anxious, on edge… and, more than anything else, fascinated.

tw-book1-chapter5_Sc2.description: I discovered that the sight or prospect of blood makes me lightheaded and nearly faint.
tw-book1-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: Can someone take Bella to the nurse, please?

tw-book1-chapter5_Sc2.description: I admitted to myself that I was too much of a coward to risk ditching class even when tempted.
tw-book1-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: I was far too big a coward to risk getting caught.

tw-book1-chapter5_Sc2.description: I felt a growing complicated pull toward Edward despite his admission of danger.
tw-book1-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: He just looked at me, eyes full of some emotion I couldn't comprehend.

tw-book1-chapter5_Sc3.description: I felt that fainting spells always exhausted me.
I learned that I was seventeen when I answered Edward's question.
tw-book1-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: "I'm seventeen," I responded, a little confused.

tw-book1-chapter5_Sc3.description: I recognized Clair de Lune because my mother plays a lot of classical music around the house.
tw-book1-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: "My mother plays a lot of classical music around the house — I only know my favorites."

tw-book1-chapter5_Sc3.description: I discovered that I was excused from Gym and that Edward intended to take me home and have Alice drop off my truck.
tw-book1-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: "Bella has Gym next hour, and I don't think she feels well enough. Actually, I was thinking I should take her home now. Do you think you could excuse her from class?" / "I'll have Alice drop it off after school."

tw-book1-chapter5_Sc3.description: I felt a twinge of enthusiasm at the idea that Edward might join the La Push outing when I invited him.
I noticed that Edward gripped a fistful of my jacket and pulled me toward his car.
tw-book1-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: He was gripping a fistful of my jacket in one hand.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc1.description: I listened for my truck and noticed when it arrived during the storm.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: As I sat in my room, trying to concentrate on the third act of Macbeth, I was really listening for my truck.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc1.description: I learned that Mike kept quiet about details and that Edward's involvement was unknown to others.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: Luckily Mike had kept his mouth shut, and no one seemed to know about Edward's involvement.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc1.description: I wasn't looking forward to Friday and I found my low expectations confirmed.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: I wasn't looking forward to Friday, and it more than lived up to my non-expectations.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc1.description: I still hoped to see Edward even though I knew he would not be there.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: The worst part about Friday was that, even though I knew he wasn't going to be there, I still hoped.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc1.description: I noticed Rosalie, Alice, and Jasper sitting together at Edward's table when I entered the cafeteria.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: When I walked into the cafeteria with Jessica and Mike, I couldn't keep from looking at his table, where Rosalie, Alice, and Jasper sat talking, heads close together.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.description: I noticed I was right behind Lauren and very close to her hair.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: I was right behind her, just a foot from her slick, silver blond hair, and she was evidently unaware of that.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.description: I realized Lauren disliked me after hearing her sneer my name and suggest I sit with the Cullens.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: …don't know why Bella" — she sneered my name — "doesn't just sit with the Cullens from now on.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.description: I heard Mike defend me by insisting that I was his friend and that I sat with their group.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: "She's my friend; she sits with us," Mike whispered back loyally, but also a bit territorially.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.description: I decided to pause and avoid hearing any more of the hostile conversation.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: I paused to let Jess and Angela pass me. I didn't want to hear any more.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.description: I was surprised by the malice in Lauren's voice and I reassessed my assumption about our relationship.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: I really didn't know her well at all, certainly not well enough for her to dislike me — or so I'd thought. "I was surprised by the malice in it."

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.description: I learned that my dad seemed enthusiastic about my trip to La Push the next morning.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: That night at dinner, Charlie seemed enthusiastic about my trip to La Push in the morning.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.description: I thought my dad might feel guilty for leaving me home alone on weekends and I inferred that he knew many details about the other kids and families.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: I think he felt guilty for leaving me home alone on the weekends, but he'd spent too many years building his habits to break them now. Of course he knew the names of all the kids going, and their parents, and their great-grandparents, too, probably.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.description: I decided not to tell my dad about my plan to ride to Seattle with Edward Cullen.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: I wondered if he would approve of my plan to ride to Seattle with Edward Cullen. Not that I was going to tell him.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.description: I learned that Goat Rocks was described as a poor camping choice because of bears and hunting season.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: "It's not a very good place for camping." He sounded surprised. "Too many bears. Most people go there during the hunting season."

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: I opened my eyes to see a clear yellow light streaming through my window.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: I opened my eyes to see a clear yellow light streaming through my window.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: I noticed the sun was in the wrong place in the sky, too low and seeming farther than it should be.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: It was in the wrong place in the sky, too low, and it didn't seem to be as close as it should be, but it was definitely the sun.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: I learned that the Newtons' Olympic Outfitters store was just north of town.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: The Newtons' Olympic Outfitters store was just north of town.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: I saw Mike's Suburban and Tyler's Sentra in the parking lot when I arrived.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: In the parking lot I recognized Mike's Suburban and Tyler's Sentra.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: I recognized Eric and two other boys from my class, fairly sure their names were Ben and Conner, and I saw Jess flanked by Angela and Lauren.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: As I pulled up next to their vehicles, I could see the group standing around in front of the Suburban. Eric was there, along with two other boys I had class with; I was fairly sure their names were Ben and Conner. Jess was there, flanked by Angela and Lauren.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: I noticed a girl I remembered from Gym gave me a dirty look and Lauren eyed me scornfully while Jessica glowered.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: That one gave me a dirty look as I got out of the truck, and whispered something to Lauren. Lauren shook out her cornsilk hair and eyed me scornfully. ... I could see Jessica glowering at us now.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: I heard Mike call delightedly that I had come and remind me he said it would be sunny today.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: "You came!" he called, delighted. "And I said it would be sunny today, didn't I?"

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: I accepted Mike's offer to ride in his car and I was promised shotgun.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: "Will you ride in my car? It's that or Lee's mom's minivan." "Sure." He smiled blissfully. "You can have shotgun," he promised.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: I lied that I hadn't invited anyone while secretly wishing a miracle and that Edward would appear.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: "Nope," I lied lightly, hoping I wouldn't get caught in the lie. But also wishing that a miracle would occur, and Edward would appear.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: I hid my chagrin about the seating arrangement while trying to make both Mike and Jessica happy.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: I hid my chagrin. It wasn't as simple to make Mike and Jessica happy at the same time.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.description: I found that Lee brought two extra people so every seat was necessary and I managed to wedge Jess between Mike and me, which seemed to appease her.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: The numbers worked out in my favor, though. Lee brought two extra people, and suddenly every seat was necessary. I managed to wedge Jess in between Mike and me in the front seat of the Suburban. ... at least Jess seemed appeased.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.description: I learned the drive to La Push from Forks is only fifteen miles through dense green forest and along the Quillayute River.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: It was only fifteen miles to La Push from Forks, with gorgeous, dense green forests edging the road most of the way and the wide Quillayute River snaking beneath it twice.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.description: I realized I had the window seat and that the Suburban felt claustrophobic with nine people inside.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: I was glad I had the window seat. We'd rolled the windows down — the Suburban was a bit claustrophobic with nine people in it — and I tried to absorb as much sunlight as possible.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.description: I remembered that I had been to the beaches around La Push many times during my Forks summers with Charlie.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: I'd been to the beaches around La Push many times during my Forks summers with Charlie, so the mile-long crescent of First Beach was familiar to me.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.description: I observed the beach features including dark gray water, islands with sheer cliffs, a thin sand border, millions of smooth stones, and huge bleached driftwood trees.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: It was still breathtaking. The water was dark gray, even in the sunlight, white-capped and heaving to the gray, rocky shore. Islands rose out of the steel harbor waters with sheer cliff sides, reaching to uneven summits, and crowned with austere, soaring firs. The beach had only a thin border of actual sand at the water's edge, after which it grew into millions of large, smooth stones that looked uniformly gray from a distance, but close up were every shade a stone could be: terra-cotta, sea green, lavender, blue gray, dull gold. The tide line was strewn with huge driftwood trees, bleached bone white in the salt waves, some piled together against the edge of the forest fringe, some lying solitary, just out of reach of the waves.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.description: I noticed a fire circle filled with black ashes and a ring of driftwood logs clearly used for gatherings like ours.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: We picked our way down to the beach, Mike leading the way to a ring of driftwood logs that had obviously been used for parties like ours before. There was a fire circle already in place, filled with black ashes.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.description: I watched Eric and Ben gather dry branches and build a teepee fire structure while Mike set it alight.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: Eric and the boy I thought was named Ben gathered broken branches of driftwood from the drier piles against the forest edge, and soon had a teepee-shaped construction built atop the old cinders. "Have you ever seen a driftwood fire?" Mike asked me. ... Eric and the boy I thought was named Ben gathered broken branches of driftwood from the drier piles against the forest edge, and soon had a teepee-shaped construction built atop the old cinders. He lit another small branch and laid it alongside the first.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.description: I learned that driftwood fires can burn blue and green because of the salt, and I found the colors striking.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: "It's blue," I said in surprise. "The salt does it. Pretty, isn't it?"

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.description: I noticed Mike came to sit beside me while Jess sat on his other side and claimed his attention.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: He lit one more piece, placed it where the fire hadn't yet caught, and then came to sit by me. Thankfully, Jess was on his other side. She turned to him and claimed his attention.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.description: I felt surprised and pleased by the unexpected beauty of the blue and green flames.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: "It's blue," I said in surprise. "The salt does it. Pretty, isn't it?"

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc5.description: I loved the tide pools since childhood and looked forward to them when coming to Forks.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc5.source_text: They had fascinated me since I was a child; they were one of the only things I ever looked forward to when I had to come to Forks.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc5.description: I had fallen into the tide pools a lot as a child.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc5.source_text: I'd also fallen into them a lot.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc5.description: I was very cautious not to lean too far over the little ocean ponds.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc5.source_text: I was very cautious not to lean too far over the little ocean ponds.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc5.description: I hated to lose the sky in the woods and found the forest's green light murky and ominous.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc5.source_text: I hated to lose the sky in the woods. The green light of the forest was strangely at odds with the adolescent laughter, too murky and ominous to be in harmony with the light banter around me.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc5.description: I remembered Edward's request that I not fall into the ocean and let that memory influence my caution.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc5.source_text: It reminded me of Edward's request — that I not fall into the ocean.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc5.description: I fell a few times on the return hike and sustained shallow scrapes and green-stained knees.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc5.source_text: I got some shallow scrapes on my palms, and the knees of my jeans were stained green, but it could have been worse.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc6.description: I learned that I had bought Billy's truck and that Jacob Black identified himself as Billy's son when he introduced himself.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc6.source_text: I quote 'You bought my dad's truck' and 'I'm Jacob Black' from the scene.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc6.description: I became disturbed when I realized that my perception of time in Forks varied and I knew exactly what caused that difference.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc6.source_text: I quote 'I knew exactly what caused the difference, and it disturbed me.' from the scene.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc6.description: I found Jacob easy to talk with and I noticed that his appreciative smile made me and others recognize a growing rapport.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc6.source_text: I quote 'He flashed a brilliant smile, looking at me appreciatively in a way I was learning to recognize. I wasn't the only one who noticed.' from the scene.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.description: I heard Mike and Jessica approaching the beach and calling out to the group.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.source_text: "There you are, Bella," Mike called in relief, waving his arm over his head.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.description: I noticed that Mike asked about a boyfriend, signaling that others were curious about Bella's relationship status.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.source_text: "Is that your boyfriend?" Jacob asked, alerted by the jealous edge in Mike's voice.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.description: I felt guilty for using Jacob's eagerness to flirt with him, even though I wanted to make him happy.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.source_text: I felt guilty as I said this, knowing that I'd used him.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.description: I realized that I really did like Jacob and that I could easily be friends with him.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.source_text: But I really did like Jacob. He was someone I could easily be friends with.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.description: I winked at Jacob and I noticed he responded with elation at my inept flirting.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.source_text: I winked at him, carefully turning away from Mike to do so. He smiled, elated by my inept flirting.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.description: I promised Jacob that I would come to Forks next time Charlie visited Billy, updating our plan to see each other again.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.source_text: "Next time Charlie comes down to see Billy, I'll come, too," I promised.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.description: I crawled into the backseat by Angela and Tyler and I announced I had already ridden shotgun.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.source_text: I crawled into the backseat by Angela and Tyler, announcing that I'd already had my turn in the shotgun position.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc1.description: I heard Bella tell Charlie that she was busy with homework and declined dinner.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: I heard Bella tell Charlie she's busy with homework and declines dinner.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc1.description: I observed Bella lock her door and remove headphones and a CD as soon as she was alone.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: I observed Bella lock her door, dig out headphones and a CD, and use loud music.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc1.description: I felt that Bella was deliberately using loud music to try to drown out her thoughts about recent events.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: I noticed Bella used loud music to try to drown her thoughts and avoid thinking about recent events.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc1.description: I saw the music eventually lull Bella to sleep after she used it to cope.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: I saw the music eventually lull her to sleep.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc2.description: I realized that I was in a lucid dream feeling pulled toward both forest light and the ocean.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc2.source_text: I heard 'drawn toward forest light and the ocean'.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc2.description: I felt my fear about Jacob's warnings intensify while my fascination with Edward deepened.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc2.source_text: I recalled 'fuses Bella's fears about Jacob's warnings and her fascination with Edward'.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc2.description: I understood that Jacob acts as a force pulling me back from dangerous impulses in the dream.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc3.description: I learned that I woke abruptly at about 5:30 a.m., dislodging my CD player and struggling to settle back to sleep.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: Bella wakes abruptly at about 5:30 a.m., dislodging her CD player, and struggles to settle back to sleep.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc3.description: I learned that I showered and readied myself slowly while the dream images persisted.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: She showers and readies herself slowly while reflecting on the persistence of the dream images.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc3.description: I learned that I checked Charlie's cruiser and concluded he had gone fishing.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: She checks Charlie's cruiser and concludes he's gone fishing.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc3.description: I learned that I dressed in comfortable clothes and made my bed before moving to do research.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: She dresses in comfortable clothes and makes her bed before moving to do research.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc3.description: I changed my belief about how effective routine can be, shifting from dream-state anxiety to concrete morning tasks that steady me.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: (This small, domestic scene transitions from dream-state anxiety to concrete morning routine and sets up her next action: research.)

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc3.description: I updated my view of Charlie as someone whose absence in the morning leaves space for my own actions and planning.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: She checks Charlie's cruiser and concludes he's gone fishing.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc4.description: I learned about a single myth that mentions 'good' vampires and considered it relevant to the Cullens.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I read: 'She finds mostly conflicting or irrelevant accounts but notes a single myth that mentions 'good' vampires.'

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc4.description: I noticed that the sunlight incompatibility problem puzzles me because traditional folklore did not explain the Cullens' behavior.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I read: 'The sunlight incompatibility problem puzzles her.'

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc4.description: I shifted from inward brooding to active investigation by searching online and comparing multiple sources.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I read: 'This scene shifts the narrative focus from internal emotion to investigative action.'

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc4.description: I compared entries with Jacob's statements and with my own observations, which made me consider that the Cullens might differ from usual vampire myths.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I read: 'She sifts through myths and folklore, comparing entries with what she and Jacob have said and with her own observations of the Cullens.'

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc5.description: I learned that I left the house wearing boots and a raincoat and that I walked east into the surrounding forest to escape my thoughts.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: I put on boots and a raincoat and walked east into the surrounding forest.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc5.description: I learned that the path grew quiet and close and that I sat briefly on a fallen log hidden from the trail.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: I sat briefly on a fallen log, hidden from the trail, as the path grew quiet and close.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc5.description: I began to seriously consider that the Cullens could be vampires and that this possibility needed real consideration.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: I reflected on whether the Cullens could be vampires.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc5.description: I recognized that I could not make myself stay away from the Cullens even if I thought they might be vampires.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: I weighed options and recognized I could not make myself stay away.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc5.description: I felt conflicted about how to relate to the Cullens and I found myself leaning toward maintaining contact rather than complete avoidance.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: I weighed avoidance versus maintaining contact and could not force myself to avoid them.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc6.description: I realized the rain-darkened forest exacerbated my fears.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: Bella realizes the rain-darkened forest exacerbates her fears and decides to leave.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc6.description: I hurried back along the path, emerged onto Charlie's lawn, and returned home.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: She hurries back along the path, emerges onto Charlie's lawn, and returns home.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc6.description: I dressed and concentrated on schoolwork, outlining a Macbeth paper as a means of self-control.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: She dresses and concentrates on schoolwork — outlining a Macbeth paper — as a means of self-control.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc6.description: I finished the paper before evening after a productive afternoon.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: The afternoon passes productively; she finishes the paper before evening.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc6.description: I recognized this scene as a decision point prompting temporary self-discipline.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: This scene marks a decision point and temporary self-discipline.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc7.description: I planned to pick up cookbooks the next day.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: Bella plans to pick up cookbooks.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc7.description: I spent the evening watching TV with my father.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: She spends the evening watching TV with him

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc7.description: I asked permission to go to Port Angeles the next night with Jessica and Angela to help choose dresses.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: and asks permission to go to Port Angeles the next night with Jessica and Angela to help choose dresses.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc7.description: I noticed Charlie reluctantly agreed to let me go.
We arranged dinner instructions to make things easy for him while I was out.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: and they arrange dinner instructions for his convenience.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc7.description: I felt grounded by the routine family interaction despite my inner turmoil.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: (This scene provides social dynamics of family, grounding Bella's life amid her inner turmoil.)

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc8.description: I learned that Bella woke to bright sun and felt buoyant while daydreaming through Trig on the picnic benches.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc8.source_text: I read 'Bella wakes to bright sun and a buoyant mood' and 'she sat on the picnic benches doing Trig problems but drifted into daydreams.'

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc8.description: I felt my hope of seeing the Cullens rise during the bright morning and carried that anticipation through the day.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc8.source_text: I read 'Bella's hope of seeing the Cullens rises.'

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc8.description: I noticed my fixation on Edward grew and that this growing focus began to shift my social dynamics among peers.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc8.source_text: I read 'the scene shifts social dynamics, showing Bella among peers while her fixation on Edward grows.'

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc8.description: I learned that Bella and her classmates planned to go to Port Angeles after school.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc8.source_text: I read 'school ends with plans to go to Port Angeles.'

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc9.description: I learned that I returned home and read briefly outdoors on a quilt before falling asleep.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: I returned home, read briefly outdoors on a quilt and fell asleep.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc9.description: I learned that I woke to Charlie arriving and that dinner was prepared so we watched television together.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: I woke to Charlie arriving; dinner was prepared, and I watched TV with him.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc9.description: I learned that Jessica called to cancel the original plan but rescheduled the shopping trip for the next night.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: I received a call from Jessica canceling but rescheduling the shopping trip for the next night.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc9.description: I learned that I composed a brief email to my mother before making preparations for the planned outing.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: I composed a brief email to my mother and prepared for the planned outing.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc9.description: I realized that the domestic calm of the afternoon made the forthcoming social excursion feel more significant and like an interruption to routine.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: I sensed a link between domestic calm and the forthcoming social excursion that will take me out of Forks for the evening.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc9.description: I noted that my relationship with Charlie is domestic and comfortable enough to share a prepared dinner and watch television together.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: I woke to Charlie arriving; dinner was prepared, and I watched TV with him.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc10.description: I learned that I woke to a sunny morning, dressed for warmth, and drove to school hoping to see Edward.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: Bella wakes to another sunny morning, dresses for warmth, and drives to school hoping to see Edward.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc10.description: I learned that I left a note for Charlie and swapped my wallet before leaving with friends.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: After school Jessica picks her up; Bella leaves a note for Charlie, swaps her wallet, and they drive off, excited to leave town limits and go to Port Angeles with Angela.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc10.description: I felt my anxiety heighten when I noticed the Cullen table was again empty.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: The Cullen table is again empty, heightening her anxiety.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc10.description: I realized that leaving Forks would physically move me away from familiar people and close the chapter of the morning's tension.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: (This closing scene closes the chapter’s arc by moving Bella physically away from Forks toward the evening outing that will further the plot.)

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc1.description: I learned we made it to Port Angeles by four after Jess drove faster than the Chief.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: Jess drove faster than the Chief, so we made it to Port Angeles by four.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc1.description: I felt invigorated by the estrogen rush and I enjoyed having a girls' night out.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: It had been a while since I'd had a girls' night out, and the estrogen rush was invigorating.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc1.description: I listened to whiny rock songs while Jessica jabbered about the boys we hung out with.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: We listened to whiny rock songs while Jessica jabbered on about the boys we hung out with.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc1.description: I learned that Jessica's dinner with Mike had gone very well and that she hoped they would progress to a first kiss by Saturday night.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: Jessica's dinner with Mike had gone very well, and she was hoping that by Saturday night they would have progressed to the first-kiss stage.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc1.description: I interrupted to spare Angela from a revealing question, which shows I wanted to protect her feelings.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: Jess tried to get her to confess who her type was, but I interrupted with a question about dresses after a bit, to spare her.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc1.description: I noticed Angela threw a grateful glance my way, indicating a positive moment between us.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: Angela threw a grateful glance my way.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc1.description: I observed that Port Angeles was more polished and quaint than Forks.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: Port Angeles was a beautiful little tourist trap, much more polished and quaint than Forks.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc1.description: I noted that Jess drove straight to the one big department store in town instead of lingering on the boardwalk.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: Jess drove straight to the one big department store in town, which was a few streets in from the bay area's visitor-friendly face.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc2.description: I learned that I had never been to a dance in Phoenix until I told Jessica and Angela about it.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: Both Jessica and Angela seemed surprised and almost disbelieving when I told them I'd never been to a dance in Phoenix.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc2.description: I acknowledged that I had never had a boyfriend or anything close and that I didn't go out much.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: 'I've never had a boyfriend or anything close. I didn't go out much.'

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc2.description: I discovered that Tyler had been telling people he was taking me to prom.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: Tyler told everyone he's taking you to prom, Jessica informed me with suspicious eyes.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc2.description: I became annoyed and gloomy about the Tyler rumor and the situation surrounding his guilt over the accident.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: The girls'-night high was wearing off in the wake of my annoyance at Tyler, leaving room for the gloom to move back in.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc2.description: I found myself beginning to really like Angela because she responded calmly and didn't pry into everything.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: I was beginning to really like Angela.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc2.description: I felt that Jessica was skeptical and teasing about my social life and about why Tyler might be acting the way he was.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: "That's why Lauren doesn't like you," Jessica giggled while we pawed through the clothes.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc3.description: I planned to meet Jess and Angela for dinner at a little Italian restaurant on the boardwalk but I wanted to look for a bookstore first.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: We planned to go to dinner at a little Italian restaurant on the boardwalk, but the dress shopping hadn't taken as long as we'd expected. I told them I would meet them at the restaurant in an hour — I wanted to look for a bookstore.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc3.description: I preferred to browse books alone because I became preoccupied when surrounded by books.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: they didn't know how preoccupied I could get when surrounded by books; it was something I preferred to do alone.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc3.description: I found a bookstore whose windows featured crystals and spiritual items and I didn't go inside.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: The windows were full of crystals, dream-catchers, and books about spiritual healing. I didn't even go inside.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc3.description: I saw an older woman with long gray hair dressed in a sixties-style dress smiling behind the counter through the bookstore glass.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: Through the glass I could see a fifty-year-old woman with long, gray hair worn straight down her back, clad in a dress right out of the sixties, smiling welcomingly from behind the counter.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc3.description: I became increasingly despairing and I tried to beat down my hopes for Saturday because I feared a painful disappointment.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: I was wrestling with despair. I was trying so hard not to think about him, and what Angela had said… and more than anything trying to beat down my hopes for Saturday, fearing a disappointment more painful than the rest,

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc3.description: I noticed a silver Volvo parked along the street and I felt my emotions crash when I saw it.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: when I looked up to see someone's silver Volvo parked along the street and it all came crashing down on me.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc3.description: I thought of him as a stupid, unreliable vampire in my own mind and I reacted with anger and disappointment.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: Stupid, unreliable vampire, I thought to myself.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc3.description: I realized I was going the wrong direction and I decided to turn east and loop around to try a different street back toward the boardwalk.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: I started to realize, as I crossed another road, that I was going the wrong direction. I decided to turn east at the next corner, and then loop around after a few blocks and try my luck on a different street on my way back to the boardwalk.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc4.description: I realized that I was being herded rather than merely followed.
I discovered that two men from the group walked quietly behind me while the other two positioned themselves farther down the street.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: I realized with a shock that two men were walking quietly twenty feet behind me.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc4.description: I learned that my pepper spray was inaccessible because it was still in my duffle bag under the bed.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: I knew exactly where my pepper spray was — still in my duffle bag under the bed, never unpacked.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc4.description: I noted that I had wandered far past the part of Port Angeles where I was supposed to be as a guest and that the area felt isolated and industrial.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: I'd wandered far past the part of Port Angeles that I, as a guest, was intended to see.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc4.description: I shifted from thinking the men's earlier boisterous behavior might be harmless to believing their actions were intentionally threatening and coordinated.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: I realized then that I wasn't being followed.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc4.description: I now viewed the men as predators with hostile intent who were deliberately corralling me.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc5.description: I learned that I was being pursued and felt cornered by several men on the street.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc5.source_text: The footsteps behind me were louder now.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc5.description: I prepared to defend myself by slipping my purse over my head and readying it as a weapon.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc5.source_text: With a quick movement I slipped my purse over my head, gripping the strap with one hand, ready to surrender it or use it as weapon as need demanded.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc5.description: I rehearsed specific self-defense moves in my head such as a heel thrust, eye gouge, and knee to the groin.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc5.source_text: Heel of the hand thrust upward, hopefully breaking the nose or shoving it into the brain. Finger through the eye socket — try to hook around and pop the eye out. And the standard knee to the groin, of course.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc5.description: I felt my choking fear vanish and an immediate sense of security when I heard the rescuer's voice.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc5.source_text: It was amazing how instantaneously the choking fear vanished, amazing how suddenly the feeling of security washed over me — even before I was off the street — as soon as I heard his voice.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc5.description: I trusted the driver instantly and studied his face with profound relief, seeing him as my rescuer.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc5.source_text: I stared at his face in profound relief, relief that went beyond my sudden deliverance, until it occurred to me that his expression was murderously angry.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc6.description: I plan to run over Tyler Crowley tomorrow before school as a way to stop him taking anyone to prom.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc6.source_text: "I'm going to run over Tyler Crowley tomorrow before school?"

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc6.description: I might total Tyler's Sentra to ensure he has no ride and cannot take anyone to prom.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc6.source_text: "I might have to total his Sentra, though. If he doesn't have a ride he can't take anyone to prom…"

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc6.description: I was supposed to meet Jessica and Angela and I know they will be worried about my lateness.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc6.source_text: "Jessica and Angela will be worried," I murmured.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc6.description: I felt that the simple word I offered was inadequate after Edward admitted his temper problem and I couldn't think of a better response.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc6.source_text: "The word seemed inadequate, but I couldn't think of a better response."

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc6.description: I noticed the clock on the dashboard and I learned it was past six-thirty.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward found me and intended to take me to dinner.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc7.source_text: "I'm taking you to dinner." He smiled slightly, but his eyes were hard.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward threatened to track down my friends if I did not stop them.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc7.source_text: "Go stop Jessica and Angela before I have to track them down, too. I don't think I could restrain myself if I ran into your other friends again."

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward offered to drive me home so my friends would not have to wait while I ate.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc7.source_text: "Do you mind if I drive Bella home tonight? That way you won't have to wait while she eats."

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc7.description: I felt frightened by the threat in his voice and I realized his presence could be intimidating to others.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc7.source_text: I shivered at the threat in his voice.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc7.description: I now view Edward as my perpetual savior and I wanted to be alone with him to ask questions.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc7.source_text: I wanted nothing more than to be alone with my perpetual savior.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward could influence others with a controlled, authoritative presence and that I complied when he insisted I go inside to eat.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc7.source_text: "Humor me." He walked to the door of the restaurant and held it open with an obstinate expression.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc8.description: I noticed that the hostess welcomed Edward more warmly than necessary and assessed him differently than me.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc8.source_text: She welcomed him a little more warmly than necessary.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc8.description: I felt surprised by how much the hostess's attention to Edward bothered me.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc8.source_text: I was surprised by how much that bothered me.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc8.description: I realized that Edward can 'dazzle' people with his smile and that it visibly unsettled the hostess.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc8.source_text: He flashed his gleaming smile, dazing her momentarily.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc8.description: I understood that Edward pays close attention to my physical state and acts protectively when he asks about how I am feeling.
I learned that I drank both Cokes, felt cold from the icy soda, shivered, and had left my jacket in Jessica's car.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc8.source_text:
I realized I had finished the whole thing when he pushed his glass toward me.
"The cold from the icy soda was radiating through my chest, and I shivered.
"Oh — I left it in Jessica's car," I realized.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc9.description: I noticed Edward wearing a light beige leather jacket and an ivory turtleneck that emphasized his muscular chest.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc9.source_text: I read 'Edward was shrugging out of his jacket'

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc9.description: I smelled his jacket and found its scent amazing and not like cologne.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc9.source_text: I read 'It smelled amazing. I inhaled, trying to identify the delicious scent. It didn't smell like cologne'

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc9.description: I confessed that I felt very safe with him and that the admission affected his expression.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc9.source_text: I read 'I feel very safe with you,' I confessed

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc9.description: I observed that his eyes were lighter and golden butterscotch at times and that his eyes became black when he was crabby.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc9.source_text: I read 'I saw how light his eyes were, lighter than I'd ever seen them, golden butterscotch' and I read 'You're always crabbier when your eyes are black'

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc9.description: I learned that he plays along with hypothetical questioning about mind reading and that he corrected the number of exceptions to one.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc9.source_text: I read 'with a few exceptions' and I read 'Just one exception,' he corrected

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc9.description: I learned that he told me I was a magnet for trouble and that anything dangerous within ten miles would find me.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc9.source_text: I read 'You are a magnet for trouble. If there is anything dangerous within a ten-mile radius, it will invariably find you'

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc9.description: I noticed that I reached for his hands and that he slid them away minutely, which updated my understanding of his reluctance to fully reveal the truth.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc9.source_text: I read 'I reached forward, without thinking, to touch his folded hands, but he slid them away minutely'

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc10.description: I learned that my number was up the first time he met me.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc10.source_text: "Your number was up the first time I met you."

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc10.description: I learned that he could find someone by listening to their mind and that he had been keeping tabs on Jessica and randomly searching people's thoughts on the street.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc10.source_text: "It's harder than it should be — keeping track of you. Usually I can find someone very easily, once I've heard their mind before... I was keeping tabs on Jessica, not carefully — like I said... I was just waiting for you, randomly searching through the thoughts of people on the street — to see if anyone had noticed you so I would know where you were."

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc10.description: I realized that my fear was stifled by an overwhelming sense of safety in his presence.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc10.source_text: "but the overwhelming sense of safety I felt in his presence stifled it."

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc10.description: I understood that he felt protective and was willing to consider taking me away at the expense of others' lives.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc10.source_text: "It was very… hard — you can't imagine how hard — for me to simply take you away, and leave them… alive."

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc11.description: I felt warm in his jacket and breathed its scent when I thought he couldn't see.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc11.source_text: I was warm in his jacket, though, breathing in the scent of it when I thought he couldn't see.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc11.description: I realized he didn't seem to be able to know what I was thinking in that moment.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc11.source_text: I looked at the sidewalk, grateful that he didn't seem to be able to know what I was thinking.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc11.description: I noticed he was careful not to touch me while still being attentive and polite, indicating a protective but distant behavior.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc11.source_text: He walked close beside me to the door, still careful not to touch me.

tw-book1-chapter8_Sc11.description: I felt amazed by his grace and believed he wasn't the kind of person anyone got used to.
tw-book1-chapter8_Sc11.source_text: I had a feeling Edward wasn't the kind of person anyone got used to.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward followed my scent when he tracked where I had gone.
I learned that Edward can read minds but only he possesses that ability and it is limited by distance.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: "No, it's just me. And I can't hear anyone, anywhere. I have to be fairly close."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward perceives many thoughts as a background hum and must focus to hear one mind clearly.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: "It's a little like being in a huge hall filled with people, everyone talking at once. It's just a hum — a buzzing of voices in the background. Until I focus on one voice, and then what they're thinking is clear."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward cannot read my thoughts and that he speculated my mind works differently, using a frequency analogy.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: "I don't know... The only guess I have is that maybe your mind doesn't work the same way the rest of theirs do. Like your thoughts are on the AM frequency and I'm only getting FM."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc1.description: I felt that my long-held suspicion that there was something odd about my mind was confirmed and embarrassing.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: "My mind doesn't work right? I'm a freak?"

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc1.description: I decided to keep Edward's explanation in mind and study it later, which changed how I would observe him going forward.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: I couldn't think of an acceptable response to that, but I filed it carefully away for future study.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: I became more afraid that Edward would be angry with me when I considered confessing about Jacob.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "I'm more afraid that you'll be angry with me."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob Black's father is one of the Quileute elders and that Jacob told me an old legend about vampires.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "His dad is one of the Quileute elders." "He told me one… about vampires."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: I confessed that I tricked Jacob into telling me the story by flirting with him and I now feel protective of him.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "I tricked it out of him." "I tried to flirt — it worked better than I thought it would."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: I discovered that Internet research did not provide convincing evidence about the legends and that most of what I found seemed silly.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "I did some research on the Internet." "No. Nothing fit. Most of it was kind of silly."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: I decided that it didn't matter to me what Edward was and I expressed willingness to be with him regardless.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: "I decided it didn't matter," I whispered.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward is seventeen and that he has remained that age for a long time.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: "Seventeen," he answered promptly. "A while," he admitted at last.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward cannot sleep at all.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: "I can't sleep." "Never," he said, his voice nearly inaudible.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned that his family generally hunts animals, tries not to hunt people, but can still be dangerous and make mistakes.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: "He said you didn't… hunt people. He said your family wasn't supposed to be dangerous because you only hunted animals." "We try... We're usually very good at what we do. Sometimes we make mistakes."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: I became more determined to spend time with Edward despite warnings and I felt panic at the thought of losing the chance to be with him.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: "It doesn't matter to me what you are." "I couldn't waste one minute I had with him."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward and his family hunt animals rather than people and that they call themselves vegetarians as a private joke.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.source_text: "I can't be sure, of course, but I'd compare it to living on tofu and soy milk; we call ourselves vegetarians, our little inside joke."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward went hunting with Emmett over the weekend.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.source_text: "Were you hunting this weekend, with Emmett?" "Yes."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward and his companions were away for three days and that they got back Sunday.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.source_text: "It was a very long three days. We got back Sunday."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: I changed my belief about the relevance of Edward's nature and decided that it doesn't matter what he is because it is too late for me to change my feelings.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.source_text: "I told you, it doesn't matter what you are. It's too late."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: I realized that I become anxious and deeply attached when Edward is absent and that his absence torments me.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: I learned that Edward promised to see me tomorrow and to save me a seat at lunch.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.source_text: "I'll save you a seat at lunch."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: I felt my attraction to Edward intensify, as the promise sent flutters through my stomach and made me unable to speak.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.source_text: It was silly, after everything we'd been through tonight, how that little promise sent flutters through my stomach, and made me unable to speak.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: I learned that Edward asked me not to go into the woods alone and implied that other dangers exist there.
I felt relieved and willing to obey his warning despite a shudder at the bleakness in his voice.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.source_text: I shuddered slightly at the sudden bleakness in his voice, but I was relieved.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: I noticed the scent on his jacket and then on his breath when he leaned close, which stunned me.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.source_text: His breath blew in my face, stunning me. It was the same exquisite scent that clung to his jacket, but in a more concentrated form.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: I realized that Edward both wants closeness and tries to control the timing of our meetings, as he sighed and indicated he wanted me to leave.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.source_text: "I'll see you tomorrow," he sighed, and I knew he wanted me to leave now.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: I felt a physical, startling reaction to his proximity, as my heart stopped beating when he leaned toward me.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: I learned that Edward was a vampire.
I learned that there was part of him that thirsted for my blood and I didn't know how potent that part might be.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc6.source_text: Second, there was part of him — and I didn't know how potent that part might be — that thirsted for my blood.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: I became unconditionally and irrevocably in love with him.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc6.source_text: And third, I was unconditionally and irrevocably in love with him.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: I experienced dizziness, coldness, and violent shudders that required a hot shower to relax my rigid muscles.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc6.source_text: I was really feeling dizzy now. I was freezing. I shuddered violently for several minutes before the steaming spray could finally relax my rigid muscles.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: I learned that I had left my jacket in Jessica's car and I called her to ask her to bring it tomorrow.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc6.source_text: "I left my jacket in her car — could you bring it to me tomorrow?"

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: I noticed that my father sounded concerned and he suggested I go lie down.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc6.source_text: "Are you all right?" "Well, maybe you should go lie down." He sounded concerned.

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.description: I realized that I was officially eighteen years old today.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: I was officially eighteen years old.

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.description: I felt dread and a changed perspective about my birthday because I recognized that I would age while Edward would remain forever seventeen.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: And now that it had hit, it was even worse than I'd feared it would be. I could feel it—I was older... And Edward never would be.

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.description: I discovered within my dream that my mirror-reflection appeared ancient, creased, and withered, representing a terrifying possible future.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: There was no Gran. That was me. Me in a mirror. Me—ancient, creased, and withered.

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.description: I acknowledged that my love for Edward is a secret that nobody, including my grandmother, knows about.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: Gran didn't know that I was in love with a vampire—nobody knew that—

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.description: I panicked at the thought that my grandmother might notice Edward's inhuman glittering in sunlight and thus discover our secret.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: I panicked because Gran didn't know that I was in love with a vampire—nobody knew that—so how was I supposed to explain the fact that the brilliant sunbeams were shattering off his skin into a thousand rainbow shards like he was made of crystal or diamond?

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.description: I learned that he can hear other people's thoughts clearly but that I am the only person whose thoughts he cannot hear.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: I usually felt grateful that I was the only person whose thoughts he couldn't hear just as clearly as if they were spoken aloud.

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc2.description: I felt furious and horrified that Edward seriously considered ending his life rather than live without me.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: "Well, I wasn't going to live without you."

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc2.description: I learned that the Volturi are an ancient and powerful vampire family who function like a royal authority in the vampire world.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: "The Volturi are a family," he explained, his eyes still remote. "A very old, very powerful family of our kind. They are the closest thing our world has to a royal family, I suppose. Carlisle lived with them briefly in his early years, in Italy, before he settled in America—do you remember the story?"

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc2.description: I understood that Edward's devotion to me was so strong that he considered provoking the Volturi as a possible way to end his life rather than live apart from me.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: "But I wasn't sure how to do it—I knew Emmett and Jasper would never help… so I was thinking maybe I would go to Italy and do something to provoke the Volturi."

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc2.description: I recalled that Carlisle once lived with the Volturi in Italy during his early years before settling in America.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: "Carlisle lived with them briefly in his early years, in Italy, before he settled in America—do you remember the story?"

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc3.description: I observed that Carlisle could bear the smell of my blood without suffering intense temptation.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: Though the rest of them had given up the traditional diet of vampires just as absolutely as Carlisle had, he was the only one who could bear the smell of my blood without suffering from the intense temptation.

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc3.description: I learned that Carlisle believed in some form of God and that he hoped vampires might get some measure of credit for trying to be good.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: But never, in the nearly four hundred years now since I was born, have I ever seen anything to make me doubt whether God exists in some form or the other. "It's a long shot, I'll admit," he continued in an offhand voice. "By all accounts, we're damned regardless. But I hope, maybe foolishly, that we'll get some measure of credit for trying."

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc3.description: I found myself agreeing that Carlisle's hope was not foolish and that I could imagine a heaven that would include Edward.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: "I don't think that's foolish," I mumbled. "And I don't think anyone else would, either." "Besides, the only kind of heaven I could appreciate would have to include Edward."

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc3.description: I noted that Edward shared Carlisle's belief in God and hell only partially and that this affected how I viewed Edward's spiritual stance.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: "Edward's with me up to a point. God and heaven exist… and so does hell. But he doesn't believe there is an afterlife for our kind."

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.description: I received a CD from Edward that contained his original music and I recognized my lullaby as the first track.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: "It was his music, his compositions. The first piece on the CD was my lullaby."

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward acquired a piano so he could play for me here.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: "I didn't think you would let me get a piano so I could play for you here," he explained.

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.description: I experienced pain in my injured arm under the bandage and I accepted Tylenol from Edward because the burning worsened.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: Actually, it was starting to blaze under the bandage. I wanted ice. "I'll get you some Tylenol."

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.description: I discovered that Edward frequently stayed over at my house and I knew Charlie was not aware of those visits.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: Charlie wasn't exactly aware that Edward frequently stayed over. "He won't catch me," Edward promised as he disappeared silently out the door.

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.description: I realized that Edward's restraint can falter and that he can become urgently tempted during an intimate moment.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: Suddenly his lips became much more urgent, his free hand twisted into my hair and held my face securely to his. "That was out of line."

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.description: I felt closer to Edward because of his thoughtful gifts and care, and I also felt wary because his tenderness coexists with a dangerous intensity.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: He put me down with my head on my pillow and tucked the quilt around me. Suddenly his lips became much more urgent...

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.description: I learned that Billy answered my first call and said Jacob was still in bed and had been taken to a doctor.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: The first time I called, Billy answered and told me that Jacob was still in bed.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.description: I learned from Charlie that Harry said there had been trouble with the phone lines and that Billy said Jake had mono and no visitors.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: "Harry says there's been some trouble with the phone lines, and that's why you haven't been able to get through. Billy took Jake to the doc down there, and it looks like he has mono. He's real tired, and Billy said no visitors," he reported.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.description: I began to distrust Billy's account and I admitted to myself that I didn't really believe him.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: for some reason I couldn't nail down, I didn't really believe him.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.description: I learned from online research that mono could last more than a month.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: I stopped when I got to the part about how mono could last more than a month.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.description: I felt anxious and afraid of not being allowed to see Jacob which made me nervous.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: I was afraid of not being allowed to see Jacob—that made me nervous.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.description: I decided to give Billy a week before I got pushy about visiting Jacob.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: I'd give Billy a week, I decided, before I got pushy.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: I experienced a week during which I felt certain I might not survive until Saturday because the loneliness overwhelmed me.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.source_text: A week was long. By Wednesday, I was sure I wasn't going to live till Saturday.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: I left Billy and Jacob alone for a week and I had doubted Jacob would comply with Billy's rule when I made that decision.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.source_text: When I'd decided to leave Billy and Jacob alone for a week, I hadn't really believed that Jacob would go along with Billy's rule.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: I tried calling Jacob three times and I discovered the phone lines still weren't working.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.source_text: I cheated three times by trying to call him, but the phone lines still weren't working.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: I realized I wasn't handling being alone well as isolation allowed repressed fears and dreams to resurface.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.source_text: I was in the house much too much, and much too alone. Without Jacob, and my adrenaline and my distractions, everything I'd been repressing started creeping up on me.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: I began having intense recurring dreams of being in the forest and the empty fern sea where the white house no longer existed, and I sometimes saw Sam Uley there.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.source_text: The dreams got hard again. I could no longer see the end coming. Just the horrible nothingness—half the time in the forest, half the time in the empty fern sea where the white house no longer existed. Sometimes Sam Uley was there in the forest, watching me again.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: I experienced severe physical panic described as a hole in my chest that worsened, causing me to clutch my sides and gasp for air.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.source_text: The hole in my chest was worse than ever. I'd thought that I'd been getting it under control, but I found myself hunched over, day after day, clutching my sides together and gasping for air.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: I felt intense relief and hope on Saturday because I could finally try to contact Jacob and go to La Push if necessary to end the loneliness.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.source_text: I was relieved beyond measure the morning I woke up—screaming, of course—and remembered that it was Saturday. Today I could call Jacob. And if the phone lines still weren't working, then I was going to La Push.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: I learned that Billy answered my call on the second ring.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: It caught me off guard when Billy answered on the second ring.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob is not at home right now and that he left to give friends a ride up to Port Angeles.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: "He's giving some friends a ride up to Port Angeles—I think they were going to catch a double feature or something. He's gone for the whole day."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob's illness turned out not to be mono but just some other virus.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: "Turns out it wasn't mono after all. Just some other virus."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: I realized that Jacob was better but still had not called me.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: Jacob was better, but not well enough to call me.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: I feared that Jacob had changed his mind about me and might no longer return my feelings.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: Jacob must have changed his mind, just like I'd feared. He was going to take my advice and not waste any more time on someone who couldn't return his feelings.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: I felt increasingly lonely, worried, bored, and desolate as the week apart seemed to affect Jacob less than it affected me.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: I was sitting home, missing him more every hour. I was lonely, worried, bored… perforated—and now also desolate as I realized that the week apart had not had the same effect on him.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.description: I learned that Charlie was packing food to take out to the river because the weather was nice.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.source_text: "No, I'm just packing something to take out to the river…"

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.description: I learned that Charlie offered to stay with me since Jake was out.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.source_text: "Say, did you want me to stay with you, since Jake's out?"

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.description: I learned that the rangers found a missing hiker's camp but no sign of him and that large animal prints were discovered, so traps were being set.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.source_text: "We've got a missing hiker—the rangers found his camp early this morning, but no sign of him. There were some really big animal prints… ... Anyway, they're setting traps for it now."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.description: I decided that I wasn't going to stay home and that I needed to go out rather than be watched.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.source_text: "It only took about two minutes of staring at the silent kitchen phone to decide that I wasn't staying home today."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.description: I acknowledged that I lied to Charlie about calling Jessica because I preferred to be alone rather than have him watching me.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.source_text: "I fibbed quickly. I'd rather be alone than have him watching me all day."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.description: I considered driving to La Push to get my motorcycle but I learned that I worried about who would drive me to the emergency room if I needed it.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.source_text: "I could drive to La Push and get my motorcycle—an appealing thought but for one minor problem: who was going to drive me to the emergency room if I needed it afterward?"

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.description: I felt a twinge of guilt about how Charlie would react to my leaving but I chose to ignore that guilt.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.source_text: "I felt a brief twinge of guilt as I realized how Charlie would feel about this, but I ignored it."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: I spent about fifteen minutes studying the little needle on the compass face and the markings on the now worn map before I set off into the woods.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.source_text: After I parked in the usual spot, I had to spend a good fifteen minutes studying the little needle on the compass face and the markings on the now worn map.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: I stepped through a low arch of vine maples and chest-high ferns and I entered the meadow abruptly.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.source_text: And then, with an abruptness that disoriented me, I stepped through a low arch made by two vine maples—pushing past the chest-high ferns—into the meadow.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: I observed that the clearing was perfectly round, that the stream bubbled to the east, and that the ground was thick with tall grass in the wrong season for wildflowers.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.source_text:
It was the same place, of that I was instantly sure.... To the east, I could hear the stream bubbling quietly.

The place wasn't nearly so stunning without the sunlight, but it was still very beautiful and serene. The place wasn't nearly so stunning without the sunlight, but it was still very beautiful and serene. It was the wrong season for wildflowers; the ground was thick with tall grass that swayed in the light breeze like ripples across a lake.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: I felt the forest was creepier than usual because it reminded me of my most recent nightmare and because I was alone.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.source_text: Somehow, though, even with the birds chirping and cawing, the insects buzzing noisily around my head, and the occasional scurry of the field mice through the shrubs, the forest seemed creepier today; it reminded me of my most recent nightmare.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: I experienced breathing difficulty that I attributed to the stupid hole in my chest rather than physical exertion.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.source_text: Breathing started to get more difficult—not because of exertion, but because I was having trouble with the stupid hole in my chest again.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: I noticed I was getting better at bushwhacking and I could tell I was faster.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.source_text: I was getting better at this bushwhacking thing; I could tell I was faster.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: I felt nearly instantaneous disappointment when I realized the clearing did not hold what I had been searching for and I sank down gasping.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.source_text:
It was the same place… but it didn't hold what I had been searching for.

The disappointment was nearly as instantaneous as the recognition. I sank down right where I was, kneeling there at the edge of the clearing, beginning to gasp.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: I learned that the meadow itself felt empty without him and triggered intense pain.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.source_text: There was nothing special about this place without him.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: I felt my grief fracturing me into pieces and realized I needed to be alone rather than share the moment.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.source_text: how I was fracturing into pieces, the way I had to curl into a ball to keep the empty hole from tearing me apart?

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: I recognized Laurent stepping out from the trees and experienced a brief, suppressed hope before realizing he was not the one I wanted.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.source_text: At precisely that moment, a figure stepped out from the trees to the north, some thirty paces away. "Laurent!" I cried in surprised pleasure.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.description: I learned that Laurent had been part of James's coven when we first met.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.source_text: I read that Laurent had been part of James's coven when we first met.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.description: I learned that Laurent had gone to Alaska to live with the Denali family who refused to drink human blood.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.source_text: I read that Laurent went to Alaska to live with the Denali family that refused to drink human blood.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.description: I noticed that Laurent's eyes were dark red rather than the golden color associated with the Cullens.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.source_text: I noticed that Laurent's eyes were dark red instead of golden.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.description: I felt overwhelming satisfaction and a renewed sense of connection when I saw Laurent in the meadow.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.source_text: I felt overwhelming satisfaction and a sense of connection on seeing Laurent.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.description: I realized that fear did not dominate me in that moment and that my reaction was more of release than terror.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.source_text: I realized that my response to Laurent's presence was satisfaction rather than fear.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.description: I felt that Laurent was someone I did not have to pretend for and who already knew things I could not say.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.source_text: I sensed that Laurent was someone I did not have to pretend for and who already knew what I could not say.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.description: I understood that the Cullen house appeared vacant and that the Cullens had apparently moved on, leaving the place empty at least for a time.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.source_text: I understood that the Cullen place seemed empty and that they had moved on.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.description: I admitted to myself that I lied about how often the Cullens visited and that I tried to avoid mentioning Laurent to Edward because of his temper.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.source_text: I acknowledged that I lied about the Cullens' visits and avoided telling Edward because of his temper.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.description: I recognized through a remembered voice that I was in significant danger and that Laurent's nearness was threatening.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.source_text: I remembered a voice warning that I was in danger and that Laurent posed a threat.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc8.description: I learned that Laurent admitted he likes Tanya and her sister Irina and enjoys staying with them.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc8.source_text: "I like Tanya very much," he mused. "And her sister Irina even more…"

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc8.description: I learned that Laurent confessed to breaking the coven's restrictions sometimes.
I learned that Laurent said he came to the area as a favor to Victoria and was aware of her plans.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc8.source_text: "I actually came here as a favor to her."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc8.description: I learned that Victoria wanted Laurent to kill me as revenge for James's death.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc8.source_text: "She thought it more appropriate to kill you than Edward—fair turnabout, mate for mate."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc8.description: I felt my belief in Edward's protection weaken when Laurent suggested Edward left me here unprotected.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc8.source_text: "apparently it wouldn't be the revenge she imagined, since you must not mean very much to him if he left you here unprotected."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc8.description: I learned that Laurent was hunting, felt thirsty, and found my scent extremely tempting.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc8.source_text: "I'm quite thirsty, and you do smell… simply mouthwatering."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc9.description: I heard a beautiful delusion command me to threaten Laurent.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc9.source_text: "Threaten him," the beautiful delusion ordered, his voice distorted with dread.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc9.description: I pleaded aloud with a frightened "Please" while confronting Laurent.
I realized I loved Edward as his name burst through all the walls I'd built to contain it.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc9.source_text: Edward, Edward, Edward. I was going to die. It shouldn't matter if I thought of him now. Edward, I love you.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc9.description: I feared I was going to die as Laurent closed in and I accepted the immediacy of the threat.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc9.source_text: I was going to die. It shouldn't matter if I thought of him now.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.description: I learned that a huge black wolf and at least two other giant wolves emerged from the trees and approached the meadow.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.source_text: A huge black shape eased out of the trees, quiet as a shadow, and stalked deliberately toward the vampire.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.description: I learned that Laurent backed away in fear and then ran into the trees when the wolves attacked.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.source_text: Laurent was backing toward the edge of the trees... without warning, he spun and disappeared into the trees. He ran away.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.description: I changed my belief that wild animals were minor threats and decided that these wolves could be more dangerous and terrifying than I had imagined.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.source_text: Why was Laurent retreating? Granted, the wolf was monstrous in size, but it was just an animal.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.description: I felt grateful that Jacob was not present and relieved that he would not die here.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.source_text: At least Jacob wasn't going to die, too. At least I wouldn't have his death on my hands.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc11.description: I learned that I ran headlong into the trees and later had to set my compass on the muddy ground to read it.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc11.source_text: I turned and ran headlong into the trees.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc11.description: I changed my belief that vampires would not run from wolves after seeing one flee.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc11.source_text: A vampire should not have run from overgrown dogs like that.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc11.description: I changed my belief about wolf behavior because I could not understand why they would pursue Laurent instead of a warmblooded, weak human like me.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc11.source_text: And the wolves should have given Laurent a wide berth.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc11.description: I learned that I was physically overcome with panic and shaking, collapsing onto my hands with sobs.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc11.source_text: My knees buckled under me, and I fell onto my hands, sobs building in my throat.
