tw-book2-chapter10_Sc11.description: I became wary of Laurent and wondered if he would turn on the wolves or come looking for me.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc11.source_text: How long would the wolves chase Laurent before they doubled back for me? Or would Laurent turn on them? Would he be the one that came looking?

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc12.description: I saw five wolves including a big black one, and gray, and reddish-brown.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc12.source_text: I saw the bear." I tried to say it calmly, but my voice was high and shaky. "It's not a bear, though—it's some kind of wolf. And there are five of them. A big black one, and gray, and reddish-brown…

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc12.description: I noticed the wolves didn't pay any attention to me and then I ran away and fell down a lot.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc12.source_text: They didn't pay any attention to me. But aftet they were gone, I ran away and I fell down a lot.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc12.description: I learned that the rangers said the tracks were wrong for a bear and that my father expressed disbelief that wolves could get that big.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc12.source_text: The rangers said the tracks were wrong for a bear—but wolves just don't get that big…

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc12.description: I felt too shaken to pretend that I'd spent an uneventful day and I promised I would not go into the forest again.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc12.source_text: I was too shaken to pretend that I'd spent an uneventful day. "Don't worry, I won't do it again."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc12.description: I fudged the location of where I saw the wolves so my dad would not know how deep I'd gone and so others would not wander near where I feared Laurent might be searching.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc12.source_text: I fudged a little bit about where exactly I'd seen the wolves—claiming I'd been on the trail that led to the north. I didn't want my dad to know how deep I'd gone into the forest against his wishes, and, more importantly, I didn't want anyone wandering near where Laurent might be searching for me.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc12.description: I heard my father forbid further hiking when he said "No more hiking."
I knew that my father called the station to report what I had seen.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc12.source_text: Charlie called the station to report what I'd seen.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.description: I learned that there was nothing I could do and no place I could hide from the danger closing in on me.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.source_text: There was nothing I could do. There were no precautions I could take. There was no place I could hide. There was no one who could help me.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.description: I realized that my scent would lead them to my home whether I was there or not and that Charlie would be endangered by my presence.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.source_text: My scent would lead them here, whether I was here or not.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.description: I became convinced that my good vampires were never coming back and that I could not rely on their protection.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.source_text: My good vampires were never coming back; how soothing it was to imagine that the other kind could also disappear.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.description: I began to find comfort in the impossible fantasy that the wolves could catch and massacre Laurent to prevent Victoria from learning my location.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.source_text: To calm myself, I fantasized the impossible: I imagined the big wolves catching up to Laurent in the woods and massacring the indestructible immortal the way they would any normal person.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.description: I learned that I was waking terrified each morning and needed to verify that Charlie had survived the night.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: EACH TIME THAT I OPENED MY EYES TO THE MORNING light and realized I'd lived through another night was a surprise to me. After the surprise wore off, my heart would start to race and my palms would sweat; I couldn't really breathe again until I'd gotten up and ascertained that Charlie had survived as well.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob had not called for a week and that his continued absence was worrying me.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: The terror that was always foremost in my thoughts usually distracted me from the fact that another week had passed, and Jacob still hadn't called me.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.description: I realized that Sam Uley had gotten to Jacob and that Jacob had been pulled into Sam's cult or gang.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: It was Sam Uley. Even my nightmares had been trying to tell me that. Sam had gotten to Jacob.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.description: I recognized that I missed Jacob horribly and craved his laugh, grin, and comforting presence.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: I missed him horribly. It had been bad enough to be alone before I was scared silly. Now, more than ever, I yearned for his carefree laugh and his infectious grin. I needed the safe sanity of his homemade garage and his warm hand around my cold fingers.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.description: I decided that it was safer for Jacob to avoid me even though that hurt me deeply.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: As much as it hurt me, I knew it was better for Jacob that he was avoiding me. Safer for him.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.description: I contacted Charlie to report my fears about Jacob and I observed that Charlie took my concern seriously in his professional voice.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: Charlie answered the phone it the station himself. "Chief Swan." "Dad, it's Bella." "What's wrong?'" "What kind of stuff?" He used his professional, police business voice. That was good; he was taking me seriously.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.description: I noted that no vampires had come for me in a week, which suggested to me that I was not their current priority.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: It had been a week, and no vampires had come for me yet. A week was more than enough time for them to have returned, so I must not be a priority.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.description: I resolved that rescuing Jacob from Sam's influence was worth the danger of traveling to La Push despite the risks.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: This was no idle visit to see what was going on. I knew what was going on. This was a rescue mission. I was going to talk to Jacob—kidnap him if I had to.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc2.description: I learned that Quil saw Jacob with Embry and that they disappeared into the trees.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: "From a distance," he finally said. "I tried to follow them—he was with Embry."

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc2.description: I learned that Quil suspected Sam and his crew might have been with Jacob and Embry.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: "I think Sam and his crew might have been with them."

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc2.description: I learned that I waited in my truck outside Jacob's house and that Billy watched me from a window.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: A movement flashed in my peripheral vision—I turned and spotted Billy looking at me through the front window with a confused expression.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc2.description: I began to see the gatherings and changes described by others as a cult.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: That was the second time I'd heard it described as a cult.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc2.description: I became afraid for Jacob and I worried that he was turning away from his previous friends and toward Sam's influence.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.description: I felt betrayed by Jacob when I believed we were friends and then heard him blame the Cullens.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: My jaw tightened, and I spoke through my teeth. "I thought we were friends."

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob blames the Cullens for the damage he feels and frames them as the cause of current problems.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: "If you want to blame someone, why don't you point your finger at those filthy, reeking bloodsuckers that you love so much?"

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.description: I recognized that my relationship with Jacob had become strained and that he recoiled from my touch.
I discovered that Quil and other friends were frightened for Jacob and possibly for themselves.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: "I ran into Quil today," I yelled after him. "You remember your friend, Quil? Yeah, he's terrified."

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.description: I noticed that Jacob exhibited physical signs of extreme agitation including shaking hands, deep breaths, and violent outburst against a tree.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: "He was so mad that his hands were shaking." "His fist slammed against the tree. ... the trunk gave way and snapped off loudly under his blows."

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.description: I learned that Charlie called and told others that I was on my way home.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "Charlie just called, Bella. I told him you were on your way home."

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.description: I learned that Sam Uley said Jacob could not be my friend anymore as conveyed through Jacob.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "Sam Uley says Jacob can't be my friend anymore."

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.description: I realized that Jacob had not been healing my pain but had been creating his own wound that left me riddled and hurting.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "I'd thought Jake had been healing the hole in me—or at least plugging it up, keeping it from hurting me so much. I'd been wrong. He'd just been carving out his own hole, so that I was now riddled through like Swiss cheese."

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.description: I felt that Charlie was firmly on my side and I felt supported by his anger toward those blaming me.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "At least Charlie was on my side now."

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.description: I admitted to myself that I still sought comfort in the memory of Edward's voice and I used that memory to soothe my tears.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "I pulled out the memory—nor a real memory that would hurt too much, but the false memory of Edward's voice in my mind this afternoon—and played it over and over in my head until I fell asleep with the tears still streaming calmly down my empty face."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.description: I saw a huge dark shape wobble erratically on the other side of the glass and lurch toward me.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: A huge, dark shape wobbled erratically on the other side of the glass, lurching toward me like it was going to smash right through.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob said he was trying to keep his promise as he balanced in the spruce.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: "I'm trying to keep"—he huffed, shifting his weight as the treetop bounced him—"my promise!"

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.description: I saw Jacob swing agilely into my room and land on the balls of his feet with a low thud.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: To my shock, he swung agilely into my room, landing on the balls of his feet with a low thud.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.description: I felt Jacob's noisy arrival reminded me of Edward and that the reminder picked viciously at my unhealed wounds.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: Worse than that, even though his arrival had been noisy and awkward, it reminded me of when Edward used to sneak in through my window, and the reminder picked viciously at the unhealed wounds.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.description: I became so brutally tired that I thought I might collapse right there on the floor.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: I was so brutally tired that I thought I might collapse right there on the floor.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob had previously told the story that revealed Edward's vampiric nature.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: Without realizing what he was doing, Jacob had told me exactly what I needed to know that day—that Edward was a vampire.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc2.description: I recognized that I had a secret I felt bound to protect and that it was not mine to tell.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: So, I couldn't argue with that. He was exactly right—I had a secret that wasn't mine to tell, yet a secret I felt bound to protect.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc2.description: I felt my relationship with Jacob grow more complicated as he apologized, pressed me for answers, and showed both anger and intimacy.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: "I'm so sorry, Bella." "He took my face in his enormous, too-warm hands and held it just a few inches from his. He stared into my eyes while he whispered, as if to communicate something besides the words he spoke."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.description: I learned that the dream I experienced was the same dream I had the night after I walked with Jacob on the beach, the night I first knew Edward was a vampire.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: This was the dream I'd had the night after I'd walked with Jacob on the beach, the first night I knew that Edward was a vampire.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.description: I learned that the forest in this dream smelled like the ocean and that I could not see the sky but I sensed sunlight through bright jade leaves.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: It smelled, not like the damp earth of the woods, but like the brine of the ocean. I couldn't see the sky; still, it seemed like the sun must be shining—the leaves above were bright jade green.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.description: I became convinced that my dreams can shift memories from other times and that they can bring up vivid, frightening scenes I thought were buried.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: The abrupt wave of deja vu was so strong it nearly woke me up. I knew why I recognized this place now. It was because I'd been here before, in another dream.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.description: I felt my connection to Jacob complicated because I experienced him as both a frightened boy grabbing my hand and as a gigantic wolf trying to warn me.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: "Jacob, what's wrong?" I asked. "Run, Bella, you have to run!" he whispered, terrified. In his place was an enormous, red-brown wolf with dark, intelligent eyes.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: I learned from Jacob that Quileute oral history includes legends about the Flood, a wolf ancestry, and the existence of "cold ones."
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.source_text: "Do you know any of our old stories, about where we came from—the Quileutes, I mean?" "Well, there are lots of legends, some of them claiming to date back to the Flood—supposedly, the ancient Quileutes tied their canoes to the tops of the tallest trees on the mountain to survive, like Noah and the ark." "Another legend claims that we descended from wolves—and that the wolves are our brothers still. It's against tribal law to kill them." "Then there are the stories about the cold ones."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob said his great-grandfather made a treaty that kept the cold ones off Quileute land.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.source_text: "According to legend, my own great-grandfather knew some of them. He was the one who made the treaty that kept them off our land."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: I learned that the cold ones are described as natural enemies of the wolves that turn into men, i.e., werewolves.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.source_text: "The cold ones are the natural enemies of the wolf—well, not the wolf really, but the wolves that turn into men, like our ancestors. You would call them werewolves."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: I realized that Jacob had been warning about werewolves and that my prior observations of strange tracks and missing hikers might connect to them.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.source_text: "There've been another attack—the wolves again. It was real close to the resort by the hot springs—there's a witness this time. The victim was only a dozen yards from the road when he disappeared. His wife saw a huge gray wolf just a few minutes later, while she was searching for him, and ran for help."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: I felt my sense of reality change because learning about werewolves added to the supernatural truth I already accepted about vampires.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.source_text: "Hadn't I already accepted the existence of vampires long ago—and without all the hysterics that time?" "Exactly, I wanted to scream back at the voice. Wasn't one myth enough for anyone, enough for a lifetime?"

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: I discovered that Jacob, my friend and the person I related to most, was not fully human and that realization altered how I saw him.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.source_text: "But Jacob? Jacob, who was just Jacob, and nothing more than that? Jacob, my friend? Jacob, the only human I'd ever been able to relate to… And he wasn't even human."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: I learned from Charlie that the rangers were going out armed with volunteers and that hunters were being incentivized with a reward for wolf carcasses.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.source_text: "The rangers are going out armed, taking armed volunteers. There're a lot of hunters who are eager to be involved—there's a reward being offered for wolf carcasses."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob and half the men in town were out in the woods with guns, hunting giant wolves.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc5.source_text: He and half the other men in town are all out in the woods with guns, hunting giant wolves.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc5.description: I decided I couldn't condone what Jacob and his pack were doing and felt that overlooking it would make me a monster.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc5.source_text: I couldn't condone what Jacob and his friends, his pack, were doing. ... That would make me a monster, too.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc5.description: I resolved to tell Jacob to his face because I felt I owed him a face-to-face conversation rather than calling and being cowardly about it.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc5.source_text: I owed him a face-to-face conversation, at least. I could have called him as he'd suggested, but that felt cowardly.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc5.description: I felt my revulsion dissolve into pity and experienced an overpowering, illogical urge to protect Jacob after seeing him asleep and vulnerable.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc5.source_text: Seeing Jacob like that—innocent and vulnerable in sleep—had stolen all my revulsion, dissolved all my anger. ... When I pictured him sleeping so peacefully, I felt an overpowering urge to protect him.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob and his group call themselves protectors and claim to try to keep people safe in the woods.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc6.source_text: We're trying to do our job, Bella. We're trying to protect them, but we're always just a little too late.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc6.description: I changed my belief and realized that Jacob's physical transformation does not make me love him less, but his potential to hurt people is what upsets me.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc6.source_text: I really didn't care if he turned into a big wolf—he was still Jacob.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc6.description: I accepted Jacob's apology and embraced him, which strengthened our trust and repaired the tension between us.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc6.source_text: I threw my arms around him.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.description: I learned that Victoria is hunting me and has been killing strangers in the woods.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.source_text: "Victoria was here. Looking for me. Killing strangers in the woods."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.description: I learned that Laurent died about a week ago and that someone else is killing people now.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.source_text: "'Laurent is dead,' I gasped, and my entire body went ice cold." and "If Laurent died… a week ago… then someone else is killing people now."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.description: I realized that I am still human and that the Cullens left partly because of the danger around me.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.source_text: "I'm nothing but a human, after all. Nothing special," I explained, shrugging weakly.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.description: I feel that Jacob is protective of me and willing to mobilize his pack to keep me and my family safe.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.source_text: "We're going to take care of this. And we're keeping a special eye on Charlie and the others—we won't let anything happen to him. Trust me on that." and "This is exactly what we needed to know. We've got to tell the others right away."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.description: I learned that Sam is the Alpha and that his commands can prevent pack members from bringing guests or sharing information.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.source_text: I was afraid Sam would tell me I couldn't bring you.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.description: I felt my hostility toward Sam decrease when I understood that he had been alone and had no help during his change.
I acknowledged that I wanted Victoria stopped while also insisting that I did not want Jacob to be the one to confront her.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.source_text: I did want Victoria to be stopped, preferably before she tortured me to death or ran into Charlie or killed another stranger. I just didn't want Jacob to be the one to stop her, or rather to try.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.description: I recognized that Edward's abilities as a mind-reading vampire complicate matters and that I avoid saying or hearing his name because of the pain associated with him.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.source_text: "Like the stuff about the mind-reading bloodsucker," and "He? Oh, you mean Edward—oops, sorry. I forgot. You don't like to say his name. Or hear it."

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc1.description: I learned that Charlie and half the other men in town were out in the woods with guns hunting giant wolves.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: He and half the other men in town are all out in the woods with guns, hunting giant wolves.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob had been out late a lot recently and that he probably needed rest.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: He's out late a lot these days. Kid needs his rest—probably you shouldn't wake him.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc1.description: I felt my revulsion dissolve and I could not condemn Jacob after seeing him innocent and vulnerable in sleep.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: Seeing Jacob like that—innocent and vulnerable in sleep—had stolen all my revulsion, dissolved all my anger.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc1.description: I decided that Jacob was still my friend whether he killed people or not and I could not simply walk away.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: Jacob was my friend whether he killed people or not.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc1.description: I realized that I had to try to protect him even though that position was illogical.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: But I couldn't not warn him, either. I had to do what I could to protect him.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.description: I felt relieved to learn that Laurent is dead and no longer a threat to me or Charlie.
I learned that Jacob and his pack killed Laurent in the meadow to protect me.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.source_text: "You… killed… Laurent?" He nodded. "Well, it was a group effort," he qualified.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob's pack defines themselves as protectors whose purpose is to defend humans from one enemy.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.source_text: "Protectors?" "Exactly." "We're trying to do our job, Bella. We're trying to protect them... We only protect people from one thing—our one enemy. It's the reason we exist—because they do."

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.description: I apologized to Jacob and embraced him, which repaired tension and expressed forgiveness.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.source_text: "Sorry I called you a hypocrite," he apologized. "Sorry I called you a murderer." I threw my arms around him.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob can become a wolf without needing a full moon and that his anger could make transformation dangerous for me.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.source_text: "I'd turn into a wolf," he whispered back. "You don't need a full moon." "Hollywood's version doesn't get much right."

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.description: I learned that when werewolves are wolves they can hear each other's thoughts no matter the distance.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.source_text: Not hear sounds," he went on, "but we can hear… thoughts—each other's anyway—no matter how far away from each other we are.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob claimed werewolves were made to kill vampires.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.source_text: But Jake said this was what werewolves were made for…

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.description: I learned that Sam is the head of the pack and has authority to forbid Jacob from telling me things.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.source_text: Sam told me I couldn't tell you. He's… the head of the pack, you know. He's the Alpha.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.description: I became less confident in the idea that anyone was truly safe and I doubted that the werewolves could guarantee Charlie's safety.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.source_text: How could I trust that? None of us were safe! Jacob the very least of all, if he was trying to put himself between Victoria and Charlie… between Victoria and me.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.description: I felt that Jacob was protective toward me and promised to take care of me and my father.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.source_text: "Don't be. We'll take care of you—and Charlie, too. I promise."

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: I got out of the truck and stood close beside Jacob.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: I got out of the truck, hurrying around the front end to stand close beside Jacob.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: I remembered the giant monsters in the meadow.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: I remembered only too clearly the giant monsters in the meadow.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: My hands were trembling with fear.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: My hands were trembling like Jacob's had been before, but with fear rather than rage.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: I realized that my fear was intense and immediate in the moment.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: My hands were trembling like Jacob's had been before, but with fear rather than rage.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: I felt supported when Jacob took and squeezed my hand.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: Jake took my hand and squeezed it.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc1.description: I learned that werewolves can violently transform from human boys into massive wolves in an instant.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc1.source_text:
Halfway to the ground, there was a loud ripping noise, and the boy exploded.
Dark silver fur blew out from the boy, coalescing into a shape more than five-times his size—a massive, crouched shape, ready to spring.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc1.description: I changed my expectation that the werewolves would appear as wolves rather than as large, half-naked boys.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: I'd gotten the image of the wolves stuck in my head. These were just four really big half-naked boys.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc1.description: I felt protected by Jacob when he put himself between me and the other boys and charged the attacking wolf.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: Jacob took a step to put himself in front of me.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.description: I learned that Victoria is targeting me because the Cullens killed her mate last year.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: The Cullens got her mate last year, and she's after Bella now.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.description: I learned that the pack plans to split into inner and outer perimeters and collapse in to trap Victoria.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: Paul, Jared, and Embry will take the outer perimeter, and Jacob and I will take the inner. We'll collapse in when we've got her trapped.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.description: I was advised that it would be best if I spent as much time as possible in La Push to make it harder for Victoria to find me.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: Jacob thinks it would be best if you spent as much time as possible here in La Push. She won't know where to find you so easily, just in case.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.description: I realized that the pack was more domestic and protective than I had expected.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: All in all, it wasn't exactly what I'd been expecting from a pack of werewolves.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.description: I decided that I did not want to move Renee or anyone else into danger by drawing Victoria away from Forks.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: I don't want to lead Victoria anywhere else," I whispered.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.description: I felt Emily's fierce concern and recognized her as family-like during the meal.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: Her expression clearly stated that this was her family.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.description: I was often alone in La Push for safety because Jacob had a horrible, dangerous job he felt compelled to do.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: But Jacob had a horrible, dangerous job he felt compelled to do, and so I was often alone, stuck in La Push for safety, with nothing to do to keep my mind off any of my worries.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.description: I studied for an upcoming Calculus test but found that I could only look at math for so long.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: I did some studying for another Calculus test that was coming up next week, but I could only look at math for so long.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.description: I felt awkward taking up space at Billy's and felt pressure to make conversation when I had nothing to do.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: I felt awkward, always taking up space at Billy's. I did some studying for another Calculus test that was coming up next week, but I could only look at math for so long. When I didn't have something obvious to do in my hands, I felt like I ought to be making conversation with Billy—the pressure of normal societal rules.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.description: I realized that alone time worsened my fixation on the Cullens and could make me physically unable to breathe.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: Alone time wasn't good for me. Thanks to the new honesty with Jacob, I'd been talking and thinking about the Cullens way too much. ... Eventually, I couldn't even walk anymore, because I couldn't breathe. I sat down on a patch of semidry rocks and curled up in a ball.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.description: I recognized that Jacob's physical presence comforted me and that his warmth helped me breathe again.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: Jacob found me like that, and I could tell from his expression that he understood. 'Sorry,' he said right away. He pulled me up from the ground and wrapped both arms around my shoulders. I hadn't realized that I was cold until then. His warmth made me shudder, but at least I could breathe with him there.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.description: I thought that jumping off a cliff with Jacob would help me stop craving Edward's voice and delusions.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: But it had been days since I'd heard Edward's voice. That was probably part of the problem. I was addicted to the sound of my delusions. ... Jumping off a cliff was certain to remedy that situation.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.description: I learned that it was spring break in Forks again.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: IT WAS SPRING BREAK IN FORKS AGAIN.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.description: I remembered that last spring break I had been hunted by a vampire.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: Last spring break, I'd been hunted by a vampire, too.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.description: I spent Sunday mostly on the beach while Charlie hung out with Billy at the Blacks' house.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: I'd spent Sunday mostly on the beach, while Charlie hung out with Billy at the Blacks' house.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.description: I noticed that when we walked along the beach Jacob always held my hand.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: When we walked along the beach now, he always held my hand.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.description: I decided I shouldn't let outside assumptions bother me about how Jake and I really were.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: As long as Jake and I knew how it really was, I shouldn't let those kinds of assumptions bother me.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc2.description: I learned that I worked Tuesday afternoon and that Jacob followed me on his bike to make sure I arrived safely.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: I worked Tuesday afternoon—Jacob followed me on his bike to make sure I arrived safely—and Mike noticed.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc2.description: I learned that Mike noticed Jacob's presence and asked if I was dating him.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: "Are you dating that kid from La Push? The sophomore?" He Asked, poorly disguising the resentment in his tone.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc2.description: I stated that Jacob is my best friend and that I spend most of my time with him.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: "Not in the technical sense of the word. I do spent most of my time with Jacob, though. He's my best friend."

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc2.description: I learned that Mike believed Jacob was head over heels for me.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: Mike's eyes narrowed shrewdly. "Don't kid yourself, Bella. The guy's head over heels for you."

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc2.description: I admitted that I knew Jacob had strong feelings and that I felt life was complicated.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob had a dangerous job that often left me alone and stuck in La Push for safety.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: But Jacob had a horrible, dangerous job he felt compelled to do, and so I was often alone, stuck in La Push for safety, with nothing to do to keep my mind off any of my worries.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.description: I discovered that I attempted to study by preparing for another Calculus test during my downtime.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: I did some studying for another Calculus test that was coming up next week, but I could only look at math for so long.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.description: I became aware that I was addicted to the sound of my delusions and that the absence of Edward's voice worsened things.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: That was probably part of the problem. I was addicted to the sound of my delusions. It made things worse if I went too long without them.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.description: I felt overwhelmed by the concentrated aura of love and contentment at Emily's and realized I couldn't handle it for long.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: The aura of love and contentment that surrounded them was harder to take in concentrated doses, with no one else around to dilute it.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.description: I recognized that I was getting in deeper and deeper with Jacob without having consciously decided to progress our relationship.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: I was getting in deeper and deeper with Jacob without ever having consciously decided to progress in that direction and I didn't know what to do about it—

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.description: I experienced Jacob finding me collapsed, pulling me up, and wrapping his arms around my shoulders which helped me breathe.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: Jacob found me like that, and I could tell from his expression that he understood. "Sorry," he said right away. He pulled me up from the ground and wrapped both arms around my shoulders. I hadn't realized that I was cold until then. His warmth made me shudder, but at least I could breathe with him there.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc6.description: I flung myself off the cliff and experienced exhilaration and cold as I entered the water.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc6.source_text: And I flung myself off the cliff. I screamed as I dropped through the open air like a meteor, but it was a scream of exhilaration and not fear. Yes! The word echoed through my head as I sliced through the surface of the water. It was icy, colder than I'd feared, and yet the chill only added to the high.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc6.description: I realized that I felt exhilaration instead of terror when I jumped.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc6.source_text: I screamed as I dropped through the open air like a meteor, but it was a scream of exhilaration and not fear.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc6.description: I defied Edward's pleading voice because I wanted to be human and to prove that to him.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc6.source_text: You wanted me to be human, I reminded him. Well, watch me. "Don't do this," he pleaded.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc7.description: I knew that the correct way to escape a riptide is to swim parallel to the beach rather than trying to swim directly toward the shore.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc7.source_text: I knew the right way to avoid a riptide: swim parallel to the beach rather than struggling for the shore.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc7.description: I discovered that I could not tell which way the surface or shore was because the water was black and featureless, removing any visual cue for orientation.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc7.source_text: I couldn't even tell which way the surface.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc7.description: I became resigned and almost happy about dying, finding the prospect of death oddly peaceful and making the whole experience bearable.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc7.source_text: I was almost happy that it was over. This was an easier death than others I'd faced. Oddly peaceful.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc7.description: I realized that my final conscious thought was a direct, loving farewell to Edward: goodbye and I love you.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc7.source_text: Goodbye, I love you, was my last thought.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.description: I learned that I was alive and breathing despite shattered airways and severe cold after the fall.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.source_text: The quiet whooshing inside my ears was not the waves—it was the air moving in and out of my lungs again. Each breath burned—the passageways were as raw as if I'd scrubbed them out with steel wool. But I was breathing.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob found me quickly and carried me out of the surf without apparent effort.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.source_text: He slid his arms under me and lifted me without effort—like picking up an empty box.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.description: I began to feel profound guilt and self-reproach for risking my life and adding worry to others during an emergency.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.source_text: Abruptly, I felt really sick with guilt—felt truly horrible about the brainless cliff dive.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.description: I realized that I depend on Jacob's presence and protection more than I had acknowledged after he searched for and rescued me.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.source_text: I was searching for you," he told me. "I followed the tire tracks to your truck, and then I heard you scream…

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.description: I was left on a short couch at Jacob's house, given dry clothes, and told I could stay there.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: "You can stay here," Jacob said as he dumped me on the short couch. "I mean it—right here I'll get you some dry clothes."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.description: I felt warm and almost dry next to the radiator while my throat and lungs burned with every breath.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: "Billy's sofa was right next to the radiator, and I was warm now, despite my soaked clothes." "The inside of my throat burned with every breath I took."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.description: I fell asleep quickly to Jacob's soft snoring and had a normal, wandering dream made of vivid memories.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: Jacob began softly snoring, and the sound of it soothed like a lullaby. I fell asleep quickly.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.description: I realized that Harry's heart attack forced perspective on me and I admitted I might have to change my reckless ways.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: Harry's heart attack had pushed everything suddenly into perspective for me. Perspective that I didn't want to see, because—if I admitted to the truth of it—it would mean that I would have to change my ways.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.description: I felt that Jacob's presence and warmth were comforting and I thought I could maybe give up dangerous habits if I had his support.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: Jacob's slow, deep breathing was the only sound in the room—like a lullaby hummed to a child, like the whisper of a rocking chair, like the ticking of an old clock when you had nowhere you needed to go…It was the sound of comfort. "But maybe I should do it. And maybe I could. If I had Jacob."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.description: I remained emotionally attached to Edward, lingering on his face in my thoughts even as I tried to think of other things.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: Edward's face… I lingered there for a long time.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.description: I learned that Charlie was still at the hospital with Sue and that there were arrangements to be made.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: "Your dad is still at the hospital with Sue. There are a lot of… arrangements to be made."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.description: I learned that Billy was deeply grief-stricken and that Sam's usual composure had broken.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: "He nodded slowly, his expression hard with grief." "Sam was right behind Billy, pushing his chair through the door. His normal composure was absent from his agonized face."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob and his pack were still hunting the vampire and that Jacob was not going home because they hadn't caught it.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: "I'm not going home. We still haven't caught the bloodsucker, remember?"

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.description: I felt like a peeping tom and I became aware that I was intruding on a private sorrow that felt foreign to me.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: "I felt like a peeping torn, peering through the cracks at a private sorrow that wasn't mine."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.description: I felt physically unwell and I realized I didn't look or feel so good in that moment.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: "I don't feel so good, either, I guess."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.description: I felt Jacob's protectiveness and closeness as he helped me up, kept his arm around my shoulder, and pulled me next to his side.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: "He helped me up from the couch without speaking, keeping his arm around my shoulder when the cold air outside made me shiver. He took the driver's seat without asking, and then pulled me next to his side to keep his arm tight around me. I leaned my head against his chest."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.description: I noticed that my mind was alert and working very hard and very fast.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: I read: "My mind was alert, and it was working very hard and very fast."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.description: I realized that my desire for Jacob was not brotherly but a need to stake a claim on him.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: I recalled: "I remembered wishing that Jacob were my brother. I realized now that all I really wanted was a claim on him."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.description: I concluded that Jacob had become essential to my survival and that his presence was a safe harbor for me.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: I noted: "Somehow, he'd become essential to my survival... Jacob was a safe harbor."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.description: I accepted that I would have to tell Jacob everything about my brokenness and the voices and I believed he would take me in spite of it all.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: I read: "I'd have to tell him everything... But, even as I recognized that necessity, I knew he would take me in spite of it all."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob can detect vampires by scent.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.source_text: "Vampire," he spit out. "Because I can smell it. Dammit!"

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.description: I recognized a parked black Mercedes S55 AMG as Carlisle's car and knew details about it.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.source_text: It was a black car... It was a Mercedes S55 AMG. I knew the horsepower and the color of the interior. I knew the feel of the powerful engine purring through the frame. I knew the rich smell of the leather seats and the way the extra-dark tint made noon look like dusk through those windows.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.description: I realized that the Cullens were present because of Carlisle's car.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.source_text: "It's Carlisle's car." "It's the Cullens. I know it."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.description: I became dizzy and frightened when Jacob announced the vampire and I felt the blood rush from my head.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.source_text: The blood rushed from my head and left me dizzy.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.description: I trusted Jacob to prioritize my safety and get me out immediately.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.source_text: "Phase or get her out of here?" he hissed at himself. "Right. Get you out."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc7.description: I learned that the black car outside belonged to Carlisle.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc7.source_text: It was just Carlisle, I told myself.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc7.description: I learned that the doorknob twisted easily when I tried to unlock it.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc7.source_text: When I grabbed the doorknob to unlock it, it twisted easily under my hand.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc7.description: I learned that Victoria had been in the harbor with me and Jacob.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc7.source_text: She'd been right there. Right there in the harbor with me and Jacob.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc7.description: I decided to go back into my house despite knowing a vampire might be inside.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc7.source_text: "Of course," I said, my voice blank with surprise at his question. Of course I wanted to go back.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc7.description: I felt remorse for how I had pushed Jacob and noticed the spasm of betrayal in his eyes.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc7.source_text: Just before he had the mask in place, I caught the spasm of betrayal that flashed in his eyes.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc1.description: I learned that Alice appeared unnaturally still and white with large black eyes which immediately drew my full attention.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: UNNATURALLY STILL AND WHITE, WITH LARGE BLACK EYES intent on my face, my visitor waited perfectly motionless in the center of the halt, beautiful beyond imagining.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc1.description: I learned that Alice's body felt hard and cool, like cement or a contoured stone when I slammed into her.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: I'd forgotten how hard she was; it was like running headlong into a wall of cement.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc1.description: I felt overwhelming relief and happiness at Alice's arrival and I sobbed because I was so happy to see her.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: "I'm just… so happy… to see you!"

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc1.description: I realized that Alice was thirsty and that I smelled appetizing to her in that moment.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: She was thirsty. And I smelled appetizing.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc1.description: I recognized that Alice both comforted me physically by pulling me into her lap and rubbing my back and also offered mild disapproval about my exuberance.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: Alice dragged me to the living room couch and pulled me into her lap. She rubbed my back in a gentle rhythm, waiting for me to get control of myself. "I'd forgotten how exuberant you are," she said, and her tone was disapproving.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc1.description: I was confronted with Alice's direct question demanding an explanation for how I was alive, which indicated surprise or concern about my survival.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: Speaking of which, would you like to explain to me how you're alive?

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc2.description: I learned that Alice believed she had seen me jump off a cliff into the water.
I clarified that I was not committing suicide and that my fall had been recreational cliff diving.
I admitted that I had seen some of Jacob's friends cliff diving and that I hadn't considered the storm's effect on the currents.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: "I'd seen some of Jacob's friends cliff diving," ... "I didn't think about how the storm would affect the currents."

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob jumped in after me and pulled me out when I was drowning.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: It's true that I probably would have drowned if Jacob hadn't jumped in after me. Well, okay, there's no probably about it. But he did, and he pulled me out, and I guess he towed me back to shore, though I was kind of out for that part.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob grabbed me within about a minute of my submersion and towed me to shore.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: It couldn't have been more than a minute that I was under before he grabbed me.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob is 'sort of a werewolf' and that the Quileute tribe turns into wolves when vampires are around.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: "See, well, he's… sort of a werewolf," I admitted in a rush. "The Quileutes turn into wolves when there are vampires around."

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: I felt uncertain about Jacob's place in my life when I called him sort of my best friend and then added that he was, implying a possible change.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: "Jacob Black. He's… sort of my best friend, I guess. At least, he was…"

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: I decided to tell Alice about Jacob because I reasoned that Jacob knew everything and I might as well include Alice in that knowledge.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: Jacob knew everything, why not Alice, too?

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.description: I learned that Bella's best friend is a werewolf.
I learned that Bella reports Jacob has been a werewolf for only a few weeks.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: 'He's only been a werewolf for just a few weeks.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.description: I remembered Bella recalling a fight between Paul and Jacob in the road.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: wincing as I remembered Paul and Jacob fighting in the road.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.description: I understood that Bella relies on Jacob and his friends to protect her from vampires.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: 'If it weren't for Jake and his friends, Laurent would have gotten me before she could, I guess, so—'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.description: I realized that Bella believes not all vampires left Forks and that the werewolves are necessary to keep her safe.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: 'No, Alice, the vampires didn't really leave—not all of them, anyway. That's the whole trouble.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc5.description: I noticed Alice looked dangerous when I described the strange flame on the water.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc5.source_text: It was strange to see her look so… so dangerous—like a vampire.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc5.description: I learned that Alice declared she would not leave that night and told me to take a deep breath.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc5.source_text: 'All right,' she said, enunciating each word with slow precision. 'I'm not going anywhere tonight. Take a deep breath.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc5.description: I remembered that I had drowned earlier that day.
I felt overwhelmed by borrowed grief for Harry and became worried about how Charlie would react when he came home.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc5.source_text: I fell quiet, struck again by the borrowed grief at Harry's passing. I thought of Charlie; he would be home soon.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc5.description: I became aware of my dependence on Alice as I gripped her collar, hyperventilated, and begged her not to leave.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc5.source_text: 'Don't go, Alice,' I whispered. My fingers locked around the collar of her white shirt and I began to hyperventilate. 'Please don't leave me.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob called and identified himself during the phone call.
I worried that Jacob's call would be problematic for the situation.
I felt very protective and attached to Alice as I grabbed her hand and refused to let her out of my sight.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc6.source_text: I grabbed Alice's stone hand and dragged her with me to the kitchen. I wasn't about to let her out of my sight.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc6.description: I felt disappointed but resigned when Alice reminded me she had a house and could not fully stay.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc6.source_text: 'I have a house, Bella.' I nodded, disappointed but resigned.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc7.description: I noticed that I couldn't smell anything but the brine and seaweed scent of the ocean after showering.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc7.source_text: I sniffed my shoulders as I undressed, but I couldn't smell anything but the brine and seaweed scent of the ocean.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc7.description: I observed that I couldn't see any signs that Charlie had eaten recently and expected he would be hungry when he returned.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc7.source_text: I couldn't see any signs that Charlie 'lad eaten recently, and he would probably be hungry when he got back.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc7.description: I made up the couch with sheets and an old pillow specifically so Charlie would notice it when he came home.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc7.source_text: While Thursday's casserole rotated in the microwave, I made up the couch with sheets and an old pillow. Alice wouldn't need it, but Charlie would need to see it.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc7.description: I drank approximately a half gallon of water because I was dehydrated from the salt in my system.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc7.source_text: I must have drunk a half gallon of water by the time I was finished.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc7.description: I felt much better and relieved when Alice arrived early and provided comfort.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc7.source_text: Alice was already there, sitting on her improvised bed. Her eyes were a liquid butterscotch. She smiled and patted the pillow.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc7.description: I leaned on Alice and accepted her physical comfort when she put her cold arms around me, showing closeness between us.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc7.source_text: I sat down next to her and leaned my head on her shoulder. She put her cold arms around me and sighed.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc8.description: I learned that Charlie returned home grieving Harry and worrying about Harry's family.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc8.source_text: 'I'm really going to miss him,' Charlie mumbled. 'Those poor kids. Leah's just a year older than you, and Seth is only fourteen…'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc8.description: I learned that Charlie agreed to let Alice stay at our house to keep me company.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc8.source_text: 'She can stay here, can't she?' I pleaded. 'I already asked her.' 'Of course,' Charlie said mechanically. 'We'd love to have you, Alice.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc8.description: I noticed that Charlie hugged me fiercely and kept his arms tight around me, which reinforced our close father-daughter bond.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc8.source_text: I hugged him around the waist. He embraced me back fiercely. He kept his arms tight around me as he started toward the door again.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc8.description: I learned that Carlisle and Esme were on a hunting trip and that Alice did not plan to tell Carlisle about her visit.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc8.source_text: 'He and Esme were on a hunting trip. I'll hear from him in a few days, when he gets back.' 'You won't tell him, though… when he checks in again?' I asked. 'No. He'd bite my head off,' Alice said grimly.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.description: I learned Bella had been so withdrawn she wouldn't eat or move and that a doctor used the word 'catatonic'.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.source_text: 'I didn't know what to do. That first week—I thought I was going to have to hospitalize her. She wouldn't eat or drink, she wouldn't move. Dr. Gerandy was throwing around words like 'catatonic,' but I didn't let him up to see her.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.description: I learned Bella violently resisted being sent to Florida and threw a fit when packing was attempted.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.source_text: 'I had Renee come to take her to Florida. I just didn't want to be the one… if she had to go to a hospital or something. I hoped being with her mother would help. But when we started packing her clothes, she woke up with a vengeance. I've never seen Bella throw a fit like that. She was never one for the tantrums, but, boy, did she fly into a fury. She threw her clothes everywhere and screamed that we couldn't make her leave—and then she finally started crying.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.description: I learned Bella resumed routines like school, work, eating, and sleeping but remained emotionally empty and avoided reminders of her loss.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.source_text: 'She went back to school and work, she ate and slept and did her homework. She answered when someone asked her a direct question. But she was… empty. Her eyes were blank.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.description: I believe Bella has not fully recovered because she remains isolated, avoids music and reading, and screams in her sleep.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.source_text: 'She wouldn't listen to music anymore; I found a bunch of CDs broken in the trash. She didn't read; she wouldn't be in the same room when the TV was on... I still hear her screaming in her sleep…'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.description: I learned Bella has been spending time with Jacob Black and appears happier and more colored when she returns home from being with him.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.source_text: 'Ever since she started hanging out with Jacob Black, I've noticed a real improvement. She has some color in her cheeks when she comes home, some light in her eyes. She's happier.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc10.description: I learned that others think Bella may not heal from whatever is troubling her and that they view her as a constant who does not get past things.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc10.source_text: 'I don't know if she's going to get over it—I'm not sure if it's in her nature to heal from something like this. She's always been such a constant little thing. She doesn't get past things, change her mind.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc10.description: I became more worried that my visit might negatively affect Bella because Charlie explicitly voiced concern about what the visit would do to her.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc10.source_text: 'Now, you know how fond I am of you, and I can tell that she's happy to see you, but… I'm a little worried about what your visit will do to her.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc10.description: I noticed that Charlie is fond of Bella and simultaneously protective and apprehensive about outsiders influencing her.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc10.source_text: 'Now, you know how fond I am of you, and I can tell that she's happy to see you, but… I'm a little worried about what your visit will do to her.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.description: I learned that Alice's human name was Mary Alice Brandon and that she had a sister named Cynthia and a niece alive in Biloxi.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.source_text: 'My name was Mary Alice Brandon,' she told me quietly. 'I had a little sister named Cynthia. Her daughter—my niece—is still alive in Biloxi.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.description: I learned that Alice located the asylum where she had spent the last years of her human life and that the admission date matched the date on her tombstone.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.source_text: I also filched my admissions sheet from the old asylum archives. The date on the admission and the date on my tombstone are the same.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.description: I learned that Carlisle was working nights in Ithaca and teaching part time at Cornell.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.source_text: Carlisle was working nights in Ithaca and teaching part time at Cornell.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.description: I learned that Esme was restoring a seventeenth century house, a historical monument, in the forest north of the city.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.source_text: Esme was restoring a seventeenth century house, a historical monument, in the forest north of the city.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.description: I learned that Emmett and Rosalie had gone to Europe for a few months on another honeymoon and had returned.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.source_text: Emmett and Rosalie had gone to Europe for a few months on another honeymoon, but they were back now.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.description: I learned that Jasper was at Cornell studying philosophy again.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.source_text: Jasper was at Cornell, too, studying philosophy this time.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.description: I learned that the Cullens were reassembled except for one who was spending Cornell's spring break in Denali with Tanya and her family.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.source_text: The Cullens were reassembled now, with the one exception, spending Cornell's spring break in Denali with Tanya and her family.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.description: I learned that Charlie had left to help Sue Clearwater with funeral arrangements and that he would be headed back to the reservation for Harry's funeral the next morning.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.source_text: Charlie had to leave then—he was helping Sue Clearwater with the funeral arrangements. He would be headed back to the reservation first thing in the morning for Harry's funeral, so he turned in early.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.description: I realized that I knew Alice's leaving was inevitable but that I purposely put the thought out of my mind.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.source_text: I knew it was inevitable, but I put it out of my mind.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.description: I noticed that I listened too eagerly to even the most trivial news about the Cullens.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.source_text: I listened too eagerly to even the most trivial news.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.description: I felt that listening to the Cullens' stories made me feel closer to the family I had once dreamed of belonging to.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.source_text: It was enough to listen to the stories of the family I'd once dreamed of belonging to.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.description: I was grateful that Alice never mentioned the one I was most interested in.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc11.source_text: She never mentioned the one I was most interested in, and for that I was grateful.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc12.description: I felt Charlie was almost a stranger when he came down the stairs before the sun was up.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc12.source_text: Charlie was almost a stranger when he came down the stairs before the sun was up, wearing an old suit I'd never seen him in before.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc12.description: I noticed Charlie was wearing an old, unfamiliar suit with a wide tie and the jacket hung open.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc12.source_text: Charlie was almost a stranger when he came down the stairs before the sun was up, wearing an old suit I'd never seen him in before. The jacket hung open; I guessed it was too tight to fasten the buttons. His tie was a bit wide for the current style.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc12.description: I decided to catch up on my chores to make life easier for Charlie and to come home to a cleaner, organized house.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc12.source_text: All the time I'd been spending in La Push meant a pile of things I'd been neglecting at home, and I decided to catch up on my chores. I wanted to do something, anything that might make life easier for Charlie—maybe it would make him feel just a little better to come home to a clean, organized house.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc12.description: I felt guilty about eavesdropping on Alice's conversation with Charlie and that guilt altered how I perceived Alice's reaction to my answers.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc12.source_text: Her face stayed casual and emotionless, but I sensed her disapproval when she realized how little I could tell her. Or maybe I just had a guilty conscience after eavesdropping on her conversation with Charlie yesterday morning.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc12.description: I learned that Alice could not see werewolves when Alice grimaced and admitted as much.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc12.source_text: 'You can't see werewolves?' She grimaced. 'So it would seem.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc13.description: I learned that Alice explicitly refused to remain in the room because she wanted to avoid being with Jacob Black.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc13.source_text: Trust me—it wouldn't be a good idea to have me and Jacob Black in a room together.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc13.description: I learned that Alice kissed my cheek swiftly and then left through Charlie's door and likely out his back window.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc13.source_text: She kissed my cheek swiftly before she vanished through Charlie's door—and out his back window, no doubt.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc13.description: I recorded that I told Alice she did not have to go anywhere because she was here first, indicating my attempt to keep her from leaving.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc13.source_text: You don't have go anywhere, Alice. You were here first.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob arrived at my house with Jared driving and Embry in the passenger seat.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: Jacob's Rabbit idled by the curb with Jared behind the wheel and Embry in the passenger seat.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: I learned that Alice Cullen is staying at my house while I am alone.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.source_text:
One of the Cullens is staying here with you" 
"Yes. Alice Cullen.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: I learned that the rest of the Cullens are not returning to town.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: No." I said finally. Grudgingly. "They aren't coming back.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: I felt that I had deeply alienated Jacob and feared he might not forgive me.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: What a disaster. How could I have alienated him so completely in such a short amount of time?

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: I realized that I had hurt Jacob and I cried when I understood the extent of the damage.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: It was only when I saw the clear drops sparkling in my hands that I realized I was crying.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: I know that my choosing a Cullen over Jacob has strained our relationship and created distance between us.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: After all, I'd picked the bloodsucker over him last night.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.description: I felt hurt and torn when I asked if I could be friends with both Jacob and Alice and admitted loving Alice too.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.source_text:
"Can't I be friends with you both at the same time?" I asked, my voice not hiding an ounce of the hurt I felt.

"But you'll wait, right? You'll still be my friend, even though I love
Alice, too?"

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob promised to always be my friend no matter what I love.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.source_text:
"Yeah, I'll always be your friend," he said gruffly. "No matter what you love."

"Promise?"

"Promise."

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.description: I recognized that I felt conflicted about choosing between a fairy-tale love and comfort with Jacob and that Alice's return did not change the loss of 'true love.'
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.source_text:
Alice was back for the moment, but that changed nothing. True love was
forever lost.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.description: I became undecided and frozen when Jacob pressed his palm against my cheek and began to bend his face toward me, worried about the consequences of accepting him.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.source_text:
"He pressed his palm against my cheek, so that my face was trapped between his burning hands.

"Bella," he whispered.

I was frozen.

No! I hadn't made this decision yet..."

"Keeping his eyes on mine, Jacob began to bend his face toward me. And I was still absolutely undecided."

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward believes I am dead after Alice tells me that the caller was Edward and that he thinks I'm dead.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: I read: "It was Edward." "He thinks you're dead."

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward is going to Italy to provoke the Volturi after Alice says, "He's going to Italy."
I shifted from hopeful anticipation of hearing Edward's voice to the conviction that he left because he no longer wanted me after hearing that he believed I was dead.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: I read: "He left! He didn't want me anymore!"

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.description: I felt betrayed and angry toward Edward when I realized he decided to die because he believed I was dead.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.description: I learned that I was instructed to write a note to Charlie while Alice said she would call the airlines.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.source_text: You write a note to Charlie. I'll call the airlines.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.description: I learned that I needed ID and that a passport was expected because Alice asked if I had one.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.source_text: Get your wallet—you'll need ID. Please tell me you have a passport. I don't have time to forge one.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.description: I learned that I had a passport because my mother had wanted to marry Phil on a beach in Mexico, which left practical arrangements in place.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.source_text: my mother had wanted to marry Phil on a beach in Mexico.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.description: I decided that I would go to help Edward despite the danger and Jacob's pleas, shifting from hesitation to determined action.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.source_text: I'll go alone if you're afraid.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.description: I showed deep emotional closeness to Jacob by hugging him tightly and kissing his palm during a tearful farewell.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.source_text: I threw my arms around his waist and hugged for one too-short moment, burying my tear-wet face against his chest. He put his big hand on the back of my hair, as if to hold me there. 'Bye, Jake.' I pulled his hand from my hair, and kissed his palm.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.description: I learned that Alice had visions of Edward committing violent, public acts that would expose the family and force a reaction.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: "A killing spree through the city, attacking the guard, lifting a car over his head in the main square… mostly things that would expose them—he knows that's the fastest way to force a reaction…"

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.description: I learned that Alice can lie with her thoughts and that such mental lying could prevent Edward from knowing the truth.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: "If he were listening," she explained. "But believe it or not, it's possible to lie with your thoughts."

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.description: I changed my belief about Edward's capacity for dangerous action when I realized he might react to perceived loss with extreme violence.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: "I still couldn't believe that he was capable of reacting like this. It made no sense!"

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.description: I recognized that Alice was protecting Jasper by keeping Emmett and Rosalie away even if that decision endangered me or Edward.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: "She was protecting Jasper, at our expense, and maybe at Edward's, too."

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.description: I learned that Alice promised Jasper she would get out before they killed her but admitted she could not guarantee her escape.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: "I promised him I would get out before they killed me, too. It's not something I can guarantee—not by a long shot."

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.description: I learned that the Volturi are an old, powerful family described as royalty.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: He just said they were an old, powerful family—like royalty.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.description: I learned that the Volturi core family originally consisted of Aro, Caius, and Marcus and later included two females.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: There were three of them originally, Aro, Caius, and Marcus. Two females joined them over time, and the five of them make up the family.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.description: I learned that the Volturi keep a guard of vampires, nine permanent members the last time the Cullens heard and additional transitory members.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: There were nine members of the guard that were permanent, the last time we heard. Others are more… transitory.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.description: I learned that many of the Volturi's guard are gifted and that the Volturi select guards for formidable abilities.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: Many of them are gifted as well—with formidable gifts, gifts that make what I can do look like a parlor trick. The Volturi chose them for their abilities, physical or otherwise.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.description: I learned that the Volturi act as enforcers of vampire rules and punish transgressors, fulfilling a duty that makes them dangerous.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: There's a reason he called them royalty… the ruling class. Over the millennia, they have assumed the position of enforcing our rules—which actually translates to punishing transgressors. They fulfill that duty decisively.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.description: I learned that there is one core restriction for vampires in this world: to keep their existence secret.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: There's only one core restriction—and if you think about it, you can probably figure it out for yourself. We just have to keep our existence a secret.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.description: I felt much more frightened and aware of how dangerous the Volturi are after hearing that antagonizing them could mean death.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: That you didn't antagonize them unless you wanted to… die.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.description: I felt angry and resentful that the Cullens had not explained the rules to me sooner after I expressed a desire to become one of them.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: Shouldn't somebody have mentioned this to me earlier? I mean, I wanted to be a… to be one of you! Shouldn't somebody have explained the rules to me?

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc3.description: I found it amazingly easy to say his name now.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc3.source_text: It was amazingly easy to say his name now.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc3.description: I felt comforted by the idea that I would have an easy out.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc3.source_text: It was comforting to know that I would have an easy out.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc3.description: I learned that the Volturi are so protective that they don't allow hunting within Volterra's walls.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc3.source_text: They are so protective of their city that they don't allow hunting within its walls.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc3.description: I accepted that Alice thought our chances were poor.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc3.source_text: I let her comfort me, though I knew she thought our chances were poor.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc3.description: I promised to avoid causing trouble and to accept being returned to Forks if necessary.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc3.source_text: If we're too late for Edward, I'm going to do my damnedest to get you back to Charlie, and I don't want any trouble from you. Do you understand that?

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc4.description: I accepted that the pain I felt was the price I had to pay to save his life and that I would pay it.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: This was the price I had to pay to save his life. I would pay it.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc4.description: I noticed that I had many months' practice controlling my thoughts which helped me avoid dwelling on terrifying possibilities.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: I was grateful that I'd had so many months' practice with controlling my thoughts.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc4.description: I concentrated on lesser problems like what I was going to say to Charlie and whether Jacob's promise to wait would still apply.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: Instead of dwelling on the terrifying possibilities that, no matter what Alice said, I did not intend to survive, I concentrated on lesser problems. Like, what I was going to say to Charlie if I got back:' That was a thorny enough problem to occupy several hours. And Jacob? He'd promised to wait for me, but did that promise still apply?

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc4.description: I believed that saving Edward would not make me any more special to him or give me a reason to stay with him.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: But I wasn't so stupid as to think that saving him would mean that I could stay with him. I was no different, no more special than I'd been before.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc6.description: I learned that Alice once foresaw Bella becoming a vampire.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc6.source_text: "You saw me become one of you."

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc6.description: I felt immediate hope that Alice might change me when she suggested she could change me herself.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc6.source_text: "I'm debating whether to just change you myself."

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc6.description: I learned that Alice judged changing Bella on the plane impractical because of time, severe pain, and other passengers' reactions, and because they needed to reach Volterra tomorrow.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc6.source_text: "Try to be reasonable," she whispered. "We don't have enough time. We have to get into Volterra tomorrow. You'd be writhing in pain for days."

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc6.description: I became more certain that Bella trusted Alice and preferred an immediate dangerous change rather than uncertainty.
I concluded that Bella believed Edward would be furious but ultimately unable to prevent the transformation.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc6.source_text: "He'll be furious, but what will he be able to do about it?" "Nothing at all."

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.description: I learned that someone had refused Edward, expressed as "They've told him no."
I learned that Edward had been rapidly changing plans and that Alice was only getting flickers of his decisions.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.source_text: I was only getting flickers, he was changing plans so quickly.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward briefly decided to go hunting and that the hunt would have been in the city before he changed his mind at the last minute.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.source_text: He'd decided to go hunting. "In the city," she explained. "It got very close. He changed his mind at the last minute."

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward plans to walk out into the sun in a public place and that he is choosing the main plaza under the clock tower.
