tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.source_text: "He's going to keep it simple. He's just going to walk out into the sun." "He wants the biggest audience possible, so he'll choose the main plaza, under the clock tower."

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.description: I became panicked and believed we might be too late to stop his planned spectacle.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.source_text: "We'll be too late," I whispered, my throat closing in panic.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.description: I resolved that I wouldn't let Edward be distracted and that I would follow him when I could so I could help or intervene.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.source_text: I wouldn't let him be distracted. Maybe, when I was beautiful and strong, he wouldn't want distractions.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.description: I learned that Alice stole a bright yellow Porsche and brought me to the airport sidewalk in it.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.source_text: A bright yellow Porsche screamed to a stop a few feet in front of where I paced, the word TURBO scrawled in silver cursive across its back.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.description: I learned that Volterra is holding a festival called Saint Marcus Day and that the festival is tied to a legend about Marcus driving vampires away.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.source_text: 'Well, that's ironic. It's Saint Marcus Day.' 'The city holds a celebration every year. As the legend goes, a Christian missionary, a Father Marcus—Marcus of the Voltun, in fact—drove all the vampires from Volterra fifteen hundred years ago.'

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.description: I learned that Edward decided to wait until noon and that people are waiting for him.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.source_text: 'He's still planning on noon?' I checked. 'Yes. He's decided to wait. And they're waiting for him.'

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.description: I became more terrified of the daylight and more aware that bleeding would make me dangerously visible.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.source_text: The sun was terrifyingly high in the pale blue sky. Bleeding was not the best idea right now.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.description: I trusted Alice's driving and plan despite my fear because I knew I could rely on her behind the wheel.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.source_text: Alice's driving frightened me, despite the fact that I knew I could trust her behind the wheel.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.description: I learned Alice's tactical plan to get me as close as possible, point where to run, and warn me not to trip.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.source_text: 'I'm going to get you as close as possible, and then you're going to run in the direction I point you.' 'Try not to trip,' she added. 'We don't have time for a concussion today.'

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.description: I learned that Carlisle stayed calm and spoke with clear authority, reflecting long emergency-room experience.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: Centuries of experience in the emergency room were evident in his quiet, authoritative voice.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.description: I observed Edward crouch over me protectively, growl a warning, and appear not to be breathing.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: Edward's face was whiter than bone as he wheeled to crouch over me, taking a clearly defensive position. A low warning growl slid from between his clenched teeth. I could tell that he wasn't breathing.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.description: I felt more reassured by Carlisle's leadership and less panicked because of his calm competence.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: Centuries of experience in the emergency room were evident in his quiet, authoritative voice.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.description: I realized that Rosalie maintained a strangely smug expression even while helping restrain Jasper.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: Rosalie, her divine face strangely smug, stepped in front of Jasper—keeping a careful distance from his teeth—and helped Emmett wrestle him through the glass door

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.description: I chose to be treated at home to keep Charlie from finding out about the injury.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: "Here, please," I whispered. If he took me to the hospital, there would be no way to keep this from Charlie.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.description: I noticed Carlisle used a scrap of the tablecloth to make a tourniquet and began treating my arm.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: He reached over and ripped a long, thin scrap from the bottom of the white tablecloth. He twisted it around my arm above the elbow to form a tourniquet.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.description: I decided not to let my usual squeamishness get the best of me while Carlisle worked.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: I was determined not to let my usual squeamishness get the best of me.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.description: I felt reassured by Carlisle's competence when he comforted me and treated the wound.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: "It's not your fault," Carlisle comforted me with a chuckle. "It could happen to anyone."

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.description: I noticed Alice quietly leave the room when she couldn't bring herself to watch the procedure.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: If she hadn't been in my line of sight, I wouldn't have noticed Alice give up and steal out of the room.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc3.description: I observed Bella feeling nauseous and using conversation to distract herself during the procedure.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc3.source_text: I read 'I was tempted to glance at the growing pile, just to check the size, but I knew that idea would not be helpful to my no-vomiting strategy.'

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc3.description: I noticed Bella's sense of wonder and amazement at Carlisle's calm increase as she questioned how he could tolerate the scent.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc3.source_text: I read 'How can you do this?' I demanded. 'Even Alice and Esme…' I trailed off, shaking my head in wonder.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc3.description: I recognized Bella expects Edward to explain family stories and relies on him for context about the Cullens' choices.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc3.source_text: I heard 'Hasn't Edward told you this story?'

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc4.description: I realized my own life was fairly devoid of belief but I did not think Carlisle's hope was foolish.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc4.source_text: My own life was fairly devoid of belief. "I don't think that's foolish," I mumbled.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc4.description: I realized that Edward does not believe there is an afterlife for our kind and that he thinks vampires have lost their souls.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc4.source_text: Edward's with me up to a point. God and heaven exist… and so does hell. But he doesn't believe there is an afterlife for our kind.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc4.description: I understood that Edward's doubt about souls is the reason he is being difficult about a relationship with me.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc4.source_text: "That's the real problem, isn't it?" I guessed. "That's why he's being so difficult about me."

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc5.description: I saw that my shirt was soaked with my blood and that my right shoulder was covered in thick pink frosting.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc5.source_text: I looked down at my shirt; the light blue cotton was soaked and spotted with my blood. My right shoulder was covered in thick pink frosting.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc5.description: I felt that I was to blame for what happened and kept insisting that it was my fault.
I declared that I would rather die than be with anyone but Edward, reaffirming my exclusive devotion to him.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc5.source_text: I'd rather die than be with Mike Newton," I protested. "I'd rather die than be with anyone but you.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc5.description: I asked Edward to stay for my birthday and wanted him to share that occasion with me.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc6.description: I learned that my arm is injured, that I have stitches, and that the anesthetic was losing its effectiveness.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc6.source_text: I held my arm close to my side. The slight pressure burned, and I wrinkled my nose. The anesthetic was apparently losing its effectiveness.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc6.description: I learned that I received several gifts including a stereo for my truck, plane tickets to Jacksonville, and a CD of Edward's music that contains my lullaby.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc6.source_text: A stereo for my truck. "We're going to Jacksonville?" ... He handed back a clear CD jewel case, with a blank silver CD inside. "It was his music, his compositions. The first piece on the CD was my lullaby."

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc6.description: I realized that Edward underestimated how I would react to gifts and that my appropriate response surprised him.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc6.source_text: "If I'd had any idea that you could respond to a gift this appropriately, I would have made you open it in front of Carlisle and Esme. I thought you'd complain."

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc6.description: I felt loved and deeply moved by Edward's thoughtfulness when I listened to his music and became tearful.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc6.source_text: I listened, speechless and wide-eyed. Tears welled up, and I reached up to wipe them away before they could spill over. "It's beautiful, Edward. You couldn't have given me anything I would love more."

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward said he was thinking about right and wrong.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.source_text: "I was thinking about right and wrong, actually."

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward admitted being tempted equally by my blood and my body.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.source_text: "Which is tempting you more, my blood or my body?" I challenged. "It's a tie."

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward's skin was cool and that pressing my injured arm to his shoulder soothed the burning.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.source_text: Trying to be sneaky about it, I pressed my injured arm against his shoulder, so his cool skin would sooth the burning.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.description: I realized that Edward's usual self-control could falter and that he could become urgently passionate.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.source_text: Suddenly his lips became much more urgent, his free hand twisted into my hair and held my face securely to his.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.description: I felt that my intimacy with Edward deepened when he allowed greater contact and then apologized, and I accepted it.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.source_text: "Sorry," he said, and he was breathless, too. "That was out of line." "I don't mind," I panted.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.description: I developed a foreboding sense that something worse might come tomorrow, changing my sense of safety.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.source_text: Almost as if something worse was coming tomorrow. It was a silly premonition—what could be worse than today?

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.description: I saw that the climb grew congested and we slowed to a crawl behind a little tan Peugeot.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: As we wound higher, the cars became too close together for Alice to weave insanely between them anymore. We slowed to a crawl behind a little tan Peugeot.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.description: I noticed that no one was being allowed to drive through and that people were walking into the city from parked cars.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: No one was being allowed to drive through.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.description: I noticed that the color red was everywhere and that a brilliant crimson scarf was caught and twisted up into the air like it was alive.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: I also noticed that the color red was everywhere. Red shirts, red hats, red flags dripping like long ribbons beside the gate, whipping in the wind—as I watched, the brilliant crimson scarf one woman had tied around her hair was caught in a sudden gust. It twisted up into the air above her, writhing like it was alive.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.description: I felt urgent panic as the clock on the dash seemed to be speeding up and time became a pressing concern.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: 'Alice,' I moaned. The clock on the dash seemed to be speeding up.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.description: I learned that Alice bribed the guard by putting a thick roll of money into his hand and that the outside bill was a thousand dollar bill.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.source_text:
She put something into his palm, and folded his fingers around it.
The outside bill was a thousand dollar bill.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.description: I trusted Alice's decisiveness and resourcefulness when she accelerated, negotiated past the uniformed man, and quietly bought our way into the city.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.source_text:
Alice accelerated, edging around him and heading for the gate. He shouted something at us, but held his ground, waving frantically to keep the next car from following our bad example.
She put something into his palm, and folded his fingers around it.
Alice's smile was blinding.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc2.description: I watched Bella shove through the crowd, splash through a knee-deep fountain, and scream Edward's name as she raced toward the clock tower.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: I shoved a heavy woman out of my way and ran flat out, head down, paying little attention to anything but the uneven stones beneath my feet. I started screaming as I ran.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc2.description: I realized that Bella believed she was stupid, slow, and human and that this made her fear everyone was going to die because of it.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: I was stupid and slow and human, and we were all going to die because of it.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc2.description: I noticed that Bella used the fountain as a quick route across the square and that the cold water and wind made her physical pain and urgency more acute.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: I was nearly crying with relief as I flung my leg over the edge and ran through the knee-deep water. It sprayed all around me as I thrashed my way across the pool.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.description: I learned that Alice slid down an open hole in the street and caught me when I was lowered.
I learned that Edward put his arm around me, held me close, and towed me swiftly forward through the tunnel.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: He put his arm around me, holding me close to his side, and began to tow me swiftly forward.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.description: I learned that the heavy grate slid over the drain hole and closed with metallic finality behind us.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: The sound of the heavy grate sliding over the drain hole behind us rang with metallic finality.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.description: I learned that the others could hear everything, including my every breath and my every heartbeat.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: The others could hear everything—my every breath, my every heartbeat.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.description: I felt that Edward wanted me in that moment and that belief helped offset my terror in the tunnel.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: For now, it felt like he wanted me, and that was enough to offset the horror of the subterranean tunnel and the prowling vampires behind us.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.description: I realized that being with Edward again before any possible death changed my view of our reunion as a solace rather than only tragedy.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: At least I could be with him again before I died.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.description: I noticed the hallway was brightly lit with off-white walls, industrial gray carpet, and evenly spaced fluorescent lights and that it felt warmer compared to the sewers.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: WE WERE IN A BRIGHTLY LIT, UNREMARKABLE HALLWAY. The walls were off-white, the floor carpeted in industrial gray. Common rectangular fluorescent lights were spaced evenly along the ceiling. It was warmer here, for which I was grateful. This hall seemed very benign after the gloom of the ghoulish stone sewers.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.description: I observed myself cowering in the corner and cringing against Edward while his hand rubbed against my arm.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: I cowered in the corner, cringing against Edward. His hand still rubbed against my arm. He never took his eyes off Jane.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.description: I felt both grateful for the warmth of the reception area and frightened by the Volturi presence, and I found reassurance in Edward's physical closeness.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: It was warmer here, for which I was grateful. I cowered in the corner, cringing against Edward. His hand still rubbed against my arm.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.description: I realized I relied on Edward for protection and comfort as I clung to his side during the visit.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: Alec chuckled, and examined me as I clung to Edward's side. "And this is the cause of all the trouble?" he asked, skeptical.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.description: I learned that Gianna, the receptionist, knows everything about the situation.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: "Yes. She knows everything," Edward told me.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.description: I learned that Gianna knows it's a possibility that they will kill her.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: "She's knows it's a possibility," he said.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.description: I learned that Gianna is hoping they'll decide to keep her.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: "She's hoping they'll decide to keep her."

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.description: I realized that I was shaking violently and that the ripping noise I heard was my own sobs.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: It was only then that I realize I was shaking, shaking hard, my entire frame vibrating until my teeth chattered and the room around me seemed to wobble and blur in my eyes.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.description: I felt a guilty, intense happiness at being alive and together with Edward despite impending danger.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: "Is it really sick for me to be happy right now?" I asked.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.description: I felt closer to Edward and I pretended he felt the same to make the moment sweeter.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: So that's what I did. I pretended, to make the moment sweeter.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc1.description: I cowered in the corner and cringed against Edward, showing my fear and vulnerability in the presence of the Volturi.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: I cowered in the corner, cringing against Edward.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc1.description: I felt grateful for the warmth of the brightly lit hallway after emerging from the colder, ghoulish stone sewers, indicating a shift from dread to temporary relief.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: It was warmer here, for which I was grateful.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc1.description: I noticed Edward's protective behavior when he pulled me along and kept his hand rubbing my arm, which strengthened my sense of his guardianship.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: He pulled me along, and Alice walked on my other side.  His hand still rubbed against my arm.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc2.description: I saw a different kind of reception beyond the wooden doors.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: On the other side of the wooden doors was a different kind of reception.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc2.description: I clung to Edward's side, signaling physical closeness and reliance.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: Alec chuckled, and examined me as I clung to Edward's side.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc2.description: I felt irritated and wanted to groan when Edward pulled me through to the other side of the door.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: I wanted to groan when Edward pulled me through to the other side of the door.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc3.description: I learned that Aro recognized and greeted me enthusiastically, indicating he knew I was alive.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: I read "'And Alice and Bella, too!' he rejoiced, clapping his thin hands together. 'This is a happy surprise! Wonderful!'"

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc3.description: I noticed that Edward tightened his arm around my waist, showing his protective posture toward me in front of the Volturi.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: I read "'Yes, Aro, I am,' he agreed, tightening his arm around my waist."

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc3.description: I felt astonished that Aro addressed me informally and warmly, which changed my expectation of his reception.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: I read "I stared in shock as he called our names informally, as if we were old friends dropping in for an unexpected visit."

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc3.description: I observed the chamber's layout and atmosphere, noting high windows, stone walls, throne-like chairs, and a central drain.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: I read "The stone antechamber was not large. It opened quickly into a brighter, cavernous room, perfectly round like a huge castle turret... Two stories up, long window slits threw thin rectangles of bright sunlight onto the stone floor below."

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc4.description: I observed Aro reach out and press his insubstantial-looking skin against Bella's hand during a test, then call the experience 'So very interesting' and later 'A first' while wondering if she was immune to their talents.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc4.source_text:
Aro reached out, as if to shake my hand, and pressed his insubstantial-looking skin against mine.

"So very interesting," he said as he released my hand and drifted back.

"A first," he said to himself "I wonder if she is immune to our other talents… Jane, dear?"

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc4.description: I felt Bella's terror at the thought of Aro touching her and also her perverse intrigue about feeling his strange skin.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: I was horrified at the thought of allowing him to touch me, and yet also perversely intrigued by the chance to feel his strange skin.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc4.description: I noticed Edward nodded in encouragement when Bella raised her hand to allow Aro to touch her, though his motivation for the nod was unclear.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: Edward nodded in encouragement—whether because he was sure Aro would not hurt me, or because there was no choice, I couldn't tell.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.description: I learned that Aro directly asked whether I wanted to join the Volturi.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: "And you, Bella?" Aro raised his eyebrows.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.description: I learned that Caius declared I "know too much" and framed that knowledge as exposing Volturi secrets.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: "She knows too much. You have exposed our secrets."

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.description: I learned that Caius stated that for this situation "only her life is forfeit," indicating my life could be at stake if considered a liability.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: "Though it is true, for this, only her life is forfeit."

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.description: I learned that Aro offered freedom to leave if Edward would truly commit to changing me, saying they would be free to go home and give his regards to Carlisle.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: "Why, then you would be free to go home and give my regards to my friend Carlisle."

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.description: I realized I was wavering about the idea of immortality for fear that Edward might choose to change me rather than die.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: Was it really such a loathsome idea? Would he rather die than change me? I felt like I'd been kicked in the stomach.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.description: I felt frightened when I whispered my refusal, recognizing how vulnerable I was in front of the Volturi.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: "No, thank you," I spoke up in barely more than a whisper, my voice breaking in fright.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.description: I understood more clearly that Edward was deeply protective of me and willing to contemplate hard choices to keep me safe.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: Edward's lips tightened into a fierce line. He stared into my eyes, and I stared back.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.description: I learned that a large crowd of humans entered the smaller stone chamber and that Demetri motioned for us to make room.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: A large crowd was coming through the little door, filling the smaller stone chamber. Demetri motioned for us to make room.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.description: I learned that Aro's voice was audible from the turret room welcoming the guests to Volterra.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: "Welcome, guests! Welcome to Volterra!" I could hear Aro sing from the big turret room.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.description: I learned that some tourists were snapping pictures and that one small, dark woman wearing a rosary was panicked and speaking in an unfamiliar language while touching others.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: Some studied the setting like tourists. A few even snapped pictures. I noticed one small, dark woman in particular. Around her neck was a rosary, and she gripped the cross tightly in one hand. She walked more slowly than the others, touching someone now and then and asking a question in an unfamiliar language. No one seemed to understand her, and her voice grew more panicked.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.description: I learned that Heidi was present alone in the ornate golden hallway and that Demetri greeted her as if welcoming her home.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: The ornate golden hallway was quiet, empty except for one gorgeous, statuesque woman. She stared at us curiously, me in particular. "Welcome home, Heidi," Demetri greeted her from behind us.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.description: I learned that Heidi's appearance was deliberately attention-grabbing and that I understood she functioned as both fisherman and bait.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: She was dressed to emphasize that beauty. Her amazingly long legs, darkened with tights, were exposed by the shortest of miniskirts. Her top was long-sleeved and high-necked, but extremely close-fitting, and constructed of red vinyl. ... I suddenly understood the attention-grabbing outfit she wore… she was not only the fisherman, but also the bait.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.description: I realized with horror and tears that the situation was dangerous as soon as the smallest break in the crowd appeared.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: Edward pulled my face against his chest, but it was too late. I already understood. As soon as the smallest break appeared, Edward pushed me quickly toward the door. I could feel the horrified expression on my face, and the tears beginning to pool in my eyes.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.description: I compared Heidi's unforgettable beauty to Rosalie and updated my perception of Heidi as exceptionally striking despite their differences.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: She reminded me of Rosalie, though they looked nothing alike—it was just that her beauty, too, was exceptional, unforgettable.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.description: I recognized Edward's protective and urgent behavior toward me when the crowd arrived and when danger became apparent.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: Edward pulled my face against his chest, but it was too late. As soon as the smallest break appeared, Edward pushed me quickly toward the door.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc1.description: I learned that Demetri warned us not to leave until dark.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: "Do not leave until dark," he warned us.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc1.description: I realized my fear had overwhelmed me and I was shaking and sobbing uncontrollably.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: "I was shaking, shaking hard, my entire frame vibrating until my teeth chattered and the room around me seemed to wobble and blur in my eyes."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc1.description: I cannot forget the panicked face of the tiny woman with the rosary that haunted me behind my tears.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: "the panicked face of the tiny woman with the rosary."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.description: I learned that Gianna knows the truth about what is happening and that she is aware of the danger to her life.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: "Yes. She knows everything," Edward told me.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.description: I learned that Gianna understands it is possible they will kill her someday.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: "She's knows it's a possibility," he said.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.description: I learned that Gianna hopes they will decide to keep her and that she wants to be one of them.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: "She's hoping they'll decide to keep her." "She wants to be one of them?"

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.description: I felt surprised and disturbed to accept that someone would want to join the vampires despite the mortal risk.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I shuddered. "How can she want that?" I whispered, more to myself than really looking for an answer.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.description: I realized that Edward comforts and protects me physically and emotionally by holding me, rubbing my back, and reassuring me that we are alive together.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: He didn't push me away. He pulled me tight against his ice-hard chest, so tight it was hard to breathe, even with my lungs securely intact.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.description: I felt both relief and acute anxiety as I found happiness in the present moment while fearing the impending future and wishing the moment would last or that I would not have to face what comes next.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: "Oh, Edward," I cried, and I was sobbing again... I only had until sunset for sure. Like a fairy tale again, with deadlines that ended the magic.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.description: I learned that Alice believes she will see Jasper in less than twenty-four hours and seems confident in that knowledge.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: "I'll see Jasper in less than twenty-four hours," she added in a satisfied tone.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.description: I decided to pretend Edward felt the same way to make the moment sweeter despite my doubts.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "So that's what I did. I pretended, to make the moment sweeter."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward claims he is in unusually good control of his vampiric nature at that moment.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "I've never been in better control of that side of my nature than right now."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.description: I learned that vampires have a term for someone who smells the way Bella does to Edward and they call her 'my singer' because her blood 'sings' for him.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "They have a name for someone who smells the way Bella does to me. They call her my singer—because her blood sings for me."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.description: I felt that being held and kissed by Edward made me much happier and allowed me to ignore dangerous questions for the moment.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "Here in his arms, it was so easy to fantasize that he wanted me... But it didn't matter. I was so much happier pretending."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.description: I inferred that Edward and Alice were quietly planning how to get home and that their plan might involve additional theft.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "He stared at my face like he was doing the same, while he and Alice discussed how to get home... It sounded like more theft would be involved, though."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.description: I updated my view of Edward as someone who can show tenderness and affection even while remaining a potential threat.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "Now and then, as he talked with Alice, he would lean down suddenly and kiss me—his glass-smooth lips... Each time it was like an electric shock to my long dormant heart."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.description: I heard Alec tell us we were free to leave and that we were asked not to linger in the city.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: "You're free to leave now," Alec told us, his tone so warm you'd think we were all lifelong friends. "We ask that you don't linger in the city."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.description: I remembered that I had access to a toothbrush and that the memory brightened my outlook.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: I'd forgotten that I had access to a toothbrush. It brightened my outlook considerably.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.description: I learned that Alice went to retrieve my bags from where she had stashed them this morning.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: "She went to retrieve your bags from where she stashed them this morning."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.description: I felt relieved that there was another way out because I wasn't sure I could handle another tour through the underground.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: I was relieved there was another way out; I wasn't sure if I could handle another tour through the underground.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.description: I felt Edward's protectiveness and warmth when he wound his arm around my waist and supported most of my weight as we walked.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: He wound his arm around my waist and supported most of my weight as we walked.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.description: I admitted to myself that I lied about not being tired because I was afraid to close my eyes.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: "I don't want to sleep. I'm not tired." Just the second part was a lie.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.description: I learned that Alice bought Edward new clothes and that Edward left a dark cloak on a pile of trash in an alley.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.source_text: Alice bought Edward new clothes, too, and he left the dark cloak on a pile of trash in an alley.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.description: I learned that the flight from Rome to Atlanta would be long and that I asked the flight attendant for a Coke to stay awake.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.source_text: I knew the flight from Rome to Atlanta would be another matter entirely, so I asked the flight attendant if she could bring me a Coke.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.description: I decided that staying awake was necessary to avoid seeing things I did not want to see and to prevent nightmares.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.source_text: If I close my eyes now, I'll see things I don't want to see. I'll have nightmares.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.description: I felt Edward's closeness as he held me and kissed my hair, forehead, and wrists while deliberately not kissing my lips, which affected how I viewed our intimacy.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.source_text: Edward seemed perfectly content to hold me in his arms, his fingers tracing my face again and again. He continued to kiss my hair, my forehead, my wrists… but never my lips, and that was good.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.description: I noticed that Alice was behind us and that I could hear her murmuring to Jasper on the phone.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.source_text: Alice was behind us. I could hear her murmuring to Jasper on the phone.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.description: I stayed awake for the entire trip to Atlanta and watched the sun begin to rise over Seattle's cloud cover before Edward slid the window shut.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.source_text: I was awake when we reached the airport in Atlanta, and I even watched the sun beginning to rise over Seattle's cloud cover before Edward slid the window shut.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc6.description: I learned that I was overwhelmingly exhausted and disconnected after the previous night, to the point of almost collapsing.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc6.source_text: The sleepless night was suddenly overpowering. My head felt disconnected from my body.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc6.description: I felt more forgiving toward Rosalie after she apologized and expressed gratitude for my actions.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc6.source_text: "I'm so very sorry, Bella. I feel wretched about every part of this, and so grateful that you were brave enough to go save my brother after what I did. Please say you'll forgive me."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc6.description: I perceived Edward as my protector who would physically carry me and insist on staying close until I was safe.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc6.source_text: "Just let me get her upstairs," Edward said. "I won't be far," Edward promised, whispering so low in my ear that Charlie didn't have a hope of hearing.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc6.description: I experienced strained relations with my father in public, noting his anger toward Edward and demand to take me away.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc6.source_text: "I can't believe you have the nerve to show your face here." Charlie bellowed at Edward. "Give her to me. Get your hands off her!"

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.description: I woke with the sense that I'd been asleep for a very long time and felt stiff and dazed.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I HAD THE SENSE THAT I'D BEEN ASLEEP FOR A VERY long time—my body was stiff, like I hadn't moved once through all that time, either.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.description: I experienced strange, colorful, vivid dreams that mixed horrible and heavenly images, including monsters and an angel.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: My mind was dazed and slow; strange, colorful dreams—dreams and nightmares—swirled dizzily around the inside of my head. They were so vivid. The horrible and the heavenly, all mixed together into a bizarre jumble.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.description: I could remember names from the dream and the dream remained strong as I woke.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: The dream was still strong—I could even remember the names.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.description: I found the angel to be the strongest, clearest part of the dream and had difficulty letting him go on waking.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: But the strongest, clearest part of the dream was not the horror. It was the angel that was most clear. It was hard to let him go and wake up.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.description: I felt something cold touch my forehead with the softest pressure as I was waking.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: Something cold touched my forehead with the softest pressure.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.description: I decided to enjoy the pleasant delusions because I accepted, for a moment, that I might be insane.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: It took less than half a second for me to realize that, as long as I was truly insane now, I might as well enjoy the delusions while they were pleasant.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.description: I believed I had drowned and thought I was dead when I woke up.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: "I'm dead, right?" I moaned. "I did drown. Crap, crap, crap! This is gonna kill Charlie."

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.description: I realized that Edward was really, truly there with me and not just a hallucination.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: I started to remember details… and I felt a faint, unfamiliar blush warm the skin over my cheekbones as I slowly realized that Edward was really, truly here with me, and I was wasting time being an idiot.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.description: I moved from insisting I was dead to accepting that I was awake after Edward said so.
I felt relief and embarrassment at Edward's presence and chastised myself for being an idiot about it.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: I started to remember details… and I felt a faint, unfamiliar blush warm the skin over my cheekbones as I slowly realized that Edward was really, truly here with me, and I was wasting time being an idiot.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.description: I worried that my presumed death would hurt Charlie, Renee, and Jake and I felt horror at what I might have done.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: "This is gonna kill Charlie." ... "Poor Charlie. And Renee and Jake…" I trailed off in horror at what I had done.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.description: I heard Edward say he owed me an apology for what he had done.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: I owe you an apology. No, of course I owe you much, much more than that.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward had been hunting and attempting tracking before he came back to me.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: I was… hunting. I wasn't hunting for food… I was actually trying my hand at… tracking. I'm not very good at it.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.description: I decided that I did not want to be a source of guilt and anguish in Edward's life and I tried to free him from blame.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: I didn't want to be a source of guilt and anguish in his life. He should be happy, no matter what it cost me.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.description: I noticed that Edward was deeply remorseful and anguished about leaving me vulnerable.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: I feel sick, sick to my core, even now, when I can see and feel you safe in my arms. I am the most miserable excuse for—

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc5.description: I changed my belief about why Edward went to Italy from thinking he went out of guilt to understanding he went because he thought I was dead.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: "Bella, I went to the Volturi because I thought you were dead," he said, voice soft, eyes fierce.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc5.description: I learned that Edward stated he would have gone to Italy even if he had no hand in my death.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: "Even if I'd had no hand in your death"—he shuddered as he whispered the last word—"even if it wasn't my fault, I would have gone to Italy."

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc5.description: I felt betrayed and hurt when I realized Edward admitted to being a good liar, which undermined my trust in his previous explanations.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: "I'm a good liar, Bella, I have to be."

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc5.description: I updated my belief about Edward's emotional stakes when I heard him say he cannot live in a world where I do not exist.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: "Bella, I can't live in a world where you don't exist."

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc6.description: I learned that Edward staged the farewell and lied about not wanting me as a way to try to make me move on.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc6.source_text: I lied to save you, and it didn't work.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc6.description: I changed from thinking I might be dreaming to understanding that the goodbye was a conscious deception and that Edward truly loves me.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc6.source_text: I have always loved you, and I will always love you.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc6.description: I recognized that my relationship with Edward was reaffirmed when I declared that my love would never change and when we kissed passionately.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc6.source_text: I kissed him back, my heart pounding out a jagged, disjointed rhythm while my breathing turned to panting and my fingers moved greedily to his face.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc7.description: I felt intensified skepticism about promises because I whispered, "Don't promise me anything," fearing that hope would hurt me.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc7.source_text: "Don't promise me anything," I whispered. If I let myself hope, and it came to nothing… that would kill me.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc7.description: I reconsidered Edward's earlier coldness as potentially motivated by love when I heard him say he left to give me a chance at a normal life.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc7.source_text: "I only left you in the first place because I wanted you to have a chance at a normal, happy, human life."

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc7.description: I recognized that I was attempting to remain objective and clinical about Edward's motives to avoid falling into hope.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc7.source_text: I shook my head, trying to think it through coherently. To examine the hypothesis that he did love me, while staying objective, clinical, so I wouldn't fall into the trap of hoping.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.description: I learned that Bella felt as if many pieces of herself had gone missing and that she had not been able to breathe properly for a long time.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.source_text: Lots of pieces of me went missing, too. I haven't been able to really breathe in so long.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.description: I realized that Bella was in danger of hoping again because Edward's presence rekindled strong feelings.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.source_text: I was very much in danger of hoping.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.description: I understood that Bella relied on Edward's promise that he would not leave and held him to that promise.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.source_text: Didn't you just promise that you weren't going to leave?

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.description: I noticed that Bella considered Jacob and the werewolves a lesser problem compared to other issues she faced.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.source_text: I wasn't talking about Jacob. My problems are a lot worse that a handful of adolescent wolves getting themselves into trouble.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.description: I learned that Bella believes the Volturi represent a greater, long-term threat than Victoria.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.source_text: I heard: "The Volturi are only the second greatest?"

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.description: I learned that Bella explicitly worries about being thirty and the implications of aging while remaining human.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.source_text: I heard: "I paused. I wasn't sure I could say the name. 'There are others who are coming to look for me,' I reminded him in a subdued whisper."

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.description: I became convinced that Bella's hope in Edward's promises is shaken by the idea that he might not stay indefinitely.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.source_text: I heard: "So his promises meant nothing, in the end. If I were going to turn thirty someday, then he couldn't be planning on staying long."

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.description: I noticed that Bella expresses resentment and vulnerability toward Edward while still depending on his protection and reassurance.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.source_text: I heard: "'You don't have to be afraid,' he said... 'I won't let them hurt you.' 'While you're here.'"

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.description: I decided to leave and go to Edward's house.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.source_text: "I'm going to your house," I told him, still feeling around blindly.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.description: I planned to use my truck to get to his house.
I expected to be grounded for weeks if I left.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.source_text: "But honestly, I'll be grounded for weeks as it is. How much more trouble can I really get in?"

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.description: I believed this decision wasn't just about Edward anymore and that his family should have input.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.source_text: "This isn't just about you anymore. You're not the center of the universe, you know."

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.description: I noticed that the idea of me leaving hurt him and that realization made my heart flutter.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.source_text: "Do you want me to leave?" he asked, and it made my heart flutter to see that this idea hurt him, though he tried not to show it.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.description: I teased him to make himself at home and felt surprised at how natural my teasing sounded.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.source_text: "But you go ahead and make yourself at home," I encouraged, surprised at how natural my teasing sounded, and headed for the door.

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.description: I learned that running through the forest on his back felt comforting and that the dark felt familiar and protecting to me.
tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: Like the thick quilt I'd played under as a child, the dark felt familiar and protecting.

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.description: I confessed that I trust him while acknowledging that I do not trust myself to be enough for him.
tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: "I trust you," I assured him. "It's me I don't trust."

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.description: I discovered that I could hear his voice most clearly during dangerous or reckless moments, which comforted me and made him feel present.
tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: I could remember how your voice sounded when you were angry. I could hear it, like you were standing right there next to me.

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.description: I realized that some subconscious part of me never stopped believing that he still cared whether I lived or died.
tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: Some part of me, my subconscious maybe, never stopped believing that you still cared whether I lived or died.

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.description: I learned that my things were not gone and that he had hidden them under my floorboards as a reminder of himself.
tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: "Your things were never gone," he told me. "I knew it was wrong, since I promised you peace without reminders. It was stupid and childish, but I wanted to leave something of myself with you. The CD, the pictures, the tickets—they're all under your floorboards."

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc2.description: I learned that Carlisle said he was able to perform the change and that I would be in no danger of him losing control.
tw-book2-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: "I'm able to do it," he answered my question. "You would be in no danger of me losing control."

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc2.description: I believed that staying human was actively hurting the people I love and that changing would reduce the danger to them.
tw-book2-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: "At the same time, I was hurting them more by staying human. Putting Charlie in constant danger through my proximity. Putting Jake in worse danger still by drawing his enemies across the land he felt bound to protect. And Renee—I couldn't even risk a visit to see my own mother for fear of bringing my deadly problems along with me!"

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc2.description: I trusted Alice to do what she promised and I reminded her of her promise despite her panic.
tw-book2-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: "You promised," I reminded her."You can do it," I encouraged.

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc2.description: I agreed to consider postponing my change until after graduation as a way to keep Charlie uninvolved and safe.
tw-book2-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: "In the interest of remaining inconspicuous," Edward said, "I suggest that we put this conversation off, at the very least until Bella finishes high school, and moves out of Charlie's house.""I'll consider it."

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc2.description: I learned that Billy told me Jacob did not want to talk when I called from work, indicating avoidance.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc2.source_text: "Billy said he didn't want to talk to me," I fumed, glaring at the rain oozing down the passenger window.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc2.description: I began to believe that being angry about things was easier for me than feeling guilty.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc2.source_text: Being angry about things was easier than feeling guilty.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc2.description: I updated my view that Jacob has entrenched enmity toward Edward and is deliberately avoiding him.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc2.source_text: "Jacob knows we're back, and I'm sure that he's ascertained that I'm with you," Edward said. "He won't come anywhere near me. The enmity is rooted too deeply."

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.description: I learned that my motorcycle was parked in Charlie's driveway.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: My motorcycle, flaunting itself in the driveway.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.description: I inferred that only Jacob could be behind the motorcycle being placed there.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: There was only one person who could be behind this treachery.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob was waiting near the trees for us.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: Yes. He's waiting for us there.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob was acting as a spokesperson for the pack.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: He's acting as… spokesperson for the pack.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.description: I changed from trusting Jacob implicitly to feeling betrayed and considering him capable of being petty and mean.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: I had trusted Jacob implicitly—trusted him with every single secret I had. I would have never imagined that Jake could be so petty and just plain mean.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.description: I felt betrayed by Jacob and no longer saw him as the safe harbor I could always rely on.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: He was supposed to be my safe harbor—the person I could always rely on. I had been betrayed.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.description: I became worried that Charlie would be mad and hurt and that my actions would add to his burdens.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: Charlie was going to be so mad—and worse than that, he was going to be hurt and worried.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward said Charlie would be ready to kill me, indicating Edward knew Charlie's likely reaction.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: Edward had said that Charlie was ready to kill me, so he must know that—that it was mine.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward physically restrained me because he was faster and to prevent me from confronting Jacob.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: He caught me around the waist before I made the path. Why did Edward have to be so much faster than me?

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc4.description: I saw Jacob waiting up the path, lounging against a mossy tree trunk with a hard, bitter face.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: He lounged against a mossy tree trunk as he waited, his face hard and bitter, exactly the way I knew it would be.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc4.description: I realized my anger toward Jacob weakened when I remembered seeing him with tears in his eyes the last time I saw him.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: Instead, it reminded me of the last time I'd seen him, with tears in his eyes. My fury weakened, faltered, as I stared at Jacob.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc4.description: I know that I am already grounded and that being grounded will not keep me away from Edward.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: "I'm already grounded! Why do you think I haven't been down to La Push to kick your butt for avoiding my phone calls?" ... "But that won't keep me away from Edward. There's nothing that can do that."

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc4.description: I feel firmly committed to Edward when I whispered 'Never' in response to his promise to stay until I order him away.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: "I'm a quick learner, Jacob Black, and I don't make the same mistake twice. I'm here until she orders me away." ... "Never," I whispered, still locked in Edward's eyes.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc1.description: I woke feeling absolutely hideous with poor sleep, a burning arm, and an aching head.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: I FELT ABSOLUTELY HIDEOUS IN THE MORNING. I HADN'T slept well; my arm burned and my head ached.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc1.description: I felt my anxiety increase and noticed the pounding in my head intensify.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: The anxiety seemed to ratchet up the intensity of the pounding in my head.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc1.description: I lied when Edward asked how I felt and said "Perfect," while cringing at the slamming door.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: "How do you feel?" "Perfect," I lied, cringing as the sound of the slamming door echoed in my head.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc1.description: I kept questions for Alice about Jasper, what had been said while I was unconscious, and Rosalie's response.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: There were so many questions I wanted to ask, but most of those questions would have to wait, because they were for Alice: How was Jasper this morning? What had they said when I was gone? What had Rosalie said?

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc1.description: I hoped Alice's visions could reveal what might happen and whether Edward's mood had a clear cause.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: And most importantly, what could she see happening now in her strange, imperfect visions of the future? Could she guess what Edward was thinking, why he was so gloomy?

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: I was impatient to see Alice and expected to find her at lunch.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: I was impatient to see Alice, though I wouldn't be able to really talk to her with Edward there.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: I lied about my arm when Edward asked and I minimized my injury.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: Occasionally he would ask about my arm, and I would lie.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: I noticed Alice was not at the lunch table when I expected her to be.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: But she wasn't at the table, waiting with a tray of food she wouldn't eat.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: I saw Conner and Ben and I realized they were in Alice's fourth hour French class.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: until I saw Conner and Ben, who were in her fourth hour French class.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: I learned that Alice was with Jasper and that Jasper had "gone away for a while."
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: "She's with Jasper." "He's gone away for a while." "Yes. She'll be gone for a while."

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: I felt guilty and I believed I had run them out of their home, thinking of myself as a plague.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: I'd run them out of their home, just like Rosalie and Emmett. I was a plague.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc2.description: I dismissed the importance of my arm by muttering about it in disgust.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: "Who cares about my stupid arm?" I muttered in disgust.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc3.description: I had to work and I had traded with Mrs. Newton to get yesterday off.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: "I have to work. I had to trade with Mrs. Newton to get yesterday off."

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc3.description: I noticed he kissed my forehead before he shut the door on me.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: "He kissed my forehead again before he shut the door on me."

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc3.description: I felt suddenly unsure about this relationship when I realized I hated that I felt unsure.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: "I hated that I felt suddenly unsure about this."

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc3.description: I told myself that what had happened last night was nothing compared to the attack by James.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: "After all, what had happened last night was nothing. Nothing had happened."

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc3.description: I suspected his distance might be because his family was disappearing and because the threat involved his brother.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: "Maybe it was because, this time, it wasn't an enemy he'd had to protect me from? Because it was his brother?"

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc3.description: I considered going away to college with him or pretending to go to college like Rosalie and Emmett did this year.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: "We could go away to college, or pretend that's what we were doing, like Rosalie and Emmett this year."

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc3.description: I grew slightly less depressed as I considered the possibility of uninterrupted alone time with him.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: "I grew slightly less depressed as I considered all the uninterrupted alone time."

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc5.description: I followed Edward out the front door and saw him go to his car.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: I got awkwardly to my feet—I was stiff from sitting so still—and followed Edward out the front door.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc5.description: I asked Edward to stay and heard his refusal.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: I asked, no hope in my voice.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc5.description: I realized I would miss the woods and that they no longer seemed sinister to me.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: I realized I would miss this—the green, the timelessness, the mystery of the woods.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc5.description: I took morning photographs of my truck, the front of the house, and the nearby forest.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: I took one of my truck, and then the front of the house.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc5.description: I experienced a long night with little rest and got up at first light.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: It was a long night, with little in the way of rest.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc5.description: I began to feel impatience and fear about how long Edward's distance would last.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: I was beginning to feel impatience.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc6.description: I picked up my developed pictures and saw Edward staring out of the first print with the warm eyes I'd missed.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc6.source_text: When I pulled it out, I gasped aloud. Edward looked just as beautiful as he did in real life, staring at me out of the picture with the warm eyes I'd missed for the past few days.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc6.description: I saw that one of Edward's pictures showed him watching ESPN with Charlie and that his expression there was careful and reserved.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc6.source_text: The second was Edward and Charlie, watching ESPN. The difference in Edward's expression was severe. His eyes were careful here, reserved.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc6.description: I realized that Edward's behavior had changed because he still hadn't come over and I couldn't remember the last time he'd stayed away without excuse.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc6.source_text: Edward still hadn't come over. I didn't want to admit that he was the reason I'd stayed up so late, but of course he was. I tried to remember the last time he'd stayed away like this, without an excuse, a phone call… He never had.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc6.description: I felt painfully aware of a gap between us when I noticed he looked godlike in the photo while I looked very average and almost shamefully plain.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc6.source_text: He looked like a god. I looked very average, even for a human, almost shamefully plain.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc6.description: I chose to fold the photograph of Edward and me and tuck it into my album with Edward's side up rather than display it openly.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc6.source_text: I folded it in half and stuck it under the metal tab, Edward-side up.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward told Bella that his family and himself are leaving Forks.
I learned that Edward explicitly said that Bella cannot go with them because the place they are going is not right for her.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc7.source_text: I quote: "You can't, Bella. Where we're going… It's not the right place for you."

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc7.description: I realized that Bella experiences Edward's statement that he does not want her to come as rejection and that this shifts her perception of their relationship.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc7.source_text: I quote: "Bella, I don't want you to come with me."

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc7.description: I changed my belief about Bella's willingness to sacrifice when I saw her declare that she would give her soul to remain with Edward.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc7.source_text: I quote: "You can have my soul. I don't want it without you—it's yours already!"

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc8.description: I learned that I had to keep moving because if I stopped looking for him it would mean my love, life, and meaning were over.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: I had to keep moving. If I stopped looking for him, it was over. Love, life, meaning… over.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc8.description: I learned that Sam Uley found me in the woods and that Charlie had sent someone to look for me.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: Bella, my name is Sam Uley. Charlie sent me to look for you.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc8.description: I learned that I was dazed, numb, and wet, and that rain woke me from a stupor while I lay on the bracken.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: I was just lost in an unthinking stupor, holding with all my strength to the numbness that kept me from realizing what I didn't want to know. The rain woke me up.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc8.description: I realized that Charlie mattered to me when I recognized his voice and clung to that recognition amid my disorientation.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: Charlie? That struck a chord, and I tried to pay more attention to what he was saying. Charlie mattered, if nothing else did.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc8.description: I noticed that Charlie carried me home and that people gathered with lanterns and voices to help me.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: I've got her! ... I'm right here, baby. We're almost home now, honey.

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc1.description: I learned that my father intends to send me to Renee in Jacksonville.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: "I'm sending you to Renee, to Jacksonville," he clarified.

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc1.description: I learned that my father perceives me as lifeless and accuses me of doing nothing.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: "You're just… lifeless, Bella. I think that's the word I want."

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc1.description: I feel that my relationship with my father is strained and that he is worried enough to consider drastic action.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: "I want you to be happy—no, not even that much. I just want you not to be miserable."

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc1.description: I insist that I am not waiting for anyone and that I do not expect anything from the absent person.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: "I'm not waiting for anything. I don't expect anything," I said in a low monotone.

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc1.description: I turned to academics as a coping mechanism and increased my time spent on Calculus dramatically.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: In the last several months, I'd spent ten times the amount of time on Calculus than I'd ever spent on math before.

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: I arranged to go to a movie with Jessica after school.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: "Do you have plans?" "No… I guess I can go with you. What do you want to see?"

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: I chose the zombie movie Dead End as the preferred film to see.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: "My dad just saw Dead End and he really liked it." "That sounds perfect."

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: I noticed a black garbage bag in my closet that held my present from my last birthday and could see the shape of the stereo inside.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: My eyes did not stray toward the black garbage bag that held my present from that last birthday, did not see the shape of the stereo where it strained against the black plastic;

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: I experienced a thick haze that blurred my days and caused me to lose track of the drive home and even opening the front door.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: The thick haze that blurred my days now was sometimes confusing. I was surprised when I found myself in my room, not clearly remembering the drive home from school or even opening the front door.

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: I preferred dealing with real zombies to watching a romance.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: "I'd rather deal with real zombies than watch a romance."

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: I used Jessica as a way to avoid Charlie and to change my routine.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: She was at least the first person I thought of when I wanted to avoid Charlie. after all, I was getting what I wanted—Charlie off my back.

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: I relied on keeping Jessica talking so I could manage with only a few mumbled responses.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: I knew from experience that once I got Jessica talking, I would be able to get away with a few mumbled responses at the appropriate moments.

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: I swiftly moved my wallet from my schoolbag into an old purse when Jess honked to hurry me.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: I swiftly traded my wallet from my schoolbag into the purse.

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.description: I scanned radio stations until I found one that felt harmless so I could avoid being distracted by the music.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: I scanned through the stations until I found one that was harmless.

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc3.description: I felt a senseless impulse to approach the four men on the street and I followed it despite not understanding why.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: It was a senseless impulse, but I hadn't felt any kind of impulse in so long… I followed it.

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc3.description: I experienced adrenaline returning to my body even though I lacked the usual fear and sensation.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: Something unfamiliar beat through my veins. Adrenaline, I realized, long absent from my system, drumming my pulse faster and fighting against the lack of sensation.

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc3.description: I remembered physical sensations from the prior attack that my mind could not clearly recall, including being addressed by a dark-haired man as "sugar."
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: the tension in my legs as I tried to decide whether to run or to stand my ground, the dryness in my throat as I struggled to build a decent scream, the tight stretch of skin across my knuckles as I clenched my hands into fists, the chills on the back of my neck when the dark-haired man called me "sugar."…

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc3.description: I realized that I was not suicidal because I felt responsible to Charlie and Renee and had promised not to do anything reckless.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: No, I'm not." My voice sounded defensive, but it was true. I wasn't suicidal. Even in the beginning, when death unquestionably would have been a relief, I didn't consider it. I owed too much to Charlie. I felt too responsible for Renee. I had to think of them.

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc3.description: I perceived Edward's voice as angry but caring and I interpreted that voice as concern when it told me to "Keep your promise."
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: "Go back to Jessica," the lovely voice ordered, still angry. "You promised—nothing stupid." "Keep your promise."

tw-book2-chapter4_Sc3.description: I suspected that the voice I heard might be a hallucination or my subconscious projecting what I wanted rather than Edward actually being present.
tw-book2-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: I began to suspect that I was having some kind of hallucination. Triggered, no doubt, by the memory—the deja vu, the strange familiarity of the situation. Option two: My subconscious mind was giving me what it thought I wanted.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc1.description: I heard Mike suggest that I take off from the store.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc1.source_text: "BELLA, WHY DON'T YOU TAKE OFF," MIKE SUGGESTED

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc1.description: I realized I hadn't been able to sink back into my protective shell of numbness and that everything seemed oddly close and loud.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc1.source_text: I still hadn't been able to sink back into my protective shell of numbness, and everything seemed oddly close and loud today, like I'd taken cotton out of my ears.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc1.description: I heard two dedicated backpackers arguing about a very large black bear sighting near the trailhead.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc1.source_text: "On all fours it was taller than you," the bearded man insisted while I gathered my things together.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc1.description: I noticed Mike trying to take care of me by murmuring he would close the place down if the hikers didn't leave and by engaging with their safety questions.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc1.source_text: "Seriously, Bella, as soon as these two give up, I'm closing the place down," Mike murmured.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc3.description: I noticed a hand-printed FOR SALE, AS IS sign and dilapidated motorcycles rusting in the Markses' front yard.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: the dilapidated motorcycles rusting in the Markses' front yard beside the hand-printed FOR SALE, AS IS sign were serving some higher purpose by existing there, right where I needed them to be.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc3.description: I had the Marks boy help me load both heavy bikes into the back of my truck in the downpour.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: He followed me out into the downpour and helped me load both of the heavy bikes into the back of my truck.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc3.description: I wanted to be stupid and reckless and to break promises that I had kept before, including the one about never riding motorcycles.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: I wanted to be stupid and reckless, and I wanted to break promises.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc3.description: I learned that the bikes didn't work and that the Marks family intended to have them removed with the garbage.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: If you really want one, just take it. My mom made my dad move them down to the road so they'd get picked up with the garbage.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc4.description: I learned the route to the Blacks' place from Charlie so I could visit Jacob.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc4.source_text: No. I just wanted directions to the Blacks' place—I'm not sure I can remember the way. I want to visit Jacob. I haven't seen him in months.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc4.description: I confirmed that I would be back for dinner even though Charlie tried to tell me not to hurry.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc4.source_text: I assured him that I would be back for dinner, though he tried to tell me not to hurry.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc4.description: I noticed that Charlie was pleased and supportive about my visiting Jacob and that he even offered to join me, which I refused.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc4.source_text: That's a great idea, Bells. Do you have a pen? ... He wanted to join me in La Push, and I wasn't having that.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc4.description: I decided I needed to get Jacob alone and I made plans to hurry to La Push to try to do so.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc4.source_text: I hoped I could get Jacob alone.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc4.description: I worried that Billy would be pleased to see me and I feared that he would tell on me, which would remind me of the one I could not bear to remember.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc4.source_text: Billy would probably tell on me if he knew what I was up to. ... His pleasure and relief would only remind me of the one I couldn't bear to be reminded of. Not again today, I pleaded silently.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc5.description: I learned that I liked my truck very much and that Jacob found its speed restrictions limiting.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc5.source_text: I liked my truck very much, but Jacob seemed to consider the speed restrictions a shortcoming.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc5.description: I learned that I needed to feed Charlie and that I used that as a reason to decline dinner.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc5.source_text: No, I've got to feed Charlie, you know.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc5.description: I felt an unfamiliar surge of enthusiasm at Jacob's smile and I realized that I was pleased to see him, which surprised me.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc5.source_text: I felt an unfamiliar surge of enthusiasm at his smile. I realized that I was pleased to see him. This knowledge surprised me.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc5.description: I remembered how much I really liked Jacob Black after something clicked silently into place between us.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc5.source_text: I smiled back, and something clicked silently into place, like two corresponding puzzle pieces. I'd forgotten how much I really liked Jacob Black.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc6.description: I learned that I recently acquired a couple of bikes that were not in the greatest condition.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc6.source_text: I recently acquired a couple of bikes, and they're not in the greatest condition.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc6.description: I felt a rare lightness and buoyancy that changed my usual mood and made it harder to manage my reactions.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc6.source_text: It was a long time since I'd felt so light and buoyant. The rarity of the feeling made it more difficult to manage.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc6.description: I decided to use some of my college fund to pay for parts and to deceive our parents in order to have Jacob help me.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc6.source_text: deceiving both our parents while repairing dangerous vehicles using money meant for my college education.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.description: I offered to pay to rebuild Jacob's motorcycles and to cover riding lessons so Jacob would supply labor and expertise.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: No way. I'm bankrolling this party. You just have to supply the labor and expertise. Not to mention the riding lessons, I added.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.description: I realized I was enjoying myself and felt unexpectedly light and happy while I laughed alone in the trees.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: I giggled quietly. The sound made my eyes widen in wonder. I was laughing, actually laughing, and there wasn't even anyone watching. I felt so weightless that I laughed again, just make the feeling last longer.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.description: I felt closer to Jacob and trusted his mechanical skills and judgment enough to let him handle the rebuilds.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: Jacob started pulling the first bike—the red one, which was destined for me—to pieces immediately. That would be great!

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.description: I cooked dinner for Charlie and I handled household chores and homework after returning from Jacob's shed.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: I beat Charlie home. When he walked in I was just taking the fried chicken out of the pan and laying it on a pile of paper towels. After dinner, I dithered around, cleaning the kitchen twice, and then did my homework slowly in the front room while Charlie watched a hockey game.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.description: I attended Billy's spaghetti dinner with friends and family after Charlie mentioned the invitation.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: "Billy invited us for dinner," Charlie said to us in an absentminded tone.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.description: I noticed increased closeness with Jacob when I felt his hand around mine and sensed Charlie's attention toward us.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: Charlie stared at me with wide eyes that flashed down to note Jacob's hand around mine.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.description: I felt guilty about my distant relationship with Renee after reading her long, journal-like letter and recognizing my own lack of responsiveness.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: Remorse flooded through me, leaving an uncomfortable sting behind. Some daughter I was.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.description: I stayed up late finishing homework and wrote a quick, detailed reply to Renee describing the spaghetti party and my feelings watching Jacob work.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: I wrote back to her quickly, commenting on each part of her letter, volunteering information of my own—describing the spaghetti party at Billy's and how I felt watching Jacob build useful things out of small pieces of metal—awed and slightly envious.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.description: I experienced recurring nightmares in which Sam Uley was present and watched me without offering help.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: Last night I had not been alone in the woods. Sam Uley—the man who had pulled me from the forest floor that night I couldn't bear to think of consciously—was there.
