tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.description: I recognized Charlie's continued protectiveness as he watched me cautiously at breakfast after my injury.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: Charlie stared at me during breakfast, and I tried to ignore him.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.description: I perceived that at school I faded into the background and that classmates and teachers did not seem to notice me.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: School was the opposite. Now that I was paying attention, it was clear that no one was watching here.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc4.description: I felt comforted by Jacob's embrace and I realized it felt like friendship, unlike the last time someone had embraced me.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: This didn't feel anything like the last time someone had embraced me this way. This was friendship.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc4.description: I offered Jacob that he could come live with me and Charlie if it gets worse and I took on a protective, caring role.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: If it gets worse you can come live with me and Charlie. Don't be scared, we'll think of something!

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc4.description: I noticed that Jacob was very warm during the hug and I registered the physical difference from other embraces.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc1.description: I noticed a strange sense of repetition and a coincidence of the date that made things feel like starting over.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: The other part was the strange sense of repetition I'd felt at school today, the coincidence of the date.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc1.description: I started to believe I was trying to punish myself by returning and that this was unhealthy.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: Was I trying to push myself back into the zombie stupor? Had I turned masochistic—developed a taste for torture? This was not a healthy thing to do.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc1.description: I knew that part of my compulsion came from a nightmare whose nothingness gnawed on my nerves.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: I knew that part of the reason I did this was the nightmare, now that I was really awake, the nothingness of the dream gnawed on my nerves, a dog worrying a bone.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc1.description: I felt much, much healthier around Jacob and regretted not going to La Push.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: I should have gone straight down to La Push I felt much, much healthier around Jacob

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc1.description: I believed he was out there somewhere and that I had to believe that.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: There was something to search for. Unattainable and impossible, uncaring and distracted… but he was out there, somewhere. I had to believe that.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc1.description: I feared being erased or forgotten, encapsulated by the thought 'It will be as if I'd never existed.'
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: It will be as if I'd never existed.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc2.description: I realized that my strongest motivation for coming was to hear his voice again.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc2.source_text: The truth was that I wanted to hear his voice again, like I had in the strange delusion Friday night.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc2.description: I admitted that I had been lying to myself by splitting my reason for coming into just two parts and changed my view of my own motives.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc2.source_text: I was lying to myself by splitting my reason for coming here into just two parts.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc2.description: I learned that hearing his voice in that delusion allowed me to remember without pain.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc2.source_text: For that brief moment, when his voice came from some other part of me than my conscious memory, when his voice was perfect and honey smooth rather than the pale echo my memories usually produced, I was able to remember without pain.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc3.description: I saw the meadow flooded with tall ferns crowding the trees and even the wide porch.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: The tall ferns had infiltrated the meadow around the house, crowding against the trunks of the cedars, even the wide porch.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc3.description: I felt that the house, which had once seemed beautiful, now looked like a fitting haunt for vampires.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: For the first time since I'd seen the beautiful house, it looked like a fitting haunt for vampires.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc3.description: I noticed that there was no voice in my head and no lingering sense of their presence.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: But nothing happened. No voice in my head. There was nothing here. No lingering sense of their presence… of his presence.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc3.description: I felt hideously empty and compared that emptiness to the numbness I had felt before and to my grandmother's funeral.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: I felt hideously empty, and I wanted to see Jacob. Maybe I was developing a new kind of sickness, another addiction, like the numbness before. Like my grandmother's funeral, when my mother had insisted that I stay outside during the viewing.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc3.description: I believed that everything might remain untouched and forgotten behind them, which made me feel left behind and abandoned.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: It would be second only to the house disappearing all together, to see that there was no physical possession that tied them in anyway. That everything remained, untouched and forgotten, behind them. Just like me.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.description: I felt immediate relief and easier breathing when I saw Jacob waiting for me.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I read, "My chest seemed to relax as soon as I saw him, making it easier to breathe."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.description: I saw that Jacob had fixed the red bike so it looked like a motorcycle rather than a pile of jagged metal.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I read, "When I walked into the garage, I was shocked to see the red bike standing up, looking like a motorcycle rather than a pile of jagged metal."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.description: I committed to continuing to come over to Jacob's place and to spend time with him despite my concerns about being a bother.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I read, "But as long as you let me come over, I'll be here."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob becomes obsessive when he has a project and that he admits this about himself.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I read, "I get obsessive when I have a project."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.description: I agreed with Jacob to add structure by doing homework together and I suggested increasing the frequency to twice a week.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I read, "Homework once a week?" he proposed. "Maybe we'd better go with twice," I suggested, thinking of the pile I'd just been assigned today.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.description: I embraced a playful balance of responsibility and recklessness in my time with Jacob, formalized by our soda toast.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I read, "Here's to responsibility," he toasted. "Twice a week." "And recklessness every day in between," I emphasized.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.description: I learned that Charlie had ordered a pizza when I arrived home late and that he refused my apology.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: I got home later than I'd planned and found Charlie had ordered a pizza rather than wait for me.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.description: I learned that Renee sent a long e-mail and that I replied with an exhaustive description of my day that omitted the motorcycles.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: I checked my e-mail before I started on my homework, and there was a long one from Renee. She gushed over every detail I'd provided her with, so I sent back another exhaustive description of my day. Everything but the motorcycles.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.description: I learned that Angela and Mike seemed ready to welcome me back while Jess was more resistant.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: Angela and Mike seemed ready to welcome me back with open arms—to kindly overlook my few months of aberrant behavior. Jess was more resistant.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.description: I learned that Mike was animated at work and that he suggested we see a non-scary movie together, implying it could be a date.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: Mike was animated and chatty at work. ... "We could go see something that isn't scary at all." ... "Like a date?" I asked.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.description: I decided to decline a date and to try to keep Mike as a friend by postponing because I had plans already.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: "That would be fun. But I actually have plans already this Friday, so maybe next week?"

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.description: I realized that I don't date and that that whole world seemed impossibly distant to me.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: "I don't date," I said slowly, realizing how true that was. That whole world seemed impossibly distant.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.description: I felt that I had come full circle and that my interactions now felt like an empty echo without the interest they used to have.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: I'd come full circle, and now everything felt like an echo—an empty echo, devoid of the interest it used to have.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.description: I noticed Charlie didn't seem the smallest bit surprised to find Jacob and me sprawled across the living room floor with our books scattered around us.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: Charlie didn't seem the smallest bit surprised to find Jacob and me sprawled across the living room floor with our books scattered around us, so I guessed that he and Billy were talking behind our backs.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.description: I learned that I had spent the afternoon making lasagna while Jacob watched and occasionally sampled and that Jacob stayed for dinner and took a plate home for Billy.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: The smell of the lasagna I'd spent the afternoon making—while Jacob watched and occasionally sampled—wafted down the hall; I was being good, trying to atone for all the pizza. Jacob stayed for dinner, and took a plate home for Billy.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.description: I felt very sensible and mature about our routine and about watching Monster Garage on TV.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: When he got back, we were all done—feeling very sensible and mature about it, too—and watching Monster Garage on the Discovery Channel.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.description: I tried to shake off a recurring Litest nightmare and shoved the dream out of my conscious mind.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: I cleaned the house the next morning—waiting for Jacob to call and trying to shake off the Litest nightmare. I shoved the dream out of my conscious mind, hoping it would stay locked up somewhere and not escape again.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.description: I heard Jacob say in a strange, formal tone, "I believe that… we have a date," and I learned that "they run and everything."
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: "Bella," Jacob said, a strange, formal tone to his voice. "I believe that… we have a date" ... "Yeah, they run and everything."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.description: I told Jacob he was the most talented and wonderful person I know and rewarded him verbally after his news.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: "Jacob, you are absolutely, without a doubt, the most talented and wonderful person I know. You get ten years for this one."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.description: I parked my truck off to the side of the Blacks' house, close to the trees, to make it easier for us to sneak the bikes out.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: I parked my truck off to the side of the Blacks' house, close to the trees, to make it easier for us to sneak the bikes out.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.description: I noticed two shiny motorcycles, one red and one black, hidden under a spruce and invisible from the house.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: When I got out, a splash of color caught my eye—two shiny motorcycles, one red, one black, were hidden under a spruce, invisible from the house.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.description: I noticed a piece of blue ribbon tied in a small bow around each of the handlebars.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: There was a piece of blue ribbon tied in a small bow around each of the handlebars.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.description: I watched Jacob load the bikes into the bed of the truck with ease, laying them carefully on their sides so they didn't show.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: Jacob loaded the bikes into the bed of the truck with ease, laying them carefully on their sides so they didn't show.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.description: I didn't feel quite as excited as before about going on the motorcycle and I found myself trying to imagine actually being on it.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: "Yeah," I said, but I didn't feel quite as excited as before; I was trying to imagine myself actually on the motorcycle.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.description: I drove south out of town on a dirt road that wound through forest and opened to a view of the Pacific Ocean from the sea cliffs.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: We drove south out of town. The dirt road wove in and out of the forest—sometimes there was nothing but trees, and then there would suddenly be a breathtaking glimpse of the Pacific Ocean, reaching to the horizon, dark gray under the clouds.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc8.description: I realized that the falling figures were cliff divers engaging in recreation rather than victims in need of rescue.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc8.source_text: "They're just cliff diving, Bella. Recreation. La Push doesn't have a mall, you know."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc8.description: I became surprised that Jacob could show irritation, which changed my belief that he was nearly impossible to upset.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc8.source_text: It surprised me a little. I would have thought Jacob was nearly impossible to upset.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc8.description: I asked Jacob to take me cliff diving, indicating my desire to share an adventurous activity with him and to be included in his world.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc8.source_text: "Jake, you have to take me cliff diving."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.description: I heard Jacob call the group "The La Push gang."
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: I heard Jacob say "The La Push gang."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.description: I heard that they ran a man from the Makah reservation off their land for selling meth to kids.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: I heard that "they ran him off our land" when Jacob described a meth seller being expelled.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.description: I heard that the council actually meets with Sam Uley, according to Embry's report.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: I heard Jacob say "the council actually meets with Sam" as something Embry mentioned.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.description: I noticed I view the protectors as annoyingly goody-two-shoes and showy tough guys after Jacob's description.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: I noticed Jacob call them "annoyingly goody-two-shoes" and say "They're always showing off—like the cliff thing."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.description: I remembered my nightmare and I began to suspect that the trio in my vision might have been members of Sam's group.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: I recalled thinking "Had that been Sam's gang?" when the nightmare image returned.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc10.description: I learned that Jacob feels the council favors his father because of family lineage and ancestral chiefs.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: It's just… the way they treat me. It creeps me out. "You know, the council is supposed to be made up of equals, but if there was a leader, it would be my dad. I've never been able to figure out why people treat him the way they do. Why his opinion counts the most. It's got something to do with his father and his father's father. My great-grandpa, Ephraim Black, was sort of the last chief we had, and they still listen to Billy, maybe because of that."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc10.description: I learned that Jacob feels overlooked by the council and that he resents inconsistent treatment of others like Sam and his sister.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: "Yeah. He was supposed to go to college, but he stayed. And no one gave him any crap about it, either. The whole council pitched a fit when my sister turned down a partial scholarship and got married. But, oh no, Sam Uley can do no wrong."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc10.description: I felt the motorcycle suddenly look intimidating and frightening when I realized I would soon be astride it.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: The bike suddenly looked intimidating, frightening, as I realized I would soon be astride it.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc10.description: I noticed Jacob acted protective and attentive when he gave me the bike and promised he would take it slow.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: "Happy late birthday. Are you ready for this?" ... "We'll take it slow," he promised.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.description: I learned that Sam pays more attention to Jacob than the other guys and that Jacob hates the attention.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.source_text: "He pays more attention to me than any of the other guys. I hate it."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.description: I learned that Embry had been avoiding Jacob, returned looking terrified, and then began hanging out with Sam and the others.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.source_text: "It's Embry. He's been avoiding me lately." "Then this week, out of nowhere, Embry's hanging out with Sam and the rest of them. He was out on the cliffs today."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.description: I felt selfish for realizing that I'd been monopolizing Jacob's time and attention.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.source_text: "You've been hanging out with me a lot," I reminded him, feeling selfish. I'd been monopolizing him.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.description: I embraced Jacob to comfort him and I offered him the option to come live with my family if the situation got worse, reinforcing my protective friendship.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.source_text: "I threw my arms around him instinctively, wrapping them around his waist and pressing my face against his chest." "If it gets worse you can come live with me and Charlie. Don't be scared, we'll think of something!"

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.description: I felt comforted by Jacob's contact and I understood the hug as friendship rather than romance.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.source_text: "We stood like that for a moment, and it didn't upset me; in fact, I felt comforted by the contact. This didn't feel anything like the last time someone had embraced me this way. This was friendship."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc1.description: I learned the locations and functions of the motorcycle controls, including the clutch on the left handlebar, the primary front brake operated by the right-hand lever, the throttle on the right grip, and the gearshift operated with the left foot.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: "I pointed to the lever on my left handlebar." "Behind my right foot." "He grabbed my right hand and curled my fingers around the lever over the throttle." "Throttle?" "Gearshift?"

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc1.description: I learned how the bike behaves when mishandled, including wobbling, bucking forward, and stalling when the clutch is released too quickly or the engine is choked.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: The heavy bike wobbled underneath me, threatening to knock me sidewise. "The bike bucked under me, yanking me forward and then collapsing to the ground half on top of me. The growling engine choked to a stop."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc1.description: I realized that surviving past trauma did not erase my physical fear response, because my stomach and voice betrayed intense anxiety despite my rational arguments.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: "I tried to tell myself that the fear was pointless. I'd already lived through the worst thing possible. In comparison with that, why should anything frighten me now? I should be able to look death in the face and laugh." "My stomach wasn't buying it."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc1.description: I began to believe that the hallucinated internal voice might be triggered by adrenaline, danger, or intense emotional states rather than by familiarity or deja vu.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: "There was no familiarity here—on a road I'd never seen, doing something I'd never done before—no deja vu So the hallucinations must be triggered by something else… I felt the adrenaline coursing through my veins again, and I thought I had the answer. Some combination of adrenaline and danger, or maybe just stupidity."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc1.description: I felt Jacob was patient, protective, and physically supportive while teaching me to ride, as he steadied the bike, guided my hands, and caught the motorcycle when it threatened to fall.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: "He wrapped his hand around mine and made me squeeze the lever down." "He put his hand on the back of the seat, too, just to be safe." "Jacob jerked the heavy bike off me with ease."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc2.description: I learned that I started and rode a motorcycle, crashed, and sustained a bleeding cut on my forehead.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: I quoted: "It took several good tries, and even more poor tries, before the engine caught and roared to life under me... The motorcycle landed on top of me again, roaring loudly, pulling me across the wet sand until it hit something stationary... I clapped my hand over my head. Sure enough, it was wet and sticky."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc2.description: I began to believe that the experience might be a hallucination caused by adrenaline and shock.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: I noted: "This had to be it, the recipe for a hallucination—adrenaline plus clanger plus stupidity."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc2.description: I trusted Jacob to protect me, to drive me to safety, and to help avoid getting me in trouble with Charlie.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: I observed: "He wrapped a long arm around my waist and pulled me to my feet... 'Let's just take the bikes back first, and then we'll make a stop at my house so I can dispose of the evidence before we go to the hospital.'"

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc2.description: I felt envious of Jacob's athletic ease and skill while he started and rode the motorcycle.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: I remembered: "He looked athletic and professional as he leaned over the handlebars, head low, face forward, his shiny hair whipping against the russet skin of his back. My eyes narrowed enviously."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.description: I learned that I required seven stitches for a cut on my forehead and that a doctor warned my father I might possibly have a concussion.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: I had to have seven stitches to c lose the cut on my forehead.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.source_text_full: Dr. Gerandy called to warn my father that I might possibly have a concussion and advised him to wake me up every two hours through the night to make sure it wasn't serious.

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.description: I felt that being with Jacob would make me feel better and that his presence eased the emptiness that follows my episodes.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: Also, I knew I would feel better tomorrow when I was with Jacob again.

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.description: I noticed that I was hiding details from Charlie and that Charlie was becoming suspicious about my explanations for injuries.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: Charlie's eyes narrowed suspiciously at my weak explanation about tripping again.

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.description: I realized that I planned to go to the meadow that I associated with Edward because I believed it would make him feel more real to me.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: The beautiful meadow I'd seen only once in my life, lit by sunshine and the sparkle of his skin.

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob navigates with skill using a compass and a map.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: "He held the compass in a skilled way, twisting the map around till it angled the way he wanted."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.description: I learned that Embry is still with Sam and has not 'come back to normal.'
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: "No. He's not back to normal," Jacob said ... "Still with Sam."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.description: I found that it wasn't as hard as I had expected to keep focused on the present when Jacob set a different mood.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: It wasn't as hard as I would have thought to keep focused on the present. The forest looked a lot like any other part of the peninsula, and Jacob set a vastly different mood.

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.description: I noticed that Jacob was patient with my slow pace and that he didn't complain about being slowed down.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: I could tell that I was slowing Jacob up, but he didn't complain.

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.description: I discovered that my new boots were causing many blisters and that I was feeling sore from the hike.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: I bet you can feel those new boots right now. It felt like I had more blisters than I had space to fit them.

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.description: I found the truck at the edge of the trail and I agreed to try the search again the next day.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: "On the other side was the truck." ... "So you up for another try tomorrow?' he asked ... 'Sure.'

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.description: I felt cared for when Jacob put his arm around my shoulder and I did not push him away because he looked troubled.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: "He put his arm around my shoulder, and he looked so troubled that I didn't playfully shake it off, as I might have otherwise."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.description: I noticed that Jacob used teasing humor about bears and about how I might 'taste,' which lightened the mood.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: "I hope we see the bear tomorrow. I'm sort of disappointed about that." ... 'Of course, you might be an exception. I bet you'd taste good.'

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.description: I noticed I settled into a routine of school, work, and Jacob that felt neat and effortless.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: School, work, and Jacob—though not necessarily in that order—created a neat and effortless pattern to follow.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.description: I felt less miserable and realized I couldn't completely fool myself about the implications of my behavior.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: And Charlie got his wish: I wasn't miserable anymore. Of course, I couldn't fool myself completely. When I stopped to take stock of my life, which I tried not to do too often, I couldn't ignore the implications of my behavior.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.description: I observed that I was getting better with my bike, which meant fewer bandages and coincided with the voice in my head beginning to fade.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: I was getting better with my bike, which meant fewer bandages to worry Charlie. But it also meant that the voice in my head began to fade, until I heard it no more.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.description: I panicked quietly when the voice in my head disappeared and threw myself into the search for the meadow with frenzied intensity.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: Quietly, I panicked. I threw myself into the search for the meadow with slightly frenzied intensity.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.description: I stopped keeping track of the days and tried to live as much in the present as possible to avoid dwelling on past or future.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: I didn't keep track of the days :hat passed—there was no reason, as I tried to live as much in the present as possible, no past fading, no future impending.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.description: I felt connected to Jacob in an odd way and noticed his pain produced little stabs of my own, making me avoid hurting him.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: I couldn't stand hurting Jacob; we seemed to be connected in an odd way, and his pain set off little stabs of my own.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned that Ben called to say Angela was sick with the stomach flu and that they would not be coming.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: It was Ben. Angela was sick with the stomach flu, and he didn't feel like coming without her. He apologized for bailing on us.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned that I (Bella) do not like music and that the lack of music was noted by Jacob in the car.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: "Yes," Jacob answered. "But Bella doesn't like music.""I shrugged. "I don't know. It just irritates me."

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.description: I admitted to myself that I felt selfishly upset about Ben and Angela bailing on the evening.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: I really hoped Angela would feel better soon, but I had to admit that I was selfishly upset by this development.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.description: I realized that I enjoyed being with Jacob a lot and that enjoyment made me worry about the blurring lines in our relationship.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: How was I ever going to fight the blurring lines in our relationship when I enjoyed being with him so much?

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.description: I decided to follow Mike when he bolted from the theater to make sure he was okay and told him to stay while offering to check on him.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: Mike groaned again, and bolted for the door. I got up to follow him, and Jacob copied me immediately. "No, stay," I whispered. "I'll make sure he's okay."

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc4.description: I learned that I admit liking Jacob more than other guys and even the girls around me.
I noticed that I whispered 'Yes' when Jacob asked if I liked him, indicating I accepted my feeling for him in that moment.
I realized that I value being with Jacob and I told him I couldn't imagine not liking being with him while also warning him not to expect more.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc4.source_text: "I can't imagine how I could not like being with you" and "Just don't expect more," I warned him.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc4.description: I observed that I feel physically colder than usual and I found Jacob's hand noticeably warmer and comforting.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc4.source_text: "Truthfully, it felt nice. His hand was so much warmer than mine; I always felt too cold these days."

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc4.description: I noticed that Jacob traced the scar from James on my hand and murmured that it was cold while his presence often kept me whole.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc4.source_text: "That's a funny scar you've got there," he suddenly said... "It's cold," he murmured... "But, as it so often did, Jacob's presence kept me whole."

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob arrived home but was too sick to call.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc5.source_text:
"He\'s here," Billy said tonelessly.
"He was… too sick to call. He\'s not feeling well right now."

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc5.description: I learned that I had the same stomach flu as Mike and that my twenty-four hours were up.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc5.source_text:
"Stomach flu," he finally said.
"My twenty-four hours were up."

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc5.description: I became more worried rather than reassured even after being told Jacob had made it home.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc5.source_text: "Well, at least he\'d made it home. Oddly, I didn\'t feel less worried."

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc5.description: I noticed that Billy sounded distant and nearly rude when he told me to stay at my place.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc5.source_text: "The way he said it was almost rude."

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc5.description: I viewed Charlie as caring and practical because he left water for me, carried me to my room, and called to check on Mike\'s condition.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc5.source_text:
"He left a glass of water on the floor beside me to keep me hydrated."
"Charlie must have carried me to my room—he'd also put the glass of water on my bedside table."

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc6.description: I discovered that I had been sick earlier but I was fine now.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc6.source_text: Yes, I got it, too. But I'm fine now.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc6.description: I felt guilty for making Jacob go out with me.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc6.source_text: I'm so sorry I made you go out with me. This sucks.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob was experiencing intense, pervasive pain.
I noticed Jacob became abrupt and distant, which changed how I felt about our immediate relationship.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc6.source_text: He was abrupt. It reminded me of Billy the other night.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob sent an angry written reply to my pleading note that was passed via Charlie to Billy to him.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: His answer to my pleading note — passed from Charlie to Billy to him, just like second grade, as he’d pointed out — was no surprise.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.description: I learned that I had already known the essential content of Jacob’s reply before I opened it.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: I’d known the essence of what it would say before I’d opened it.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.description: I realized that Jacob’s pain affected me more deeply than I expected and cut me deeper than my own hurt.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: More than that, behind each angry beginning lurked a vast pool of hurt; Jacob’s pain cut me deeper than my own.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.description: I noticed physical evidence on the paper that Jacob had pressed the pen so hard it nearly broke and that ink splatters suggested frustration.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: I ran my fingers across the page, feeling the dents where he had pressed the pen to the paper so hard that it had nearly broken through.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.description: I understood that Jacob stated he could not be friends with me because of my associations and choices.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: We can’t be friends when you’re spending all your time with a bunch of

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc2.description: I smelled a smoking burner and found the jar of spaghetti sauce in the microwave.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: While I was pondering this, I caught the unmistakable scent of a smoking burner rising from the kitchen.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc2.description: I removed the lid from the jar and transferred sauce to a bowl because metal is bad for microwaves.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: “You’re supposed to take the lid off first, Dad. Metal’s bad for microwaves.” I swiftly removed the lid as I spoke, poured half the sauce into a bowl, and then put the bowl inside the microwave and the jar back in the fridge; I fixed the time and pressed start.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc2.description: I tried to de-clump the mushy, scalded pasta on the stove while stirring and answering Charlie's questions.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: I looked in the pan on the stove — the source of the smell that had alerted me. “Stirring helps,” I said mildly. I found a spoon and tried to de-clump the mushy hunk that was scalded to the bottom.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc2.description: I noticed Charlie's badge and jacket as he hung them up, and I saw his gun belt already slung in place.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: “You would know,” I replied, grinning as I eyed the badge pinned to his leather jacket. He shrugged out of the jacket as if my glance had reminded him he still had it on, and hung it on the peg reserved for his gear. His gun belt was already slung in place — he hadn’t felt the need to wear that to the station for a few weeks.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc2.description: I felt uneasy and rejected the word 'fiancée' as a label for my relationship because it made me tense.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: The wordboyfriend had me chewing on the inside of my cheek with a familiar tension while I stirred. It wasn’t the right word, not at all. I needed something more expressive of eternal commitment. . . . But words likedestiny andfate sounded hokey when you used them in casual conversation. Edward had another word in mind, and that word was the source of the tension I felt. It put my teeth on edge just to think it to myself. Fiancée. Ugh. I shuddered away from the thought.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc2.description: I glanced at the clock routinely and noted there was less than half an hour remaining.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: I glanced at the clock routinely — something I did every few minutes around this time. Less than a half hour to go now.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc3.description: I learned that my father limited Edward's visits to seven till nine-thirty p.m. inside the house under his supervision.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: Ever since my former best friend (and werewolf), Jacob Black, had informed on me about the motorcycle I’d been riding on the sly — a betrayal he had devised in order to get me grounded so that I couldn’t spend time with my boyfriend (and vampire), Edward Cullen — Edward had been allowed to see me only from seven till nine-thirty p.m., always inside the confines of my home and under the supervision of my dad’s unfailingly crabby glare.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc3.description: I know that Edward can climb easily and silently through my second-story window and that he can read my dad's mind.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: Edward's ability to climb easily and silently through my second-story window was almost as useful as his ability to read Charlie's mind.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc3.description: I know that I still see Edward at school and that he spends almost every night in my room despite my father's restrictions.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: Of course, I still saw Edward at school, because there wasn’t anything Charlie could do about that. And then, Edward spent almost every night in my room, too, but Charlie wasn’t precisely aware of that.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc3.description: I have accepted that I earned the grounding and that I cannot bear to move out now because I would hurt my dad when a more permanent separation feels imminent.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: Still, I endured my punishment without complaining because — for one thing — I knew I’d earned it, and — for another — because I couldn’t bear to hurt my dad by moving out now, when a much more permanent separation hovered, invisible to Charlie, so close on my horizon.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc3.description: I now consider Jacob my former best friend and feel betrayed by his informing on me about the motorcycle.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: Ever since my former best friend (and werewolf), Jacob Black, had informed on me about the motorcycle I’d been riding on the sly — a betrayal he had devised in order to get me grounded so that I couldn’t spend time with my boyfriend (and vampire), Edward Cullen —

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc4.description: I wrenched the door out of my way and I saw Edward there as my personal miracle, feeling ridiculously eager.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: I wrenched the door out of my way — ridiculously eager — and there he was, my personal miracle.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc4.description: I felt guilty for even imagining that Edward's perfection cost a soul and I was glad that my thoughts were a mystery to him.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: No. I didn’t believe that. I felt guilty for even thinking it, and was glad — as I was often glad — that I was the one person whose thoughts were a mystery to Edward.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc4.description: I reached for his hand and I felt relief when his cold fingers found mine and I understood our touch soothed me.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: I reached for his hand, and sighed when his cold fingers found mine. His touch brought with it the strangest sense of relief — as if I’d been in pain and that pain had suddenly ceased.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc4.description: I knew that the scent of my blood was much sweeter to him and that it caused him actual pain from the burning thirst it engendered.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: I knew that the scent of my blood — so much sweeter to him than any other person’s blood, truly like wine beside water to an alcoholic — caused him actual pain from the burning thirst it engendered.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc4.description: I heard Edward tell me that he had brought another set of applications and I noticed he was holding up a stuffed manila envelope.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: “I brought another set of applications,” Edward told me then, holding up a stuffed manila envelope.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc5.description: I learned that I received an acceptance to the University of Alaska.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc5.source_text: I just gotmy acceptance to the University of Alaska!

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc5.description: I learned that I have a curfew on school nights set to ten -thirty.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc5.source_text: Right. Okay,ten -thirty. You still have a curfew on school nights.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc5.description: I noticed that I moved Wuthering Heights to the counter while we prepared forms.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc5.source_text: When I moved Wuthering Heights to the counter, Edward raised one eyebrow.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc5.description: I realized that I was no longer grounded but that the freedom was conditional.
I noticed that Edward was playful and supportive with me about my college decision.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc5.source_text: Edward turned his face slightly to the side so that he could wink at me. I stifled a giggle.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc6.description: I know my transformation date is tentatively set for shortly after my high school graduation.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc6.source_text: I’d already won this argument. The date for my transformation was tentatively set for shortly after my graduation from high school, only a handful of weeks away.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc6.description: I have been accepted in Alaska and I can almost afford the first semester's tuition.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc6.source_text: I really don’t need to apply anywhere else. I’ve been accepted in Alaska. I can almost afford the first semester’s tuition.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc6.description: I believe it is too dangerous to attend college in person because of newborn vampires and the Volturi threat.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc6.source_text: It’s just too dangerous to mess around with.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc6.description: I realize Jacob would know exactly what was going on when I disappeared and that his revulsion would hurt me more than my parents' suspicion.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc6.source_text: And Jacob, who, unlike my parents, would know exactly what was going on when I disappeared to some distant school.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc7.description: I read five names in the paper and understood they were real victims of murder with grieving families.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc7.source_text: The five people whose lives were over, whose families were mourning now. . . . Maureen Gardiner, Geoffrey Campbell, Grace Razi, Michelle O’Connell, Ronald Albrook.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc7.description: I felt certain that Edward would not let me become like the victims and I entertained fleeing to remote Alaska or Antarctica.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc7.source_text: “It won’t be the same for me,” I whispered, half to myself. “You won’t let me be like that. We’ll live in Antarctica.”

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc7.description: I recognized Jacob as my best friend and I felt responsible for his hurting, believing I owed him my help.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc7.source_text:
“He was my best friend, Edward,” I muttered. “Of course the idea offends me.”
“Charlie says Jake is having a hard time. He’s hurting right now, and . . . it’s my fault.”

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc8.description: I now believe that the vampires' presence may have triggered the return of the werewolves rather than my personal bad luck doing so.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc8.source_text: I quote: "The werewolves came back because the vampires did."

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc8.description: I recognize that I owe Jacob his life many times over and that I feel indebted to him for preserving my sanity.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc8.source_text: I quote: "I knew I must be patient with Edward. It wasn’t that he was unreasonable, it was just that he didn’t understand. He had no idea how very much I owed Jacob Black — my life many times over, and possibly my sanity, too."

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc8.description: I learned that werewolves and vampires began crossing paths about seventy years ago and that Carlisle negotiated a truce with Ephraim Black.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc8.source_text: I quote: "We started crossing paths with the wolves about seventy years ago. . . . Carlisle. He managed to convince Ephraim Black that coexisting was possible, and eventually we made the truce."

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: I know I was told that I would be safe with Edward nearby.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: "I won’t be far away. You’ll be safe."

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: I felt my irritation at Edward leaving shift toward reassurance after he promised to stay close.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: "I won’t be far away. You’ll be safe."

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: I learned that my planned transformation timing is tied to graduation.
I noticed Jacob's protectiveness and teasing toward me, which affected how I experienced his visits.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: "I’ll just be a minute." and "By the way, your room reeks."

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc2.description: I learned that I apparently received a Dartmouth acceptance envelope in the mail.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc2.source_text: "Dartmouth? Is this a joke?" "I’m sure it’s an acceptance. It looks exactly like mine."

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc2.description: I felt reassured that Edward intends to protect me and insisted that no one will hurt me.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc2.source_text: "No one is going to hurt you. You have all the time in the world."

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc2.description: I noticed that I have a close, teasing, and complicated friendship with Jacob who invites me to social events and shows physical affection.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc2.source_text: "Thanks, Bella," he said, and then he grabbed my hand and wrenched me into one of his bone-crushing hugs." "do you think you can come to La Push tonight? We’re having a bonfire party. Emily will be there, and you could meet Kim . . . And I know Quil wants to see you, too."

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: I learned that Charlie had no problem with me going to La Push for a bonfire.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: To no one’s surprise, Charlie had no problem at all with me going to La Push for a bonfire.

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward asked me to allow him to drive me to the boundary line and to take a cell phone so he would know when to pick me up.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: I hope you won’t mind taking a few precautions? Allowing me to drive you to the boundary line, for one. And then taking a cell phone, so that I’ll know when to pick you up?

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: I felt conflicted and more eager to escape the surrounding danger for a few hours by spending time with Jacob despite the risks.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: I wanted to escape the death threats, for just a few hours . . . to be the less-mature, more-reckless Bella who could laugh it off with Jacob, if only briefly.

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: I decided that I would not sell my motorcycle and that I would take it back to La Push where it belonged, with the intention that Jacob could later profit from it.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: I had decided, after a short internal debate, that I would not sell my motorcycle. I would take it back to La Push where it belonged and, when I no longer needed it anymore . . . well, then, I would insist that Jacob profit from his work somehow. He could sell it or give it to a friend.

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc4.description: I struggled to get free from Jacob's hug while I heard the Volvo's engine growl.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc4.source_text: I heard the Volvo’s engine growl, and I struggled to get free.

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc4.description: I let some sarcasm into my tone when I commented "Nice," revealing my irritation.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc4.source_text: “Nice,” I commented, allowing some acid to leak into my voice.

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc4.description: I tried to see Jacob's joke as he walked around the Rabbit to hold my door open for me, showing I was trying to interpret his teasing more charitably.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc4.source_text: I tried to see the joke as he walked around the Rabbit to hold my door open for me.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: I noticed Jacob leaned back against my knees and toyed with the hot dog he had spitted on a straightened wire hanger.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: Jacob leaned back against my knees and toyed with the hot dog he had spitted on a straightened wire hanger; the flames at the edge of the bonfire licked along its blistered skin.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob had eaten many hot dogs plus a super-sized bag of chips and a two-liter bottle of root beer, yet his stomach stayed flat.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: He heaved a sigh and patted his stomach. It was somehow still flat, though I’d lost count of how many hot dogs he’d eaten after his tenth. Not to mention the super-sized bag of chips or the two-liter bottle of root beer.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: I worried that hanging out with no one but extremely dexterous people all the time was going to give me a complex.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: Hanging out with no one but extremely dexterous people all the time was going to give me a complex.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: I realized I had completely lost track of time and that the sun had set while we sat by the bonfire.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: Funny, I hadn’t noticed that the sun had set. For the first time, I wondered how late it had gotten. I’d lost track of time completely.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: I felt it was easier being with my Quileute friends than I had expected.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: It was easier being with my Quileute friends than I’d expected.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: I began to worry I'd be considered a traitor for showing up with Jacob.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: I’d started to worry about showing up with him at the bonfire — wondering if the werewolves would consider me a traitor now.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: I learned Jacob and I had dropped off my bike at the garage and that he admitted ruefully the helmet was a good idea.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: Jacob and I had dropped off my bike at the garage — and he had admitted ruefully that the helmet was a good idea that he should have thought of himself —

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: I noticed Jacob towed me out of the forest to the clifftop meeting place.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: But when Jacob had towed me out of the forest to the clifftop meeting place — where the fire already roared brighter than the cloud-obscured sun —

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: I heard Embry greet me loudly as 'Hey, vampire girl!'
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: “Hey, vampire girl!” Embry had greeted me loudly.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: I noticed Quil jumped up to give me a high five and kiss me on the cheek.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: Quil had jumped up to give me a high five and kiss me on the cheek.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: I noticed Emily squeezed my hand when we sat on the cool stone ground beside her and Sam.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: Emily had squeezed my hand when we’d sat on the cool stone ground beside her and Sam.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: I felt treated like someone who belonged despite teasing complaints about keeping the bloodsucker stench downwind.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: Other than a few teasing complaints — mostly by Paul — about keeping the bloodsucker stench downwind, I was treated like someone who belonged.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: I learned that Billy attended the council and that his wheelchair was stationed at what seemed the natural head of the circle.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: Billy was here, his wheelchair stationed at what seemed the natural head of the circle.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: I learned that Old Quil sat beside Billy on a folding lawn chair and that he looked brittle and elderly.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: Beside him on a folding lawn chair, looking quite brittle, was Quil’s ancient, white-haired grandfather, Old Quil.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: I learned that Sue Clearwater appeared to have taken Harry's place on the council based on how Billy and Old Quil spoke to her.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: From the way Billy and Old Quil spoke to Sue, it sounded to me like she’d taken Harry’s place on the council.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: I was surprised to realize that Sue and her children Leah and Seth were now in on the secret.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: This surprised me, but all three were clearly in on the secret now.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: I compared Leah’s perfect features to Emily’s ruined face and I wondered what Leah thought of Emily’s scars now that she knew the truth.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: Looking at the perfection of Leah’s features, I couldn’t help but compare them to Emily’s ruined face. What did Leah think of Emily’s scars, now that she knew the truth behind them?

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: I noticed that Little Seth Clearwater had a huge, happy grin and a long, gangly build that reminded me very much of a younger Jacob.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: Little Seth Clearwater wasn’t so little anymore. With his huge, happy grin and his long, gangly build, he reminded me very much of a younger Jacob.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: I worried that Seth might be doomed to have his life change as drastically as the rest of these boys and I questioned whether that was why his family was allowed to be there.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: Was Seth doomed to have his life change as drastically as the rest of these boys? Was that future why he and his family were allowed to be here?

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: I learned that the whole pack was present and I took note of the members named together with who they were paired with.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: The whole pack was there: Sam with his Emily, Paul, Embry, Quil, and Jared with Kim, the girl he’d imprinted upon.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: I formed a first impression of Kim as a nice, a little shy, and a little plain girl with a wide face and small eyes.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: My first impression of Kim was that she was a nice girl, a little shy, and a little plain. She had a wide face, mostly cheekbones, with eyes too small to balance them out. Her nose and mouth were both too broad for traditional beauty. Her flat black hair was thin and wispy in the wind that never seemed to let up atop the cliff.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc4.description: I observed Jared's stare and learned that imprinting can manifest as an overwhelming, reverent gaze.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: The way he stared at her! It was like a blind man seeing the sun for the first time. Like a collector finding an undiscovered Da Vinci, like a mother looking into the face of her newborn child.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc4.description: I noticed physical details about Kim that I had not seen before because Jared's attention made them obvious to me.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: His wondering eyes made me see new things about her — how her skin looked like russet-colored silk in the firelight, how the shape of her lips was a perfect double curve, how white her teeth were against them, how long her eyelashes were, brushing her cheek when she looked down.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc4.description: I better understood imprinting and came to believe it is a powerful, hard-to-resist level of commitment and adoration.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: Watching them, I felt like I better understood what Jacob had told me about imprinting before —it’s hard to resist that level of commitment and adoration.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc4.description: I gained increased empathy for Jacob's explanations after seeing imprinting in action and trusted his description more.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: Watching them, I felt like I better understood what Jacob had told me about imprinting before —it’s hard to resist that level of commitment and adoration.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc6.description: I observed that Bella Swan was present during the telling of the Taha Aki and Utlapa legend.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc6.source_text: Characters present: Billy, Old Quil, Bella Swan, Jacob Black, Quil, Sam

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc7.description: I realized the circle around the dying fire consisted of descendants of Taha Aki.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc7.source_text: the circle was made up of Taha Aki’s great — to however many degrees — grandsons.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc7.description: I learned that some of Taha Aki's sons became warriors with him and no longer aged.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc7.source_text: Some of the sons became warriors with Taha Aki, and they no longer aged.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc7.description: I learned that those who gave up their spirit wolves began to age again and could grow old like anyone else.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc7.source_text: These began to age again, and the tribe discovered that the wolf-men could grow old like anyone else if they gave up their spirit wolves.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc7.description: I learned that Taha Aki chose to give up his spirit wolf so he would die when his true spirit wife did.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc7.source_text: He decided to give up his spirit wolf so that he would die when she did.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.description: I learned that the Quileute wolves could still read each other’s thoughts while in their wolf forms.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.source_text: The wolf-men could still read each other’s thoughts while in their wolf forms, just like their ancestors had while in their spirit forms.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.description: I learned that the wolves followed a strange, sweet scent in the forest that burned their noses to the point of pain.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.source_text: They came across something they had never encountered before — a strange, sweet scent in the forest that burned their noses to the point of pain.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.description: I learned that Yaha Uta returned carrying a strange, cold, stony corpse in pieces.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.source_text: Only one came back. He was Yaha Uta, the oldest son of Taka Aki’s third wife, and the youngest in the pack. He brought something with him that had never been seen in all the days of the Quileutes — a strange, cold, stony corpse that he carried in pieces.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.description: I learned that the severed pieces of the creature could reach for each other and try to reassemble, which horrified the elders.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.source_text: One severed hand lay beside a piece of the creature’s granite arm. The two pieces touched when the elders poked them with sticks, and the hand reached out towards the arm piece, trying to reassemble itself.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.description: I learned that the elders burned the creature’s remains, spread the ashes far and wide, and that Taha Aki kept a bag of ashes around his neck as a warning.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.source_text: Horrified, the elders set fire to the remains. A great cloud of choking, vile smoke polluted the air. When there was nothing but ashes, they separated the ashes into many small bags and spread them far and wide — some in the ocean, some in the forest, some in the cliff caverns. Taha Aki wore one bag around his neck, so he would be warned if the creature ever tried to put himself together again.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.description: I felt more afraid of the Cold Ones after hearing that the creature was hard as granite, cold as ice, and had glowing red eyes and blood on its lips.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.source_text: Yaha Uta described what had happened: he and his brothers had found the creature, who looked like a man but was hard as a granite rock, with the two Makah daughters. One girl was already dead, white and bloodless on the ground. The other was in the creature’s arms, his mouth at her throat. She may have been alive when they came upon the hideous scene, but the creature quickly snapped her neck and tossed her lifeless body to the ground when they approached. His white lips were covered in her blood, and his eyes glowed red.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.description: I noticed Jacob’s arm tighten around me and his mouth twitch with humor, which made me feel closer to him during the story.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.source_text: I shrank a little closer to Jacob’s side. I saw the corner of his mouth twitch with humor, and his arm tightened around me.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc9.description: I learned that the Quileutes called the vampire a Cold One and feared that it might not be alone.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc9.source_text: I quote: "They called it The Cold One, the Blood Drinker, and lived in fear that it was not alone."

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc9.description: I learned that Taha Aki's third wife deliberately sacrificed herself by plunging a knife into her heart to distract the Cold Woman.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc9.source_text: I quote: "And then the third wife did something the Cold Woman did not expect. She fell to her knees at the blood drinker’s feet and plunged the knife into her own heart."

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc9.description: I learned that Yaha Uta, Taha Aki, and their sons transformed into spirit wolves to fight the cold ones and that the pack knowledge was transmitted across generations.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc9.source_text: I quote: "Yaha Uta transformed into his spirit wolf as soon as he heard the news."

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc9.description: I felt a new appreciation for the danger the Cold Ones posed and for the personal cost borne by the tribe's defenders.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc9.source_text: I quote: "Taha Aki never rejoined the tribe. He never changed back to a man again. He lay for one day beside the body of the third wife, growling whenever anyone tried to touch her, and then he went into the forest and never returned."

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc10.description: I learned that an unnamed third wife saved the entire tribe and that she was described as just a human woman with no special gifts or powers.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc10.source_text: I was trying to imagine the face of the unnamed woman who had saved the entire tribe, the third wife.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc10.description: I felt growing admiration for the human woman's pivotal role and I wished the tribe had remembered her name.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc10.source_text: I wish they’d remembered her name. . . .

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc10.description: I noticed Leah Clearwater's eyes were closed and I thought I saw something sparkle on her cheek like a tear before it vanished.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc10.source_text: Leah Clearwater’s eyes did not open. I thought I saw something sparkling on her cheek like a tear, but when I looked back a moment later it was gone.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.description: I realized that I had fallen asleep and that I was in Jacob’s car rather than on the cliff.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.source_text: How did I get in Jacob’s car?

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.description: I discovered that it was not even midnight yet and that Jacob had already called Edward for me.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.source_text: Easy. It’s not even midnight yet. And I already called him for you. Look — he’s waiting there.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.description: I patted my pockets and could not find my phone until Jacob put a small shape into my hand.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.source_text: "Dang it, where’s that stupid phone?" "Here," Jacob said, and he put a small shape into my other hand. The phone.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.description: I felt touched and more positively toward Jacob after he called Edward for me and handed me the phone.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.source_text: "I figured if I played nice, I’d get more time with you." "Thanks, Jake," I said, touched.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.description: I appreciated Jacob’s company and felt that my presence had meant something to him.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.source_text: No, I’m glad you liked it. It was . . . nice for me. Having you there.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.description: I promised Jacob I would come back soon when he asked me to.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.source_text: "Go ahead. But come back soon, okay?" Jacob said, noticing my distraction.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.description: I learned Jacob said he would be watching out for me that night.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.source_text: "Sleep tight, Bells. Don’t worry about anything — I’ll be watching out for you tonight."

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.description: I felt the outing was amazing and I wished Edward could have gone because the legends felt like magic.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.source_text: "Yeah — it was amazing, Edward. I wish you could have come. I can’t even explain it. Jake’s dad told us the old legends and it was like . . . like magic."

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.description: I noticed Edward met me at the boundary and hugged me tightly with relief in his voice.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.source_text: "Bella," he said, relief strong in his voice; his arms wound tightly around me.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.description: I observed Edward open my car door, lift me in, and buckle my seat belt for me.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.source_text: Edward chuckled. He opened my door for me, lifted me in, and buckled my seat belt around me.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc13.description: I waited at my open window while I waited for Edward to come back.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc13.source_text: I leaned out the open window while I waited for Edward to come back.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc13.description: I felt icy droplets spatter against my face as the rain began to fall.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc13.source_text: Icy droplets spattered against my face as the rain began to fall.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc13.description: I dreamed that I held a long, sharp blade that was ancient and silver and crusted in dried, blackened blood.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc13.source_text: I held a long, sharp blade, ancient and silver, crusted in dried, blackened blood.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc13.description: I realized that sitting next to Jacob on the windy cliffs had kept me from noticing the cold.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc13.source_text: I hadn’t noticed it at all on the windy cliffs; I imagined that had less to do with the fire than it did with sitting next to Jacob.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc13.description: I believed that Edward's scent and warmth would chase my nightmares away more effectively than anything else.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc13.source_text: I turned to bury my face in Edward’s chest, knowing the sweet scent of his skin would chase the nightmare away more effectively than anything else.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc1.description: I agreed to attend the graduation party when Alice told me about it.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: Okay, Alice. I’ll be there. And I’ll hate every minute of it. Promise.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc1.description: I decided I will hate every minute of the party.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: Okay, Alice. I’ll be there. And I’ll hate every minute of it. Promise.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc1.description: I realized Alice already had a gift and said she loved it.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: By the way, I love my gift. You shouldn't have.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc1.description: I felt panic trying to remember what I’d decided to get her for graduation.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: I racked my brains in panic, trying to remember what I’d ever decided to get her for graduation that she might have seen.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc1.description: I noticed that graduation was exactly one week away on Monday the fourth.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: Yes. It is Monday . . . the fourth.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc2.description: I learned that the date was the fourth of June.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: “It’s the fourth?Of June? Are you sure?”

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc2.description: I learned that my time had disappeared and that I was out of time.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: The weeks of stress, of worry . . . somehow in the middle of all my obsessing over the time, my time had disappeared. My space for sorting through it all, for making plans, had vanished. I was out of time.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc2.description: I became suddenly terrified of getting what I wanted—immortality—even though I had wanted it to stay with Edward.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: I knew exactly what I wanted, but I was suddenly terrified of getting it.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc2.description: I learned that I was being hunted by known and unknown parties.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: And then there was the fact that I was being hunted by known and unknown parties.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc2.description: I realized that I would have to say goodbye to Charlie, Renée, and Jacob as part of leaving my human life.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: I didn’t know how to do this. How to say goodbye to Charlie and Renée . . . to Jacob . . . to being human.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc3.description: I learned that the approaching date took me off guard and caused me to panic.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: “The date took me off guard,” I whispered.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc3.description: I admitted that I wasn't ready after trying to lie that I was ready.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: “I am,” I lied immediately, a reflex reaction. I could tell he saw through it, so I took a deep breath, and told the truth.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc3.description: I recognized that threats from Victoria, Jane, and Caius were frightening and influencing my sense of urgency.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: “Victoria, Jane, Caius, whoever was in my room . . . !”

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc3.description: I understood that Edward vowed to take care of the problems and to let me decide freely when I'm not threatened.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: “We will take care of the problems, and I will take care of you,” he vowed. “When we’re through it, and there is nothing forcing your hand, then you can decide to join me, if you still want to. But not because you’re afraid. You won’t be forced into this.”

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc4.description: I asked whether Edward did not want me to be a vampire and revealed my fear aloud.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc4.source_text: I asked, "You don't want me to be a vampire."

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc4.description: I felt relief when Edward assured me that he still wanted me even if I changed.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc4.source_text: I heard him say, "You’ll always be my Bella, you’ll just be a little more durable."

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc4.description: I realized that I would not accept immortality alone and that forever without Edward had no appeal.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc4.source_text: I said, "There's no point to forever without you. I wouldn't want one day without you."

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc4.description: I confessed that I did not want to be the type of girl who marries right out of high school and worried about appearances.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc4.source_text: I complained, "I'm not that girl, Edward. The one who gets married right out of high school like some small-town hick who got knocked up by her boyfriend!"

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc5.description: I learned that Seattle is being terrorized by a series of homicides and disappearances that may be linked into a single rampage.
I learned that a suspect—if one exists—would be responsible for 39 linked homicides and disappearances within the last three months.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc5.source_text: This killer — if, in fact, it is one person — would then be responsible for 39 linked homicides and disappearances within the last three months alone.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc5.description: I learned that victims have been burned beyond recognition, show signs of brutal pre-mortem crushing of bones, leave no forensic evidence, and that the crimes are accelerating.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc5.source_text: Every victim discovered has been burned to the extent that dental records were necessary for identification. More gruesome yet, most of the remains show evidence of brutal violence — bones crushed and snapped by some kind of tremendous pressure... And the most alarming pattern? Acceleration. Six of the homicides were committed in the first month, 11 in the second. Twenty-two have occurred in the last 10 days alone.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc5.description: I felt a thrill of fear when I read the article and I became convinced that immediate action might be necessary.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc5.source_text: I felt a thrill of fear as I leaned closer to read the front-page story.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc5.description: I noticed Edward took my hand and expressed urgency, which reinforced my sense that he is protective and willing to act.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc5.source_text: We’re going to have to do something . . quickly. Then he was suddenly at my side, taking my hand.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc5.description: I noticed that Alice cannot see anything right now and that she fears her vision is slipping away.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc5.source_text: She can’t see anything . . . though we’ve made up our minds half a dozen times to check it out. She’s starting to lose confidence. She feels like she’s missing too much these days, that something’s wrong. That maybe her vision is slipping away.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc5.description: I noticed Charlie had left the paper on the table and I was reminded that I needed the phone number in the concert ad for tickets while I still had finals to study for.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc5.source_text: Charlie was already gone. He’d left the paper on the table, and that reminded me that I had some shopping to do. I hoped the ad for the concert was still running; I needed the phone number to get the stupid tickets.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc6.description: I learned that Jasper explicitly said I am considered "one of us" by the family.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc6.source_text: "Bella should understand this, too. She’s one of us now."

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc6.description: I realized that Jasper has a scar exactly like mine and that we share crescent marks from the same attack.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc6.source_text: "Jasper, you have a scar exactly like mine."

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc6.description: I was surprised that Jasper thought of me that way and that the family already regarded me as part of them.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc6.source_text: His words took me by surprise.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc6.description: I remembered that my crescent scar was caused by the shape of James's teeth during his attack.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc6.source_text: I stared at the shape of James’s teeth, embossed forever on my skin.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc6.description: I realized that despite Jasper's prior attempt to kill me last year, he now regards me as part of the family.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc6.source_text: As little as I’d had to do with Jasper, especially since my last birthday when he’d tried to kill me, I hadn’t realize that he thought of me that way.

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc1.description: I learned that their venom is the only thing that leaves a scar.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: "Our venom is the only thing that leaves a scar."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc1.description: I learned that there are places where the life span of the never-aging is measured in weeks and not centuries.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: "you must understand that there are places inour world, Bella, where the life span of the never-aging is measured in weeks, and not centuries."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc1.description: I learned that the Volturi keep the southern covens in check.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: "Not that the covens in the South care much for what the humans notice or do not. It’s the Volturi that keep them in check."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc1.description: I learned that southern covens have been at constant war for centuries and that they regard humans chiefly as food.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: "Because it has been war in the South, constant war for centuries, with never one moment of truce."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc1.description: I learned that vampires fight for control of the densest human populations represented as the thickest red on Jasper's imagined map.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: "They fight for control of the thickest red."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc1.description: I learned about Benito as an example of a vampire who massacred rival covens to eliminate competition.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: "The first anyone ever heard of him, he came down from somewhere north of Dallas and massacred the two small covens that shared the area near Houston."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc1.description: I felt horrified and appalled by Jasper's story and by the brutal nature of the southern wars.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: "I breathed in horror, feeling rude but unable to stop staring at his subtly ravaged skin."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc1.description: I noticed that I found the Volturi's role complicated and that I had trouble accepting the idea of them in any positive light despite Jasper's respectful mention.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: "I frowned at the way he pronounced the name — with respect, almost gratitude. The idea of the Volturi as the good guys in any sense was hard to accept."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc2.description: I learned that Benito created an army of newborn vampires and was initially unstoppable.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc2.source_text: Benito had created an army of newborn vampires. He was the first one to think of it, and, in the beginning, he was unstoppable.

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc2.description: I learned that newborn vampires are extremely powerful physically for the first year but are volatile, unpredictable, and often lack fighting skill.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc2.source_text: Very young vampires are volatile, wild, and almost impossible to control. One newborn can be reasoned with, taught to restrain himself, but ten, fifteen together are a nightmare.

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc2.description: I learned that the Volturi intervened after massive vampire-caused human deaths, executed anyone found with newborns, and cleaned house in Mexico for almost a year.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc2.source_text: When the body count reached epidemic proportions — in fact, your histories blame a disease for the population slump — the Volturi finally stepped in. Anyone who was found with the newborns was executed immediately. The Volturi were cleaning house for almost a year.

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc2.description: I changed my view of Jasper when I realized that he had been changed during the Civil War era and that I had never seen him afraid or horrified before.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc2.source_text: Jasper shuddered. I realized that I had never before seen him either afraid or horrified. That's how you were changed. When I was human, I lived in Houston, Texas. I was almost seventeen years old when I joined the Confederate Army in 1861.
