tw-book3-chapter13_Sc3.description: I learned no direct information about Bella Swan from this scene.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc3.source_text: I was placed in charge of evacuating the women and children from the city when the Union’s mortar boats reached the harbor.

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc4.description: I learned that Maria recruited Nettie and Lucy and that the three were survivors of lost battles who formed a partnership of convenience.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "Their names were Maria, Nettie, and Lucy. They hadn’t been together long — Maria had rounded up the other two — all three were survivors of recently lost battles. Theirs was a partnership of convenience."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc4.description: I learned that Maria deliberately sought out humans with potential, trained them intensively, and rewarded their success to build a superior army.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "Maria wanted a superior army, so she sought out specific humans who had potential. Then she gave us much more attention, more training than anyone else had bothered with. She taught us to fight, and she taught us to be invisible to the humans. When we did well, we were rewarded...."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc4.description: I learned that Jasper proved quicker and better at combat than his peers and that Maria promoted him to lead because his leadership reduced casualties and improved cooperation.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "I was quicker than the others, better at combat. Maria was pleased with me... Maria decided to put me in charge of the others — as if I were being promoted. It suited my nature exactly. The casualties went down dramatically, and our numbers swelled to hover around twenty."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc4.description: I learned that Jasper's as yet undefined ability to control the emotional atmosphere made the newborns cooperate more effectively than usual.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "My ability, as yet undefined, to control the emotional atmosphere around me was vitally effective. We soon began to work together in a way that newborn vampires had never cooperated before."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc4.description: I learned that Jasper organized twenty-three newborns, that they took Monterrey with minimal losses, and that Maria extended control across Texas and northern Mexico before rivals arrived.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "I pulled together an army of twenty-three in the end... We crept down toward Monterrey, her former home, and she unleashed us on her enemies. They had only nine newborns at the time... losing only four in the process.... That first year, she extended her control to cover most of Texas and northern Mexico."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc4.description: I wasn’t sure whether Jasper had edited his story for my sake or because he was responding to the tension I could feel from Edward, and I changed my belief about the straightforwardness of his recounting.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "A few days later," he finally said, and I wasn’t sure if he had edited his story for my sake or because he was responding to the tension that even I could feel exuding from Edward, "I was introduced to my new life."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc4.description: I realized that Jasper worshipped Maria and that Maria both depended on and favored him, which updated my view of his loyalty and devotion.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "Maria grew quite fond of me — she began to depend upon me. And, in some ways, I worshipped the ground she walked on."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc6.description: I learned that Jasper could feel everything his prey felt and that he lived their emotions while killing them.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc6.source_text: "I couldfeel everything my prey was feeling. And I lived their emotions as I killed them."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc6.description: I realized that Jasper's repeated killing produced a worsening depression and an aversion to hunting that made him withdraw from others.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc6.source_text: "The depression got worse, and I wandered away from Peter and Charlotte."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc6.description: I saw that Alice's presence and warmth restored hope in Jasper and altered his emotional trajectory.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc6.source_text: "For the first time in almost a century, I felt hope."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc7.description: I learned that there is an army of newborn vampires in Seattle, fewer than twenty, untrained and likely to attract the Volturi.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc7.source_text: "There is an army of newborn vampires in Seattle. Fewer than twenty, I'd guess. The difficult part is that they are totally untrained. Whoever made them just set them loose. It will only get worse, and it won't be much longer till the Volturi step in."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc7.description: I became convinced that Jasper has found peace and happiness with Alice and that her presence changed him profoundly.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc7.source_text: "Alice has made all the difference," Jasper agreed. "This is a climate I enjoy."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc7.description: I noticed a softer, more trusting expression from Jasper toward me and toward the Cullens after his reunion with Alice.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc7.source_text: They smiled at each other for a long moment, and then Jasper looked back to me, the soft expression lingering.

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc8.description: I believed Bella is included among the targets and therefore at increased risk from the newborn army.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc8.source_text: “Does it occur to anyone else that the only possible threat in the area that would call for the creation of an army is . . . us?”

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc8.description: I learned that Alice is experiencing only flickers and cannot see a clear picture of what is happening, implying an active concealment of events.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc8.source_text: “Flickers,” Alice said. “I can’t see a clear picture when I try to see what’s going on, nothing concrete. But I’ve been getting these strange flashes. Not enough to make sense of. . . .”

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc9.description: I saw Aro's dream of Edward and Alice in black, flowing robes with cold, blood-red eyes.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc9.source_text: I could see it in my head now, Aro’s dream. Edward and Alice in black, flowing robes, drifting along at Aro’s side with their eyes cold and blood-red. . . .

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc9.description: I felt numb, horrified, and deathly afraid while also sensing I was missing something important that would explain the chaos.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc9.source_text: There was something bothering me, and I couldn’t put my finger on it. I was numb, horrified, deathly afraid. And yet, under that, I could feel that I was missing something important.

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc9.description: I inferred that the Volturi are reputed to strictly follow their rules and would not deliberately break them.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc9.source_text: “They’re too committed to their mission. They would never break the rules themselves. It goes against everything they’ve worked for.”

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc10.description: I learned that Irina was more involved with Laurent than we had realized and that she was holding a grudge against the wolves for destroying him to save me.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc10.source_text: “Irina was more involved with our friend Laurent than we knew. She’s holding a grudge against the wolves for destroying him to save Bella. She wants —”

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc10.description: I felt fear and shock when I whispered Laurent's name and felt the blood emptying from my face upon realizing Irina's possible threat.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc10.source_text: “Laurent?” I whispered, the blood emptying from my face, but Edward didn’t respond, focused on Carlisle’s thoughts.

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc10.description: I remembered that Laurent had been sent by Victoria to observe me and that he had lived with Tanya's family in Alaska for almost a year before his death.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc10.source_text:
“I actually came here as a favor to her. . . . Victoria. Laurent had been her first maneuver — she’d sent him to observe, to see how hard it might be to get to me. He hadn’t survived the wolves to report back.”

“Laurent had been with them for almost a year previous to his death.”

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc11.description: I learned that our skill would give us the upper hand but that we lacked numbers, making the fight too even.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc11.source_text: It’s too even a fight. We’d have the upper hand in skill, but not numbers.

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc11.description: I learned that we could win the battle while still suffering deadly losses among our group.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc11.source_text: We would win, but we would lose. Some wouldn’t survive.

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc11.description: I became desperate and wanted to scream as I grasped that victory would cost lives.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc11.source_text: I wanted to scream out loud as I grasped what Jasper meant.

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc11.description: I recognized the other vampires in the room as my family when I looked at their faces.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc11.source_text: I looked around the room at their faces — Jasper, Alice, Emmett, Rose, Esme, Carlisle . . . Edward — the faces of my family.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc1.description: I learned that Alice insisted the party was still on and that invitations had already been sent.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: "Say whatever you like about me," Alice answered. "The party is still on." "Besides, the invitations are already sent."

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc1.description: I learned that Bella had already bought Alice's present.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: "You’ve already bought my present," she reminded me.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc1.description: I learned that some allies planned to leave in a week.
I realized that Bella offered to help and then had her hope defeated when told she would be no good in a fight and would endanger Edward.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: "Icould help." "There’s not enough time to make you helpful, Bella," she disagreed coolly. "Do you remember how Jasper described the young ones? You’d be no good in a fight. You wouldn’t be able to control your instincts, and that would make you an easy target. And then Edward would get hurt trying to protect you."

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc1.description: I noticed Bella leaned into Edward's protection when he put his arm around her and told her to trust him.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: Edward put his arm around me and pulled me tightly against his side. "It’s going to be fine, Bella. Trust me."

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc2.description: I learned that there are sixty-five guests expected for the event.
I learned that Renée canceled a planned surprise for my graduation.
I learned that I will receive a message at home explaining what went wrong with my mother's plans.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: She was going to surprise you for your graduation, but something went wrong. You’ll have a message when you get home.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc2.description: I felt relief and was eternally grateful that whatever went wrong prevented my mother from coming.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: For a moment, I just let myself enjoy the relief. Whatever it was that went wrong for my mother, I was eternally grateful to it.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc2.description: I did not want my mother to come to Forksnow and I felt overwhelmed by the thought that her arrival would make my head explode.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: If she had come to Forksnow . . . I didn’t want to think about it. My head would explode.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc3.description: I learned that Phil tangled up with the catcher, broke his thigh bone, and became entirely dependent on Renée.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: My mother describe Phil’s accident on the ball field — while demonstrating a slide, he’d tangled up with the catcher and broken his thigh bone; he was entirely dependent on her, and there was no way she could leave him.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc3.description: I felt relieved that I had at least one person less to worry about getting killed this week because of Phil's injury.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: One person I don’t have to worry about getting killed this week.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc3.description: I felt Edward's patience and affection during the call and I became more aware of how his smile affects me.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: Edward’s patience was endless. He waited politely through the whole conversation, just playing with my hair and smiling whenever I looked up. It was probably superficial to notice such things while I had so many more important things to think about, but his smile still knocked the breath out of me.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc3.description: I discovered that Edward lifted me onto the kitchen counter to make it easier for me to kiss him.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: He put his hands around my waist and lifted me onto the kitchen counter, so I wouldn’t have to reach as far.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.description: I learned that I called Jacob in the middle of the afternoon and that my call woke him up.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.source_text: Though it was the middle of the afternoon, my call woke Jacob up, and he was grouchy at first.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.description: I learned that the Quileute school was already out for the summer and that Jacob told me to come over as early as I could.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.source_text: The Quileute school was already out for the summer, so he told me to come over as early as I could.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.description: I felt more dignity spending the day with Jacob than being babysat, and I recognized that preference.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.source_text: I was pleased to have an option besides being babysat. There was a tiny bit more dignity in spending the day with Jacob.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.description: I wanted Edward and Jacob to be friends and I tried to hold them together rather than accept them only as vampire and werewolf.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.source_text: I wanted Edward to come to me. I wanted to make both of them get out of their cars and shake hands and be friends — be Edward and Jacob rather thanvampire andwerewolf.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.description: I chose to hang out at Jacob's place because he didn't look up for much more than that.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.source_text: “Let’s just hang out at your place for now,” I suggested.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.description: I have a graduation party to attend that I resent because Alice invited the whole town.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.source_text: “Well, I do have to go to a graduation party. Mine.”

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.description: I felt safer in Jacob's house than in my own because no one had ever come looking for me there.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.source_text: This house felt safer than my own, probably because no one had ever come looking for me here.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.description: I noticed that Jacob's sleeping face reminded me of the boy who had been my very best friend before werewolf tensions intervened.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.source_text: While he slept, every trace of defensiveness and bitterness disappeared and suddenly he was the boy who had been my very best friend before all the werewolf nonsense had gotten in the way.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.description: I withheld details about my mysterious visitor because I knew Jacob would read too much into my qualms.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.source_text: I didn’t want to get into it now. For one thing, he didn’t look up for any difficult conversations. For another, I knew he would read too much into my qualms.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.description: I felt conflicted about graduating because it symbolized the end of my human life and evoked unease rather than simple celebration.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.source_text: Finals were done, and most of them had been a cakewalk. Calculus, the one exception, was behind me, pass or fail. My high school education was over. And I didn’t really know how I felt about that. I couldn’t look at it objectively, tied up as it was with my human life being over.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc7.description: I knew that asking Carlisle to change me immediately after graduation made the most practical sense.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc7.source_text: If I were thinking practically, I knew it made more sense to ask Carlisle to change me the second I made it through the graduation line.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc7.description: I realized that I wasn't quite ready yet to be changed into a vampire.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc7.source_text: But Edward was right — I wasn’t quite ready yet.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc7.description: I wanted Edward to be the one to change me even though the desire wasn't rational.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc7.source_text: I didn’t want to be practical. I wanted Edward to be the one.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc7.description: I felt that Edward being the one to make the choice and to bite me would make me belong to him in a tangible way.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc7.source_text: There was just something about him being the one to make the choice — to want to keep me enough that he wouldn’t just allow me to be changed, he would act to keep me. It was childish, but I liked the idea thathis lips would be the last good thing I would feel. Even more embarrassingly, something I would never say aloud, I wantedhis venom to poison my system. It would make me belong to him in a tangible, quantifiable way.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc7.description: I understood that Edward planned to stick to a marriage scheme as a way to delay changing me.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc7.source_text: But I knew he was going to stick to his marriage scheme like glue — because a delay was what he was clearly after and it was working so far.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc7.description: I believed it would be easier to tell my parents I was becoming a vampire than to tell them I was getting married.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc7.source_text: It would be easier to tell them I was becoming a vampire.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc7.description: I pictured a simpler domestic life with Edward in another world where wearing his ring would be expected.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc7.source_text: Then, for just a second, I saw that same odd vision of Edward and me on a porch swing, wearing clothes from another kind of world. A world where it would surprise no one if I wore his ring on my finger.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.description: I realized my pockets were empty and that I would have to borrow Jacob's phone to call Edward.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.source_text: I patted my pockets as I spoke, and realized they were empty. “Shoot, I’ll have to borrow your phone. I think I must have left his in the car.”

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.description: I learned that Jacob wanted to talk to me and had intended to do it more smoothly but said he was out of time.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.source_text: “Look,” Jacob said. “I was planning to do this a little bit differently.” He laughed, and it sounded like he was laughing at himself. “Smoother,” he added. “I was going to work up to it, but” — and he looked at the clouds — “I’m out of time to work.”

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.description: I began to suspect that Jacob had something important to tell me and that he was nervous about confessing it.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.source_text: He laughed again, nervous. We were still pacing slowly.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.description: I noticed Jacob pulled me off the couch and insisted I stay because he valued the time with me and did not want to waste it.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.source_text: “No!” Jacob insisted, grabbing my hand. “No, stay. You hardly ever make it down. I can’t believe I wasted all this time.” He pulled me off the couch as he spoke, and then led the way outside.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc9.description: I planted my feet and folded my arms across my chest as a defensive, closed posture.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc9.source_text: I planted my feet, and he came to a stop. I took my hand away and folded my arms across my chest.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc9.description: I became suddenly sure that I didn't want to know what he was building up to.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc9.source_text: I was suddenly sure that I didn’t want to know what he was building up to.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc9.description: I saw Jacob press me to choose him by stating his love and asking me to pick him instead of the other man.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc9.source_text: I’m in love with you, Bella. And I want you to pick me instead of him.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc1.description: I observed that Bella tried to end the conversation and said she had to leave.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: "I can't — I mean I don't . . . I have to go."

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc1.description: I realized that Bella distinguished between familial love and romantic love toward Jacob and explicitly denied being in love with him.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: "You’re family. I love you, but I’m not in love with you."

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc1.description: I acknowledged that Bella did not want Jacob to disappear from her life even though she would not return his romantic feelings.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: "No, I don’t want that," I finally admitted.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc2.description: I realized that trying to keep my friend when it would hurt him was wrong.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: If I wasn’t mean — and greedy, too — I would tell him I didn’t want to be friends and walk away. It was wrong to try to keep my friend when that would hurt him.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc2.description: I affirmed that I love him and that he is my whole life.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: I love him, Jacob. He’s my whole life.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob explicitly will not give up and finds me irresistible as a lost cause.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: Because I recently decided that I’m not giving up. There really is something irresistible about a lost cause.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.description: I learned that shutting down calms Edward and makes his anger seem to evaporate.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.source_text: Acting on instinct, I let my hands drop to my side, and shut down. I opened my eyes and didn’t fight, didn’t feel . . . just waited for him to stop. It worked. The anger seemed to evaporate, and he pulled back to look at me.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.description: I learned that punching him produced a crunching sound and that my hand was broken from the impact.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.source_text: I pulled my arm back and then let it snap forward, punching him in the mouth with as much power as I could force out of my body. There was a crunching sound. "Ow! OW!" I screamed, frantically hopping up and down in agony while I clutched my hand to my chest. It was broken, I could feel it.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.description: I became determined to refuse Jacob's help and to walk toward the border instead of accepting his drive.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.source_text: "No, thanks," I hissed. "I'd rather walk." I turned toward the road. It was only a few miles to the border. As soon as I got away from him, Alice would see me. She'd send somebody to pick me up.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.description: I view Jacob as pushy, obnoxious, and moronic and I angrily wished harm upon him in the moment.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.source_text: "Fine!" I growled. "Do! I can't wait to see what Edward does to you! I hope he snaps your neck, you pushy, obnoxious, moronic DOG!"

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.description: I judged Jacob as pathetic for not reacting theatrically after being hit, noting he didn't rub his jaw like in the movies.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.source_text: I jerked away from him. "Fine!" I growled. "Do! I can't wait to see what Edward does to you! I hope he snaps your neck, you pushy, obnoxious, moronic DOG!" Jacob rolled his eyes. He walked me to the passenger side of his car and helped me in. When he got in the driver’s side, he was whistling.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc4.description: I learned that my hand was injured and possibly broken after the struggle.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: I held up my injured hand.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc4.description: I declared that I hate Jacob Black during the argument.
I stated that I can't be happy without Edward and rejected the idea of being with anyone else.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: Jacob, I can’t be happy without him.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc4.description: I insisted that Edward will not leave me again despite Jacob's suggestion he might.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: "No, he will not," I said through my teeth.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc4.description: I felt the pain of remembering Edward's departure as a sharp, lashing memory.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: The pain of the memory bit into me like the lash of a whip.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc6.description: I learned that Bella called Edward after being driven home by Jacob and that she had left her phone.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc6.source_text: "You left the phone . . . I’m sorry, did Jacob drive you home?"

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc6.description: I learned that Bella thought her hand might be broken after punching Jacob and asked Edward to get her so Carlisle could look at it.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc6.source_text: I want Carlisle to look at my hand. I think it’s broken.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc6.description: I felt Bella take some grim satisfaction in Jacob's discomfort and in Edward's quick response.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc6.source_text: I smiled a grim smile, imagining his discomfort.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc7.description: I noted that Edward examined my injured hand gently and promised to take care of it.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc7.source_text: He examined my hand gently, so carefully that it caused me no pain at all.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc7.description: I felt less angry and comforted when Edward stayed close after the altercation.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc7.source_text: I wasn’t so angry anymore, now that Edward was with me.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc7.description: I understood that Edward is protective of me and willing to use threats to ensure my safety.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc7.source_text: if you return her to me in less than the perfect condition that I left her in, you will be running with three legs.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc8.description: I learned that I punched a werewolf in the face and sustained a broken hand with a tiny fissure in one knuckle.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc8.source_text: I heard: "No, Emmett. I punched a werewolf in the face." and I read: "My hand was broken, but there wasn’t any serious damage, just a tiny fissure in one knuckle."

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc8.description: I learned that Emmett and Jasper are betting on how many times I will 'slip up' in my first year as a vampire.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc8.source_text: I heard: "They’re betting on how many times you . . . slip up in the first year."

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc8.description: I became more afraid that I might become a bloodthirsty newborn who could not stop myself from killing people.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc8.source_text: I read: "Wild. Bloodthirsty. Maybe I would not be able to stop myself from killing people."

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc8.description: I came to trust Edward absolutely to keep me from doing anything I would regret and to protect me from myself.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc8.source_text: I read: "I trusted Edward, trusted him absolutely, to keep me from doing anything I would regret."

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc8.description: My desire to be strong, beautiful, and to stand next to Edward and feel like I belonged there intensified.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc8.source_text: I read: "I hoped that I would be as strong as Edward said I would be. Strong and fast and, most of all, beautiful. Someone who could stand next to Edward and feel like she belonged there."

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc1.description: I discovered that every item of clothing I owned was strewn across my bed and that my drawers and closets were bare.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc1.source_text: Every item of clothing I owned was strewn across my bed; my drawers and closets were bare.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc1.description: I noticed my khaki skirt was lying over the back of the rocking chair as a potential piece to build an outfit around.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc1.source_text: My khaki skirt lay over the back of the rocking chair, waiting for me to discover something that went with it just exactly right.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc1.description: I realized that my kidnapped red blouse was missing and that it was the exact item I would have worn for the occasion.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc1.source_text: The kicker was that I knew exactly what I would have worn if it were still available — my kidnapped red blouse.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc1.description: I became angry and blamed a vampire for stealing my blouse.
I worried that unless I found something suitable quickly I would be forced to graduate in my old sweats.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc1.source_text: Unless I could find something better here — and the odds weren’t looking good at this point — I was going to graduate in them.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc2.description: I realized that the thief who broke into my room and the new vampires in Seattle are connected and likely the same person.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc2.source_text: The one who broke in and stole my things, and the new vampires in Seattle. They’re together!

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc2.description: I learned that the intruder stole my scent so that others could locate me.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc2.source_text: He stole my scent . . . so that others could find me.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc2.description: I concluded that Edward's original interpretation was incorrect and that the break-in had been a test to see if using the holes in my vision would work.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc2.source_text: “Edward had it wrong,” I whispered. “It was a test . . . to see if it would work. If he could get in and out safely as long as he didn’t do anything you would be watching out for. Like trying to kill me. . . .

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc2.description: I felt relieved for a moment believing that nobody was trying to exterminate the Cullens now that I understood the real target.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc2.source_text: “Well,” I whispered, “everyone can relax. Nobody’s trying to exterminate the Cullens after all.”

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc3.description: I learned that Bella is nervous and possibly crying.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: I read: "Are you crying?" "No. I'm nervous. Go away."

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc3.description: I learned that Bella speaks hoarsely while preparing for the ceremony.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: I read: "Almost. Give me a minute," I said hoarsely.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc3.description: I changed my belief that the graduation ceremony is not the best time for Edward to learn about Bella's state.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: I read: "I couldn't keep it from him for long, but maybe the graduation ceremony wasn’t the best time for his reaction."

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc3.description: I learned that Bella follows Alice's quick instructions under stress.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: I read: "Put it on," Alice commanded as she flitted out the window.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.description: I learned my hair hung straight and boring because I ran out of time to style it.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: I’d been planning to do something more sophisticated with my hair, but time was up, so it hung straight and boring as on any other day.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.description: I learned I didn’t bother to look in the mirror and therefore had no idea how Alice’s sweater and skirt ensemble worked.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: I didn’t bother to look in the mirror, so I had no idea how Alice’s sweater and skirt ensemble worked.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.description: I learned I threw the ugly yellow polyester graduation robe over my arm and hurried down the stairs.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: I threw the ugly yellow polyester graduation robe over my arm and hurried down the stairs.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.description: I learned Charlie said I looked nice and asked if my outfit was new.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: “You look nice,” Charlie said, already gruff with suppressed emotion. “Is that new?”

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.description: I felt nervous about the ceremony when Edward asked if I was all right and I answered that I was nervous.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: “Are you all right?” Edward whispered when he helped me from the front seat in the school parking lot. “Nervous,” I answered, and it wasn’t even a lie.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.description: I admitted that I was not really excited about graduation.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: “Are you excited?” he asked me. “Not really,” I admitted.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.description: I noticed Charlie was imagining things about the situation that would get him in trouble if he said them out loud.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: Which almost certainly meant that Charlie was imagining things that would get him in trouble with me if he said them out loud.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.description: I felt Edward’s affection when he told me I was beautiful and appeared to want to say more.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: “You are so beautiful,” he said. He looked like he wanted to say more, but Charlie, in an obvious maneuver that he meant to be subtle, shrugged in between us and put his arm around my shoulders.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.description: I learned that I graduated from high school and received my diploma during the commencement.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: "'Congratulations, Miss Swan,' he mumbled to me, pressing the diploma into my good hand."

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.description: I felt that the ceremony marked an ending for me more than the beginning Eric described.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: "Because it was an ending, no matter what Eric, the valedictorian, had to say about commencement meaning “beginning” and all the rest of the trite nonsense."

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.description: I noticed that Alice had not been at first but then suddenly appeared to take her diploma onstage.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: "I watched as Alice, suddenly appearing, danced across the stage to take hers, a look of deep concentration on her face."

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.description: I felt that my relationship with Jessica had been patched up enough to end our time together on a good note.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: "I paid attention as well as I could while I shrugged into my robe. And I found that I was glad that things could end on a good note with Jessica."

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.description: I observed my father Charlie become choked up and tell me that I was not his little girl anymore.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: "'You’re not my little girl anymore.' Charlie choked up a bit at the end."

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.description: I realized that I felt oddly unexcited and disconnected from the expected joy of graduation.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: "'I don’t know, Dad. I guess it hasn’t hit yet or something.'"

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc6.description: I realized that one person is manipulating Alice's visions and that the attacks seem to be focused on me.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc6.source_text: “I think it’s mostly coming at us from one side . . . and I think it’s coming at me, really. It’s all connected, it has to be. It’s just one person who’s messing with Alice’s visions.”

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc6.description: I changed my belief and concluded that telling Edward in public was a bad idea and that Alice was right to keep her thoughts clouded.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc6.source_text: “Okay, so telling Edward had been a really bad idea. Alice was right to keep her thoughts clouded.”

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc6.description: I noticed Edward's panic and subsequent fury made me fear his volatility and feel the need to avoid being near breakable objects when he loses control.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc6.source_text: “His hands were halfway extended toward me, like he was about to grab me and make a run for it.”

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob and Billy had been at the gathering but had to leave early.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc6.source_text: “Jacob and Billy had to take off — did you see that they were here?”

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc8.description: I was in the parking lot when Edward appeared from the shadows and I sighed in relief.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc8.source_text:
Something moved in the shadows.
My gasp turned into a sigh of relief as Edward appeared out of the gloom.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc8.description: I was kissed by Edward in the parking lot after he pulled my face up to his lips.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc8.source_text: Without a word, he pulled me tightly against his chest. One cool hand found my chin, and pulled my face up so that he could press his hard lips to mine. I could feel the tension in his jaw.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc8.description: I asked Edward how he was and I learned that he said he was 'not so great' and apologized for losing control earlier.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc8.source_text:
“How are you?” I asked as soon as he let me breathe.
“Not so great,” he murmured. “But I’ve got a handle on myself. I’m sorry that I lost it back there.”

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc8.description: I felt that it was my fault for not waiting to tell him whatever I had to say.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc8.source_text: “My fault. I should have waited to tell you.”

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc8.description: I perceived increased intimacy and protectiveness from Edward when he kissed me and said he would follow me to my house.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc8.source_text:
He suddenly kissed me again, not letting me answer. He pulled away after just a second. “Charlie’s on his way.”
“I’ll have him drop me at your house.”
“I’ll follow you there.”

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc8.description: I planned to have Charlie drop me at Edward's house and I observed Charlie's impatience upon arrival.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc8.source_text:
“I’ll have him drop me at your house.”
“Charlie’s on his way.”
“Charlie sauntered out to the car, muttering about impatience.”

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc9.description: I felt worried about the party despite saying I felt fine.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc9.source_text: "I feel fine," I lied. "Worried about the party?" he guessed. "Yeah," I lied again.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc9.description: I found that my left hand bore a dark brace and a broken knuckle from the earlier conflict.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc9.source_text: My left hand rested lightly on the dark brace I rarely thought about. My broken knuckle didn’t hurt much anymore.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc9.description: I decided that moving in with Charlie was the best idea I ever had.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc9.source_text: And I’m really glad I came to live with you, Dad. It was the best idea I ever had.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc9.description: I acknowledged that Charlie does a fantastic job as a father and that I feel grateful to live with him.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc9.source_text: That’s ridiculous. You do a fantastic job. World’s best dad. And . . . And I’m really glad I came to live with you, Dad.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc9.description: I learned that Carlisle and Esme would be at the party to help keep things under control.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc9.source_text: Don’t worry about it, Dad. Carlisle and Esme are going to be there.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc9.description: I felt resigned to endure the party despite my misgivings when I saw the extensive decorations.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc9.source_text: The black velvet darkness was interrupted ahead, just where the Cullens’ drive should be. Someone had wrapped the trees on either side in thousands of twinkle lights, impossible to miss.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc1.description: I felt frightened by Edward's kiss because it carried a desperate edge, as if we only had a limited amount of time left.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: This kiss frightened me. There was too much tension, too strong an edge to the way his lips crushed mine — like he was afraid we only had so much time left to us.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc1.description: I resolved to suppress thinking about our limited time so I could act human for the next several hours at the party.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: I couldn't let myself think about that. Not if I was going to have to act human for the next several hours.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc1.description: I realized I prioritize others' safety over my own when I told him I wasn't worried about myself so much.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: "I'm not worried about myself so much."

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc1.description: I felt reassured by Edward's promise that he would not let anything happen to me.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: "I won't let anything happen to you."

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc2.description: I learned that the interior of the Cullens' home had been transformed into a nightclub for a party.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: I read: "The interior of the Cullens’ home had been transformed into a nightclub — the kind that didn’t often exist in real life, only on TV."

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc2.description: I felt underdressed and insecure about my outfit and my ability to contribute to the preparations.
I doubted that I would ever be able to get things done the way Alice did even after losing the need for sleep and gaining speed.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: I read: "I doubted that — even after I didn’t need sleep and moved at a much faster speed — I would ever be able to get things done the way Alice did."

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc2.description: I decided I could not stay behind waiting and that I would go mad if I only waited for them to come home.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: I read: "I couldn't stay behind, waiting and hoping for them to come home. I wouldn't. I would go mad."

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc3.description: I hosted a joint party with Alice and Edward.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: Though the party had been billed as a joint event for Alice, Edward, and me, there was no denying that I was the most popular target for congratulations and thanks.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc3.description: I greeted Jessica and Mike and let Angela and Ben in as guests arrived.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: I went to greet Jess and Mike, hoping the edge in my voice sounded like the right kind of excitement. Before I could get to anyone else, the bell rang again. I let Angela and Ben in, leaving the door wide, because Eric and Katie were just reaching the steps.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc3.description: I felt that hosting the party was not as hard as I had expected.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: It wasn’t as hard as I’d thought it would be.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc3.description: I felt like I was acting every bit as much as the Cullens.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: Tonight I felt like I was acting every bit as much as they were.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc3.description: I realized Alice deliberately pushed me into the center of attention to make me be more human in the way she thought I should be.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: Probably Alice had done this on purpose, to force me into the center of attention — a place she thought I should enjoy more. She was forever trying to make me be human the way she thought humans should be.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc4.description: I felt Edward at my side still refusing to let go and kept one hand securely at my waist pulling me closer.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: Edward was at my side — still refusing to let go of me. He kept one hand securely at my waist, pulling me closer now and then in response to thoughts I probably didn’t want to hear.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc4.description: I became immediately suspicious when he dropped his arm and edged away from me.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: So I was immediately suspicious when he dropped his arm and edged away from me.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc4.description: I watched him reach the dark shadow beside the kitchen doorway where the lights only shone intermittently.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: I watched him as he reached the dark shadow beside the kitchen doorway, where the lights only shone intermittently.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc4.description: I saw a red light flash across his back and glint off the red sequins of Alice's shirt which briefly illuminated the scene.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: A red light flashed across his back and glinted off the red sequins of Alice’s shirt.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc4.description: I found Alice still in the dark with a blank, expressionless face and one hand gripping the door frame as if she needed support.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: Edward was gone, but Alice was still there in the dark, her face blank — the kind of expressionless look you see on the face of someone who has just witnessed a horrible accident. One of her hands gripped the door frame, like she needed the support.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc4.description: I felt alarmed and more distrustful of Edward after seeing his face go empty and him disappear into the shadows.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: His face was empty as a stone. He turned and disappeared into the shadows under the stair.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc5.description: I realized Alice had seen something important that caused her to leave immediately to talk to Carlisle.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc5.source_text: I knew this was it. Alice had seen what she’d been waiting for, and I honestly didn’t feel I could stand the suspense long enough to answer the door.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc5.description: I felt that I could not stand the suspense and I avoided answering the door as a result.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc5.source_text: I knew this was it... I honestly didn’t feel I could stand the suspense long enough to answer the door.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc5.description: I admitted guilt for inviting Jacob and I had thought I rescinded that invitation despite not expecting him to come.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc5.source_text:
“Guilty.”
I’d thought I’d rescinded that invitation — not that I’d ever dreamed Jacob would come here, regardless.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc6.description: I discovered that the Cullens, including Alice and Edward, were not visible at the party and that I could not find them in the crowd.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc6.source_text: I read: "Where had they gone? My eyes scanned the darkened room."

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob presented me with a silver bracelet that included a tiny wooden wolf charm which he carved himself.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc6.source_text: I read: "The present is inside, Bella." and "I didn't make the bracelet," he admitted. "Just the charm."

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc6.description: I accepted Jacob's apology for kissing me and adjusted my immediate feelings to avoid escalating the conflict.
I became more anxious and preoccupied because I believed Alice and Edward might have information I needed about Alice's vision and Carlisle's input.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc6.source_text: I read: "I wanted to know what Alice had seen and what Edward and Carlisle were saying about it."

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc6.description: I acknowledged that I care about Jacob's happiness, that I liked his genuine smile, and that I would wear the bracelet he gave me.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc6.source_text: I read: "He grinned at me — it was the happy smile that I loved to see him wear." and "Of course I will."

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc7.description: I learned that a psychic saw something important.
I learned that a decision had been made regarding the threat.
I learned that the attackers were coming to Forks rather than Seattle.
I learned that one of the attackers had carried my red shirt.
I learned that there would not be enough of them to protect the town and that some attackers would come to search Forks.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc7.source_text: But it doesn’t matter where we stop them. There still won’t be enough of us, and some of them will come here to search.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc7.description: I felt guilty and responsible because my presence had put the town at risk.
I felt reassured and dependent on Alice when she put her arm around my waist and stepped in for me.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc7.source_text: She put her arm around my waist.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.description: I learned that many of their kind are coming specifically for me.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.source_text: “Our kind. Lots of them.” "For Bella. That’s all we know."

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.description: I learned the wolves and vampires set a rendezvous for three o'clock about ten miles due north of the Hoh Forest ranger station and that approaching from the west will let the wolves follow their scent in.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.source_text: “Three o’clock?” "About ten miles due north of the Hoh Forest ranger station. Come at it from the west and you’ll be able to follow our scent in."

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.description: I learned that Alice's visions currently show twenty-one attackers today but that the numbers are going down.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.source_text: “It changes — twenty-one today, but the numbers are going down.”

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.description: I changed my belief that I could keep the wolves out of the conflict after Jacob and the pack made it clear they would join.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.source_text: “You didn’t honestly think you were going to keep us out of this?” Jacob asked.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.description: I felt helpless and scared as Jacob ignored my pleas and left with his friends.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.source_text: “Wait, Jake!” I called after him. “Please! Don’t do this!”

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc1.description: I complained that the party had been the longest in history and felt exhausted on the drive home.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: "THAT HAD TO BE THE LONGEST PARTY IN THE HISTORYof the world," I complained on the way home.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc1.description: I realized that the Cullens had been reassured and were relaxed after Jacob's solution.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: Jacob’s solution had them all relaxed, almost euphoric after the long weeks of stress.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc1.description: I felt increasingly anxious and overwhelmed by being the cause of potential conflict and could not bear the idea of others fighting for me.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: Bad enough — horrible — that the Cullens would fight for me. It was already too much that I would have to allow that.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc1.description: I decided I would not be left behind and threatened to call Jacob if Edward refused to take me.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: "If you won’t take me, then I’ll call Jacob."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc2.description: I entered the house silently and observed my father asleep on the living room sofa and snoring very loudly.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc2.source_text: I tiptoed in the front door. Charlie was asleep in the living room, overflowing the too-small sofa, and snoring so loudly I could have ripped a chainsaw to life and it wouldn’t have wakened him.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc2.description: I shook his shoulder vigorously and called for him to get up.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc2.source_text: I shook his shoulder vigorously. "Dad! Charlie!"

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc2.description: I helped him up to his bed where he collapsed fully dressed and began snoring again.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc2.source_text: I helped him up to his bed, where he collapsed on top of the covers, fully dressed, and started snoring again.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc2.description: I became convinced he was not going to be looking for me anytime soon.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc2.source_text: He wasn’t going to be looking for me anytime soon.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc2.description: I feel a caretaker obligation toward my father and acted to prevent him from hurting his back while he slept awkwardly.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc2.source_text: I’m home now — you’re going to hurt your back sleeping like that. C’mon, time to move.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc4.description: I realized we were in the baseball clearing and I remembered the earlier evening with the Cullens that had been interrupted by James and his coven.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc4.source_text: It took me a minute, because it was so dark with the moon hidden behind the clouds, but I realized that we were in the baseball clearing. It was the same place where, more than a year ago, that first lighthearted evening with the Cullens had been interrupted by James and his coven.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc4.description: I began to believe that patterns might be broken and I doubted that the Volturi were necessarily the only flexible force in the situation.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc4.source_text: But James and Laurent were never coming back. That pattern wouldn’t be repeated. Maybe all the patterns were broken. Yes, someone had broken out of their pattern. Was it possible that the Volturi were the flexible ones in this equation? I doubted it.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc4.description: I suspected that Victoria could be responsible for the Seattle newborns and I suggested that she might be creating and directing them as her army from a safe distance.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc4.source_text: I think it’s all connected. Not just the two, but all three. "Three bad things have happened since you came back." "Because I agree with Jasper — the Volturi love their rules. They would probably do a better job anyway." "See — she could have gotten the idea there. But she doesn’t know what she’s doing, so the newborns are all out of control."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc4.description: I felt more dependent on Edward's protection and I was shaken by his ferocious longing to finish Victoria himself.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc4.source_text: "She’ll never touch you, Bella," he said. "Yet, what I wouldn’t give to have her that close," he murmured. "Victoria, and anyone else who’s ever thought of hurting you. To have the chance to end this myself. To finish it with my own hands this time."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc5.description: I learned that the visiting wolves planned to arrive in their wolf forms and that Edward said he would have to translate because they did not trust the Cullens to use human forms.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc5.source_text: "A minute and a half. But I’m going to have to translate. They don’t trust us enough to use their human forms."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc5.description: I felt my fear deepen when I remembered the two times I had seen Jacob in his wolf form and how both memories had been terrifying.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc5.source_text: "I swallowed once, remembering the two times I’d seen Jacob in his wolf form — the first time in the meadow with Laurent, the second time on the forest lane where Paul had gotten angry at me. . . . They were both memories of terror."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc5.description: I realized that the wolf pack had grown beyond the six members I had expected and that there were actually ten wolves facing the Cullens.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc5.source_text: "The pack has grown," Edward murmured. "There were ten of them."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc5.description: I noticed that Edward was protective of my feelings and that he was cautious of my reaction as the wolves approached.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc5.source_text: "He nodded, cautious of my reaction." "I tightened my hand around his."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc6.description: I learned that both the vampires and the wolves agreed to watch and not attack the newborns beyond observation.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc6.source_text: I read: "We will watch and listen, but no more. That is the most we can ask of our self-control."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc6.description: I learned the expected arrival time and interception plan for the newborns, including Alice's role in redirecting them.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc6.source_text: I read: "They'll come across the mountains in four days, in the late morning. As they approach, Alice will help us intercept their path."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc6.description: I learned the estimated enemy strength and inexperience, with twenty newborns described as 'children' in skill and strategy.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc6.source_text: I read: "Tonight their numbers stand at twenty. Ten for us, ten for you — it shouldn't be difficult. The numbers may go down. The new ones fight amongst themselves."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc6.description: I learned Jasper's tactical rules for fighting newborns: avoid letting them get arms around you and avoid the obvious kill by attacking from the side and keeping moving.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc6.source_text: I read: "The two most important things you'll need to remember are, first, don't let them get their arms around you and, second, don't go for the obvious kill. That's all they'll be prepared for. As long as you come at them from the side and keep moving, they'll be too confused to respond effectively."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc6.description: I felt reassured by Carlisle's careful approach and explanation, which changed my sense of dread into a more controlled confidence about the plan.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc6.source_text: I read: "Carlisle took a slow, deliberate step forward. It was a careful movement, designed to reassure."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.description: I learned that the wolf pack was very large and intimidating, with more than ten animals led by Sam.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.source_text:
Now that I could see them all, match the vastness with each pair of eyes, it looked like more than ten.
Sam was in the lead, of course.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.description: I learned that Jacob appears as an enormous russet-colored wolf with familiar black eyes and a casual, shaggy stance.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.source_text: The enormous russet-colored wolf seemed to feel my gaze, and he looked up at me with familiar black eyes.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.description: I felt closer to Jacob when I touched his fur and laughed at his wolfish grin and affectionate lick.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.source_text:
I reached my hand out, my fingers trembling slightly, and touched the red-brown fur on the side of his face.
Without warning, Jacob suddenly licked my face from chin to hairline.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.description: I realized that I would not react with terror to the wolves despite earlier fear, and I felt wonder and fascination instead of exhaustion or panic.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.source_text:
My eyes were wide again, exhaustion forgotten.
I stared back at him, trying to believe what I already knew.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.description: I learned that the two groups—the Cullens and the wolves—were tense with each other and that most of the pack withdrew after the encounter.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.source_text:
The other wolves were backing away now, not taking their eyes off the Cullens as they departed.
Soon, they disappeared into the murky forest.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc10.description: I learned that Edward wants to hide me somewhere I haven't been frequently because I have left trails.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc10.source_text: She’s been back and forth too much. She’s left trails all over the place.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc10.description: I learned that Charlie will be with Billy during the event, according to Jacob.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc10.source_text: He’ll be with Billy," Jacob assured me quickly.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc10.description: I felt that Edward was being overcautious but also protective when he insisted on precautions.
I felt hurt when Jacob left abruptly and then trusted Edward when he said Jacob would come back to speak for himself.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc10.source_text: "Why did he leave?" I asked, hurt. "He’s coming back," Edward said. He sighed. "He wants to be able to talk for himself."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc10.description: I learned that I was being considered for evacuation and that hiding me was discussed as a precaution rather than a permanent relocation.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc10.source_text: You can’t evacuate everyone," he said in a gentle voice. "Hiding you is just a precaution."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc11.description: I learned that Bella's scent is very strong and distinct enough to attract attention when combined with Edward's scent.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc11.source_text: Her scent is too strong and, combined with mine, especially distinct. Even if I carried her, it would leave a trail.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc11.description: I felt uncomfortable and self-conscious when Jacob carried me because the close contact felt too intimate.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc11.source_text: I was pouting, uncomfortable in Jacob’s arms. It felt too intimate to me — surely he didn’t need to hold me quite so tightly — and I couldn’t help but wonder what it felt like to him.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc11.description: I noticed that Edward protected and supported me physically by putting his arm around my waist and planning the scent test.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc11.source_text: Edward put his arm around my waist, pulling me closer and supporting my weight.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc12.description: I learned that the plan is to use my scent as a false trail to lure newborns into the clearing.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc12.source_text: “We’re — well,you’re — going to leave a false trail to the clearing, Bella. The newborns are hunting, your scent will excite them, and they’ll come exactly the way we want them to without being careful about it. Alice can already see that this will work.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc12.description: I felt sick and resolved that I wouldn't allow them to endanger both Edward and Jacob for my sake.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc12.source_text: I felt sick. How could they be so eager for this? How could I stand havingboth of them in danger? I couldn’t. I wouldn’t.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc12.description: I learned that Edward planned to bring me Friday afternoon to lay the false trail and that I would be carried afterward to a separate, defensible location while he took another route.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc12.source_text: “I’ll bring her here Friday afternoon to lay the false trail. You can meet us afterward, and carry her to a place I know. Completely out of the way, and easily defensible, not that it will come to that. I’ll take another route there.”

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward carried me home in his arms and that I must have fallen asleep on the way.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: I quote: 'EDWARD CARRIED ME HOME IN HIS ARMS, EXPECTING that I wouldn’t be able to hang on. I must have fallen asleep on the way.'

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc1.description: I learned that I woke up in my bed with light coming from the west so that it felt like afternoon.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: I quote: 'When I woke up, I was in my bed and the dull light coming through my windows slanted in from a strange angle. Almost like it was afternoon.'

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc1.description: I learned that I had been very restless and talking all day according to Edward.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: I quote: 'You’ve been very restless — talking all day.'

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc1.description: I felt reassured by Edward’s explanation that I had earned a day in bed and I accepted staying put for recovery.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: I quote: 'You’d earned a day in bed.'

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc1.description: I felt cared for and watched over when Edward held my hand, guided me, and offered breakfast in bed.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: I quote: 'He held my hand on the way to the kitchen, eyeing me carefully... "Hungry?" he guessed. "Do you want breakfast in bed?"'

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc2.description: I was still wearing the wooden wolf Jacob gave me at the party.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: I was still wearing the gift that Jacob had given me at the party.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc2.description: I felt a fleeting fear that he might crush the little wooden wolf in his palm before I realized he handled it gently.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: For a fleeting moment, I was afraid. Just the slightest twist of his fingers could crush it into splinters.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc2.description: I like homemade gifts and I told him so during the conversation.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: You know I like the homemade kind.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc2.description: I believe Edward is more important than everyone else and that his presence outweighs additional gifts.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: You're more important than everyone else. And you've given meyou . That’s already more than I deserve, and anything else you give me just throws us more out of balance.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.description: I learned that Leah Clearwater is a werewolf and a direct descendant who can transform.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: I quote: 'She’s a direct descendant, all right.'

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.description: I learned that Leah knows me and that her recognition was explicitly mentioned.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: I quote: 'She knows you. Her name is Leah Clearwater.'

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.description: I learned that the pack shares thoughts and that Sam's orders are binding on the pack.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: I quote: 'When Sam gives an order, the pack simply isn’t able to ignore it.'

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.description: I felt sympathy for Leah because I recalled her losses and the pain caused by the imprinting situation.
I noticed that Edward judged Leah as malicious for airing others' private thoughts and that his opinion influenced my mixed feelings toward her.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: I quote: 'She’s making life exceedingly unpleasant for the rest of them.'

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.description: I learned that a rumor about Embry's paternity circulates within the pack's shared consciousness and causes speculation.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: I quote: 'So the prime candidates for his father are Quil Ateara Sr., Joshua Uley, or Billy Black, all of them married at that point, of course.'

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc5.description: I insisted that I had to be in the clearing because I needed to be where Edward was.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc5.source_text: "I have to be in that clearing, Edward."

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc5.description: I accused myself of being cruel and selfish and felt intense guilt for wanting Edward to stay with me.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc5.source_text: Cruel,I accused myself.Selfish, selfish, selfish! Don’t do it!

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc5.description: I realized that Edward was fundamental to my survival and that I could not bear the thought of him leaving me again.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc5.source_text: But the survival instinct was stronger. There was no question that he was fundamental to my survival.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc5.description: I told Edward that my priority was being together with him and that I could live with either him sitting out or me being there.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc5.source_text: “Or to let me be there. Either way, so long as we’re together.”

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc6.description: I felt conflicted by two voices inside me, one urging me to be good and brave and the other telling me to keep quiet.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc6.source_text: Two voices struggled inside me. One that wanted to be good and brave, and one that told the good one to keep her mouth shut.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc6.description: I learned that I had mumbled the phrase the third wife in my sleep and that Edward noticed.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc6.source_text: You were mumbling something about ‘the third wife’ last night. The rest made a little sense, but you lost me there.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc6.description: I noticed Edward showed affection by putting one finger under my chin and tilting my face up to kiss me goodbye.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc6.source_text: He put one finger under my chin and tilted my face up to kiss me goodbye.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc6.description: I worried that my behavior or revelations might make things more dangerous for Alice and I apologized for that possibility.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc6.source_text: I’m sorry," I apologized again. "Do you think this will make it more dangerous for you?

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc6.description: I realized that I had wasted the whole day sleeping and I felt glad that I would not always squander my time that way.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc6.source_text: Wow, I’d really lost the whole day. It felt like such a waste. I was glad I wouldn’t always have to squander my time with sleeping.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc7.description: I was fully dressed and preparing dinner when Charlie came home.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc7.source_text: I was entirely presentable when Charlie got home — fully dressed, hair decent, and in the kitchen putting his dinner on the table.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc7.description: I sat beside Charlie while Alice occupied Edward's usual place and I watched that make Charlie happy.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc7.source_text: Alice sat in Edward’s usual place, and this seemed to make Charlie’s day.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc7.description: I agreed to go shopping with Alice and I cleared my Saturday for an all-day trip out of town.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc7.source_text:
“Sure,” I agreed. “Shopping. Okay.”
“You don’t have anything going on Saturday, do you? I want to get out of town to shop, and it will be an all-day thing.”

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc7.description: I became suspicious that Alice's devastated expressions were partly an act to influence events.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc7.source_text: It was probably an act, but it was too perfect for me to be positive.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc7.description: I accepted a closer, cooperative plan with Alice by agreeing to accompany her shopping.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc8.description: I learned that Alice left with Edward.
I learned that Edward claimed they were leaving early in the morning.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc8.source_text: He claimed they were leaving early in the morning

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc8.description: I learned that we were meeting with the wolves in an hour.
I realized that Edward sometimes seemed unsure of his hold on me.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc8.source_text: It was mind-boggling, but, somehow, he still seemed unsure of his hold on me.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc8.description: I felt that being alone with Edward would mean just him and me.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc8.source_text: Just him and me — really alone.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc9.description: I enjoyed the trip to the clearing more than I had last night and felt less terrified.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc9.source_text: I enjoyed the trip to the clearing more than I had last night.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc9.description: I began to almost believe that maybe it would be okay and that I could see past what was coming.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc9.source_text: I could see past what was coming, and almost believe that maybe it would be okay.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc9.description: I realized that I was still guilty and afraid but able to function rather than paralyzed with terror.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc9.source_text: I still felt guilty, still afraid, but I wasn’t terrified anymore. I could function.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc9.description: I felt a conflicted sympathy toward the wolves as friends who could bleed and die, increasing my concern for them.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc9.source_text: Friends who didn’t look nearly as indestructible as Emmett and Jasper did, moving faster than cobra strikes while the moonlight glinted off their granite-hard skin. Friends who didn’t seem to understand the danger involved here. Friends who were still somewhat mortal, friends who could bleed, friends who could die. . . .

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.description: I felt worried about the upcoming fight and told Jacob that I didn’t want to watch.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.source_text: “I’m fine,” I answered, not needing the translation that Edward was about to give. “Just worried, you know.”

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.description: I sat down on the cold ground and pulled my fingers through Jacob’s neck fur while he lay beside me.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.source_text: Absently, I began pulling my fingers through the fur on his neck.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.description: I realized that Jacob’s wolf form brought back an easy, effortless friendship that I thought had been lost.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.source_text: It was strange. Even though he was in this bizarre form, this felt more like the way Jake and I used to be — the easy, effortless friendship that was as natural as breathing in and out — than the last few times I’d been with Jacob while he was human.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.description: I felt comforted and closer to Jacob when he scooted closer and pressed his warm fur against my left side.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.source_text: Jacob scooted himself closer to me, pressing his warm fur against my left side.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc1.description: I walked from Spanish toward the cafeteria holding hands with Edward and felt oddly buoyant.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: IFELT ODDLY BUOYANT AS I WALKED FROM SPANISHtoward the cafeteria, and it wasn’t just because I was holding hands with the most perfect person on the planet, though that was certainly part of it.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc1.description: I considered Edward the most perfect person on the planet.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: I was holding hands with the most perfect person on the planet

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc1.description: My knowledge that my sentence was served made me feel like a free woman again.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: Maybe it was the knowledge that my sentence was served and I was a free woman again.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc1.description: I noticed posters and spilled fliers covering the cafeteria walls with reminders about yearbooks, class rings, graduation gowns, tassels, class campaigns, and prom.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: Posters crowded together on the cafeteria walls, and the trashcans wore a colorful skirt of spilled-over fliers: reminders to buy yearbooks, class rings, and announcements; deadlines to order graduation gowns, hats, and tassels; neon-bright sales pitches — the juniors campaigning for class office; ominous, rose-wreathed advertisements for this year’s prom.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc1.description: I learned that the big dance was scheduled for the coming weekend and that I had an ironclad promise from Edward I would not attend.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: The big dance was this coming weekend, but I had an ironclad promise from Edward that I would not be subjected to that again. After all, I’d already hadthat human experience.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc1.description: I felt nervous to the point of nausea about the ending of the school year even though other students seemed pleased.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: The ending of the school year did not give me the pleasure it seemed to give the other students. Actually, I felt nervous to the point of nausea whenever I thought of it.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc2.description: I learned that I had not sent announcements because Renée already knew when I was graduating.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: "No," I answered Angela. "There's no point, really. Renée knows when I'm graduating. Who else is there?"

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc2.description: I learned that Charlie un-grounded me the previous night.
I learned that I volunteered to help Angela hand-address invitations despite my awful handwriting.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: "I'll help you," I volunteered. "If you don't mind my awful handwriting."

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc2.description: I felt surprised and newly free about being un-grounded but decided to delay big celebrations to be cautious and confirm Charlie's seriousness.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: "I'm more surprised than you are. I was sure I would at least have finished high school before he set me free." and "Look, let's give it a couple of days to make sure he wasn't joking. It's a school night, anyway."

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc2.description: I noticed Edward smile and I inferred that he liked my fulfilling Charlie's conditions without involving werewolves.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: From the corner of my eye, I saw Edward smile. He must like that, too — me fulfilling Charlie's conditions without involving werewolves.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc2.description: I noticed Alice's tendency to scrutinize my clothing and to imagine grandiose plans, which made me self-conscious and wary of over-the-top celebrations.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: Alice was scrutinizing my boring jeans-and-a-t-shirt outfit in a way that made me self-conscious. Probably plotting another makeover. ... Alice's ideas were usually a little grandiose for me, and I could see it in her eyes now — the tendency to take things too far kicking into action.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc2.description: I learned that we agreed to celebrate the weekend rather than that night.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc3.description: I learned that I have a persistent intrusive image of Jacob’s face crumpled in pain that returns at regular intervals.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc3.source_text: It popped into my thoughts at regular intervals like some annoying alarm clock set to sound every half hour, filling my head with the image of Jacob’s face crumpled in pain.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc3.description: I felt that my freedom was incomplete and less gratifying because I could go anywhere except La Push and could do anything except see Jacob.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc3.source_text: Sure, I was free to go to anywhere I wanted — except La Push; free to do anything I wanted — except see Jacob.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc3.description: I became disgruntled and restless during the discussion about plans in Port Angeles or Hoquiam.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc3.source_text: While they discussed things to do in Port Angeles or maybe Hoquiam, I began to feel disgruntled.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc3.description: I waited anxiously for a chance to ask Edward what Alice had seen in her vision but I had no private moment to do so.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc3.source_text: I waited anxiously for a chance to ask Edward what Alice had seen in her vision, but the afternoon passed without one minute of alone time.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc4.description: I observed Edward slow his pace to match Ben’s after lunch and talk about an assignment he had already finished.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc4.source_text: After lunch, Edward slowed his pace to match Ben’s, talking about some assignment I knew he’d already finished.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc4.description: I watched Edward strike up a conversation with Mike Newton and walk with him toward the parking lot after the final bell.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc4.source_text: When the final bell rang, Edward struck up a conversation with Mike Newton of all people, falling into step beside him as Mike headed for the parking lot.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc4.description: I began to believe Edward was deliberately avoiding being alone with me and dodging my questions.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc4.source_text: It looked to me like Edward was trying to avoid my questions.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc4.description: I felt that Alice might have seen something at lunch that Edward did not want me to know, which made me tense.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc4.source_text: I waited, wondering if he would bring it up himself. He didn’t, and this made me tense. Whathad Alice seen today at lunch? Something he didn’t want to tell me

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc4.description: I grew more suspicious of Edward's secrecy and resolved to confront him when he was alone so I could handle whatever he revealed.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc4.source_text: Fine. He would have to be alone with me soon enough. It was only a matter of time.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc5.description: I noted that I had an unanswered e-mail from my mother that needed attention.
