tw-book3-chapter2_Sc5.source_text: There was an unanswered e-mail from my mom to attend to, and she got panicky when I took too long.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc5.description: I feel that I would spend the majority of my time kissing Edward and that kissing him is deeply intoxicating.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc5.source_text: If I had my way, I would spend the majority of my time kissing Edward.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc5.description: I realized that I view myself as very different from my mother, seeing myself as thoughtful, cautious, and the responsible one.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc5.source_text: I was a very different person from my mother. Someone thoughtful and cautious. The responsible one, the grown-up.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc5.description: I learned that Charlie didn’t throw a fit when Edward picked me up for school, indicating some tolerance for Edward being around.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc5.source_text: Charlie didn’t throw a fit when you picked me up for school.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc6.description: I recognized that the flat black box with wires was the car stereo given to me by Emmett, Rosalie, and Jasper for my last birthday.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc6.source_text: After a second, I recognized the car stereo Emmett, Rosalie, and Jasper had given me for my last birthday.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc6.description: I learned that the stereo was damaged with wires curling crookedly away from the main square in a way that didn’t look healthy.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc6.source_text: He was examining a flat black box with wires curling crookedly away from the main square in a way that didn’t look healthy for whatever it was.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc6.description: I discovered that Esme and Carlisle had given me a voucher for airplane tickets to visit Renée in Florida and that it was another present.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc6.source_text: It was another present — the voucher for airplane tickets that Esme and Carlisle had given me so that I could visit Renée in Florida.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc6.description: I learned from Edward that the airplane ticket vouchers were about to expire.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc6.source_text: Do you realize these are about to expire?

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc6.description: I felt surprised and reluctant to remember my disastrous eighteenth birthday when Edward brought it up, even though he seemed more sensitive about it than I was.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc6.source_text: My disastrous eighteenth birthday — with all its far-reaching consequences — wasn’t something I cared to remember, and I was surprised that he would bring it up.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc6.description: I feared that my voice would shake when Edward reminded me about the voucher and the birthday, so I didn’t answer immediately.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc6.source_text: I didn’t answer, for fear my voice would shake.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc7.description: I decided not to visit Renée this weekend to avoid fighting with Charlie and to prevent further fallout.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc7.source_text: Not this weekend. I don’t want to fight with Charlie. Not so soon after he’s forgiven me.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc7.description: I stated that nobody has custody of me because I am an adult.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc7.source_text: Nobody has custody of me. I’m an adult.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc7.description: I thought that if my mother saw how happy I was with Edward, she would tell Charlie to ease up.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc7.source_text: And maybe, if she saw how happy I was with Edward, she would tell Charlie to ease up.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc7.description: I suspected that Edward's sudden insistence on visiting Renée might have been intended to distract me from my earlier worries.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc7.source_text: I’d almost forgotten my worries about this afternoon — had that been his intention?

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc7.description: I learned from Edward that Alice has been seeing Jasper in a strange place in the southwest and that Jasper has no conscious intentions to go back.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc7.source_text: She’s been seeing Jasper in a strange place, somewhere in the southwest, she thinks, near his former . . . family. But he has no conscious intentions to go back.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc8.description: I learned that Edward's parents gave me airplane tickets on my last birthday so I could visit Renée.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc8.source_text: Did Bella ever tell you that my parents gave her airplane tickets on her last birthday, so that she could visit Renée?

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc8.description: I learned that the airplane tickets Edward mentioned are about to expire and that Edward felt Esme might be hurt if I did not use them.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc8.source_text: They're about to expire. I think it might hurt Esme’s feelings if Bella doesn’t use her gift. Not that she’d say anything.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc8.description: I learned that I cooked stroganoff from Grandma Swan’s recipe for Charlie with Edward helping me.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc8.source_text: I made stroganoff from Grandma Swan’s recipe, because I was sucking up.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc8.description: I realized I had genuinely forgotten about the plane tickets when Charlie reacted with surprise.
I wondered if Edward would take issue with Charlie spending time in La Push and felt uncertain about how Edward viewed Charlie's presence there.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc8.source_text: I wondered if Edward would have a problem with Charlie hanging out in La Push.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc9.description: I learned that Edward said his parents had given one ticket for me and one for himself.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc9.source_text: “Just one for her . . . and one for me.”

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc9.description: I felt more confident asserting my adulthood and independence after arguing with my father about the trip.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc9.source_text: “I’m not a child, Dad. And I’m not grounded anymore, remember?”

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc9.description: I perceived my relationship with my father as more adversarial and recognized his prejudice against Edward during the dispute.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc9.source_text: “I’ll do my time without complaining when I’ve done something wrong, Dad, but I’m not going to put up with your prejudices.”

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc11.description: I learned that I spent the evening with Alice and Jasper and that Edward beat Alice at chess while I lost to Jasper.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc11.source_text: Hung out with Alice and Jasper. Edward beat Alice at chess, and then I played Jasper. He buried me.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc11.description: I revealed that I am a virgin and that I have no immediate plans to change that status.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc11.source_text: I am a . . . virgin, and I have no immediate plans to change that status.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc11.description: I felt reassured when Charlie's face smoothed and he seemed to believe me after I said I was a virgin.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc11.source_text: We both cringed, but then Charlie’s face smoothed out. He seemed to believe me.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc11.description: I noticed that Charlie remains awkward but caring in his role as my father and that he tries to be open-minded about my relationship choices.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc11.source_text: I am your father. I have responsibilities. I will try to be open-minded, though. I know the times have changed.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc12.description: I learned that Edward was long gone and that he would not be back until Charlie was asleep.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc12.source_text: Edward was long gone and he wouldn’t be back until Charlie was asleep — he was probably out hunting or something to pass the time —

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc12.description: I learned that Jacob had refused to answer my phone calls since Edward’s return.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc12.source_text: Jacob had refused to answer my phone calls since Edward’s return.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc12.description: I decided that Edward was only concerned about my safety and that his anger was not a sufficient reason to avoid seeing Jacob.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc12.source_text: Edward was only concerned about my safety, and I knew that there was really no problem on that count.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc12.description: I needed to see Jacob to replace the awful last memory of his face warped and twisted by pain so I could have peace of mind.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc12.source_text: Besides, I needed tosee him — see him smiling again the way he used to. I needed to replace that awful last memory of his face warped and twisted by pain if I was ever going to have any peace of mind.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc12.description: I discovered that Charlie unexpectedly granted me permission to go see Jake when I asked him.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc12.source_text:
“You care if I go see Jake tonight?” I asked breathlessly. “I won’t stay long.”

“Sure, kid. No problem. Stay as long as you like.”

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc13.description: I learned that my future abruptly disappeared when I mingled my fate with the wolves.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc13.source_text: She got nervous when your future rather abruptly disappeared five minutes ago.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc13.description: I learned that Alice cannot see the wolves, which left her unable to tell if I had come home.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc13.source_text: Because she can’t see the wolves, you know.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc13.description: I felt more exposed and uneasy about the wolves and about my safety after hearing that my future could vanish and that Alice could not verify my whereabouts.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc13.source_text: Alice saw you disappear, and she couldn’t even tell if you’d come home or not.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc13.description: I noticed Edward’s protectiveness and anxiety and I understood that he watches me closely and will act to keep me safe.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc13.source_text: I’ll put your car back together in time for school, in case you’d like to drive yourself.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc14.description: I learned that my truck won't start.
I refused Charlie's offers to look at the truck and to use his car.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc14.source_text: "Want me to look at it?" "No. I'll try it in the morning." "Want to use my car?" "No. I'm tired," I grumbled.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc14.description: I know that I wasn't supposed to drive Charlie's police cruiser.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc14.source_text: I wasn't supposed to drive his police cruiser.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc14.description: I felt nearly as desperate as Charlie to get to La Push.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc14.source_text: Charlie must be really desperate to get me to La Push. Nearly as desperate as I was.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc14.description: I felt tired and irritated and I chose to end the conversation quickly.
I perceived Charlie as desperate and I judged his insistence as motivated by that desperation.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc14.source_text: Charlie must be really desperate to get me to La Push.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc14.description: I slammed the window roughly until the glass trembled and then I opened it wide.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc14.source_text: I shoved the metal frame roughly — it crashed shut and the glass trembled. I stared at the shivering black glass for a long moment, until it was still. Then I sighed, and opened the window as wide as it would go.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc14.description: I maintained a facade of normalcy in front of Charlie by pretending nothing was wrong.

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.description: I learned that my bag was packed for my two-day visit with Alice and that it waited on the passenger seat of my truck.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: I read: "I was packed for my two-day visit with 'Alice,' and my bag waited for me on the passenger seat of my truck."

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.description: I learned that I had given the concert tickets to Angela, Ben, and Mike and that Mike was going to take Jessica.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: I read: "I’d given the concert tickets to Angela, Ben, and Mike. Mike was going to take Jessica, which was exactly as I’d hoped."

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.description: I learned that Billy borrowed Old Quil Ateara’s boat and invited Charlie down for open sea fishing before the afternoon game.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: I read: "Billy had borrowed Old Quil Ateara’s boat and invited Charlie down for some open sea fishing before the afternoon game started."

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.description: I learned that Collin and Brady, the two youngest werewolves, were staying behind to protect La Push and that both were thirteen.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: I read: "Collin and Brady, the two youngest werewolves, were staying behind to protect La Push — though they were just children, both of them only thirteen."

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.description: I realized that I was ready to join Edward's family and his world and to act as an asset rather than a liability.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: I read: "I was ready to join his family and his world. The fear and guilt and anguish I was feeling now had taught me that much."

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.description: I understood that I would insist on keeping certain human experiences even as I contemplated becoming inhuman.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: I read: "I’d had plenty of time to think through the ramifications of Jasper and Emmett’s bet — to figure out the things I was willing to lose with my humanity, and the part that I was not willing to give up."

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.description: I acknowledged that the desperate way I loved Edward had not changed despite other developments.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: I read: "One piece, because there were some things that had not changed, and that included the desperate way I loved him."

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.description: I noticed that I felt nervous while driving down the long path to his house and that Edward sat in the passenger seat smiling at my slow pace.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: I read: "As decided as I was, I wasn’t surprised that I still felt nervous as I drove down the long path to his house — I didn’t know how to do what I was trying to do, and that guaranteed me some serious jitters. He sat in the passenger seat, fighting a smile at my slow pace."

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.description: I experienced Edward opening my door, lifting me from the cab with one arm, slinging my bag over his shoulder, kissing me, and carrying me into the house.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: I read: "As soon as I cut the engine he was at my door, opening it for me. He lifted me from the cab with one arm, slinging my bag out of the truck bed and over his shoulder with the other. His lips found mine as I heard him kick the truck’s door shut behind me. Without breaking the kiss, he swung me up so that I was cradled in his arms and carried me into the house."

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.description: I decided that Edward would never have to choose between me and his family again and that we would aim to be partners like Alice and Jasper.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: I read: "We would be partners, like Alice and Jasper. Next time, I would do my part. He would never have to make the choice between me and his family again."

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc2.description: I observed that Bella was not frightened by the kiss and experienced enthusiasm rather than panic.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: This kissing did not frighten me. It wasn’t like before when I could feel the fear and panic leaking through his control.

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc2.description: I noticed Bella moved from cautious optimism about getting what she wanted to a quick return to realism about its difficulty.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc2.source_text:
I began to feel cautiously optimistic. Perhaps getting what I wanted would not be as difficult as I’d expected it to be.
No, of course it was going to be just exactly that difficult.

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc2.description: I learned that Bella received a silver bracelet augmented by a brilliant heart-shaped crystal and found it beautiful.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc2.source_text:
On the opposite side of the chain from the wolf, there now hung a brilliant heart-shaped crystal.
“You forgot the most important similarity,” I murmured. “It’s beautiful.”

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc2.description: I sensed Bella’s physical and emotional closeness to Edward deepen when she leaned into him and cuddled into his side.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: I leaned into him, ducking my head under his arm and cuddling into his side.

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc3.description: I proposed negotiating the marriage condition that Edward had set because I wanted to clarify other details.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: “Well, I guess, first, I wanted to talk to you about that whole ridiculous marriage condition thing.”

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc3.description: I became worried that after becoming nonhuman I might be consumed by slaughter and might not want Edward the same way I do now.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: “All of you just seem so convinced that the only thing I’m going to be interested in, afterward, is slaughtering everyone in town,”

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc3.description: I learned that I could ask Edward for a specific thing to be allowed before my transformation and that he gave an earnest promise to grant it.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: “Tell me what you want, and you can have it.”

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc4.description: I learned that I felt too innocent and had no idea how to be seductive.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: I was too innocent — which was, of course, central to the discussion. I didn’t have the faintest idea how to be seductive.

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc4.description: I showed that I tried to escalate intimacy by kissing Edward and attempting to unbutton his shirt.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: I took a deep breath and shifted forward so that I was kneeling on the bed. Then I wrapped my arms around his neck and kissed him. My fingers slid down his neck to the collar of his shirt. The trembling didn’t help as I tried to hurry to undo the buttons before he stopped me.

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc4.description: I experienced that Edward immediately pushed me away and refused my advance.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: He pushed me away at once, his face heavily disapproving. "Be reasonable, Bella."

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc4.description: I felt rejected and briefly believed I was unwanted and unwantable despite knowing his protective motives.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: Rejection washed through me, instinctive and strong. I scowled at the golden comforter that matched his eyes and tried to banish the reflex reaction that told me I was unwanted and unwantable.

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc4.description: I recognized that Edward desires me but places my safety above acting on that desire.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: "You know why I have to say no," he murmured. "You know that I want you, too."

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc4.description: I doubted my own desirability in spite of his words and felt awkward and insecure.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: I doubted if awkward, self-conscious, and inept added up to desirable in anyone’s book.

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc5.description: I learned that Bella listed marriage, tuition payment, more time, and a faster car as conditions she offered to secure a chance to be transformed.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: “Tell me if I have anything wrong.” I tried to sound detached. “Your demands are marriage” — I couldn’t say the word without making a face — “paying my tuition, more time, and you wouldn’t mind if my vehicle went a little faster.”

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc5.description: I realized that I believe Edward could kill me yet I also believe he would not intentionally do so because of how he feels about me.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc5.source_text:
“Bella, I could kill you,” he whispered.

“I don’t think you could.”

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc5.description: I recognized that I fear the physical consequences of becoming a vampire, specifically that I would always be extremely thirsty and crave blood above all.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: “But that will always be what I want most, won’t it?” I challenged. “Blood, blood, and more blood!”

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc5.description: I became willing to accept Edward’s demands, including marriage and financial arrangements, in order to be allowed to try the transformation.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: “I’ll marry you. I’ll let you pay for Dartmouth, and I won’t complain about the bribe to get me in. You can even buy me a fast car if that makes you happy! Just . . .please.”

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc5.description: I noticed a change in my understanding of Edward as someone who is emotionally torn and in pain at the thought of refusing my plea.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: “This is unbearable. So many things I’ve wanted to give you — and this is what you decide to demand. Do you have any idea how painful it is, trying to refuse you when you plead with me this way?”

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc6.description: I learned that I felt powerful and brave after achieving a momentary advantage in kissing Edward.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: The thrill of victory was a strange high; it made me feel powerful. Brave.

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc6.description: I learned that Edward kissed me with a brand-new edge of conflict and desperation while his body felt colder than ever to my overheated skin.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: His mouth was not gentle; there was a brand-new edge of conflict and desperation in the way his lips moved. I trembled, but it was not from the chill.

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc6.description: I realized that Edward would not simply push me away and that he desired me as intensely as I desired him.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: I was wrong. His mouth was not gentle; there was a brand-new edge of conflict and desperation in the way his lips moved. He didn’t stop kissing me.

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc6.description: My relationship with Edward now explicitly includes his demand that we wait until marriage before having sex.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: 'I’m not saying no,' he reassured me. 'I’m just saying not tonight.' 'That’s the deal — take it or leave it. Compromise, remember?'

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc7.description: I promised to marry Edward and intend to keep that promise.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc7.source_text: "I said I would marry you, and I will. I promise. I swear."

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc7.description: I refuse to sleep with Edward before marriage and I emphasized that I 'technically' cannot ever sleep with him.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc7.source_text: "So that’s it. You won’t sleep with me until we’re married." "Technically, I can’t eversleep with you."

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc7.description: I admitted that I was 'a little bit' happy about our engagement despite earlier resistance.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc7.source_text: "A little bit," I admitted when I could speak.

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc7.description: I felt that Edward was playful, teasing, and protective, and I recognized his desire to protect my virtue.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc7.source_text: "No, silly girl," he muttered against my shoulder. "I’m trying to protectyours. And you’re making it shockingly difficult."

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc1.description: I observed that Bella woke to a bright sun and wind that rocked the treetops.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: The sun was bright outside the window-wall when I woke, with small clouds scuttling too quickly across the sky. The wind rocked the treetops till the whole forest looked as if it was going to shake apart.

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc1.description: I learned that Bella felt emotionally burdened after returning the hand-me-down ring even though she tried to give it back without hurting his feelings.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: Somehow, my plan for last night had gone horribly awry, and I needed come to grips with the consequences. Though I’d given back the hand-me-down ring as soon as I could do it without hurting his feelings, my left hand felt heavier, like it was still in place, just invisible.

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc1.description: I realized that Bella believed the ceremony would be brief and manageable but that she was starting to feel overwhelmed by the situation.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: This shouldn’t bother me, I reasoned. It was no big thing — a road trip to Vegas. The ceremony certainly couldn’t take very long; no more than fifteen minutes at the most, right? So I could handle that.

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc1.description: I noticed that Bella considers Alice like a sister and felt guilty for having excluded her from the wedding plans.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc1.source_text:
I love you like you were my own sister.
“To me, Alice, you are my sister.”

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc1.description: I learned that Bella was asked to call Jacob to tell him to meet them and that Jacob was not home when she called, so Billy promised to contact a werewolf.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc1.source_text:
“Why don’t you call Jacob and tell him we’ll be ready for him in an hour or so. He knows where to meet us.”
Jacob wasn’t home, but Billy promised to call around until he could find an available werewolf to pass the news to.

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc2.description: I used my hair to strengthen the trail by draping strands over ferns and wedging them into branches.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: I quote: I draped them over the ferns; I wedged another hair into a broken branch that cut through my path.

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc2.description: I injured my left hand when a small branch snapped and gouged into my palm during a fall.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: I quote: I fell; a small branch snapped off under my left hand and gouged into my palm.

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc2.description: I felt resigned that Alice would probably get her way and I admitted that I am a sucker for guilt trips.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: I quote: I had a sinking feeling that Alice was going to get her way, mostly because she was totally unscrupulous when there was something she wanted, and also because I was a sucker for guilt trips.

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc2.description: I preferred a small wedding with just us and I joked that Emmett could get a clerical license off the Internet.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: I quote: Well, even if she does get her way, we can keep it small; Just us; Emmett can get a clerical license off the Internet.

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc3.description: I learned that I have only kissed Edward and that I do not count Jacob's kiss as a real kiss.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: “Edward is the only person I’ve ever kissed.” “Besides me.” “But I don’t count that as a kiss, Jacob. I think of it more as an assault.”

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc3.description: I felt guilty and cowardly for convincing Edward to stay with me and feared responsibility if anyone was hurt.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: “Edward isn’t going to fight tomorrow.” “I am making him stay with me. I am a huge coward.”

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc3.description: I recognized Jacob's love and protectiveness and felt ashamed about how my choice affected him.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: “That doesn’t mean that he loves you more than I do.” “Don’t cry, Bella,”

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.description: I learned that the werewolf pack structure includes only one Alpha.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: "There’s only one Alpha," he answered automatically.

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.description: I learned that Levi Uley was considered 'sort of a Beta' in the lineage Jacob referenced.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: "Sort of a Beta, I guess." He snorted at my term. "Like me."

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.description: I felt unexpected awe and began to see Jacob as more of a grown-up than I had previously credited him for.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: I stared at him, feeling an unexpected kind of awe for my friend. He was more of a grown-up than I’d ever given him credit for.

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.description: I began to address Jacob as 'Chief Jacob' and felt a new respect when I said the words.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: "Chief Jacob," I whispered, smiling at the way the words sounded together.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc1.description: I felt the temperature dropping and sensed the cold through the down bag and my jacket.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: The temperature was dropping. I could feel it through the down bag, through my jacket.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc1.description: I was fully dressed with my hiking boots still laced into place.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: I was fully dressed, my hiking boots still laced into place.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc1.description: I decided I didn't want to go outside because I was terrified of the storm and thought staying in the tent might preserve our efforts.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: No, I’m f-f-f-f-f-fine, r-r-r-really. I don’t w-w-w-want to g-go outside.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc1.description: I noticed Edward sat as far from me as possible and was afraid to even breathe on me, which made me see him as protective but anxious.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: Edward sat as far from me as possible in the cramped space, afraid to even breathe on me when I was already so cold.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc2.description: I learned that I was extremely cold and shivering to the point of stuttering incoherently.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: "I tried to ask what they were talking about, but all that came out of my mouth was, “W-w-w-w-w-w,” as the shivering made me stutter uncontrollably."

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc2.description: I learned that the parka was frozen and meant for tomorrow rather than for immediate use.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: "The parka’s for tomorrow — she’s too cold to warm it up by herself. It’s frozen."

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc2.description: I felt conflicted about Jacob because I was grateful for his help yet outraged at his invasion of my personal space.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: "I stared at him in outrage. No wonder Edward was reacting this way."

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc2.description: I became more fearful of conflict as I pleaded with them not to fight and felt terrified of the consequences.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc3.description: I learned that Bella was extremely cold, shivering, and had blue lips.
I felt Bella shift from resistance to acceptance as she stopped objecting and settled into Jacob's warmth.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: And then I couldn’t object — I didn’t want to anymore. He was so warm. His arms constricted around me, holding me snugly against his bare chest.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc3.description: I realized that Bella found safety and comfort in Jacob's physical closeness despite ongoing tensions with Edward.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: It was already warm and snug inside the sleeping bag. Jacob's body heat seemed to radiate from every side — maybe because there was so much of him.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob is furrier because his hair is longer.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: "Because my hair is longer," he said, amused — my question hadn’t offended him, at least.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob grew his hair out because he thought I liked it better long.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: "I was growing my hair out because . . . it seemed like you liked it better long."

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.description: I remembered that Jacob used to be my replacement sun and felt a renewed warmth toward him in that moment.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: This warm little space made me think of the early days with Jacob, and I remembered how it used to be when he was my replacement sun, the warmth that made my empty life livable.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.description: I understood that Seth was outside and that the howling was part of the pack's watch and communication.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: "Seth is here," Edward muttered to Jacob, and I suddenly understood the point of the howling.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.description: I felt awkward admitting I like Jacob's hair both ways and tried to reassure him that he need not be inconvenienced for me.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: I, er, like it both ways, Jake. You don’t need to be . . . inconvenienced.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc5.description: I heard them talk about me and could not bring myself to ask them to stop.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc5.source_text: I was too far gone to ask them to stop talking about me like I wasn’t there.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc5.description: I realized that Edward admitted he was jealous of Jacob.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc5.source_text: “Yes,” Edward answered an unspoken thought in a murmur so low I barely made it out. “I’m jealous of that, too.”

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc5.description: I noticed Jacob act protectively by tightening his arms around me while Edward expressed a grudging gratitude for Jacob’s presence.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc5.source_text:
The wind ripped around the tent, shaking it like an earthquake. Jacob’s arms tightened around me protectively.

“Thank you,” Edward whispered. “Odd as this might sound, I suppose I’m glad you’re here, Jacob.”

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc6.description: I learned that Edward believed I was "more or less safe" with Jacob and that he stopped pressuring me to extremes for that reason.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc6.source_text: After I’d accepted that she was more or less safe with you — as safe as Bella ever is — it seemed best to stop driving her to extremes.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc6.description: I realized that I feel guilty about how his leaving affected me and that Edward acknowledged I "feel horrible about bringing that up."
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc6.source_text: She feels horrible about bringing that up, but she’s right.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc6.description: I know that I have a horror of getting older and that my birthday in September is a pressure point for my decision.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc6.source_text: She has a horror of getting older, and her birthday is in September. . . .

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc7.description: I learned that Bella might be okay after time and that there is a very good chance she would be okay.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc7.source_text: I think there’s a very good chance that she would be okay. After time.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc7.description: I learned that Bella had jumped off a cliff in March, which affected the timing of potential outcomes for her.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc7.source_text: if she hadn’t jumped off a cliff in March . . . and if you’d waited another six months to check on her.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc7.description: I learned that Bella could be human again and live with Charlie and Renée and potentially have children and grow up.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc7.source_text: she could be human, with Charlie and Renée, and she could grow up, and have kids and . . . be Bella.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc7.description: I noticed that Bella currently wants Edward, and that Edward intends to remain with her as long as she chooses him.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc7.source_text: As long as she wants me, I’m here.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc8.description: I learned that Bella seemed reluctant to tell the story about a third wife.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc8.source_text: It’s just a story that Bella seemed reluctant to tell me about the other day. Something about a third wife . . . ?

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc8.description: I learned that Bella wants to be in the clearing to do what little she can.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc8.source_text: She wants to be there in the clearing. To do what little she can, as she puts it.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc8.description: I noticed that Edward stayed with Bella partly so she could be present at the clearing.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc8.source_text: That was the secondary reason for my staying with her tomorrow. She’s quite inventive when she wants something.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc8.description: I noticed that Edward hummed the narrator's lullaby and that the hum helped the narrator sink into unconsciousness.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc8.source_text: But it was my lullaby he hummed, and, despite my growing discomfort with this whispered dream, I sank deeper into unconsciousness . . . into other dreams that made better sense. . . .

tw-book3-chapter23_Sc1.description: I woke up with Jacob's arms wrapped around me and I was sweating in the tent.
tw-book3-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I read: "Jacob was snoring lightly in my ear, his arms still wrapped around me."

tw-book3-chapter23_Sc1.description: I feared that this might be the last time I would see Jacob and I felt physical pain at the thought.
tw-book3-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I read: "Pain crackled down my spine and lodged in my stomach as I abruptly realized that this could be the last time I would see him."

tw-book3-chapter23_Sc1.description: I put myself between Edward and Jacob to stop their fight and I discovered that my touch calmed Jacob.
tw-book3-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I read: "The growling erupted from all around. I yelled, scrambling awkwardly to put myself between them... Under my touch, Jacob began to calm himself."

tw-book3-chapter23_Sc1.description: I leaned against Edward's shoulder and I agreed with him that we would stay together no matter what.
tw-book3-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I read: "I huddled in my coats, and leaned against Edward’s shoulder... 'We stay together. No matter what.' 'No matter what,' he agreed."

tw-book3-chapter23_Sc2.description: I realized that Jacob heard our conversation and responded with an agonized howl.
tw-book3-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: "The silence outside the tent was ripped apart by an earsplitting howl of pain."

tw-book3-chapter23_Sc2.description: I believed I was a hideous person who was hurting Jacob every time I turned around.
tw-book3-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: "I’m hurting him. Every time I turn around, I’m hurting him again."

tw-book3-chapter23_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward apologized for doing something that caused Jacob's reaction.
I discovered that Edward would go to find Jacob and asked me to stay by the tent.
tw-book3-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: "Stay by the tent. I’ll be back soon."

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc2.description: I kissed Edward impulsively to force him to fight back and to make myself forget Jacob and my own shame.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "Make me forget him. Make me forget my own name. Fight back!"

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc2.description: I became convinced that I wanted every part of Edward and that I would claim what I needed from him despite circumstances.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "You said I could have any part of you I wanted. I want this part. I want every part."

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc2.description: I noticed that I was physically tense and prone to panic as I clenched my hand until Edward smoothed my fingers to calm me.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "I didn’t realize my left hand was clenched into a fist, nails biting into my bandaged palm, until Edward took it and gently smoothed my fingers out."

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc2.description: I felt conflicted and ashamed about Jacob’s presence in my thoughts and I tried to actively erase him from my mind.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "Make me forget him. Make me forget my own name."

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc2.description: I perceived fear for Alice’s safety and I voiced worry that Alice’s small size might be a problem if she were caught.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "Alice is so small," I moaned.

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc3.description: I heard that the first group was in the clearing and that fighting could be heard.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: I read: "We can hear the fighting"

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc3.description: I learned that Victoria had crossed Edward's scent and was following the newborns toward their camp.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: I read: "She crossed my scent, following the newborns in to watch"

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc3.description: I realized that the immediate danger was not in the clearing but had moved to our camp when the sudden silence occurred.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: I read: "The sudden absence of sound was the only warning"

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc3.description: I accepted that I would be willing to die to save my friends and family if necessary.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: I read: "I would die to do it, like the third wife"

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc3.description: I noticed that Edward held my hand and positioned himself protectively between me and the threat.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: I read: "Edward held a defensive position — half-crouched, his arms extended slightly"

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc4.description: I learned that my blood can attract and momentarily stun vampires and that I intended to use that effect again as a distraction.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc4.source_text: That night, my flowing blood had been enough to catch every vampire’s attention, to freeze them all in place for an instant. I prayed it would work that way again.

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc4.description: I understood that Seth had been severely struck by Riley and was incapacitated and in immediate danger.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc4.source_text: Seth’s huge body soared ten feet and crashed into the rocky wall over my head with a force that seemed to shake the whole peak. A low whimper escaped through Seth’s teeth.

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc4.description: I decided that I was willing to deliberately wound myself to create a diversion and help my allies even at great personal cost.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc4.source_text: I raked the point of the shard up my arm, yanking my thick sweater back to expose the skin, and then pressed the sharp tip to the crease at my elbow.

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc4.description: I recognized that Edward was actively protecting me and positioning himself to keep Victoria from reaching me.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc4.source_text: “Nothing is impossible,” Edward murmured, voice velvet soft as he moved another inch closer to her. “Except what you want. You’ll never touch her.”

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc5.description: I thought I heard a familiar, exasperated sigh in the split second I stared into Victoria's eyes.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc5.source_text: But, in the split second that I stared into Victoria’s eyes, I thought I heard a familiar, exasperated sigh.

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc5.description: I felt relief and renewed trust in Edward's protection when I saw that he stood straight and perfect.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc5.source_text: Relief swelled in my heart when I saw that he stood straight and perfect.

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc5.description: I watched Riley's fingers twitch and his arm drag itself mindlessly across the ground after Seth's attack.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc5.source_text: The fingers were still twitching; grasping at blades of grass, Riley’s arm began to drag itself mindlessly across the ground.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc1.description: I could not move and found my feet bolted to the stone so I could not approach Edward.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: I couldn’t go to him — I could not make my feet respond; they were bolted to the stone beneath them.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc1.description: I scrutinized Edward's every action minutely to check for signs of harm.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: I scrutinized his every action minutely, looking for any evidence that he had been harmed.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc1.description: My fear that Edward had been injured eased when my heart slowed to a healthier rhythm after finding nothing wrong.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: My heart slowed to a healthier rhythm when I found nothing.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc1.description: I perceived Edward as physically uninjured and lithe, which affected how I viewed his safety and resilience.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: He was lithe and graceful as ever. I couldn’t even see a tear in his clothes.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc2.description: I learned that Bella had been holding a rock as a crude weapon and that she dropped it only when Edward asked her to do so carefully.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc2.source_text: "Bella, can you drop the rock, please? Carefully. Don’t hurt yourself."

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc2.description: I noticed that Bella's fear shifted toward relief when she understood that her family and friends were safe and that Victoria was no longer pursuing her.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc2.source_text: "It was over. We were all going to be fine."

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc2.description: I observed that Bella physically sought comfort from Edward by burying her face in his chest, sobbing, and then kissing him intimately.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc2.source_text: "Edward caught me, and I buried my face in his chest and started to sob."

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc2.description: I saw Bella reestablish emotional and physical closeness with Edward as she clung to him until she could breathe and then kissed him repeatedly.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc2.source_text: "I clung to him until I could breathe, and then I was kissing him — his chest, his shoulder, his neck — every part of him that I could reach."

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc3.description: I learned that Seth was only feigning that he was hurt.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: “Seth was only feigning that he was hurt, Bella. It was a trick. And then you . . . !”

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc3.description: I felt my relief after the confrontation give way to renewed anxiety when I remembered a complication and my unfinished words to Jacob.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: “It was over. Or . . . was it?” and “About a complication? And Alice, needing to nail down the schedule for Sam. You said it was going to be close. What was going to be close?”

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc3.description: I realized that I still had something important I wanted to say to Jacob but that I could not bring myself to finish, leaving my heart splintered.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: “Hold on. Didn’t you say something before — ?” and “what was I going to say to Jacob? My splintered heart throbbed out a painful, aching beat.”

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward called for Sam, indicating the problem involved others beyond those present.
I changed my belief about the location of the crisis when I realized the emergency was not here with us but concerned the pack elsewhere.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "This time, the crisis was not here. He was using the pack plural."

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc4.description: I saw Edward fall to his knees clutching his head and I heard Seth howl in blistering agony, showing physical pain attacked them suddenly.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "A spasm rocked through Seth's body, and a howl, blistering with agony, ripped from his lungs. Edward fell to his knees at the exact same moment, gripping the sides of his head with two hands, his face furrowed in pain."

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc4.description: I felt compelled to rush to Edward and try to help him, which reinforced my close, protective feelings toward him in moments of crisis.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "I screamed once in bewildered terror, and dropped to my knees beside him. Stupidly, I tried to pull his hands from his face; my palms, clammy with sweat, slid off his marble skin."

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.description: I learned that Alice had foreseen the danger and had relayed it through Sam to Seth.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.source_text: Earlier this morning, Alice saw it and passed it through Sam to Seth.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.description: I learned that the Volturi decided to intercede in the situation.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.source_text: The Volturi decided it was time to intercede.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.description: I felt that it would be safer for us to return to the clearing and present a united front.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.source_text: Mostly, it will be safer for us to present a united front at this point.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.description: I became more afraid of Jane and of Demetri being with her and of the risk if I was separated from the group.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.source_text: Jane’s with them. If she thought we were alone somewhere away from the others, it might tempt her. Like Victoria, Jane will probably guess that I’m with you. Demetri, of course, is with her. He could find me, if Jane asked him to.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.description: I experienced complete physical exhaustion and I was carried by Edward as we escaped through the woods.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.source_text: My body had nothing left. I sagged, and Edward caught me before I could hit the rocks.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.description: I dreaded thinking of Demetri’s face and I felt close to breaking when the image came to mind.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.source_text: I didn’t want to think that name. I didn’t want to see that blindingly exquisite, childlike face in my head.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc6.description: I learned that the Volturi do not honor truces with werewolves.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc6.source_text: "The Volturi do not honor truces with werewolves."

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc6.description: I learned that Alice could not see the newborn who was hiding.
I learned that Leah found the hiding newborn and engaged him alone and that Leah wasn’t hurt.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc6.source_text: "One of the newborns was hiding. . . . Leah found him — she was being stupid, cocky, trying to prove something. She engaged him alone. . . ." "Leah wasn’t hurt,"

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob had been hurt.
I became briefly relieved when I heard Leah was not hurt and then became overwhelmed and fainted when I learned Jacob was hurt.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc6.source_text: "Leah wasn’t hurt,""Jacob," he said. "Everything went black."

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc6.description: I noticed that Edward tried to protect me by reassuring me and deflecting my questions about the events that caused Seth’s howling.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc6.source_text: "Shh, Bella, shh. It’s all going to be fine. Alice can see that." "They had to leave quickly. The Volturi do not honor truces with werewolves." "We’re going to be fine, he had said before . . . and Seth, howling in agony . . . Edward had avoided my first question, distracted me with the Volturi."

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc7.description: I learned that I had been unconscious and trapped in agony, feeling totally disconnected from my body.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc7.source_text: I felt totally disconnected from my body. Like I was caged in some small corner of my head, no longer at the controls. But I couldn’t do anything about it. I couldn’t think. The agony was too strong for that.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc7.description: I moved from desperate fear for Jacob’s life to belief that he would survive when I heard Edward say he was healing.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc7.source_text: “He’s going to live, Bella. Jacob Black is healing as I speak. He’ll be fine.”

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc7.description: I felt reassured by Edward’s physical comfort and by Carlisle’s calm authority, which strengthened my trust in them both.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc7.source_text: “Oh, Bella,” Edward sighed in relief, and his lips touched mine. Carlisle’s expression was serious and reassuring at the same time.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc8.description: I learned that a very young newborn vampire surrendered and that Carlisle offered her the option to surrender rather than immediately destroy her.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc8.source_text: "She surrendered," he told me quietly. "That's one I've never seen before. Only Carlisle would think of offering. Jasper doesn't approve."

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc8.description: I learned that Jasper was physically affected by the newborn encounter and that his condition was described as the venom stinging.
I felt unnerved and imagined that the newborn's feral, red eyes made me look into a possible mirror of my own future.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc8.source_text: I stared at her, mesmerized, wondering if I were looking into a mirror of my future.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc8.description: I realized that Edward prioritized my safety by placing me at the heart of the Cullens' defensive formation.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc8.source_text: A united front, as Edward had said, with me at the heart, in the safest place.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc9.description: I learned that Victoria held a grudge against Bella.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc9.source_text: "Victoria held a grudge against Bella," Edward told her, his voice impassive.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc9.description: I felt more directly threatened after Jane smiled at me and noted that I bring out unusually strong reactions in vampires.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc9.source_text: "This one seems to bring out bizarrely strong reactions in our kind," she observed, smiling directly at me, her face beatific.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc9.description: I believe Edward is protective and assumes responsibility, as he admitted to dealing with the creator when questioned by Jane.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc10.description: I learned that Jane suggested Caius would be interested to hear that I was still human and might visit.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc10.source_text: “Caius will beso interested to hear that you’re still human, Bella. Perhaps he’ll decide to visit.”

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc10.description: I felt deeply grateful that the strange glitch in my system which had protected me from Jane before was still in effect.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc10.source_text: I shivered, deeply grateful that the strange glitch in my system — which had protected me from Jane the last time we’d met — was still in effect.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc10.description: I felt Edward’s protection as his arm tightened around me and I relied on his physical comfort in the aftermath.
I heard a deep rumbling growl followed by a high-pitched keen and then the sickening sounds of crunching and snapping.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc10.source_text: there was a deep, rumbling growl, and then a high-pitched keen that was horribly familiar. That sound cut off quickly, and then the only sound was a sickening crunching and snapping.

tw-book3-chapter26_Sc2.description: I promised my father that I would tell him before I do anything major or leave with someone.
tw-book3-chapter26_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "Just promise me one thing." "If it makes you happy, . . . I promise."

tw-book3-chapter26_Sc2.description: I realized that I could not live without Edward and that the idea of giving up being human felt like a true sacrifice.
tw-book3-chapter26_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "I already knew that I couldn’t live without Edward. ... For the first time, giving up being human felt like a true sacrifice."

tw-book3-chapter26_Sc2.description: I acknowledged that I would have to break Jacob even though I love him and that the thought made him seem fragile to me.
tw-book3-chapter26_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "Maybe that had just been my imagination, coupled with the knowledge that I was going to have to break him." "It was hard to look at his face, knowing that I loved him."

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc1.description: I experienced a sudden physical breakdown while driving that forced me to stop on the shoulder.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc1.source_text:
IDIDN’T GET VERY FAR BEFORE DRIVING BECAME IMPOS sible.
When I couldn’t see anymore, I let my tires find the rough shoulder and rolled slowly to a stop.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc1.description: I began to sob uncontrollably and I blubbered out Charlie’s name during my breakdown.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc1.source_text: he just let me sob until I began to blubber out Charlie’s name.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc1.description: I concluded that I was right to hide this breakdown from Jacob and I believed no one should ever see this side of me.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc1.source_text: Yes, I had been right to hide this from Jacob. No one should ever see this.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc1.description: I felt guilty because a smaller, angrier part of me craved a different set of arms, specifically Jacob’s, while Edward comforted me.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc1.source_text: Because there was that smaller part of me — smaller, but getting louder and angrier every minute, screaming at the rest of me — that craved a different set of arms. So then there was fresh guilt to season the pain.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc1.description: I needed to get home before it got late enough for Charlie to call Billy and I was determined to reach the house.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc1.source_text: I needed to get past Charlie before it got late enough for him to call Billy.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc2.description: I went upstairs and intended to be alone in my room after the confrontation.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc2.source_text: Once inside, I headed straight for the stairs.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc2.description: I felt my emotional control slipping and became more aware of my vulnerability in front of Charlie.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc2.source_text: I could feel the control slipping.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc2.description: My father is anxious, protective, and particularly frightened by my tears.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc2.source_text: Nothing scared Charlie worse than tears.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc3.description: I learned that my emotional outbursts are part of who I am.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc3.source_text: "No, Bella," Edward whispered, capturing my hands. "It's part of who you are."

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc3.description: I realized that I had been wrong about the magnets and that I had been trying to force two parts of myself together that could not coexist.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc3.source_text: And I realized that I’d been wrong all along about the magnets. It had not been Edward and Jacob that I’d been trying to force together, it was the two parts of myself, Edward’s Bella and Jacob’s Bella. But they could not exist together, and I never should have tried.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc3.description: I recognized the pain I had caused Jacob and the wounds I had given Edward and felt guilty about both.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc3.source_text: Each pain I’d caused Jacob, each wound I’d given Edward, stacked up into neat piles that I could not ignore or deny.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc3.description: I remembered the promise I had made to myself not to make Edward see me shed another tear for Jacob Black.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc3.source_text: At some point in the night, I remembered the promise I’d made to myself early this morning — that I would never make Edward see me shed another tear for Jacob Black.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc3.description: I accepted that the new tear in my heart would always ache and that time might ease it but my priority was Jacob's recovery.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc3.source_text: Instinctively, I knew that the new tear in my heart would always ache. That was just going to be a part of me now. Time would make it easier — that’s what everyone always said. But I didn’t care if time healed me or not, so long as Jacob could get better. Could be happy again.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc4.description: I woke up without disorientation and met Edward's anxious gaze.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc4.source_text: When I woke up, there was no disorientation. I opened my eyes — finally dry — and met his anxious gaze.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc4.description: I reaffirmed that I could not live without Edward and that being with him is the only way I can live.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc4.source_text: I know who I can\'t live without.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc4.description: I accepted that I would not be self-sacrificing and that I must choose to be with Edward even if it causes him pain or doubt.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc4.source_text: You may be brave enough or strong enough to live without me, if that\'s what\'s best. But I could never be that self-sacrificing. I have to be with you.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc4.description: I used a passage from a book to explain my feelings and found the dog-eared page I had read many times.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc4.source_text: 'If all else perished, and he remained, I should still continue to be; and if all else remained, and he were annihilated, the universe would turn to a mighty stranger.'

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc4.description: I decided that we are going to go see Alice and that I would set limitations for her over-enthusiasm.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc4.source_text: We are going to go see Alice.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc5.description: I learned that Alice had secretly arranged a wedding dress for me.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc5.source_text: “When did you get me a dress?”

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc5.description: I learned that Alice commissioned or obtained work from Perrine Bruyere because of a waiting list and specialized fabric work.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc5.source_text: “Perrine Bruyere has a waiting list, you know,” she said.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc5.description: I learned that the dress included design elements that Alice described as partly her design with a train and veil and that the lace was vintage.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc5.source_text: “Some of it is my design, the train, the veil. . . .” She touched the white satin as she spoke. “The lace is vintage. Do you like it?”

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc5.description: I felt that the dress was perfect and especially right for Edward and our wedding.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc5.source_text: “It’s beautiful. It’s just right for him.”

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc5.description: I viewed Alice as proactive, thoughtful, and excited about planning wedding details on my behalf.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc5.source_text: “These things take time, Bella,” she explained.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc6.description: I learned that our wedding date was suggested as August thirteenth.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc6.source_text: "August thirteenth?" he asked casually after a few minutes of comfortable silence. "That gives me a month till my birthday. I didn’t want to cut it too close."

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc6.description: I decided that my age was not important and I had chosen my life and wanted to start living it.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc6.source_text: “My age is not really that important. Edward, I’m ready. I’ve chosen my life — now I want to start living it.”

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc6.description: I chose to let Alice have free reign of the wedding planning so Charlie, Renée, and Phil could have their goodbye and know I chose Edward.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc6.source_text: “It wouldn’t be fair to keep Charlie out of this,” I concluded. "And that means Renée and Phil. I might as well let Alice have her fun, too. Maybe it will make the whole thing easier for Charlie if he gets his proper goodbye. Even if he thinks it’s much too early, I wouldn’t want to cheat him out of the chance to walk me down the aisle."

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc6.description: I worried that Jacob might feel he should come and that he could be hurt if he was not invited.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc6.source_text: “I’m not sure if Alice would feel the need to invite . . . a few werewolves. I don’t know if . . . Jake would feel like . . . like he should come. Like that’s the right thing to do, or that I’d get my feelings hurt if he didn’t. He shouldn’t have to go through that.”

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc7.description: I learned that Bella had chosen someone else over me.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc7.source_text: It didn’t matter so much that Bella’d chosen someone else over me.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc7.description: I learned that Bella was in danger of losing her humanity and becoming like them.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc7.source_text: Because she was giving up everything — that she was letting her heart stop and her skin ice over and her mind twist into some crystallized predator’s head.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc7.description: I changed my belief about what would be worse than death when I realized that Bella becoming one of them might be as painful as her dying.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc7.source_text: I would have thought there was nothing worse than that, nothing more painful in the whole world. But, if he killed her . . .

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc1.description: I experienced disorientation about time after the long flight chasing the sun westward.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: After the long flight — chasing the sun westward so that it seemed unmoving in the sky — it was especially disorienting; time seemed oddly variable.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc1.description: I felt more relieved than sad about leaving my mother's visit.
I realized it was useless and unnecessary to ask him to keep his eyes on the road.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: I knew it was useless and — much as I hated to admit it — unnecessary to ask him to keep his eyes on the road.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc1.description: I went for a walk along the beach with my mother who wanted to show off her new home and to talk with me alone.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: This morning we’d gone for a walk along the beach. She wanted to show off all the beauties of her new home, still hoping, I think, that the sun might lure me away from Forks. She’d also wanted to talk with me alone, and that was easily arranged.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc1.description: I noticed my mother's wide blue eyes change from confused to concerned as she watched me.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: And as she’d watched, her wide blue eyes had become first confused and then concerned.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc1.description: I learned that Phil was busy coaching the high school baseball team in the playoffs which left my mother alone with Edward and me.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: Phil was busy — the high school baseball team he coached was in the playoffs — and being alone with Edward and me had only sharpened Renée’s focus.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc2.description: I learned that my mother Renée is worried about my relationship with Edward.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: I'm worried about you . . . and Edward.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc2.description: I realized that my mother can see truths about my relationship that I had assumed I could hide.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: I’d forgotten how much my mother saw. Something about her simple view of the world cut through all the distractions and pierced right to the truth of things.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc2.description: I recognized that I unconsciously orient my movements around Edward and that this behavior looks like magnetism or gravity to an observer.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: The way you move — you orient yourself around him without even thinking about it. When he moves, even a little bit, you adjust your position at the same time. Like magnets . . . or gravity.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc2.description: I noticed that my mother otherwise seemed happy and affectionate toward Phil, indicating she has a satisfying life separate from me.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: Other than her worries about me, she seemed happy enough. Content. She still looked at Phil with goo-goo eyes, and that was comforting.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc4.description: I learned that I grabbed the phone mid-ring and answered Jacob's call while twisting to face the wall.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc4.source_text: I grabbed the phone mid-ring, and twisted around so that I was facing the wall. "Hello?"

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc4.description: I felt a wave of wistfulness and homesickness when I heard Jacob's familiar husky voice and I remembered vivid shared memories.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc4.source_text: His familiar husky voice sent a wave of wistfulness through me. A thousand memories spun in my head, tangling together — a rocky beach strewn with driftwood trees, a garage made of plastic sheds, warm sodas in a paper bag, a tiny room with one too-small shabby loveseat.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc4.description: I questioned my understanding of Jacob's motives when I realized his brief, insistent questions about school felt like a clue rather than casual curiosity.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc4.source_text: “You going to school tomorrow?” I frowned to myself, unable to make sense of this question.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc5.description: I learned that my conversion would take three painful days and would free me from mortality while making me a prisoner to thirst.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: How I couldn’t be anywhere near people after I’d gone through the painful three-day conversion that would set me free from mortality, so that I could spend eternity with Edward?

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc5.description: I decided that we would have to leave before the treaty could be broken and that we wouldn't be able to come back.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: "We’ll have to leave," I whispered. "Before. So that it doesn’t break the treaty. We won’t ever be able to come back."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc5.description: I felt watched and tested by Jacob's question, which made me doubt how he viewed my choices and whether he believed I would return to Charlie if I had been bitten.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: Had Jacob really been asking me if I was still human? Making sure that the werewolves’ treaty was unbroken — that none of the Cullens had dared to bite a human . . . bite, not kill . . . ? ... But did he honestly think I would come home to Charlie if that was the case?

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc7.description: I learned that Victoria is actively pursuing me and will not stop until I am dead.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc7.source_text: Victoria was never going to give up till I was dead. She would keep repeating the same pattern — feint and run, feint and run — until she found a hole through my defenders.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc7.description: I realized Edward lied about Alice's vision and that I had expected this attack would recur.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc7.source_text: Something Alice had seen in a vision last week — a vision Edward had lied to me about. Something I’d been waiting for anyway.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc7.description: I decided I would rather be killed a hundred times than watch Edward suffer mental torture again.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc7.source_text: I’d rather Victoria killed me a hundred times over than watch Edward suffer that way again.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc7.description: I felt Edward’s overprotectiveness when he physically placed himself between me and Jacob and promised to keep me safe.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc7.source_text: Edward held me tight to his side, angling his body so that he was still between me and Jacob, and stroked my face with anxious hands. “It’s fine,” he whispered to me. “It’s fine. I’ll never let her get close to you, it’s fine.”

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc8.description: I learned that Jacob still has my motorcycle in his garage and did not sell it as he had promised Charlie.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: "Hey, if you ever feel like having a life again, you could come see me. I’ve still got your motorcycle in my garage." "You were supposed to sell that. You promised Charlie you would."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc8.description: I realized that Edward’s protective hold can feel like a restraint that prevents me from comforting Jacob.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: "I was vividly conscious of Edward, his arms still wrapped protectively around me, motionless as a stone." "Edward’s shielding arms had become restraints."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc8.description: I felt a renewed protective impulse toward Jacob and a wish to comfort him despite the emotional complications.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: "Jacob’s suffering had always triggered my protective side... my arms, pinned beneath Edward’s, yearned to reach out to him."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc9.description: I learned that Victoria escaped by following the Quileute boundary line as if she knew it like a map.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc9.source_text: I read: "Victoria seems to have some instinct for evasion. She escaped right down the Quileute boundary line as if she were reading it from a map."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc9.description: I learned that Alice's abilities were nullified when the Quileutes became involved in the chase.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc9.source_text: I read: "it didn’t help that Alice’s abilities were nullified by the Quileutes’ involvement."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc9.description: I learned that Emmett, Jasper, Alice, Rosalie, and Carlisle all participated in the attempt to stop Victoria and that Esme might have been involved.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc9.source_text: I read: "All of them had been in on it — Emmett, Jasper, Alice, Rosalie, and Carlisle. Maybe even Esme, though he hadn’t mentioned her."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc9.description: I became more afraid at the thought that the Cullens and the Quileute pack could have come to blows and that anyone could have been hurt.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc9.source_text: I read: "It might so easily have turned into a fight, pitting my future family and my old friends against each other. Any one of them could have been hurt."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc9.description: I felt reassured by Edward's protective attitude and his promise to tell me everything next time.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc9.source_text: I read: "I wasn’t about to send you off alone." and "You will tell me next time."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc10.description: I heard the gossip in Calculus about a potential confrontation between Jacob and Edward.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc10.source_text: It was later, in Calculus — my one class without Edward — that I heard the gossip.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc10.description: I learned that classmates were actively betting on who would win, saying things like "Ten on Jacob" and "Ten on Edward."
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc10.source_text: "Anyone in the mood for a bet?" "Ten on Jacob," Austin said at once. "Ten on Cullen," Tyler chimed in. "Ten on Edward," Ben agreed. "Jacob," Mike said.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc10.description: I noticed that the boys glanced at me and looked away quickly when they realized I could hear them, which updated my sense of their awareness of my presence.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc10.source_text: From their expressions, none of them had realized I was in easy hearing distance. They all looked away quickly, shuffling the papers on their desks.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc1.description: I learned that Quil joined the pack and is enthusiastic about it.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc1.source_text: “Quil’s not looking for pity. Just the opposite — he’s jazzed. Totally thrilled.”

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc1.description: I changed my belief that all of the wolves were depressed about joining the pack when I learned that most of them actually enjoyed the changes.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc1.source_text: “Honestly . . . most of them do,” Jacob admitted slowly.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc1.description: I noticed that Jacob was uncomfortable and avoiding eye contact but remained physically close by holding my hand.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc1.source_text: “’S not so bad,” he said, but he wouldn’t meet my eyes. He walked slowly back to the driftwood bench, staring at the rainbow-colored pebbles, and pulling me along at his side. He kept my hand.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc1.description: I understood that Jacob was willing to be protective and stay with me instead of letting me return to Charlie.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc1.source_text: “So don’t go back. I’ll sleep on the couch.”

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.description: I became convinced that Edward would not hurt Jacob because I believe he knows hurting Jacob would hurt me.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: “At leasthe can be a grown-up about this. He knows that hurting you would hurt me — and so he never would.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.description: I felt anger and distance from Jacob when I ripped my hand out of his and shoved his head away because his behavior made me feel that he did not care about how I would be affected.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: “Ugh!” I ripped my hand out of his and shoved his head away. Then I pulled my knees up to my chest and wrapped my arms tightly around them.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.description: I learned that Sam’s first phasing terrified him and that he thought he had gone insane, taking two weeks to calm down enough to change back.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: “The first time it happened — the first time he phased — he thought he’d gone insane. It took him two weeks to calm down enough to change back.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.description: I learned that Sam’s grandfather died before Sam was born and that Sam’s father has never been around, leaving Sam essentially alone when he first phased.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: “Sam’s grandfather died before he was born, and his father has never been around.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.description: I remembered that Harry Clearwater had died of a heart attack this past spring and felt pity when Leah was mentioned in connection with searching for Sam.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: “Harry Clearwater, Charlie’s life-long friend, had died of a heart attack this past spring.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: I noticed the way Sam looked at Emily reminded me of a look I’d seen sometimes in Edward’s eyes when he was looking at me.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: The way he looked at her . . . well, it reminded me of a look I’d seen sometimes in Edward’s eyes — when he was looking at me.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: I decided it was silly for me to imagine that Sam had never loved anyone before Emily.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: I supposed it was silly for me to imagine that Sam had never loved anyone before Emily. Most people fall in and out of love many times in their lives.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: I felt Jacob put his hand on my cheek and I entwined my fingers with his, which changed my sense of our intimacy in that moment.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: Jacob put his hand on my cheek and pulled my face around to look at him — he was leaning toward me, his face was just a few inches away. I reached up casually, to take his hand away and free my face, but wound my fingers through his so that I wouldn't hurt his feelings.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc4.description: I became enraged and felt the unfairness of aging alone after hearing Jacob's revelation.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc4.source_text: I felt blood flood my face. Tears — tears of rage — filled my eyes.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob and the tribe do not age while they are phasing.
I noticed Jacob trying to calm me by tugging my arm and patting the tree, which showed me his concern.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc4.source_text: Jacob tugged my arm gently, trying to make me sit.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc5.description: I learned that the werewolf gene triggers a rapid physical growth spurt that reaches full growth in a few months.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc5.source_text: Because we reach full growth inside of a few months when the werewolf gene gets triggered. It's one hell of a growth spurt.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob is physically about twenty-five even though he appears sixteen.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc5.source_text: Physically, I'm probably twenty-five or something.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc5.description: I felt my worry about being too old for Jacob ease after he told me there was no need to freak out for at least another seven years.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc5.source_text: So there's no need for you to freak out about being too old for me for at least another seven years.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc5.description: I apologized and acknowledged that age is a touchy subject for me after feeling dizzy and unsettled by the conversation.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc5.source_text: Sorry. Age is a touchy subject for me. That hit a nerve.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc8.description: I learned that Edward is never in my head and that he only wishes.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc8.source_text: “Oh, no. Edward’s never in my head. He only wishes.”

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc8.description: I learned that Edward can’t hear me and that we do not know why.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc8.source_text: “He can’t hear me,” I explained, my voice a tiny bit smug from old habit. “I’m the only one like that, for him. We don’t know why he can’t.”

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc8.description: I admitted that there might be something wrong with my brain.
