tw-book3-chapter5_Sc8.source_text: “It probably means there’s something wrong with my brain,” I admitted.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc8.description: I felt Jacob’s physical closeness and warmth when he leaned against my arm and rested his cheek on the top of my head.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc8.source_text: Jacob settled closer to me, so that he was leaning against my arm. He made a little sound of contentment in the back of his throat, and rested his cheek on the top of my head.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc9.description: I learned that a memory which used to cause me stress and confusion now makes me laugh and feels oddly pleasant.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc9.source_text: I laughed, too, surprised by how time had changed the memory. It used to be one of stress, of confusion. So much had changed that night. . . . And now I could laugh. it was the last night Jacob and I had had before he’d learned the truth about his heritage. The last human memory. An oddly pleasant memory now.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc9.description: I learned that Jacob was thinking about me Monday morning and that his thought had bothered Edward.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc9.source_text: Do you mind telling me what you were doing Monday morning? You were thinking something that bothered Edward." "I was just thinking about you. Didn’t like that much, did he?

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc9.description: I set a firm boundary with Jacob by demanding a promise that he would not show those memories to Edward again, and I accepted his apology and promise.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc9.source_text: Jacob Black, don’t you ever do that again! Promise me you won’t." "No way. I haven’t had that much fun in months." "I’m sorry. And . . . okay, I won’t do it again. Promise.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.description: I learned that Angela Weber was expecting me and that Alice was worried about me.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.source_text: "Angela Weber is expecting me, and I know Alice is worried."

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.description: I noticed that time had passed quickly and that the sun was already directly overhead.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.source_text: "I glared up at the sun, somehow already directly overhead. How had the time passed so quickly?"

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.description: I promised to come back the next time he is away.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.source_text: "I'll come back the next time he's away," I promised impulsively.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.description: I decided that supernatural categories were irrelevant and that only personal identities mattered.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.source_text: "I don't care who's a vampire and who's a werewolf. That's irrelevant. You are Jacob, and he is Edward, and I am Bella. And nothing else matters."

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.description: I admitted that I had really missed Jacob and I promised to return as soon as I could.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.source_text: "I've really missed you, Jake," I admitted impulsively. "As soon as I can," I promised.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob had shared a flood of information with me that I was trying to sort out.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: I was thinking about the flood of information Jacob had shared with me, trying to sort it out, to force it all to make sense.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.description: I felt lighter after Jacob confided in me and I believed that having the secrets thrashed out made things better.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: Despite the overload, I felt lighter. Seeing Jacob smile, having all the secrets thrashed out . . . it didn’t make things perfect, but it made them better.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.description: I believed I was right to have gone to see Jacob because I perceived that Jacob needed me.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: I was right to have gone. Jacob needed me.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.description: I noticed a silver Volvo was right on my tail and I interpreted its presence as a direct pursuit.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: The next minute, the sun was glinting off a silver Volvo right on my tail.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.description: I felt too cowardly to face the driver immediately and I wanted prep time and Charlie nearby as a buffer.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: I considered pulling over. But I was too much of a coward to face him right away. I’d been counting on some prep time . . . and having Charlie nearby as a buffer.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.description: I learned that I interpreted my anxiety as being caused by Edward and I admitted to Angela that he was the problem.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: No," I said. "You’re right. I am anxious. It’s . . . it’s Edward." "What’s wrong?" "Oh, he’s mad at me.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc2.description: I helped Angela address and stamp all of her announcements for the Webers.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: We got all her announcements addressed.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc2.description: I think I will recover the full use of my hand someday after flexing my fingers.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: I flexed my fingers. "I think I’ll recover the full use of it . . . someday."

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc2.description: I decided not to miss out on last chances with friends despite feeling a swell of quiet sadness.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: A swell of quiet sadness crashed over me; maybe it was a mistake to get closer to Angela now. But wouldn't it be sadder still to miss out on these last chances? I shook off the unhappy thoughts, so that I could answer her teasingly.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc2.description: I felt Edward as cold and icy when I hugged him and perceived his posture as hard and tense.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: Next to the warmth of the last of the afternoon sun streaming through the window, his skin felt especially icy.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc2.description: I insisted that Jacob isn't dangerous and believed neither others nor I needed to worry about him.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: "There's nothing to worry about. Jacob isn't dangerous."

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc3.description: I declared neutrality in the vampire–werewolf conflict and compared myself to Switzerland.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: I am a neutral country. I am Switzerland.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc3.description: I stated that Jacob is family and that I consider Edward the love of my existence.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: Jacob is family. You are . . . well, not exactly the love of my life, because I expect to love you for much longer than that. The love of my existence.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc3.description: I was taken by Alice to stay at the Cullen house for two nights with Esme's permission.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: Esme cleared it with Charlie; you’re staying with me two nights, and I will drive you to and from school tomorrow.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc3.description: I planned to call Jacob during a brief window when Edward took the Volvo home to let him know I’d be coming over on Saturday.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: I didn’t feel guilty calling Jake — during my brief window of opportunity when Edward took the Volvo home before climbing back in through my window — to let him know I’d be coming over on Saturday again.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc3.description: I decided that Jacob would pick me up if Edward broke my truck again.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: And if he broke my truck again, then I’d have Jacob pick me up.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc3.description: I learned that I was to sleep in Edward’s room while staying at the Cullen house.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc4.description: I left a voicemail that warned someone, saying "You are in trouble" and describing the trouble as "enormous" with "angry grizzly bears" compared to what awaited at home.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: I read: "'You are in trouble,' I said slowly, emphasizing each word. 'Enormous trouble. Angry grizzly bears are going to look tame next to what is waiting for you at home.'"

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc4.description: I found my pajamas folded neatly on the foot of the bed and my bag of toiletries placed to one side.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: I read: "My pajamas were folded neatly on the foot of the bed, my bag of toiletries to one side."

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc4.description: I felt more irritated than flattered by the extravagant gestures, thinking that Porsches as bribes and king-sized beds in empty houses were beyond irritating.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: I read: "Porsches as bribes and king-sized beds in houses where nobody slept — it was beyond irritating."

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc4.description: I trusted that Alice would know if I planned to sneak out and would catch me if I tried, so I told her I was not going to sneak out.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: I read: "I'm not going to sneak out. You would know if I was planning to, and you'd catch me if I tried."

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc4.description: I moved a puffy feather pillow and the gold cover from the huge bed to the couch and curled up there to sleep instead of using the bed.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: I read: "I grabbed a puffy feather pillow off the huge bed and dragged the gold cover to the couch."

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc1.description: I learned that Rosalie specifically asked for a private conversation and checked that she had not woken me.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: I quote: "Do you mind talking to me for a few minutes?" she asked. "I didn’t wake you or anything, did I?"

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc1.description: I learned that Rosalie intended to explain why she thinks I should remain human and that she would make the same choice if she were me.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: I quote: "I’m going to try to tell you why I think you should stay human — why I would stay human if I were you."

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc1.description: I felt that Rosalie was apologetic and self-aware about past hurts, which softened my perception of her hostility.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: I quote: "Please don’t think I’m horribly interfering," Rosalie said. "I’m sure I’ve hurt your feelings enough in the past, and I don’t want to do that again."

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc1.description: I noticed my own nervousness and uncertainty about Rosalie’s motives as my stomach twisted while she sat down.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: I quote: "My stomach twisted nervously as the one Cullen who did not like me moved silently to sit down in the open space."

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc2.description: I learned from Edward that Rosalie's transformation resembled my Port Angeles incident but lacked any rescue.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc2.source_text: He said it was close to what happened to me that time in Port Angeles, only no one was there to saveyou .

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc2.description: I learned that Rosalie offered to tell her own story and that it began in 1933 when she was eighteen and thought her life perfect.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc2.source_text: Would you like to hear my story, Bella? ... It was nineteen thirty-three. I was eighteen, and I was beautiful. My life was perfect.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc2.description: I felt somber and frightened by the implications of Rosalie's past after Edward's brief explanation.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc2.source_text: I nodded slowly, suddenly somber. ... I nodded, though I was frightened by the edge in her voice.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc2.description: I noticed Rosalie's smile was harsh and bitter despite being stunning, and I adjusted my view of her as more complex and resentful.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc2.source_text: She looked up at me and smiled; it was a harsh, bitter — but still stunning — expression.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc3.description: I learned that Rosalie's parents were thoroughly middle class and that her father had a stable job in a bank.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: My parents were thoroughly middle class. My father had a stable job in a bank, something I realize now that he was smug about — he saw his prosperity as a reward for talent and hard work, rather than acknowledging the luck involved.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc3.description: I learned that Rosalie's family had social aspirations and that her beauty was treated as a valuable asset by her parents.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: They weren’t satisfied, but I was. I was thrilled to be me, to be Rosalie Hale. Pleased that men’s eyes watched me everywhere I went, from the year I turned twelve. Delighted that my girlfriends sighed with envy when they touched my hair. Happy that my mother was proud of me and that my father liked to buy me pretty dresses.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc3.description: I realized that Rosalie was more complex than merely vain because I learned she felt genuine jealousy over a close friend's simple domestic happiness.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: My very closest friend was a girl named Vera. She married young, just seventeen. She married a man my parents would never have considered for me — a carpenter. A year later she had a son, a beautiful little boy with dimples and curly black hair. It was the first time I’d ever felt truly jealous of anyone else in my entire life.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc4.description: I learned that Rosalie once yearned for a conventional life with a house, husband, and children.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I yearned for my own little baby. I wanted my own house and a husband who would kiss me when he got home from work — just like Vera.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc4.description: I learned that Royce King owned the bank and nearly every other really profitable business in Rochester.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: In Rochester, there was one royal family — the Kings, ironically enough. Royce King owned the bank my father worked at, and nearly every other really profitable business in town.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc4.description: I learned that Royce King the Second courted Rosalie by sending roses nightly and later sent violets as a compliment to her eyes.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: Two days later, my mother conveniently forgot to send my father’s lunch to work with him. ... That night the first of the roses came. Every night of our courtship, he sent a bouquet of roses to me. ... He said my eyes were like violets, and then those started showing up alongside the roses.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc4.description: I learned that Rosalie and Royce were engaged before she had known him for two months.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: We were engaged before I’d known him for two months.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc4.description: I learned that Royce preferred public appearances, cited many work responsibilities, and limited their private time together.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: We didn’t spend a great deal of time alone with each other. Royce told me he had many responsibilities at work, and, when we were together, he liked people to look at us, to see me on his arm.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc4.description: I realized that Rosalie’s story sounded more like a fairy tale than history to me.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: Her story sounded more like a fairy tale than history to me.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc4.description: I noticed that Rosalie said she was completely happy and that she no longer felt jealous of Vera once she imagined life with Royce.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I was completely happy. When I called at Vera’s, I no longer felt jealous.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc4.description: I wondered if my world seemed as baffling to Edward as Rosalie’s world seemed to me.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I wondered — while Rosalie sat silent for a moment — if my world seemed as baffling to him as Rosalie’s did to me?

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc5.description: I learned that Rosalie's wedding was only a week away and she worried about the weather as she hurried home.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: The wedding was only a week away, and I was worrying about the weather as I hurried home — I can remember that clearly.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc5.description: I learned that Rosalie was a few streets from her house when she heard a cluster of well dressed, drunken men under a broken streetlamp, including Royce and his friends.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: I was a few streets from my house when I heard them. A cluster of men under a broken streetlamp, laughing too loud. Drunk. I hadn’t realized the drunks were so well dressed. It was Royce and some of his friends, sons of other rich men.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc5.description: I learned that Royce physically assaulted Rosalie by ripping her jacket, popping the brass buttons, tearing her hat, and wrenching pins from her hair.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: Suddenly, Royce ripped my jacket from my shoulders — it was a gift from him — popping the brass buttons off. They scattered all over the street. ... he tore my hat out of my hair. The pins wrenched my hair from the roots, and I cried out in pain.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc5.description: I noticed that Rosalie's bone white face appeared paler in the moonlight as she told the story.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: It was hard to tell in the moonlight, but it looked like her bone white face got paler.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc5.description: I learned about the dark-haired man named John who inspected Rosalie in a predatory way.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: The man named John was dark-haired and suntanned. He looked me over like I was a horse he was buying.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc5.description: I realized there would be no happy ending to Rosalie's story and I suspected her extra bitterness came from losing her human life when she was close to fulfillment.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: It pulled me out of her story, and I realized that the horror was not far off. There would be no happy ending, as she’d promised. I wondered if this was why she had so much more bitterness in her than the rest of them — because she’d been within reach of everything she’d wanted when her human life was cut short.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc5.description: I updated my view of Royce as abusive rather than protective after I heard him mock Rosalie, call her 'Rose', and participate in her assault.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: 'Here's my Rose!' Royce shouted, laughing with them, sounding just as stupid. 'You're late. We're cold, you've kept us waiting so long.'

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.description: I learned that Rosalie was left in the street by Royce and that people thought she was dead.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: They left me in the street, still laughing as they stumbled away. They thought I was dead.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.description: I learned that Carlisle found Rosalie because he smelled the blood and then carried her away quickly as he tried to save her life.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: Carlisle found me then. He’d smelled the blood, and come to investigate. I remember being vaguely irritated as he worked over me, trying to save my life.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.description: I learned that Rosalie underwent a painful transformation during which she screamed, begged to be killed, and felt fire cutting through her.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: I screamed in shock, thinking he’d brought me there to hurt me more. Then fire started burning through me, and I didn’t care about anything else. I begged him to kill me.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.description: I learned that the pain eventually ended, that the Cullens explained to Rosalie what she was becoming, and that she felt the thirst and saw her red eyes.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: The pain finally ended and they explained to me again what I was. This time I believed. I felt the thirst, my hard skin; I saw my brilliant red eyes.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.description: I learned that Rosalie felt intensely beautiful after her transformation and admired her reflection despite the new eyes.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: Shallow as I was, I felt better when I saw my reflection in the mirror the first time. Despite the eyes, I was the most beautiful thing I’d ever seen.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.description: I noticed that Rosalie’s feelings shifted from pride in her beauty to seeing that beauty as a curse that caused her loss and suffering.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: It took some time before I began to blame the beauty for what had happened to me — for me to see the curse of it.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.description: I learned that Carlisle refused to leave Rosalie to die because he felt it would be too much waste and he sat with her, apologized, and promised the pain would end.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: ‘I couldn’t just let her die,’ Carlisle said quietly. ‘It was too much — too horrible, too much waste.’ ... Carlisle sat with me. He held my hand and said that he was so sorry, promising that it would end.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.description: I learned that Edward reacted with irritation and disgust at the idea of transforming Rosalie and questioned Carlisle’s decision aloud.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: ‘What were you thinking, Carlisle?’ Edward said. ‘Rosalie Hale?’ ... ‘What are we going to do with her?’ Edward said disgustedly

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.description: I learned that Rosalie believed the Kings, specifically Royce, were guilty of her attack and that the Cullens recognized that possibility.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: ‘People die all the time,’ Edward reminded him in a hard voice. ‘Don’t you think she’s just a little recognizable, though? The Kings will have to put up a huge search — not that anyone suspects the fiend,’ he growled. ... It pleased me that they seemed to know that Royce was guilty.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.description: I noticed that Rosalie came to long for a normal human life, marriage, and children like Vera had, and that she resented how being beautiful robbed her of that possibility.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: To wish that I had been . . . well, not ugly, but normal. Like Vera. So I could have been allowed to marry someone who loved me, and have pretty babies. That’s what I’d really wanted, all along.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc7.description: I learned that Rosalie claimed she had never tasted human blood and deliberately avoided spilling their blood to prevent herself from being tempted.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: "I’ve never tasted human blood," she announced proudly. "I did murder five humans," she told me in a complacent tone. "I was very careful not to spill their blood — I knew I wouldn’t be able to resist that, and I didn’t want any part of them in me, you see."

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc7.description: I learned that Rosalie killed Royce last, also killed his guards, and used theatrical methods such as wearing a stolen wedding dress to increase his terror.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: "I saved Royce for last. I hoped that he would hear of his friends’ deaths and understand, know what was coming for him... Oops — seven murders," she corrected herself. "I was overly theatrical. It was kind of childish, really. I wore a wedding dress I’d stolen for the occasion. He screamed when he saw me. He screamed a lot that night. Saving him for last was a good idea — it made it easier for me to control myself, to make it slower —"

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc7.description: I became wary because I realized Edward had not told me the whole story about Rosalie's past and that he sometimes withholds details.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: "I’m surprised Edward didn’t tell you more about it." "He doesn’t like to tell other people’s stories — he feels like he’s betraying confidences, because he hears so much more than just the parts they mean for him to hear." "He just didn’t tell you the whole story."

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc7.description: I felt unable to compete with Rosalie after she admitted she had been jealous because Edward wanted me and not her.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: "Well, that’s probably putting it too strongly. He just didn’t tell you the whole story... at first, I was mostly jealous because he wanted you and not me." "I could not compete with Rosalie."

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc7.description: I admitted that I lied about being fine and realized I was frightened by Rosalie's casual tone about murder.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: "I’m sorry," she said in a chagrined voice. "I’m frightening you, aren’t I?" "I’m fine," I lied.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc8.description: I learned that Rosalie envies my human life and considers that I have everything she wanted.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc8.source_text: You already haveeverything . You have a whole life ahead of you — everything I want.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc8.description: I learned that Rosalie rescued Emmett from a bear and intervened to have him changed by Carlisle.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc8.source_text: I saved Emmett from a bear that was mauling him, and carried him home to Carlisle.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc8.description: I learned that Rosalie asked Carlisle to change Emmett for her out of selfishness and that the choice altered the course of her life.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc8.source_text: I was selfish enough to ask Carlisle to change him for me.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc8.description: I felt my view of Rosalie soften after she revealed regret and vulnerability beneath her arrogance.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc8.source_text: And I was so sure that I could do this calmly.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc8.description: I experienced a nightmare that left me unsettled and conscious of the dark image of leaving a bloody trail in the snow.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc8.source_text: I was crawling across the dark, cold stones of an unfamiliar street, under lightly falling snow, leaving a trail of blood smeared behind me.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc9.description: I was driven to school by Alice while I stared grumpily out the windshield.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: Alice drove me to school while I stared grumpily out the windshield.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc9.description: I felt sleep-deprived that morning, which intensified my irritation about my imprisonment.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: I was feeling sleep-deprived, and it made the irritation of my imprisonment that much stronger.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc9.description: I realized I actually felt guilty despite believing the situation was not Alice's fault.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: I couldn't believe I actually felt guilty.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc9.description: I suggested that I be locked in the basement and forgo the sugar coating as a reflection of my frustration.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: “Why don’t you just lock me in the basement,” I suggested, “and forget the sugar coating?”

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc9.description: I planned to see Alice at lunch before going into school.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.description: I knew that Edward was not at school and that his absence made the day unbearable for me.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: Without Edward, the day was guaranteed to be unbearable.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.description: I learned that I could bluff my way out of staying at school by telling Mike I was sick and leaving quickly.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: “I got really sick and went home, okay?” I said to Mike, my voice filled with sudden excitement.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.description: I trusted Jacob enough to jump on the back of his motorcycle and rely on him to get me to safety.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: I jumped on the back of his seat, wrapping my arms tightly around his waist.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.description: I felt liberated and joyful after escaping school with Jacob and I relished the freedom.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: It felt great to be free.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.description: I feared Alice's ability to restrain me in public and I was wary of how far she might go.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: How far would Alice go to restrain me in public?

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc1.description: I knew that the vampires would not come looking for Jacob.
I felt that Charlie’s preference for my Quileute friends was blatantly unfair.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: Charlie’s blatant preference for my Quileute friends was so unfair.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc1.description: I noticed that Jacob reached out and took my hand and that we walked like a couple.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: Without seeming to think about it, he reached out and took my hand.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc1.description: I learned that Quil had imprinted and that it was the third imprinting in the pack.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: "Quil imprinted. That’s three now. The rest of us are starting to get worried. . . ."

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc2.description: I learned that Quil imprinted on a two-year-old girl named Claire.
I learned that Quil had not been around Emily's place much until recently and had only just met Claire.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: "Quil hasn't been hanging out with us, you know, until just recently. So he hadn't been around Emily's place much."

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc2.description: I became horrified and judgmental about the idea of imprinting on a toddler even as I tried to withhold judgment.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: I was trying my hardest not to be critical, but, in truth, I was horrified.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc2.description: I noticed Jacob's strong defense of Quil and I perceived a bitter edge in his feelings about Sam when he compared future happiness.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: "And then, when she's grown up, they'll be as happy as Emily and Sam." A strange, bitter edge sharpened his tone at the very end, when he spoke of Sam.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob says he will never see anyone else and that he only sees me.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: I noted: "No, I haven't," he said in a low voice. "But I'll never see anyone else, Bella. I only see you. Even when I close my eyes and try to see something else. Ask Quil or Embry. It drives them all crazy."

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc3.description: I felt softer toward Jacob when I saw him revert to the sunny, warm persona I missed.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: I noted: Jacob grinnedmy grin, and he was suddenly the Jacob I missed the most, sunny and warm.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc3.description: I recognized that Jacob's feelings for me are strong and exclusive and that this shapes our relationship.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: I noted: "No, I haven't," he said in a low voice. "But I'll never see anyone else, Bella. I only see you."

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc5.description: I confirmed that I had been bitten when Jacob asked if he had bitten me and I whispered yes.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc5.source_text: "You know. When you said it was none of my business . . . if — if he bit you." "Yes," I whispered.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc5.description: I accepted that we would leave first to avoid immediate danger if the treaty was threatened.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc5.source_text: "We’ll leave first," I said in a small voice.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc5.description: I realized that Jacob said my identity would change and that our friendship would effectively end.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc5.source_text: "You won't be Bella anymore," he told me. "My friend won't exist."

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc6.description: I recognized that I have only weeks left before the change rather than years.
I accepted that Edward is all I want and I see no point in waiting.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc6.source_text: “He’s all I want. What else can I do?”

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc6.description: I felt the relationship with Jacob fracture after he told me I would be better off dead.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc6.source_text: “Anything. Anything else. You’d be better off dead. I’d rather you were.”

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc6.description: I became angry and lashed out by saying maybe I would get hit by a truck on my way back.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc6.source_text: “Maybe you’ll get lucky,” I said bleakly, lurching to my feet. “Maybe I’ll get hit by a truck on my way back.”

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc7.description: I learned that Alice was waiting for me at the Cullens' garage, perched on the hood of her Porsche when I arrived.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc7.source_text: I walked the bike into the Cullens’ cavernous garage and was unsurprised to find Alice waiting for me, perched lightly on the hood of her Porsche.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc7.description: I realized that I appeared visibly shaken and that my teeth were rattling when I spoke.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc7.source_text: "Sorry," I spit through my rattling teeth.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc7.description: I decided to stay at the Cullens to make things easier for Alice despite my initial wish to go home.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc7.source_text: "I’ll stay if it makes things easier for you."

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc8.description: I realized that I woke up comfortable on Edward's sofa because he was holding me instead of letting me fall to the floor.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc8.source_text: It took me a second before I realized that the movement should have dumped me onto the floor. And that I was much too comfortable.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc8.description: I stopped caring about being angry with him and with everyone after feeling the sweetness of our reunion.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc8.source_text: I didn’t care that I was supposed to be angry with him. I didn’t care that I was supposed to be angry with everyone.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc8.description: I sought his hands in the darkness and pulled myself close, showing my desire for intimate physical closeness.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc8.source_text: I reached out for him, found his hands in the darkness, and pulled myself closer to him.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc8.description: I admitted that I like danger despite Edward's repeated warnings about the risks.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc9.description: I learned that Jacob told Bella he would rather see her dead.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc9.source_text: “He said he’d rather see me dead.”

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc9.description: I realized that I expected Edward to be glad about Jacob's attitude but I learned that he felt sorry and protective instead.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc9.source_text: “I thought you’d be glad,” I whispered. “Glad over something that’s hurt you?” he murmured into my hair. “I don’t think so, Bella.”

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc9.description: I felt unwelcome in La Push after Jacob's reaction and I believed that Bella thought Jacob would have realized the situation but was surprised that it happened so soon.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc9.source_text: “I don’t think I’m welcome anymore,” I whispered. “I thought Jacob would have realized . . . I didn’t think it would surprise him.”

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc1.description: I learned that Alice dropped me off in the morning as part of a slumber party charade.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: ALICE DROPPED ME OFF IN THE MORNING, IN KEEPINGwith the slumber party charade.

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob called and left a message apologizing and asking me to call him and to be given a break.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: He said he didn’t mean it, and that he’s sorry. He wants you to call him. Be nice and give him a break. He sounded upset.

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc1.description: I decided that I didn't want to talk to Jacob and felt justified in not calling him.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: I didn’t want to talk to him.

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc1.description: I realized that Alice had been in my room earlier, had borrowed my pillow, and had apparently cleaned while she was passing through.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: And then I remembered that Alice had been here to get my pajamas. I hadn’t noticed that she’d borrowed my pillow, too — probably since I’d avoided the bed. It looked like she had cleaned while she was passing through.

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc1.description: I learned that a vampire had been in the house early that morning, that the intruder did not touch Charlie, and that the intruder seemed to be looking for me.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: That’s why I think it must have been them — it wasn’t long ago, early this morning while Charlie was sleeping. And whoever it was didn’t touch him, so there must have been another purpose.

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc2.description: I learned that Alice claimed she didn’t see anything related to the visit.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "I have no idea. I didn’t see anything."

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc2.description: I learned that the Cullen household had been put on alert after Edward’s call.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "They were waiting for us, on alert after Edward’s call."

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc2.description: I learned that Jasper and Emmett followed a trail that went east then south and disappeared, with a car waiting.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "The trail went East, then South, and disappeared on a side road. Had a car waiting."

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc2.description: I learned that Jasper produced something green and crumpled that turned out to be a broken fern frond as a potential clue.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "He held out something green and crumpled."

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc2.description: I learned that Alice was waiting for an official command from Aro before assigning more watchers.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "Aro hasn’t asked anyone to look for her yet. I will see that. I’m waiting for it."

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc2.description: I began to believe that vampires were much larger participants in the world and that the future would be more crowded with them.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "I was slowly realizing that vampires were much bigger participants in this world than I’d once thought."

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc2.description: I defended Alice when Edward spoke harshly to her and I felt protective of her role.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "Edward," I said, a quiet reproof. I didn’t like him talking to Alice this way."

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc2.description: I experienced comfort from Esme when she murmured that everything was going to be fine and smoothed my hair.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "It’s going to be fine, Bella," Esme murmured, smoothing my hair."

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.description: I felt comforted knowing I wasn’t alone and I admitted it was nice to have someone keeping an eye on Charlie and me.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: I had to admit it was nice, knowing I wasn’t alone.

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward sang me to sleep and I slept free of nightmares because I sensed he was there.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: He sang me to sleep again and — aware even in unconsciousness that he was there — I slept free of nightmares.

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.description: I forgave Jacob when he apologized profusely and I accepted his plea for clemency.
I discovered that Edward wanted to speak to Jacob about a scent and I handed the phone to him because I was uncertain how to explain.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: Do you mind speaking to Edward? ... I handed the phone to Edward; I hoped he could read the warning in my eyes.

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.description: I became convinced that Edward might be over the anti-werewolf prejudice when I saw him accept Jacob’s conciliatory tone.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: It seemed like Edward really was over the whole anti-werewolf thing.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc1.description: I admitted to myself that I couldn't lie convincingly even to myself about whether people were staring.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: But, because I couldn’t lie convincingly even to myself, I had to check.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc1.description: I realized that Mrs. Weber's windows were so darkly tinted that she probably had no idea if it was even me in here.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: Then I remembered that these windows were so darkly tinted that she probably had no idea if it was even me in here, let alone that I’d caught her looking.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc1.description: I noticed that townspeople like the two pedestrians and Mr. Marshall were openly staring at my car, which made me feel scrutinized.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: I glanced to the left and groaned. Two pedestrians were frozen on the sidewalk, missing their chance to cross as they stared. Behind them, Mr. Marshall was gawking through the plate-glass window of his little souvenir shop.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc1.description: I discovered that stamping the gas made the car lunge forward with terrifying force, slamming me into the seat.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc1.source_text:
In my hurry to escape, I stomped on the gas pedal without thinking—the normal way I would have punched it to get my ancient Chevy truck moving.
Engine snarling like a hunting panther, the car jolted forward so fast that my body slammed into the black leather seat and my stomach flattened against my spine.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc1.description: I felt that any doubt about who was driving the car was erased after the car's violent reaction to my foot on the pedal.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: If there had been any doubt as to who was driving this car before, it was gone now.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc1.description: I learned that a very small, precise push on the gas made the car shoot forward again.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: With the toe of my shoe, I gently nudged the gas pedal down one half millimeter, and the car shot forward again.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc2.description: I learned that strangers identified my car as a Mercedes Guardian and noted that the model was rare and not expected in Europe.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: “I know. But I was wondering, is that… are you driving a Mercedes Guardian?” ... “They aren’t supposed to be available in Europe yet,” the man went on, “let alone here.”

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc2.description: I acknowledged that I am engaged to Edward Cullen and that the wedding is only days away.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: my… my fiancé (there really was no getting around that truth with the wedding just days away).

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc2.description: I felt self-conscious about my engagement ring drawing attention and recognized that feeling as stupid and irrational.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: It was stupid to be so self-conscious, and I knew that.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc2.description: I decided to avoid public exposure by cutting small comforts and purchases, such as Pop-Tarts and shoelaces.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: I was going without a lot of things these days, like Pop-Tarts and shoelaces, to avoid spending time in public.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc2.description: I inferred that other people would admire Edward Cullen and his possessions and that his association increases the attention I receive.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: I had a feeling this guy would get along well with Edward Cullen, my… my fiancé

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc2.description: I realized that my own automotive knowledge was basic and that I was proud simply to distinguish common brands like Toyota, Ford, and Chevy.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: Personally, I didn’t get it. But then, I was just proud I could distinguish between the symbols for Toyota, Ford, and Chevy.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc3.description: I didn't know the car's make and model when asked.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: "I don't know," I told him honestly.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc3.description: I heard men describe the car as capable of withstanding extreme damage, including missile-proof glass and heavy body armor.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: "Of course not. You could roll a tank over this baby. Not much of a market for one over here. Designed for Middle East diplomats, arms dealers, and drug lords mostly." "Body armor. Four thousand pounds of body armor. And missile-proof glass? Nice."

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward provided a 'before' loaner car and that an 'after' car was hidden under a sheet in the Cullens' garage.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: "The 'before' car and the 'after' car, he’d explained... This was just the 'before' car. He'd told me it was a loaner and promised that he was returning it after the wedding."

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc3.description: I noticed that my old truck died shortly after Edward and I agreed he could replace it.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: Very, very convenient—too convenient—that my truck would wheeze its last wheeze just weeks after Edward and I had agreed to our lopsided compromise...

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc3.description: I had no way to verify Edward's story about the truck's demise or to restore the truck on my own.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: Of course, I had no way to verify his story or to try to raise my truck from the dead on my own.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc3.description: I first assumed the armored loaner was a joke by Edward and his brothers and then I considered that he might actually be very worried about my safety.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: I was sure he and his brothers had enjoyed the joke quite a bit behind my back. Or maybe, just maybe, a small voice whispered in my head, it’s not a joke, silly. Maybe he’s really that worried about you.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc3.description: I couldn't reconcile the ordinary notion of 'husband' with my image of Edward, likening the mismatch to casting an archangel as an accountant.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: But more than that, I just couldn’t reconcile a staid, respectable, dull concept like husband with my concept of Edward. It was like casting an archangel as an accountant;

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc3.description: I expected Edward's choice of replacement to embarrass me and make me the focus of stares and whispers.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: I knew his idea of a replacement was probably going to embarrass me. Make me the focus of stares and whispers.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.description: I learned that my father Charlie printed and spread HAVE YOU SEEN THIS BOY? flyers all over Forks and the Olympic Peninsula and made sure police stations had the same flyer.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: The HAVE YOU SEEN THIS BOY? posters were not Jacob’s father’s idea. It had been my father, Charlie, who’d printed up the flyers and spread them all over town. And not just Forks, but Port Angeles and Sequim and Hoquiam and Aberdeen and every other town in the Olympic Peninsula. He’d made sure that all the police stations in the state of Washington had the same flyer hanging on the wall, too.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.description: I felt the flyers like a fresh slap in the face and I had the usual big, fat lump in my throat and stinging tears whenever I saw them.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: Each one of them, stapled to telephone poles and taped to street signs, was like a fresh slap in the face. The flyers put the usual big, fat lump in my throat, the usual stinging tears in my eyes

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.description: I knew that Jacob was my best friend and that the pictures on the flyers were of my favorite mechanic.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: My best friend. My Jacob. ... My mind was sucked back into the thought I’d interrupted so immediately before. I couldn’t avoid it on this road. Not with pictures of my favorite mechanic flashing past me at regular intervals.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.description: I took Billy's side over my dad regarding the search, which caused my father to be disappointed and frustrated with me.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: And he was frustrated with me, for taking Billy’s side.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.description: I knew that Billy and I roughly knew where Jacob was and that no one had seen him, which influenced my decision not to put up posters.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: Because both Billy and I knew where Jacob was, roughly speaking, and we also knew that no one had seen this boy.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.description: I noticed that my dad had skipped fishing and was still sulking about the wedding, which affected my ability to use the phone inside the house.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: He’d skipped fishing again today. Still sulking about the wedding.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.description: I used the cell phone Edward had given me for emergencies and I kept my finger on the end button while dialing.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: I pulled the cell phone Edward had given me for emergencies out of the glove compartment. I dialed, keeping my finger on the “end” button as the phone rang.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob is somewhere in northern Canada and not coming home.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.source_text: He's not coming home, Bella. Sorry.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob hears the pack and is trying not to think human.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.source_text: He won't talk, though we know he hears us. He's trying not to think human, you know. Just going with his instincts.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.description: I learned that Seth and his mom will attend the wedding.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.source_text: Yeah, me and my mom will be there. It was cool of you to ask us.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.description: I changed from hoping Jacob might return to accepting that he won't come home while still wishing he would.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.source_text: I knew before I asked. I just can't help wishing.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.description: I updated my view that vampires and werewolves could get along because the friendship between Edward and Seth surprised me.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.source_text: The friendship that had sprung up between Edward and Seth was something that still boggled my mind. It was proof, though, that things didn't have to be this way. That vampires and werewolves could get along just fine, thank you very much, if they were of a mind to.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc6.description: I know that I am about to become a Mrs. in just a few days' time.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc6.source_text: his barely-a-legal-adult daughter who was about to become a Mrs. in just a few days’ time.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc6.description: I felt that my engagement ring suddenly weighed a hundred pounds on my finger.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc6.source_text: the ring suddenly weighed a hundred pounds on my finger.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc6.description: I believed that people would immediately assume I was pregnant because I was getting married at eighteen.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc6.source_text: I’d told Edward that people would immediately jump to this conclusion! What other possible reason would sane people have for getting married at eighteen?

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc6.description: I realized that I could not get the words out when everyone expected me to announce something.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc6.source_text: There was no way I was going to get the words out.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc6.description: I noticed Edward's cool, firm grasp on my hand and his calming presence during my panic.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc6.source_text: Edward’s cool, firm grasp kept it front and center.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc6.description: I heard Charlie angrily accuse me of being pregnant before he accepted my denial.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc7.description: I know that Bella has already accepted Edward's proposal prior to the conversation with Charlie.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc7.source_text: I mean no disrespect, but since Bella has already said yes and I don't want to diminish her choice in the matter, instead of asking you for her hand, I'm asking you for your blessing.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc7.description: I learned that I feel urgency about marrying because I am getting closer to nineteen while Edward remains seventeen.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc7.source_text: The rush was due to the fact that I was getting closer to nineteen every stinking day, while Edward stayed frozen in all his seventeen-year-old perfection, as he had for over ninety years.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc7.description: I experienced a rare moment of insight into Edward's perspective when I listened to the absolute confidence in his voice.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc7.source_text: For just an instant, listening to the absolute confidence in his voice, I experienced a rare moment of insight. I could see, fleetingly, the way the world looked to him.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc7.description: I am aware that Bella and Edward are planning to marry and have presented the marriage intent to Charlie.
I observed that Charlie reacted strongly and physically to seeing the ring, changing color and causing me to hold my breath.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc7.source_text: I held my breath while his skin changed colors—fair to red, red to purple, purple to blue.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc8.description: I learned that Charlie ultimately relented and said Get married.
I learned that Charlie insisted Bella tell her mother himself and refused to say anything to Renée.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc8.source_text: But you have to tell your mom! I’m not saying one word to Renée! That’s all yours!

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc8.description: I learned that Bella told her mother the engagement by stuttering out Mom, I’m marrying Edward.
I saw Bella's fear about telling Renée change to surprise and relief after Renée responded supportively and practically rather than with condemnation.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc8.source_text: I’d choked and stuttered out the impossible words: Mom, I’m marrying Edward.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc8.description: I observed that Bella's relationship with her mother is more accepting than Bella expected, with Renée calling Bella a completely different person and affectionately referring to her as My little middle-aged child.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc8.source_text: You’re a completely different person than I am. You make your own kinds of mistakes, and I’m sure you’ll have your share of regrets in life. My little middle-aged child. Luckily, you seem to have found another old soul.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc9.description: I learned that Renée accepted my engagement and was not angry about my decision.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc9.source_text: “You’re not… mad? You don’t think I’m making a humongous mistake?” “Well, sure, I wish you’d wait a few more years. ... But this isn’t about me. This is about you. Are you happy?”

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc9.description: I learned that Renée immersed herself in wedding planning and coordinated with Edward’s family so I did not have to organize the nuptials.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc9.source_text: For the last few weeks, Renée had unexpectedly immersed herself in wedding plans. She’d spent hours every day on the phone with Edward’s mother, Esme—no worries about the in-laws getting along. ... Edward’s family and my family were taking care of the nuptials together without my having to do or know or think too hard about any of it.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc9.description: I realized that I was having an out-of-body experience about the engagement and that the moment felt unreal to me.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc9.source_text: “I don’t know. I’m having an out-of-body experience right now.”

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc9.description: I realized that Edward makes me happy and that I do not expect to want anyone else in the future.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc9.source_text: “Does he make you happy, Bella?” “Yes, but—” “Are you ever going to want anyone else?” “No, but—”

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc9.description: I observed that my father, Charlie, was furious about the situation but that his anger was directed at Renée rather than at me, which relieved me.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc9.source_text: Charlie was furious, of course, but the sweet part was that he wasn’t furious at me. Renée was the traitor.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc9.description: I noted that Renée behaved like a supportive almost-mother-in-law and seemed to know what was best for me.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc9.source_text: “You’ve never been a teenager, sweetie. You know what’s best for you.” ... Renée adored Esme, but then, I doubted anyone could help responding that way to my lovable almost-mother-in-law.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc10.description: I learned that Alice asked me to wait briefly and promised my patience would be rewarded for a fitting.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc10.source_text: "Thirty seconds, please, Bella," Alice told me. "Your patience will be rewarded."

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc10.description: I learned that a white garment bag had been placed across the sofa and drew my attention after looking at Dad.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc10.source_text: I peeled my gaze off the unusually elegant Charlie for the first time and saw the dreaded white garment bag laid carefully across the sofa.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc10.description: I learned that I was expected to strip to my underwear and hold my arms out so Alice could check the fit.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc10.source_text: I stripped down to my underwear and held my arms straight out.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc10.description: I found that using my "happy place" helped me manage my nervousness about the fitting.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc10.source_text: "Go to your happy place, Bella. It won't take long."

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc10.description: I noticed that Alice took charge of the fitting and positioned herself as the confident dresser for both me and my father.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc10.source_text: "No one dressed by me ever looks like an idiot."

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.description: I recognized that in my happy place the whole wedding mess was over and done.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.source_text: In my happy place, the whole wedding mess was over and done.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.description: I remembered that I had married him and that marrying him fulfilled my side of our compromise.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.source_text: I’d married him. That was the big one.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.description: I noted that I had accepted all his outrageous gifts and was registered, however futilely, to attend Dartmouth College in the fall.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.source_text: I’d also accepted all his outrageous gifts and was registered, however futilely, to attend Dartmouth College in the fall.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.description: I knew a little about what I was going to be like when I wasn’t human anymore because I’d seen newborn vampires and heard my family-to-be’s stories.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.source_text: I knew a little about what I was going to be like when I wasn’t human anymore. I’d seen newborn vampires firsthand, and I’d heard all my family-to-be’s stories about those wild early days.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.description: I wanted the complete human experience of a real honeymoon before I traded my warm, breakable, pheromone-riddled body for something beautiful, strong, and unknown.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.source_text: I wanted the complete experience before I traded in my warm, breakable, pheromone-riddled body for something beautiful, strong… and unknown.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.description: I felt reassured that Edward and I were together so the where of the honeymoon wasn’t especially concerning to me.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.source_text: Edward and I were together, and I’d fulfilled my side of our compromise perfectly.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.description: I was only vaguely aware of Alice and the slip and slide of satin over my skin while I focused on being with Edward.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.source_text: I was only vaguely aware of Alice and the slip and slide of satin over my skin.

tw-book4-chapter19_Sc1.description: I learned that my placenta detached and that the detachment threatened my baby.
tw-book4-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: I heard 'The placenta must have detached!'

tw-book4-chapter19_Sc1.description: I learned that the baby was named Renesmee and that Edward spoke her name as she was born.
I learned that Renesmee had chocolate-brown irises, a thick layer of matted bloody curls, pale creamy skin, flushed cheeks, and an unexpected set of milk teeth.
tw-book4-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: I read 'Her irises were a familiar—but astonishing—chocolate brown.'

tw-book4-chapter19_Sc1.description: I decided that Renesmee was even more beautiful than her father, which surprised and amazed me.
tw-book4-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: I read 'She was even more beautiful than her father. Unbelievable. Impossible.'

tw-book4-chapter19_Sc1.description: I realized that Edward and I were bound together so tightly that if one of us died the other could not survive, and that understanding strengthened my will to live.
tw-book4-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: I thought 'If I were gone, he wouldn't live through it, either.'

tw-book4-chapter19_Sc2.description: I learned that morphine can pin me down and gag me, holding me paralyzed while venom burns through my veins.
tw-book4-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: I hadn’t guessed that the morphine would have this effect—that it would pin me down and gag me. Hold me paralyzed while I burned.

tw-book4-chapter19_Sc2.description: I learned that venom can burn ahead of medicine and seal veins, making painkillers ineffective against its spread.
tw-book4-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: Carlisle had tried with Emmett, but the venom had burned ahead of the medicine, sealing his veins.

tw-book4-chapter19_Sc2.description: I changed from wanting to die to fighting to survive for Renesmee, Edward, Jacob, and my family.
tw-book4-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: I had to survive this. Edward was depending on me. Jacob. Charlie Alice Rosalie Carlisle Renée Esme… Renesmee.

tw-book4-chapter19_Sc2.description: I found my heart again amid the transformation and felt a blazing heat that made me wish I had embraced death.
tw-book4-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: I could feel the pulse behind the fire raging now in my chest and realized that I’d found my heart again, just in time to wish I never had.

tw-book4-chapter19_Sc2.description: I hid the truth about morphine and venom from Edward because I did not want to make him more unwilling to change me.
tw-book4-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: Because I’d had morphine and venom together in my system before, and I knew the truth. I knew the numbness of the medicine was completely irrelevant while the venom seared through my veins. But there’d been no way I was going to mention that fact. Nothing that would make him more unwilling to change me.

tw-book4-chapter19_Sc3.description: I learned that Bella had a large amount of morphine in her system which complicates understanding her experience.
tw-book4-chapter19_Sc3.source_text: “We don’t know that. She had so much morphine in her system. We don’t know the effect that will have on her experience.”

tw-book4-chapter19_Sc3.description: I learned that Bella experienced a spreading, changing pain that began in her fingertips and toes and later concentrated in her throat and heart with intense thirst.
tw-book4-chapter19_Sc3.source_text: “On the good-news side of things, it started to fade from my fingertips and toes. ... And then the bad news. The fire in my throat wasn’t the same as before. I wasn’t only on fire, but I was now parched, too. Dry as bone. So thirsty. Burning fire, and burning thirst… Also bad news: The fire inside my heart got hotter.”

tw-book4-chapter19_Sc3.description: I learned that Bella’s wrists and ankles became free even while the internal burning continued.
tw-book4-chapter19_Sc3.source_text: “My wrists were free, though, and my ankles. The fire was totally extinguished there.”

tw-book4-chapter19_Sc3.description: I changed my belief about Bella’s prognosis from doubt to optimism after Alice and Carlisle judged that Bella was clearing and would be fine.
tw-book4-chapter19_Sc3.source_text: “She’s really going to be fine,” he breathed. “I couldn’t see right two days ago. But now that she’s free of all the blind spots, it’s a piece of cake.”

tw-book4-chapter2_Sc1.description: I noticed that I was kissing a vampire and that the scent of my blood still causes him pain.
tw-book4-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: But I knew the smell of my blood still caused him pain—still burned his throat like he was inhaling flames.

tw-book4-chapter2_Sc1.description: I learned that my mind is immune to Edward's ability to see into others' thoughts.
tw-book4-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: He couldn’t see into my mind, though, the way he saw into everyone else’s.

tw-book4-chapter2_Sc1.description: I decided that I want Edward and that I want him forever and am committed to marrying him.
tw-book4-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: I want you, and I want you forever.

tw-book4-chapter2_Sc1.description: I realized that Edward possesses a soul and that I consider his soul more beautiful than any other aspect of him.
tw-book4-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: He had the most beautiful soul, more beautiful than his brilliant mind or his incomparable face or his glorious body.

tw-book4-chapter2_Sc1.description: I observed that Edward is attempting to change lifelong habits of rejecting physical gratification.
tw-book4-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: Edward had spent most of his life rejecting any kind of physical gratification.

tw-book4-chapter2_Sc3.description: I learned that Tanya, Kate, and Irina had been joined by Carmen and Eleazar and that their coven resembled the Cullens in size and compassion.
tw-book4-chapter2_Sc3.source_text: Tanya had a big family now, almost as big as the Cullens. There were five of them; Tanya, Kate, and Irina had been joined by Carmen and Eleazar much the same way the Cullens had been joined by Alice and Jasper, all of them bonded by their desire to live more compassionately than normal vampires did.

tw-book4-chapter2_Sc3.description: I learned about the plague of the immortal children and that those children were frozen at their developmental level and could not be taught or controlled.
tw-book4-chapter2_Sc3.source_text: The woman who created Tanya, Kate, and Irina—who loved them, I believe—lived many years before I was born, during a time of plague in our world, the plague of the immortal children... However, they could not be taught. They were frozen at whatever level of development they’d achieved before being bitten.

tw-book4-chapter2_Sc3.description: I learned that the Volturi studied the immortal children and ultimately destroyed them because Caius decided they could not protect the vampires' secret.
tw-book4-chapter2_Sc3.source_text: The Volturi studied the immortal children, at home in Volterra and all around the world. Caius decided the young ones were incapable of protecting our secret. And so they had to be destroyed.

tw-book4-chapter2_Sc3.description: I felt revulsion imagining infant vampires but came to accept Carlisle's framing of a single overriding rule: Keep the secret, with many practical implications.
tw-book4-chapter2_Sc3.source_text: Only one rule, actually—one law that broke down into a thousand different facets: Keep the secret.

tw-book4-chapter2_Sc3.description: I felt increased sympathy for Tanya and her sisters because they were pardoned yet left with unhealing hearts and suspicion toward their mother's choices.
tw-book4-chapter2_Sc3.source_text: Tanya and her sisters were pardoned, but left with unhealing hearts and a very healthy respect for the law. . . . I don’t think they’ve ever truly forgiven her.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: I saw extreme visual clarity including an unnamed eighth color at the edge of the spectrum.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: I could see each color of the rainbow in the white light, and, at the very edge of the spectrum, an eighth color I had no name for.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: I watched dust motes spinning like little planets in a celestial dance and found them visually beautiful.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: They spun like little planets, moving around each other in a celestial dance.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: I realized that I did not need to breathe and that my lungs reacted indifferently to the influx of air.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: I didn’t need the air. My lungs weren’t waiting for it. They reacted indifferently to the influx.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: I discovered that I liked the air despite not needing it.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: I did not need the air, but I liked it.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: I tasted an intense almost-honey-lilac-and-sun scent as the strongest presence along with many complex flavors and smells.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: And most of all, I could taste an almost-honey-lilac-and-sun-flavored scent that was the strongest thing, the closest thing to me.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: I heard a rich mixture of scents translated into flavor comparisons that included cinnamon, hyacinth, pear, seawater, rising bread, pine, vanilla, leather, apple, moss, lavender, and chocolate.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: Cinnamon, hyacinth, pear, seawater, rising bread, pine, vanilla, leather, apple, moss, lavender, chocolate.…

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: I heard household sounds including a muted television and someone shifting weight on the first floor that I suspected might be Rosalie.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: The TV downstairs had been muted, and I heard someone—Rosalie?—shift her weight on the first floor.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: I heard a faint, thudding rhythm with a voice shouting angrily to the beat and wondered briefly if I could hear as far as the freeway.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.source_text:
I also heard a faint, thudding rhythm, with a voice shouting angrily to the beat. Rap music? I was mystified for a moment, and then the sound faded away like a car passing by with the windows rolled down.
With a start, I realized that this could be exactly right. Could I hear all the way to the freeway?

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.description: I realized someone was holding my hand when it was squeezed lightly and noticed the skin was perfectly smooth and an unexpected temperature.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: I didn’t realize someone was holding my hand until whoever it was squeezed it lightly. Like it had before to hide the pain, my body locked down again in surprise. This was not a touch I expected. The skin was perfectly smooth, but it was the wrong temperature. Not cold.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward wouldn’t feel cold to me and that we were the same temperature now.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: Oh. Of course. Edward wouldn’t feel cold to me. We were the same temperature now.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc2.description: I found that my reflexive response occurred within about a sixteenth of a second and involved flipping off my back and crouching defensively.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: I flipped off my back in a spin so fast it should have turned the room into an incomprehensible blur—but it did not...So by the time I found myself crouched against the wall defensively—about a sixteenth of a second later—I already understood what had startled me, and that I had overreacted.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc2.description: I realized that I had never truly seen Edward's face before and that my previous conviction about its perfection was mistaken.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: I had never seen it before this second. I may as well have been blind.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc2.description: I understood that my vampire family considered me the danger in that moment.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: What I hadn’t grasped immediately was that I was the danger.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc2.description: I noticed that my vision took in microscopic details like every dust mote, splinter, and loose thread while I spun.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: I saw every dust mote, every splinter in the wood-paneled walls, every loose thread in microscopic detail as my eyes whirled past them.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc3.description: I learned that I am a newborn vampire and that thirst is my immediate condition.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: I was a newborn vampire. The dry, scorching ache in my throat gave proof to that.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc3.description: I realized that I still experienced intense desire when Edward touched me despite expecting to feel only thirst as a newborn.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: But as Edward’s hand curled to the shape of my face like satin-covered steel, desire raced through my dried-out veins, singing from my scalp to my toes.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc3.description: I demonstrated immediate and overwhelming attachment to Edward by throwing my arms around him.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: I threw my arms around him.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc3.description: I discovered that I was temporarily stronger than Edward, enough to make him say 'ow'.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: You’re just a bit stronger than I am for the moment.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc3.description: I became worried about how my transformation affected my relationships, including concern for Renesmee, Jacob, the Cullens, and Charlie.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: Everything? My mind spun out, spiraling back to my last human hour. Already, the memory seemed dim, like I was watching through a thick, dark veil—because my human eyes had been half blind.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc4.description: I felt reassured that I still felt like myself after the transformation despite the intense changes.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: "I feel like me. Sort of. I didn’t expect that."

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc4.description: I declared my love to Edward and noticed my voice sounded unusually clear and bell-like.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: "I love you," I said, but it sounded like singing. My voice rang and shimmered like a bell.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc4.description: I experienced overwhelming emotions and sensory distraction that made it hard to stick to one train of thought.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: These emotions were so much stronger than I was used to that it was hard to stick to one train of thought despite the extra room in my head.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc4.description: I shared a kiss with Edward that felt unlike any before and deepened my sense of closeness with him.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: He kissed me, soft as a whisper at first, and then suddenly stronger, fiercer.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc4.description: I realized we were not alone when Emmett cleared his throat and I adjusted my posture because of company.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: Someone cleared his throat. Emmett. I recognized the deep sound at once, joking and annoyed at the same time.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc4.description: I understood that morphine had been used during my transformation and that Carlisle wanted to know what I remembered.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: "It seems like we did something right with the morphine this time. Tell me, what do you remember of the transformation process?"

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc6.description: I learned that my vampire appearance is strikingly beautiful, fluid in stillness, and characterized by pale flawless skin, dark heavy hair, and luminous limbs.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: I read: "My first reaction was an unthinking pleasure. The alien creature in the glass was indisputably beautiful, every bit as beautiful as Alice or Esme. She was fluid even in stillness, and her flawless face was pale as the moon against the frame of her dark, heavy hair. Her limbs were smooth and strong, skin glistening subtly, luminous as a pearl."

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc6.description: I learned that my eyes are currently blazing crimson and I was told they will darken to amber and then gold over the course of months due to diet.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: I read: "'They'll darken up in a few months,' Edward said in a soft, comforting voice. 'Animal blood dilutes the color more quickly than a diet of human blood. They'll turn amber first, then gold.'"

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc6.description: I realized that I possess an unexpected ability to control and stop emotional reactions, which surprised the others and is unusual for a newborn.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: I read: "'I've never seen a newborn do that—stop an emotion in its tracks that way. You were upset, but when you saw our concern, you reined it in, regained power over yourself.'"

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc6.description: I felt horror and anxiety when I saw my terrifying eyes in the mirror and I feared that I might snap or become a monster at any moment.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: I read: "My second reaction was horror." and "At any moment, would I snap? Turn into a monster?"

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc6.description: I felt Edward's comfort and protective concern when he stroked his hand down my arm as if encouraging me to calm down.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: I read: "Edward stroked his hand down my arm, as if encouraging me to thaw."

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc1.description: I realized that detailed visibility made heights less appealing to me.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: I’d never really been afraid of heights per se, but being able to see all the details with such clarity made the prospect less appealing.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc1.description: I noticed that Renesmee and Jacob were downstairs and that Jacob's heart was the one I heard.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: Renesmee and Jacob are downstairs. . . . I realized belatedly that it must have been Jacob’s heart I’d heard below.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc1.description: I felt validated and pleased when Edward called my landing graceful because no one had called me graceful before.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: That was quite graceful—even for a vampire. It was the first time anyone had ever applied the word graceful to me in my entire life... or, well, existence anyway.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc1.description: I understood that I was now the monster and had to avoid scents that might trigger my wild side around people I love.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: Right. I was the monster now. I had to keep away from scents that might trigger my wild side. From the people that I loved in particular.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.description: I learned that I can cross a fifty-yard river in a single bound and land safely in the trees.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: The fifty yard width was slightly too easy a distance. . . . It was a strange, giddy, electrifying thing, but a short thing. An entire second had yet to pass, and I was across.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.description: I discovered a sudden, raw, massive strength thrilling in my limbs that made nearby objects seem fragile.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: the raw, massive strength thrilling in my limbs. I was suddenly sure that if I wanted to tunnel under the river, to claw or beat my way straight through the bedrock, it wouldn’t take me very long. The objects around me—the trees, the shrubs, the rocks… the house—had all begun to look very fragile.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.description: I became worried about damaging the forest because my strength made the trees and surroundings seem vulnerable.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: I was more worried about the forest getting hurt.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.description: I learned that my skirt could be a hindrance and that I could rip it carefully to move more freely.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: And then stopped when the tight satin split six inches up my thigh. Alice! ... I bent to carefully grasp the hem at the undamaged right seam between my fingers and, exerting the tiniest amount of pressure possible, I ripped the dress open to the top of my thigh. Then I fixed the other side to match.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.description: I realized that Jacob might be watching and that I couldn't imagine what he was thinking about me now.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: So Jacob was watching, too? I couldn’t imagine what he was thinking now, or what he was still doing here.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.description: I decided that any reunion with Jacob should wait until I was more stable and after time had healed past wounds.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: I’d envisioned our reunion—if he could ever forgive me—taking place far in the future, when I was more stable, and time had healed the wounds I’d inflicted in his heart.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: I learned that I was stronger and that every stride of mine matched the length of three of Edward's.
