tw-book4-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: He was faster than me. I couldn’t imagine how he moved his legs with such blinding speed, but it was beyond me. However, I was stronger, and every stride of mine matched the length of three of his.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: I learned that I could see each tiny leaf clearly even while rocketing through the forest at high speed.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: For, while I rocketed over, under, and through the thick jade maze at a rate that should have reduced everything around me to a streaky green blur, I could plainly see each tiny leaf on all the small branches of every insignificant shrub that I passed.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: I realized that I did not tire as expected because my breath came effortlessly and my strength only increased.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: I kept waiting to feel winded, but my breath came effortlessly. I waited for the burn to begin in my muscles, but my strength only seemed to increase as I grew accustomed to my stride.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: I found myself more captivated and distracted by Edward's beauty and the way his lips moved when he spoke.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc3.source_text:
He was so beautiful that I could only stare.

"What are we hunting?" ... "It was hard not to become sidetracked with everything fresh in my strong new eyes. "What are we hunting?" "Elk. I thought something easy for your first time . . ." He trailed off when my eyes narrowed at the word easy.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc3.description: I noticed that I was becoming very thirsty and that the dry burn in my throat was worsening.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: But I wasn’t going to argue; I was too thirsty. As soon as I’d started to think about the dry burn in my throat, it was all I could think about.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc4.description: I learned to use enhanced hearing and smell when Edward instructed me to close my eyes and listen.
I learned that the prey was located by the creek to the northeast after I identified the lapping and heavy hearts.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: "By the creek, to the northeast?" I asked. "Yes." His tone was approving.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc4.description: I learned that there were five animals at the stream, not three as I initially guessed.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: "Three?" I guessed. "Five. There are two more in the trees behind them."

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc4.description: I felt that the warm, tangy smell of prey became less objectionable as my thirst intensified.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: Another bout of baking thirst intruded on my awareness, and suddenly the warm, tangy odor wasn’t quite so objectionable.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc4.description: I trusted Edward's touch and voice to calm and guide me, which momentarily eased the urgency of my thirst.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: "Hold still for a minute," he said, putting his hands lightly on my shoulders. The urgency of my thirst receded momentarily at his touch.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc6.description: I realized my thirst was stronger when Edward touched me than I had expected.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: I’d been prepared for the thirst part, but not this. I’d been so sure it wouldn’t be the same when he touched me. Well, truthfully, it wasn’t the same. It was stronger.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc6.description: I admitted that I still wanted Edward despite my uncertainty and the danger of my thirst.
I detected a different warm scent and followed a faint trail to the east, leading the way with Edward following me.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: There was a hint of something different, a faint trail to the east. . . . My eyes flashed open, but my focus was still on sharper senses as I turned and darted silently eastward.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc6.description: I saw a very large tawny cat in the branches hunting and preparing to spring.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: I saw the tawny hide of the great cat slinking along the wide branch of a spruce just down and to the left of my perch. He was big—easily four times my mass. The lion’s tail twitched spasmodically as he prepared to spring.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc7.description: I learned that I killed the mountain lion with ease and drank its blood.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc7.source_text:
My jaws locked easily over the precise point where the heat flow concentrated.
It was effortless as biting into butter. My teeth were steel razors; they cut through the fur and fat and sinews like they weren’t there.
The flavor was wrong, but the blood was hot and wet and it soothed the ragged, itching thirst as I drank in an eager rush.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc7.description: I learned that I remained thirsty even after drinking the lion's blood.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc7.source_text:
The lion was finished before I was. The thirst flared again when he ran dry, and I shoved his carcass off my body in disgust.
"Why am I still thirsty?"

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc7.description: I observed that I was dirty and my dress was bloodstained and torn after the encounter.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc7.source_text: I wiped my face off on the back of my arm and tried to fix the dress. I was covered in dirt, my hair knotted, my dress bloodstained and hanging in tatters.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc7.description: I thought I could have done the kill better than I actually did.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc7.source_text: "I guess I could have done that better."

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc8.description: I learned that watching Edward hunt was a surprisingly sensual and beautiful experience from my vampire perspective.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc8.source_text: It was a surprisingly sensual experience to observe Edward hunting. His smooth spring was like the sinuous strike of a snake; his hands were so sure, so strong, so completely inescapable; his full lips were perfect as they parted gracefully over his gleaming teeth.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc8.description: I learned that Edward can kill multiple deer quickly and neatly without ruffling a hair or staining his shirt.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc8.source_text: He’d finished with two before I was done with the first, not a hair ruffled, not a spot on his white shirt.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc8.description: I felt a sudden jolt of both pride and desire and I came to believe that he was mine and nothing could ever separate him from me now.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc8.source_text: He was glorious. I felt a sudden jolt of both pride and desire. He was mine. Nothing could ever separate him from me now.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc8.description: I learned that after feeding I would feel very full and sloshy and that the burn in my throat would be only muted but that thirst was an inescapable part of this life.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc8.source_text: Done, I think. I felt very full, sort of sloshy, even. I wasn’t sure how much more liquid would fit into my body. But the burn in my throat was only muted. Then again, I’d known that thirst was just an inescapable part of this life.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc9.source_text: “I want to see Renesmee,” I said.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc9.description: I noticed my thirst was tamed but not erased.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc9.source_text: Now that my thirst was tamed (if nothing close to erased), my earlier worries were hard to forget.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc9.description: I realized I could love Edward more than I had before and perhaps more than anyone in history.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc9.source_text: Maybe I would just love Edward more than anyone in the history of the world had ever loved anyone else.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc9.description: I felt Edward's skin warmer than before and noticed his cheek faintly flushed and the shadows under his eyes all but vanished.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc9.source_text: He held out his hand to me. I took it, and his skin felt warmer than before. His cheek was faintly flushed, the shadows under his eyes all but vanished.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc9.description: I wrapped my arms around him and felt him lock his arms around my waist and kiss me forcefully, which increased our intimacy.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc9.source_text: I stretched up on my toes and wrapped my arms around him. Gently. He was not so hesitant in his movements; his arms locked around my waist and pulled me tight against his body. His lips crushed down on mine, but they felt soft.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc9.description: I felt my memories of Renesmee become dreamlike and artificial and feared they would slip away, making me hurry to see her.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc9.source_text: But my memory of Renesmee, before and after her birth, was becoming more and more dreamlike to me. More unlikely. All my memories of her were human memories; an aura of artificiality clung to them. Every minute, the reality of that little stranger slipped further away.

tw-book4-chapter22_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob's scent had an animal edge that repelled me and that his blood smelled less human than a mountain lion's.
tw-book4-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "Jacob didn’t smell that much more human than the mountain lion, there was an animal edge to his blood that instantly repelled"

tw-book4-chapter22_Sc2.description: I became hopeful that Jacob and I could be friends now that his physical revulsion might prevent romantic love between us.
tw-book4-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "Maybe now I could truly be his friend, since I disgusted him enough physically that he couldn't love me the same way as before"

tw-book4-chapter22_Sc2.description: I felt Edward's protectiveness and love as he held me, whispered 'I love you', and insisted I should see our daughter.
tw-book4-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "I love you" and "Bella needs to see our daughter, Get out of her way"

tw-book4-chapter22_Sc2.description: I discovered that my daughter, Renesmee, had grown quickly into a small, alert child with both my coloring and Edward's features and a startlingly adult awareness.
tw-book4-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "She was maybe twice the size of the baby in my dim memory, her shiny bronze-colored hair fell in ringlets past her shoulders, her chocolate brown eyes examined me with an interest that was not at all childlike"

tw-book4-chapter22_Sc3.description: I learned that Renesmee can communicate by projecting a memory-like image into my mind.
tw-book4-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: “It was the only memory she had of you,” Edward explained.

tw-book4-chapter22_Sc3.description: I felt a renewed, powerful attachment to Renesmee because she had been the anchor that pulled me back from the edge of darkness.
tw-book4-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: She was hot in my arms, reminding me of the moment when the blackness had almost won, when there was nothing in the world left to hold on to.

tw-book4-chapter22_Sc3.description: I noticed that Jacob was willing and able to hold Renesmee and that his hands shook as he did so, which updated my view of his protective role.
tw-book4-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: I watched in shock as he reached for Renesmee, and then in utter horror as Rosalie surrendered her to him without a fight.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: I felt that I should have been the one apologizing for my temper and that my guilt outweighed others' reactions.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I heard myself think, "So shouldn’t I have been the one apologizing?"

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: I learned that Renesmee is not venomous and that fact reduced one of my fears about her harming others.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I was told, "Lucky thing Ness—Renesmee’s not venomous," and I remembered being the first person she’d bitten.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: I believed I was a bad person in the aftermath and I said aloud, "I’m a bad person."
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I heard myself admit, "I’m a bad person."

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: I noticed Edward taking blame for things and I did not want him to shoulder this fault as he often does.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I observed, "Stop that," when Edward began to apologize for me and I thought, "I didn’t want him taking the blame for this the way he always took everything on himself."

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: I learned that Seth would likely recover quickly and that Carlisle had treated his injuries sufficiently for him to rest.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I watched Carlisle say, "Try to not move for, oh, a few hours, I guess," and I saw Seth fall asleep shortly after.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: I learned that the feud with Sam’s pack had ended and the truce was renewed and stronger than before.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: The main thing was the end of the feud with Sam’s pack—which was why the others felt safe to come and go as they pleased again. The truce was stronger than ever.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: I learned that Renesmee was untouchable because of Jacob’s imprinting on her and that no wolf would ever intentionally kill the object of another wolf’s imprinting.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: the most absolute of all the pack’s laws was that no wolf ever kill the object of another wolf’s imprinting. So Renesmee was untouchable because of the way Jacob now felt about her.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: I learned that Alphas could speak to each other while in their wolf form now but that the communication was limited to the thoughts they chose to share.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: Alphas could speak to each other while in their wolf form. It wasn’t the same as before; they couldn’t hear every thought the way they had prior to the split. It was more like speaking aloud, Seth had said. Sam could only hear the thoughts Jacob wanted to share, and vice versa.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: I became conflicted about whether telling Charlie that I had died was the kindest option or whether letting him see me later, even if he made wrong assumptions, would be better to protect him.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: What would be the right thing to tell him? Were the Cullens right? Was telling him that I’d died the best, the kindest way? ... There was still my idea—let Charlie see me, when I was ready for that, and let him make his own wrong assumptions.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: I realized that I owed Jacob a great deal because he had allowed my transformation as Alpha and that my feelings about him had shifted toward family even while I felt chagrin.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: And Sam couldn’t get mad about my transformation, either, because Jacob—speaking as the rightful Alpha—had allowed it. You said we belonged in each other’s lives, right? That we were family.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: I learned that Renesmee is being measured frequently because she is still growing quickly.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc3.source_text: Four times a day, Carlisle corrected absently as he motioned the others toward the couch.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: I became more horrified and fearful as I realized how fast Renesmee had matured and what that could mean.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc3.source_text: She had matured from a single cell to a normal-sized baby in the course of a few weeks.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: I discovered that Renesmee experiences memories like visions and can recall recent events vividly.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc3.source_text: Though I was prepared, it still made me gasp to see the memory like a vision in my head.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: I felt a deeper connection and protectiveness toward Renesmee when she fit easily in my arms and touched my face.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc3.source_text: She fit so easily in my arms, like they’d been shaped just for her.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc4.description: I learned that Renesmee can replay memories and transmit them like an instant replay.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: Renesmee touched my neck, repeating the scene of departure right back, like an instant replay.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc4.description: I learned that a memory of thirst could smell like human blood and cause a strong visceral reaction.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: The smell coming from a strange metal cup—hard enough not to be bitten through easily—sent a flash burn through my throat.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc4.description: I accepted the supernatural quality of Renesmee's gift and abandoned my prior skepticism.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: It seemed an entirely natural part of her, almost to be expected.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc4.description: I began to believe that my exceptional self-control might allow me to avoid the violent newborn phase entirely.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: What if I didn’t have to be a newborn? Not in the crazed killing-machine sense, anyway.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc4.description: I felt uncertain about Jasper's reaction to Renesmee and worried that he might be upset with me until Edward reassured me.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: Is he mad at me? I asked quietly.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc5.description: I learned that I can stand motionless for very long periods without fatigue and remain equally relaxed afterward.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: I knew I would be able to stand like this for a week without moving and I would feel just as relaxed at the end of the seven days as I did at the beginning.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc5.description: I learned that Renesmee communicates her experiences through detailed memory-stories that I can feel when I hold her and that her memories can blur as she tires.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: Renesmee told me about every minute happening of the day...After almost an hour...Renesmee’s memory stories began to slow. They got slightly blurry around the edges and drifted out of focus before they came to their conclusions.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc5.description: I began to consider my extreme self-control as possibly being a gift akin to Siobhan's ability to will goals into reality rather than solely the result of preparation.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: “Have you ever seen an equivalent to self-control as a talent?” Edward asked Carlisle. “It’s slightly similar to what Siobhan has always been able to do, though she wouldn’t call it a gift.”

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc5.description: I felt my connection to Renesmee deepen as I was pleased to find my faces appeared often in her unconscious thoughts, rivaling Jacob in frequency.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: I was pleased by how often my face—both of my faces, hideous human and glorious immortal—cropped up in her unconscious thoughts. More than Edward or Rosalie. I was neck and neck with Jacob; I tried not to let that get to me.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc5.description: I learned that my nineteenth birthday was being celebrated by the family on September thirteenth with Alice presenting a decorated key.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: Alice held the key out for me, and I automatically gripped Renesmee more securely in my right arm so that I could open my left. “Happy birthday!” she squealed. “We’re not celebrating your vampire birthday. Yet. It’s September thirteenth, Bella. Happy nineteenth birthday!”

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc1.description: I learned that I stopped aging three days ago and consider myself eighteen forever.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: No, this doesn’t count. I stopped aging three days ago. I am eighteen forever.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc1.description: I learned that my present was from all of the family and that Esme was mentioned especially.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: “Enjoy your gift,” Rosalie said. “It’s from all of us. Esme especially.”

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc1.description: I realized that many of my essential core traits carried over into my new body and that I still disliked surprises and gifts.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: I realized that lots of things about me—like truly hating surprises, and not liking gifts in general much more—had not changed one bit.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc1.description: I believe my relationship with Rosalie has softened and that shared struggle helped wash away much of her resentment.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: I hadn’t been entirely sure it would last after Renesmee’s life was no longer tied to mine. But maybe we had fought together on the same side long enough that we would always be friends now. That seemed to have washed away her resentment for all my other choices.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc1.description: I learned that Renesmee is habitually held and has never been set down in her entire life.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: “Where does she usually sleep?” Alice shrugged. “In Rose's arms. Or Jacob's. Or Esme's. You get the picture. She has never been set down in her entire life.”

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc2.description: I learned that Alice deliberately prevented me from seeing as part of a playful test.
I learned that the woods held unfamiliar scents that piqued my curiosity and suggested human activity nearby.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: There were new scents here, piquing my interest, increasing my curiosity. Scents that didn’t belong in the deep woods. Honeysuckle. Smoke. Roses. Sawdust? Something metallic, too. The richness of deep earth, dug up and exposed.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc2.description: I realized I was able to keep up easily and that I could control sudden urges of force when needed.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: I kept up easily. I wasn’t afraid of hitting a tree; the tree would be the only one getting hurt in that scenario.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc2.description: I felt reassured by Edward when I felt his fingers weave through mine and when he guided me forward.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: I felt Edward’s fingers weave through mine. "Just a few seconds more, Bella. Then she’ll go annoy someone else." He pulled me forward.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc3.description: I saw a tiny stone cottage in a clearing that was lavender gray in the starlight with honeysuckle, roses, and an amethyst path.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: There, nestled into a small clearing in the forest, was a tiny stone cottage, lavender gray in the light of the stars.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc3.description: I learned that Esme had thought we might like a place of our own for a while and that the family had renovated the cottage.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: "Esme thought we might like a place of our own for a while, but she didn’t want us too far away," Edward murmured. "And she loves any excuse to renovate. This little place has been crumbling away out here for at least a hundred years."

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc3.description: I discovered that my closet in the cottage was already stocked and that Alice expected me to use it wisely.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: Anyhoo, your closet is stocked. Use it wisely.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc3.description: I realized that my initial shock turned into genuine love for the cottage despite my surprise.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: "You like it." I shook my head. "Love it?" I nodded.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc3.description: I understood that Edward considered the gift to be for both of us when he corrected me by saying "Us."
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: "You're giving me a house for my birthday?" I whispered. "Us," Edward corrected.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc4.description: I unlocked the cottage door and entered while Edward led the way.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc4.source_text: He held his hand out toward the doorknob, waiting for me to do the honors. I stuck the key in the lock and turned it.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc4.description: I realized the cottage felt like a fairy tale and that Edward belonged there rather than in horror stories.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc4.source_text: It was a place where anyone could believe magic existed. A place where you just expected Snow White to walk right in with her apple in hand, or a unicorn to stop and nibble at the rosebushes. Edward had always thought that he belonged to the world of horror stories. Of course, I’d known he was dead wrong. It was obvious that he belonged here. In a fairy tale. And now I was in the story with him.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc4.description: I noticed Esme's artistic sense in the cottage decor and thought Esme was an artist.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc4.source_text: Right now, I’m thinking that Esme is an artist. It’s so perfect!

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc4.description: I felt overwhelmed by many emotions at once about our future, ranging from joy to worry to amazement.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc4.source_text: “Everything,” I told him. “All at the same time, you know. Good things and things to worry about and things that are new. How I keep using too many superlatives in my head.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc4.description: I decided that I would lie to Alice and tell her I spent hours in the closet playing dress-up.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc4.source_text: “We’re going to tell Alice that I ran right to the clothes,” I whispered, twisting my fingers into his hair and pulling my face closer to his. “We’re going to tell her I spent hours in there playing dress-up. We’re going to lie.”

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc5.description: I learned that I have dramatically heightened senses and perception as a vampire, including stronger vision, taste, and tactile sensitivity.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc5.source_text: I could really appreciate him now—could properly see every beautiful line of his perfect face, of his long, flawless body with my strong new eyes, every angle and every plane of him. I could taste his pure, vivid scent on my tongue and feel the unbelievable silkiness of his marble skin under my sensitive fingertips.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc5.description: I learned that I and my mate no longer needed to breathe, rest, eat, or tend to mundane human needs after transformation.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc5.source_text: We didn’t have to catch our breath or rest or eat or even use the bathroom; we had no more mundane human needs.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc5.description: I realized that I am finally an equal, active participant with Edward in our physical relationship.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc5.source_text: We could love together—both active participants now. Finally equals.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc5.description: I understood that my desire could be endless and that I could always want more without a natural stopping point.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc5.source_text: I was always going to want more. And the day was never going to end. So, in such a situation, how did we ever stop?

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc5.description: I noticed that Edward appeared to be a different, more uninhibited person physically after my change.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc5.source_text: He was all new, a different person as our bodies tangled gracefully into one on the sand-pale floor. No caution, no restraint.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc1.description: I realized Renesmee would be awake soon and that it must be nearly seven in the morning.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: "It must be nearly seven in the morning."

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc1.description: I experienced a sudden panic that made my body freeze up.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: "Abruptly, something close to panic had my body freezing up."

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc1.description: I discovered that Alice had prepared an enormous wardrobe with everything wrapped in garment bags.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: "Everything was wrapped in garment bags, pristine and white, row after row after row."

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward used scent to find casual clothes for me, producing artfully faded blue jeans and a long-sleeved white t-shirt almost instantly.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: "With a triumphant grin, he held out a pair of artfully faded blue jeans." and "He followed his nose to a half-rack, unearthing a long-sleeved white t-shirt."

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc1.description: I found it difficult to think of myself as a mother despite Renesmee being very real and vital in my life.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: "Though Renesmee was very real and vital in my life, it was still difficult to think of myself as a mother."

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc1.description: I felt Edward as a strong, steady presence who reassured me and helped me stay composed.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: "It’s all right, love. Get dressed, and we’ll be back to the house in two seconds." and "He smiled, but didn’t laugh; he was a strong man."

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob phased in front of Charlie and displayed himself to him in the woods.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: “He phased in front of Charlie,” Edward hissed.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob told Charlie that I had been sick but had changed and now looked more like Esme than Renée.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: “I told him that you had been sick, but you were fine now—it was just that you’d had to change a little bit in the process of getting better. He wanted to know what I meant by ‘change,’ and I told him that you looked a lot more like Esme now than you looked like Renée.”

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.description: I felt relief when I heard that Charlie requested to be told as little as possible and to only learn need-to-know details.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: “His main request is that he be told as little as possible about all of this. If it’s not absolutely essential for him to know something, then keep it to yourself. Need to know, only.”

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.description: I felt furious at Jacob and threatened to give Renesmee to Rosalie and rip his head off for putting Charlie at risk.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: “You have thirty seconds to tell me every single word before I give Renesmee to Rosalie and rip your miserable head off. Seth won’t be able to stop me this time.”

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.description: I learned that Charlie wanted two things: to see me and to be told as little as necessary so he could pretend things were normal.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.source_text:
“After he got calmed down, he just wanted two things. He wanted to see you, and I said it would be better if he gave me a head start to explain.”
“Other than that, he’d just like to pretend things are normal.”

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc5.description: I learned that Charlie smiled at the idea of being a grandfather to Renesmee.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc5.source_text: 'Congrats, Gramps,' and all of that. He even smiled a little.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc5.description: I realized that my fear about Charlie meeting Renesmee softened into something less anguished.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc5.source_text: The stinging returned to my eyes, but not out of fear or anguish this time.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc5.description: I accepted Jacob's hand and I considered our relationship reconciled into a balanced friendship.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc5.source_text: He held out his hand: an offer.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc6.description: I learned that Alice prepared cosmetic contacts to cloud Bella's vision and hide her eye color and that the venom in Bella's eyes will dissolve those contacts in a few hours.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc6.source_text: These will irritate your eyes—they won’t hurt, but they’ll cloud your vision. Keep in mind that those won’t last forever—the venom in your eyes will dissolve them in a few hours.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc6.description: I felt undiluted fear about gambling on my iffy self-control with my pure human father and feared the emotional and physical consequences of failure.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc6.source_text: Undiluted fear ripped through my stomach as the enormity of what I was about to do hit me. I was going to gamble on my iffy self-control with my pure human father as the guinea pig.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc6.description: I realized that I needed Charlie in my life and that others believed keeping him in my life would make me happier.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc6.source_text: If I didn't believe you could handle it, we'd disappear today. This very minute. But you can. And you'll be happier if you can have Charlie in your life.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc7.description: I learned that my body changed into a vampire form with sharper teeth and a different, wind-chime voice.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc7.source_text: My new teeth were sharper against my granite skin than my human teeth had been against my soft human lips. I winced at my wind-chime voice.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc7.description: I learned that I experienced an intense physical thirst and attraction to Charlie's scent while also feeling remorse and restraint.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc7.source_text: Charlie’s scent was a fistful of flames, punching straight down my throat. But it was so much more than pain. It was a hot stabbing of desire, too.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc7.description: I stated ownership of Renesmee and declared that I wanted to keep her, defining my maternal claim.
I decided to accept and use a cover story presenting Renesmee as our adopted niece to protect her from Charlie's scrutiny.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc7.source_text: 'This is her. The orphan Jacob said you’re adopting.' 'My niece,' Edward lied smoothly.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc8.description: I held Renesmee back when she reached toward Charlie in curiosity and thirst.
I noticed Renesmee pushed her hand against my neck and sent a thought containing thirst, curiosity, and Charlie’s face.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc8.source_text: She pushed her other hand against my neck, thirst, curiosity, and Charlie’s face in her thoughts.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc8.description: I felt relieved when Charlie agreed to go along with the public story to protect Bella and Renesmee.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc8.source_text: “Can you go along with the lies for them?”

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc8.description: I realized that my relationship with Charlie is strained but that he is willing to cooperate for our safety.

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: I learned that Bella reassured Charlie and cradled sleeping Renesmee briefly to soothe him.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc1.source_text: I read 'Bella reassures him, cradles sleeping Renesmee briefly, and they share a tender father-daughter exchange.'

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: I feel that Bella's relationship with Charlie was strengthened by the tender father-daughter exchange and by letting him hold Renesmee.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc1.source_text: I read 'they share a tender father-daughter exchange' and 'asks if he may hold her, which Bella allows.'

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: I realized that Bella felt elated and stunned that she managed the day without hurting Charlie, which changed her confidence about handling the situation.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc1.source_text: I read 'leaving Bella feeling elated and stunned that she managed the day without hurting him.'

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc2.description: I saw Edward come to Bella and embrace her.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc2.source_text: Edward comes to Bella and embraces her.

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc2.description: I noticed Emmett teasing Bella about her newborn status and that the teasing provoked a low snarl from her.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc2.source_text: Emmett teases Bella about her newborn status, provoking a low snarl from her.

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc2.description: I inferred Bella is emotionally close to Edward because he comes to her and embraces her.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc2.source_text: Edward comes to Bella and embraces her.

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc2.description: I began to believe Bella is more relaxed and integrated with the Cullen family after the group's human charade slipped slightly.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc2.source_text: The group’s human charade has slipped slightly, and the family members are at ease — Alice lounging, Jasper nearby, Carlisle reading, Esme sketching, Rosalie and Emmett building a house of cards, Edward at the piano, and Jacob raiding the fridge.

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc3.description: I learned that Bella challenged Emmett to an arm-wrestling match with a wager that he stop teasing her about her private life.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc3.source_text: Bella challenges Emmett to an arm-wrestling match with a wager that he stop teasing her about her private life.

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc3.description: I learned that Bella resisted Emmett's enormous force and then overpowered him, causing a crack in the boulder and sending fragments flying.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc3.source_text: Emmett exerts enormous force, but Bella resists and then overpowers him, causing a crack in the boulder and sending fragments flying.

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc3.description: I noticed that Bella's confidence in her physical strength increased after she overpowered Emmett and broke the rock.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc3.source_text: Bella gleefully tests her strength further by crushing and splitting the stone with her hands.

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc3.description: I observed that Bella's dynamic with Emmett is competitive and teasing, as shown by the wager and his vow of a rematch.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc3.source_text: Emmett vows a rematch; he punches the rock in frustration, shattering parts of it, while Bella gleefully tests her strength further by crushing and splitting the stone with her hands.

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc4.description: I saw Bella continue to play with a rock and revel in her newfound capabilities.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc4.source_text: I quoted: As Bella continues to play with the rock and revel in her newfound capabilities

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc4.description: I noticed Bella's skin take on a startling crystalline quality in the sunlight.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc4.source_text: I quoted: the sun breaks through the clouds in a dramatic sunset, illuminating everyone — and in particular the startling crystalline quality of Bella’s skin and the dazzling effect on Edward

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc4.description: I felt Bella recognize that she belongs and that she shines in her new existence after a life of feeling ordinary.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc4.source_text: I quoted: Bella reflects internally on the rare feeling of being naturally gifted; after a life of feeling ordinary, she now recognizes that she belongs and that she shines in this new existence

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc4.description: I noticed the family's astonishment as a response that reinforces Bella's changed status among them.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc4.source_text: I quoted: The family watches in astonishment as the child demonstrates her own strength by denting a rock and clapping with delight

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc1.description: I learned that I had become a vampire and that I took mythology more seriously afterward.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc1.source_text: I took mythology a lot more seriously since I’d become a vampire.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc1.description: I believed that my life's thread had changed color from a modest beige to bright crimson or glistening gold as I adjusted to immortality.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc1.source_text: I was sure my thread must have changed color; I thought it had probably started out as a nice beige, something supportive and non-confrontational, something that would look good in the background. Now it felt like it must be bright crimson, or maybe glistening gold.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc1.description: I updated my view that my tapestry of family and friends was a beautiful, glowing thing that now included unexpected threads and eased tensions because of Renesmee.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc1.source_text: The tapestry of family and friends that wove together around me was a beautiful, glowing thing, full of their bright, complementary colors. The tensions between our families eased, mostly due to Renesmee. She was easy to love.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc2.description: I feel that my life is dominated by happiness now and that this happiness is the dominant pattern in my daily experience.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc2.source_text: I quote: Happiness was the main component in my life now, the dominant pattern in the tapestry.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc2.description: I found that my relationship with Jasper has become much closer than I had ever dreamed it would be.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc2.source_text: I quote: So much so that my relationship with Jasper was now much closer than I’d ever dreamed it would be.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc2.description: I remember that I was really annoyed at first about the changes in closeness with Jasper.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc2.source_text: I quote: At first I was really annoyed, though.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc3.description: I put Renesmee in her wrought-iron crib that night and I complained to Edward about Jasper hovering.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc3.source_text: “Yeesh!” I complained to Edward one night after we’d put Renesmee in her wrought-iron crib.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc3.description: I learned that Jasper gravitates toward me because he cannot resist a good emotional climate.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc3.source_text: You know how Jasper is—he can’t resist a good emotional climate. You’re so happy all the time, love, he gravitates toward you without thinking.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc3.description: I felt euphoric the vast majority of the time as I adored my daughter and needed Edward constantly.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc3.source_text: And I was euphoric the vast majority of the time. The days were not long enough for me to get my fill of adoring my daughter; the nights did not have enough hours to satisfy my need for Edward.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc3.description: I imagined that beneath our joy there was a backside woven in bleak grays of doubt and fear.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc3.source_text: If you turned the fabric of our lives over, I imagined the design on the backside would be woven in the bleak grays of doubt and fear.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc5.description: I learned that Carlisle calculated Renesmee's body growth was gradually slowing while her mind continued to race ahead and that she could be an adult in no more than four years.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc5.source_text: By Carlisle’s calculations, the growth of her body was gradually slowing; her mind continued to race on ahead. Even if the rate of decrease held steady, she’d still be an adult in no more than four years.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc5.description: I learned that Renesmee would be an old woman by fifteen and that she effectively had just fifteen years of life.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc5.source_text: Four years. And an old woman by fifteen. Just fifteen years of life.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc5.description: I decided to be happy with Renesmee in the moment because her conspicuous well-being made it easy for me to leave the future for tomorrow.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc5.source_text: she was so healthy. Vital, bright, glowing, and happy. Her conspicuous well-being made it easy for me to be happy with her in the moment and leave the future for tomorrow.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc5.description: I learned that Carlisle and Edward had exhausted the research they could do from a distance and were preparing to follow old legends at their source by going back to Brazil to investigate Ticuna legends about children like Renesmee.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc5.source_text: Carlisle and Edward had exhausted the research they could do from a distance, and now we were preparing to follow old legends at their source. We were going back to Brazil, starting there. The Ticunas had legends about children like Renesmee.…

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc5.description: I realized that I was the holdup for the Brazil trip because I wanted to stay near Forks for Charlie and because I felt I had to go to the Volturi alone before anything else.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc5.source_text: The only real question left was exactly when we would go. I was the holdup. A small part of it was that I wanted to stay near Forks until after the holidays, for Charlie’s sake. But more than that, there was a different journey that I knew had to come first—that was the clear priority. Also, it had to be a solo trip. I had to go see the Volturi, and I had to do it absolutely alone.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc6.description: I learned that Alice had sent a wedding announcement to the Volturi leaders to delay their actions after seeing a vision.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc6.source_text: Until the day that Aro’s present showed up, I didn’t know that Alice had sent a wedding announcement to the Volturi leaders; we'd been far away on Esme’s island when she’d seen a vision of Volturi soldiers—Jane and Alec, the devastatingly powerful twins, among them.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc6.description: I learned that Aro sent an ornate present and a note that explicitly expressed his wish to see the new Mrs. Cullen in person.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc6.source_text: I so look forward to seeing the new Mrs. Cullen in person.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc6.description: I learned that Caius was planning to send a hunting party to see if I was still human, in defiance of their edict.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc6.source_text: Caius was planning to send a hunting party to see if I was still human, against their edict (because I knew about the secret vampire world, I either must join it or be silenced… permanently).

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc6.description: I resolved that I must go alone to keep the Volturi from learning about Renesmee and to protect our life in Forks.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc6.source_text: There was only one way to keep our life here safe.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc6.description: I saw Aro as a collector whose most prized treasures are living pieces, which made me determined to deny him access to Renesmee.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc6.source_text: Even in the short time I’d known Aro, I’d been able to see that he was a collector—and his most prized treasures were his living pieces.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc6.description: I learned that I was the only one whose thoughts Aro could not hear, which made me the only person who could safely go alone to meet the Volturi.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc6.source_text: And I was the only one whose thoughts he could not hear.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc6.description: I learned that Carlisle would accompany me and that his being only a few hours away would make both Edward and me feel more relaxed.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc6.source_text: Carlisle was coming instead. It made both Edward and me a little more relaxed, knowing that Carlisle would be only a few hours away from me.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc7.description: I learned we bought the tickets for Italy the day after Renesmee turned three months.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc7.source_text: We bought the tickets for Italy the day after Renesmee turned three months.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc7.description: I decided to keep the trip short and not tell Charlie, reflecting an increased secrecy about travel plans.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc7.source_text: I planned for it to be a very short trip, so I hadn’t told Charlie about it.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc7.description: I noticed Jacob knew about the trip and took Edward’s view on things, which altered my perception of Jacob’s alignment.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc7.source_text: Jacob knew, and he took Edward’s view on things.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc7.description: I learned that the three of us, Jacob, Renesmee, and I, were hunting together.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc7.source_text: The three of us, Jacob, Renesmee, and I, were hunting together.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.description: I watched Renesmee open her hands to show a perfectly formed eight-pointed ice star in her palm before it melted.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: She turned to us with her shocking smile—truly, it wasn’t something you could get used to—and opened her hands to show us the perfectly formed eight-pointed ice star in her palm before it melted.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.description: I noticed Renesmee still preferred not to speak aloud and used gestures when she had something to say.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: She did this when she had something to say. She still preferred not to speak aloud.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.description: I observed that Jacob and Renesmee had their move perfectly synchronized when she leaped into his arms.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: She bounded back to Jacob; he held his arms out at exactly the moment she leaped into them. They had the move perfectly synchronized.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.description: I learned that Edward was with Carlisle planning the trip to Rio and was talking behind Jacob's back.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: But Edward was with Carlisle today, planning the trip to Rio, talking behind Jacob’s back.…

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.description: I decided that I would take Jacob's side when I returned and I believed he should come with us.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: When I returned, I would take Jacob’s side. He should come with us.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.description: I saw the fluttering snow thinning above me and I learned from Alice that it wouldn’t stick for many weeks.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: The fluttering snow was thinning above me, almost gone. Alice had seen that it wouldn’t stick for many weeks.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.description: I scanned the distant cliff and I saw a glint that revealed a vampire with marble-white skin, pale blond hair, and dark golden eyes.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.source_text:
As my eyes flitted across the edge of a distant cliff, standing out starkly blue-gray against the green-black forest, a glint of silver—or was it gold?—gripped my attention.

My gaze zeroed in on the color that shouldn’t have been there, so far away in the haze that an eagle wouldn’t have been able to make it out. I stared.

She stared back.

That she was a vampire was obvious. Her skin was marble white, the texture a million times smoother than human skin. Even under the clouds, she glistened ever so slightly.

Her hair was pale, pale blond, almost silver. This was the gleam that had caught my eye.

She was a stranger to me. I was absolutely certain I’d never seen her before, even as a human. None of the faces in my muddy memory were the same as this one. But I knew her at once from her dark golden eyes.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.description: I recognized the vampire on the cliff as Irina when I realized who she was.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: Irina had decided to come after all.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.description: I viewed Jacob as more of a child than Renesmee sometimes because of his playful teasing and behavior.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: Jacob was more a child than Renessee sometimes.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.description: I felt that Jacob had as big a stake in the coming events as any of us and I believed his entire life was at stake just like mine.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: He had as big a stake in this as any of us—his entire life was at stake, just like mine.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc9.description: I saw Irina recognize me and become hostile when her lip twisted and her face turned suddenly hostile.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc9.source_text: For one moment I stared at her, and she stared back. I wondered if she would guess immediately who I was as well. I half-raised my hand, about to wave, but her lip twisted the tiniest bit, making her face suddenly hostile.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc9.description: I heard Renesmee's cry and Jacob's echoing howl and I saw Irina jerk reflexively to the sound, indicating Irina noticed Jacob.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc9.source_text: I heard Renesmee’s cry of victory from the forest, heard Jacob’s echoing howl, and saw Irina’s face jerk reflexively to the sound when it echoed to her a few seconds later.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc9.description: I felt bad and worried that Irina might seek vengeance because vampires' vengeance is hard to suppress.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc9.source_text: Vengeance was a common obsession for vampires, one that was not easy to suppress.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc9.description: I sprinted into the forest after Renesmee and Jacob to keep them in my sight and to try to assess Irina's mood and direction.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc9.source_text: I sprinted into the forest after Renesmee and Jacob, unwilling to have them out of my sight.

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc1.description: I learned that Irina disappeared into the sound and could not be tracked along the eastern shore.
tw-book4-chapter28_Sc1.source_text: Carlisle and Edward had not been able to catch up with Irina before her trail disappeared into the sound.

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc1.description: I blamed myself for Irina's disappearance because I believed my camaraderie with Jacob had angered her.
tw-book4-chapter28_Sc1.source_text: It was all my fault. She had come, as Alice had seen, to make peace with the Cullens, only to be angered by my camaraderie with Jacob.

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc1.description: I learned that we would go to Italy soon and then travel to South America with Jacob included in the plans.
tw-book4-chapter28_Sc1.source_text: I would leave for Italy in just a few days. When I got back, we’d all be off to South America. Now that it was accepted that Jacob would come with us, he figured prominently in the plans—

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: I learned that the Volturi are coming and that their full council and even the wives will attend.
tw-book4-chapter28_Sc2.source_text: "They’re all coming—Aro, Caius, Marcus, every member of the guard, even the wives."

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: I learned that Irina decided to go to the Volturi and that her decision will prompt the Volturi's action.
tw-book4-chapter28_Sc2.source_text: "She decided to go to them," Alice said. "Irina decided to go to the Volturi. And then they will decide.…"

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: I became convinced that Renesmee is the reason the Volturi will come.
tw-book4-chapter28_Sc2.source_text: Renesmee was the reason why, I was sure.

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: I felt cold for the first time since my rebirth as a vampire when I realized the threat.
tw-book4-chapter28_Sc2.source_text: For the first time since I’d been reborn a vampire, I felt cold.

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: I learned that the Volturi's arrival is predicted to be in little more than a month with snow on the forest and town.
tw-book4-chapter28_Sc2.source_text: "There’s snow on the forest, snow on the town. Little more than a month."

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc3.description: I learned that Irina had seen a child and that her testimony had been shown to Aro.
tw-book4-chapter28_Sc3.source_text: "Aro's seen Irina's proof in her thoughts."

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc3.description: I became convinced that Renesmee is not like the frozen immortal children and that she is dangerous only in the Volturi's misunderstanding.
tw-book4-chapter28_Sc3.source_text: "But she's wrong... Renesmee isn't like those other children. They were frozen, but she grows so much every day."

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc3.description: I realized that our alliance with the Quileute pack now put them at risk because Irina had revealed it to the Volturi.
tw-book4-chapter28_Sc3.source_text: "Not to mention that, thanks to Irina, Aro knows about our alliance with the pack now, too."

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc4.description: I learned that the Volturi have condemned the Cullen family and that the family believes they face execution.
tw-book4-chapter28_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "All of us, Jacob," I whispered. And it was there in my voice, too—the sound of the inside of a grave. "It’s over. We’ve all been sentenced to die."

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc4.description: I realized that hope had shifted to despair as I accepted that the verdict felt final and lethal.
tw-book4-chapter28_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "All of us, Jacob," I whispered. And it was there in my voice, too—the sound of the inside of a grave. "It’s over. We’ve all been sentenced to die."

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc4.description: I noticed Jacob's immediate protective devotion toward Renesmee and felt him become a direct ally in the crisis.
tw-book4-chapter28_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "Is she okay?" he demanded, touching her forehead, tilting his head as he listened to her heart. "Don't mess with me, Bella, please!"

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc1.description: I learned that Alice never came back after leaving during the night.
I realized I no longer had the ability to smile because my face felt permanently set into a fixed mask.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc1.source_text: My face felt permanently set into the fixed mask it had worn all night.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc1.description: I became acutely aware that losing Edward would be unbearable as we stared at what neither of us could live through losing: the other.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc1.source_text: We’d stared at each other all night, staring at what neither of us could live through losing: the other.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc1.description: I learned that Sam knew everything and that the wolves were readying themselves for what was coming.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc1.source_text: Sam knew everything—the wolves were readying themselves for what was coming.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc2.description: I told Jacob to stay with Renesmee as I sprinted out the door.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc2.source_text: “Stay with Renesmee!” I all but shrieked at Jacob as I sprinted through the door.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc2.description: I noticed that I was still stronger than the rest of them and used that strength to push myself forward.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc2.source_text: I was still stronger than the rest of them, and I used that strength to push myself forward.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc2.description: I overtook Esme and Rosalie quickly while racing through the forest to catch up with Edward and Carlisle.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc2.source_text: I overtook Esme in a few bounds, and Rosalie in just a few strides more.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc2.description: I observed Alice and Jasper’s trail curling into a wide arc that went east of the house, north across the river, and back west after a few miles.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc2.source_text: Alice and Jasper’s trail was curling into a wide arc; it stretched first east of the house, but headed north on the other side of the river, and then back west again after a few miles.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc2.description: I smelled the hint of wolf in the breeze coming from the east as we neared the treaty line.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc2.source_text: I could smell the hint of wolf in the breeze blowing from the east.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc2.description: I learned that Aro knows Renesmee better than anyone, even better than Edward apparently does.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc2.source_text: “But Aro knows her better than anyone else. Better than I do.”

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc3.description: I learned that Alice and Jasper went into the ocean and did not return.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc3.source_text: They went immediately into the water and did not return.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc3.description: I realized that a page torn from one of my books was used as the note.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc3.source_text: I realized it was a page torn from one of my books.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc3.description: I felt urgent impatience and a strong need to be in motion and to have my arms around Alice to know she was safe.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc3.source_text: I didn’t want time to think about what was happening. I wanted to be in motion, to be doing something. I wanted to have my arms around Alice, to know beyond a doubt that she was safe.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc3.description: I learned that Alice and Jasper chose to leave without goodbyes and that they stated they loved us.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc3.source_text: Don’t look for us. There isn’t time to waste. Remember: Tanya, Siobhan, Amun, Alistair, all the nomads you can find. We’ll seek out Peter and Charlotte on our way. We’re so sorry that we have to leave you this way, with no goodbyes or explanations. It’s the only way for us. We love you.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc4.description: I learned that I couldn't cry in this body and that I felt numb and unreal.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc4.source_text: I didn’t know how to cry in this body; I couldn’t do anything but stare. There was no feeling yet. Everything seemed unreal, like I was dreaming again after all these months.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc4.description: I realized that the Cullens were not an indivisible unit and that I had overlooked differences in how members joined the family.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc4.source_text: I’d always thought of the Cullens as a whole, an indivisible unit. Suddenly, I remembered that it had not always been so.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc4.description: I understood that Alice had adopted the Cullens and that she and Jasper had past lives separate from the family.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc4.source_text: But in truth, Alice had adopted the Cullens. She had shown up with her unconnected past, bringing Jasper with his, and fit herself into the family that was already there.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc4.description: I felt hopeless about any chance to convince Alice to remain after she had seen a future where the Cullens were overrun.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc4.source_text: There was no hope at all. Not one ray, one flicker that might have convinced Alice she had a chance at our side.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc4.description: I learned that the Cullens planned to fight for Renesmee and intended to involve the wolves, accepting that they might all die.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc4.source_text: We would fight, they would fight, and we all would die. The wolves, too, would fight with us for Renesmee.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc5.description: I learned that there was another, fresh trail near the river.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc5.source_text: There was that other trail. It was fresh.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc5.description: I realized that the faint trail smelled like Alice alone, without Jasper.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc5.source_text: I was new to this, but it smelled exactly the same to me, just minus the scent of Jasper.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc5.description: I learned that Alice's note had somehow ended up on a page from my book, which puzzled me.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc5.source_text: After all, how had Alice’s note ended up on a page from my book?

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc5.description: I understood that I would feel real pain at any separation from Edward and could not bear being divided from him.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc5.source_text: I thought of being divided from him now and realized I would have felt the same pain, no matter how short the separation.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc5.description: I felt Edward's protectiveness when he said he couldn't let me walk away and then took my hand.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc5.source_text: I held my hand out to him, and he took it.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc6.description: I discovered that a page had been torn from my book and that the torn edge led me to the cottage.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc6.source_text: There, next to the feathered edge left by the torn page, under the words The Merchant of Venice by William Shakespeare, was a note.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc6.description: I read a note in my book that said "Destroy this" and I saw a name and an address in Seattle beneath it.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc6.source_text: Destroy this. Below that was a name and an address in Seattle.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc6.description: I became convinced that Alice's action of tearing the page was intended as a message for me rather than for Edward.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc6.source_text: But it was my book, so the message must be for me. If it were something she wanted Edward to know, wouldn’t she have pulled a page from one of his books… ?

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc6.description: I noticed Alice's scent was fresh in the cottage and I noticed a fire burning low and hot, indicating recent presence.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc6.source_text: Alice’s scent was fresh—less than a day old. A fire that I had not set burned low but hot in the fireplace.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc6.description: I felt uneasy and I preferred to investigate the torn page alone despite having Edward with me.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc6.source_text: I was glad to have Edward’s hand in mine, but I also felt as if I should be here alone.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc6.description: I interpreted Alice's odd behavior as intentionally sending a personal message to me, which changed how I viewed Alice's interventions.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc6.source_text: Tearing out the page and carrying it back to Jasper was such an odd thing for Alice to do. It felt like there was a message in her action—one I didn’t understand at all.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc7.description: I learned that someone ripped a page from my book and used it to write Alice's note.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc7.source_text: She ripped a page out of my book to write her note on.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc7.description: I learned that Alice lied to Jasper on the plane to Italy to keep him from following and facing the Volturi.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc7.source_text: When we were on the plane to Italy," I whispered—this was not a lie, except perhaps in context—"on our way to rescue you… she lied to Jasper so that he wouldn’t come after us.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc7.description: I believed that Alice prioritized Jasper's safety over others and might have been willing to die or let us die to protect him.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc7.source_text: She was willing to die herself rather than put him in danger. Willing for me to die, too. Willing for you to die.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc7.description: I realized that I am the only person in the world who can lie to Edward and that this fact connects to Alice's decision to confide in me alone.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc7.source_text: I was the only person in the world who could lie to Edward.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc8.description: I learned that Alice had given only me the name J. Jenks and that I needed to figure out who he was.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc8.source_text: I quote: "I had to figure out who this J. Jenks person was and why Alice had gone to such lengths to give his name to only me."

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc8.description: I wished I could feel the family's hope and I wanted to be alone with the computer to investigate J. Jenks.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc8.source_text: I quote: "I watched them leave, wishing I could feel whatever hope bolstered them, and wishing I could be alone with the computer for just a few seconds."

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc8.description: I noticed Carlisle kissed my forehead and Esme hugged us both and Emmett punched us both on the arm, which I took as clear family support.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc8.source_text: I quote: "Carlisle put his hand on Edward’s shoulder for a second and then kissed my forehead. Esme hugged us both, and Emmett punched us both on the arm."

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc9.description: I observed that Renesmee already understood the situation and was anxious but not frightened.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc9.source_text: I quote: "Renesmee already understood only too clearly what was going on."

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc9.description: I noted that I searched the cottage computer and discovered a Jason Jenks lawyer entry with an address that did not match and seemed nonexistent.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc9.source_text: I quote: "Not a J. Jenks, but there was a Jason Jenks. A lawyer. Jason Jenks had a fancy website for his firm, but the address on the homepage was wrong. In Seattle, but in a different zip code. I noted the phone number and then stroked the keyboard in rhythm. This time I searched the address, but nothing at all came up, as if the address didn’t exist."

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc9.description: I held Renesmee and felt her cling and smell strongly of werewolf as I accepted my role as her protector in that moment.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc9.source_text: I quote: "Renesmee reached for me, and I held my arms open. She launched herself into them, smelling strongly of werewolf, and nestled her head against my neck."

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc9.description: I felt that shielding Renesmee was more important than answering her questions when tensions were high.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc9.source_text: I quote: "Wasn’t shielding her more important than answering her questions?"

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc10.description: I resolved that saving my daughter was the only thing that mattered and that I would bear anything else for her survival.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc10.source_text: She was the one thing I simply had to save.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc10.description: I believed that Alice would have left a way to save Renesmee and that Alice would know what to do.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc10.source_text: I was more positive than ever that this was what Alice would give me. She would know. She would have left me a way.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc10.description: I noticed the mother-daughter bond reverse when Renesmee mirrored and soothed my grief, changing how I related to her.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc10.source_text: I’d never thought to see the mother-daughter bond reversed between us, the way it had always been for Renée and me.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc10.description: I realized that Renesmee was only worrying and that Jake had kept the worst from her about our fate.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc10.source_text: She was only worrying, though. Jake had kept the worst from her as far as I could tell.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc10.description: I felt my priority shift so that my daughter's life outranked fear for my own and for Edward's.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc10.source_text: As much as I feared for my life, for Edward’s, for the rest of my family’s, it was not the same as the gut-wrenching terror I felt for my daughter.

tw-book4-chapter29_Sc10.description: I saw that Renesmee could show thoughts by flipping through faces and that she longed for Alice.
tw-book4-chapter29_Sc10.source_text: Renesmee’s hand touched my cheek lightly. She showed me my own face, Edward’s, Jacob’s, Rosalie’s, Esme’s, Carlisle’s, Alice’s, Jasper’s, flipping through all our family’s faces faster and faster.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc1.description: I woke from a nightmare and lay shivering and gasping in my warm bed for several minutes while trying to break free of the dream.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: I lay shivering and gasping in my warm bed for several minutes, trying to break free of the dream.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc1.description: I saw the sky outside my window turn gray and then pale pink while I waited for my heart to slow.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: The sky outside my window turned gray and then pale pink while I waited for my heart to slow.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc1.description: I became annoyed with myself after the dream, especially given the timing before my wedding.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: When I was fully back to the reality of my messy, familiar room, I was a little annoyed with myself.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc1.description: I blamed my obsession with disturbing stories in the middle of the night for provoking the nightmare.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: That’s what I got for obsessing over disturbing stories in the middle of the night.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc1.description: I felt unsettled about having such a dream the night before my wedding, which made me more anxious about the upcoming event.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc1.source_text: What a dream to have the night before my wedding!

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc2.description: I woke early, cleaned the house, and made pancakes for Charlie to be helpful after a nightmare.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: Eager to shake off the nightmare, I got dressed and headed down to the kitchen long before I needed to. First I cleaned the already tidy rooms, and then when Charlie was up I made him pancakes.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc2.description: I felt too keyed up to eat breakfast and experienced physical restlessness during the morning.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: I was much too keyed up to have any interest in eating breakfast myself—I sat bouncing in my seat while he ate.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc2.description: I reminded Charlie about picking up Mr. Weber at three o'clock and also reminded him to be dressed and presentable.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: "You’re picking up Mr. Weber at three o’clock," I reminded him. "That’s not your only job. You also have to be dressed and presentable."

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc2.description: I took on a caretaker and managerial role for Charlie's wedding-day responsibilities, reinforcing a parental dynamic between us.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc2.source_text: First I cleaned the already tidy rooms, and then when Charlie was up I made him pancakes. "You’re picking up Mr. Weber at three o’clock," I reminded him.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc3.description: I observed Alice arriving with her hair smoothed into pin curls and a businesslike expression.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: Alice’s short black hair was not in its usual spiky do—it was smoothed into sleek pin curls around her pixie face, which wore a contrastingly businesslike expression.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc3.description: I rode with Alice in her Porsche.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: Alice appraised me as I got into her Porsche.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc3.description: My relationship with Alice is that she is my best girlfriend and soon-to-be sister.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: get the door for my best girlfriend and soon-to-be sister.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc3.description: I noticed that three miles of driveway were wrapped in hundreds of thousands of twinkle lights and white satin bows.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: Three miles of drive were once again wrapped in hundreds of thousands of twinkle lights. This time, she’d added white satin bows.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc3.description: I noticed Emmett's big Jeep was gone from the garage.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: Emmett’s big Jeep was still gone.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc3.description: I changed my feeling about the mystery of our destination and I wasn't too stressed about it despite finding the unknown strange.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: I wasn't too stressed about the mystery, but it was strange not knowing where I would be sleeping tomorrow night.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc3.description: I worried that I might fall asleep during the ceremony and that Edward might make his escape.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: I think the bigger problem is that I might fall asleep during the ceremony and not be able to say 'I do' at the right part, and then Edward will make his escape.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc3.description: I was told that I would not be allowed to see the interior decorations until it was time to come down the stairs.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc3.source_text: Enjoy this, because you don’t get to see the inside decorations until it’s time.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc4.description: I learned the specific fragrances Alice used were orange blossoms, lilac, freesia, and roses.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc4.source_text:
“It smells wonderful!” I assured her—almost intoxicating, but not at all overwhelming, the balance of the different fragrances was subtle and flawless. “Orange blossoms… lilac… and something else—am I right?”

“Very good, Bella. You only missed the freesia and the roses.”

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc4.description: I learned that I was the first human to be in their house and that Alice was concerned about making the right impression.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc4.source_text: “Is it too much?” Alice’s voice was abruptly worried. “You’re the first human in here; I hope I got it right.”

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc4.description: I felt convinced that I would look plain next to him no matter what Alice did.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc4.source_text: “Is this really necessary? I’m going to look plain next to him no matter what.”

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc4.description: I came to trust Alice's confidence and skill because she assured me no one would call me plain after her work.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc4.source_text: “No one will dare to call you plain when I’m through with you.”

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc4.description: I experienced Alice treating me like a salon client as she masked, buffed, and polished every surface of my body while I drifted in and out of sleep.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc4.source_text: I did drift in and out a little bit while she masked, buffed, and polished every surface of my body.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc4.description: I used a teasing comment about Alice sucking blood to acknowledge the vampires' intimidating reputation and to deflect my self-consciousness.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc4.source_text: “Only because they’re afraid you’ll suck their blood,” I muttered.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc5.description: I felt so overwhelmed and nearly cried because Rosalie was so beautiful.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: She was so beautiful it made me want to cry.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc5.description: I questioned the point of dressing up with Rosalie around because her presence made me feel overshadowed.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: What was even the point of dressing up with Rosalie around?

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc5.description: I learned that Edward had returned home when Rosalie announced that they were back.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: They’re back," Rosalie said, and immediately my childish fit of despair passed. Edward was home.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc5.description: I learned that Esme had people finishing things up out back as part of the preparations.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: Esme's got them finishing things up out back.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc5.description: I learned that Alice began braiding my hair, that the veil was to go underneath, and that Rosalie finished shaping my hair before being sent to retrieve my dress and locate Jasper.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: You can start braiding. I want it intricate. The veil goes here, underneath." ... "Once Rosalie received Alice’s commendation on my hair, she was sent off to retrieve my dress and then to locate Jasper, who had been dispatched to pick up my mother and her husband, Phil, from their hotel.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc6.description: I learned that Alice helped me into my wedding dress and did my hair and makeup.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc6.source_text: I quote: "Alice made me stand so that she could ease the dress over my hair and makeup."

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc6.description: I learned that my knees shook badly and that the satin of the dress quivered as Alice fastened the pearl buttons up my back.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc6.source_text: I quote: "My knees shook so badly as she fastened the long line of pearl buttons up my back that the satin quivered in little wavelets down to the floor."

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc6.description: I became convinced that seeing myself in the wedding dress could trigger a full-scale panic attack.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc6.source_text: I quote: "I was afraid to look in the mirror—afraid the image of myself in the wedding dress would send me over the edge into a full-scale panic attack."

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc6.description: I learned that I practiced controlled breathing by counting each movement of my lungs to steady myself.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc6.source_text: I quote: "I concentrated on my breathing, counting each movement of my lungs, and stared at the patterns that the bathroom light made on the shiny fabric of my skirt."

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc6.description: I noticed that Alice was focused on calming and helping me, indicating a supportive relationship during this stressful moment.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc6.source_text: I quote: "Deep breaths, Bella," Alice said. "And try to lower your heart rate. You’re going to sweat off your new face."

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc8.description: I learned that the piano music (Pachelbel’s Canon) triggered my hyperventilation.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: Rosalie—the best musician in the family next to Edward—began playing the piano downstairs. Pachelbel’s Canon. I began hyperventilating.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc8.description: I noticed my father Charlie became nervous and protective, checking if I would make it and holding my hand tightly.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: “Easy, Bells,” Charlie said. He turned to Alice nervously. “She looks a little sick. Do you think she’s going to make it?”
