tw-book4-chapter3_Sc8.description: I realized that having Alice as my only bridesmaid would make me look more uncoordinated and that I would feel awkward following her.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: I should have realized that having Alice as my only bridesmaid was a mistake. I would look that much more uncoordinated coming behind her.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc9.description: I saw the aisle decorated with abundant white blossoms and long lines of white gossamer ribbons.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc9.source_text: the profusion of white blossoms that hung in garlands from everything in the room that wasn’t alive, dripping with long lines of white gossamer ribbons.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc9.description: I noticed the man I loved standing before an arch overflowing with flowers and gossamer.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc9.source_text: I searched across the rows of satin-draped chairs—blushing more deeply as I took in the crowd of faces all focused on me—until I found him at last, standing before an arch overflowing with more flowers, more gossamer.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc9.description: I felt at home the moment I touched the cool miracle of his skin.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc9.source_text: I touched the cool miracle of his skin, and I was home.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc9.description: I recognized Charlie took my hand and, in a symbol as old as the world, placed it in Edward's hand.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc9.source_text: Charlie took my hand and, in a symbol as old as the world, placed it in Edward’s.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc9.description: I felt overwhelmed by Edward's face which filled my vision and by the breathtaking, exultant smile he gave me.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc9.source_text: All I really saw was Edward’s face; it filled my vision and overwhelmed my mind. And then, as he met my awed gaze, he broke into a breathtaking smile of exultation.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc10.description: I learned the minister traded the line "till death do us part" for "as long as we both shall live."
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc10.source_text: He obligingly traded the line “till death do us part” for the more appropriate “as long as we both shall live.”

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc10.description: I felt my world settle into its proper position and I saw that I had been silly to fear the wedding.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc10.source_text: In that moment, as the minister said his part, my world, which had been upside down for so long now, seemed to settle into its proper position. I saw just how silly I’d been for fearing this—

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc10.description: I cried and I managed to choke out my vow as a nearly unintelligible whisper of 'I do.'
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc10.source_text: I didn’t realize I was crying until it was time to say the binding words. "I do," I managed to choke out in a nearly unintelligible whisper, blinking my eyes clear so I could see his face.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc10.description: I knew I was winning too and I understood that nothing else mattered but that I could stay with him.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc10.source_text: I looked into Edward’s shining, triumphant eyes and knew that I was winning, too. Because nothing else mattered but that I could stay with him.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc10.description: I felt him kiss me tenderly and I forgot the crowd, remembering only that he loved me, wanted me, and that I was his.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc10.source_text: He kissed me tenderly, adoringly; I forgot the crowd, the place, the time, the reason… only remembering that he loved me, that he wanted me, that I was his.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc11.description: I recognized the difference between the soft, warm hugs of my human friends and the gentle, cool embraces of my new family.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc11.source_text: I did recognize the difference between the soft, warm hugs of my human friends and the gentle, cool embraces of my new family.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc11.description: I felt my mother's arms were the first to find me and I saw her tear-streaked face when I finally tore my eyes unwillingly from Edward.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc11.source_text: My mother’s arms were the first to find me, her tear-streaked face the first thing I saw when I finally tore my eyes unwillingly from Edward.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc11.description: I centered my attention on Edward's hand clutched tightly in my own, reinforcing the closeness between us at the reception.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc11.source_text: my attention centered on Edward’s hand clutched tightly in my own.

tw-book4-chapter3_Sc11.description: I was handed through the crowd and passed from embrace to embrace while only being vaguely aware of who held me.
tw-book4-chapter3_Sc11.source_text: And then I was handed through the crowd, passed from embrace to embrace, only vaguely aware of who held me, my attention centered on Edward’s hand clutched tightly in my own.

tw-book4-chapter30_Sc1.description: I learned I needed to find time alone to hunt down J. Jenks and wondered why Alice wanted me to know about him.
tw-book4-chapter30_Sc1.source_text: How was I going to find time alone to hunt down J. Jenks, and why did Alice want me to know about him?

tw-book4-chapter30_Sc1.description: I realized Alice's clue might have nothing to do with Renesmee and worried how to save my daughter if that were true.
tw-book4-chapter30_Sc1.source_text: If Alice’s clue had nothing to do with Renesmee, what could I do to save my daughter?

tw-book4-chapter30_Sc1.description: I became convinced I could be too untrained to pose any danger to the Volturi after only a month of training.
tw-book4-chapter30_Sc1.source_text: I didn’t know how to fight. How was I going to learn in just a month? Was there any chance at all that I could be taught fast enough that I might be a danger to any one member of the Volturi? Or was I doomed to be totally useless? Just another easily dispatched newborn?

tw-book4-chapter30_Sc1.description: I felt my relationship with Edward shift toward urgent, intense physical passion that made my questions seem unimportant for the night.
tw-book4-chapter30_Sc1.source_text: He spun and was across the room in what seemed like no time at all, not even the smallest part of a second. I only had time to register the ferocious expression on his face before his lips were crushing against mine and his arms were locked around me like steel girders. I didn’t think of my questions again for the rest of that night.

tw-book4-chapter30_Sc1.description: I decided that taking Renesmee home to our cottage at bedtime would provide normality for her.
tw-book4-chapter30_Sc1.source_text: Wanting some normality for Renesmee, I’d insisted on taking her home to our cottage at bedtime.

tw-book4-chapter30_Sc2.description: I asked Edward to teach me how to fight so that I might be able to help in a confrontation with the Volturi.
tw-book4-chapter30_Sc2.source_text: I read: "Edward, will you teach me how to fight?" I asked him, tensed for his reaction, as he held the door for me.

tw-book4-chapter30_Sc2.description: I planned to use my immunity to Alec's power and my physical attributes to distract or attack Alec and possibly Jane in order to even the odds.
tw-book4-chapter30_Sc2.source_text: I read: "Well, he probably can’t do that to me, can he? If what he does is like Aro and Jane and you. Maybe… if he’s never really had to defend himself… and I learned a few tricks—"

tw-book4-chapter30_Sc2.description: I decided to keep my plans to myself instead of sharing my willingness to sacrifice with Edward.
tw-book4-chapter30_Sc2.source_text: I read: "I nodded. I would keep my plans to myself, then."

tw-book4-chapter30_Sc2.description: I recognized that I might be "a tiny bit special" because of my supernaturally thick skull and I wondered if that could be useful.
tw-book4-chapter30_Sc2.source_text: I read: "I was a tiny bit special, in my own way—if a having a supernaturally thick skull could really be considered special."

tw-book4-chapter30_Sc2.description: I held Renesmee close and I felt overwhelmed by her scent and the urgency of time to prepare.
tw-book4-chapter30_Sc2.source_text: I read: "I pulled Renesmee, still sleeping, from her bed and held her close so that her curls were pressed against my face; her sweet scent, so close, overpowered every other smell."

tw-book4-chapter30_Sc3.description: I learned that Bella is Renesmee's biological mother who conceived, carried, and gave birth while still human and that the birth nearly killed her.
tw-book4-chapter30_Sc3.source_text: Bella is her biological mother. She conceived, carried, and gave birth to Renesmee while she was still human. It nearly killed her.

tw-book4-chapter30_Sc3.description: I realized that I had thought I was prepared for their reaction but I was unready for their shock and hostility.
tw-book4-chapter30_Sc3.source_text: I thought I’d prepared myself for their reaction. For accusations, for shouting, for the motionlessness of deep stress.

tw-book4-chapter30_Sc3.description: I felt Edward acting protectively toward me and Renesmee when he put his arm around us and defended our explanation.
tw-book4-chapter30_Sc3.source_text: Edward put his arm around Renesmee and me.

tw-book4-chapter30_Sc4.description: I learned that Bella had Renesmee with her when Irina saw them in the mountains.
tw-book4-chapter30_Sc4.source_text: “When Bella saw Irina that day in the mountains,” Edward explained, “she had Renesmee with her.”

tw-book4-chapter30_Sc4.description: I realized my hope vanished when I remembered that Alice had left us.
tw-book4-chapter30_Sc4.source_text: And then I remembered that Alice had left us, and my hope vanished as quickly as it had appeared.

tw-book4-chapter30_Sc4.description: I heard Renesmee declare that she never hurt certain humans and that she loves humans and wolf-people like my Jacob.
tw-book4-chapter30_Sc4.source_text: “I never hurt Grandpa or Sue or Billy. I love humans. And wolf-people like my Jacob.”

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: I learned that Eleazar perceived me as a shield and believed I was blocking his ability to read or sense him.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc1.source_text: I read "A shield, I think. She’s blocking me now, so I can’t be sure."

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: I felt confused about being described as a shield and I reconsidered my understanding of my own defensive ability in response to Eleazar's comment.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc1.source_text: I read "I stared at Eleazar, my brows furrowing in confusion. Shield? What did he mean about my blocking him? I was standing right here beside him, not defensive in any way."

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc1.description: I noticed Edward immediately defended me by confronting Eleazar and calling me his wife, which reinforced our protective partnership in front of the council.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc1.source_text: I read "What did you just call my wife?"

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc2.description: I learned that Bella possesses a defensive mental talent categorized as a shield that protects some aspect of her being.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc2.source_text: Talents that are purely defensive, that protect some aspect of the bearer, are always called shields.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward has never been able to hear Bella's thoughts, even when she was human, indicating the shield's longstanding strength.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc2.source_text: No, Edward murmured. But I’ve never been able to do that. Even when she was human.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc2.description: I learned that Bella's shield is selective and does not prevent Jasper from affecting her mood or Alice from seeing her future.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc2.source_text: It only works with certain things. My head is sort of… private. But it doesn’t stop Jasper from being able to mess with my mood or Alice from seeing my future.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc2.description: I learned that powerful adversaries such as Jane, and abilities like Demetri's tracking and Alec's power, cannot affect Bella through her shield.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc2.source_text: Jane tried to hurt me, but she couldn’t. Edward thinks Demetri can’t find me, and that Alec can’t bother me, either.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc2.description: I learned that Eleazar considers Bella's talent rare and still raw because she is only a few months old as a vampire.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc2.source_text: I can’t feel a way through her shield to get a sense of it at all. Yet she must be raw still—she’s only a few months old.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc3.description: I learned that Renata is Aro's personal bodyguard and that Eleazar described her as a very practical and very strong shield.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc3.source_text: "Renata is Aro’s personal bodyguard," Eleazar told me. "A very practical kind of shield, and a very strong one."

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc3.description: I learned that Renata's shield repels and diverts attackers by affecting minds so they change direction and retain a confused memory about their original intent.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc3.source_text: "If someone approaches her—or Aro, as she is always close beside him in a hostile situation—they find themselves… diverted. There’s a force around her that repels, though it’s almost unnoticeable. You simply find yourself going a different direction than you planned, with a confused memory as to why you wanted to go that other way in the first place."

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc3.description: I learned that Renata can project her shield several meters out from herself and that she protects Caius and Marcus when needed while prioritizing Aro.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc3.source_text: She can project her shield several meters out from herself. She also protects Caius and Marcus, too, when they have a need, but Aro is her priority.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc3.description: I learned that Eleazar emphasized that Renata's and most other gifts operate inside the mind rather than through physical means.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc3.source_text: "What she does isn’t actually physical, though. Like the vast majority of our gifts, it takes place inside the mind."

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc3.description: I became uncertain whether my self-control is an innate vampiric gift or merely the product of training and preparation after remembering Edward's initial explanation and Carlisle's suggestion.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc3.source_text: I felt disoriented. Didn’t I already know my gift? I had my super-self-control that had allowed me to skip right over the horrifying newborn year. Vampires only had one extra ability at most, right? Or had Edward been correct in the beginning? Before Carlisle had suggested that my self-control could be something beyond the natural, Edward had thought my restraint was just a product of good preparation—focus and attitude, he’d declared.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc3.description: I learned that Kate has been working on projecting offensively and that her best result over centuries is to run a current over her skin.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc3.source_text: "Can you project?" Kate asked interestedly. "Project?" I asked. "Push it out from yourself," Kate explained. "I don’t know. I’ve never tried. I didn’t know I should do that." "Oh, you might not be able to," Kate said quickly. "Heavens knows I’ve been working on it for centuries and the best I can do is run a current over my skin."

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc3.description: I flinched away from Kate automatically and I updated my view of her as someone who can be threatening because Edward called her skill offensive.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc3.source_text: "Kate’s got an offensive skill," Edward said. "Sort of like Jane." I flinched away from Kate automatically, and she laughed.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc4.description: I learned that projection can be radiated over the body and used as a defense.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc4.source_text: But after a lot of practice, I can radiate the current all over my body. It’s a good defense.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc4.description: I learned that shielding someone besides yourself might be possible and could include another person in my strange, quirky silent head.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc4.source_text: Shield someone besides yourself, she’d said. As if there were some way for me to include another person in my strange, quirky silent head.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc4.description: I came to believe that I might be able to protect Edward and Renesmee if I learned projection.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc4.source_text: What if I could stop that from happening ever again? What if I could protect him? Protect Renesmee? What if there was even the faintest glimmer of a possibility that I could shield them, too?

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc4.description: I felt an urgent, desperate desire to learn projecting because I had never wanted anything so badly as to protect what I loved.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc4.source_text: It felt like I had never wanted anything so badly before this: to be able to protect what I loved.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc4.description: I realized that my shield prevented me from feeling Kate’s projected current when Kate tested me.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc4.source_text: “You didn’t feel anything just now?” “No, I didn’t feel anything. Were you doing your electric current thing?”

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc5.description: I noticed a silent exchange between Edward and Eleazar escalate into a spoken conversation while everyone watched them closely.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc5.source_text:
"Can you think of even one exception, though?" Edward asked.
I looked over to make sense of his comment and realized that everyone else was already staring at the two men. They were leaning toward each other intently, Edward’s expression tight with suspicion, Eleazar’s unhappy and reluctant.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc5.description: I felt the atmosphere change from casual to tense when Eleazar reacted angrily and began pacing, which made me sense that something serious had been uncovered.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc5.source_text:
"I don’t want to think of them that way," Eleazar said through his teeth. I was surprised at the sudden change in the atmosphere.
"If you’re right—," Eleazar began again.
... Then he shrugged out from under her hand and began his pacing again, faster even than before.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc5.description: I reconsidered my view of Eleazar as merely another elder after hearing him agonize about lives harmed and the possible consequences of his actions.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc5.source_text:
"If I’m right… I can’t even grasp what that would mean. It would change everything about the world we’ve created. It would change the meaning of my life. What I have been a part of."
"Would that even matter? What have I done? How many lives . . ."

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc6.description: I learned that Aro would orchestrate punitive expeditions and then pardon a single repentant vampire who possessed a gift he admired, recruiting that vampire into the guard.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc6.source_text: Aro does not often personally attend a punishing expedition. But in the past, when Aro wanted something in particular, it was never long before evidence turned up proving that this coven or that coven had committed some unpardonable crime. The ancients would decide to go along to watch the guard administer justice. And then, once the coven was all but destroyed, Aro would grant a pardon to one member whose thoughts, he would claim, were particularly repentant. Always, it would turn out that this vampire had the gift Aro had admired. Always, this person was given a place with the guard. The gifted vampire was won over quickly, always so grateful for the honor. There were no exceptions.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc6.description: I realized why the guard obeyed the Volturi masters so gladly and with almost lover-like devotion.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc6.source_text: It had not made sense to me before how the guard obeyed their masters so gladly, with almost lover-like devotion.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc6.description: I now view Aro and the Volturi as manipulative actors who use engineered punishment and selective mercy to recruit loyalty and maintain power.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc6.source_text: So Chelsea would break the ties that bound them together. It seemed a great kindness to me, evidence of Aro’s mercy. I did suspect that Chelsea kept our own band more tightly knit, but that, too, was a good thing. It made us more effective. It helped us coexist more easily.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc7.description: I learned that Aro desires Alice above all else.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc7.source_text: From what I saw of his thoughts last spring, Aro’s never wanted anything more than he wants Alice.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc7.description: I learned that Alice left to prevent Aro from acquiring her gift.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc7.source_text: To keep Aro from gaining the thing he wants most of all. To keep her power out of his hands.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc7.description: I became convinced that Aro might want me as well.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc7.source_text: He wants you, too, I whispered.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc7.description: I felt reassured by Edward's confidence that Aro would have difficulty forcing him to obey.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc7.source_text: Not nearly as much. I can’t really give him anything more than he already has. And of course that’s dependent on his finding a way to force me to do his will. He knows me, and he knows how unlikely that is.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc8.description: I learned that Aro likely knows my weaknesses and could coerce me by threatening Edward.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc8.source_text: "He also knows your weaknesses," Eleazar pointed out. "If Aro wanted me to do something—anything—all he had to do was threaten Edward and I would comply."

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc8.description: I began to question whether death was the lesser concern and whether capture was the greater threat.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc8.source_text: Was death the lesser concern? Was it really capture we should fear?

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc8.description: I recognized that Edward's safety could force my compliance and that my safety could force his, creating mutual leverage.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc8.source_text: "If Aro wanted me to do something—anything—all he had to do was threaten Edward and I would comply. And vice versa."

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc9.description: I heard the sound of tires turning off the highway pavement onto the Cullens’ dirt drive.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc9.source_text: Then I heard the sound of tires turning off the highway pavement onto the Cullens’ dirt drive.

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc9.description: I thought it might be Charlie and I suggested the Denalis could hang out upstairs until the situation was clearer.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc9.source_text: “Oh crap, Charlie,” I muttered. “Maybe the Denalis could hang out upstairs until—”

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc9.description: I learned from Edward that the arriving cars were not my father's and that Alice had sent Peter and Charlotte as scouts.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc9.source_text: “No,” Edward said in a distant voice. His eyes were far away, staring blankly at the door. “It’s not your father.” His gaze focused on me. “Alice sent Peter and Charlotte, after all. Time to get ready for the next round.”

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc9.description: I changed my belief that the cars belonged to my father when Edward told me Alice had sent scouts.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc9.source_text: “No,” Edward said in a distant voice. His eyes were far away, staring blankly at the door. “It’s not your father.” His gaze focused on me. “Alice sent Peter and Charlotte, after all. Time to get ready for the next round.”

tw-book4-chapter31_Sc9.description: I noticed Edward's gaze focus on me and his directive to prepare made me see him as the one organizing the family's response.
tw-book4-chapter31_Sc9.source_text: His gaze focused on me. “Alice sent Peter and Charlotte, after all. Time to get ready for the next round.”

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc1.description: I learned that the Cullens' house was overcrowded with visiting vampires who did not sleep.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc1.source_text: I saw the Cullens' enormous house more crowded with guests than anyone would assume could possibly be comfortable.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc1.description: I learned that mealtimes were dicey and that the visitors cooperated by hunting out of state and giving Forks and La Push a wide berth.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc1.source_text: I noticed that mealtimes were dicey, though our company cooperated as best they could and they gave Forks and La Push a wide berth, only hunting out of state.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc1.description: I tried to tell myself that the vampires would be hunting somewhere in the world regardless, though I felt uncomfortable with the compromise.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc1.source_text: I told myself that they’d all be hunting somewhere in the world, regardless, and I felt uncomfortable about the compromise.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc1.description: I was amazed to find that the visiting vampires accepted Jacob easily and treated him as neither prey nor fully a person.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc1.source_text: I was amazed at the easy acceptance the visiting vampires had for Jacob; they treated him not quite a person, but also not food, either.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc2.description: I replayed the scene of Renesmee’s introduction to the Denali coven a half dozen times.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc2.source_text: We’d replayed the scene of Renesmee’s introduction to the Denali coven a half dozen times.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc2.description: I learned that Alice and Jasper had sent Peter and Charlotte our way without giving them any explanation at all.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc2.source_text: First for Peter and Charlotte, whom Alice and Jasper had sent our way without giving them any explanation at all; like most people who knew Alice, they trusted her instructions despite the lack of information.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc2.description: I learned that neither Peter nor Charlotte had ever seen an immortal child.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc2.source_text: Neither Peter nor Charlotte had ever seen an immortal child.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc2.description: I realized that Peter and Charlotte's negative reaction was not as powerful as the Denali vampires' had been at first.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc2.source_text: their negative reaction was not as powerful as the Denali vampires’ had been at first.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc2.description: I observed that Peter and Charlotte became as committed to witnessing as Tanya’s family.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc2.source_text: Now they were as committed to witnessing as Tanya’s family.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc3.description: I learned that the Irish clan accepted our story absolutely before even touching Renesmee.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc3.source_text: Maggie declared that Edward spoke the truth, and so Siobhan and Liam accepted our story absolutely before even touching Renesmee.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc3.description: I felt reassured that Siobhan and Liam trusted our judgment and accepted Renesmee without suspicion.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc3.source_text: Maggie declared that Edward spoke the truth, and so Siobhan and Liam accepted our story absolutely before even touching Renesmee.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.description: I learned that Amun refused to touch Renesmee and ordered his coven to leave.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.source_text: Even after two younger members of his coven, Benjamin and Tia, had been convinced by Renesmee’s explanation, Amun refused to touch her and ordered his coven to leave.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.description: I learned that Benjamin persuaded Amun to stay by implying threats about disbanding their alliance.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.source_text: Benjamin—an oddly cheerful vampire who looked barely older than a boy and seemed both utterly confident and utterly careless at the same time—persuaded Amun to stay with a few subtle threats about disbanding their alliance.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.description: I learned that Amun would not allow his mate Kebi to touch Renesmee either.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.source_text: Amun stayed, but continued to refuse to touch Renesmee, and would not allow his mate, Kebi, to touch her, either.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.description: I learned that the Egyptian coven had a familylike appearance with midnight hair and olive-toned pallor.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.source_text: It seemed an unlikely grouping—though the Egyptians all looked so alike, with their midnight hair and olive-toned pallor, that they easily could have passed for a biological family.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.description: I learned that Amun was the senior member and the outspoken leader of the coven.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.source_text: Amun was the senior member and the outspoken leader.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.description: I learned that Kebi never strayed farther away from Amun than his shadow and never spoke while I watched.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.source_text: Kebi never strayed farther away from Amun than his shadow, and I never heard her speak a single word.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.description: I learned that Tia was quiet but spoke with insight and gravity when she did.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.source_text: Tia, Benjamin’s mate, was a quiet woman as well, though when she did speak there was great insight and gravity to everything she said.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.description: I learned that Benjamin appeared boyish, confident, and careless yet held influence over the coven.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.source_text: Benjamin—an oddly cheerful vampire who looked barely older than a boy and seemed both utterly confident and utterly careless at the same time—persuaded Amun to stay...

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.description: I became convinced that Benjamin had a magnetic influence or talent that drew the others to him.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.source_text: Still, it was Benjamin whom they all seemed to revolve around, as if he had some invisible magnetism the others depended upon for their balance.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.description: I noticed Eleazar staring at Benjamin with wide eyes and assumed that observation indicated recognition of Benjamin's talent.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc4.source_text: I saw Eleazar staring at the boy with wide eyes and assumed Benjamin had a talent that drew the others to him.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc5.description: I learned that Benjamin can actually influence the elements—earth, wind, water, and fire through true physical manipulation and not by mental illusion.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc5.source_text: "He can actually influence the elements—earth, wind, water, and fire. True physical manipulation, no illusion of the mind."

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc5.description: I learned that Amun has been keeping Benjamin from Aro's attention.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc5.source_text: "Amun has been keeping Benjamin from Aro’s attention."

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc5.description: I learned that Amun created Benjamin knowing he would be special.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc5.source_text: "Amun created Benjamin, knowing he would be special."

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc5.description: I learned that Benjamin is still experimenting with his power and that Amun tries to mold him into a weapon.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc5.source_text: "Benjamin’s still experimenting with it, and Amun tries to mold him into a weapon."

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc5.description: I learned that even my shield would do nothing against Benjamin's ability.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc5.source_text: "Something that even your shield would do nothing against."

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc5.description: I realized that Edward likes Benjamin based on his tone.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc5.source_text: "You like him," I surmised from the tone of his voice.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc5.description: I noticed that Edward admires Benjamin's clear sense of right and wrong.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc5.source_text: "He has a very clear sense of right and wrong. I like his attitude."

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc6.description: I learned that Emmett and Rosalie sent nomad friends of Carlisle and that Garrett, Mary, and Randall arrived to listen to Renesmee's story.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc6.source_text: I read: "Emmett and Rose sent individuals—any nomad friends of Carlisle’s that they could track down. Garrett came first... Mary and Randall also came—friends already, though they did not travel together. They listened to Renesmee’s story and stayed to witness like the others."

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc6.description: I felt better when Carlisle and Esme returned a week later and when Emmett and Rosalie returned a few days afterward.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc6.source_text: I read: "Carlisle and Esme returned a week after they had gone, Emmett and Rosalie just a few days later, and all of us felt better when they were home."

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc6.description: I learned that Alistair was brought by Carlisle, that Alistair shunned company, and that Alistair refused to touch Renesmee.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc6.source_text: I read: "Carlisle brought one more friend home with him... Alistair was a misanthropic English vampire who counted Carlisle as his closest acquaintance, though he could hardly stand a visit more than once a century. Alistair very much preferred to wander alone... refusing, like Amun, to touch her."

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc6.description: I realized that Carlisle counts Alistair as his closest acquaintance despite Alistair's general misanthropy and reluctance to visit.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc6.source_text: I read: "Alistair was a misanthropic English vampire who counted Carlisle as his closest acquaintance, though he could hardly stand a visit more than once a century."

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc7.description: I learned that Alice had sent the Amazons to us.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc7.source_text: I quote: 'But Alice had sent them, and that was interesting news, to put it mildly.'

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc7.description: I brought Renesmee out to meet the Amazons.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc7.source_text: I quote: 'I brought Renesmee out to meet them.'

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc7.description: I felt oddly comforted to know Alice was on a separate mission and avoiding Aro.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc7.source_text: I quote: 'The news about Alice was oddly comforting.'

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc7.description: I noticed I regarded the Amazons as wilder and less civilized than other vampires.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc7.source_text: I quote: 'I’d never met any vampires less civilized.'

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc7.description: I became more worried about having the Amazons so close to Renesmee because of their swift, jerky movements.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc7.source_text: I quote: 'I couldn’t help worrying as I watched their swift, jerky movements so close beside her.'

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc8.description: I learned that I am immune to Zafrina's illusions and cannot see them.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc8.source_text: I quote: "It’s a very straightforward illusion," Edward explained when it turned out that I couldn’t see anything, as usual.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc8.description: I became worried that Zafrina might create disturbing images and I changed my assessment of allowing Renesmee unrestricted viewing.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc8.source_text: I quote: "I worried, because I was quite sure that Zafrina was able to create images that were not pretty at all."

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc8.description: I felt protective of Renesmee and anxious about her exposure to Zafrina's visions.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc8.source_text: I quote: "After that, it was hard to keep Renesmee away from Zafrina and her pretty pictures. I worried, because I was quite sure that Zafrina was able to create images that were not pretty at all."

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc9.description: I needed instruction and I had very little time to learn both physically and mentally.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc9.source_text: I needed my hands. I had so much to learn, both physically and mentally, and the time was so short.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc9.description: I experienced my first attempt at fighting and I was pinned by Edward in about two seconds.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc9.source_text:
My first attempt at learning to fight did not go well.
Edward had me pinned in about two seconds.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc9.description: I learned that Edward could not teach me because I realized he could not bear analyzing me as a target or imagining ways to kill me.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc9.source_text: "Looking at you that way, analyzing you as a target. Seeing all the ways I can kill you . . ." "It just makes it too real for me."

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc9.description: I found Emmett to be more than willing to help and I felt his teaching was almost revenge for past arm-wrestling losses.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc9.source_text: Emmett was more than willing to help, though his teaching felt to me a lot like revenge for all the lost arm-wrestling matches.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc9.description: I noticed that Rosalie, Tanya, and Eleazar were patient and supportive during my training.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc9.source_text: Rose, Tanya, and Eleazar all were patient and supportive.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc9.description: I discovered that the nomad Garrett was a surprisingly good teacher and I wondered how he had never joined a coven.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc9.source_text: The nomad Garrett took a few turns—he was a surprisingly good teacher; he interacted so easily with others in general that I wondered how he’d never found a coven.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc9.description: I fought once with Zafrina while Renesmee watched and I learned that I liked Zafrina but I was also terrified of her wildness.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc9.source_text: I even fought once with Zafrina while Renesmee watched from Jacob’s arms. I liked Zafrina very much and I knew she wouldn’t really hurt me, the wild woman scared me to death.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc9.description: I realized my overall knowledge felt basic and I did not know how many seconds I would last against powerful opponents like Alec and Jane.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc9.source_text: I learned many things from my teachers, but I had the sense that my knowledge was still impossibly basic. I had no idea how many seconds I would last against Alec and Jane.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc10.description: I learned that I spent every spare minute in the backyard working with Kate to push my internal shield outside my own brain to protect someone else.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc10.source_text: Every minute of the day that I wasn’t with Renesmee or learning to fight, I was in the backyard working with Kate, trying to push my internal shield outside of my own brain to protect someone else.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc10.description: I learned that my attempts produced only faint, sporadic success and that my weariness was entirely mental.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc10.source_text: Over and over I tried to force the nebulous shield outside of myself, with only faint, sporadic success. My weariness was all mental.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc10.description: I began to hate the practice and to resent Kate for appearing to enjoy causing Edward pain.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc10.source_text: I hated this practice, and I wished that Zafrina would help instead of Kate. Then all Edward would have to do was look at Zafrina’s illusions until I could stop him from seeing them. But Kate insisted that I needed better motivation—by which she meant my hatred of watching Edward’s pain. I was beginning to doubt her assertion from the first day we’d met—that she wasn’t sadistic about the use of her gift. She seemed to be enjoying herself to me.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc10.description: I realized that I had a raging desire to be of use and to keep Edward, Renesmee, and as much of my family as possible safe with me.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc10.source_text: I had only my raging desire to be of use, to be able to keep Edward, Renesmee, and as much of my family as possible safe with me.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc11.description: I protected Renesmee with a mental shield and positioned myself so she was completely swaddled inside it.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc11.source_text: I stretched it around myself, out from myself, swaddling Renesmee completely inside it, just in case Kate got past my guard.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc11.description: I experienced intense maternal rage that altered my perception and increased my physical strength.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc11.source_text: I was so furious that my vision took on a strange reddish tint, and my tongue tasted like burning metal. The strength I usually worked to keep restrained flowed through my muscles...

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc11.description: I knew I could physically annihilate Kate if she pushed me to it and prepared to act on that threat.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc11.source_text: I knew I could crush her into diamond-hard rubble if she pushed me to it.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc11.description: I began to accept that pressure and urgency might help Renesmee learn faster despite my dislike of harsh methods.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc11.source_text: But I was in better control of myself, and I could see the wisdom of Kate’s words. The anger helped me. I would learn faster under pressure.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc11.description: I regarded Kate as a direct threat to my child and made clear that she must keep her distance.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc11.source_text: "Stay away from us, Kate," I warned her.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc12.description: I learned that my shield behaves like an elastic, one-way barrier that grows heavier the longer I hold it.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc12.source_text: My fury had almost entirely ebbed, and I clenched my teeth together, panting faster as I pushed out against the elastic shield; it felt like it was getting heavier the longer I held it.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc12.description: I discovered that my shield can recoil if stretched too far and snap back into its original shape.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc12.source_text: But she’d spoken too soon; with a sharp gasp, I felt my shield recoil like a rubber band stretched too far, snapping back into its original shape.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc12.description: I confirmed that I could include Renesmee within the shield and restore her sight after a collapse.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc12.source_text: Wearily, I fought back against the elastic pull, forcing the shield to include her again.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc12.description: I became convinced that using the shield can physically drain me even though I am a vampire and previously did not need rest.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc12.source_text: Can I have a minute? I panted. Since I’d become a vampire, I hadn’t felt the need to rest even once before this moment.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc12.description: I observed that I could extend the shield far enough for Kate and Garrett to regain sight and signal that they could see.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc12.source_text: I only watched Kate’s anxious expression while I worked, and I groaned quietly with relief when her eyes blinked and focused. She raised her hand.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc13.description: I learned that two unexpected Romanian vampires, Vladimir and Stefan, arrived and spoke in tandem about wishing to see the Volturi challenged.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc13.source_text:
"No one sent us," a deep whispery voice answered Carlisle’s question.

"We’ve been waiting a millennium and a half for the Italian scum to be challenged," said the first.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc13.description: I became more wary of the Romanians after hearing their dark, menacing words and noticing the hostile reaction in the room.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc13.source_text: "I didn’t like the sound of their voices, or the dark menace in their words."

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc13.description: I learned that several vampires positioned themselves defensively between the newcomers and Renesmee, indicating immediate protective concern.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc13.source_text: A few—Carmen, Tanya, Zafrina, and Senna—repositioned themselves subtly into defensive poses between the newcomers and Renesmee.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc13.description: I observed the Romanians' physical appearance as slight, short, powdery-skinned, with dark burgundy eyes and simple black clothing that hinted at older styles.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc13.source_text:
The vampires at the door were both slight and short, one dark-haired and the other with hair so ashy blond that it looked pale gray.

They had the same powdery look to their skin as the Volturi...Their sharp, narrow eyes were dark burgundy...They wore very simple black clothes that could pass as modern but hinted at older designs.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc14.description: I learned that we had pulled together seventeen witnesses from multiple covens to supplement our family of eleven.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc14.source_text: In the end, we had pulled together seventeen witnesses—the Irish, Siobhan, Liam, and Maggie; the Egyptians, Amun, Kebi, Benjamin, and Tia; the Amazons, Zafrina and Senna; the Romanians, Vladimir and Stefan; and the nomads, Charlotte and Peter, Garrett, Alistair, Mary, and Randall—to supplement our family of eleven.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc14.description: I practiced my shield with Zafrina and Kate while others watched.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc14.source_text: They watched me practice my shield with Zafrina and Kate, watched Edward answer unspoken questions, watched Benjamin pull geysers of water from the river or sharp gusts of wind from the still air with just his mind, and their eyes glowed with their fierce hope that the Volturi had finally met their match.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc14.description: I became a little bit hopeful about our chances against the Volturi because Renesmee had won over so many in a short time.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc14.source_text: We all were beginning to be a little bit hopeful. Even I couldn’t help it. Renesmee had won over so many in such a brief time.

tw-book4-chapter32_Sc14.description: I noticed that the last two surviving Romanians would not touch Renesmee yet showed no aversion to her and seemed pleased by our alliance with the werewolves.
tw-book4-chapter32_Sc14.source_text: The last two surviving Romanians—focused only on their bitter resentment of the ones who had overthrown their empire fifteen hundred years earlier—took everything in stride. They would not touch Renesmee, but they showed no aversion to her. They seemed mysteriously delighted by our alliance with the werewolves.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc1.description: I will bring Renesmee over to see Charlie instead of having Charlie visit.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc1.source_text: How about I bring Renesmee over to see you?

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc1.description: I know a visit to Charlie is not a good idea right now because of a strictly need-to-know situation.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc1.source_text: Charlie, we’ve still got that strictly need-to-know company situation going. I know it’s been more than a week since you saw Renesmee, but a visit is just not a good idea right now.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc1.description: I felt urgency about the visit and I acknowledged that I had already put this off too long.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc1.source_text: The sooner the better. I’d already put this off too long.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc1.description: I heard Charlie ask if Jake was coming with us.
I recognized the attachment between Jacob and Renesmee as obvious even if Charlie did not know about imprinting.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc1.source_text: Though Charlie didn’t know anything about werewolf imprinting, no one could be oblivious to the attachment between Jacob and Renesmee.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc2.description: I acknowledged that I had told Edward I was taking Renesmee to Charlie as an excuse to keep my father away, and I knew that was not my real reason.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc2.source_text: This was the excuse I’d given Edward: I was taking Renesmee to Charlie so that he wouldn’t decide to come here. It was a good reason for leaving the house, but not my real reason at all.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc2.description: I learned that twenty-seven oddly matched vampires had sworn not to kill anyone in a three-hundred-mile radius but that I still believed no human should be near them.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc2.source_text: This trip was about more than protecting my father from the twenty-seven oddly matched vampires—who all had sworn not to kill anyone in a three-hundred-mile radius, but still… Obviously, no human being should get anywhere near this group.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc2.description: I felt reassured and happy that Jacob still treated me as human rather than as a vampire.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc2.source_text: It made me happy that I didn’t really count as a vampire to him. I was still just Bella.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc2.description: I decided to keep Renesmee away from the Romanians after hearing Vladimir's account and threat about gouging out eyes.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc2.source_text: We sat still for a very long time, child," Vladimir had answered, with Stefan nodding along... "I imagine that will give us an advantage when we gouge theirs from their sockets.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc3.description: I noticed my eyes were not as ghoulish as they had been and were moving from bright crimson toward a dull reddish orange, soon to be amber enough to quit the contacts.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc3.source_text: My eyes were not as ghoulish as they had been in the beginning—definitely closer to a dull reddish orange than to bright crimson. Soon they'd be amber enough for me to quit the contacts.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc3.description: I hoped the change wouldn't upset Charlie too much.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc3.source_text: I hoped the change wouldn’t upset Charlie too much.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc3.description: I decided not to risk going any further with my conversation when I couldn't tell how interested Renesmee was.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc3.source_text: I couldn’t tell how interested she was in our conversation, but I decided not to risk going any further.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc3.description: I noticed the tone of my voice caught Jacob's attention when I broached the subject.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc3.source_text: The tone of my voice caught his attention.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc4.description: I noticed Renesmee had grown significantly and that Charlie remarked she had grown half a foot and looked skinny.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc4.source_text: I quoted: "I swear you’ve grown half a foot. And you look skinny, Ness."

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc4.description: I smelled food from the kitchen and also detected fresh pine and packing dust that implied holiday decorations were up.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc4.source_text: I quoted: "The smell of chicken, tomato, garlic, and cheese issued from the kitchen; it probably smelled good to everyone else. I could also smell fresh pine and packing dust."

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc4.description: I inferred that Charlie must have put up the old decorations because of the packing dust.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc4.source_text: I quoted: "That explained the packing dust. Charlie must have put the old decorations up."

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc4.description: I believed Jacob had no idea what I was up to and therefore could not divulge my plans.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc4.source_text: I quoted: "Even if he couldn’t help but think about this near Edward, at least there wasn’t much for him to share. He had no idea what I was up to."

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc4.description: I realized that I had not been thinking about the holidays at all despite Charlie's comments.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc4.source_text: I quoted: "I rolled my eyes at him, but in truth, I hadn’t thought about the holidays at all."

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc5.description: I know that driving no longer intimidates me because my reflexes are well up to the job.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc5.source_text: The roads were slick and dark, but driving didn’t intimidate me anymore. My reflexes were well up to the job, and I barely paid attention to the road.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc5.description: I recognize that keeping my speed from attracting attention when I have company is a practical problem.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc5.source_text: The problem was keeping my speed from attracting attention when I had company.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc5.description: I have learned that anger is the key motivator and that Kate no longer needs to push me to find reasons to be angry.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc5.source_text: Kate didn’t feel the need to motivate me anymore—it wasn’t hard to find reasons to feel angry, now that I knew that was the key—and so I mostly worked with Zafrina.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc5.description: I can extend my shield to cover almost a ten-foot area for more than a minute though doing so exhausts me.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc5.source_text: She was pleased with my extension; I was able to cover almost a ten-foot area for more than a minute, though it exhausted me.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc5.description: I tried to push the shield away from my mind to strengthen myself but I wasn’t very good at it and I only got one glimpse of the jungle river Zafrina showed me.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc5.source_text: This morning she’d been trying to find out if I could push the shield away from my mind altogether. I didn’t see what the use of that would be, but Zafrina thought it would help strengthen me, like exercising muscles in the stomach and back rather than just the arms. Eventually, you could lift more weight when all the muscles were stronger. I wasn’t very good at it. I had only gotten one glimpse of the jungle river she was trying to show me.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc5.description: I have memorized the appropriate maps and I was able to find the address for J. Jenks that did not exist online and I plan to seek Jason Jenks at an address Alice did not give me.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc5.source_text: I’d memorized the appropriate maps, and I had no problem finding my way to the address that didn’t exist online, the one for J. Jenks. My next step would be Jason Jenks at the other address, the one Alice had not given me.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc5.description: I want to finish today’s mission quickly so that I can return to the vital work of learning to protect some and learning to kill others.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc5.source_text: I wanted to be done with today’s mission, to have the mystery sorted out so that I could get back to the vital task of learning. Learning to protect some, learning to kill others.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc5.description: I mostly work with Zafrina now and I note that she is pleased with my extension while Kate no longer feels the need to motivate me.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc5.source_text: Kate didn’t feel the need to motivate me anymore—it wasn’t hard to find reasons to feel angry, now that I knew that was the key—and so I mostly worked with Zafrina. She was pleased with my extension;

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.description: I learned that the target address was in a dilapidated, gray ghetto street with peeling paint and boarded windows.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.source_text: I read: "To say that it wasn’t a nice neighborhood would be an understatement. Everything had faded to shades of gray."

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.description: I learned that the abandoned building at the curb corresponded to the address I was given and that the tattoo parlor beside it was two numbers off.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.source_text: I read: "I was so bemused by the carefree whistler, I didn’t realize at first that the abandoned building was right where the address I was looking for should exist. The tattoo parlor beside it was just two numbers off."

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.description: I learned that the whistler identified himself as Max and that he had a surprisingly well-kept appearance beneath ragged clothing.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.source_text: I read: "The man laid his paper aside, and his clothes surprised me, now that I could see them. Under his long ragged duster, he was a little too well dressed."

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.description: I learned that Max works for J. Jenks as a local gatekeeper and that Max intended to call J to describe me before deciding whether to help.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.source_text: I read: "Tell you what I’ll do. I’ll give J a call and describe you to him. Let him make the decision."

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.description: I learned that I gave my last name as Cullen to Max during the interaction.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.source_text: I read: "My last name is Cullen," I told Max, wondering if that was too much information.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.description: I realized that I felt fascination rather than the fear I would have had as a human in the same neighborhood.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.source_text: I read: "My old Chevy would have looked healthy here. During my human years, I would have locked the doors and driven away as fast as I dared. As it was, I was a little fascinated."

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.description: I formed the impression that Max could be an uneasy ally because he needs the job and fears repercussions if he helps the wrong people.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.source_text: I read: "I want to help you, I do, but—and of course I’m speaking hypothetically...—if I pass somebody through that could get him in trouble, I’m out of work."

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.description: I suspected that J. Jenks might already know my sister, which made me consider how my description could affect our chances of entry.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.source_text: I read: "J knows your sister?" "I think so."

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.description: I grew irritated with Alice for providing insufficient information about the contact and location.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc6.source_text: I read: "I was starting to get irritated with Alice. Did I really have to be quite this blind?"

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc7.description: I went to Jason Scott's law office in a strip mall to meet the forger.
I asked for two birth certificates, two passports, and one driver's license.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc7.source_text: "Two birth certificates, two passports, one driver’s license," I said in a low, strained tone.

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc7.description: I provided the names Jacob Wolfe and Vanessa Wolfe for the forged documents.
I specified ages of twenty-seven for the man and five for the girl on the documents.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc7.source_text: "Twenty-seven for the man, five for the girl."

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc7.description: I realized that Renesmee would need a forger only if she was running and that running would mean we had lost.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc7.source_text: "The only reason Renesmee would need a forger was if she was running. And the only reason Renesmee would be running was if we had lost."

tw-book4-chapter33_Sc7.description: I felt my hope fade and accepted that we couldn't win but that we needed a chance to kill Demetri so Renesmee could run.
tw-book4-chapter33_Sc7.source_text: "We couldn’t win. But we must have a good shot at killing Demetri before we lost, giving Renesmee the chance to run."

tw-book4-chapter34_Sc2.description: I hadn’t seen my mother since the wedding and felt that the gradual distancing was preferable because my mother was too fragile for my world.
tw-book4-chapter34_Sc2.source_text: I hadn’t seen my mother since the wedding, but I found I could only be glad for the gradual distancing that had begun two years ago. She was too fragile for my world.

tw-book4-chapter34_Sc2.description: I held Renesmee on my lap while she played with her locket.
tw-book4-chapter34_Sc2.source_text: Renesmee sat on my lap, playing with her locket, opening and closing it.

tw-book4-chapter34_Sc2.description: I planned to give Jacob the documents and a note for Charlie and a letter for Renesmee in case I couldn’t tell them I loved them anymore.
tw-book4-chapter34_Sc2.source_text: I would have to give Jacob the documents before it was too late. I would give him a note for Charlie, too. And a letter for Renesmee. Something for her to read when I couldn’t tell her I loved her anymore.

tw-book4-chapter34_Sc2.description: I believed that Charlie was stronger and might be able to handle a goodbye, but I felt that I wasn’t ready to say goodbye.
tw-book4-chapter34_Sc2.source_text: Charlie was stronger. Maybe even strong enough for a goodbye now, but I wasn’t.

tw-book4-chapter34_Sc3.description: I learned that several covens, including the Romanians, decided to oppose the Volturi and to fight alongside Carlisle.
tw-book4-chapter34_Sc3.source_text: "That we must stand against them while there is still hope." "We fight," Stefan said. "We fight," Vladimir agreed.

tw-book4-chapter34_Sc3.description: I learned that we planned to wait near the big baseball clearing Alice had seen so the Volturi could be led away from town.
tw-book4-chapter34_Sc3.source_text: We all would hunt again nearer to the time we expected the Volturi. As the deadline was not exact, we were planning to stay a few nights out in the big baseball clearing Alice had seen, just in case.

tw-book4-chapter34_Sc3.description: I learned that Demetri would lead the Volturi to us and that he would probably track Edward since he could not track me.
tw-book4-chapter34_Sc3.source_text: We didn’t want the Volturi too close to town, and Demetri would lead them to wherever we were. I wondered who he would track in, and guessed that it would be Edward since he couldn’t track me.

tw-book4-chapter34_Sc3.description: I felt increasingly responsible and anxious about my mental shield because I worried that trusting me to protect others might cause failure.
tw-book4-chapter34_Sc3.source_text: I know the others are hoping that I’ll be able to shield Zafrina and Benjamin, even if I can only keep it up for a few seconds at a time. What if your trust in me is the reason that we fail?

tw-book4-chapter34_Sc3.description: I noticed that Edward, Renesmee, and Jacob accompanied me on hunts after the meeting, showing immediate practical support and involvement.
tw-book4-chapter34_Sc3.source_text: Edward, Renesmee, and I went to hunt. Jacob tagged along.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc1.description: I took Edward's Volvo again and I noted that detail about my travel.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc1.source_text: I took his Volvo again, wondering if he’d read the odometer after my last errand.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc1.description: I watched him hug Renesmee a little bit tighter to his chest and I registered the gesture.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc1.source_text: He hugged Renesmee just a little bit tighter to his chest.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc1.description: I came to believe Edward had pieced together that I had a secret.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc1.source_text: How much had he pieced together? That I had a secret, absolutely.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc1.description: I began to think Edward might have concluded that Aro could soon know everything he knew.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc1.source_text: Did he guess that Aro might soon know everything he knew? I thought Edward could have come to that conclusion,

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc1.description: I inferred Edward was deliberately not demanding reasons from me to avoid speculating about my behavior.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc1.source_text: which explained why he had demanded no reasons from me. I guessed he was trying not to speculate too much, trying to keep my behavior off his mind.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc1.description: I was unsure whether Edward had connected my odd performance the morning after Alice left, including burning my book in the fire, to my secret.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc1.source_text: Had he put this together with my odd performance the morning after Alice left, burning my book in the fire? I didn’t know if he could have made that leap.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward estimated we had about two more days.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.source_text: Edward estimated that we had about two more days.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: I learned that the plan was to set ourselves in the clearing to draw the Volturi to our chosen place.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.source_text: Then we would set ourselves in the clearing, drawing the Volturi to our chosen place.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: I learned that Alice sent me to a dilapidated drop point where J. Jenks referred his shadier clients.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.source_text: I thought I knew Alice’s purpose in sending me to the dilapidated drop point where J. Jenks referred his shadier clients.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: I learned that Jenks had a legitimate persona and a hidden one as a purveyor of illegal documents.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.source_text: If I’d met him as Jason Jenks or Jason Scott, legitimate lawyer, would I ever have unearthed J. Jenks, purveyor of illegal documents?

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: I learned that I had to make my visit clearly illicit as the clue to unearthing Jenks.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.source_text: I’d had to go the route that made it clear I was up to no good. That was my clue.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: I learned that I arrived early, ignored the valets, and waited inside after putting in my contacts.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.source_text: It was black when I pulled into the parking lot of the restaurant a few minutes early, ignoring the eager valets by the entrance.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: I learned that I gave the name Jenks at the podium and was led upstairs to a private room with a fire crackling in a stone hearth.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.source_text: I gave the name Jenks at the podium, and the obsequious maître d’ led me upstairs to a small private room with a fire crackling in a stone hearth.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: I felt flattered and changed about being perceived as beautiful by others rather than only Edward.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.source_text: I couldn’t help being a little flattered; I still wasn’t used to being beautiful to everyone rather than just Edward.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: I learned that I practiced a handshake and noted that it was still a good habit given the Cullen situation.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.source_text: Not that J wasn’t obviously aware that there was something up with the Cullens, but it was still a good habit to practice.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: I learned that I briefly wondered what it would feel like to put my hand in the fire.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.source_text: For one half second, I wondered what it would feel like to put my hand in the fire. What it would feel like when I burned. . . .

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.description: I updated my view of J by noting that he seemed careful to keep himself untainted by baser associations and would be offended by a dark parking lot handoff.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc2.source_text: J seemed careful to keep himself untainted by his baser associations; I had a feeling a handoff in the dark parking lot would offend his sensibilities.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc3.description: I handed J his bonus envelope and took the forged documents from him before leaving with the contraband.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc3.source_text: As I spoke, I took the thick white envelope with his bonus from my bag and handed it to him.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc3.description: I discovered that J had modified Jacob's identity papers by flipping his picture and altering the coloring so the passport and driver's license would not be obviously identical.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc3.source_text: J had flipped Jacob’s picture and changed the coloring so that it wasn’t immediately evident that it was the same picture on both his passport and driver’s license.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc3.description: I am preparing a safe place for the little girl in case something should happen to my husband and me.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc3.source_text: I’m simply preparing a safe place for her in case something were to happen to my husband and me.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc3.description: I began to view J as a nervous, apologetic professional who appeared anxious and regretful despite his criminal work.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc3.source_text: Sweat was dewing up on his forehead again, and he pulled a blue silk handkerchief from his pocket and began mopping.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc3.description: I confirmed that I am to be Mr. Edward's bride when asked directly about my relation to the Cullen family.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc3.source_text: “You would be Mr. Edward’s bride, then?” “Yes.”

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc4.description: I noticed that most of the cars, including Alice’s Porsche and my Ferrari, were missing when I returned to the house.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc4.source_text: When I got back to the house, most of the cars, including Alice’s Porsche and my Ferrari, were missing.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc4.description: I learned that the traditional vampires were going as far away as possible to satiate their thirst.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc4.source_text: The traditional vampires were going as far away as possible to satiate their thirst.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc4.description: I saw only Kate and Garrett in the front room arguing playfully about the nutritional value of animal blood.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc4.source_text: Only Kate and Garrett were in the front room, arguing playfully about the nutritional value of animal blood.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc4.description: I inferred that Edward must have taken Renesmee home to sleep.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc4.source_text: Edward must have taken Renesmee home to sleep.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc4.description: I inferred that Jacob was in the woods close by the cottage.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc4.source_text: Jacob, no doubt, was in the woods close by the cottage.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc4.description: I found a small black leather backpack in Alice and Jasper’s closet and I raided their petty cash and put the envelope with fake passports and IDs into the bag.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc4.source_text: I rooted silently through their huge closet until I found the right sort of bag. It must have been Alice’s; it was a small black leather backpack, the kind that was usually used as a purse, little enough that even Renesmee could carry it without looking out of place. Then I raided their petty cash, taking about twice the yearly income for the average American household. The envelope with the fake passports and IDs went into the bag on top of the money.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc4.description: I felt helpless and believed that the small package was pitifully insignificant to save my daughter and my best friend.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc4.source_text: Then I sat on the edge of Alice and Jasper’s bed and looked at the pitifully insignificant package that was all I could give my daughter and my best friend to help save their lives. I slumped against the bedpost, feeling helpless.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc4.description: I decided to take advantage of having the house to myself to take supplies that might help.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc4.source_text: Which basically gave me the house to myself, and I was quick to take advantage.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc5.description: I learned that if Jacob and Renesmee escaped, Demetri would be dead and that would spare Alice and Jasper for a time.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc5.source_text: If I was to assume that Jacob and Renesmee were going to escape, then that included the assumption that Demetri would be dead. That gave any survivors a little breathing room, Alice and Jasper included.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc5.description: I realized that Alice could not see Jacob or Renesmee because they were blind spots for her.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc5.source_text: There was no reason why this couldn’t happen, except for the fact that Jake and Renesmee both were blind spots for Alice. How would she begin to look for them?

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc5.description: I left the room and crossed the hall to Carlisle and Esme’s suite to prepare a written plan.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc5.source_text: I deliberated for a moment, then left the room, crossing the hall to Carlisle and Esme’s suite.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc5.description: I wrote RIO DE JANEIRO in all caps as the place to send Jacob and Renesmee.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc5.source_text: Slowly, deliberately, I wrote the words RIO DE JANEIRO in all caps across the page.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc5.description: I put the note at the bottom of the duffel bag where Jacob would find it soon enough.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc5.source_text: I took a deep breath and put the note at the bottom of the duffel bag, where Jacob would find it soon enough.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc5.description: I decided that it was better for Renesmee to go on without me and I already missed her intensely.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc5.source_text: It was better that Renesmee go on without me. But I already missed her so much I could barely stand it.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc6.description: I stayed in the clearing with Edward and Carlisle for two days while waiting for the Volturi.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc6.source_text: For two days, Edward and Carlisle stayed in the clearing where Alice had seen the Volturi arrive.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc6.description: I stayed physically very close to Edward and avoided saying goodbyes to keep things from feeling final.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc6.source_text: Edward and I had not had a last grand scene of farewell, nor did I plan one.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc6.description: I set up a tent for Renesmee and dressed her in durable clothes while packing a backpack with documents, money, a clue, and love notes.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc6.source_text: We set up a tent for Renesmee a few yards back into the protective forest... I helped her dress in the clothes I’d carefully picked out two days before... Over her jacket I put on the black leather backpack with the documents, the money, the clue, and my love notes for her and Jacob, Charlie and Renée.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc6.description: I placed Aro’s wedding present—a large diamond on a thick gold rope—around my neck as a hopeful sign of trying a peaceful opening.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc6.source_text: Now I fastened the thick gold rope around my neck and felt the weight of the enormous diamond nestle into the hollow of my throat.

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc6.description: I realized I still harbored a blind, senseless hope that attempting a friendly start might help despite expecting conflict.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc6.source_text: But why not try to start things out as friendly as possible? I asked myself. What could it hurt? So I guess I must have had some hope left after all—blind, senseless hope—

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc6.description: I told Renesmee to leave me when I gave the signal and to not tell Jacob about the escape plan until then.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc6.source_text: Don’t tell Jacob until I tell you to run, okay?

tw-book4-chapter35_Sc6.description: I positioned myself a few feet behind the front line with Renesmee on my back and accepted responsibility to protect Benjamin and Zafrina.
tw-book4-chapter35_Sc6.source_text: I stood a few feet behind the front line... Close beside me were Benjamin and Zafrina; it was my job to protect them as long as I was able.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc1.description: I counted thirty-two Volturi and learned that we were outnumbered even when considering our fighters and the wolves.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc1.source_text: There were thirty-two of them. Even if you did not count the two drifting, waifish black-cloaked figures in the very back, who I took to be the wives—their protected position suggesting that they would not be involved in the attack—we were still outnumbered. There were just nineteen of us who would fight, and then seven more to watch as we were destroyed. Even counting the ten wolves, they had us.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc1.description: I saw the Volturi arrive with pageantry in a rigid, formal formation that moved together as a dark shape above the snow.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc1.source_text: They came with pageantry, with a kind of beauty. They came in a rigid, formal formation. They moved together, but it was not a march; they flowed in perfect synchronicity from the trees—a dark, unbroken shape that seemed to hover a few inches above the white snow, so smooth was the advance.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc1.description: I observed the configuration fold outward like an angular fan with gray-cloaked figures on the flanks and darker forms surging forward in the center.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc1.source_text: At some sign I did not see—or perhaps there was no sign, only millennia of practice—the configuration folded outward. The motion was too stiff, too square to resemble the opening of a flower, though the color suggested that; it was the opening of a fan, graceful but very angular. The gray-cloaked figures spread to the flanks while the darker forms surged precisely forward in the center, each movement closely controlled.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc1.description: I identified two waifish black-cloaked figures in the very back whom I took to be the wives, whose protected position suggested they would not be involved in the attack.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc1.source_text: Even if you did not count the two drifting, waifish black-cloaked figures in the very back, who I took to be the wives—their protected position suggesting that they would not be involved in the attack—we were still outnumbered.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc1.description: I realized that the Volturi displayed no gloating or vindictive joy and instead showed strict discipline, which changed my expectation from my nightmare.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc1.source_text: This was almost my old nightmare. The only thing lacking was the gloating desire I’d seen on the faces in my dream—the smiles of vindictive joy. Thus far, the Volturi were too disciplined to show any emotion at all.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc1.description: I viewed our collection of vampires as suddenly disorganized and unprepared when compared to the Volturi's cohesion and control.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc1.source_text: They showed no surprise or dismay at the collection of vampires that waited for them here—a collection that looked suddenly disorganized and unprepared in comparison.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc1.description: I noticed that the Volturi showed no surprise at the giant wolf that stood in our midst, indicating their composure and control.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc1.source_text: They showed no surprise at the giant wolf that stood in our midst.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc2.description: I saw more vampires entering the clearing behind the Volturi, swelling their ranks beyond the original force.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc2.source_text: more vampires began entering the clearing behind them.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc2.description: I learned that the backing force was large, totaling more than forty vampires altogether.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc2.source_text: This motley, disorganized horde—more than forty vampires altogether—was the Volturi’s own kind of witness.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc2.description: I felt an increased sense of despair as the realization sank in that we didn’t have a prayer against such overwhelming numbers.
I felt crushed by the pressure of despair as the comprehension of our situation pushed me down.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc2.source_text: Despair weighted the air, pushing me down with more pressure than before.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc2.description: I recognized the vampire world’s collective hostility toward the immortal children after reading the faces in that mob.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc2.source_text: I did not fully realize the vampire world’s feeling toward the immortal children before I read these faces.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc2.description: I saw the mob as the Volturi’s chosen witnesses who would later proclaim that the criminals had been eradicated and would be willing to help enact violence.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc2.source_text: When we were dead, they would spread the word that the criminals had been eradicated, that the Volturi had acted with nothing but impartiality.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc3.description: I noticed Irina standing between the companies with a horrified gaze locked on Tanya.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc3.source_text: Irina’s horrified gaze was locked on Tanya’s position in the front line.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc3.description: I saw the Volturi freeze into absolute stillness as one about a hundred yards away.
