tw-book4-chapter36_Sc3.source_text: the Volturi froze into absolute stillness as one. They stood about a hundred yards away from us.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc3.description: I counted the wolves who joined us and recognized that there were sixteen newcomers plus Jacob, making seventeen total.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc3.source_text: There were sixteen of them spaced evenly around us—seventeen total, counting Jacob.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc3.description: I felt my hopeless despair vanish and become murderously enraged, wanting to destroy the Volturi in that moment.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc3.source_text: Abruptly, I was furious. Beyond furious, I was murderously enraged. My hopeless despair vanished entirely.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc3.description: I grew to hate the Volturi more deeply and imagined brutal violence against them as retribution.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc3.source_text: all I wanted in that moment was the chance to sink my teeth into them, to rip their limbs from their bodies and pile them for burning.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc3.description: I realized the wolves who had joined us were very young and likely the result of a population surge caused by the vampire gathering.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc3.source_text: It was clear from their heights and oversized paws that the newcomers all were very, very young. I supposed I should have foreseen this. With so many vampires encamped in the neighborhood, a werewolf population explosion was inevitable.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc3.description: I understood that Sam and the wolves had effectively gambled their entire species by standing with us because exposure would invite Volturi retaliation.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc3.source_text: If any of the wolves stood with us, the Volturi would be sure to search out the rest. They had gambled their entire species on this stand.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc4.description: I observed Aro and Caius touching hands and communicating while the guard paused, apparently waiting for the order to kill.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc4.source_text: In the very center, touching hands, Aro and Caius had paused to evaluate, and the entire guard had paused with them, waiting for the order to kill.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc4.description: I noticed Marcus touching Aro’s other hand but appearing bored and not truly part of the conversation.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc4.source_text: Marcus, though touching Aro’s other hand, did not seem part of the conversation. His expression was not as mindless as the guards’, but it was nearly as blank. Like the one other time I’d seen him, he appeared to be utterly bored.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc4.description: I saw the Volturi’s witnesses leaning toward us with eyes fixed on Renesmee and me while still keeping a wide berth from the Volturi soldiers.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc4.source_text: The bodies of the Volturi’s witnesses leaned toward us, their eyes fixed furiously on Renesmee and me, but they stayed near the fringe of the forest, leaving a wide berth between themselves and the Volturi soldiers.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc4.description: I wondered if the woman touching Aro’s back was Renata and whether she would be able to repel me.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc4.source_text: There was a woman in one of the darker gray cloaks just behind Aro. I couldn’t be sure, but it looked like she might actually be touching his back. Was this the other shield, Renata? I wondered, as Eleazar had, if she would be able to repel me.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc4.description: I identified Alec and Jane as the small, dark-cloaked witch twins whose powers were described as the cornerstone of the Volturi offensive.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc4.source_text: Alec and Jane, easily the smallest members of the guard, stood just to Marcus’s side, flanked by Demetri on the other. Their lovely faces were smooth, giving nothing away; they wore the darkest cloaks beside the pure black of the ancients. The witch twins, Vladimir had called them. Their powers were the cornerstone of the Volturi offensive.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc4.description: I felt nothing but gratitude that Alice had run and was not present to be targeted.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc4.source_text: In that moment, I was nothing but grateful that Alice had run.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc4.description: I read disappointment in Aro’s face as he scanned our line looking for someone who was missing.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc4.source_text: Aro’s and Caius’s clouded red eyes flickered across our line. I read disappointment in Aro’s face as his gaze roved over our faces again and again, looking for one that was missing.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc5.description: I hated to see Carlisle alone and unprotected.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc5.source_text: I hated to see him alone, unprotected.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc5.description: I noticed Renesmee clung to my back with her fingers still tangled in Jacob's fur.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc5.source_text: where she clung to my back, her fingers still tangled in Jacob's fur.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc5.description: I began to believe Carlisle truly meant peace when he offered his hand and insisted no law had been broken.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc5.source_text: No one has broken the law, Aro. Let me explain.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc5.description: I felt increased protectiveness and fear for Renesmee when Irina's identification drew Caius's violent attention.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc5.source_text: “We see the child, Carlisle,” Caius snarled. “Do not treat us as fools.”

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc6.description: I learned that Irina testified the child looked bigger but might still be the same child she had seen before.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc6.source_text: I quote: "She’s not the same, but I think it’s the same child. What I mean is, she’s changed. This child is bigger than the one I saw, but—"

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc6.description: I felt no relief and became numb with rage while waiting for the layers of strategy Edward had promised.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc6.source_text: I quote: "I felt no relief. I waited, almost numb with rage, for the layers of strategy Edward had promised."

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc6.description: I believed Edward would act and possibly shield our thoughts, yet I feared the Volturi intended to read his mind and thereby access all of our secrets.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc6.source_text: I quote: "Of course he wanted Edward. Once he could see into Edward’s mind, he would know all our thoughts. Except mine."

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc7.description: I learned that I could project my shield much farther and with far greater ease than before, sending it ten times my previous distance.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc7.source_text: I threw my shield with all the force in my mind, flung it across the impossible expanse of the field—ten times my best distance—like a javelin.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc7.description: I learned that my shield felt like a muscle I could flex and that I could sense the life force of everything it covered.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc7.source_text: I could feel it flex like just another muscle, obedient to my will.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc7.description: I realized that the recoil and backlash I had feared were of my own making and that I could let that restraint go and set the power free.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc7.source_text: There was no recoil to the elastic fabric now; in that instant of raw force, I saw that the backlash I’d felt before was of my own making—I had been clinging to that invisible part of me in self-defense, subconsciously unwilling to let it go.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc7.description: I noticed Jacob's reaction to my action and inferred that he thought I had lost my mind, which affected how I perceived his support in the moment.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc7.source_text: I felt the others glancing at me and saw Jacob’s big black eye roll down to stare at me like I’d lost my mind.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc8.description: I learned that Aro could access every secret thought and memory Edward had, including visions and family moments.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc8.source_text: Every secret thought, every strategy, every insight—everything Edward had heard in the minds around him during the last month—was now Aro’s.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc8.description: I observed that Edward physically reacted when Aro touched him as his eyes snapped shut and his shoulders hunched under the onslaught of information.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc8.source_text: His eyes snapped shut at once, and then his shoulders hunched under the onslaught of information.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc8.description: I felt my protective shield respond with visible agitation and I became more frustrated and aware of my vulnerability in front of the Volturi.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc8.source_text: I hissed with frustration, and the shield roiled with my irritation, shifting its shape and contracting around our side.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc8.description: I judged Renata as a protector rather than a warrior and I perceived her as panicky and weak despite being useful to Aro.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc8.source_text: For a moment, I examined this powerful shield that seemed so panicky and weak; though she was useful to Aro, I could tell she was no warrior. It was not her job to fight but to protect.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc9.description: I learned that Aro expressed an intense curiosity and asked to meet Renesmee directly.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc9.source_text: I heard Aro ask, 'May I meet her?'

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc9.description: I learned that Aro acknowledged that the law may not have been broken and that the original justice might no longer apply.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc9.source_text: I noticed Aro say that 'the law had not been broken' and that 'the justice we intended to deliver no longer applies.'

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc9.description: I felt hopeful and relieved when Aro suggested a compromise and said, 'We will meet in the middle.'
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc9.source_text: I heard Aro say, 'I think a compromise on this one point is certainly acceptable, under the circumstance. We will meet in the middle.'

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc9.description: I noticed that Aro took Edward's hand, maintained skin contact, and later threw an arm over Edward's shoulder, and I perceived a closer, influential connection between Aro and Edward.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc9.source_text: I watched Aro grip Edward's hand and later throw his arm over Edward's shoulder while maintaining contact with Edward's skin.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc10.description: I chose Jacob and Emmett to escort Renesmee to the summit.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc10.source_text: I heard 'Jacob? Emmett?' I asked quietly.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc10.description: I deployed my mental shield to protect my family while Renesmee was left exposed in the center.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc10.source_text: I noticed 'My shield rippled out behind me like a cape, protecting the rest of my family while Renesmee was left exposed.'

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc10.description: I trusted Edward to detect any treachery from Aro and to guide our interactions at the summit.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc10.source_text: I felt 'I trusted Edward. He would know if Aro was planning any treachery at this point.'

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc11.description: I learned that Renesmee is described as half mortal, half immortal and was conceived and carried while Bella was still human.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc11.source_text: “Half mortal, half immortal,” Aro announced to him and the rest of the guard without turning his enthralled gaze from Renesmee. “Conceived so, and carried by this newborn while she was still human.”

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc11.description: I felt Aro's voice was unexpectedly comforting at first, which momentarily affected my guard before Edward and Maggie reacted.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc11.source_text: Aro’s voice was so comforting and affectionate, it took me in for a second. And then I heard Edward’s teeth grind together and, far behind us, Maggie’s outraged hiss at the lie.

tw-book4-chapter36_Sc11.description: I realized that Aro's pleasant manner concealed motives that made me and my family distrustful and defensive.
tw-book4-chapter36_Sc11.source_text: “Of course I have no desire to harm your loved ones, precious Renesmee.”

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc1.description: I noticed Edward started backing up immediately and pulled my arm and Emmett’s.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc1.source_text: Edward started backing up immediately, pulling my arm and Emmett’s.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc1.description: I noticed Renesmee grabbed the end of Jacob’s tail and held it like a leash, forcing him to stay with us.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc1.source_text: Renesmee grabbed the end of his tail as we retreated; she held it like a leash, forcing him to stay with us.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc1.description: I realized the approaching group was close enough that the fifty yard distance could be crossed in a fraction of a second, making the threat feel immediate.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc1.source_text: Now there were only fifty yards between them and us—a distance any of us could leap in just a fraction of a second.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc2.description: I learned that Caius angrily confronted Aro about an alleged infamy and deception during the meeting.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc2.source_text: "How can you abide this infamy? Why do we stand here impotently in the face of such an outrageous crime, covered by such a ridiculous deception?" He held his arms rigidly at his sides, his hands curled into claws.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc2.description: I learned that Aro defended the claim by citing multiple witnesses and the sensation of the child's warm blood.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc2.source_text: "Because it’s all true," Aro told him calmly. "Every word of it. See how many witnesses stand ready to give evidence that they have seen this miraculous child grow and mature in just the short time they’ve known her. That they have felt the warmth of the blood that pulses in her veins." Aro’s gesture swept from Amun on one side across to Siobhan on the other.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc2.description: I learned that I possess a mental shield that can be flexed into a dome and tailored to cling to individual allies and move with them.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc2.source_text: Anxiously, I inspected my shield; it felt just as impenetrable as before. I flexed it now into a low, wide dome that arced over our company.... The shield clung to them willingly, moving as they moved.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc2.description: I changed from anger to worry about Caius’s deliberation and about the possibility that the guard might act again on some invisible signal.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc2.source_text: Caius was frowning, deep in thought. His speculative expression stoked the flames of my smoldering anger at the same time that it worried me. What if the guard acted again on some invisible signal, as they had in their march?

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc3.description: I realized that Bella learned the pack members present are not true werewolves but are described as shape-shifters.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc3.source_text: “Though the creatures think of themselves as werewolves, they are not. The more accurate name for them would be shape-shifters. The choice of a wolf form was purely chance. It could have been a bear or a hawk or a panther when the first change was made.”

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc3.description: I noticed that Bella felt mystified when Edward announced they were not werewolves and when Jacob shrugged, showing Jacob did not understand Edward either.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc3.source_text: “Not werewolves? I shot a mystified look at Jacob. He lifted his huge shoulders and let them drop—a shrug. He didn’t know what Edward was talking about, either.”

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc4.description: I learned that Irina's accusation against the Cullens was false.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc4.source_text: It was clear on her face that she knew now her accusation had been totally false.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc4.description: I learned that Irina publicly retracted her claim, took responsibility, and stated the Cullens were innocent.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc4.source_text: No, I have no complaint against the wolves, or the Cullens. You came here today to destroy an immortal child. No immortal child exists. This was my mistake, and I take full responsibility for it. But the Cullens are innocent, and you have no reason to still be here. I’m so sorry,

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc4.description: I learned that Caius produced and used a strange metal object that spewed flames to burn Irina.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc4.source_text: Caius raised his hand as she spoke, and in it was a strange metal object, carved and ornate. Caius stood alone beside the blazing remains of Irina, the metal object in his hand still throwing a thick jet of flame into the pyre.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc4.description: I learned that the Volturi guards executed the burning with sudden, precise coordination.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc4.source_text: Three of the Volturi soldiers leaped forward, and Irina was completely obscured by their gray cloaks. In the same instant, a horrible metallic screeching ripped through the clearing.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc4.description: I learned that Caius intended the burning not to punish Irina but to provoke violence between the factions.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc4.source_text: He had not wanted Irina’s complaint; he had wanted her defiance. His excuse to destroy her, to ignite the violence that filled the air like a thick, combustible mist.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc4.description: I realized that Caius valued starting a slaughter over preserving reputation, changing my understanding of his motivations.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc4.source_text: If the coming slaughter was so much more essential to Caius than an untarnished reputation.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc4.description: I understood that Caius deliberately exploited the strength of true family ties as part of his plan.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc4.source_text: In that second I understood that Caius had never underestimated the ties of a true family.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc4.description: I realized that once open fighting began at the summit there would be no way to stop the escalation.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc4.source_text: Once the fight began, there would be no way to stop it. It would only escalate until one side was entirely extinct.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc5.description: I pulled my shield even tighter against the sparks of my friends, peeling it back carefully from Kate while trying to keep it around Garrett.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc5.source_text: Desperately, but with all the delicacy I could manage, I pulled my shield even tighter against the sparks of my friends, peeling it back carefully from Kate while trying to keep it around Garrett, making it a thin skin between them.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc5.description: I saw Edward cry out to stop Tanya and I watched him jump to grab her arm as she lurched toward Caius.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc5.source_text: "Stop them!" Edward cried out, jumping to grab Tanya’s arm as she lurched forward toward the smiling Caius with a maddened cry of pure rage.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc5.description: I saw Kate shock Rosalie so violently that she crumpled and I saw Emmett stagger after being shocked before Garrett threw himself at Kate and bound her arms.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc5.source_text: Rosalie was closest to her, but before Rose could clinch her in a headlock, Kate shocked her so violently that Rose crumpled to the ground. Emmett caught Kate’s arm and threw her down, then staggered back, his knees giving out. Garrett flung himself at her, knocking her to the ground again. He bound his arms around hers, locking his hands around his own wrists. I saw his body spasm as she shocked him.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc5.description: I heard Tanya hiss that she wanted her sight back and I observed her fall into grief as Carlisle reasoned with her.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc5.source_text: "Give me my sight back," Tanya hissed.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc5.description: I felt the situation shift from uncontrollable panic to tense containment once Garrett held Kate and Carlisle and Garrett began consoling the sisters.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc5.source_text: And then Garrett was in command of himself again, holding Kate to the snow. Carlisle and Garrett continued to console the sisters with words too urgent to sound like comfort.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc6.description: I learned that Aro had felt Kate's potency through Edward's memories.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc6.source_text: He knew what Kate could do. He had felt her potency through Edward’s memories.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc6.description: I learned that my shield had grown in strength and subtlety far beyond what Edward knew me to be capable of.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc6.source_text: Did he understand what was happening now—did he see that my shield had grown in strength and subtlety far beyond what Edward knew me to be capable of?

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc6.description: I felt pity for the mass of strangers the Volturi had brought to watch us die and I believed the Volturi would slaughter their witnesses after using them.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc6.source_text: I felt a strange, sudden pity for the mass of the strangers the Volturi had brought to watch us die. After they finished with us, surely they would slaughter their witnesses for that purpose.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc6.description: I realized that Aro's need for an audience had backfired and I noticed his face betray a flash of vexation.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc6.source_text: Aro glanced back swiftly while I watched, his face betraying him with one flash of vexation. His need for an audience had backfired badly.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc6.description: I heard Aro state that Irina had been punished for bearing false witness as the Volturi's official excuse.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc6.source_text: Aro touched Caius’s shoulder lightly. “Irina has been punished for bearing false witness against this child.” So that was to be their excuse.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc7.description: I learned that Aro questioned Amun about his observations and that Amun reported that 'That the child is his biologically. That she grows. That she learns.'
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc7.source_text: "That the child is his biologically. That she grows. That she learns."

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc7.description: I became more convinced that Aro's genial manner concealed a threat after seeing Amun's tight reaction and the tense exchange.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc7.source_text: Amun’s lips were a tight line as he inclined his head once, acknowledging the barely concealed threat.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc7.description: I noticed Edward's protectiveness and controlled fury when he hissed and then wrapped a restraining hand around my wrist.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc7.source_text:
Edward hissed, his hands balling up in fists so tight it looked like the bones in his knuckles would split through his diamond-hard skin.

Edward stepped back and wrapped a restraining hand around my wrist.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc7.description: I learned that Amun and Kebi left the meadow quickly after testifying and that they would run a long distance.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc7.source_text: the two of them ran quickly to the southern edge of the meadow and disappeared into the trees. I knew they wouldn’t stop running for a very long time.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc8.description: I learned that Aro considers Renesmee's unknown potential a possible danger to the vampire world.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc8.source_text: This amazing child… if we could but know her potential—know with absolute certainty that she could always remain shrouded within the obscurity that protects us. But we know nothing of what she will become!

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc8.description: I became more protective and angrier, and I reinforced my shield to ensure everyone was guarded against Aro's threats.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc8.source_text: I fought back the rage that tried to claw its way up my throat and snarl out my defiance. I hurled the fury into my shield, thickening it, making sure everyone was protected.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc8.description: I regarded Aro and the Volturi as a more immediate threat after he framed the unknown as a vulnerability that might justify action against Renesmee.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc8.source_text: Only the known is safe. Only the known is tolerable. The unknown is… a vulnerability.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc9.description: I learned that Bella Swan was present at the confrontation among the listed attendees.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc9.source_text: Characters present: Garrett, Kate, Aro, Makenna, Charles, Eleazar, Bella Swan, Carlisle

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc9.description: I noticed that Garrett framed his defense around Carlisle and his family, which implies Bella as part of the group he is defending.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc9.source_text: He gestured toward Carlisle and Tanya.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc9.description: I began to feel that Bella's safety and the Cullen way of life were central to the dispute rather than only the child's fate.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc9.source_text: The Volturi come to erase what they perceive as the competition.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc10.description: I noticed Bella Swan was listed among the present characters at the hearing.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc10.source_text: I quote: "Characters present: Aro, Makenna, Charles, Marcus, Caius, Renata, Felix, Demetri, Bella Swan, Garrett"

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc10.description: I became more worried for Bella's safety as the council debated the family's fate and many witnesses prioritized protecting their world.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc10.source_text: I quote: "Let us ask our witnesses," Aro suggested. I quote: "We are outnumbered, dearest ones," he said. I quote: "No, master," they whispered in unison. I quote: "Is the protection of our world worth perhaps the loss of some of our number?" I quote: "Yes," they breathed.

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc11.description: I arranged for Renesmee to escape with Jacob and gave explicit instructions about waiting for distraction and using Renesmee's capacity to lift them into the air.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc11.source_text: "Wait until they’re totally distracted, then run with her. Get as far from this place as you possibly can. When you’ve gone as far as you can on foot, she has what you need to get you in the air."

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc11.description: I acknowledged Jacob as the only one I could trust with Renesmee and affirmed my love and lifelong bond by calling him my best man.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc11.source_text: "You’re the only one we could ever trust her with," I murmured. "I love you, too, Jake. You’ll always be my best man."

tw-book4-chapter37_Sc11.description: I accepted that I knew only my own fate while maintaining hope for others and I included Edward unequivocally in that shared fate as my other half.
tw-book4-chapter37_Sc11.source_text: "There is absolutely hope," I murmured back. "I only know my own fate." "We were just halves of the whole."

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc1.description: I learned that my shield can repel direct psychic assaults and atmospheric hazes aimed at Carlisle and those behind it.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc1.source_text: I read that when Edward said Jane's name, a dozen pointed attacks hit the shield and it did not seem like Jane had been able to pierce it and I read that a strange clear haze from Alec hit the shield and could not get through.

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc1.description: I realized that I could realistically hold the protective screen and that my holding it would substantially equalize our odds against the Volturi.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc1.source_text: I read that the narrator thought, 'And then I knew that I could do this' and that holding the shield put them 'on more than equal footing with the Volturi.'

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc1.description: I recognized that Zafrina and Benjamin would actively support and protect me with their powers and that allies pledged to defend me explicitly.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc1.source_text: I read that Zafrina nodded solemnly and promised, 'No one will touch this young one' and that Benjamin cheered, 'Well done, Bella!'

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc2.description: I heard Aro offer the Volturi's welcome to many of us and explicitly list Bella among possible recruits.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc2.source_text:
It will be a regrettable waste to our kind to lose any of you.
But you especially, young Edward, and your newborn mate. The Volturi would be glad
to welcome many of you into our ranks. Bella, Benjamin, Zafrina, Kate. There are many
choices before you. Consider them.

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc2.description: I felt Chelsea's attempt to persuade us fail against my shield.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc2.source_text: Chelsea’s attempt to sway us fluttered impotently against my shield.

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc2.description: I realized that Aro was desperate to keep Edward and me and that he would not win if I lived.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc2.source_text:
I knew he was desperate to keep Edward and me, to imprison us the way he had hoped
to enslave Alice. But this fight was too big. He would not win if I lived.

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc2.description: I felt fierce gladness that my power made me an unavoidable threat to Aro's plans.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc2.source_text: I was fiercely glad to be so powerful that I left him no way not to kill me.

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc2.description: I experienced a sharp pressure against my shield from Jane's attack that ceased when Edward intervened and asked Aro to stop.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc2.source_text: Aro, would you ask Jane to stop attacking my wife?" Edward asked courteously. "The pressure disappeared.

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc2.description: I noticed Edward's expression of triumph that I found both beautiful and terrifying in the moment he prepared his gambit.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc2.source_text: His face glowed with an expression of triumph that I didn’t understand—it was the expression an angel of destruction might wear while the world burned.

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc4.description: I learned Aro judged us as no danger and compared the half-vampire children to vampires.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc4.source_text: "Brother," he said softly to Caius. "There appears to be no danger. This is an unusual development, but I see no threat. These half-vampire children are much like us, it appears."

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc4.description: I learned Aro examined Carlisle and Edward before focusing his attention on me.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc4.source_text: "Aro stared at Carlisle, and then Edward, and at last his eyes rested on me."

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc4.description: I felt relieved when Aro declared there was no danger yet I remained skeptical of his benign outward expression.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc4.source_text: "His face was as benign as ever, but unlike before, I sensed a strange blankness behind the façade."

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc4.description: I viewed Caius as enraged and uncompromising while I perceived Aro as outwardly warm but inscrutable.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc4.source_text: "Caius growled. 'We take care of the aberration here, and then follow it south,' he urged Aro."

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc5.description: I learned that Aro and the Volturi withdrew peacefully after an exchange with Carlisle, ending the immediate threat.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc5.source_text: "We watched in silence as the last four Volturi disappeared into the trees."

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc5.description: I learned that Nessie was safe, healthy, and would remain with us.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc5.source_text:
"Nessie, Nessie, Nessie," I crooned.

"I get to stay with you?" Nessie demanded.

"Forever," I promised her.

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc5.description: I realized that my sense of overwhelming happiness and permanence with my family had shifted to something almost unbearably joyful.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc5.source_text: Happiness expanded like an explosion inside me—so extreme, so violent that I wasn’t sure I’d survive it.

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc5.description: I felt my bond with Edward reaffirmed as he immediately wrapped his arms around Nessie and me and echoed our promise of forever.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc5.source_text:
"Edward’s arms were around us in the same second.

"Forever," Edward echoed in my ear."

tw-book4-chapter38_Sc5.description: I noticed a warm, familiar rapport with Jacob as he laughed and playfully poked the back of my head with his nose after returning Nessie.
tw-book4-chapter38_Sc5.source_text:
"I half-climbed the giant russet wolf to rip my daughter off his back and then crushed her to my chest.

Jacob laughed his big, barky laugh and poked the back of my head with his nose."

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc1.description: I agreed to bring my child to Zafrina after she insisted on seeing the child.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc1.source_text: "You must bring the child to see me," Zafrina had insisted. "Promise me, young one."

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc1.description: I noticed Nessie pressed her hand to my neck in a pleading gesture.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc1.source_text: Nessie had pressed her hand to my neck, pleading as well.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc1.description: I expect Nessie to form a friendship with Zafrina after the woman's warm declaration.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc1.source_text: "We shall be great friends, my Nessie," the wild woman had declared before leaving with her sisters.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc3.description: I learned that Alice's defection was a deliberate ruse because Edward had to believe she had abandoned us.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc3.source_text: that her defection was only a ruse because Edward had to believe that she’d abandoned us,

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc3.description: I became irritated and conflicted because I loved Alice insanely but felt hurt by her deception.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc3.source_text: I loved her insanely, of course. I was beginning to feel pretty irritated with her.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc3.description: I forgave Alice and reconnected with her emotionally after she explained the necessity of the ruse.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc3.source_text: I missed you like crazy, Alice. Don't do that to me again.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward declared my shield was responsible for making the Volturi run away.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc4.source_text: I read 'Edward went back to analyzing every shift of intention and control that had happened in the meadow today, declaring that it was my shield that had made the Volturi run away with their tails between their legs.'

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc4.description: I felt my sense of self shift because I noticed everyone looking at me with impressed stares and I became uncomfortable with that attention.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc4.source_text: I read 'The way everyone looked at me made me uncomfortable. Even Edward. It was like I had grown a hundred feet during the course of the morning.'

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc4.description: I realized that I would always be just Bella to Jacob and that realization brought me relief.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc4.source_text: I read 'I would always be just Bella to him, and that was a relief.'

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc5.description: I wanted some peace, some normality and I wanted Nessie in her own bed and my home around me.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc5.source_text: I wanted some peace, some normality. I wanted Nessie in her own bed; I wanted the walls of my own little home around me.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc5.description: I felt oddly tired and I no longer wanted to be under a deadline but instead wanted to take my time.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc5.source_text: I felt oddly tired. Not sleepy, of course, but just like the day had been long enough.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc5.description: I thanked Jacob and I touched his cheek to show I appreciated his help.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc5.source_text: I touched his cheek. “Thank you, Jacob.”

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc5.description: I sensed I could read Edward's mind for a moment and I saw that he felt the same need for peace.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc5.source_text: I looked at Edward and felt for a moment like I could read his mind. I could see he felt exactly the same way. Ready for some peace.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc5.description: I promised myself I would take over the working relationship with J. Jenks to spare Jasper from causing another heart attack.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc5.source_text: I frowned, promising myself that I would take over that working relationship from now on and spare J the heart attack that was surely on the way.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc6.description: I realized that I feel an overwhelming certainty and happiness about being with Edward forever.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc6.source_text: But most significant in this tidal wave of happiness was the surest fact of all: I was with Edward. Forever.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc6.description: I learned that I expected my father's fear to be replaced by joy and that I imagined Sue with Charlie so my father would not be alone.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc6.source_text: Tomorrow I would go see my father; he would see that the fear in my eyes had been replaced with joy, and he would be happy, too. Suddenly, I was sure that I wouldn’t find him there alone. I hadn’t been as observant as I might have been in the last few weeks, but in this moment it was like I’d known all along. Sue would be with Charlie—the werewolves’ mom with the vampire’s dad—and he wouldn’t be alone anymore.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc7.description: I carried Nessie to her bed and tucked her in and I noticed that she smiled as she slept.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc7.source_text: We carried Nessie to her bed and gently tucked her in. She smiled as she slept.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc7.description: I removed Aro's gift from around my neck and I left it in Nessie's room for her to play with.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc7.source_text: I took Aro’s gift from around my neck and tossed it lightly into the corner of her room. She could play with it if she wished; she liked sparkly things.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc7.description: I realized that pulling away from Edward was a first for me and I recognized that my behavior had changed in that moment.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc7.source_text: As a general rule, I didn’t pull away. Okay, it was more than a general rule. This was a first.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc7.description: I understood that part of my shield fights separation and I recognized the shield's automatic instinct to preserve self above all else.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc7.source_text: I hadn’t done very well with this when Zafrina had tried to teach me before, but I knew my shield better now. I understood the part that fought against separation from me, the automatic instinct to preserve self above all else.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc7.description: I had to strain to push my shield entirely away from me and I experienced the intense focus that required.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc7.source_text: I had to strain to push it entirely away from me; it took all of my focus.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc7.description: I dredged up specific memories I had saved for this moment and I tried to let them flood my mind and his as well.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc7.source_text: I knew it was working then, so I concentrated even harder, dredging up the specific memories I’d saved for this moment, letting them flood my mind, and hopefully his as well.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc7.description: I recalled both dim human memories and sharp immortal memories and I attempted to use them to reach Edward.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc7.source_text: Some of the memories were not clear—dim human memories, seen through weak eyes and heard through weak ears: the first time I’d seen his face… the way it felt when he’d held me in the meadow… the sound of his voice through the darkness of my faltering consciousness when he’d saved me from James… his face as he waited under a canopy of flowers to marry me… every precious moment from the island… his cold hands touching our baby through my skin… And the sharp memories, perfectly recalled: his face when I’d opened my eyes to my new life, to the endless dawn of immortality… that first kiss… that first night…

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc7.description: I lost my concentration when Edward's sudden fierce kiss interrupted my attempt to expose my memories.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc7.source_text: His lips, suddenly fierce against mine, broke my concentration.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc8.description: I felt the mental shield snap back and protect my thoughts when I lost my grip.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc8.source_text: With a gasp, I lost my grip on the struggling weight I was holding away from myself. It snapped back like stressed elastic, protecting my thoughts once again.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc8.description: I learned that Zafrina suggested the shield exercise and that we had practiced it a few times.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc8.source_text: Zafrina’s idea. We practiced with it a few times.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc8.description: I declared that no one had ever loved anyone as much as I love Edward.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc8.source_text: No one’s ever loved anyone as much as I love you.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc8.description: I realized that I cannot keep the shield up if I become even the slightest bit distracted.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc8.source_text: “I can’t keep it up if I’m even the slightest bit distracted,” I warned him.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc8.description: I could lift the shield out of my mind and recall the crystal-clear memory of the first night of my new life.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc8.source_text: I pressed my hands to his face again, hefted the shield right out of my mind, and then started in where I’d left off—with the crystal-clear memory of the first night of my new life… lingering on the details.

tw-book4-chapter39_Sc8.description: I accepted Edward’s promise and we continued blissfully into a small, perfect piece of our forever together.
tw-book4-chapter39_Sc8.source_text: And then we continued blissfully into this small but perfect piece of our forever.

tw-book4-chapter4_Sc1.description: I learned that Alice flawlessly planned the wedding, making the reception flow smoothly.
tw-book4-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: The wedding flowed into the reception party smoothly—proof of Alice’s flawless planning.

tw-book4-chapter4_Sc1.description: I learned that the ceremony was timed to end at sunset to create a twilight setting.
tw-book4-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: It was just twilight over the river; the ceremony had lasted exactly the right amount of time, allowing the sun to set behind the trees.

tw-book4-chapter4_Sc1.description: I felt proud and elated when Edward introduced me as his wife for the first time.
tw-book4-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: “Let me introduce you to my wife.”

tw-book4-chapter4_Sc1.description: I felt welcomed by the Denali clan after they introduced themselves and apologized for earlier behavior.
I learned that the reception kept wedding traditions such as the cake cutting and flashbulb photos.
tw-book4-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: All the standard traditions were kept. I was blinded by flashbulbs as we held the knife over a spectacular cake—too grand, I thought, for our relatively intimate group of friends and family.

tw-book4-chapter4_Sc1.description: I felt overwhelmed by the Denali vampires' beauty and my nervousness at meeting them.
tw-book4-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: And they were all four so beautiful that it made my stomach hurt.

tw-book4-chapter4_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob physically grabbed and shook my arms during the reception.
tw-book4-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "His enormous hands gripped the tops of my arms, wrapping all the way around, fingers overlapping."

tw-book4-chapter4_Sc3.description: I decided to hide the incident and not let it ruin the wedding night.
tw-book4-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "I would put this away, shove it in a drawer and lock it up to deal with later."

tw-book4-chapter4_Sc3.description: I reinforced that only my relationship with Edward matters and I asked him to promise to let Jacob go for the night.
tw-book4-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "You and me. That's the only thing that matters. The only thing you're allowed to think about now."

tw-book4-chapter4_Sc3.description: I affirmed that I was not afraid and I expressed my love to Edward.
tw-book4-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "By the way, I love you."

tw-book4-chapter4_Sc4.description: I said goodbye to my mother and expressed my love before leaving.
tw-book4-chapter4_Sc4.source_text: "Goodbye, Mom. I love you," I said again, my throat thick.

tw-book4-chapter4_Sc4.description: I hugged my father, told him I loved him forever, and promised to call soon.
tw-book4-chapter4_Sc4.source_text: "I love you forever, Dad," I told him. "Call me," he said. "Soon," I promised...

tw-book4-chapter4_Sc4.description: I decided that my parents could not be allowed to see me again because I would be too different and dangerous.
tw-book4-chapter4_Sc4.source_text: My father and my mother could not be allowed to see me again; I would be too different, and much, much too dangerous.

tw-book4-chapter4_Sc4.description: I knew I was ready to leave and felt certain about that readiness.
tw-book4-chapter4_Sc4.source_text: "Are you ready?" he asked. "I am," I said, and I knew that it was true.

tw-book4-chapter4_Sc4.description: I saw many different kinds of love among my families and felt hopeful about that harmony.
tw-book4-chapter4_Sc4.source_text: So many different kinds of love, harmonious in this one moment. It seemed a very hopeful picture to me.

tw-book4-chapter5_Sc2.description: I experienced a panic attack after the shower, with accelerated breathing and trembling hands.
tw-book4-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: My breathing started to accelerate again and my hands trembled—so much for the calming effects of the shower.

tw-book4-chapter5_Sc2.description: I resisted wearing Alice's packed lingerie and felt unready to face Edward in French lingerie.
tw-book4-chapter5_Sc2.source_text:
I didn’t even want to think about the things Alice had packed for me.
I was afraid to walk out of this room and face the unknown. Especially in French lingerie.

tw-book4-chapter5_Sc2.description: I became certain that Edward loved me unconditionally and that my trust in him made facing my fear possible.
tw-book4-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: If it weren’t Edward out there, if I didn’t know in every cell of my body that he loved me as much as I loved him—unconditionally and irrevocably and, to be honest, irrationally—I’d never be able to get up off this floor.

tw-book4-chapter5_Sc2.description: I walked into the warm, moonlit water, removed my towel without hesitation, and joined Edward side by side.
tw-book4-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: I slipped the towel off without hesitation, leaving it on the tree with his clothes, and walked out into the white light; it made me pale as the snowy sand, too.

tw-book4-chapter5_Sc2.description: I nodded solemnly and agreed to tell Edward at once if he ever did something that hurt me.
tw-book4-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: I nodded solemnly, keeping my eyes on his.

tw-book4-chapter5_Sc2.description: I woke in the bright room with sunlight on my back, comfortable and unwilling to disturb the perfect feeling of lying against him.
tw-book4-chapter5_Sc2.source_text:
The sun, hot on the bare skin of my back, woke me in the morning.
I didn’t open my eyes. I was too happy to change anything, no matter how small.

tw-book4-chapter5_Sc3.description: I felt physical soreness after our encounter but I judged it as mild and comparable to ordinary muscle soreness.
tw-book4-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "I was feeling more of the soreness now, but it wasn’t that bad. Sort of like the day after lifting weights."

tw-book4-chapter5_Sc3.description: I realized that I considered that experience more wonderful and perfect than any of my previous happiest memories.
tw-book4-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "I was perfectly happy. Totally and completely blissed out... It was like that for me."

tw-book4-chapter5_Sc3.description: I asserted that I am not pretending for Edward's sake and I insisted that my happiness is genuine and not meant to ease his guilt.
tw-book4-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "I am not pretending anything for your sake, okay?... I’ve never been so happy in all my life... So just deal with it."

tw-book4-chapter5_Sc3.description: I told Edward that his unhappiness was the only thing wrong and I asked him to stop being unhappy so I could remain happy.
tw-book4-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "Then don’t you be unhappy. That’s the only thing that’s wrong here."

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc1.description: I stated that I want to go to college and that I was offering to wait and remain human for a while.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: I want to go to college.

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc1.description: I decided to try compromise by proposing a deal with Edward instead of demanding immediate decisions.
I realized that Edward was intentionally keeping me busy and distracted to avoid talking about sex and risky choices.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: I knew what was going on.

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc2.description: I learned that Bella is having recurring, unusually vivid dreams that feel very real and are often colorful and sensory.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: "It’s all so bright and real. Usually, when I’m dreaming, I know that I am. With these, I don’t know I’m asleep. It makes them scarier."

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc2.description: I learned that Bella’s dreams have included both a vampire child and a human boy whom she feels compelled to protect.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: "He wasn’t the same boy as that first dream—the vampire child with the bloodred eyes who sat on a pile of dead people I loved. This boy I’d dreamed of four times in the last week was definitely human; his cheeks were flushed and his wide eyes were a soft green."

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc2.description: I learned that Bella deliberately withholds full details of one nightmare because she feels that particular horror is private.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: "I wasn’t sure why, but I didn’t want to tell him about the child in my recurring nightmare; there was something private about that particular horror. So, instead of giving him the full description, I gave him just one element."

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc2.description: I noticed that Bella believes she will fail to protect the boy despite feeling compelled to try, and that belief contributes to her fear.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: "At the same time, I knew that I would fail."

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc2.description: I felt Bella wanted the dream to be real and that waking from it produced overwhelming grief and urgent need for comfort.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: "I wanted it to be real." and "It was a good dream."

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc2.description: I sensed that Bella is emotionally dependent on Edward for comfort and reassurance when she is frightened or grieving.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: "He hugged me tighter. 'They aren’t going to bother us anymore. You’ll be immortal soon, and they’ll have no reason.'"

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc3.description: I learned that I cooked breakfast this morning and ate eggs sunny-side up.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: I cooked this morning, frying up some eggs—too hungry to do anything more elaborate.

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc3.description: I learned that we can stay a few more weeks before leaving and that Dartmouth is the planned college.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: “We’re fine on time. A few more weeks, if you want. And then we can visit Charlie before we go to New Hampshire.”

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward says we already have a house in Dartmouth.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: “Well, we sort of already have a house there. You know, just in case.”

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc3.description: I realized that I enjoy being human more than I expected and that I want more time being human with Edward.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: “I really do want a little more time being human.”

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc3.description: I felt tempted to postpone my previous plans because being human with Edward made the choice trickier.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: “Eighteen or nineteen, nineteen or twenty… Did it really matter? I wouldn’t change so much in a year. And being human with Edward… The choice got trickier every day.”

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc3.description: I noticed that I and Edward are more intimate and comfortable after the practice, reducing my fear of his anger.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc3.source_text:
“I’m not angry.”
“I’m not angry.”
“Why not?”
“Well . . .” He paused. “I didn’t hurt you, for one thing. It was easier this time, to control myself, to channel the excesses.”

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc3.description: I learned that I feel guilty about seducing Edward even though he teases me about it.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc3.source_text:
“So you seduced your all-too-willing husband. That’s not a capital offense.”
“I feel guilty,” I muttered.

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc3.description: I learned that I lack equilibrium after the practice and that Edward steadies and worries about me.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc3.source_text:
“If I don’t have a better sense of equilibrium in my next life, I’m demanding a refund.”
“Are you all right?”

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward had already mangled the headboard in the other room beyond repair.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: I don’t know.… I’ve already mangled the headboard in the other room beyond repair—maybe if we limit the destruction to one area of the house, Esme might invite us back someday.

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc4.description: I noticed Gustavo and Kaure moved quietly through the house while I waited.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: Gustavo and Kaure moved quietly through the house while I waited impatiently for them to finish and tried to pay attention to the happily-ever-after on the screen.

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc4.description: I heard Edward answer Gustavo in flowing Portuguese before Gustavo left.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: Edward sat up, keeping me cradled against him, and answered Gustavo in flowing Portuguese.

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc4.description: I realized Edward preferred to wait until we were alone to limit furniture destruction so as not to scare others.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: Maybe it would be more polite to wait until we’re alone. You may not notice me tearing the furniture apart, but it would probably scare them.

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc4.description: I felt my pulse racing and recognized that my attraction and excitement around Edward had intensified.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: “It would only be a matter of time,” I agreed casually, but my pulse was racing in my veins.

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward knew my facial expressions so well that he did not need to read my mind to understand me.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: He knew my face so well, it didn’t matter that he couldn’t read my mind.

tw-book4-chapter6_Sc4.description: I felt our intimacy deepen when Edward swept me up and kissed me, carrying me with inhuman speed to the blue room.
tw-book4-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: But I didn’t finish. He’d already swept me up into his arms, and his lips silenced mine as he carried me with inhuman speed to the blue room.

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward went to the mainland to hunt and intended to return soon.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: I’m hoping you won’t wake and notice my absence, but, if you should, I’ll be back very soon. I’ve just gone to the mainland to hunt. Go back to sleep and I’ll be here when you wake again. I love you.

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc1.description: I found a folded note addressed to Mrs. Cullen explaining his absence.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: The outside of the note was addressed to Mrs. Cullen.

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc1.description: I experienced a vivid nightmare of the Volturi approaching and felt panic turn into bloodlust within the dream.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: The line of black advanced on me through the shroud-like mist. The panic changed to bloodlust as I crouched forward, a smile on my face, and a growl ripped through my bared teeth.

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc1.description: I discovered that I got food poisoning after eating fried chicken that tasted off.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: I made some chicken last night. It tasted off, so I threw it out. But I ate a few bites first. "Damn rancid chicken," I moaned.

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc1.description: I felt that the house seemed big and empty without Edward and that our time there felt somehow outside of normal time.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: It felt so big and empty without Edward there. Different. We seemed to exist outside of time here, just drifting along in a perfect state.

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc1.description: I noticed that Edward is attentive and caring because he soothed me, wiped my forehead, held my hair while I was sick, watched my temperature, and tended to my needs.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: "I’m sorry," Edward was murmuring as he wiped a wintry hand across my clammy forehead. He held my hair again. He put a cold hand on my forehead. He made me wait an hour and keep down a big glass of water before he fried me some eggs.

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc2.description: I discovered a small, rock-hard bump on my stomach that suggested I might be pregnant.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc2.source_text: I yanked the blue fabric out of the way and stared at my stomach. I ran my fingers over the subtle bulge, surprised by how rock hard it felt under my skin.

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc2.description: I felt a soft little nudge bump my hand from inside my body that I interpreted as fetal movement.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc2.source_text: a soft little nudge bumped my hand— from inside my body.

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc2.description: I reconsidered the assumption that vampires could not father children and began to consider that Edward might be capable of fathering my child.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc2.source_text: Vampires couldn’t have children. The only person I’d ever had sex with was a vampire, for crying out loud.

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.description: I learned that Carlisle believes I am pregnant.
I learned that Edward called the airport and arranged that we would go home immediately.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: I heard "The airport. We're going home."

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward spent more than an hour on the phone speaking in another language and arguing while packing.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: I noticed "Edward was on the phone for more than an hour without a break... he wasn’t speaking English. It sounded like he was arguing; he spoke through his teeth a lot."

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.description: I realized that I wanted the baby intensely and that my feelings about motherhood had changed from indifferent to essential.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: I remembered "I wanted him like I wanted air to breathe."

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.description: I became afraid that Edward might want to harm or remove the baby after he referred to it as "that thing."
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: I heard "We’re going to get that thing out before it can hurt any part of you."

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.description: I felt my trust in Edward wobble because his cold, controlled behavior and his words about removing the baby frightened me.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: I observed "His voice was too cold, too careful. His face matched his voice, empty and hard."

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc4.description: I learned that a woman touched my stomach and pronounced a single Portuguese word implying death.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc4.source_text:
In answer, she walked slowly forward until she was close enough to lay her small hand on top of mine, over my stomach. She spoke one word in Portuguese.

“Morte,” she sighed quietly.

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc4.description: I realized that I could no longer discount legends because my life was surrounded by them and they proved true.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: My life was circled by legend on every side. They were all true.

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc4.description: I reached out to Rosalie for urgent help by calling her on Edward’s phone, showing reliance on her.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: “Rosalie?” I whispered. “It’s Bella. Please. You have to help me.”

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward Cullen gave me a ride to the house.
I became more fearful about being alone with Billy and therefore stayed in the room to watch him.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: I had a lot of homework that was going undone, but I was afraid to leave Billy alone with Charlie.

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc1.description: I felt relieved and slept better after Charlie offered to stay home and I sensed the situation had calmed.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: I slept better that night, too tired to dream again.

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc1.description: I noticed that Jacob was protective of both his father and me and that he reacted strongly when teased about me.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: I watched anxiously as Charlie and Jacob helped Billy out of the car and into his wheelchair. Jacob scowled and ducked his head while I fought back a surge of remorse.

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc2.description: I decided to forget the tense evening with Billy and Jacob.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: I decided to forget it completely.

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc2.description: I hurried so I would be ready to go the second Charlie left.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: I hurried so I would be ready to go the second Charlie left.

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc2.description: I refused to be convinced to fear Edward despite acknowledging potential danger.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: I refused to be convinced to fear him, no matter how real the danger might be.

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc2.description: I felt that Edward was perfect and that there was nothing about him that could be improved upon.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: There was nothing about him that could be improved upon.

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc3.description: I learned that the meadow was small, perfectly round, and filled with wildflowers of violet, yellow, and soft white.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: The meadow was small, perfectly round, and filled with wildflowers — violet, yellow, and soft white.

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc3.description: I learned that I could hear the bubbling music of a nearby stream while standing in the meadow.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: Somewhere nearby, I could hear the bubbling music of a stream.

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc3.description: I felt sudden alarm when I realized Edward was not where I thought he'd be and I spun around searching for him.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: I halfway turned, wanting to share this with him, but he wasn't behind me where I thought he'd be. I spun around, searching for him with sudden alarm.

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc3.description: I realized that Edward watched me from the dense shade with cautious, wary eyes, which updated my sense of his reluctance and guardedness around the sun.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: Finally I spotted him, still under the dense shade of the canopy at the edge of the hollow, watching me with cautious eyes.

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward held up a hand in warning and that he later stepped out into the bright glow of the midday sun.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: He held up a hand in warning, and I hesitated, rocking back onto my heels. Edward seemed to take a deep breath, and then he stepped out into the bright glow of the midday sun.

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: I noticed that he could drive very well and that he sang along to an oldies station, knowing every line.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: He could drive well, when he kept the speed reasonable, I had to admit. ... He had turned the radio to an oldies station, and he sang along with a song I'd never heard. He knew every line.

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: I learned that he was born in Chicago in 1901 and that Carlisle found him in a hospital in the summer of 1918 when he was seventeen and dying of the Spanish influenza.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: "I was born in Chicago in 1901." ... "Carlisle found me in a hospital in the summer of 1918. I was seventeen, and dying of the Spanish influenza."

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: I heard that his parents had already died from the disease and that Carlisle chose him because he would go unnoticed in the chaos of the epidemic.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: "Your parents?" ... "They had already died from the disease. I was alone. That was why he chose me. In all the chaos of the epidemic, no one would ever realize I was gone."

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: I came to see Carlisle as the most humane and compassionate of their kind because of the way Edward described him and his actions.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: "But Carlisle has always been the most humane, the most compassionate of us… I don't think you could find his equal throughout all of history."

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: I discovered that Rosalie was brought to Carlisle first for Edward's family, that she later found Emmett after carrying him more than a hundred miles following a bear attack, and that they sometimes live separately as a married couple.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: "Carlisle brought Rosalie to our family next. ... It was only two years later that she found Emmett. She was hunting — we were in Appalachia at the time — and found a bear about to finish him off. She carried him back to Carlisle, more than a hundred miles ... Sometimes they live separately from us, as a married couple."

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: I learned that Alice and Jasper possess rare gifts, with Alice seeing possible future events in a subjective way and Jasper having wandered depressed before Alice found him.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: "Alice and Jasper are two very rare creatures. ... Jasper belonged to another… family, a very different kind of family. He became depressed, and he wandered on his own. Alice found him. ... She sees things — things that might happen, things that are coming. But it's very subjective. The future isn't set in stone."

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: I felt reassured by his unclouded smile when I asked about his age and I became more willing to hear the full story after that reaction.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: "Does it matter much?" His smile, to my relief, remained unclouded. ... "Try me," I finally said.

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc2.description: I feared my father discovering Edward's presence and took actions to hide him in my room.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "Should your father know I'm here?" he asked.

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc2.description: I noticed physical signs of anxiety when my hand shook and the milk trembled as I set down my glass.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "As I set the glass down, I noticed the milk trembling and realized my hand was shaking."

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc2.description: I asked for a minute to be human, showing that I wanted to experience normalcy despite the surreal situation.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "Can I have a minute to be human?" I asked.

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc2.description: I trusted Edward to wait and to be gentle as he picked me up and sat me beside him on the bed.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "He leaned forward and reached out with his long arms to pick me up, gripping the tops of my arms like I was a toddler. He sat me on the bed beside him."

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward watched me sleep the first night and that I murmured his name in my sleep.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: I heard "That was the first night I came here... as you were sleeping, you said my name. You spoke so clearly... you rolled over restlessly and mumbled my name once more."

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: I changed my belief about how dangerous being with Edward is after he told me that I risk my life every second I spend with him.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: I heard "You only have to risk your life every second you spend with me... You only have to turn your back on nature, on humanity… what's that worth?"

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: I realized that Edward finds me uniquely attractive and that no one, not even Rosalie, can compete with the attraction he has for me.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: I heard "She could never have one tenth, no, one hundredth of the attraction you hold for me."

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward planned to leave and return around dusk.
I learned that Billy brought Harry Clearwater's homemade fish fry for Charlie and suggested putting it in the fridge.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: "It's some of Harry Clearwater's homemade fish fry — Charlie's favorite. The fridge keeps it drier."

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc1.description: I felt relieved that Charlie wasn't home when I saw Billy and Jacob arrive.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: I felt weak with relief that Charlie wasn't home yet.

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc1.description: I recognized Edward's protectiveness and affection when he smiled the crooked smile that I loved and kissed me before leaving.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: He smiled the crooked smile that I loved. "I'll be back soon," he promised. His eyes flickered back to the porch, and then he leaned in to swiftly kiss me just under the edge of my jaw.

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: I learned that I have a date with Edward Cullen tonight and that he wanted to introduce me to his parents.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: "Well, I sort of have a date with Edward Cullen tonight, and he wanted to introduce me to his parents…Dad?"

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: I learned that I am expected to watch or play baseball with Edward's family.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: "We're going to play baseball with his family."

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: I realized that my father Charlie is protective and initially disapproving about my going out with Edward, worrying that Edward is too old for me.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: "He's too old for you," he ranted.

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: I felt reassured about Edward's intentions after hearing the sincerity in his promise that I would be safe.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: "She'll be safe with me, I promise, sir."

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: I felt panic about the idea that I might have to run with the Cullens and reacted physically before Edward calmed me.
I continued to view Edward as beautiful and almost godlike in my thoughts.

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward ended our flight when I felt dizzy and said, "It's over, Bella."
I learned that Edward admitted his existence put me at risk and that he sometimes hated himself for that.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "My very existence puts you at risk. Sometimes I truly hate myself."

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: I realized that Edward's black moods were not anger directed at me but guilt and self-blame about endangering me.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "I infuriate myself. The way I can't seem to keep from putting you in danger."

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: I felt our relationship deepen when Edward said, "I love you," and kissed me softly for the first time in so many words.

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc4.description: I heard that Esme had asked whether "they" were thirsty, implying a potential threat.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: "Whether they were thirsty," he muttered unwillingly.

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc4.description: I became more afraid because the family scanned the dark forest and reacted to sounds I could not hear.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: Carlisle, Emmett, and the others turned in the same direction, hearing sounds of passage much too faint for my ears.

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc4.description: I felt both protected and distressed by Edward after he apologized for exposing me and took a defensive position.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: "I'm sorry, Bella," he muttered fiercely. "It was stupid, irresponsible, to expose you like this. I'm so sorry."

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc1.description: I learned that Alice's visions show the course a person is on but that the future can shift when someone changes their mind.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: Some things are more certain than others… like the weather. People are harder. I only see the course they're on while they're on it. Once they change their minds — make a new decision, no matter how small — the whole future shifts.

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc1.description: I noticed that Jasper can create a calming atmosphere that helps me control my emotions and think clearly.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: I felt a tranquil atmosphere settle around me.

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc1.description: I prepared practical means for escape by hiding money in a sock and by placing an unmarked envelope for Edward where he would find it.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: I dug through my bag until I found my sock full of money. I pulled the unmarked envelope out of my pocket and set it on top of Alice's black leather bag.

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc1.description: I became resolved to escape even while every cell in my body longed for Edward's arrival, forcing me to balance desire and determination.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: It was amazing how every cell in my body seemed to know he was coming, to long for his coming.

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc1.description: I realized that Alice and Jasper would watch me more closely after Alice's vision and that their scrutiny would make escape much harder.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: They would be watching me twice as carefully now, anyway, after Alice's vision.

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.description: I learned that Jasper could track by scent and that I would have only seconds if he followed me.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I read: "I would have only seconds if he was following my scent."

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.description: I learned that a shuttle to the Hyatt was available and that I caught a cab to Scottsdale by paying cash for speed.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I read: "A shuttle to the Hyatt was just closing its doors a few feet behind me."

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.description: I became more emotionally dependent on Edward and I believed that being with him would be safety and a kind of heaven.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I read: "I spent the twenty minutes' drive with Edward." and "I would be in his marble arms, finally safe."

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.description: My view of Edward solidified into seeing him as protector and refuge rather than simply a distant romantic figure.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I read: "I imagined that I had stayed at the airport to meet Edward...and I would be in his marble arms, finally safe."

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.description: I learned that an unknown, easy voice called to say my mother was fine and to arrange a meeting at the ballet studio around the corner.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I read: "Hello, Bella,' that easy voice answered. 'That was very quick. I'm impressed.'"

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.description: I felt acute loneliness and terror despite brief happiness during my daydreams about Edward.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I read: "I'd never been more alone in my entire life." and "despite all the horror and hopelessness, I was fleetingly happy."

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc3.description: I learned that my mother was safe in Florida and had not received my message.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: My mother was safe. She was still in Florida. She'd never gotten my message.

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc3.description: I learned that the hunter admitted he had tricked me.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: "You don't sound angry that I tricked you."

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc3.description: I felt relieved and almost giddy because Charlie and Mom would never be harmed and would never have to fear.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: "Yes," I answered, my voice saturated with relief. Charlie and Mom would never be harmed, would never have to fear. I felt almost giddy.

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc3.description: I learned that the hunter was recording a video intended for Edward using a palm-sized camera with a red light.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: "Would you mind, very much, if I left a little letter of my own for your Edward?" He took a step back and touched a palm-sized digital video camera balanced carefully on top of the stereo. A small red light indicated that it was already running.

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc3.description: I realized that Alice had been the one prey who escaped this antagonist long ago and that her coven might derive comfort from that fact.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: The one and only time my prey escaped me. "Alice," I breathed, astonished.

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc4.description: I heard the final growl of the hunter as if from underwater.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: I heard, as if from underwater, the final growl of the hunter.

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc4.description: I saw a dark shape coming toward me through the long tunnels my eyes had become.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: I could see, through the long tunnels my eyes had become, his dark shape coming toward me.

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc4.description: I raised my hand instinctively to protect my face with my last effort.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: With my last effort, my hand instinctively raised to protect my face.

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc4.description: My eyes closed and I drifted into unconsciousness.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: My eyes closed, and I drifted.

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc4.description: I realized I was losing control of the situation and that I could not stay conscious to continue resisting.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: With my last effort, my hand instinctively raised to protect my face. My eyes closed, and I drifted.

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc1.description: I realized that Edward was taking me to the prom.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: "You're taking me to the prom!" I yelled.

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc1.description: I noticed that Alice had dressed me in a deep blue, frilly, off-the-shoulders dress and that I had only one shoe because my other foot was in plaster.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: "Then she'd dressed me in the most ridiculous dress — deep blue, frilly and off the shoulders, with French tags I couldn't read — a dress more suitable for a runway than Forks." "Only one shoe, as my other foot was still securely encased in plaster."

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc1.description: I felt increasingly awed and breathless at Edward's surreal beauty and perfection.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: "Would I ever get used to his perfection?" "His beauty was absolutely surreal."

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc1.description: I noted that there had been no progress with Rosalie while I was on quite good terms with her sometimes-husband.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: There had been no progress with Rosalie, though I was on quite good terms with her sometimes-husband.

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc2.description: I observed that the prom was held in the school gym with balloon arches and pastel crepe paper decorations.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc2.source_text: I saw actual balloon arches and twisted garlands of pastel crepe paper festooning the walls.

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc2.description: I realized that I could enjoy dancing a little when I allowed Edward to lead the waltz despite my earlier panic.
