tw-book1-chapter9_Sc1.description: I perceived Edward as secretive but willing to explain, which adjusted my sense of trust and curiosity toward him.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: I thought we were past all the evasiveness," I grumbled.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: I observed that Edward drives extremely fast, even claiming that he always drives like that and that he has never been in an accident or even gotten a ticket.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "You're going a hundred miles an hour!" "I always drive like this." "I've never been in an accident, Bella — I've never even gotten a ticket."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: I noticed Edward grew tense and fell silent when I mentioned that Jacob's dad was an elder and that legends involved his family.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "His confused expression froze in place." "He was silent, staring at the road." "I saw his knuckles tighten convulsively on the wheel."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: I perceived Edward's promise not to laugh and his mixture of gentleness and severity when I prepared to tell him what I had learned.
I noticed that Edward implied a protective distinction between him and me when I suggested that he might walk away from a crash but I could not.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "'Probably,' he agreed with a short, hard laugh. 'But you can't.'"

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: I observed that Edward reacted with incredulity and anger when told that I didn't care what he was and I learned that he prefers honesty about my thoughts.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: "You don't care if I'm a monster? If I'm not human!" "I'd rather know what you're thinking — even if what you're thinking is insane."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward cannot sleep at all.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: "I can't sleep." "Never," he said, his voice nearly inaudible.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward believes the Quileutes are right to keep their distance and that his family is still dangerous.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: "They're right to keep their distance from us. We are still dangerous." "The Quileutes have a long memory."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: I realized that Edward considered allowing himself to be alone with me to be a very dangerous mistake, revealing his internal conflict about our closeness.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: "Me, for example, allowing myself to be alone with you." "A very dangerous one."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward experiences an ongoing thirst that is only partially sated by animal blood and that restraint is required to avoid becoming a monster.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.source_text: "It doesn't completely satiate the hunger — or rather thirst. It keens us strong enough to resist. Most of the time."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward sometimes finds it much more difficult to resist his hunger at certain times and that he is struggling now.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.source_text: "Sometimes it's more difficult than others." "Is it very difficult for you now?" "Yes."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward feels anxious when he is away from Bella and that he worries about her safety constantly.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.source_text: "It makes me… anxious… to be away from you."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: I realized that Edward believes my involvement with him is wrong and dangerous, and I heard him urgently warn me not to be so involved.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.source_text: "Don't you see, Bella? ... It's wrong. It's not safe. I'm dangerous, Bella — please, grasp that."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward apologizes for his behavior and for making Bella miserable about his distance and danger.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: I learned that Edward promised to be at school the next day and explicitly offered to reserve a seat for me at lunch.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.source_text: "I'll save you a seat at lunch."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: I learned that Edward warned me not to go into the woods alone and admitted he is not always the only danger outside.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.source_text: "Don't go into the woods alone." "I'm not always the most dangerous thing out there. Let's leave it at that."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: I observed Edward show tenderness and intimacy when he leaned close, breathed in my face, and told me to sleep well.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.source_text: "Sleep well," he said. His breath blew in my face, stunning me.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.description: I noticed that Edward wanted to end the evening and sent a clear signal that our meeting should conclude for now.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc5.source_text: He sighed, and I knew he wanted me to leave now.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: I learned that Edward was a vampire.
I learned that part of Edward thirsted for my blood and I didn't know how potent that part might be.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc6.source_text: Second, there was part of him — and I didn't know how potent that part might be — that thirsted for my blood.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc6.description: I realized that I am unconditionally and irrevocably in love with Edward despite knowing that part of him thirsts for my blood.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc6.source_text: Second, there was part of him — and I didn't know how potent that part might be — that thirsted for my blood. And third, I was unconditionally and irrevocably in love with him.

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.description: I noticed that he sparkles in sunlight as though the sunbeams shatter off his skin into rainbow shards.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: the brilliant sunbeams were shattering off his skin into a thousand rainbow shards like he was made of crystal or diamond?

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.description: I recognized that he is described as forever seventeen and does not age.
I observed that he cast no reflection in the mirror during my dream.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: Edward stood beside me, casting no reflection, excruciatingly lovely and forever seventeen.

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.description: I experienced him kissing my cheek in the dream, which emphasized the intimacy and permanence of our relationship from my perspective.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: He pressed his icy, perfect lips against my wasted cheek.

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.description: I understood that he and his family live in Forks because the persistent rain allows them to be outside without revealing their secret.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: The whole reason he lived in Forks, the rainiest place in the world, was so that he could be outside in the daytime without exposing his family's secret.

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc2.description: I admitted that I had made contingency plans and seriously considered ways to end my existence after Bella was nearly killed.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: "Of course I was trying to focus on finding you alive, but part of my mind was making contingency plans. Like I said, it's not as easy for me as it is for a human."

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc2.description: I observed that Edward expressed the belief that humans have it easy when it comes to suicide, mentioning the simplicity of plant extracts.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: "You humans have it so easy! All you have to do is throw down one tiny vial of plant extracts…"

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc2.description: I revealed that I could not imagine living without Bella and that I contemplated drastic measures rather than exist without her.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc2.source_text: "Well, I wasn't going to live without you."

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc3.description: I understood that Edward believed God, heaven, and hell existed but did not believe that vampires would have an afterlife.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: "Edward's with me up to a point. God and heaven exist… and so does hell. But he doesn't believe there is an afterlife for our kind."

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc3.description: I realized that Edward agreed with Carlisle's theology only in part, indicating a nuanced difference between their beliefs.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: "Edward's with me up to a point. God and heaven exist… and so does hell. But he doesn't believe there is an afterlife for our kind."

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward composes his own music and that he had prepared a CD of his compositions for me.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: "It was his music, his compositions. The first piece on the CD was my lullaby."

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward obtained a piano so he could play for me here.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: "I didn't think you would let me get a piano so I could play for you here," he explained.

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.description: I heard Edward admit that he was tempted equally by my blood and my body when I challenged him.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: "Which is tempting you more, my blood or my body?" I challenged. "It's a tie."

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.description: I noticed a tone of desperation in Edward when he joked about doing nothing he didn't want to do, and I reconsidered the calm composure I usually attributed to him.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: "Heaven forbid that I should do anything I don't want to do," he said in a strangely desperate tone...

tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.description: I began to view Edward as both a protective presence and a potential danger because his care is paired with intense, sometimes uncontrollable attraction.
tw-book2-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: He lay down next to me—on top of the blanket so I wouldn't get chilled—and put his arm over me. Suddenly his lips became much more urgent...

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.description: I noticed that Edward is not mentioned among the people involved in this scene.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Billy, Charlie, Harry Clearwater

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: I understood that my agony in the meadow was directly tied to his absence and the memories I could recall of him.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.source_text: Nothing more than the memories that I could have called back whenever I wanted to, if I was ever willing to endure the corresponding pain—the pain that had me now, had me cold.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: I suppressed a piercing hope when I glimpsed a figure because I desperately wanted it to be him and then felt renewed agony when it was not.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.source_text: a rush of piercing hope rocked through me. I suppressed it viciously, fighting against the equally sharp lash of agony as my eyes continued to the face beneath the black hair, the face that wasn't the one I wanted to see.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: I perceived that my connection to him left me vulnerable and fracturing, showing how central he was to my emotional state.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.source_text: There was nothing special about this place without him.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.description: I heard that Carlisle had told us Laurent stayed with Tanya's family in Denali.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.source_text: I heard that Carlisle said Laurent had stayed with Tanya's family in Denali.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.description: I believed that Edward would be touchy or angry about the whole James incident and that mentioning Laurent might provoke him.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc7.source_text: I believed that Edward remained touchy about the James incident and might react badly.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc8.description: I learned that Laurent stated Edward killed James.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc8.source_text: "She thought it more appropriate to kill you than Edward—fair turnabout, mate for mate. She asked me to get the lay of the land for her, so to speak."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc8.description: I learned that Laurent implied Edward left Bella unprotected, which frames Edward's actions as leaving vulnerability behind.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc8.source_text: "apparently it wouldn't be the revenge she imagined, since you must not mean very much to him if he left you here unprotected."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc8.description: I began to suspect that others view Edward's protection of Bella as imperfect after Laurent's remarks.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc8.source_text: "apparently it wouldn't be the revenge she imagined, since you must not mean very much to him if he left you here unprotected."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc9.description: I heard Edward's furious roar echoing distantly in the back of my head.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc9.source_text: and the sound of Edward's furious roar echoed distantly in the back of my head.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc9.description: I understood that Bella's love for Edward intensified under threat as she mentally called out his name and declared her love.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc9.source_text: Edward, Edward, Edward. I was going to die. It shouldn't matter if I thought of him now. Edward, I love you.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.description: I learned that Edward was close by and whispered a warning for me not to move.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.source_text: 'Don't move an inch,' Edward's voice whispered.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.description: I learned that Edward was observing the situation and trying to control my actions to keep me safe.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.source_text: I stared at the monstrous creature, my mind boggling as I tried to put a name to it. 'Don't move an inch,' Edward's voice whispered.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.description: I realized I was dependent on Edward's instructions in dangerous moments and felt both vulnerable and protected by his presence.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.source_text: 'Don't move an inch,' Edward's voice whispered.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.description: I noticed that Edward's pale, beautiful face haunted my thoughts and appeared in my mind as a disturbing image while I tried to sleep.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.source_text: Better that than the pale, beautiful face that smiled at me now from behind my lids.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.description: I accepted that the Cullens' absence meant I could not depend on their immediate protection even if I hoped they might still care.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.source_text: If he didn't return, maybe she'd think the Cullens were still protecting me.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.description: I recalled broader threats in my life including dangerous vampires and large wolves that heightened my fear and urgency.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: Sure. I'd had a lot on my mind—revenue-obsessed vampires, giant mutant wolves, a ragged hole in the center of my chest—but when I laid the evidence out, it was embarrassingly obvious.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.description: I inferred that the vampire threat was not immediately focused on me because no vampires had come after me for a week.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: It had been a week, and no vampires had come for me yet. A week was more than enough time for them to have returned, so I must not be a priority.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.description: I heard Edward's voice in my mind advising me to be quiet and not to push Jacob during the confrontation.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: "Quiet now, Bella. Don't push him," Edward cautioned in my ear.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.description: I realized that I still experienced a comforting, protective connection to Edward through his voice even when he was not physically present.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: Ever since Edward's name had broken through the careful walls I'd buried it behind, I'd been unable to lock it up again.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.description: I felt less afraid and more calmed when I heard Edward's intervening guidance, which altered my immediate emotional response.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: "Give him a chance to calm down," Edward's voice insisted.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.description: I kept a replayed memory of Edward's voice in my mind and I used it as solace when I was hurting.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "I pulled out the memory—nor a real memory that would hurt too much, but the false memory of Edward's voice in my mind this afternoon—and played it over and over in my head until I fell asleep with the tears still streaming calmly down my empty face."

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.description: I felt that Edward's presence, even as a remembered voice or dream image, continued to fracture and deepen my longing and sadness.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "And then his face became so beautiful that it shattered my heart. I reached for him, but he took a step away, raising his hands like a shield. And then Edward vanished."

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.description: I acknowledged that Edward remained central to my emotional life and I allowed that longing to guide my nighttime reveries.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "I pulled out the memory... and played it over and over in my head until I fell asleep with the tears still streaming calmly down my empty face."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.description: I remembered that Edward used to sneak in through my window at night.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: it reminded me of when Edward used to sneak in through my window

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.description: I felt that the reminder of Edward's visits reopened unhealed wounds and intensified my pain about our past.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: the reminder picked viciously at the unhealed wounds.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc2.description: I learned again that Edward is a vampire because Jacob's stories had already conveyed that fact to Bella.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: Without realizing what he was doing, Jacob had told me exactly what I needed to know that day—that Edward was a vampire.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc2.description: I understood that Bella's loyalty to Edward and the Cullens constrained her willingness to share information with others.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: "Sometimes, loyalty gets in the way of what you want to do. Sometimes, it's not your secret to tell."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.description: I expected Edward to appear in the dream with faintly glowing skin, black dangerous eyes, a beckoning smile, and pointed teeth.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: A light was coming toward me from the beach. In just a moment, Edward would walk through the trees, his skin faintly glowing and his eyes black and dangerous. He would beckon to me, and smile. He would be beautiful as an angel, and his teeth would be pointed and sharp…

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.description: I felt my anticipation of Edward's beautiful but dangerous presence intensify my dread when the dream did not play out as I expected.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: I was getting ahead of myself. Something else had to happen first. Jacob dropped my hand and yelped.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.description: I maintained a view of Edward as simultaneously alluring and threatening as I imagined him in the dream.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: He would be beautiful as an angel, and his teeth would be pointed and sharp…

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: I remembered that I had already accepted vampires long before and that Edward's nature was not a new shock to me.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.source_text: "Hadn't I already accepted the existence of vampires long ago—and without all the hysterics that time?"

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: I kept the belief that Edward was above and beyond ordinary, and the new werewolf revelation simply reinforced how unusual my life was.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.source_text: "Besides, there'd never been one moment that I wasn't completely aware that Edward Cullen was above and beyond the ordinary. It wasn't such a surprise to find out what he was—because he so obviously was something."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc6.description: I learned that Edward's voice in my head can warn me and influence my behavior during tense situations.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc6.source_text: I listened to him, though. I would do anything for that voice.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc6.description: I felt compelled to obey Edward's warning and I attempted to soften the confrontation with Jacob as a result.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc6.source_text: I listened to him, though. I would do anything for that voice.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc6.description: I increased my reliance on Edward's guidance even when he was not physically present, showing deeper dependence on his counsel.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc6.source_text: I would do anything for that voice.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward killed James.
I sensed Edward's fury when Victoria's name was said.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.source_text: "In my head, Edward snarled in fury at the name."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.description: I realized that things are not mate-for-mate with Edward and that his relationship with me is different from those vampire expectations.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.source_text: "That things aren't like that with us anymore. Not for Edward, anyway."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.description: I learned from Jacob's words that stories about mind-reading vampires are true and that such abilities make conflicts more complicated.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.source_text: "Like the stuff about the mind-reading bloodsucker... That really sucks that those stories are true. It makes everything more complicated."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.description: I confirmed that I still avoid saying Edward's name and that thinking about him produces physical pain for me.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.source_text: You don't like to say his name. Or hear it.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.description: I remembered Edward telling me that it was difficult to kill a vampire and that only another vampire could do the job.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.source_text: Edward—I clutched automatically at my chest—had told me how difficult it was to kill a vampire. Only another vampire could do the job.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.description: I found Jacob's claim about werewolves able to kill vampires surprising in light of Edward's warning, which made me more anxious about conflicting protections.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.source_text: But Jake said this was what werewolves were made for…

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: I heard him say "They'll deal with it" and then grin while asking "Who's afraid of the big, bad wolf?"
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: "They'll deal with it," he said, and then he grinned. "Who's afraid of the big, bad wolf?"

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: I perceived him as projecting confidence or trying to dismiss fear with a grin and a taunt.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: "They'll deal with it," he said, and then he grinned. "Who's afraid of the big, bad wolf?"

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward is not present or mentioned in this scene.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.description: I had not heard Edward's voice for days and noticed that absence keenly.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: But it had been days since I'd heard Edward's voice.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.description: I became addicted to the sound of my delusions, meaning Edward's imagined voice intensified my longing.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: That was probably part of the problem. I was addicted to the sound of my delusions.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.description: I entertained the idea of a date with Edward alongside a date with Jacob, showing conflicted attachments.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: Maybe it would be fun. A date with Jacob, a date with Edward… I laughed darkly to myself.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.description: I recalled being hunted by a vampire during the previous spring break.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: Last spring break, I'd been hunted by a vampire, too.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.description: I hoped that being hunted by a vampire wouldn't become some kind of recurring tradition.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: I hoped this wasn't some kind of tradition forming.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.description: I noted that it had been days since I had heard Edward's voice.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: It had been days since I'd heard Edward's voice.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.description: I realized that my reliance on imagined conversations with Edward was an addiction that affected my mood.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: I was addicted to the sound of my delusions. It made things worse if I went too long without them.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.description: I understood that my emotional attachment to Edward persisted through delusions and that his absence intensified my distress.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: That was probably part of the problem. I was addicted to the sound of my delusions. It made things worse if I went too long without them.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc6.description: I heard Edward's voice in my head as a vivid memory that was disapproving and pleading.
I noticed that his anger and disapproval registered as intimate and even lovely in my perception.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc6.source_text: "No, Bella!" He was angry now, and the anger was so lovely.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc6.description: I perceived Edward as emotionally invested in my safety and willing to beg and plead to stop me.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc7.description: I heard Edward begging me to keep swimming and urgently commanding me not to give up while I was drowning.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc7.source_text:
"Keep swimming!" Edward begged urgently in my head.
"Stop that!" he ordered. "Don't you dare give up!"
"Fight!" he yelled. "Damn it, Bella, keep fighting."

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward's voice remained unnaturally clear in my mind despite the physical drowning around me.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc7.source_text: My ears were flooded with the freezing water, but his voice was clearer than ever.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc7.description: I perceived Edward as furious and deeply invested in my survival when I pictured his perfect face, gold eyes, clenched teeth, and flared nostrils.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc7.source_text: I could see his perfect face as if he were really there; the exact shade of his icy skin, the shape of his lips, the line of his jaw, the gold glinting in his furious eyes. He was angry, naturally, that I was giving up. His teeth were clenched and his nostrils flared with rage.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.description: I learned that the vampires have an advantage in the water, making the ocean particularly dangerous for someone who went missing there.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.source_text: She took off into the water—the bloodsuckers have the advantage there.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.description: I became more convinced that entering the water was especially reckless because of the supernatural threat lurking there.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.source_text: She took off into the water—the bloodsuckers have the advantage there.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.description: I shifted my immediate reliance toward Jacob for rescue and comfort rather than any unseen vampire allies because Jacob physically carried and sheltered me.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.source_text: His chest was bare and warm; he hunched his shoulders to keep the rain off of me.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.description: I noticed that Edward's face occupied my thoughts and that I lingered on that image while drifting in and out of sleep.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: Edward's face… I lingered there for a long time.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.description: I recognized that my attachment to Edward persisted and influenced my thinking about danger, loss, and how to move forward.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: Edward's face… I lingered there for a long time.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.description: I inferred that my fixation on Edward complicates my willingness to accept other forms of comfort or change in my life.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: I thought about reality instead—about jumping off the cliff and what a brainless mistake that had been. Images from my ill-considered afternoon stunt rolled through my head while I tried to come up with something pleasant to think about… the feel of the air as I fell, the blackness of the water, the thrashing of the current… Edward's face… I lingered there for a long time.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.description: I heard Edward's velvet voice whisper the words 'Be happy' in my ear.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: I quoted: "'Be happy,' he told me."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.description: I believed that Edward, even if indifferent, would want me to be as happy as possible under the circumstances and would not begrudge a small bit of love given to Jacob.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: I thought: "Wouldn't Edward, indifferent as he might be, want me to be as happy as possible under the circumstances?"

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.description: I learned that members of the Cullen family, indicated by Carlisle's car, were nearby.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.source_text: "It's Carlisle's car." "It's the Cullens. I know it."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.description: I felt a new tension because recognition of the Cullens did not remove my fear of the vampire threat Jacob had detected.
I experienced conflicted feelings toward the Cullens in this moment, combining familiarity with apprehension.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.source_text: "It's Carlisle's car." "It's the Cullens. I know it."

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc2.description: I learned that Alice had told Edward her vision and that Edward had not believed her, responding that "Bella promised."
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: "I told him this would happen, but he didn't believe me. 'Bella promised,'"

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc2.description: I became defensive and cut Alice off when she began to mention Edward's name, indicating sensitivity about his perception of the situation.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: "And my brother? Do you have any idea what Edward—" I cut her off then, as soon as she said his name.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: I learned that the Quileute tribe knows Carlisle from a long time ago, linking them historically to the Cullens.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: They know Carlisle from a long time ago.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: I observed that Alice did not perceive Jacob's presence during the rescue despite sensing a smell, raising questions about what the Cullens noticed.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: I watched curiously as an enigmatic range of emotions flitted across her face. Something was bothering her—her imperfect vision? But I wasn't sure.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: I inferred that Bella's decision to tell Alice about Jacob indicates growing trust in Alice and, by extension, in the Cullen inner circle.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: Jacob knew everything, why not Alice, too?

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward had warned Bella that she attracts danger.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: 'Edward was right—you're a magnet for danger.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.description: I noticed that Alice references Edward's warning when criticizing Bella's choices.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: 'A young werewolf? Even worse! Edward was right—you're a magnet for danger.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.description: I inferred that Edward's prior concern is taken seriously by others in Alice's circle.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: 'Edward was right—you're a magnet for danger.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc7.description: I learned from Alice that Edward did not know she was there.
I learned that Edward checks in with Carlisle and Esme only every few months.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc7.source_text: 'He's not with Carlisle and Esme?' 'He checks in every few months.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc7.description: I inferred that Edward was still out enjoying his distractions rather than being nearby.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc7.source_text: He must still be out enjoying his distractions.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.description: I learned that Bella's grief is described as if someone died, implying the loss represents a death-like devastation.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.source_text: 'Not like someone… left her, but like someone died.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.description: I realized Bella's loss cost her a whole envisioned future and family, not just the loss of a romantic partner.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.source_text: 'It was also losing a whole future, a whole family—the whole life that I'd chosen…'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.description: I learned Bella's grief permeates daily life and motivates her avoidance of reminders like music and reading.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.source_text: 'She wouldn't listen to music anymore; I found a bunch of CDs broken in the trash. She didn't read; she wouldn't be in the same room when the TV was on, not that she watched it so much before.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc10.description: I learned that Edward was in South America and that he did not know Alice was visiting.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc10.source_text: 'He doesn't even know I'm here. The last time I spoke with him, he was in South America.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc10.description: I noticed that Alice defended Edward against Charlie's assumptions and that Charlie expressed irritation or jealousy about Edward's absence.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc10.source_text: 'That's something, at least.' Charlie snorted. 'Well, I hope he's enjoying himself.' For the first time, Alice's voice had a bit of steel in it. 'I wouldn't make assumptions, Charlie.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc13.description: I noticed that Edward Cullen is not present or mentioned in the spoken exchange of this scene.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc13.source_text: She kissed my cheek swiftly before she vanished through Charlie's door—and out his back window, no doubt.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc13.description: I realized that the immediate social tension in this moment centers on Jacob Black rather than Edward Cullen.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc13.source_text: Trust me—it wouldn't be a good idea to have me and Jacob Black in a room together.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: I learned that a member of the Cullen family, Alice, is currently staying at my house.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.source_text:
One of the Cullens is staying here with you" 
"Yes. Alice Cullen.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: I learned that the Cullen family as a whole is not returning to town.
I understood that my choice to align with a Cullen created resentment from Jacob toward me and the Cullens.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: I knew I wasn't being fair. After all, I'd picked the bloodsucker over him last night.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.description: I learned that Dr. Carlisle Cullen called the Swan residence and asked about Charlie.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.source_text:
"Dr. Carlisle Cullen."

"He didn't ask for you," Jacob said coldly. His face was smooth, expressionless, but his hands shook.

"He asked where Charlie was and I told him. I don't think I broke any rules of etiquette."

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.description: I noted that Jacob despised the Cullens and referred to them contemptuously as a "filthy bloodsucker."
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.source_text: "Filthy bloodsucker," he muttered under his breath.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward heard Rosalie's vision and interpreted it as my suicide which motivated his next actions.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: I read: "Rosalie told him I killed myself, didn't she?" "Yes," Alice admitted.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward planned to go to Italy to provoke the Volturi and likely die after believing I was dead, as recalled from his earlier words about going to Italy and provoking the Volturi.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: I read: "I was thinking maybe I would go to Italy and do something to provoke the Volturi... Not unless you want to die."

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.description: I understood that Edward's belief that I was beyond saving caused him to make up his mind to seek death as soon as Rosalie's confirmation arrived.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: I read: "He made up his mind as soon as your friend confirmed that it was too late to save you."

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.description: I concluded that Edward's perception of our future changed drastically when he accepted my death and chose self-destruction over living without me.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: I read: "Well, I wasn't going to live without you... so I was thinking maybe I would go to Italy..."

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward was in trouble and that others organized to help him immediately.
I resolved that Edward's danger justified abrupt, risky travel and that I would accept those risks to aid him.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.source_text: I'm only afraid of getting you killed.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward might respond to the belief that I was dead by committing public violence to expose the Cullen family and draw a reaction.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: "A killing spree through the city, attacking the guard, lifting a car over his head in the main square… mostly things that would expose them—he knows that's the fastest way to force a reaction…"

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward could be unaware of the truth if someone used mental lying, which explains why he might not know I was alive.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: "If he were listening," she explained. "But believe it or not, it's possible to lie with your thoughts. If you had died, I would still try to stop him. And I would be thinking 'she's alive, she's alive' as hard as I could. He knows that."

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.description: I changed my belief about the certainty of Edward's previous vow not to live without me when his earlier departing words undermined that promise in my mind.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: "I remembered with painful clarity his words that day on the sofa, while we watched Romeo and Juliet kill themselves, one after the other. I wasn't going to live without you, he'd said... the words he had spoken in the forest as he'd left me had canceled all that out—forcefully."

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward had warned me that the Volturi are ancient, powerful, and like royalty and that antagonizing them could lead to death.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: He just said they were an old, powerful family—like royalty. That you didn't antagonize them unless you wanted to… die.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.description: I realized that Edward had given me a brief warning but had not fully explained the Volturi's role or the vampire rules to me.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: Didn't Edward tell you what they do? No, I said, feeling the blank expression on my face.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward is planning to flout the Volturi in their own city.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc3.source_text: Is planning to flout that in their own city—the city they've secretly held for three thousand years, since the time of the Etruscans.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc3.description: I learned that the Volturi have secretly held Volterra for three thousand years since the time of the Etruscans.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc3.source_text: the city they've secretly held for three thousand years, since the time of the Etruscans.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc3.description: I noted that Alice called this an unusual situation and said 'You don't get a lot of suicidal vampires'.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc3.source_text: You don't get a lot of suicidal vampires.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc4.description: I heard Alice say that he's getting closer and deciding how he's going to ask.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: He's getting closer. He's deciding how he's going to ask.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc4.description: I hoped that I might be very, very, very lucky and somehow able to save Edward while acknowledging that saving him might not allow me to stay with him.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: Maybe, if I were very, very, very lucky, I would somehow be able to save Edward. But I wasn't so stupid as to think that saving him would mean that I could stay with him.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc6.description: I learned that Alice anticipated Edward would be furious at Bella's transformation.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc6.source_text: "He'll be furious, but what will he be able to do about it?"

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc6.description: I inferred that Bella believed Edward lacked the ability to stop Alice from changing her.
I noticed that Alice's readiness to change Bella was tempered by concern about Edward's reaction and the situation's practicality.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc6.source_text: "He'll be furious, but what will he be able to do about it?" "Try to be reasonable," she whispered.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward was changing plans quickly, as Alice only received flickers of his thoughts.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.source_text: I was only getting flickers, he was changing plans so quickly.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward had at one point decided to go hunting in the city but changed his mind at the last minute.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.source_text: He'd decided to go hunting. "In the city," she explained. "It got very close. He changed his mind at the last minute."

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward plans a public, suicidal spectacle by walking into the sun in the main plaza under the clock tower when the sun is directly overhead.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.source_text: "He's going to keep it simple. He's just going to walk out into the sun." "He wants the biggest audience possible, so he'll choose the main plaza, under the clock tower." "He'll wait till the sun is exactly overhead."

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.description: I realized that Edward is leaning toward melodrama and desires the biggest possible audience for his act.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc7.source_text: Right now, he's leaning toward the melodramatic. He wants the biggest audience possible, so he'll choose the main plaza, under the clock tower.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.description: I learned that Edward plans to wait until noon and that he must see me before he moves into the light.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.source_text: 'You don't have to do anything. He just has to see you before he moves into the light. And he has to see you before he sees me.'

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.description: I began to worry that Edward's arrival could provoke the police and complicate matters because it coincides with Saint Marcus Day.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.source_text: They're not going to be very happy if Edward messes things up for them on St. Marcus Day, are they?

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.description: I perceived Edward as cautious and deliberate because he chose to wait and coordinate timing for his arrival.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc8.source_text: 'Yes. He's decided to wait. And they're waiting for him.'

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward took a defensive, protective stance over Bella and emitted a low warning growl.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: Edward's face was whiter than bone as he wheeled to crouch over me, taking a clearly defensive position. A low warning growl slid from between his clenched teeth.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.description: I noticed that Edward did not appear to be breathing during his protective stance.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: I could tell that he wasn't breathing.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.description: I perceived that Edward trusted Carlisle's intervention when Carlisle murmured to him and Edward then relaxed and nodded.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: "Let me by, Edward," Carlisle murmured. A second passed, and then Edward nodded slowly and relaxed his stance.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.description: I saw Edward lift me effortlessly while Carlisle kept pressure on my arm.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: Edward lifted me effortlessly, while Carlisle kept the pressure steady on my arm.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.description: I observed Edward standing over me protectively and fighting an intense thirst that left him barely breathing.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.source_text:
Edward stood over me, still protective, still not breathing.
"I can handle it," he insisted. But his jaw was rigid; his eyes burned with the intensity of the thirst he fought, so much worse for him than it was for the others.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.description: I told Edward he didn't need to be a hero and urged him to get some fresh air instead of staying dangerously close.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: "You don't need to be a hero," I said. "Carlisle can fix me up without your help. Get some fresh air."

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.description: I watched Edward finally relent to our urging and sprint smoothly through the kitchen's back door to go find Jasper.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: Edward's eyes narrowed as we ganged up on him, but, finally, he nodded once and sprinted smoothly through the kitchen's back door.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.description: I started to think Edward was being masochistic for staying so close while I bled.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: "Why are you so masochistic?" I mumbled.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward had previously told Bella the story about Carlisle trying a different approach.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc3.source_text: I heard 'Hasn't Edward told you this story?'

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc3.description: I inferred that Edward serves as a familiar source of explanations for Bella about the Cullen family's past and habits.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc3.source_text: I heard 'Hasn't Edward told you this story?'

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward believes in God and heaven but doubts an afterlife for vampires and thinks our kind has lost their souls.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc4.source_text: Edward's with me up to a point. God and heaven exist… and so does hell. But he doesn't believe there is an afterlife for our kind.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward resembled his mother Elizabeth Masen and that her illness and care for him influenced Carlisle's decision.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc4.source_text: It was Edward's mother who made up my mind. "Edward looks a great deal like her—she had that same strange bronze shade to her hair, and her eyes were exactly the same color green."

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc5.description: I noticed that Edward's face was smooth and unreadable while I sensed that he was trying very hard to hide something in his eyes.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc5.source_text: His face was smooth, unreadable, but there was something wrong with his eyes—something he was trying very hard to hide.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc5.description: I heard Edward say that trying to shoulder blame would only make him more disgusted with himself, revealing his guilt and self-directed anger.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc5.source_text: Don't try to take any of this on yourself, Bella. It will only make me more disgusted with myself.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc5.description: I watched Edward argue that a normal boy like Mike Newton would be healthier for me, which I interpreted as him pushing me toward safety through distance.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc5.source_text: Mike Newton ended up in this conversation because Mike Newton would be a hell of a lot healthier for you to be with," he growled.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc5.description: I observed that Edward drove too fast on the way home and that he said he should go home instead of staying with me.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc5.source_text:
He drove too fast down the dark, serpentine lane.

"I should go home."

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc6.description: I learned that Edward composes and recorded music, that he included my lullaby on the CD, and that he considered getting a piano to play for me.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc6.source_text: "It was his music, his compositions. The first piece on the CD was my lullaby." "I didn't think you would let me get a piano so I could play for you here," he explained.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc6.description: I observed that Edward is attentive and caring toward me because he asked about my arm, retrieved Tylenol, tucked me into bed, and lay over me to keep me warm.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc6.source_text: "Does your arm hurt?" "I'll get you some Tylenol." "He scooped me up off the bed with one arm... He put me down with my head on my pillow and tucked the quilt around me. He lay down next to me—on top of the blanket so I wouldn't get chilled—and put his arm over me."

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc6.description: I realized that Edward values my reactions and sometimes regrets his choices about gift spending when he admitted he wished he'd spent money on my present.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc6.source_text: "Now I wish I'd spent money on your present. I didn't realize that you were capable of being reasonable."

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward was contemplating moral questions about right and wrong in relation to our interactions.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.source_text: "I was thinking about right and wrong, actually."

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward voiced concern about doing anything he did not want to do, showing his caution.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.source_text: "Heaven forbid that I should do anything I don't want to do," he said in a strangely desperate tone.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward can become desperate and urgent in physical contact despite his usual restraint.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.source_text: Suddenly his lips became much more urgent, his free hand twisted into my hair and held my face securely to his.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.description: I realized that Edward experiences a moral struggle around his attraction to me and that he apologizes when he thinks he crossed a line.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.source_text: "Sorry," he said, and he was breathless, too. "That was out of line."

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.description: I noticed that Edward could be playful and affectionate while also being serious about boundaries, which affected how I relate to him.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc7.source_text: "You're greedy tonight." "You're overestimating my self-control." He grinned briefly in spite of himself, and then was serious again.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward would be under the clock tower to the north of the square in a narrow alley on the right, and that he would be standing in shadow.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: Edward will be under the clock tower, to the north of the square. There's a narrow alleyway on the right, and he'll be in the shadow there.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.description: I learned that I needed to get Edward's attention before he could move into the sun.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: You have to get his attention before he can move into the sun.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.description: I learned that if Edward stuck to his plan we had only five minutes left to complete our approach.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: If Edward stuck to his plan, we had only five minutes left.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.description: I trusted Edward's role in the plan and believed that his position under the clock tower was central to our coordinated effort.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc1.source_text: Edward will be under the clock tower, to the north of the square. There's a narrow alleyway on the right, and he'll be in the shadow there. You have to get his attention before he can move into the sun.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc2.description: I understood that Bella was actively searching for Edward and listened for the crowd's gasp or scream that would announce his discovery.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: I listened, above the angry exclamations, trying to hear the sound of discovery: the gasp, maybe the scream, as Edward came into someone's view.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc2.description: I inferred that Bella feared Edward's discovery would lead to disaster and that her own human limits could doom them.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: I was stupid and slow and human, and we were all going to die because of it.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.description: I noticed that Edward's casual tone vanished and his voice became curt when he reacted to Alice's explanation.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: "Hm," Edward said curtly, and the casual tone of his voice was gone.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward's skin was wintry and cold like the underground temperature.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: My clothes were still wet, and the temperature underneath the city was wintry. As was Edward's skin.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.description: I learned that some of Edward's motivation to come was interpreted as guilt over thinking he had caused Bella's death.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: It was probably no more than guilt—the same guilt that compelled him to come here to die when he'd believed that it was his fault that I'd killed myself.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.description: I felt Edward's tenderness when he reached to hold my face and traced his thumb across my lips, updating my sense of his care.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.source_text: He reached his free hand across his body to hold my face, too, his smooth thumb tracing across my lips.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.description: I observed Edward glowering down the long hallway toward the slight, black-shrouded figure and keeping his eyes fixed on Jane.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: Edward didn't seem to agree with my assessment. He glowered darkly down the long hallway, toward the slight, black shrouded figure at the end, standing by an elevator. He never took his eyes off Jane.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.description: I noticed Edward's mood was marginally improved when Alec greeted him and commented on his disposition.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: "Welcome back, Edward," Alec greeted him. "You seem in a better mood." "Marginally," Edward agreed in a flat voice.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.description: I saw Edward react protectively and angrily to Felix's casual provocation, with Alice needing to caution him to be patient.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: "Dibs," Felix called casually from behind. Edward turned, a low snarl building deep in his chest. Alice touched Edward's arm. "Patience," she cautioned him.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.description: I observed that Edward's voice was rough with anxiety when he spoke under his breath.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: "Are you all right?" Edward asked under his breath, to low for the human woman to hear. His voice was rough—if velvet can be rough—with anxiety.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.description: I watched Edward pull me to the sofa, tuck the thick wool cloak around me, and hold me on his lap to protect me from his cold skin.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: He pulled me to the sofa farthest away from the curious human at the desk... He pulled me onto his lap and tucked the thick wool cloak around me, protecting me from his cold skin.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.description: I learned that Edward claimed he had never been in better control of that side of his nature than right now.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: "I've never been in better control of that side of my nature than right now."

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.description: I felt dependent on Edward's comfort and I experienced his physical protection as intimacy.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: I wrapped my arms around his neck—what was the worst he could do? Just push me away—and hugged myself closer to him.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.description: I noticed that Edward nodded in response to Demetri's warning before Demetri left.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: "Do not leave until dark," he warned us. Edward nodded, and Demetri hurried away.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc1.description: I observed Edward disagreeing with my assessment of the hallway and glowering darkly down the long corridor toward a slight black-shrouded figure by the elevator, signaling his wariness.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: Edward didn't seem to agree with my assessment. He glowered darkly down the long hallway, toward the slight, black shrouded figure at the end, standing by an elevator.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc1.description: I saw Edward pull me along and maintain a focused gaze on Jane, which I interpreted as a protective and watchful stance toward potential threat or intrigue.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: He pulled me along, and Alice walked on my other side.  He never took his eyes off Jane.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc1.description: I noticed Edward remained physically close and attentive to me while also monitoring Jane, suggesting divided attention between safeguarding me and assessing Jane.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: His hand still rubbed against my arm. He never took his eyes off Jane.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc2.description: I heard Alec welcome Edward back to the reception.
I noticed Edward admitted he was only marginally in a better mood.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: "Marginally," Edward agreed in a flat voice.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc2.description: I saw Felix provocatively call "Dibs" and I heard Edward's low snarl build in response.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc2.source_text:
"Dibs," Felix called casually from behind.
Edward turned, a low snarl building deep in his chest.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc2.description: I watched Alice touch Edward's arm and tell him "Patience," which I felt restrained him.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: Alice touched Edward's arm. "Patience," she cautioned him.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc3.description: I learned that Aro needs physical contact to hear thoughts and that Aro's ability surpasses mine in scope.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: I read "Aro needs physical contact to hear your thoughts, but he hears much more than I do."

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc3.description: I noticed Edward's protective behavior toward Bella in public with the Volturi, which reinforced his role as guardian in our relationship.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: I read "'Yes, Aro, I am,' he agreed, tightening his arm around my waist."

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc3.description: I came to acknowledge that Edward views Aro as exponentially more powerful and envied some aspects of Aro's talent.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: I read "'And also exponentially more powerful,' Edward added dryly."

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward demonstrates extraordinary restraint from the call of Bella's blood, a restraint that astonishes Aro and other ancient vampires.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: "But your restraint!" Aro sighed. "I did not know such strength was possible. To inure yourself against such a siren call, not just once but again and again—if I had not felt it myself, I would not have believed."

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc4.description: I understood that Aro values Edward's memories of Carlisle and that those memories make Aro 'gratified' and compare Edward to Carlisle in restraint and temperament.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: "I am gratified by his success," Aro mused. "Your memories of him are quite a gift for me, though they astonish me exceedingly. I am surprised by how it… pleases me, his success in this unorthodox path he's chosen. I expected that he would waste, weaken with time. I'd scoffed at his plan to find others who would share his peculiar vision. Yet, somehow, I'm happy to be wrong."

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc4.description: I perceived that Edward maintained a composed exterior while Bella guessed at something seething beneath his surface during Aro's questioning.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: Edward gazed back at Aro's admiration with no expression. I knew his face well enough—time had not changed that—to guess at something seething beneath the surface.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.description: I learned that Aro tried to recruit Edward for his talent, calling it "an excellent addition to our little company."
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: "Your talent would be an excellent addition to our little company."

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.description: I learned that Edward initially refused Aro's recruitment with the words "I'd… rather… not."
I learned that Edward accused the Volturi of issuing an implicit ultimatum, saying "Join or die, is that it?" and criticizing their laws.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: "Join or die, is that it? I suspected as much when we were brought to this room. So much for your laws."

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.description: I learned that Edward seriously considered the option of turning Bella when he asked what would happen "And if I do?" regarding making her immortal.
I noticed that Edward chose his words deliberately and that his anger was controlled, indicating a calculated rather than purely emotional stance.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: The tone of his voice surprised me. He sounded irate, but there was something deliberate about his delivery—as if he'd chosen his words with great care.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.description: I recognized Edward's protective devotion through his visible fury and the rumble in his chest when the Volturi threatened me.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: Edward fumed beside me. I could hear a rumble in his chest, building toward a growl.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.description: I observed Edward pull my face against his chest and then push me toward the door when the crowd presented an opening.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: Edward pulled my face against his chest, but it was too late. As soon as the smallest break appeared, Edward pushed me quickly toward the door.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.description: I realized that Edward would act immediately and protectively in a crisis, demonstrating decisiveness under pressure.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: Edward pulled my face against his chest, but it was too late. As soon as the smallest break appeared, Edward pushed me quickly toward the door.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.description: I felt Edward's protectiveness deepen my trust in his intent to keep me safe as he set a pace that made me run to keep up.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc6.source_text: Edward set a pace that had me running to keep up. But we still couldn't get through the ornate door at the end of the hallway before the screaming started.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc1.description: I noticed Edward acknowledge Demetri's warning by nodding before Demetri hurried away.
I felt Edward's anxious, rough voice and heard him chant 'It's all right, you're safe' as he pulled me onto his lap and tucked the cloak around me.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: "It's all right, you're safe, it's all right," he chanted again and again. He pulled me onto his lap and tucked the thick wool cloak around me, protecting me from his cold skin.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc1.description: I experienced comfort from Edward's protective behavior even as I noted that he answered the receptionist coldly.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.description: I heard Edward tell me that Gianna knows everything about their nature and situation.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: "Yes. She knows everything," Edward told me.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.description: I heard Edward acknowledge that Gianna knows there is a possibility she could be killed and that she hopes to be kept as one of them.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: "She's knows it's a possibility," he said. "She's hoping they'll decide to keep her."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.description: I noticed Edward watch my reaction closely and respond by comforting me, asking what's wrong, and reminding me that we are alive and together.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: "What's wrong?" he asked, still anxious, rubbing my back with gentle pats... "But we have lots of reasons to be happy. For one, we're alive."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.description: I became sure that Edward did not place the same emotional weight on being "together" as I did, altering my sense of our emotional symmetry in that moment.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I just nodded, sure that he did not place the same weight on that consideration as I did.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward verbally asserts strong control over his thirst at that time.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "I've never been in better control of that side of my nature than right now."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward and others use the label 'my singer' to describe someone whose blood 'sings' to a vampire, a label Edward applies to Bella.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "They have a name for someone who smells the way Bella does to me. They call her my singer—because her blood sings for me."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.description: I observed Edward offering physical comfort and affectionate kisses to Bella while also handling practical plans with Alice, which updated my view of his dual roles as protector and predator.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "He sighed; his sweet breath caressed my face... He stared at my face like he was doing the same, while he and Alice discussed how to get home."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.description: I noticed that Edward and Alice were coordinating quietly in ways that excluded others and that their coordination included risky practical solutions.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "Their voices were so quick and low that I knew Gianna couldn't understand. It sounded like more theft would be involved, though."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.description: I heard Edward respond coldly that leaving would not be a problem when Alec released us.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: Edward made no answering pretence; his voice was ice cold. "That won't be a problem."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.description: I observed Edward helping Bella to her feet and supporting most of her weight as they left the city.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: Edward helped me to my feet. He wound his arm around my waist and supported most of my weight as we walked.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.description: I noticed that Edward regarded the street festivities with disdain when he muttered, "Ridiculous."
I witnessed Edward's tenderness when he pressed his lips to the hollow under Bella's ear, encouraged her to try to sleep, and promised Alice a gift.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: He pressed his lips to the hollow under my ear. "Try," he encouraged. "I'll get you one for Christmas," Edward promised.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.description: I heard Edward disapprove of my Coke because he knew my low tolerance for caffeine.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.source_text: "Bella," Edward said disapprovingly. He knew my low tolerance for caffeine.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.description: I observed Edward's restraint in physical affection as he kissed my hair and forehead but avoided kissing my lips, indicating a protective or controlled closeness.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.source_text: He continued to kiss my hair, my forehead, my wrists… but never my lips, and that was good.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.description: I sensed that Edward's silence might mean he was hoping I would sleep or that he had nothing to say, which changed my expectations for discussion.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.source_text: Edward didn't speak. Maybe he was hoping I would sleep. Maybe he had nothing to say.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.description: I noticed that Edward accepted new clothes from Alice and left his dark cloak behind in an alley.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.source_text: Alice bought Edward new clothes, too, and he left the dark cloak on a pile of trash in an alley.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc6.description: I observed that Edward physically kept his arms around me and remained close during the family's reception at the airport.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc6.source_text: Esme reached for me, hugging me fiercely, yet awkwardly, because Edward kept his arms around me, too.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc6.description: I noticed that Edward showed a repentant, apologetic side with his mother after the incident.
I recognized active conflict between Edward and my father, with Edward attempting to protect me from Charlie's anger.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc6.source_text: "Give her to me. Get your hands off her!" Charlie yelled. "Edward tried to pass me to Charlie, but I clung to him with locked, tenacious fingers."

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.description: I could even remember names from the dream, indicating that named figures appeared clearly in my hallucination.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: The dream was still strong—I could even remember the names.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.description: I associated an angelic figure from the dream with a compelling presence that I could not release when I woke.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: But the strongest, clearest part of the dream was not the horror. It was the angel that was most clear. It was hard to let him go and wake up.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.description: I observed that Edward's irises were pitch-black with bruise-like shadows under them, which surprised me.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: His irises were pitch-black, with bruise-like shadows under them.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.description: I heard Edward speak in a low, anxious voice and ask if he had frightened me.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: "Did I frighten you?" His low voice was anxious.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.description: I noticed Edward watched my changing expressions with alarm and seemed genuinely concerned about my state.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: The beautiful figment of my imagination watched my changing expressions, with alarm.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.description: I understood that Edward denied that I was dead and attempted to reason with my confusion about waking.
I heard Edward tease about the idea that I might have committed murders to wind up in hell, revealing a wry attempt at levity.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: "But I can't imagine what you could have done to wind up in hell. Did you commit many murders while I was away?"

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.description: I admitted that I had been hunting and experimenting with tracking rather than hunting for food.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: I was… hunting. I wasn't hunting for food… I was actually trying my hand at… tracking. I'm not very good at it.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.description: I revealed that I had no idea of the danger I left behind and that I thought Bella was safe.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: I had no idea. I didn't realize the mess I was leaving behind. I thought it was safe for you here. So safe.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.description: I felt sick to my core and I judged myself harshly for underestimating Victoria's attachment to James.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: I feel sick, sick to my core, even now, when I can see and feel you safe in my arms. I am the most miserable excuse for—

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.description: I recognized that Victoria had an unexpectedly deep tie to James and I understood that her overconfidence hid that bond.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: I think I realize why now—she was so sure of him, the thought of him failing never occurred to her. It was her overconfidence that clouded her feelings about him—that kept me from seeing the depth of them, the bond there.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc5.description: I learned that Edward told me directly that he went to the Volturi because he believed I was dead.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: "Bella, I went to the Volturi because I thought you were dead," he said, voice soft, eyes fierce.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc5.description: I learned that Edward acknowledged feeling guilt intensely, more than I could comprehend.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: "Feel guilty? Intensely so. More than you can comprehend."

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc5.description: I recognized that Edward's admission that he cannot live in a world without me deepens the emotional urgency of our relationship despite his contradictory behavior.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: "Bella, I can't live in a world where you don't exist."

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc5.description: I revised my view of Edward's honesty when he openly stated that he is capable of lying effectively.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: "I'm a good liar, Bella, I have to be."

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc6.description: I admitted that I deliberately lied during the forest goodbye to convince Bella that I did not want her so that she might move on.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc6.source_text: I lied to save you, and it didn't work.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc6.description: I realized that my attempt to protect Bella by lying caused her pain and failed to accomplish what I intended.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc6.source_text: I lied, and I'm so sorry—sorry because I hurt you, sorry because it was a worthless effort.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc6.description: I reaffirmed that I have always loved Bella and that my love for her is enduring and unwavering.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc6.source_text: I have always loved you, and I will always love you.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward vowed aloud that he was not leaving Bella and that he would not go anywhere without her.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc7.source_text: "I'm not going anywhere. Not without you," he added more seriously.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc7.description: I learned that Edward said he left previously to protect Bella and give her the chance at a normal human life.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc7.source_text: "I only left you in the first place because I wanted you to have a chance at a normal, happy, human life. I could see what I was doing to you—keeping you constantly on the edge of danger, taking you away from the world you belonged in, risking your life every moment I was with you."

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc7.description: I understood that Edward experiences profound emptiness without Bella when he compared his life before her to a moonless night and described her as a meteor that made everything brilliant.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc7.source_text: "Before you, Bella, my life was like a moonless night. Very dark, but there were stars—points of light and reason… And then you shot across my sky like a meteor. Suddenly everything was on fire; there was brilliancy, there was beauty."

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc7.description: I perceived that Edward now regards Bella as more important than his own wants or needs and admits he will not be strong enough to leave her again.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc7.source_text: "I'm much too selfish. Only you could be more important than what I wanted… what I needed. What I want and need is to be with you, and I know I'll never be strong enough to leave again."

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.description: I learned that Edward had been tracking Victoria over long distances and that he had followed false leads as far as Texas and Brazil.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.source_text: I traced her as far as Texas, but then I followed a false lead down to Brazil—and really she came here.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.description: I heard Edward state that tracking Victoria was never a distraction for him but an obligation.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.source_text: That was never a distraction. It was an obligation.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.description: I observed Edward declare that Victoria was going to die soon and that he intended to see her eliminated.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.source_text: Victoria"—the snarl became more pronounced—"is going to die. Soon.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.description: I noticed that Edward reaffirmed his commitment to Bella by promising to keep his word to her even while pursuing Victoria.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.source_text: I will keep my promise, Bella.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.description: I learned that Edward believes the Volturi perceive time differently and might not pay attention to Bella until she is thirty.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.source_text: I heard: "Time means something very different to them than it does to you, or even me. They count years the way you count days. I wouldn't be surprised if you were thirty before you crossed their minds again," he added lightly.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.description: I observed that Edward is committed to keeping Bella human for as long as she prefers and refuses to make her immortal to 'save' her soul.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.source_text: I heard: "I will never leave you again." 'I cannot be without you, but I will not destroy your soul.'

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.description: I learned that Edward promises to remain with Bella during her life and to follow her after her death if she dies while human.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.source_text: I heard: "'I'll follow after as soon as I can.'"

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.description: I noticed that Edward claims to have plans to protect Bella despite the Volturi threat.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.source_text: I heard: "'I have a few plans.'"

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.description: I observed him hand me my shoes and ask how I planned to get there.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.source_text: "Here are your shoes. How did you plan to get there?" he asked.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.description: I heard him warn that using my truck would probably wake Charlie.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.source_text: "That will probably wake Charlie," he offered as a deterrent.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.description: I heard him say that Charlie would blame him and not me if trouble occurred.
I noticed he suggested I stay and that his suggestion lacked hopefulness.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.source_text: "Stay here," he suggested, but his expression wasn't hopeful.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.description: I felt him block my way, which signaled protectiveness and an attempt to keep me from leaving.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc10.source_text: He was there before me, blocking my way.

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.description: I saw him take me in his arms and spring lithely from my window, landing without the slightest jolt like a cat.
tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: he took me in his arms and sprang lithely from my window, landing without the slightest jolt, like a cat.

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.description: I heard him whisper that my hold on him is permanent and unbreakable and that I should never doubt that he cannot leave me.
tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: "Your hold is permanent and unbreakable," he whispered. "Never doubt that."

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.description: I noticed that he looked anguished and tormented when I admitted my fear that he might leave me.
tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: Even in the darkness, I could see the anguish twist his face—it reminded me of his expression under Jane's torturing gaze; I felt sick, and regretted speaking the truth.

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.description: I learned that he had kept my things hidden under the floorboards intentionally as a personal, childish reminder.
tw-book2-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: "Your things were never gone," he told me. "I knew it was wrong, since I promised you peace without reminders. It was stupid and childish, but I wanted to leave something of myself with you. The CD, the pictures, the tickets—they're all under your floorboards."

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc2.description: I observed Edward react with furious protectiveness and physical control when he charged back into the room and grabbed my face shouting about my sanity.
tw-book2-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: "No! No! NO!" Edward roared, charging back into the room. "Are you insane?" he shouted. "Have you utterly lost your mind?"

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward proposed a cryptic trade by asking "Five years?" after I said I would give anything to be changed.
tw-book2-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: "What would you be willing to trade for that?""Anything.""Five years?"

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc2.description: I noticed Edward calmed and relaxed when I agreed to consider postponing the transformation and then insisted on taking me home quickly.
