He put a cold hand on my forehead. He made me wait an hour and keep down a big glass of water before he fried me some eggs.

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc1.description: I noticed that Edward admitted he had not thought about how hot I would be in his absence and offered to install an air conditioner.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: "So much for thoroughness. I didn’t think about how hot you would be with me gone. I’ll have an air conditioner installed before I leave again."

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc1.description: I realized that Edward is protective and concerned for my health because he suggested going back to Rio to see a doctor when my stomach pain recurred.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: "Maybe we should go back to Rio, see a doctor," he suggested anxiously.

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc2.description: I observed Edward turned into a sculpture with a glassy stare and an unanswered ringing phone.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc2.source_text: He had turned into a sculpture. Edward’s stare seemed glassy, as if he couldn’t see me anymore. In the same moment, Edward’s phone rang, shrill and demanding.

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc2.description: I suspected Edward might be the father of my possible pregnancy because he was the only person I had ever slept with and he is a vampire.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc2.source_text: The only person I’d ever had sex with was a vampire, for crying out loud.

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward informed Carlisle and then relayed that Carlisle believed Bella was pregnant.
I learned that Edward arranged immediate travel home by calling the airport and spending a long time on the phone.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: I noticed "The airport. We're going home." and "Edward was on the phone for more than an hour without a break."

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward referred to the embryo as "that thing" and explicitly said Carlisle would remove it to prevent it from hurting Bella.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: I heard "We’re going to get that thing out before it can hurt any part of you."

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.description: I perceived that Edward's behavior shifted from protective to cold and controlled, revealing deep agitation or conflict.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: I noticed "His voice was too cold, too careful. His face matched his voice, empty and hard."

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.description: I saw Edward both reassure Bella that she would be fine and simultaneously plan an invasive action, complicating my understanding of his protective instincts.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: I heard "Don’t be afraid. We’ll be home in sixteen hours. You’ll be fine... We’re going to get that thing out before it can hurt any part of you."

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc4.description: I observed Edward frozen and wearing a tortured expression after the woman’s pronouncement.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: Edward was frozen again, staring after her with the tortured expression fixed on his face.

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc4.description: I heard Edward attempt to dismiss the woman’s warning as mere legend and call it old lies for entertainment.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: “Don’t worry about what she said. It’s nothing but legends, old lies for the sake of entertainment.”

tw-book4-chapter7_Sc4.description: I felt Edward try to comfort and protect me by packing, promising to get me to Carlisle soon, and taking responsibility for preparations.
tw-book4-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: “Don’t worry about anything. We’ll get to Carlisle in just a few hours, really. This will all be over soon.”

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward Cullen was the person who had driven me earlier and that his presence explained others' odd behavior.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: "Edward Cullen." "Guess that explains it, then," he said. "I wondered why my dad was acting so strange."

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc1.description: I realized that Charlie does not like the Cullens and that this dislike influences how others react.

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward would be leaving with Alice after lunch to go hunting.
I learned that Edward planned to bring Bella's truck and leave the key in the ignition for her.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: "Your truck will be here, and the key will be in the ignition — unless you're afraid someone might steal it."

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc2.description: I noticed that Edward is highly protective and that he takes precautions about being alone with Bella.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: "If I'm going to be alone with you tomorrow, I'm going to take whatever precautions I can."

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward finds Bella unpredictable and fascinating and that he believes she confounds his expectations.

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc3.description: I observed Edward standing under the dense shade at the edge of the hollow watching Bella with cautious eyes.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: Finally I spotted him, still under the dense shade of the canopy at the edge of the hollow, watching me with cautious eyes.

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc3.description: I observed Edward hold up a hand in warning when Bella beckoned and stepped toward him.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: He held up a hand in warning, and I hesitated, rocking back onto my heels.

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc3.description: I observed Edward seem to take a deep breath and then step out into the bright glow of the midday sun.
tw-book1-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: Edward seemed to take a deep breath, and then he stepped out into the bright glow of the midday sun.

tw-book1-chapter12_Sc3.description: I noticed Edward's eyes were described as wary and reluctant, which updated my understanding of his cautious demeanor in Bella's presence.

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: I heard him say that he was born in Chicago in 1901 and that Carlisle found him in 1918 when he was dying of the Spanish influenza.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: "I was born in Chicago in 1901." ... "Carlisle found me in a hospital in the summer of 1918. I was seventeen, and dying of the Spanish influenza."

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: I observed that he spoke of Carlisle's process as difficult and painful and that not many have the restraint required to accomplish it.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: "How did he… save you?" ... "It was difficult. Not many of us have the restraint necessary to accomplish it. ... For me, it was merely very, very painful."

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: I noticed that he holds profound respect and gratitude for Carlisle and believes Carlisle acts from loneliness and compassion when creating family members.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: "He acted from loneliness. That's usually the reason behind the choice. ... For me, it was merely very, very painful." ... "But Carlisle has always been the most humane, the most compassionate of us…"

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: I heard him explain that Rosalie and Emmett joined their family through dramatic circumstances and that the family sometimes pretends to be younger to stay longer in one place, hence enrolling in high school in Forks.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: "Carlisle brought Rosalie to our family next. ... Sometimes they live separately from us, as a married couple. But the younger we pretend to be, the longer we can stay in any given place. Forks seemed perfect, so we all enrolled in high school."

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: I learned from him that Alice's visions are about possible futures and are subjective, and that Jasper's background involved wandering and depression before Alice found him.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: "Alice and Jasper are two very rare creatures. ... Jasper belonged to another… family, a very different kind of family. He became depressed, and he wandered on his own. Alice found him. ... She sees things — things that might happen, things that are coming. But it's very subjective."

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.description: I recognized that Edward believes his ability to hear minds is unique among them while Alice's abilities differ and focus on non-humans and looming threats.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: "Really?" I interrupted, fascinated. "But you said you were the only one who could hear people's thoughts." ... "She saw Jasper and knew that he was looking for her before he knew it himself. She saw Carlisle and our family, and they came together to find us. She's most sensitive to non-humans. She always sees, for example, when another group of our kind is coming near. And any threat they may pose."

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc2.description: I observed Edward appear silently and laugh softly behind me, surprising me with his stealth.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "The quiet, laughing response came from behind me. 'Yes?'"

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc2.description: I watched Edward become motionless like a statue when I instructed him to stay at the edge of my bed.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: I quote: " 'Yes, ma'am.' And he made a show of becoming a statue on the edge of my bed."

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc2.description: I felt Edward's hand as cold when he placed a cold hand on mine while suggesting I sit with him.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: I quote: " 'Why don't you sit with me,' he suggested, putting a cold hand on mine. 'How's the heart?' "

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc2.description: I experienced Edward's protective and playful restraint when he gently picked me up and listened with me to my heartbeat slowing.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "He sat up slowly, so as not to startle me again. Then he leaned forward and reached out with his long arms to pick me up, gripping the tops of my arms like I was a toddler. We sat there for a moment in silence, both listening to my heartbeat slow."

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward admits to feeling jealousy and that he finds that emotion unexpectedly powerful and irrational.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: I heard "But jealousy… it's a strange thing. So much more powerful than I would have thought. And irrational!"

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward consciously resists his predatory nature in order to preserve essential humanity and that Carlisle has a theory about their differing abilities.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: I heard "To try to retain whatever essential humanity we can." and "Carlisle has a theory… he believes that we all"

tw-book1-chapter14_Sc3.description: I felt Edward's admission that I am 'resurrecting the human' in him and that his feelings are intensified because this resurgence is new to him.
tw-book1-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: I heard "I'm new at this; you're resurrecting the human in me, and everything feels stronger because it's fresh."

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc1.description: I observed Edward react angrily to the Blacks' visit by saying that it was crossing the line.
I learned that Edward preferred to leave immediately and claimed he could walk home faster than my truck moves.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: "I could walk home faster than this truck moves."

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc1.description: I noted Edward's protective and teasing attitude when he instructed me to get the Blacks inside so he could leave and joked about preparing Charlie to meet my new boyfriend.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: "Get them inside," he instructed, "so I can leave. I'll be back around dusk." "After you get rid of them" — he threw a dark glance in the Blacks' direction — "you still have to prepare Charlie to meet your new boyfriend."

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: I observed Edward arrive in the heavy rain and stand in the porch light looking strikingly model‑like.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: "Edward stood in the halo of the porch light, looking like a male model in an advertisement for raincoats."

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: I noticed Edward address my father respectfully and accept the offer to take his jacket.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: "Thanks, Chief Swan," Edward said in a respectful voice.

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: I watched Edward lift me into the Jeep with one hand, demonstrating unexpected physical strength.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: "He sighed, and then lifted me in with one hand."

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: I learned that the Jeep Edward drove is Emmett's and that it uses an off‑roading harness.
I noticed that Edward's promise and demeanor convinced Charlie and me of his sincerity and protective intent.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: "Charlie couldn't doubt Edward's sincerity, it rang in every word."

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.description: I noticed Edward tell me that I smelled good in the rain and that he commented on my scent.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: "You smell so good in the rain," he explained.

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward claimed he was never angry with me and that he admired my bravery and warmth.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "I'm never angry with you — how could I be? Brave, trusting… warm as you are."

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward explicitly expressed self-directed hatred for the danger he posed to me and his desire to be stronger.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "Sometimes I truly hate myself. I should be stronger, I should be able to —"

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc3.description: I noticed that Edward's confession of love marked a shift from teasing to intense protectiveness and vulnerability.
I observed that Edward's tenderness, his holding my face and kissing me, reinforced his protective and affectionate role toward me.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "Don't be mad, I couldn't help myself. You should have seen your face."

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc4.description: I saw Edward plant himself in front of me and angle between me and what was coming.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: And he planted himself in front of me. He took a half step, angling himself between me and what was coming.

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc4.description: I obeyed Edward when he told me to take my hair down and to stay very still at his side.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: "Take your hair down," Edward said in a low, even voice. "Yes, stay very still, keep quiet, and don't move from my side, please."

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc4.description: I sensed Edward's guilt and responsibility when he apologized for exposing me, which altered my view of his protectiveness.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: "I'm sorry, Bella," he muttered fiercely. "It was stupid, irresponsible, to expose you like this. I'm so sorry."

tw-book1-chapter17_Sc4.description: I noticed Edward's protective actions reinforced that he prioritized my safety over the game's casual mood.
tw-book1-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: And he planted himself in front of me. He pulled my long hair forward, around my face.

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward's plane was scheduled to land in terminal four, which I identified as the terminal I needed.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: Edward's plane was landing in terminal four, the largest terminal, where most flights landed — so it wasn't surprising that his was.

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.description: I perceived Edward as my potential savior whose presence would render me safe and calm my fear.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I read: "I imagined that I had stayed at the airport to meet Edward...I would be in his marble arms, finally safe."

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.description: I inferred that Edward's ability to be outside in daylight would affect where we could go together.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I read: "I wondered where we would have gone. North somewhere, so he could be outside in the day."

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.description: I allowed myself brief comfort from thoughts of Edward and I lost track of time in escapist daydreams.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I read: "So involved was I in my escapist daydreams, I lost all track of the seconds racing by."

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc3.description: I learned that the hunter expected Edward to be unable to resist hunting him after watching the videotape he was making.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: "I'm sorry, but I just don't think he'll be able to resist hunting me after he watches this. And I wouldn't want him to miss anything. It was all for him, of course."

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc3.description: I learned that I had asked Edward not to avenge me and that I had left him a letter.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: "No, I don't think so. At least, I asked him not to." "I left him a letter."

tw-book1-chapter22_Sc3.description: I learned that the hunter claimed Edward was too weak to make the choice the older vampire made in saving a human.
tw-book1-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: "You see, the vampire who was so stupidly fond of this little victim made the choice that your Edward was too weak to make."

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward called people about my plans and told one caller that I was unavailable tonight and would be unavailable every night to others.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: "I'm sorry if there's been some kind of miscommunication, but Bella is unavailable tonight." "To be perfectly honest, she'll be unavailable every night, as far as anyone besides myself is concerned."

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc1.description: I observed Edward dressed in a tuxedo, which made his pale skin and beauty seem surreal.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: "I'd never seen him dress in black before, and, with the contrast against his pale skin, his beauty was absolutely surreal."

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc1.description: I understood that Edward was protective and possessive about my time and presence around others.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: "To be perfectly honest, she'll be unavailable every night, as far as anyone besides myself is concerned."

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc1.description: I noticed that Edward used a mocking smile and a friendly surface tone that I could perceive as having a soft edge of menace.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: "I'm shocked that you haven't figured it out yet." He threw a mocking smile in my direction. "His voice was very friendly, on the surface. I knew it well enough to catch the soft edge of menace."

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc2.description: I observed that Edward is an exceptional dancer who could effortlessly lead and lift me during the waltz.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc2.source_text: I watched him put my arms around his neck and slide his feet under mine as we whirled and I felt him pull me closer so my feet were briefly a foot from the ground.

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc2.description: I noticed Edward's jealousy toward Jacob when Jacob approached and I watched Edward step back but remain visibly angry.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc2.source_text: I heard Edward hiss and I watched him set me carefully on my feet before he took a step back and turned away when Jacob reached us.

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc2.description: I recognized that Edward preferred not to dance and that he used sarcasm about vampires to avoid dancing initially.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc2.source_text: I heard him mutter that there are more than enough vampires present and I watched him smile reluctantly when I joked about massacring the townsfolk.

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward promised he wouldn't let go of me that night.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: I promised I wouldn't let go of you tonight," he explained.

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc3.description: I realized Edward wanted me to experience human life and tried to prevent his existence from taking things away from my life.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: I brought you to the prom because I don't want you to miss anything. I don't want my presence to take anything away from you, if I can help it. I want you to be human. I want your life to continue as it would have if I'd died in nineteen-eighteen like I should have.

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc3.description: I noticed Edward became irritated by Jacob and specifically by Billy's son for making him break his promise and for calling me pretty.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: First of all, he made me break my promise." "He called you pretty," he finally continued, his frown deepening. "That's practically an insult, the way you look right now.

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward explicitly asserts awareness of his nature when he says he knows what he is.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: I quote "I know what I am."

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc4.description: I noted Edward's expressed self-doubt about his worthiness when he said he was not worth it.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: I quote "I'm not worth it," he said sadly.

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc4.description: I observed Edward promise to stay with Bella, indicating a commitment despite his reservations.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: I quote "I will stay with you — isn't that enough?"

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc4.description: I perceived Edward's resistance to surrendering easily when he voiced that he would not give in so simply.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: I quote "You can't really believe that I would give in so easily," he said with a sour edge to his mocking tone.

tw-book1-chapter25_Sc4.description: I noticed Edward show tenderness through small gestures such as tracing my lips and kissing my throat.
tw-book1-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: I quote "His fingers lightly traced the shape of my lips." and "he leaned down to press his cold lips once more to my throat."

tw-book3-chapter4_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward had promised he would change me himself whenever I wanted but only if I were married to him first.
tw-book3-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: Edward had promised that he would change me himself whenever I wanted . . . just as long as I wasmarried to him first.

tw-book3-chapter4_Sc1.description: I read Edward’s note telling me he would return soon and asking me to look after his heart, which he said he left with me.
tw-book3-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: I’ll be back so soon you won’t have time to miss me. Look after my heart — I’ve left it with you.

tw-book3-chapter4_Sc1.description: I knew that Edward went hunting with his brothers and that he found hunting nearby easy prey boring.
tw-book3-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: I knew how it bored him to hunt the easy, nearby prey.

tw-book3-chapter4_Sc1.description: I began to suspect that Edward could be prone to overreaction because others joked about his tendency in that way.
tw-book3-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: “Haven’t you noticed yet, Bella, that Edward is just the teeniest bit prone to overreaction?”

tw-book3-chapter4_Sc1.description: I remembered that Edward had experienced intense thirst when he returned from Italy and that his golden eyes had turned black during that time.
tw-book3-chapter4_Sc1.source_text: His golden eyes had turned black and he’d suffered from his thirst more than it was already necessary that he suffer.

tw-book3-chapter4_Sc2.description: I learned Edward left because he worried that my association with vampires would be unhealthy.
tw-book3-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: Edward left me last fall because he didn’t think I should be hanging out with vampires. He thought it would be healthier for me if he left.

tw-book3-chapter4_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward came back after leaving.
tw-book3-chapter4_Sc2.source_text: He came back, though, didn’t he?

tw-book3-chapter4_Sc2.description: I affirmed that I felt there was nothing to forgive regarding Edward’s departure.

tw-book3-chapter4_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward told Bella the same version of the attack but with fewer details than Jacob provided.
tw-book3-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "Edward told me the same story, just without quite as many details."

tw-book3-chapter4_Sc3.description: I understood that separation did not work well for Edward and Bella, based on Jacob's remark about being apart.
tw-book3-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "Being apart . . . It didn’t work out so well for either of us."

tw-book3-chapter4_Sc3.description: I observed that Edward's depiction of his coven differed from the wolves' perspective and that tensions remain between the groups.
tw-book3-chapter4_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "So did your vampire tell you we attacked for no reason and his totally innocent coven —"

tw-book4-chapter8_Sc1.description: I understood that the person I loved might be the one harming me and that loving that person removed options like running or fighting.
tw-book4-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: When you loved the one who was killing you, it left you no options.

tw-book4-chapter8_Sc1.description: I noticed thematic evidence that vampires were part of the context and that social friction about them existed, as implied by a chapter title.
tw-book4-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: You Know Things Are Bad When You Feel Guilty For Being Rude To Vampires

tw-book4-chapter8_Sc1.description: I accepted that I could not run or fight without hurting my beloved, which reframed my approach to danger and survival.
tw-book4-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: You could run from someone you feared, you could try to fight someone you hated. All my reactions were geared toward those kinds of killers—the monsters, the enemies. When you loved the one who was killing you, it left you no options. How could you run, how could you fight, when doing so would hurt that beloved one?

tw-book4-chapter8_Sc2.description: I experienced Edward leaning down to kiss my forehead and telling me to get to sleep because I had a big day tomorrow and that he would meet me at the altar.
tw-book4-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: He leaned down and kissed my forehead. “Get to sleep. You’ve got a big day tomorrow.” “I’ll meet you at the altar.”

tw-book4-chapter8_Sc2.description: I watched Edward vanish by launching himself out my window too swiftly for my eyes to follow.
tw-book4-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: He vanished—launching himself out my window too swiftly for my eyes to follow.

tw-book4-chapter8_Sc2.description: I heard Emmett curse and I heard Edward laugh quietly as preparations and teasing about the bachelor party continued outside.
tw-book4-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: Outside, there was a muted thud, and I heard Emmett curse. “You’d better not make him late,” I murmured, knowing they could hear. ... Edward laughed quietly.

tw-book4-chapter8_Sc2.description: I recognized that Edward knew my weaknesses well enough to make me feel guilty when I complained about wedding arrangements.
tw-book4-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: I had grumbled a little until Edward, who knew my weaknesses, made me feel guilty.

tw-book4-chapter8_Sc3.description: I observed that Edward intervenes immediately and forcefully when Jacob shakes Bella.
tw-book4-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: “Take your hands off her!” Edward’s voice was cold as ice, sharp as razors.

tw-book4-chapter8_Sc3.description: I noticed that Edward acts protectively and authoritatively to defend Bella in tense moments.
I inferred that Edward regards Jacob's actions as a direct threat to Bella's safety.
tw-book4-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: “Take your hands off her!” Edward’s voice was cold as ice, sharp as razors.

tw-book4-chapter8_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward consulted Carlisle and his brothers before the experiment and sought their guidance about risks and expectations.
tw-book4-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: I spoke to Carlisle after you and I made our bargain, hoping he could help me.

tw-book4-chapter8_Sc4.description: I realized that Edward experienced the act as intensely pleasurable yet feels guilt and a sense that what happened was wrong.
tw-book4-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: I didn’t dream that you would construe the way I feel about what I did to you to mean that last night wasn’t…well, the best night of my existence.

tw-book4-chapter8_Sc4.description: I observed that Edward apologized, accepted that he had caused harm, and promised to do whatever he can to make me happy now.
tw-book4-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: I’ll do whatever I can to make you happy now.

tw-book4-chapter8_Sc6.description: I remembered that Jacob had once fought alongside Edward Cullen and that some pack members referenced that past association during the argument.
tw-book4-chapter8_Sc6.source_text: I don’t care if you had fun fighting alongside Edward Cullen once upon a time.

tw-book4-chapter8_Sc6.description: I realized that the Alpha did not honestly believe the Cullens were a danger and expected them to leave after they told their story.
tw-book4-chapter8_Sc6.source_text: I… well, I don’t honestly believe that the Cullens are a danger to us. And we know that they will not be here much longer. Surely once they’ve told their story, they will disappear.

tw-book4-chapter9_Sc2.description: I saw Edward's eyes go flat black and his face show a burning, agonized expression that made me think of someone burning at the stake.
tw-book4-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: His eyes were flat black, the circles under them dark purple.

tw-book4-chapter9_Sc2.description: I observed that Edward blamed himself for Bella's condition and that he confessed the guilt aloud.
tw-book4-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: “My fault,” Edward whispered, and his knees gave out.

tw-book4-chapter9_Sc2.description: I watched Edward reach up to touch and stroke Bella's face and I understood that he remained tender toward her despite the crisis.
tw-book4-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: He reached up to touch her face, to stroke it.

tw-book4-chapter9_Sc2.description: I realized that Edward's usual superiority had been replaced by broken helplessness and that vulnerability dominated his demeanor.
tw-book4-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: His broken helplessness irritated me. I wanted a fight, not an execution. Where was his smug superiority now?

tw-book4-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward described Jacob's imprinting as being like magic and compared it to A Midsummer Night's Dream.
tw-book4-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: "Edward told me once what it was like—your imprinting thing. He said it was like A Midsummer Night’s Dream, like magic."

tw-book4-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward was one of the people Carlisle changed after near-death situations, along with Esme, Emmett, and Rosalie.
tw-book4-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: "It worked for Esme. And Emmett, and Rosalie, and even Edward. None of them were in such great shape."

tw-book4-chapter9_Sc3.description: I believed that Edward would react fiercely if Bella died and that others feared he might return to deadly alliances because of his grief.
tw-book4-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: "You know what he’s going to do when you die. You’ve seen it before. You want him to go back to those Italian killers?"

tw-book4-chapter9_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward's face had been burned and that image was part of the pack's alarm.
tw-book4-chapter9_Sc4.source_text: Bella’s bruises, Edward’s face as he burned.

tw-book4-chapter9_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward had warned that 'The thing is growing. Swiftly.'
tw-book4-chapter9_Sc4.source_text: Another of my memories, Edward’s words this time: The thing is growing. Swiftly.

tw-book4-chapter9_Sc4.description: I noticed that the pack associated Edward with the dangerous phenomenon and feared its consequences.

tw-book4-chapter10_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward requested Jacob and Bella speak privately and asked the others to leave.
tw-book4-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: We’re going to let Jacob and Bella speak privately," Edward said.

tw-book4-chapter10_Sc1.description: I noticed Edward's composure was strained and that his voice was emotionless and cracking with anger.
tw-book4-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: There was no inflection at all in his voice. Robotic. The emotionless voice was cracking, showing the anger through it.

tw-book4-chapter10_Sc1.description: I noticed Edward prioritized Bella's comfort and reassured Rosalie that Carlisle and he would remain in sight.
tw-book4-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: Carlisle and I will always be in your sight, Rosalie," Edward said.

tw-book4-chapter10_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward acknowledged the presence and rapid growth of the creature when he said the thing was growing swiftly.
tw-book4-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: "Another of my memories, Edward’s words this time: The thing is growing. Swiftly."

tw-book4-chapter10_Sc3.description: I began to see Edward not only as Bella's protector but also as centrally involved with the creation or protection of the new creature, which influenced the pack's judgment of the Cullens.
I learned that the pack believes the Cullens may have bred or created an unknown and potentially dangerous being.
tw-book4-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: "We don’t know what kind of creature the Cullens have bred, but we know that it is strong and fast-growing."

tw-book4-chapter11_Sc1.description: I learned that the Cullens practiced for a fight with newborn vampires.
tw-book4-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: "We remembered together the nights we’d watched the Cullens practicing for the fight with the newborns."

tw-book4-chapter11_Sc1.description: I learned that Emmett Cullen was considered the strongest while Jasper presented a greater danger due to speed, power, and centuries of experience.
tw-book4-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: "Emmett Cullen was strongest, but Jasper would be the bigger problem. He moved like a lightning strike—power and speed and death rolled into one. How many centuries’ experience did he have? Enough that all the other Cullens looked to him for guidance."

tw-book4-chapter11_Sc1.description: I realized that the Cullens are not necessarily my enemies.
tw-book4-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: "They aren’t—I shook my head, clearing it—they aren’t our enemies."

tw-book4-chapter11_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward expressed gratitude toward me and said he would never have asked for this from me.
tw-book4-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: I read: "This isn’t the first time I’ve owed you my gratitude, Jacob," Edward whispered. "I would never have asked for this from you."

tw-book4-chapter11_Sc2.description: I realized that Edward would cross any line when it came to protecting Bella.
tw-book4-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: I read: "When it came to Bella, there were no lines he wouldn’t cross."

tw-book4-chapter11_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward admitted Bella's condition was worse.
I felt sympathy for Edward's fear and noticed a shudder run through him as he looked back into the house.
tw-book4-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: I read: "He looked over his shoulder, back into the house, and I saw a shudder run through his whole frame."

tw-book4-chapter11_Sc3.description: I noticed that Leah loathes the Cullens and would be happier to kill them than live near them.
tw-book4-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: as much as she loathed the Cullens, as happy as she’d be to go kill all the vampires right now

tw-book4-chapter11_Sc3.description: I learned that the pack assessed an immediate attack on the Cullens as suicide while Jacob and Seth were AWOL and the vampires were forewarned.
tw-book4-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: Suicide at this point, with you and Seth AWOL and the bloodsuckers forewarned.

tw-book4-chapter11_Sc4.description: I saw Edward nod once, absently, indicating he was acknowledging things without looking at me.
tw-book4-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: From the corner of my eye, I saw Edward nod once, absently, not looking in my direction.

tw-book4-chapter11_Sc4.description: I realized that Edward was suffering intensely and perhaps more than I had expected, which shifted my understanding of his emotional state.
tw-book4-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: Edward’s mouth mashed into a hard line, and I knew I was right again.

tw-book4-chapter11_Sc4.description: I observed Edward step around Rosalie and take Bella's hand in a protective, intimate gesture.
tw-book4-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: Edward stepped around Rosalie, no humor touching his intense expression. He took her hand, not the one that was still protecting her swollen belly.

tw-book4-chapter12_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward's face showed no reaction and appeared blank and dead when Seth informed him.
tw-book4-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: Edward’s face, framed in the same window as last night, showed no reaction to the news. It was a blank face, dead.

tw-book4-chapter12_Sc1.description: I became more concerned about Edward's condition after seeing his unresponsive expression in the window.
tw-book4-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: Wow, he looks bad, Seth muttered to himself. The vampire showed no reaction to that thought, either. He disappeared into the house.

tw-book4-chapter12_Sc1.description: I updated my view of Edward to see him as emotionally distant and unreactive in this moment.
tw-book4-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: Edward’s face, framed in the same window as last night, showed no reaction to the news. It was a blank face, dead.

tw-book4-chapter12_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward stayed closely by Bella's side and prioritized time with her because he believed he did not have much time left.
tw-book4-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: “Edward didn’t want to lose any time with her, because he didn’t have much time left.”

tw-book4-chapter12_Sc2.description: I noticed Edward relied on Jacob's assistance enough to brief Carlisle about Jacob's actions and to have Carlisle come greet Jacob at the door.
tw-book4-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: “Edward said you were coming in your human form, and I came out to greet you, as he didn’t want to leave her. ... Edward told me what you had to do.”

tw-book4-chapter12_Sc2.description: I began to see Edward as urgently protective of Bella and appreciative of outside help when necessary.
tw-book4-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: “Edward didn’t want to lose any time with her, because he didn’t have much time left.”

tw-book4-chapter13_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward stayed with Bella, held her hand, and appeared too drained to sustain hope or outward emotion.
tw-book4-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: I watched Edward remain holding Bella's hand while his face looked dead and he lacked the energy to maintain even a hint of hope.

tw-book4-chapter13_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward did not volunteer the news about Leah joining the pack and he shrugged when Bella asked if she had been told.
tw-book4-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: I observed Edward shrug without taking his eyes off Bella when the question arose about whether she had been told about Leah.

tw-book4-chapter13_Sc1.description: I noticed that Edward prioritized Bella's immediate comfort over sharing secondary information while I saw him roll his eyes at Rosalie's comment.
tw-book4-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: I noted Edward roll his eyes at Rosalie and focus on making Bella avoid thinking about what she was doing any more than necessary.

tw-book4-chapter13_Sc2.description: I understood that Jacob worries the Cullens could become outright enemies again if Bella is killed and that old resentments could return.
tw-book4-chapter13_Sc2.source_text: They would probably look like enemies—like no more than bloodsucking leeches—to me all over again.

tw-book4-chapter13_Sc2.description: I recognized that the pack blames the Cullens for tearing their family apart and that tension toward the Cullens colors current deliberations.
tw-book4-chapter13_Sc2.source_text: You’ve torn our family apart. It’s not meant to be this way.

tw-book4-chapter13_Sc3.description: I heard Edward say he was hearing me more clearly as a matter of familiarity and concentration and that my thoughts were slightly easier to pick up when I was in my human form.
tw-book4-chapter13_Sc3.source_text: “I’m hearing you more clearly—it’s a matter of familiarity and concentration. Also, your thoughts are slightly easier to pick up when you’re in your human form. So I caught most of what passed out there.”

tw-book4-chapter13_Sc3.description: I saw Edward sitting at the other end of the couch with Bella’s feet in his lap and I noticed he smiled at me with a small twitch like something pleased him.
tw-book4-chapter13_Sc3.source_text: Edward sat at the other end of the couch with Bella’s burrito’ed feet in his lap. He looked up when I came in and smiled at me—just a little twitch of his mouth—like something pleased him.

tw-book4-chapter13_Sc3.description: I noticed that Edward and I had been on the same wavelength a lot lately, which made our interactions feel more connected.
tw-book4-chapter13_Sc3.source_text: Edward seemed to be in agreement with my thoughts—we were on the same wavelength so much lately it was crazy.

tw-book4-chapter13_Sc3.description: I realized Edward’s mood improved in direct correlation to Bella’s health, which changed my view of how much his emotions tied to her condition.
tw-book4-chapter13_Sc3.source_text: His mood seemed to improve in exact correlation to Bella’s health.

tw-book4-chapter13_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward can cook and that others complimented him on it.
tw-book4-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: you probably just crashed human, but you know how she is. Anyway, they had all this food and, dang,”—he turned to Edward—“man, you can cook.” “Thank you,” Edward murmured.

tw-book4-chapter13_Sc4.description: I noticed that Edward quietly said 'Bella got cold' showing concern about her condition.
I recognized physical closeness between Edward and Bella because Bella's cup of blood was tucked against Edward.
tw-book4-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: I saw that her cup of blood was wedged between her leg and Edward’s.

tw-book4-chapter13_Sc4.description: I felt that Edward was irritated by Bella's dismissive attitude when I heard him grind his teeth.
tw-book4-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: I rolled my eyes. I heard Edward grind his teeth together, and I figured her blow-it-off attitude bugged him as much at it bugged me.

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc1.description: I found that Edward Cullen is identified as Bella’s fiancé in this scene.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: I had a feeling this guy would get along well with Edward Cullen, my… my fiancé (there really was no getting around that truth with the wedding just days away).

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc1.description: I noticed that other characters in the scene reference Edward Cullen with enough recognition that a stranger comments they would get along well with him.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: I had a feeling this guy would get along well with Edward Cullen, my… my fiancé (there really was no getting around that truth with the wedding just days away).

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc2.description: I heard Edward thank the darkness when we reached the cedars.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: I read: "Thank you," Edward said to the darkness. "This is very… kind of you."

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc2.description: I observed Edward step back and leave us so that I could have time with Jacob, which felt like a deliberate and generous act.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: I read: "Rosalie won’t forgive me if she doesn’t get her official turn on the dance floor," Edward murmured, and I knew he was leaving us, giving me a gift of his own—this moment with Jacob.

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc2.description: I noticed Edward maintained a protective grip on my elbow until Jacob arrived to catch me.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: I read: "My hand flew up to my throat, and if Edward hadn’t been holding me I would have collapsed."

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc3.description: I observed Edward leading two Brazilian visitors through the house and gesturing proudly toward Bella.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: Edward led them into the room, pointing toward the kitchen on his way. Edward gestured to me with a proud smile, and I heard my name mixed in with a flurry of unfamiliar words.

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc3.description: I heard Edward explain Kaure's heritage and mention local legends like the Libishomen that might make her suspect him.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: Kaure’s part Ticuna Indian. She was raised to be more superstitious—or you could call it more aware—than those who live in the modern world. She suspects what I am, or close enough. They have their own legends here. The Libishomen—the blood-drinking demon who preys exclusively on beautiful women.

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc3.description: I realized that Edward remained unperturbed and unconcerned even when Kaure seemed to suspect him.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: He shrugged, unperturbed. He still didn’t sound worried.

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc3.description: I recognized Edward's protectiveness and affection when he wrapped his arms around me, lifted me, and suggested we wait to survey the demolition until we were alone.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: He walked swiftly to my side and wrapped his arms around me. "Maybe it would be more polite to wait until we’re alone. You may not notice me tearing the furniture apart, but it would probably scare them."

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc3.description: I noticed that Edward spoke Portuguese fluently when he interacted with Gustavo.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: Edward sat up, keeping me cradled against him, and answered Gustavo in flowing Portuguese.

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward believes he is responsible for Bella's condition and explicitly says it is his fault.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc4.source_text: My fault, ... Yes, it’s killing her.

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward is convinced that the pregnancy is fatal or severely life-threatening for Bella.
I heard Edward say that he never dreamed a human could conceive with a vampire and that such unions are normally deadly.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc4.source_text: I never dreamed ... How could we know that a human was able conceive a child with one of us— ... No one survives.

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc4.description: I saw Edward beg me to try to reach Bella because he believed my connection to her might make her listen when his would not.
I perceived Edward expressing extreme self-hatred and the belief that even my hatred could not match his own.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc4.source_text: Even you, Jacob Black, cannot hate me as much as I hate myself.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward and the Cullens are not leaving the area and are planning hunting runs and medical procurement instead.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: No. They’re not leaving. Carlisle thinks they’re going to need more blood for Bella soon. He’s going to buy some more.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward does not want to take any risks moving Bella and is determined to keep her where she can be cared for.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: Edward doesn’t want to take any risks moving her.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: I observed that Edward reacted violently to Rosalie’s comment and looked like he might 'rip her head off,' indicating intense protectiveness and anger.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: Edward looked like he was gonna rip her head off.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: I accepted that Edward’s protectiveness is a motivating factor in keeping Bella nearby rather than fleeing immediately.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: Edward doesn’t want to take any risks moving her.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: I felt conflicted about Edward’s choices—angry at the risk but understanding that his decisions aim to protect Bella.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: I had to remind myself that I’d just decided to give the Cullens that exact advice. I wasn’t ready to be logical yet. Still seems stupid.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward is willing to placate Bella now and promises not to cause her pain in the immediate term.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: I’ll deal with whatever comes," he whispered, and he turned his face down and away so that I couldn’t even read his reflection. "I won’t cause her pain now.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward estimates Bella has approximately four days of this fragile hope left.
I saw that Edward chooses to prioritize Bella's short-term happiness over confronting long-term consequences, even if he doubts the plan's viability.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: It was weak of him to let her get her way on this, just to keep her happy now.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: I noticed that Edward was absent from the trail activity despite heavy recent vampire movement.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc3.source_text: I found a heavy, somewhat recent concentration on one particular trail—all of them coming and going here except for Edward.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: I recognized that Edward had returned with his dying pregnant wife, which affected local tensions.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc3.source_text: Some reason for gathering that must have been forgotten when Edward brought his dying pregnant wife home.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: I understood that Edward's and the Cullens' return caused us to pull back our patrol lines out of deference to treaty claims.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc3.source_text: We’d pulled back the lines when the Cullens returned. This was their treaty land.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc4.description: I noticed Edward had Bella in his arms coming down the stairs and that he placed her carefully on the couch.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: The procession came down the stairs then—Edward had Bella this time.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc4.description: I observed that Edward compensated for every tiny movement of his body to keep from jostling her.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: though he compensated for every tiny movement of his body to keep from jostling her, she was hurting.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc4.description: I feared that Edward might lose control and rip Rosalie into small pieces based on Alice's comment.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: Edward’s going to end up ripping Rose into small pieces, I think.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc4.description: I saw Edward sit on the floor by Bella's head, which reinforced my view of him as protective toward her.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: Edward placed Bella carefully on her couch and sat on the floor by her head.

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc1.description: I learned that Edward Cullen is my fiancé and that our wedding is approaching in a matter of days.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc1.source_text: my… my fiancé (there really was no getting around that truth with the wedding just days away).

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc1.description: I understood that loving Edward changes how I perceive danger and makes me unable to run or fight without hurting him.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc1.source_text: When you loved the one who was killing you, it left you no options. How could you run, how could you fight, when doing so would hurt that beloved one?

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc3.description: I heard Edward tell me we would be home in sixteen hours and assure that Carlisle would be ready when we arrived.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: "Don’t be afraid. We’ll be home in sixteen hours. You’ll be fine. Carlisle will be ready when we get there."

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc3.description: I observed Edward switch from speaking Portuguese to a different, guttural pleading voice when addressing the woman.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: I heard Edward speaking Portuguese again. Not only that, but the sound was different, more guttural, the cadence off.

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc3.description: I noticed Edward physically protect me by wrapping his arm across my torso and wiping my tears while also being terse with the visitor.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: He pulled me against his chest. He wiped the tears from my cheeks and murmured in my ear... Edward snapped something at her; I’d never heard him be so impolite before.

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc3.description: I heard Edward say he had forgotten Gustavo was due and that he would get rid of him before returning.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: "Dammit! I forgot Gustavo was due today. I’ll get rid of him and be right back."

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc4.description: I learned that Sam intended to face Edward himself because Edward’s ability to read thoughts made him the greatest threat in Sam’s mind.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: He saw that he would face Edward himself; Edward’s ability to read our thoughts made him the greatest threat in Sam’s mind.

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc4.description: I learned that Sam assigned others to take on Edward and Rosalie and that Carlisle and Alice might be nearby guarding Bella.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: Paul, Jared, and I will take on Edward and Rosalie. I think, from the information Jacob has brought us, they will be the ones guarding Bella. Carlisle and Alice will also be close, possibly Esme.

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc4.description: I accepted that the pack’s tactics were shaped by fear of Edward’s mind-reading, which elevated him to the primary danger in their strategy.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: He saw that he would face Edward himself; Edward’s ability to read our thoughts made him the greatest threat in Sam’s mind.

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc5.description: I discovered that someone had left a stack of light-colored clothes on the Cullen porch that smelled strongly of vampire.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: There was a stack of light-colored fabric on the bottom step of the porch. I loped over to investigate. Holding my breath, because the vampire smell stuck to the fabric like you wouldn’t believe, I nudged the stack with my nose.

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc5.description: I felt that Edward's leaving clothes out for me was a strange but considerate gesture that made me feel a little better.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: Someone had laid out clothes. Huh. Edward must have caught my moment of irritation as I’d bolted out the door. Well. That was… nice. And weird.

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc5.description: I noticed Edward sitting at the other end of the couch with Bella's feet in his lap and offering me a brief smile when I entered.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: Edward sat at the other end of the couch with Bella’s burrito’ed feet in his lap. He looked up when I came in and smiled at me—just a little twitch of his mouth—like something pleased him.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.description: I discovered that the keyless remote I used did not activate the expected Volvo and I unexpectedly activated an Aston Martin Vanquish instead.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: The second part of it was totaling the bloodsucker’s car on my way back. So I was at a loss when I mashed the button on the keyless remote, and it was not his Volvo that beeped and flashed its lights for me. It was another car—a standout even in the long line of vehicles that were mostly all drool-worthy in their own ways. Did he actually mean to give me the keys to an Aston Martin Vanquish, or was that an accident?

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.description: I thought he would be able to buy his way out of trouble if his car drew legal attention and I judged that consequence as unlikely to stick.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: What a letdown. A little chase action might have been nice, not to mention that the license plate info would bring the heat down on the leech. Sure, he’d buy his way out of it, but it might have been just a little inconvenient for him.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.description: I associated the presence of a high-end car with wealth and influence connected to him and I reacted by both resenting and being impressed.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: It was another car—a standout even in the long line of vehicles that were mostly all drool-worthy in their own ways.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward can now make out the child's thoughts and that this mental access reveals the child's advanced development.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: Now that I can make out the child’s thoughts, it’s apparent that he or she has remarkably developed mental facilities. He can understand us, to an extent.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward wants Carlisle to deliver the baby as soon as he returns by noon tomorrow and that Edward believes proceeding now is safe.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: I’m trying to persuade Carlisle to deliver the baby as soon as he is back. By noon tomorrow. Now that I’ve convinced them it’s safe for the child if we proceed, there’s nothing to keep this from working.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc2.description: I learned that Edward told Jacob he thinks of him as a brother and a comrade in arms and that Edward regrets Jacob's suffering.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: I think of you as a… a brother in many ways. A comrade in arms, at the very least. I regret your suffering more than you realize.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc3.description: I observed Edward use his teeth to cut through vampire skin around the newborn to free it quickly.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "Vampire teeth—a surefire way to cut through vampire skin."

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc3.description: I watched Edward snatch the warm, bloody newborn from Bella's arms and murmur to the baby with possessive tenderness.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "Edward had snatched the warm, bloody thing out of her limp arms."

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc3.description: I realized that Edward would give Bella whatever she wanted, even in the midst of chaos and danger.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "I guess I should have known that he would always give her what she wanted, no matter how stupid her request might be."

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc1.description: I observed that Edward commanded the emergency, shouting for morphine and focusing single-mindedly on saving Bella and the baby.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: I quote: "Morphine!" Edward yelled at Rosalie. "The morphine—," Edward growled.

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc1.description: I noticed that Edward feared Rosalie’s loss of control and tried desperately to restrain her when she showed thirst and aggression.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: I quote: "No, Rose!" Edward roared, but his hands were trapped, trying to prop Bella upright so she could breathe.

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc1.description: I realized that Edward relies on Jacob as a trusted helper in life-or-death crises.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: I quote: "Alice, get her out of here!" Edward shouted. "Jacob, I need you!"

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: I saw Edward snatch the warm, bloody newborn from Bella’s limp arms.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc2.source_text: I read: "Edward had snatched the warm, bloody thing out of her limp arms."

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: I observed Edward inject a syringe of venom directly into Bella’s heart while I was performing CPR.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc2.source_text: I read: "His stone hand knocked mine out of the way. There was a tiny crunch as his blow broke my little finger. In the same second, he shoved the needle straight into her heart. 'My venom,' he answered as he pushed the plunger down."

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: I watched Edward bite Bella repeatedly and use his tongue over the wounds to seal them and hold the venom and blood inside her body.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc2.source_text: I read: "I heard the lush tearing of her skin as his teeth bit through, again and again... I saw his pale tongue sweep along the bleeding gashes, but before this could make me either sick or angry, I realized what he was doing. Where his tongue washed the venom over her skin, it sealed shut."

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: I began to see Edward as machine-like and fiercely single-minded in his effort to save Bella.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc2.source_text: I read: "His voice was ice, was dead. Fierce and unthinking. Like he was a machine."

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc3.description: I learned that Edward was obsessively trying to reanimate Bella's corpse and was too consumed to respond.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: He must be too busy now—too far gone in his insane denial, trying to reanimate a corpse—to listen to my plans.

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc3.description: I decided that I wanted Edward to live with nothing rather than to kill him outright as a personal act of vengeance.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: Wouldn’t it be more fair—more satisfying—to let him live with nothing, nothing at all?

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc3.description: I noted that Edward might be capable of putting his family back together if they were harmed.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: Of course, he could probably put those back together, since I wouldn’t be around to burn them.

tw-book1-chapter11_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob's passenger was his father, a heavyset man I recognized as Billy Black.
tw-book1-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: In the passenger seat was a much older man... Jacob's father, Billy Black.

tw-book1-chapter11_Sc4.description: I smiled tentatively at Jacob while he and his father scrutinized me, indicating a familiar but awkward rapport.
tw-book1-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: He was staring at me, scrutinizing my face, so I smiled tentatively at him.

tw-book1-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: "Can you believe my dad paid me twenty bucks to come to your prom?" he admitted, slightly ashamed.

tw-book1-chapter24_Sc3.description: I noticed that Jacob had grown taller and that he reported his height as six-two.
I understood that Jacob's attendance was meant to be a 'safe' place for him to talk to me as his father suggested.
tw-book1-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: He said it was a 'safe' place to talk to you.

tw-book1-chapter24_Sc3.description: I observed Jacob's embarrassment and apologetic demeanor when he approached me on the dance floor.
tw-book1-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: He was clearly uncomfortable — excruciatingly so. His face was apologetic as his eyes met mine.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob appeared to be about fourteen or fifteen and I observed his long glossy black hair, russet-colored skin, and dark eyes.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc6.source_text: I quote 'He looked fourteen, maybe fifteen, and had long, glossy black hair pulled back with a rubber band at the nape of his neck. His skin was beautiful, silky and russet-colored; his eyes were dark...' from the scene.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc6.description: I had my initial positive impression of Jacob's looks altered when I felt his first words were awkward, yet I remained receptive to his friendliness.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc6.source_text: I quote 'Altogether, a very pretty face. However, my positive opinion of his looks was damaged by the first words out of his mouth.' and 'You're Isabella Swan, aren't you?' from the scene.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob was the youngest in his family and I heard that his sisters Rachel and Rebecca were not present because Rachel went to Washington State on scholarship and Rebecca moved to Hawaii after marrying a Samoan surfer.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc6.source_text: I quote 'No, I'm the youngest of the family — you would remember my older sisters.' and 'Rachel got a scholarship to Washington State, and Rebecca married a Samoan surfer — she lives in Hawaii now.' from the scene.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob worked on building cars when he had free time and I heard him jokingly ask about finding a master cylinder for a 1986 Volkswagen Rabbit.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc6.source_text: I quote 'So you build cars? ... You wouldn't happen to know where I could get my hands on a master cylinder for a 1986 Volkswagen Rabbit?' from the scene.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc6.description: I felt increasingly comfortable with Jacob after our conversation and I noticed that others, like Lauren, were watching our interaction with interest or irritation.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc6.source_text: I quote 'He grinned. I couldn't help grinning back.' and 'I wasn't the only one who noticed.' and Lauren's reaction about the Cullens from the scene.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.description: I heard Jacob ask whether Bella had a boyfriend, showing his awareness and possible protectiveness or curiosity.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.source_text: "Is that your boyfriend?" Jacob asked, alerted by the jealous edge in Mike's voice.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.description: I saw Jacob respond with pleasure to Bella's flirtation and I noted his elation at her attention.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.source_text: He smiled, elated by my inept flirting.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.description: I was told by Jacob that he wanted Bella to come see him in Forks once he had his license, indicating an invitation to deepen their connection.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.source_text: "So when I get my license…" he began. "You should come see me in Forks. We could hang out sometime."

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.description: I noticed Jacob teasing Mike as they parted, suggesting a dynamic of rivalry or playful provocation between them.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.source_text: "It was nice to see you again," Jacob said, and I could tell he was taunting Mike just a bit.

tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.description: I saw Mike appraise Jacob and I observed that Mike seemed satisfied by Jacob's obvious youth.
tw-book1-chapter6_Sc8.source_text: I could see his eyes appraising Jacob, and looking satisfied at his obvious youth.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc2.description: I felt more afraid of Jacob's potential for violence after witnessing his transformation and attack impulse.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc2.source_text: I remembered 'Jacob panics' and 'lunges toward Edward'.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc2.description: I recognized Jacob as protective yet volatile in his relation to me and to Edward within the dream.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc2.source_text: I recalled 'pulled back by Jacob' and 'lunges toward Edward'.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc4.description: I noticed that Jacob's accounts contrast with both the folklore and the Cullens' observed behavior, highlighting divergent perspectives.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I read: 'She sifts through myths and folklore, comparing entries with what she and Jacob have said and with her own observations of the Cullens.'

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc5.description: I noted that Jacob was not present with me during this walk and that I was alone in the forest while I deliberated.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: I walked into the forest alone and Jacob was not present.

tw-book1-chapter7_Sc5.description: I observed that my relationship with Jacob was unchanged in this scene because he was absent and did not figure into my immediate deliberation.
tw-book1-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: I did not interact with Jacob and my thoughts focused on the Cullens instead.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob Black is an old family friend who I ran into at the beach.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "I ran into an old family friend —Jacob Black,"

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob's dad is identified as one of the Quileute elders and that Jacob was telling legends to scare me.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "His dad is one of the Quileute elders." "We went for a walk — and he was telling me some old legends — trying to scare me, I think."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: I realized that Jacob himself thought the vampire stories were silly and that he did not expect me to take them seriously.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.source_text: "He just thought it was a silly superstition," I said quickly. "He didn't expect me to think anything of it."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc2.description: I admitted that I manipulated Jacob by tricking the information out of him and I now feel a responsibility to protect him from fallout.

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned from my conversation that Jacob had told me the Cullens didn't hunt people and that their family was supposed to hunt animals.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: "He said you didn't… hunt people. He said your family wasn't supposed to be dangerous because you only hunted animals."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob also said the Quileutes still didn't want the Cullens on their land as a precaution.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: "The Quileutes still didn't want you on their land, just in case."

tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.description: I found that I no longer let Jacob's warnings determine my willingness to be with Edward.
tw-book1-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: "I decided it didn't matter," I whispered. "Well, Jacob said something about that."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.description: I was told that Jacob had been taken to the doctor and that he looked like he had mono and was very tired.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: Billy took Jake to the doc down there, and it looks like he has mono. He's real tired, and Billy said no visitors,

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.description: I doubted that Jacob's illness timeline fit mono because he had said he felt 'fit as a fiddle' earlier and lacked typical early symptoms.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: No horrible sore throat, no exhaustion, no headaches, at least not before he'd gone home from the movie; he'd said he felt "fit as a fiddle."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.description: I wondered why Billy would lie to Harry and I became suspicious that something else might be going on with Jacob.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: Why would Billy lie to Harry?

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob apparently followed Billy's rule and did not leave messages during the week I was away.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.source_text: When I'd decided to leave Billy and Jacob alone for a week, I hadn't really believed that Jacob would go along with Billy's rule. There never were any.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: I depended on Jacob for distraction and comfort, and I noticed that his absence intensified my despair and nightmares.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.source_text: Without Jacob, and my adrenaline and my distractions, everything I'd been repressing started creeping up on me.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.description: I attempted to reach Jacob multiple times and I planned to go to La Push to see him if phone contact failed.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc2.source_text: I cheated three times by trying to call him, but the phone lines still weren't working. I dialed, and then waited without high expectations.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob was giving friends a ride to Port Angeles and that they were likely going to catch a double feature.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: "He's giving some friends a ride up to Port Angeles—I think they were going to catch a double feature or something."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob was gone for the whole day and not at home.
I learned that Jacob's diagnosis was not mono but some other virus.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: "Turns out it wasn't mono after all. Just some other virus."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: I realized that Jacob was better but did not call me even though he was out with friends.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: Jacob was better, but not well enough to call me. He was out with friends.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: I suspected that Jacob had changed his mind about our relationship and might be choosing not to pursue me.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: Jacob must have changed his mind, just like I'd feared. He was going to take my advice and not waste any more time on someone who couldn't return his feelings.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.description: I learned that Billy would tell Jacob that I had called.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: "Well, I'll tell him that you called," Billy promised.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob was out that day, which prompted Charlie's offer to stay with me.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.source_text: "Say, did you want me to stay with you, since Jake's out?"

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.description: I felt that Jacob was absent and that his return might be uncertain, which made me anxious.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.source_text: "whenever Jacob decided to honor me with his presence again. I refused to think about how long that might be. Or if it was going to be never."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.description: I noticed that Charlie thought my other friends might feel forgotten because I had been spending so much time with Jacob.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc4.source_text: "That's a good idea. You've been spending so much time with Jacob, your other friends are going to think you've forgotten them."

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: I found that getting started took me longer than it would have taken Jacob.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.source_text: Getting started took me longer than it would have taken Jacob.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: I missed Jacob's carefree whistle and the sound of another pair of feet squishing across the damp ground while I was alone in the forest.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.source_text: I knew it was just because I was alone, missing Jacob's carefree whistle and the sound of another pair of feet squishing across the damp ground.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.description: I realized I relied on Jacob's presence for a sense of ease and company in the woods.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc5.source_text: I knew it was just because I was alone, missing Jacob's carefree whistle and the sound of another pair of feet squishing across the damp ground.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: I believed Jacob would have noticed my breakdown and that I could not have disguised the abyss I was plunging into if he had been there.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.source_text: If I'd discovered the meadow with Jacob… well, there was no way I could have disguised the abyss I was plunging into now.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: I assumed Jacob would have expected me to spend more time in the meadow after he went to the trouble to find it.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.source_text: Jacob would have assumed, after going to so much trouble to locate the stupid place, I would want to spend more than a few seconds here.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.description: I felt fortunate to be alone and repeated the word 'Alone' with grim satisfaction because I did not want him to witness my collapse.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc6.source_text: How lucky that I was alone! Alone. I repeated the word with grim satisfaction as I wrenched myself to my feet despite the pain.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.description: I felt gratitude toward Jacob for not being there and relief that he would be safe from the immediate danger.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.source_text: At least Jacob wasn't going to die, too. At least I wouldn't have his death on my hands.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.description: I inferred that the wolves had an intelligence or familiarity that made me think of Jacob when I met the reddish-brown wolf's gaze.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.source_text: The wolf's eyes were dark, nearly black. It gazed at me for a fraction of a second, the deep eyes seeming too intelligent for a wild animal. As it stared at me, I suddenly thought of Jacob—again, with gratitude.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.description: I became more confident that Jacob was not in immediate mortal danger during this encounter.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc10.source_text: At least Jacob wasn't going to die, too. At least I wouldn't have his death on my hands.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.description: I heard that Jacob was seen outside the store arguing with his friends and that he looked upset and different.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.source_text: Well, it's just that when I went to pick up Harry, I saw Jacob out in front of the store down there with some of his friends. I waved hi, but he… well, I guess I don't know if he saw me. I think maybe he was arguing with his friends. He looked strange, like he was upset about something. And… different.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.description: I wondered if Jacob had ditched me to confront Embry about the situation with Sam and felt that possibility made sense of his absence.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.source_text: I wondered if he had confronted Embry about the situation with Sam. Maybe that was the reason he'd ditched me today—if it meant he could sort things out with Embry, I was glad he had.

tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.description: I felt relieved that Jacob might prioritize resolving conflicts with his friends and pack over spending the day with me, indicating his loyalty to his group responsibilities.
tw-book2-chapter10_Sc13.source_text: If it meant he could sort things out with Embry, I was glad he had.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob had been avoiding me and that my phone calls to him went unanswered.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: I called him Tuesday, but no one answered. ... On Wednesday I called every half hour until after eleven at night, desperate to hear the warmth of Jacob's voice.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.description: I learned that other boys on the reservation were behaving strangely and that the same phenomenon had reached Jacob.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: Jacob told me about some strange stuff happening with the other boys his age. Now he's acting the same way and I'm scared.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.description: I realized that Jacob had been "sucked into Sam's cult" and that Sam Uley had influence over him.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: He'd been sucked into Sam's cult.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.description: I realized with a rush of feeling that Jacob had not given up on me despite his distance and changed behavior.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: He hadn't given up on me at all, I realized with a rush of feeling.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.description: I observed that members of Jacob's community, like Billy and Harry, provided vague or incomplete information about Jacob's whereabouts and activities.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: Harry reported that Billy had attended the council meeting Wednesday night, and never mentioned anything about leaving. ... Billy's vague, unhelpful answers.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc2.description: I noticed Jacob's physical changes including cropped short glossy hair, a hardened face, thicker neck and shoulders, and enlarged hands.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: Jacob had changed radically in the last weeks since I'd seen him. The first thing I noticed was his hair—his beautiful hair was all gone, cropped quite short, covering his head with an inky gloss like black satin. The planes of his face seemed to have hardened subtly, tightened… His neck and his shoulders were different, too, thicker somehow. His hands, where they gripped the window frame, looked enormous, with the tendons and veins more prominent under the russet skin.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob had been seen with Embry and that witnesses thought Sam and his crew might have been present.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: "From a distance," he finally said. "I tried to follow them—he was with Embry." / "I think Sam and his crew might have been with them."

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc2.description: I realized that Jacob had aligned himself with Sam's group and that he was no longer avoiding the others as he had before.
I found Jacob almost unrecognizable and I felt that the familiar friendly connection was gone.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: The open, friendly smile was gone like the hair

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob believed Sam was helping him but that Jacob ultimately blamed the Cullens for the harm he described.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: "He's helping me as much as he can." "If you want to blame someone, why don't you point your finger at those filthy, reeking bloodsuckers that you love so much?"
