tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.description: I noticed that Jacob's perspective shifted from confusion about Sam to a fervent anger that assigned blame to the Cullens and to existence itself.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: "I didn't understand him before." "For existing," he hissed.

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.description: I observed that Jacob withdrew emotionally and physically from me by cringing away, refusing touch, and walking off when the argument escalated.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: "Don't touch me," he whispered. "Let's head back. There's nothing more to say."

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.description: I saw that Jacob experienced overwhelming despair, stating that no one could help him and expressing that the damage was already done.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: "No one can help me now." "It doesn't matter anyway, the damage is done."

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.description: I was told by Jacob, and later understood, that Sam Uley had declared Jacob could not be my friend anymore.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "Sam Uley says Jacob can't be my friend anymore."

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.description: I began to believe that Jacob was hiding something bigger than an unrequited crush and I suspected a secret motive behind his actions.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "There was much more to this than an unrequited crush, and it surprised me that Billy would stoop to claiming that."

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.description: I felt that Jacob's behavior had wounded me emotionally and I perceived our friendship as compromised and painful.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "He'd just been carving out his own hole, so that I was now riddled through like Swiss cheese."

tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.description: I dreamed that Jacob transformed into a pale, golden-eyed, beautiful figure whose changing features echoed something other than the Jacob I knew.
tw-book2-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "The smooth suppleness of his walk reminded me of someone else, and, as I watched, his features started to change. The russet color of his skin leached away, leaving his face pale white like bone. His eyes turned gold, and then crimson, and then back to gold again. His shorn hair twisted in the breeze, turning bronze where the wind touched it."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.description: I heard Jacob say he had come to apologize when he was in my room.
I noticed Jacob was shirtless and that his skin was burning hot like he had a fever.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: He wasn't wearing a shirt, though the air blowing in the window was cold enough to make me shiver, and it made me uncomfortable to have my hands on his bare chest. His skin was burning hot, like his head had been the last time I'd touched him.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.description: I watched Jacob clinging precariously to the top of the spruce with his weight bowing the tree and his legs dangling twenty feet above the ground.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: Jacob was clinging precariously to the top of the spruce that grew in the middle of Charlie's little front yard. His weight had bowed the tree toward the house and he now swung—his legs dangling twenty feet above the ground...

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.description: I felt Jacob's wide grin was not the grin I had loved but a new, bitter mockery that belonged to Sam.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: A wide grin spread slowly across Jacob's face; he seemed extremely pleased with himself. It wasn't the grin that I knew and loved—it was a new grin, one that was a bitter mockery of his old sincerity, on the new face that belonged to Sam.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.description: I felt that Jacob had harshly rejected me earlier and that his rejection had punched a painful new hole in what was left of my chest.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc1.source_text: His harsh rejection had punched a painful new hole in what was left of my chest.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob came to apologize and that he claimed he could not fully explain because of a secret tied to loyalty.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: "I'm so sorry, Bella." "But I can't explain," he said, still angry. "I wish I could." "Sometimes, loyalty gets in the way of what you want to do. Sometimes, it's not your secret to tell."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc2.description: I noticed that Jacob believed Bella already knew his secret and that he became frustrated and urgent when asking her to guess it.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: "The part that kills me," he said abruptly, "is that you already know. I already told you everything!" "I think I see a way to make this work out—because you know this, Bella! I can't tell you, but if you guessed it! That would let me right off the hook!"

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc2.description: I perceived Jacob's intensity and closeness when he held Bella's face and whispered, which increased emotional and possibly romantic tension between them.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: "He took my face in his enormous, too-warm hands and held it just a few inches from his. He stared into my eyes while he whispered, as if to communicate something besides the words he spoke."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.description: I saw Jacob grab my hand, pull me toward the darkest part of the forest, and whisper urgently that I had to run.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: And then Jacob was there. He grabbed my hand, pulling me back toward the blackest part of the forest. "Run, Bella, you have to run!" he whispered, terrified.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.description: I witnessed Jacob fall to the ground and transform into an enormous, red-brown wolf with dark, intelligent, black-brown eyes.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: Jacob dropped my hand and yelped. Shaking and twitching, he fell to the ground at my feet. In his place was an enormous, red-brown wolf with dark, intelligent eyes. The black-brown, familiar eyes of Jacob Black.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.description: I understood Jacob as both a frightened boy with a ponytail and as a monstrous, intelligent wolf, which changed how I perceived him in my memories and dreams.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc3.source_text: His face was the frightened face of a boy, and his hair was beautiful again, swept back into a ponytail on the nape of his neck. This was the great russet wolf I'd stood half a foot from in the meadow, just a week ago.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: I heard Jacob explain Quileute legends and that he was knowledgeable about old stories of wolves and the cold ones.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.source_text: "Do you know any of our old stories, about where we came from—the Quileutes, I mean?" "Well, there are lots of legends..."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: I understood from Jacob that the tribe holds a legend of descent from wolves and that tribal law forbids killing those wolves.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.source_text: "Another legend claims that we descended from wolves—and that the wolves are our brothers still. It's against tribal law to kill them."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: I learned from Jacob that his family line included a tribal elder who negotiated with the cold ones, linking Jacob's family to supernatural history.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.source_text: "According to legend, my own great-grandfather knew some of them. He was the one who made the treaty that kept them off our land."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.description: I realized that Jacob was part of a werewolf pack, visualizing a pack of five gigantic, multihued wolves and understanding Jacob's deeper, nonhuman identity.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc4.source_text: "A pack of five mind-blowingly gigantic, multihued werewolves that had stalked right past me in Edward's meadow…"

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc5.description: I learned that my best friend Jacob was a werewolf.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc5.source_text: It was bad enough that my best friend was a werewolf.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc5.description: I observed that Jacob had been out late frequently and appeared weary with circles under his eyes.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc5.source_text: He's out late a lot these days. Kid needs his rest—probably you shouldn't wake him. ... There were circles under his eyes that I hadn't noticed before.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc5.description: I recognized that Jacob remained my friend whether he killed people or not and that my feelings for him complicated any logical response.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc5.source_text: Jacob was my friend whether he killed people or not. ... Love didn't work that way, I decided. Once you cared about a person, it was impossible to be logical about them anymore.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob directly denied being a murderer and asserted that he was not a killer.
I understood that Jacob sincerely believes in his role as a protector despite the ongoing disappearances and Bella's fears.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc6.source_text: We're trying to do our job, Bella. We're trying to protect them, but we're always just a little too late.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc6.description: I noticed Jacob's anger shifted to affection and apology, and I observed his sincerity when I studied his face.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc6.source_text: I studied his face, and it was clear that this was the truth.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.description: I learned that Jacob will transform into a wolf if he gets too mad and that the change does not require a full moon.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.source_text: "I'd turn into a wolf," he whispered back. and "You don't need a full moon."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.description: I noticed Jacob felt guilt for losing control and vowed to keep a better hold on himself around me.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.source_text: "That was pretty stupid of me. I have to keep a better hold on myself. I swore I wasn't going to get mad, no matter what you said to me."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.description: I observed Jacob act physically protective and nurturing when I became overwhelmed and sick with fear.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.source_text: "He draped me awkwardly across his lap, laying my limp head against his shoulder. He brushed the sweaty hair back from my face."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.description: I learned that Jacob intends to call a meeting and mobilize the pack to determine Victoria's motives and to defend the community.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc7.source_text: "I'll call a meeting. Hey, wait here for just a minute, okay?" and "This is exactly what we needed to know. We've got to tell the others right away."

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.description: I learned that Jacob can shift into a wolf to communicate with Sam and that he tried not to think about me during the change so the pack would not notice.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.source_text: I kept it real short—I tried not to think about you so they wouldn't know what was going on.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.description: I learned that Sam told Jacob he couldn't tell me certain things and that Jacob respects Sam's authority as Alpha.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.source_text: Sam told me I couldn't tell you. He's... the head of the pack, you know. He's the Alpha.

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.description: I noticed that Jacob felt morose and burdened by secrets and that he felt guilt about not being able to fully explain things to me.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.source_text: "Well, it would have stopped me," Jacob said, morose now. "Remember how I couldn't finish my sentences last night? How I couldn't just tell you the whole story?"

tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.description: I felt Jacob's protectiveness and reassurance when he squeezed my hand and led me toward the pack meeting.
tw-book2-chapter12_Sc8.source_text: Jake took my hand and squeezed it. "Here we go."

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc1.description: I learned that my best friend Jacob was a werewolf when I thought about what Billy and the town were doing.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: It was bad enough that my best friend was a werewolf.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc1.description: I observed Jacob sleeping stretched across his small bed and I noticed that he looked very young and very weary.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: Despite his ridiculous size, he looked very young now, and very weary.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc1.description: I noticed that Jacob slept deeply and peacefully with the angry lines smoothed out on his face.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc1.source_text: His face was peaceful with (deep sleep, all the angry lines smoothed out.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc1.description: I heard Jacob greet me softly on the beach which told me he had come to find me as dawn approached.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob insisted he is not a killer and that killing Laurent did not count against him because Laurent was a vampire.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.source_text: "I'm not a killer." "Now, I don't count that towards the whole murder thing," he added quickly.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob and his pack killed Laurent easily as a collective action during the meadow incident.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.source_text: "Oh, the black-haired leech?" He grinned... "Was that his name?" "Killing the bloodsucker who was going to kill you. Now, I don't count that towards the whole murder thing," he added quickly. "Vampires don't count as people."

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob framed the pack's violence as protective duty and that they try to be timely but are sometimes a little too late.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.source_text: "We're trying to do our job, Bella. We're trying to protect them, but we're always just a little too late."

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.description: I noticed that Jacob believed killing vampires was justified because vampires are the pack's enemy and not considered people.
I observed Jacob apologize, hug me, and express joy and protectiveness, indicating a closer, more trusting relationship with me.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.source_text: "You really, honestly don't mind that I morph into a giant dog?" he asked... "I'm not a killer, Bella." I threw my arms around him.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob did not initially tell me the pack's secret and that he worried being around me when angry could cause harm.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc2.source_text: "I wasn't supposed to tell you our secret, for one thing, but the other part is that it's not safe for you. If I get too mad… too upset… you might get hurt."

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.description: I noticed that Jacob can shift quickly and move through the forest with animal grace when he runs.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.source_text: He flitted into the trees, swift and sleek as a deer.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob uses short, controlled shifts to communicate with the pack and to hide thoughts about me when necessary.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.source_text: I kept it real short—I tried not to think about you so they wouldn't know what was going on.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.description: I experienced Jacob as both protective and embarrassed by pack rules, which made his promise to guard me feel sincere but constrained.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.source_text: "I kept it real short—I tried not to think about you so they wouldn't know what was going on. I was afraid Sam would tell me I couldn't bring you."

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.description: I realized that Jacob respects Sam's authority deeply and that pack hierarchy shapes what he can tell me or do.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc3.source_text: Sam told me I couldn't tell you. He's… the head of the pack, you know. He's the Alpha. When he tells us to do something, or not to do something—when he really means it, well, we can't just ignore him.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: I noticed that Jacob's hands had trembled earlier with rage.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: My hands were trembling like Jacob's had been before, but with fear rather than rage.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: I felt Jacob take my hand and squeeze it.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: Jake took my hand and squeezed it.

tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.description: I felt closer and more reassured by Jacob's physical support in that moment.
tw-book2-chapter13_Sc4.source_text: Jake took my hand and squeezed it.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob can transform instantaneously into a gigantic russet brown wolf capable of fighting other werewolves.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: One second it was Jacob diving into the air, and then it was the gigantic, russet brown wolf—so enormous that I couldn't make sense of its mass somehow fitting inside Jacob—charging the crouched silver beast.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc1.description: I observed Jacob act protectively by placing himself between me and the threatening boys and confronting the silver wolf.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: Jacob met the other werewolf's attack head-on.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc1.description: I came to believe that Jacob's physical size and strength were approaching Sam's and that he could hold his own in a fight.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc1.source_text: Sam was still the biggest, though Jacob was getting close to catching up with him.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob will take the inner perimeter with Sam as part of the trap plan.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: Paul, Jared, and Embry will take the outer perimeter, and Jacob and I will take the inner. We'll collapse in when we've got her trapped.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.description: I noticed Jacob's protectiveness and reassurance when he told me not to be afraid and promised the pack would be watching.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: Don't be afraid tonight," Jacob said. "We'll be out there, watching.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.description: I realized that Jacob treats hunting vampires as something he enjoys and as the best part of the situation.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: Hunting vampires is fun. It's the best part of this whole mess.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.description: I saw Jacob eat an entire pizza by himself after Charlie brought two pizzas.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: Jacob ate one all by himself.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.description: I expected Jacob to run off as a wolf at night once Charlie and I left.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: I knew that as soon as Charlie and I were headed home, Jacob would take off—off to run around as a wolf, as he had done intermittently through the entire day.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.description: I heard Jacob mumble that he wouldn't hurt her while looking down.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: "I won't hurt her," Jacob mumbled, looking down.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob immediately comforted me when he found me curled up and wrapped his arms around my shoulders.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: Jacob found me like that, and I could tell from his expression that he understood. 'Sorry,' he said right away. He pulled me up from the ground and wrapped both arms around my shoulders.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.description: I discovered that Jacob promised to take tomorrow morning off and suggested doing something fun for me.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: 'I'll take tomorrow morning off. The others can run without me. We'll do something fun.'

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.description: I heard Jacob recall a promise to take me cliff diving and call the outing a date, even draping his arm around my shoulders.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: 'Didn't I promise to take you cliff diving?' ... 'It's a date,' he said, and draped his arm around my shoulders.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob left with Sam to help after Embry, Jared, and Paul crossed a fresh trail early that morning.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: Embry, Jared, and Paul crossed a fresh trail early this morning. Sam and Jake took off to help.

tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.description: I realized that I was getting deeper with Jacob without consciously deciding to and that I made him seem normal despite our complications.
tw-book2-chapter14_Sc3.source_text: I was getting in deeper and deeper with Jacob without ever having consciously decided to progress in that direction and I didn't know what to do about it ... I made the werewolf seem downright normal.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.description: I heard Jacob apologize for ditching me so much.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: he apologized for ditching me so much.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob's schedule wasn't always this crazy and that the wolves were on red alert until Victoria was stopped.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: He told me his schedule wasn't always this crazy, but until Victoria was stopped, the wolves were on red alert.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.description: I realized that Jacob would have loved for things to be what they appeared between us.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: I knew that Jacob would have loved for things to be what they appeared.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.description: I noticed that his hand felt nice as it warmed mine and that I didn't protest.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: But his hand felt nice as it warmed mine, and I didn't protest.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob followed Bella on his bike to make sure she arrived safely.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: I worked Tuesday afternoon—Jacob followed me on his bike to make sure I arrived safely—and Mike noticed.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob is identified as the kid from La Push and that he is a sophomore.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: "Are you dating that kid from La Push? The sophomore?" He Asked, poorly disguising the resentment in his tone.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc2.description: I realized that Jacob is head over heels for Bella.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: Mike's eyes narrowed shrewdly. "Don't kid yourself, Bella. The guy's head over heels for you."

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc2.description: I inferred that Jacob is protective of Bella because he followed her to ensure her safety.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: I worked Tuesday afternoon—Jacob followed me on his bike to make sure I arrived safely—and Mike noticed.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob promised to take me cliff diving and explicitly called the outing a "date."
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: "Didn't I promise to take you cliff diving?" "It's a date," he said, and draped his arm around my shoulders.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.description: I heard Jacob offer to take the next morning off so he could do something fun with me.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: "I'll take tomorrow morning off. The others can run without me. We'll do something fun."

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.description: I felt Jacob's physical warmth and comfort when he wrapped his arms around me, which helped me breathe and feel cared for.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: He pulled me up from the ground and wrapped both arms around my shoulders. I hadn't realized that I was cold until then. His warmth made me shudder, but at least I could breathe with him there.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.description: I began to see Jacob as someone who would deliberately try to lift my spirits by planning carefree activities.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: "Fun is exactly what you need. Hmm…" he gazed out across the heaving gray waves, deliberating. "Got it!" he crowed. "Another promise to keep."

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc6.description: I observed that Jacob is not present in this scene and that the space in front of me was empty.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc6.source_text: I stepped out to the edge, keeping my eyes on the empty space in front of me.

tw-book2-chapter15_Sc6.description: I felt alone with Edward's voice in my head rather than feeling Jacob's presence or influence during the jump.
tw-book2-chapter15_Sc6.source_text: He sounded so real, so close. It was only when he was disapproving like this that I could hear the true memory of his voice—the velvet texture and the musical intonation that made up the most perfect of all voices.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob tracked my truck by following the tire tracks and then heard my scream before finding me.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.source_text: I followed the tire tracks to your truck, and then I heard you scream…

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob carried me up the beach and toward his house while shielding me from the rain.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.source_text: He slid his arms under me and lifted me without effort—like picking up an empty box. His chest was bare and warm; he hunched his shoulders to keep the rain off of me.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.description: I noticed that Jacob's relief quickly turned to anger and worry when he realized the risk I had taken.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.source_text: "Why would you jump, Bella? Didn't you notice that it's turning into a hurricane out here? Couldn't you have waited for me?" Anger filled his tone as the relief faded.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.description: I observed that Jacob's protectiveness and frustration reflect a deeper caring and responsibility toward me.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc2.source_text: Look, do you mind saving the stupid stuff for when I'm around? I won't be able to concentrate if I think you're jumping off cliffs behind my back.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.description: I watched Jacob offer me dry clothes, insist I stay, and promise to get more while he left me to change.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: "These will be huge on you, but it's the best I've got. I'll, er, step outside so you can change."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.description: I observed Jacob sit on the floor next to the couch, lean his head on the cushion, yawn, and fall asleep while I rested.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: Jacob sat on the floor next to me, his back against the couch. He leaned his head on the cushion next to mine and yawned. "Guess I could rest for a minute…" His eyes closed.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.description: I felt comforted by Jacob's nearness and perceived him as attentive and protective in that moment.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: Don't go anywhere. I'm too tired to move yet. Just stay with me." Jacob sat on the floor next to me, his back against the couch. "Jacob's slow, deep breathing was the only sound in the room—...It was the sound of comfort.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.description: I wondered when Jacob had last slept and concluded that he seemed as exhausted as I felt, which made me more aware of his sacrifices.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc3.source_text: I wondered when he'd slept last. He looked as exhausted as I felt.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob was still committed to hunting the vampire and that he explicitly said he was not going home because they hadn't caught the bloodsucker.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: "I'm not going home. We still haven't caught the bloodsucker, remember?"

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.description: I noticed Jacob's pain made his face suddenly childlike and I began to see his grief as raw and almost boyish.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: "The pain made his face suddenly childlike—it looked odd on top of the man's body."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.description: I felt Jacob's tenderness when he caught my hand, held it to his face, and later kept his arm tight around me while driving me home.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: "After a long moment, Jacob caught my hand and held it to his face." "He helped me up from the couch without speaking, keeping his arm around my shoulder... and then pulled me next to his side to keep his arm tight around me."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob was willing to take responsibility for my truck and drive me home to be there when Charlie returned.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: "I'll go get your truck and then take you home—you probably ought to be there when Charlie gets back."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.description: I watched Jacob stop the truck in front of my dark house, cut the engine, and throw his arm around me, crushing me against his chest.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: I observed: "Jacob stopped the truck in front of my dark house, cutting the engine so it was suddenly silent... He threw his other arm around me, crushing me against his chest..."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.description: I knew that Jacob would likely accept me despite my brokenness and that he would not pause to think it through before taking me in.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: I remembered: "He wouldn't even pause to think it through... But, even as I recognized that necessity, I knew he would take me in spite of it all."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.description: I felt that Jacob provided warmth, comfort, and familiarity and that giving him a small physical affection would be very easy.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: I read: "It just felt nice—warm and comforting and familiar. Safe... If I turned my face to the side—if I pressed my lips against his bare shoulder... I knew without any doubt what would follow. It would be very easy."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.description: I detected a vampire by scent and announced its presence aloud.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.source_text: "Vampire," he spit out. "Because I can smell it. Dammit!"

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.description: I moved from stunned alarm to urgent decision-making, weighing whether to phase or to remove Bella immediately.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.source_text: "Phase or get her out of here?" he hissed at himself.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.description: I acted protectively toward Bella, committing to get her out and physically steering the truck toward their escape.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.source_text: "Right. Get you out." The engine caught with a roar. The tires squealed as he spun the truck around, turning toward our only escape.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.description: I felt horror and agitation when Bella identified Carlisle's car, indicating the Cullens' presence.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc6.source_text: He watched dawn break across my face, and a violent tremor rocked his frame.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc7.description: I learned that Jacob refused to return to the house because he considered its occupants his enemies.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc7.source_text: "I can't go back. Treaty or no treaty, that's my enemy in there."

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc7.description: I realized Jacob was emotionally shaken and that he put distance between us by leaving abruptly.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc7.source_text: He sprinted into the darkness, shaking so hard that his shape seemed blurred; he disappeared before I could open my mouth to call him back.

tw-book2-chapter16_Sc7.description: I recognized Jacob's refusal as a personal betrayal and saw our relationship as strained.
tw-book2-chapter16_Sc7.source_text: Jacob's face hardened while I stared at him, congealing into the bitter mask that I'd thought was gone for good.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc2.description: I noted that Jacob's friends cliff dive and that their behavior inspired my decision to try cliff diving.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: "I'd seen some of Jacob's friends cliff diving,"

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc2.description: I recognized that my mention of Jacob's friends was used to explain my motivation for jumping rather than intending self-harm.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: "I'd seen some of Jacob's friends cliff diving," ... "It looked like… fun, and I was bored…"

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob is the person who saved Bella by jumping into the lake, pulling her out, and towing her to shore.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: It's true that I probably would have drowned if Jacob hadn't jumped in after me. Well, okay, there's no probably about it. But he did, and he pulled me out, and I guess he towed me back to shore, though I was kind of out for that part.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob is described as strong by Bella when she explains how he managed the rescue.
I learned that Jacob is identified by Bella as 'sort of a werewolf,' connecting him to the Quileute wolf transformations.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: "See, well, he's… sort of a werewolf," I admitted in a rush. "The Quileutes turn into wolves when there are vampires around."

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.description: I noticed Bella's ambivalence toward Jacob when she called him sort of her best friend and then added that he was, indicating a shift in their relationship.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: "Jacob Black. He's… sort of my best friend, I guess. At least, he was…"

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob is identified as Bella's best friend and a werewolf.
I learned that Jacob's transformation to a werewolf is recent, only a few weeks old.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: 'He's only been a werewolf for just a few weeks.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.description: I remembered that Jacob had been involved in a physical fight with Paul on the road.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: wincing as I remembered Paul and Jacob fighting in the road.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.description: I understood that Bella views Jacob and his wolf friends as defenders who prevented vampires like Laurent from getting her.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: 'If it weren't for Jake and his friends, Laurent would have gotten me before she could, I guess, so—'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.description: I observed that Bella defends werewolves as necessary allies despite their potential for violence when angry.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: 'There's nothing wrong with werewolves,' I grumbled, stung by her critical tone. 'Until they lose their tempers.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob said he was calling just to make sure I was still alive and then hung up.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc6.source_text: 'Just making sure you were still alive,' Jacob said sourly. 'Bye.' Jacob hung up on me.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc6.description: I perceived Jacob's tone as sour and possibly hostile during the call.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc6.source_text: 'Just making sure you were still alive,' Jacob said sourly.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.description: I learned Jacob is younger than Bella by about a year, has matured from caring for his father, and is considered good-looking.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.source_text: 'He's a year or so younger than her, and I know she used to think of him as a friend... Jake's old for his years,' he continued, still sounding defensive. 'He's taken care of his father physically the way Bella took care of her mother emotionally. It matured him. He's a good-looking kid, too—takes after his mom's side.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.description: I learned Charlie views Jacob as good for Bella and expressed a defensive, almost belligerent concern about their growing closeness.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.source_text: 'He's a year or so younger than her, and I know she used to think of him as a friend, but I think maybe it's something more now, or headed that direction, anyway.' Charlie said this in a tone that was almost belligerent. 'He's good for Bella, you know,' Charlie insisted.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.description: I believe Jacob's presence has measurably improved Bella's mood and outward signs of well-being.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc9.source_text: 'Ever since she started hanging out with Jacob Black, I've noticed a real improvement. She has some color in her cheeks when she comes home, some light in her eyes. She's happier.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc12.description: I realized that the visitor at the door might be Jacob Black or one of his friends because Alice explicitly suggested it.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc12.source_text: 'If this is a repeat of my egregious lapse in foresight yesterday, then it's most likely Jacob Black or one of his… friends.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc12.description: I began to associate Jacob Black with a potential werewolf presence at the house after Alice's speculation and her inability to see werewolves.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc12.source_text: 'If this is a repeat of my egregious lapse in foresight yesterday, then it's most likely Jacob Black or one of his… friends.' 'You can't see werewolves?' She grimaced. 'So it would seem.'

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc13.description: I learned that Alice explicitly warned that being in a room with Jacob Black would be a bad idea.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc13.source_text: Trust me—it wouldn't be a good idea to have me and Jacob Black in a room together.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc13.description: I perceived that Alice and Jacob Black would likely have a contentious or problematic interaction if left alone together.
tw-book2-chapter17_Sc13.source_text: She laughed her silvery little laugh—it had a dark edge.

tw-book2-chapter17_Sc13.description: I became convinced that Jacob's imminent presence or arrival was the reason Alice chose to leave abruptly.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: I observed that Jacob arrived hostile and with trembling hands despite trying to appear masklike.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: Hostility rolled off of him in waves. ... I could see the faint trembling of his hands.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob's friends were nearby because they were afraid to let him come alone.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: Jacob's Rabbit idled by the curb with Jared behind the wheel and Embry in the passenger seat. I understood what this meant: they were afraid to let him come here alone.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: I heard Jacob warn that the Quileute can only protect their lands with a Cullen present and that I would only be safe in La Push.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: You should know that we can only watch our own lands with a Cullen here. You'll only be safe in La Push.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: I noticed Jacob shift from a serene mask to anxious uncertainty when I began to cry.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: His face smoothed into a serene mask." ... "Jacob's calm expression was gone; his face was anxious and unsure.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.description: I saw revulsion in Jacob's eyes toward my association with the Cullens and I recognized that our relationship is strained.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: I could see the revulsion in his eyes.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob will miss Bella intensely and hopes Alice leaves soon because his love for Alice prevents him from being near her.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.source_text:
"I'll miss you," Jacob whispered, echoing my thoughts. "Every minute. I hope she leaves soon."

"Yes, it really does. Bella. You… love her. So I'd better not get anywhere near her."

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.description: I realized that Jacob believed he could lose control, break the treaty, and possibly kill a friend if he stayed near Alice.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.source_text: "I'm not sure that I'm even-tempered enough to handle that. Sam would be mad if I broke the treaty, and"—his voice turned sarcastic—"you probably wouldn't like it too much if I killed your friend."

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.description: I observed Jacob seize the phone, lie to Dr. Carlisle Cullen by saying "He's not here" and then say "He's at the funeral," and then angrily call the Cullens a "filthy bloodsucker" before abruptly leaving.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc2.source_text:
"Swan residence," Jacob said, his husky voice low and intense.

"He's not here," Jacob said, and the words were menacing.

"He's at the funeral."

"Filthy bloodsucker," he muttered under his breath.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.description: I observed Jacob tell Carlisle that Charlie was at the funeral and then hang up, which contributed to the misinformation and confusion about my status.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: I read: "He said, 'He's not here,' and when Carlisle asked where Charlie was, Jacob said, 'At the funeral.'"

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.description: I noticed that Jacob was physically trembling and gripping my arm for my balance while trying to shield me from Alice and the conversation.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: I read: "He was the one shaking, not the couch." "I realized it was Jacob's arm I was gripping for balance."

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.description: I felt Jacob act protectively and saw him try to stand between Alice and me, which reinforced my sense of his loyalty and care in that moment.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: I read: "He sit awkwardly, almost as if he were trying to shield me with his body."

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.description: I registered Jacob's resentment and emotional reaction when he explained the phone call and then realized the gravity of Edward's response.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: I read: "Then he hung up on me," Jacob spit back. "A tremor rolled down his spine, shaking me with it."

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob vowed not to let anything happen to Charlie and was willing to break the treaty to protect us.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.source_text: I'm not going to let anything happen to Charlie. Jacob's low voice was gruff and angry. 'Screw the treaty.'

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.description: I noticed Jacob's emotional vulnerability when he begged me to stay, revealing a shift from anger to pleading and tears.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.source_text: 'Please, Bella. I'm begging.' His dark eyes were glistening with tears.

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.description: I observed that Jacob cares for me deeply and protectively, as shown by his physical comfort and desperate pleas not to leave.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.source_text: 'Don't die, Bella,' he choked out. 'Don't go. Don't.'

tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob physically restrained his emotion enough to release me when I pulled away, indicating controlled but intense attachment.
tw-book2-chapter18_Sc4.source_text: I pulled my arm free, and he didn't fight me.

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.description: I noticed that Jacob was not mentioned as someone to send for help and therefore inferred he was not part of the immediate plan to intervene.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: "Tell Emmett no… Well, go after Emmett and Rosalie and bring them back…"

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc4.description: I worried that Jacob's promise to wait for me might not still apply.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: And Jacob? He'd promised to wait for me, but did that promise still apply?

tw-book2-chapter19_Sc4.description: I considered that I might end up home alone in Forks with no one at all and even wondered if I might not want to survive.
tw-book2-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: Would I end up home alone in Forks, with no one at all? Maybe I didn't want to survive, no matter what happened.

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob was not present during this scene based on the listed attendees.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: Characters present: Carlisle, Emmett, Rosalie, Esme, Alice, Jasper, Edward, Bella

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.description: My tracking notes show Jacob is being monitored as a character of interest even though he is absent from the scene.
tw-book2-chapter2_Sc1.source_text: Characters to track: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen, Jacob Black

tw-book2-chapter2_Sc6.description: I noticed that Jacob is not present in this scene and that only Bella, Charlie, and Edward are listed as present.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc2.description: I observed that Jacob is not mentioned or present in this scene and that Bella's immediate concerns center on Edward, Alice, and Jasper.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: I hoped Alice would get out. I hoped that she would see me from some dark shadow and know that I had failed, so she could go home to Jasper.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc4.description: I inferred that Jacob is included among the werewolf friends mentioned in Alice's mental glimpses.

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.description: I observed that Jacob Black was not present among the listed characters at the Volturi audience.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: Characters present: Bella, Edward, Alice, Jane, Aro, Marcus, Caius, Felix, Demetri, Alec, Gianna

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.description: I inferred that Jacob's absence emphasized my dependence on Edward during the encounter with the Volturi.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: I cowered in the corner, cringing against Edward. His hand still rubbed against my arm. Characters present: Bella, Edward, Alice, Jane, Aro, Marcus, Caius, Felix, Demetri, Alec, Gianna

tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.description: I compared my shaking to how Jacob feels just before exploding into a werewolf.
tw-book2-chapter20_Sc6.source_text: For one wild second, I wondered if this was how Jacob felt just before exploding into a werewolf.

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob Black was not present in this scene based on the listed characters in the environment.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen, Alice, Jane, Felix, Demetri

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc2.description: I observed that Jacob Black was not listed among the characters present.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen, Alice, Jane, Alec, Felix, Demetri

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc3.description: I realized that Jacob Black was not present among the named attendees in the chamber.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: I read "Characters present: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen, Alice, Jane, Felix, Demetri, Aro, Marcus, Caius, other Volturi members"

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc4.description: I noticed that Jacob Black was not listed among the characters present in this scene with the Volturi and their attendants.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen, Alice, Jane, Aro, Marcus, Caius, Felix, other Volturi

tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.description: I noticed that Jacob was not present at the Volturi council meeting when the characters present were listed.
tw-book2-chapter21_Sc5.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen, Alice, Aro, Caius, Marcus, Felix, Jane, other Volturi

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc1.description: I compared my trembling to how Jacob must feel just before transforming into a werewolf.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: "For one wild second, I wondered if this was how Jacob felt just before exploding into a werewolf."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc1.description: I began to empathize with Jacob's pre-transformation agitation after feeling my body vibrate with panic.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: "For one wild second, I wondered if this was how Jacob felt just before exploding into a werewolf."

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc5.description: I observed that Jacob was not mentioned in this scene and that no direct information about him was provided.

tw-book2-chapter22_Sc6.description: I noticed that Jacob was not present among the people waiting at Sea-Tac despite being a character to track.
tw-book2-chapter22_Sc6.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen, Alice Cullen, Jasper, Carlisle Cullen, Esme Cullen, Emmett Cullen, Rosalie Cullen, Charlie Swan

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.description: I was sure Jacob or school or work or something was waiting for me when I woke and couldn't remember the day.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I couldn't remember what day of the week it was, but I was sure Jacob or school or work or something was waiting for me.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.description: I felt sharp impatience and fear in the dream that translated into concern about facing another day and possibly seeing Jacob.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: There was sharp impatience and fear, both part of that frustrating dream where your feet can't move fast enough…

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.description: I included Jake among the people I worried about after thinking I had drowned.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: "Poor Charlie. And Renee and Jake…" I trailed off in horror at what I had done.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.description: I felt guilt at the thought that my actions would affect Jake along with Charlie and Renee.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: "Poor Charlie. And Renee and Jake…" I trailed off in horror at what I had done.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.description: I realized that Bella had to put her life in the hands of werewolves, described as immature and volatile.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: I realized that you had to put your life in the hands of werewolves, immature, volatile, the worst thing out there besides Victoria herself—

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.description: I inferred that werewolves, a group that includes Jacob, were viewed as unreliable and dangerous in this situation.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: I realized that you had to put your life in the hands of werewolves, immature, volatile, the worst thing out there besides Victoria herself—

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc7.description: I observed that this scene provides no new information about Jacob because the interaction focuses solely on Bella and Edward.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc7.source_text: "He waited, studying my face as he spoke to make sure I was really listening."

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.description: I learned that Bella suggested Jacob's pack probably scared Victoria off, implying they had confronted or threatened her.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.source_text: Maybe she's not coming back. Jake's pack probably scared her off.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.description: I observed that Bella did not view Jacob or the werewolves as her primary concern and described them dismissively as adolescent troublemakers.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc8.source_text: My problems are a lot worse that a handful of adolescent wolves getting themselves into trouble.

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.description: I noted that Bella mentioned 'others' coming to look for her, which I understood could imply additional protectors or pursuers such as Jacob or his allies.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.source_text: I heard: "'There are others who are coming to look for me,' I reminded him in a subdued whisper."

tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.description: I inferred that Bella expects assistance beyond Edward, which I took to affect how she and Edward consider outside allies like Jacob.
tw-book2-chapter23_Sc9.source_text: I heard: "'There are others who are coming to look for me,' I reminded him in a subdued whisper."

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc2.description: I recognized that Jacob would be placed in greater danger because my presence draws enemies across the land he feels bound to protect.
tw-book2-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: Putting Jake in worse danger still by drawing his enemies across the land he felt bound to protect.

tw-book2-chapter24_Sc2.description: I felt guilty that my continued humanity would hurt Jacob and that I was a threat to the people I cared about.
tw-book2-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: This was always the hardest part. Charlie, Renee. Now Jacob, too. The people I would lose, the people I would hurt.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob was avoiding contact and not answering my calls, with Billy telling me Jacob did not want to talk.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc2.source_text: "Billy said he didn't want to talk to me," I fumed, glaring at the rain oozing down the passenger window. "That he was there, and wouldn't walk three steps to get to the phone!"

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc2.description: I updated my view that Jacob harbors deep hostility toward Edward and that his distance feels like personal rejection to me.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc2.source_text: "He won't come anywhere near me. The enmity is rooted too deeply."

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc2.description: I became less certain about Jacob's temper after remembering his kitchen words implying he might kill a friend, which made me worry he could be dangerous.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc2.source_text: I'm not sure that I'm even-tempered enough to handle that… You probably wouldn't like it so much if I killed your friend.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.description: I suspected that Jacob placed my motorcycle in Charlie's driveway as a deliberate provocation.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: No!" I gasped. "Why? Why would Jacob do this to me?"

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob was waiting in the trees and intended to see me.
I learned that Jacob was acting as a spokesperson for the pack rather than seeking a fight with Edward.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: "Don't worry, he's not here to fight me. He's acting as… spokesperson for the pack."

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.description: I changed from believing the underlying foundation of my relationship with Jacob was unchanged to doubting that foundation after the perceived betrayal.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: Of course things were strained right now, but I didn't think any of the underlying foundation had changed. I didn't think that was changeable!

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.description: I felt that Jacob's actions constituted a betrayal and damaged the trust I placed in him.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: I had trusted Jacob implicitly—trusted him with every single secret I had. I had been betrayed.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc4.description: I noticed Jacob looked bigger and was still growing, to the point he would tower over Edward.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: He looked bigger than the last time I'd seen him. Somehow, impossibly, he was still growing. He would tower over Edward, if they stood next to each other.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc4.description: I learned Jacob came to remind the Cullens of treaty terms and to warn that he might kill if those terms were violated.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: I just needed to remind your bloodsucking friends of a few key points in the treaty they agreed to. The treaty chat is the only thing stopping me from ripping his throat out right this minute.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc4.description: I understood that the treaty specifically forbids vampires from biting humans and that a bite, not only a kill, would end the truce.
tw-book2-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: "The treaty is quite specific. If any of them bite a human, the truce is over. Bite, not kill," he emphasized.

tw-book2-chapter25_Sc4.description: I saw Jacob's conflicted loyalty in his hatred toward Edward coupled with an insistence that he would never hurt Bella.

tw-book2-chapter3_Sc7.description: I learned that Jacob Black is not present in this scene and that no direct information about him is provided here.
tw-book2-chapter3_Sc7.source_text: I quote: "Characters present: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen"

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc3.description: I remembered that Jacob Black had kept my truck in great shape when it had belonged to his father, Billy.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: Jacob Black had kept it in great shape when it had belonged to his father, Billy…

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc3.description: I realized that I knew someone who could work on vehicles and possibly help make the bikes usable by saying I know someone who builds cars.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: You know what? That's okay. I know someone who builds cars.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc3.description: I felt reinforced trust in Jacob's mechanical ability because I recalled his prior care of my truck.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: Jacob Black had kept it in great shape when it had belonged to his father, Billy…

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc4.description: I had not seen Jacob in months and I intended to visit him at the Blacks' place.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc4.source_text: I want to visit Jacob. I haven't seen him in months.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc4.description: I hoped to arrive at La Push in a way that would give me a chance to be alone with Jacob.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc4.source_text: I hoped I could get Jacob alone.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob had grown significantly and that his height was now notable.
I observed that Jacob had developed from a child's softer muscles into a solid, lanky teenage build with prominent tendons and veins under his red-brown skin.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc5.source_text: Jacob had grown into some of his potential in the last eight months. He'd passed that point where the soft muscles of childhood hardened into the solid, lanky build of a teenager; the tendons and veins had become prominent under the red-brown skin of his arms, his hands.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc5.description: I noticed Jacob seemed proud of his height and pleased to announce it with self-satisfaction.
I learned that Jacob had been planning to work on his car before I interrupted and that he offered to do something else with me instead.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc5.source_text: I was just heading out to work on my car, but we can do something else…

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob had some experience with motorcycles and was willing to try fixing my bikes.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc6.source_text: Some. My friend Embry has a dirt bike. We work on it together sometimes. Why?

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc6.description: I noticed that Jacob refused payment and instead wanted to help for free, later accepting a trade and the chance to teach me.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc6.source_text: No. I want to help. You can't pay me.

tw-book2-chapter5_Sc6.description: I perceived Jacob as enthusiastic and delighted by the project, which made me view him as a generous, invaluable friend.
tw-book2-chapter5_Sc6.source_text: He seemed truly pleased by the challenge. His face glowed.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.description: I learned Jacob was dismantling a red motorcycle destined for Bella and that he knew how to rebuild vehicles including a Volkswagen.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: Jacob started pulling the first bike—the red one, which was destined for me—to pieces immediately. Did you know he's rebuilding a Volkswagen?

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.description: I learned Jacob's two best friends are Quil and Embry and that they teased each other and joked around loudly.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: He updated me on the progress of his sophomore year of school, running on about his classes and his two best friends. "Quil and Embry?" I interrupted.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.description: I noticed Jacob blush and seem embarrassed when someone called his name, revealing a shy or self-conscious side.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: "No." Jacob ducked his head, and it looked like he was blushing under his brown skin.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.description: I noticed Jacob acted protective of his land and friends as he warned the other boys not to set a toe on his property.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: If either of you set so much as one toe on my land tomorrow… I heard Jacob threaten.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.description: I noticed Jacob hesitated about letting Bella pay for everything but he accepted when she argued the mechanic costs and the value of their labor.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: I'm still not sure I should let you pay for everything. Okay, you're getting a deal.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.description: I heard Jacob joke that Ragu hasn't been around that long when Billy claimed his recipe was ancient.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: Jacob snorted. "I don't think Ragu's actually been around that long."

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.description: I felt that Jacob was attentive to me because he talked mostly to me and held my hand during the gathering.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: Jacob talked mostly to me and Seth, who interrupted eagerly whenever Jacob seemed in danger of forgetting him.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.description: I observed that Seth idolized Jacob and hung on his every word.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: Seth was fourteen; he hung on Jacob's every word with idolizing eyes.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc4.description: I learned that Paul wasn't friends with Sam, stopped coming to school for a few weeks, and returned apparently 'owned' by Sam.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: And that's the way it was with Paul. Just exactly the same. He wasn't friends with Sam at all. Then he stopped coming to school for a few weeks, and, when he came back, suddenly Sam owned him.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob had talked to his father Billy and that Billy had given a vague, dismissive answer about waiting and explaining later.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: "It's nothing you need to worry about now, Jacob. In a few years, if you don't… well, I'll explain later."

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc4.description: I became frightened as Jacob's horror spread to me and I felt chills running down my neck.
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: His horror was spreading to me. I had chills running on the back of my neck.

tw-book2-chapter6_Sc4.description: I felt our friendship deepen when I threw my arms around him and his long arms wrapped hesitantly around me and he said, 'Thanks, Bella.'
tw-book2-chapter6_Sc4.source_text: I threw my arms around him instinctively, wrapping them around his waist and pressing my face against his chest. He was frozen for a second, and then his long arms wrapped hesitantly around me. "Thanks, Bella."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc1.description: I felt much, much healthier around Jacob and preferred the idea of going to La Push.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: I should have gone straight down to La Push I felt much, much healthier around Jacob

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc1.description: I associated Jacob's company with health and comfort more than returning to the Cullens.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc1.source_text: I felt much, much healthier around Jacob

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc3.description: I wanted to see Jacob and I sought him as a fix to the emptiness I felt.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: I felt hideously empty, and I wanted to see Jacob.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc3.description: I believed that going back to the human world and finding Jacob would relieve my numbness.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: I was anxious to be gone, to get back to the human world. I felt hideously empty, and I wanted to see Jacob.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.description: I noticed Jacob was waiting for me when I arrived at his place.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I read, "Jacob was waiting for me."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.description: I observed Jacob's mechanical skill in restoring the damaged red bike to look like a motorcycle.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I read, "When I walked into the garage, I was shocked to see the red bike standing up, looking like a motorcycle rather than a pile of jagged metal."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.description: I heard Jacob admit that he gets obsessive when he has a project.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I read, "I get obsessive when I have a project."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.description: I recognized Jacob's eagerness for my company and his enjoyment of teasing and playful banter with me.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I read, "You really like spending time with me?" he asked, marveling.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.description: I realized Jacob values ongoing visits enough to ask if I would still come over when he finished his work.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I read, "So you think you'll still come over when I'm done, then?"

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.description: I saw Jacob initiate a ritual of responsibility by offering soda and toasting to 'responsibility' and 'twice a week.'
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc4.source_text: I read, "He pulled out two cans of soda, cracking one open and handing it to me. He opened the second, and held it up ceremoniously. 'Here's to responsibility,' he toasted. 'Twice a week.'"

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.description: I noticed that interacting with Jacob felt effortless and more natural than interacting with others.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: I found that I was able to smile and laugh with him, though it wasn't as effortless as it was with Jacob.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.description: I preferred spending the afternoon in the garage rather than at work, implying a desire to be where Jacob was.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc5.source_text: Yeah," I agreed, though I'd much rather have spent the afternoon in the garage.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.description: I observed Jacob sprawled across the living room floor studying with me and surrounded by our scattered books.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: Charlie didn't seem the smallest bit surprised to find Jacob and me sprawled across the living room floor with our books scattered around us, so I guessed that he and Billy were talking behind our backs.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.description: I saw Jacob watch and occasionally sample the lasagna I made, stay for dinner, and take a plate home for Billy.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: The smell of the lasagna I'd spent the afternoon making—while Jacob watched and occasionally sampled—wafted down the hall; I was being good, trying to atone for all the pizza. Jacob stayed for dinner, and took a plate home for Billy.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.description: I noticed Jacob laugh at my unwilling expression when I agreed to take him home and that his laughter seemed to please him.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: He laughed at my unwilling expression—it seemed to please him.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.description: I noticed an unexplained excitement in Jacob's answering smile and that he said he would call me first before I came up.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: There was an unexplained excitement in his answering smile. "I'll call you first, okay?"

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.description: I heard Jacob speak in a strange, formal tone to announce, "I believe that… we have a date," and then confirm, "Yeah, they run and everything."
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: "Bella," Jacob said, a strange, formal tone to his voice. "I believe that… we have a date" ... "Yeah, they run and everything."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.description: I felt pleased to reward Jacob verbally and to treat him with affection for arranging the date and helping with domestic plans.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc6.source_text: "Jacob, you are absolutely, without a doubt, the most talented and wonderful person I know. You get ten years for this one."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.description: I noticed Jacob was prepared and that small blue ribbons had been tied around the motorcycles' handlebars.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: Jacob was prepared. There was a piece of blue ribbon tied in a small bow around each of the handlebars.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.description: I watched Jacob run out of the house and ask 'Ready?' in a low voice with his eyes sparkling.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: I was laughing at that when Jacob ran out of the house. "Ready?" he asked in a low voice, his eyes sparkling.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.description: I observed Jacob load the bikes into the truck with ease and say 'Let's go' with an excited, higher-than-usual voice.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: Jacob loaded the bikes into the bed of the truck with ease, laying them carefully on their sides so they didn't show. "Let's go," he said, his voice higher than usual with excitement.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.description: I heard Jacob say he knew the perfect spot where no one would catch us and I listened as he talked about finishing the bikes in technical terms.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: "I know the perfect spot—no one will catch us there." ... Jacob was talking about finishing the bikes, but his descriptions were getting technical, so I wasn't paying close attention.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.description: I felt that Jacob was competent, eager, and invested in keeping the plan secret and successful.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc7.source_text: Jacob was prepared. "Let's go," he said, his voice higher than usual with excitement. "I know the perfect spot—no one will catch us there."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc8.description: I learned that Jacob participates in cliff diving himself and that he spoke inclusively using 'we' when referring to jumpers.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc8.source_text: "You jump off the cliff?" I hadn't missed the "us." "Sure, sure." He shrugged and grinned. "It's fun. A little scary, kind of a rush."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc8.description: I learned that Jacob pointed out a lower rock on the cliff as the more common and safer jumping spot.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc8.source_text: "Well, yeah, most of us jump from lower down, that rock that juts out from the cliff about halfway." He pointed out his window.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc8.description: I noticed Jacob's teasing and mild irritation at my alarm, which revealed a familiar, teasing dynamic and a degree of concern or impatience toward me.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc8.source_text: He was teasing, but there was a strange note of irritation in his voice.

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.description: I heard Jacob describe the protectors as self-appointed peacekeepers who "don't start fights, they keep the peace."
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: I heard Jacob say "They don't start fights, they keep the peace."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.description: I heard Jacob name Sam Uley as a leader and I heard him mention followers Jared and Paul.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: I heard Jacob say "Sam came by with his followers, Jared and Paul."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.description: I heard Jacob describe Paul as volatile and I heard that Sam can calm Paul when he becomes violent.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: I heard Jacob describe how "Paul looked at him for a minute and calmed down" and that Paul was like "going to tear us up if Sam didn't stop him."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.description: I noticed Jacob's hands were clenched and I realized he felt deep resentment and anger toward the protectors.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc9.source_text: I observed that "Jacob's hands were clenched into fists, as if he'd like to hit something."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc10.description: I feel creeped out by the way the council treats me and I have never understood why my father's opinion carries so much weight.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: "It's just… the way they treat me. It creeps me out." "You know, the council is supposed to be made up of equals, but if there was a leader, it would be my dad. I've never been able to figure out why people treat him the way they do. Why his opinion counts the most."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc10.description: I know that Sam was supposed to go to college but stayed and was not criticized while my sister was criticized for turning down a scholarship and marrying.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: "Yeah. He was supposed to go to college, but he stayed. And no one gave him any crap about it, either. The whole council pitched a fit when my sister turned down a partial scholarship and got married."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc10.description: I know that my great-grandpa Ephraim Black was considered the last chief and that my family history influences how others listen to Billy and my father.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: "My great-grandpa, Ephraim Black, was sort of the last chief we had, and they still listen to Billy, maybe because of that."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc10.description: I feel that nobody treated me special until now, implying that my relationship with Bella has made me feel noticed and different.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: "But I'm just like everyone else. Nobody treats me special… until now."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.description: I learned that Jacob believes Sam manages to 'own' boys like Paul who previously had no connection to Sam.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.source_text: "And that's the way it was with Paul. Just exactly the same. He wasn't friends with Sam at all. Then he stopped coming to school for a few weeks, and, when he came back, suddenly Sam owned him. I don't know what it means."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.description: I learned that Jacob told his father about the problem and that his father dismissed it with a vague answer about explaining later.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.source_text: "It's nothing you need to worry about now, Jacob. In a few years, if you don't… well, I'll explain later."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.description: I noticed Jacob was frightened and I saw that he looked like he was about to cry because the situation with Sam terrified him.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.source_text: "I stared at Jacob, biting my lip anxiously—he was really frightened." "He looked like he was about to cry."

tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.description: I observed Jacob accept my comfort, wrap his arms hesitantly around me, and thank me, which updated my sense of our closeness.
tw-book2-chapter7_Sc11.source_text: "He was frozen for a second, and then his long arms wrapped hesitantly around me." "Thanks, Bella."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob is capable, knowledgeable about motorcycles, and uses clear, practical instruction and hands-on demonstration to teach me how to operate the bike.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: "It will when you're moving," he promised. "That is how you brake. Don't forget." "Throttle?" "Gearshift?" "Very good. I think you've got all the parts down."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob prefers I use the front brake and specifically warned me to avoid using the back brake until later.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: "But you said—" "This is the brake you want. Don't use the back brake now, that's for later, when you know what you're doing."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc1.description: I recognized Jacob as protective and physically reassuring, as he repeatedly steadied the bike, caught it when it started to fall, and encouraged me to continue learning.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: "He wrapped his hand around mine and made me squeeze the lever down." "He took a step back, and then suddenly slammed his foot down on the pedal... Jake caught the bike before it knocked me to the ground." "Jacob jerked the heavy bike off me with ease."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc2.description: I observed that Jacob was skilled and decisive with motorcycles, starting his bike in one try and loading my bike into his truck quickly.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: I watched: "Jacob jumped on the black motorcycle, kicked it to a start in one try... He threw the bike into the bed and sprinted to the driver's side."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc2.description: I noticed that Jacob acted protectively by wrapping his arm around my waist, insisting on driving me to the hospital, and tending to my wound with his shirt.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: I observed: "He wrapped a long arm around my waist and pulled me to my feet... 'I think I'd better drive you to the hospital first.'"

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc2.description: I realized that Jacob could be seriously worried and somber about my safety, which contrasted with his usual demeanor.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: I noted: "Jacob wasn't happy—his full mouth turned down in an uncharacteristic frown—but he didn't want to get me in trouble."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc2.description: I felt that Jacob was willing to help cover up evidence to keep me from getting in trouble with Charlie, demonstrating his loyalty.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: I remembered: "'What about Charlie?' 'He said he had to work today.' 'Trust me. I'm an easy bleeder.'"

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.description: I noticed Jacob drove me to the hospital shirtless and that he joked a jacket would have given them away.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: We were halfway to the hospital when I realized he was still shirtless.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.source_text_full: "That would have given us away," he teased.

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.description: I observed that Jacob looked older than sixteen with long, wiry muscles under smooth, pretty-colored skin.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: Jacob really did look older than sixteen—not quite forty, but maybe older than me.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.source_text_full: The muscles were the long wiry kind, but they were definitely there under the smooth skin.

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.description: I experienced Jacob holding my hand during the stitches and I felt comforted by his presence during the procedure.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: Jacob held my hand while Dr. Snow was sewing.

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.description: I decided that I did not want to give up riding my motorcycle even though Jacob suggested cooling it for a short while to avoid more injuries.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: Maybe we should cool it with the bikes.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc3.source_text_full: At least for a week or so. You could stay out of the hospital for a week, right?

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob handles a compass and map with practiced skill and uses a radiating grid to navigate.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: "He held the compass in a skilled way, twisting the map around till it angled the way he wanted."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.description: I observed that Jacob checked the compass frequently to keep us on a straight line.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: Jacob checked the compass every few minutes, keeping us in a straight line with one of the radiating spokes of his grid.

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob reported Embry as not being back to normal and that Embry was still with Sam.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: "No. He's not back to normal," Jacob said ... "Still with Sam."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.description: I noticed that Jacob felt the pack's scrutiny and that he was angry about Billy's unhelpful attitude.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: "Sometimes." ... 'As helpful as ever,' he said in a sour, angry voice that disturbed me.

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.description: I recognized that Jacob is affectionate and protective toward me when he put his arm around my shoulder and grabbed my hand to pull me through the ferns.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: "He put his arm around my shoulder..." and "... grabbing my hand and pulling me through a mass of ferns."

tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.description: I saw that Jacob uses teasing jokes about danger and about my taste to keep the mood light.
tw-book2-chapter8_Sc4.source_text: "I hope we see the bear tomorrow. I'm sort of disappointed about that." ... 'Of course, you might be an exception. I bet you'd taste good.'

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob greeted me with a smile, wished me a happy Valentine's Day, and offered a small pink box of conversation hearts.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: "Happy Valentine's Day," Jacob said, smiling, but ducking his head as he greeted me. He held out a small, pink box, balancing it on his palm. Conversation hearts.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.description: I noticed Jacob's face fall and read disappointment in his dark eyes when I mentioned plans for Friday, which made me feel guilty.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: But Jacob's face fell. I caught the expression in his dark eyes before he dropped them to look at the ground.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.description: I agreed that Jacob should come to the movie with my friends and suggested he bring Quil so we could make it a party.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: "You'll come too, right?" I added quickly. "Bring Quil, and we'll make it a party."

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.description: I tried to set boundaries with Jacob but realized those boundaries tended to blur and complicate our interactions.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: But I was trying to think of some way to make the boundaries clear. Again. They seemed to get blurred a lot with Jacob.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob had just finished building his car from scratch and that he offered to drive it.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: I told him he could—he just finished his car. He built it from scratch, all by himself,

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob handed Bella ten dollars because he was not old enough to get into the movie.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: When we got to the theater, Jacob handed me a ten-dollar bill. "What's this?" I objected. "I'm not old enough to get into this one," he reminded me.
