tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.description: I noticed that Jacob sniggered at the movie's excessive gore and used humor to make Bella laugh and relax.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: "Oh, c'mon!" he hissed back. "The blood squirted twenty feet out of that guy. How fake can you get?" He chuckled again,

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.description: I observed that Jacob was more comfortable and cheerful than anyone else and that he habitually took Bella's hand when possible, which increased the tension with Mike.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: He seemed more comfortable than anyone else. Jacob was in the habit of taking my hand whenever the opportunity presented itself,

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc4.description: I observed that Jacob is prepared to be annoyingly persistent and that he explicitly told me he wasn't giving up because he had loads of time.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc4.source_text: "And you think I'm good-looking—sort of. I'm prepared to be annoyingly persistent." and "Because I'm not giving up. I've got loads of time."

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob accepts my limits and is willing to be with me even if I cannot give him more than companionship.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc4.source_text: "It's what I want to do, as long as you still like to be with me."

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc4.description: I saw Jacob take practical action to help when Mike got sick by asking for an empty popcorn bucket and helping get Mike into the car.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc4.source_text: "Could I have an empty popcorn bucket?" and "He helped me get Mike into the back of the car, and handed him the bucket with a serious gaze."

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc4.description: I noticed that Jacob's teasing and casualness mask genuine care as he comforted me and insisted on staying close despite my guardedness.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc4.source_text: "He chuckled quietly for a minute while his pinky finger absently traced designs against the side of my hand." and "But don't get mad at me for hanging around, okay?" Jacob patted the back of my hand.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob left Bella\'s house feeling sick and that I had worried about him driving home.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc5.source_text: "He was getting sick when he left, and I was worried."

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob had in fact made it home.
I learned that Jacob was too ill to make a phone call after he arrived home.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc5.source_text: "He was… too sick to call. He\'s not feeling well right now."

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc5.description: I felt guilty for not insisting on driving Jacob home myself.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc5.source_text: "I should have insisted on driving him home."

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc5.description: I remained worried about Jacob\'s condition despite confirmation that he had arrived home.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc6.description: I recognized that Jacob told me he would call when he could and that I should wait for his call.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc6.source_text: I'll call you when I can. I'll let you know when you can come down again.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc6.description: I heard Jacob answer with a broken, cracking voice.
I understood that Jacob believed his illness was different and likely worse than the stomach flu.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc6.source_text: I don't think I have the same thing you did.

tw-book2-chapter9_Sc6.description: I noticed Jacob sounded bitter and refused my help, which made me feel shut out.
tw-book2-chapter9_Sc6.source_text: "Right," he agreed, and his voice had a strange, bitter edge.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.description: I saw Jacob express anger about the note-passing chain and mocked the use of Charlie and Billy as messengers.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: I don’t know why you’re making Charlie carry notes to Billy like we’re in second grade

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.description: I noticed Jacob admitted being a jerk while asserting there was no way around the situation, showing conflicted accountability and anger.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: Look, I know I’m being a jerk, but there’s just no way around

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.description: I inferred from the paper and Bella’s description that Jacob wrote with force, possibly snapping his pen, which left ink splatters and deep indentations.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: I could picture him writing this — scrawling the angry letters in his rough handwriting, slashing through line after line when the words came out wrong, maybe even snapping the pen in his too-big hand; that would explain the ink splatters.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob admitted he missed me but declared that missing me did not change his decision to distance himself.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc1.source_text: Yeah, I miss you, too. A lot. Doesn’t change anything. Sorry.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob informed on me about the motorcycle in order to get me grounded and keep me from spending time with Edward.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: Ever since my former best friend (and werewolf), Jacob Black, had informed on me about the motorcycle I’d been riding on the sly — a betrayal he had devised in order to get me grounded so that I couldn’t spend time with my boyfriend (and vampire), Edward Cullen —

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc3.description: I feel betrayed and my face hardened when Jacob was mentioned because of his actions.
I now view Jacob as my former best friend who might be my enemy after he informed on me.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc3.source_text: My former best friend who was now . . . what? My enemy? I cringed.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc4.description: I noted that Jacob Black was listed as a character to track but I did not see him present in this scene.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: Characters to track: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen, Jacob Black

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc4.description: I observed that Jacob Black was not among the characters present, since the scene listed Bella, Edward, and Charlie as present.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen, Charlie Swan

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc5.description: I noticed that Jacob Black was not present in the scene and did not participate in the conversation.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc5.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen, Charlie Swan

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc5.description: I realized that Jacob was not involved in Bella's college discussion or the curfew negotiation in this scene.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc5.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen, Charlie Swan

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc6.description: I expect Jacob to immediately understand my disappearance and to react with revulsion, which causes me emotional pain.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc6.source_text: And Jacob, who, unlike my parents, would know exactly what was going on when I disappeared to some distant school. For a moment, the idea of Jacob’s certain revulsion overshadowed every other pain.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc6.description: I see Jacob as more perceptive about my life changes than my parents and therefore as a risk to secrecy.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc6.source_text: Even if my parents didn’t grow suspicious for a long time, even if I could put off visits with excuses about travel expenses or study loads or illnesses, Jacob would know the truth.

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc7.description: I learned that Jacob was having a hard time and that Charlie reported he was hurting right now.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc7.source_text: “Charlie says Jake is having a hard time. He’s hurting right now, and . . . it’s my fault.”

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc7.description: I felt that Jacob was my best friend and that I owed him an attempt to make things better because of his pain.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc7.source_text: “He was my best friend, Edward,” I muttered. “I need to make it better, Edward. I owe him that.”

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc7.description: I accepted Edward’s warning that seeing Jacob unprotected was out of the question because of the treaty and the risk of war.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc7.source_text: “You know it’s out of the question for you to be around a werewolf unprotected, Bella. And it would break the treaty if any of us cross over onto their land. Do you want us to start a war?”

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc8.description: I learned that Jacob is sometimes not human and that he is currently in pain, motivating my desire to help him.
I acknowledged that Jacob helped me when I was 'not so human' and that his past support creates a moral obligation for me to try to help him now.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc8.source_text: I quote: "He was there for me when I was . . . not so human myself. I didn’t hold him responsible for all the stupid things I’d done in his absence, or the pain I had suffered."

tw-book3-chapter1_Sc8.description: I accepted that Jacob's lineage includes Ephraim Black as a great-grandfather and that this heritage ties into the historical truce with Carlisle.
tw-book3-chapter1_Sc8.source_text: I quote: "Jacob’s great-grandfather’s name startled me."

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: I observed that Jacob is much faster now and can move almost silently, especially without his car.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: "It was hard to get used to how much faster Jacob was without his car. How everyone seemed to be so much faster than me..." and "I’d forgotten that Jacob moved like a ghost these days."

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: I noticed Jacob commonly runs half-naked and barefoot and that he carries his clothes while he runs, sometimes by holding them in his mouth.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: "Is it really so impossible to wear clothes, Jacob?" and "My clothes don’t just pop in and out of existence when I change — I have to carry them with me while I run... it sucks to carry jeans in your mouth."

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: I recognized Jacob’s protectiveness toward Bella and his clear discomfort with her dating a vampire.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: "What’s it like — having a vampire for a boyfriend?" and "You said a few weeks... When, exactly...?"

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc1.description: I felt Jacob become saddened or alarmed when he heard that Bella’s change was scheduled so soon.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc1.source_text: "So soon," he breathed. "Graduation," I whispered back."

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob notices when I smell of vampires and that he finds the smell unpleasant.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc2.source_text: "One of the many hazards of socializing with vampires," Jacob said, shrugging. "It makes you smell bad."

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc2.description: I noticed that Jacob is openly affectionate, protective, and eager for my company as shown by his pleading and his hug.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc2.source_text: "His big dark eyes were full of unashamed pleading." "he grabbed my hand and wrenched me into one of his bone-crushing hugs."

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob invited me to a La Push bonfire and expected other pack members and friends to be there.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc2.source_text: "do you think you can come to La Push tonight? We’re having a bonfire party. Emily will be there, and you could meet Kim . . . And I know Quil wants to see you, too."

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob crowed with undisguised exultation when I told him I could come and that he agreed to meet at the boundary line at six.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: Jacob crowed with undisguised exultation when I called to give him the news, and he seemed eager enough to embrace Edward’s safety measures. He promised to meet us at the line between territories at six.

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: I noticed Jacob's protectiveness and enthusiasm toward me, which strengthened my sense of him as both eager and willing to help keep me safe with the pack.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: And Jacob’s right — about one thing, anyway — a pack of werewolves ought to be enough to protect even you for one evening.

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc3.description: I learned that my plan was to return my motorcycle to Jacob's garage and that Jacob could later sell it or give it to a friend.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc3.source_text: I would take it back to La Push where it belonged and, when I no longer needed it anymore . . . well, then, I would insist that Jacob profit from his work somehow. He could sell it or give it to a friend.

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc4.description: I was grabbed up in another vice-tight hug by Jacob, which physically constrained me.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc4.source_text: on the kickstand, and grabbed me up in another vice-tight hug.

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc4.description: I heard Jacob laugh and felt him set me down after the hug.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc4.source_text: He laughed and set me down.

tw-book3-chapter10_Sc4.description: I noticed Jacob's teasing, false innocence, and blunt humor when I heard him tell me I couldn't push what I don't have.
tw-book3-chapter10_Sc4.source_text: “Bella,” he finally said — still chuckling — as he shut the door behind me, “you can’t push what you don’t have.”

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: I heard Jacob say he was so full he was about to puke but that he thought he could force the hot dog down even though he wouldn't enjoy it.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: “I guess,” Jake said slowly. “I’m so full I’m about to puke, but Ithink I can force it down. I won’t enjoy it at all, though.”

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: I watched Jacob flip the homemade skewer across the circle toward Paul and saw Paul catch it neatly on the right end without difficulty.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: He flipped the homemade skewer across the circle. I expected it to land hot-dog-first in the sand, but Paul caught it neatly on the right end without difficulty.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: I felt that Jacob was comfortable enough with me to lean against my knees and to banter openly with other pack members like Paul.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: Jacob leaned back against my knees and toyed with the hot dog he had spitted on a straightened wire hanger; "Sheesh." Jacob laughed. "Kidding, Paul. Here."

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc1.description: I noticed Jacob sighed again sadly after mentioning he wouldn't enjoy the hot dog, and I interpreted that as resignation or mild disappointment about the situation.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc1.source_text: He heaved a sigh and patted his stomach. He sighed again sadly.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: I learned Jacob admitted ruefully that the helmet was a good idea he should have thought of himself.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: he had admitted ruefully that the helmet was a good idea that he should have thought of himself

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: I learned Jacob towed me out of the forest to the clifftop meeting place.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: when Jacob had towed me out of the forest to the clifftop meeting place

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.description: I realized Jacob had invited me and that I worried others might be angry with him for inviting me.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc2.source_text: Would they be angry with Jacob for inviting me?

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: I noticed that Seth’s appearance reminded me very much of a younger Jacob, giving me a visual reference for Jacob’s earlier look.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: With his huge, happy grin and his long, gangly build, he reminded me very much of a younger Jacob.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: I felt a personal reaction when I saw Seth’s resemblance to Jacob because the resemblance made me smile and then sigh.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: The resemblance made me smile, and then sigh.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.description: I wondered whether Jacob’s trajectory as one of the boys whose lives changed drastically might also be a fate facing Seth, which altered my concern about Jacob’s situation by extension.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc3.source_text: Was Seth doomed to have his life change as drastically as the rest of these boys? Was that future why he and his family were allowed to be here?

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc4.description: I learned from Jacob that the nighttime gathering was framed as a council meeting and that Quil, Kim, Seth, and Leah were first-timers.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: This is technically a council meeting. It’s Quil’s first time, and he hasn’t heard the stories yet. Well, he’s heard them, but this will be the first time he knows they’re true. ... Kim and Seth and Leah are all first-timers, too.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc4.description: I believed that revealing the truth of the stories would make new attendees pay closer attention as Jacob suggested.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc4.source_text: Well, he’s heard them, but this will be the first time he knows they’re true. That tends to make a guy pay closer attention.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc4.description: I recognized Jacob's role as a storyteller and organizer within the group and accepted his guiding presence for the meeting.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc6.description: I observed that Jacob Black was present during the telling of the legend.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc6.source_text: Characters present: Billy, Old Quil, Bella Swan, Jacob Black, Quil, Sam

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc6.description: I learned that Taha Aki entered a wolf's body to escape the torment of the spirit world and returned to the village in that wolf form.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc6.source_text: He asked the great wolf to make room for him, to share. The wolf complied. Taka Aki entered the wolf’s body with relief and gratitude.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc6.description: I inferred that Jacob Black's tribal heritage includes strong wolf-spirit traditions that tie leadership and protection to wolf possession and spirit journeys.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc6.source_text: As one, the man and the wolf returned to the village on the harbor. Utlapa’s first edict was to forbid any warrior to enter the spirit world.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc7.description: I realized Jacob was among the circle who were descendants of Taha Aki.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc7.source_text: the circle was made up of Taha Aki’s great — to however many degrees — grandsons.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc7.description: I felt a shock when I came back to the present and noticed Jacob as part of the circle.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc7.source_text: I was so involved in the story, it was a shock to come back to the present, to the circle around the dying fire.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.description: I noticed Jacob’s mouth twitch with humor while Old Quil told the story.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.source_text: I saw the corner of his mouth twitch with humor, and his arm tightened around me.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.description: I observed Jacob tighten his arm around me, showing a protective physical reaction to the tale.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.source_text: I saw the corner of his mouth twitch with humor, and his arm tightened around me.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.description: I felt closer to Jacob as he held me while the story unfolded, reinforcing our physical closeness in that moment.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc8.source_text: I shrank a little closer to Jacob’s side. I saw the corner of his mouth twitch with humor, and his arm tightened around me.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc9.description: I learned that Jacob's ancestor Ephraim Black negotiated with a vampire leader and secured a promise not to harm the Quileutes.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc9.source_text: I quote: "But the leader spoke to Ephraim Black as if he were a man, and promised not to harm the Quileutes."

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc9.description: I learned that the descendants of Taha Aki originally became wolves when they reached manhood but that the practice faded so wolves only returned when a cold one was near.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc9.source_text: I quote: "Time passed, and the descendants of Taha Aki no longer became wolves when they reached manhood. Only in a great while, if a cold one was near, would the wolves return."

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc9.description: I felt increased respect for Jacob's lineage as tribal guardians who passed wolf knowledge father to son and endured sacrifices to protect their people.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc9.source_text: I quote: "They'd learned how to fight the cold ones, and they passed the knowledge on, wolf mind to wolf mind, spirit to spirit, father to son."

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc10.description: I noticed Jacob was completely still and silent beside me with his breath deep and even, and I thought he might be close to sleep.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc10.source_text: Neither Jacob nor I spoke. He was so still beside me, his breath so deep and even, that I thought he might be close to sleep.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc10.description: I felt a quiet companionship with Jacob in our shared silence during the scene.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.description: I noticed that Jacob shook my arm to wake me and that I was still under his arm when I found myself in his car.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.source_text: Something shook my arm. "C’mon, Bells," Jacob said in my ear. "We’re here." I was still under his arm, but I wasn’t on the ground anymore.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.description: I observed Jacob calling Edward for me and handing me the phone so I could speak with him.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.source_text: Easy. It’s not even midnight yet. And I already called him for you. "Here," Jacob said, and he put a small shape into my other hand. The phone.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.description: I realized that Jacob wanted more time with me and that he had been deliberately nice to secure that time.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.source_text: I figured if I played nice, I’d get more time with you.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.description: I felt grateful and touched by Jacob’s invitation and his effort to include me that night.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc11.source_text: "Thanks, Jake," I said, touched. "Really, thank you. And thanks for inviting me tonight. That was . . ."

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.description: I noticed Jacob was not very patient about waiting.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.source_text: “Yeah, he’s not so patient, is he?” Jacob said, noticing my distraction.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.description: I learned Jacob told me to go ahead but to come back soon.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.source_text: "Go ahead. But come back soon, okay?" Jacob said, noticing my distraction.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.description: I felt Jacob sounded patronizing when I told him I would be fine and that he should get some rest.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.source_text: “Sure, sure,” he said, but he sounded more patronizing than agreeing.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.description: I heard Jacob whisper goodnight as I hurried away into the darkness.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc12.source_text: “’Night, Bella,” he whispered as I hurried into the darkness.

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc13.description: I learned that Jacob had called Charlie which made getting past him easier.
I asked if Jacob was out there and I was told he was somewhere.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc13.source_text:
"Is Jacob out there?" I asked, shivering as Edward pulled me into the circle of his arm.
"Yes . . . somewhere. And Esme's on her way home."

tw-book3-chapter11_Sc13.description: I noticed that sitting next to Jacob had provided enough warmth that I did not feel the cold on the cliffs.
tw-book3-chapter11_Sc13.source_text: I hadn’t noticed it at all on the windy cliffs; I imagined that had less to do with the fire than it did with sitting next to Jacob.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc1.description: I noted that Jacob Black was not present in this scene.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc2.description: I realized that I would have to say goodbye to Jacob as part of losing my human life.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: I didn’t know how to do this. How to say goodbye to Charlie and Renée . . . to Jacob . . . to being human.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc2.description: I became more terrified of leaving my human life because leaving would mean losing my connection to Jacob.
tw-book3-chapter12_Sc2.source_text: I didn’t know how to do this. How to say goodbye to Charlie and Renée . . . to Jacob . . . to being human.

tw-book3-chapter12_Sc5.description: I noted that Jacob was not present in this scene and that no direct information about him appears in the morning events.

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc3.description: I learned no direct information about Jacob Black from this scene.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc3.source_text: I was placed in charge of evacuating the women and children from the city when the Union’s mortar boats reached the harbor.

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc6.description: I noticed that Jacob is not part of this scene and that the narrative focus is on Jasper's confession and his meeting with Alice.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc6.source_text: "Jasper was lost in the story, as was I."

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc10.description: I learned that the wolves destroyed Laurent to save me and that this act is the specific reason Irina holds a grudge against the pack.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc10.source_text: “She’s holding a grudge against the wolves for destroying him to save Bella.”

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc10.description: I learned that Irina wanted revenge to take down the pack and that she and her allies would trade their help for permission to do so.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc10.source_text: “She wants revenge. To take down the pack. They would trade their help for our permission.”

tw-book3-chapter13_Sc10.description: I noted that Edward expressed indebtedness to the wolves by saying he still 'owes the wolves,' which I understood as a reinforcement of positive feelings between Edward and the pack.
tw-book3-chapter13_Sc10.source_text: “Laurent had it coming” — this was almost a growl — “and I still owe the wolves for that.”

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob was grumpy when I woke him but he cheered when I asked to visit the next day.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.source_text: Though it was the middle of the afternoon, my call woke Jacob up, and he was grouchy at first. He cheered right up when I asked if I could visit the next day.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.description: I heard Jacob tell me to come over as early as I could because the Quileute school was already out for the summer.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.source_text: The Quileute school was already out for the summer, so he told me to come over as early as I could.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.description: I observed Jacob honk his horn twice in quick, impatient honks when I arrived at the border.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.source_text: I would have pressed the issue, but then Jacob honked his horn — two quick impatient honks.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.description: I heard Edward say that it's not easy to ignore someone when he's shouting, which indicated Jacob was shouting.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.source_text: "It's not easy to ignore someone when he's shouting."

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.description: I recognized that Jacob expected me to join him and I accepted his invitation by climbing into his car.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc5.source_text: I waved to Edward before I got into the Rabbit and, from that distance, it looked like he was truly upset about the honking thing . . . or whatever Jacob was thinking about. I sighed, and climbed in Jacob's car.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob had only gotten about two hours of sleep the previous night and four the night before.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.source_text: “I got about two hours of sleep last night, and four the night before,” he told me.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob has been running double shifts because Sam distrusts the vampires and has been keeping him busy.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.source_text: “Sam’s being difficult. He doesn’t trust your bloodsuckers. I’ve been running double shifts for two weeks and nobody’s touched me yet, but he still doesn’t buy it. So I’m on my own for now.”

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.description: I noticed that Jacob framed staying with Bella as the least he could do, even joking about 'eternal servitude' to downplay his protective instinct.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.source_text: “Hey, it’s the least I can do — I offered eternal servitude, remember. I’m your slave for life.”

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.description: I observed Jacob offering to be around and staying with Bella, which reinforced his protective, loyal role in their friendship.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.source_text: “Then I’ll be around,” he said as his eyes slid closed.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.description: I noticed that Jacob’s house felt vacant and that his father had been spending time at the Clearwaters' since Harry died.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc6.source_text:
“Where’s your dad?”
“Over at the Clearwaters’. He’s been hanging out there a lot since Harry died. Sue gets lonely.”
Jacob sat down on the old couch...

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.description: I noticed Jacob fell asleep on the couch and that his arm pinned me against his body while he snorted and rolled to his side.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.source_text: Jacob snorted and rolled to his side. His arm swung off the back of the couch and pinned me against his body.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.description: I felt how heavy and hot Jacob was pressed against me and how quickly the warmth became sweltering.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.source_text: Holy crow, but he was heavy! Andhot. It was sweltering after just a few seconds.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.description: I watched Jacob wake up disoriented, ask repeatedly what was happening, and apologize for falling asleep.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.source_text: When his arm fell off me, his eyes snapped open. He jumped to his feet, looking around anxiously. “What? What?” he asked, disoriented. “Oh, man! Did I fall asleep? I’m sorry! How long was I out?”

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.description: I observed Jacob insist on going outside to walk because he felt he would pass out if he stayed inside.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.source_text: “Ugh, let’s go outside. I need to walk around or I’ll pass out again.”

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.description: I realized Jacob was embarrassed and nervous about whatever he wanted to say and that he laughed at himself while admitting he had planned a smoother approach.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.source_text: “I was planning to do this a little bit differently.” He laughed, and it sounded like he was laughing at himself. “Smoother,” he added.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.description: I saw Jacob care about spending time with me and act possessively by grabbing my hand and pulling me to stay.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc8.source_text: “No!” Jacob insisted, grabbing my hand. “No, stay. You hardly ever make it down. I can’t believe I wasted all this time.”

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc9.description: I heard Jacob say 'I'm in love with you, Bella' in a strong, sure voice.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc9.source_text: “I’m in love with you, Bella,” Jacob said in a strong, sure voice.

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc9.description: I understood that Jacob wanted me to know his feelings as an explicit option and was asking me to choose him over the other man.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc9.source_text: “Bella, I love you. And I want you to pick me instead of him.”

tw-book3-chapter14_Sc9.description: I realized Jacob intended to state his feelings aloud to avoid any miscommunication or confusion about his intentions.
tw-book3-chapter14_Sc9.source_text: “I want to tell you something. And you already know it . . . but I think I should say it out loud anyway. Just so there’s never any confusion on the subject.”

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc1.description: I heard Jacob ask Bella whether she wanted him to go away and never see her again, revealing the depth of his concern about their relationship.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: "Do you want me to go away and never see you again? Be honest."

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc1.description: I perceived that Jacob desired Bella's presence in his life and pushed for clarity about the nature of their relationship.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: "Tell me exactly why you want me around, then."

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc1.description: I noticed that Jacob accepted Bella's boundary about romance yet resolved to stay close to her despite the emotional risk.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc2.description: I experienced Jacob forcibly holding my chin and kissing me roughly, preventing my escape.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: He took my chin in his hand, holding it firmly... His lips crushed mine, stopping my protest. He kissed me angrily, roughly, his other hand gripping tight around the back of my neck, making escape impossible.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc2.description: I perceived Jacob positioning himself as a rival who will fight for me until my heart stops beating.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: Until your heart stops beating, Bella. I’ll be here — fighting.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc2.description: I sensed that Jacob believes because Edward left, Jacob is the consequence I must deal with.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: And now he’s just going to have to deal with the consequence of that choice — me.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.description: I saw Jacob react with shock and immediate concern about my injury, asking if I was all right.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.source_text: Jacob stared at me in shock. "Are you all right?"

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.description: I noticed Jacob offered practical help by saying he would get his car and later by helping me into the passenger side.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.source_text: "I'll get my car," he said calmly. ... Jacob rolled his eyes. He walked me to the passenger side of his car and helped me in.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.description: I perceived Jacob as pushy when he wrapped his arm around my waist and I jerked away from his touch.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.source_text: "Just let me drive you home," Jacob insisted. Unbelievably, he had the nerve to wrap his arm around my waist. I jerked away from him.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.description: I concluded that Jacob would still assist me despite my refusal, noting that he calmly continued and even whistled while driving.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc3.source_text: "Don't touch me! I'm going home right now!" "I'll get my car," he said calmly. ... When he got in the driver’s side, he was whistling.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob claimed I kissed him back and that he interpreted my reaction as reciprocal.
I learned that Jacob believes he could protect and make Bella happy better than her vampire, and that Charlie would approve if she chose him.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: You wouldn’t have to change anything for me. You know Charlie would be happy if you picked me. I could protect you just as well as your vampire can — maybe better. And I would make you happy, Bella.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob insists he never truly left Bella and that he used to run around her house at night to check on her.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: I never did ... I used to run around your house at night — like I do now. Just making sure you were okay.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob expected Bella to think about him that night and planned to think about her in return.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: You will. Tonight. And I’ll be thinking about you while you’re thinking about me.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob denied responsibility for Bella's injured hand and suggested she should have known better.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: That wasn’t my fault. You should have known better.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob kissed Bella, provoking her to punch him.
I observed Jacob remain calm and at ease in Charlie's living room despite the tension between him and Bella.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc6.source_text: Jacob lolled next to him on the sofa, perfectly at ease.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc6.description: I noticed Bella's frustration that she had not hurt Jacob when she punched him, indicating aggressive intent that did not achieve its aim.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc6.source_text: "I wish I’d hurt him. " I sighed in frustration. "I didn’t do any damage at all."

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc7.description: I saw Jacob follow Bella and Edward outside and close the door in Charlie's surprised face, indicating intent to stay involved.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc7.source_text: I looked back and Jacob was following us, stopping to close the door in Charlie’s surprised and uneasy face.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc7.description: I noticed Jacob responded to Edward's threats with arrogance and defiance rather than fear.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc7.source_text: What if she wants me to?

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc7.description: I perceived that Jacob was actively competing with Edward for Bella's affection and willing to trade blows or risks in that rivalry.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc7.source_text: I’ll take the trade any day.

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc8.description: I heard Jacob growl that it was no fun beating someone who forfeits and I observed him accepting a challenge with Edward.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc8.source_text: I heard: "Good," Jacob growled. "It’s no fun beating someone who forfeits."

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc8.description: I noticed a clear rivalry between Jacob and Edward when Jacob grimaced, called me 'pup,' and traded taunts with Edward.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc8.source_text: I heard: "That sounds about right . . . pup." and I read: "Jacob grimaced briefly, then he composed his face and leaned around Edward to smile at me."

tw-book3-chapter15_Sc8.description: I realized that Jacob might have stood watching me at the house after we left because I did not look up to see whether he went back inside.
tw-book3-chapter15_Sc8.source_text: I read: "I didn’t look up again as Edward walked around the car and climbed into the driver’s side, so I didn’t know if Jacob went back into the house or continued to stand there, watching me."

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc2.description: I noticed that Jacob is not present in this scene and that no new information about him is provided here.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.description: I learned Jacob Black is not present in this scene and therefore is not part of the described interactions.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Charlie, Edward

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.description: I saw Jacob pull Charlie to his feet and hoot in encouragement from the back of the gym.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: "I was conscious of cheering in the back of the gym, and I looked around to see Jacob pulling Charlie to his feet, both of them hooting in encouragement."

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.description: I noticed Billy's head near Jacob's elbow in the audience beside them.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: "I could just make out the top of Billy’s head beside Jake’s elbow."

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.description: I managed to offer Jacob and Charlie an approximation of a smile, acknowledging their support during my graduation.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: "I managed to throw them an approximation of a smile."

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc6.description: I noticed that Jacob had come to the gathering with Billy and that they did not stay for long.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc6.source_text: “Jacob and Billy had to take off — did you see that they were here?”

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc6.description: I acknowledged that Jacob's brief appearance was seen as supportive by others at the gathering.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc6.source_text: “It was nice of them to show up,” Charlie said.

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc9.description: I learned that someone kissed me without my permission and that the situation prompted a physical response.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc9.source_text: "if someone kisses you without your permission, you should be able to make your feelings clear without hurting yourself."

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc9.description: I discovered that punching Jacob resulted in a broken knuckle and that his head felt very hard when I hit him.
tw-book3-chapter16_Sc9.source_text: My left hand rested lightly on the dark brace I rarely thought about. My broken knuckle didn’t hurt much anymore. "Jacob’s head is really hard."

tw-book3-chapter16_Sc9.description: I still consider Jacob a friend despite finding him obnoxious after the incident.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc1.description: I noticed Jacob was not present in this scene and that only Bella and Edward were present.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc2.description: I noted that Jacob Black was not present among the characters in this scene.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: I read: "Characters present: Bella, Edward, Alice"

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc2.description: I learned that the scene provides no direct information about Jacob's actions or feelings.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: I read: "Characters present: Bella, Edward, Alice"

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc3.description: I noticed that Jacob Black was not listed among the guests present at the party.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: Characters present: Bella, Alice, Edward, Carlisle, Jasper, Emmett, Jessica, Mike, Tyler, Conner, Austin, Lee, Samantha, Lauren, Angela, Ben, Eric, Katie

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc3.description: I inferred that Jacob was not part of the social gathering that night.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: Characters present: Bella, Alice, Edward, Carlisle, Jasper, Emmett, Jessica, Mike, Tyler, Conner, Austin, Lee, Samantha, Lauren, Angela, Ben, Eric, Katie

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc5.description: I observed that Jacob entered with two other werewolves, Quil and Embry, making three in total.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc5.source_text: It wasn’t just one werewolf, it was three. Jacob had let himself in, flanked on either side by Quil and Embry.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc5.description: I noticed Jacob was calmer than the others as he waved, while Quil and Embry appeared tense and uneasy.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc5.source_text: Jacob was waving at me, calmer than the others, though his nose was wrinkled in disgust.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc5.description: I waved back at Jacob but I waved goodbye and turned away, indicating a distance in our interaction at that moment.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc5.source_text: I waved back — waved goodbye — and turned to look for Alice.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob brought me a graduation present, specifically a silver bracelet with a charm that he carved himself.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc6.source_text: I heard: "I brought you a graduation present and everything." and I read: "I didn't make the bracelet," he admitted. "Just the charm."

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob learned carving from Billy and that Billy is more skilled than Jacob at making such charms.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc6.source_text: I read: "It's something Billy taught me. He's better at it than I am."

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc6.description: I noticed that Jacob expressed sincere remorse for kissing me and that he believed he had misread my signals, admitting he had deluded himself.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc6.source_text: I heard: "I really am sorry. About the other day, I mean, too. I shouldn't have kissed you like that. I guess . . . well, I guess I deluded myself into thinking you wanted me to."

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc6.description: I recognized Jacob's insecurity and his fear of being forgotten, understanding that he hoped the charm would make me remember him because he worries I prefer my Cullen friends.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc6.source_text: I read: "Well, I figured that maybe it would make you remember me once in a while. You know how it is, out of sight, out of mind." and I heard: "I guess you'd rather be with your real friends," he said in the same defeated tone. "I get it."

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc7.description: I observed that Jacob demanded an explanation and pressured me directly.
I observed that Jacob asserted a communal right to know the situation about the threat.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc7.source_text: We have a right to know,

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc7.description: I felt Jacob’s protectiveness escalate into confrontation as he physically blocked our exit.
I noticed that Jacob softened his immediate aggression when Jasper intervened and he pulled his arm back.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc7.source_text: Jasper stepped in between them, and the three werewolves braced themselves.

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.description: I learned that Jacob insisted the pack would coordinate with the vampires and framed the fight as more their job than the vampires'.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.source_text: “We’ll have to coordinate,” Jacob said. “It won’t be easy for us. Still, this is our job more than yours.”

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.description: I learned that Jacob was in a hurry to return to Sam and that he committed the pack to attend the rendezvous.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.source_text: “We’ve got to get back to Sam. What time?” "We’ll be there."

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.description: I realized that Jacob believed the wolves would have the upper hand and that the fight 'won’t be even.'
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.source_text: “No,” Jacob said, and a strange, fierce half-smile spread across his face. “It won’t be even.”

tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.description: I observed Jacob tease me and dismiss my fears by calling my objections ridiculous and saying I was giving him a better gift.
tw-book3-chapter17_Sc8.source_text: “Don’t be ridiculous, Bells. You’re giving me a much better gift than the one I gave you.”

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc1.description: I felt protective of Jacob and viewed him and his brothers as foolish, eager, and potentially at risk.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: Not Jacob, too. Not his foolish, eager brothers — most of them even younger than I was.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob’s solution had relaxed the Cullens and made them almost euphoric after the stress.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: Jacob’s solution had them all relaxed, almost euphoric after the long weeks of stress.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc1.description: I used the possibility of calling Jacob as leverage to ensure I would not be left behind, indicating his importance in my decisions.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: "If you won’t take me, then I’ll call Jacob."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob Black is listed as a character to track but is not present in this scene.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc2.source_text: Characters to track: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen, Jacob Black; Characters present: Bella Swan, Charlie

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc2.description: I have no observational evidence in this passage about Jacob Black's whereabouts or actions.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc2.source_text: Characters to track: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen, Jacob Black; Characters present: Bella Swan, Charlie

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc4.description: I observed that Jacob was not present at the clearing and I learned that the werewolves were expected to arrive soon, which affected Alice's ability to see immediate events.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc4.source_text: "The werewolves are on their way, so she can’t see anything that will happen now."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc4.description: I inferred that the werewolves (including Jacob) were coordinating arrival with the Cullens and I noted that their impending presence influenced the Cullens' behavior and Alice's mood.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc4.source_text: "The werewolves are on their way, so she can’t see anything that will happen now."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc5.description: I remembered that Jacob had twice appeared to me in his wolf form and that those appearances had been a source of terror.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc5.source_text: "I swallowed once, remembering the two times I’d seen Jacob in his wolf form — the first time in the meadow with Laurent, the second time on the forest lane where Paul had gotten angry at me. . . . They were both memories of terror."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc5.description: I inferred that Jacob was part of an expanding wolf pack that had grown beyond what the Cullens expected.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc5.source_text: "The pack has grown" "There were ten of them."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc5.description: I became more convinced that the wolves, including Jacob, were physically imposing like horses, thick with muscle and with teeth like knives, which increased my fear of encountering them.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc5.source_text: "Like horses, only thick with muscle and fur — and teeth like knives, impossible to overlook."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc6.description: I learned that Sam is effectively the leader of the wolves and that he communicated limits to engagement through Edward's translation.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc6.source_text: I read: "'We will watch and listen, but no more.' 'That is more than enough,' Carlisle answered."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc6.description: I learned that the wolf pack includes many very new members only months into their life, which implies limited skill and internal conflict among them.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc6.source_text: I read: "'They are all very new — only months old to this life. Children, in a way. They will have no skill or strategy, only brute strength.'"

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc6.description: I realized that the wolves felt some enthusiasm about the plan and that they were willing to accept guidance and share the fight, which updated my view of their cooperation with the Cullens.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc6.source_text: I read: "A rumble passed down the shadowy line of wolves, a low growling mutter that somehow managed to sound enthusiastic."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.description: I learned that Jacob is willing to leave his place in the pack and approach me directly, ignoring the pack's scrutiny.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.source_text: Jacob’s grin widened over his sharp teeth. He left his place in line, ignoring the eyes of his pack as they followed him.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.description: I felt Jacob's affection when he crouched down to my level, closed his eyes as I stroked him, and leaned his head into my hand.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.source_text:
Jacob crouched down on his front legs and dropped his head so that his face was no higher than mine...
The black eyes closed, and Jacob leaned his huge head into my hand.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.description: I learned that Jacob shows playfulness and vocal amusement in wolf form, audible as a rumble and a coughing bark that reads as laughter.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.source_text:
The answering rumble deep in his chest sounded like a chuckle.
The coughing bark that came through his teeth was obviously laughter.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.description: I discovered that Jacob's presence comforts and amuses me more than frightens me, which changed my expectation of how I would react to him in wolf form.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc9.source_text:
I giggled.
I wiped my face on the sleeve of my shirt, unable to keep from laughing with him.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc10.description: I noticed a square of folded black fabric secured to Jacob's back leg as he ran into the trees.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc10.source_text: I noticed for the first time a square of folded black fabric secured to his back leg.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc10.description: I saw Jacob return in human form, bare-chested with tangled hair, wearing only black sweat pants and barefoot.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc10.source_text: Jacob loped back into view, on two legs this time. His broad chest was bare, his hair tangled and shaggy. He wore only a pair of black sweat pants, his feet bare to the cold ground.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc10.description: I noticed Jacob was confident that leaving me on the reservation with Collin and Brady staying behind would keep me safe.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc10.source_text: "Okay, so leave her on the reservation. We’re making Collin and Brady stay behind anyway. She’ll be safe there."

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc10.description: I noticed Jacob maintained hostility toward the Cullens by giving them a wide berth and addressing Edward as 'bloodsucker.'
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc10.source_text: he gave a wide berth to the Cullens, who stood talking quietly in a loose circle. "Okay, bloodsucker," Jacob said...

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc11.description: I proposed hiding Bella in the deep forest and offered to carry her to attempt to confuse and obscure her scent trail.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc11.source_text: So hide her here,” he suggested. “There’s a million possibilities — places either one of us could be in just a few minutes if there’s a need.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc11.description: I felt excited about the scent-masking plan while also uneasy about being close to rival allies during the test.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc11.source_text: He was clearly excited by whatever this new plan of his was, but he was also still uneasy so close to his enemy allies.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc11.description: I showed impatience and familiarity in physical interaction with Bella while exchanging guarded looks with Edward.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc11.source_text: Jacob rolled his eyes, impatient, and reached down to yank me up into his arms. But his eyes flickered to Edward, just like mine did.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc12.description: I learned that Jacob proposed using Seth Clearwater in wolf form as a pack-linked 'cell phone' and that the pack connection has been tested as far as three hundred miles.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc12.source_text: “As long as Seth Clearwater is in his wolf form, he’ll be connected to the pack,” Edward said. “Three hundred miles?” Edward asked. “That’s the farthest we’ve ever gone to experiment,” Jacob told me.

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc12.description: I noticed Jacob became smug when his idea was accepted and that he framed their involvement as an opportunity to fight vampires.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc12.source_text: Jacob was suddenly smug. “That’s the reason we’re here.”

tw-book3-chapter18_Sc12.description: I felt the charged physical tension between Jacob and Edward as Jacob edged closer during planning, conveying a mix of antagonism and cooperative focus.
tw-book3-chapter18_Sc12.source_text: He’d edged closer unconsciously, drawn by his absorption in the planning. He stood only three feet from Edward now, and, standing there between them, I could feel the physical tension in the air. It was like static, an uncomfortable charge.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc1.description: I noted that Jacob Black was not present in this scene and that only Bella and Edward are described as present.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: I quote: 'Characters present: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen'

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob had given me the wooden wolf charm at the party and that I was still wearing it.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: I was still wearing the gift that Jacob had given me at the party.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc2.description: I heard Edward explicitly acknowledge that Jacob Black can give me presents.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: Jacob Black can give you presents.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc2.description: I noticed Edward contrasted Jacob's freedom to give me gifts with his own restraint and framed that contrast as unfair.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: Everyone else is able to get away with giving you things. Everyone but me.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob withheld information about pack numbers and was careful to avert his thoughts when he was near me to avoid breaking pack rules.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: I quote: 'There are things he wasn’t allowed to share — their numbers, for instance.'

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.description: I realized that Jacob had told Leah's story about imprinting and that the imprinting between Sam and Emily had broken Leah's heart.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: I quote: 'the strange imprinting between Sam and her cousin Emily had broken Leah’s heart.'

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.description: I respected Jacob's discretion because I noticed he had been careful around me and had clearly been protecting certain pack secrets.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: I quote: 'Jacob was very careful to think of other things when he was near me.'

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob, Sam, and Quil now suspect that Embry might have a half-brother among their fathers, which creates tension and unanswered questions.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc4.source_text: I quote: 'Now Sam, Jacob, and Quil all wonder which of them has a half-brother.'

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc7.description: I found no mention of Jacob in this scene and I learned that he is not involved in this conversation or plan.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc7.source_text: With one easy conversation, Alice had cleared my schedule for the battle.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc8.description: I learned that Jake and his friends needed to get some sleep before the meeting.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc8.source_text: That’s good. Jake and his friends need to get some sleep.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc8.description: I realized that Edward believed the wolves didn’t need as much sleep as I did.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc8.source_text: “They don’t need as much as you do,” he pointed out.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc8.description: I felt concern for Jacob and his friends' need for rest ahead of the meeting.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc8.source_text: That’s good. Jake and his friends need to get some sleep.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc9.description: I recognized Jacob immediately and noticed that he looked up and stared at the sound of our approach.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc9.source_text: It was also easy to recognize Jacob; I would have known him at once, even if he hadn’t looked up and stared at the sound of our approach.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc9.description: I saw Jacob smile with the same wolfy grin and began to view him and the other wolves more as friends than as frightening monsters.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc9.source_text: When I forced my eyes away from the Cullens — away from the image of their play fighting that would be real and deadly in just a few days — Jacob caught my eyes and smiled. It was the same wolfy grin as before, his eyes scrunching the way they did when he was human.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc9.description: I learned that Quil and Embry were Jacob’s usual companions and that Sam did not trust sending just Jacob alone.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc9.source_text: They don’t all need to be here. One would do the job, but Sam didn’t trust us enough to just send Jacob, though Jacob was willing. Quil and Embry are his usual . . . I guess you could call them his wingmen.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc9.description: I began to feel protective toward Jacob and his pack because I noticed they were less indestructible than the Cullens and could be hurt.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc9.source_text: Friends who didn’t look nearly as indestructible as Emmett and Jasper did, moving faster than cobra strikes while the moonlight glinted off their granite-hard skin. Friends who didn’t seem to understand the danger involved here. Friends who were still somewhat mortal, friends who could bleed, friends who could die. . . .

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.description: I saw Jacob spring lightly to his feet in a massive wolf form that combined agility with sheer mass.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.source_text: Jacob sprang lightly to his feet, his agility at odds with his sheer mass, and trotted over to where Edward and I stood on the fringe of things.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.description: I observed Jacob ignore Edward’s greeting and fix his dark eyes on me instead.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.source_text: Jacob ignored him, his dark eyes on me.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.description: I heard a low whimper escape Jacob’s muzzle and later a growl that Edward described as annoyed rather than threatening.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.source_text:
A low whimper escaped his muzzle.

Jacob growled — not a threatening sound, an annoyed sound — and Edward’s lips twitched.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.description: I watched Jacob fold himself onto the ground beside me with a rumbling sigh and lean his head against my leg.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.source_text:
He folded himself on to the ground beside me with a rumbling sigh.

He leaned his head against my leg and started humming again.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.description: I felt Jacob’s contentment when he made a deep humming sound in his throat that reminded me of a purr.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.source_text: That same strange humming sound that he’d made yesterday rumbled in his throat. It was a homey kind of sound. Rougher, wilder than a cat’s purr, but conveying the same sense of contentment.

tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.description: I sensed that Jacob’s presence and behavior in wolf form restored a sense of our previous closeness and easy friendship.
tw-book3-chapter19_Sc10.source_text: It was strange. Even though he was in this bizarre form, this felt more like the way Jake and I used to be — the easy, effortless friendship that was as natural as breathing in and out — than the last few times I’d been with Jacob while he was human.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc2.description: I noticed that avoiding involvement with the werewolves was mentioned as part of my following Charlie's conditions.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc2.source_text: He must like that, too — me fulfilling Charlie's conditions without involving werewolves.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc3.description: I retained a last memory of Jacob from our goodbye in the forest, and that memory shows his face crumpled in pain.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc3.source_text: Ever since I’d said goodbye to Jacob Black in the forest outside my home, I’d been plagued by a persistent, uncomfortable intrusion of a specific mental picture. It popped into my thoughts at regular intervals like some annoying alarm clock set to sound every half hour, filling my head with the image of Jacob’s face crumpled in pain.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc3.description: I understood that I am effectively barred from seeing Jacob because I cannot go to La Push, which changes how I experience my freedom.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc3.source_text: Sure, I was free to go to anywhere I wanted — except La Push; free to do anything I wanted — except see Jacob.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc3.description: I knew exactly why I was dissatisfied with my liberty when the disturbing vision of Jacob struck me again.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc3.source_text: As the disturbing vision struck again, I knew exactly why I was dissatisfied with my liberty.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob spends most of his time with a pack of his friends down at La Push these days.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc5.source_text: Jacob is fine, I guess. I don’t see him much; he spends most of his time with a pack of his friends down at La Push these days.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc5.description: I realized that I don’t see Jacob much anymore and that our contact has become infrequent.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc8.description: I knew that I would not be allowed to go to a werewolf party even with parental supervision.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc8.source_text: I knew I wouldn’t be allowed to hit a werewolf party, even with parental supervision.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc9.description: I learned that I mentioned Jacob as a possible companion because I believed my father preferred Jacob over Edward.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc9.source_text: Would it bother you if I took Jacob?

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc9.description: I realized that invoking Jacob's name provoked a strong reaction from Edward, indicating Jacob's presence is a sensitive issue between them.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc9.source_text: I’d only picked the name because I knew of my father’s preference for Jacob, but I quickly wished I hadn’t; Edward’s teeth clenched together with an audible snap.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc9.description: I perceived that my father would prefer me to go with Jacob rather than Edward, which I used strategically during the argument.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc9.source_text: I’d only picked the name because I knew of my father’s preference for Jacob, but I quickly wished I hadn’t; Edward’s teeth clenched together with an audible snap.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc11.description: I admitted that I have not figured out how to resolve things with Jake yet.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc11.source_text: And what about Jake? ... I haven’t figured that one out yet, Dad.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc11.description: I felt annoyed when Charlie implied that failing to make things right with Jacob would make me a bad person.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc11.source_text: Keep trying, Bella. I know you’ll do the right thing. You’re a good person. ... Nice. So if I didn’t figure out some way to make things right with Jacob, then I was a bad person? That was below the belt.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc11.description: I recognized that Charlie expects me to continue trying to fix my relationship with Jacob and that this expectation influences my choices.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc11.source_text: Keep trying, Bella. I know you’ll do the right thing. You’re a good person.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc12.description: I learned that Jacob had been refusing to answer my phone calls since Edward returned.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc12.source_text: Jacob had refused to answer my phone calls since Edward’s return.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc12.description: I wanted to reconnect with Jacob because I needed to see him smiling again and replace the last painful image of him.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc12.source_text: Besides, I needed tosee him — see him smiling again the way he used to. I needed to replace that awful last memory of his face warped and twisted by pain if I was ever going to have any peace of mind.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc12.description: I decided to prioritize going to see Jacob over worrying about Edward's possible reaction and over curfew concerns.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc12.source_text:
Ten minutes maybe. Long enough to decide that the pros were valid while the cons were not.

It was past my curfew, but would Charlie really care about that when Edward wasn’t involved?

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc13.description: I learned that the wolves’ transformations may erase their futures and that in the instant of shifting they don’t really even exist.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc13.source_text: In that instant when they shift from one form to the other, they don’t really even exist. The future can’t hold them.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc13.description: I learned that the Blacks’ minds at least have been readable to Edward even though their futures disappear, which implicates Jacob’s family in the mystery.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc13.source_text: That doesn’t seem entirely likely, since I haven’t had any trouble reading their thoughts. The Blacks’ at least.

tw-book3-chapter2_Sc13.description: I realized that mingling my fate with Jacob or his pack could erase my future, and I began to view interactions with them as potentially dangerous.
tw-book3-chapter2_Sc13.source_text: When you decide to mingle your fate with theirs, you disappear, too.

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc2.description: I observed that Bella’s bracelet includes a wolf charm opposite the new crystal, indicating a symbolic wolf connection.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: On the opposite side of the chain from the wolf, there now hung a brilliant heart-shaped crystal.

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc2.description: I inferred that Jacob retained a symbolic connection to Bella because the wolf charm remained on her bracelet despite his absence.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc2.source_text: On the opposite side of the chain from the wolf, there now hung a brilliant heart-shaped crystal.

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc3.description: I noted that Jacob Black was not present during this negotiation scene between Bella and Edward.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc5.description: I learned that Bella fears she might, in a transformed state, want to drink Jacob’s blood or even harm Charlie, indicating Jacob is named as a possible target of her thirst.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: “If I’m so far gone that I’d want to kill Charlie — that I’d drink Jacob’s blood or Angela’s if I got the chance — how can that be true?”

tw-book3-chapter20_Sc5.description: I noticed Bella’s casual dismissal of drinking 'the dog’s blood' and I perceived that Edward and Bella acknowledge Jacob as associated with a canine form, which colors the perceived danger.
tw-book3-chapter20_Sc5.source_text: “I doubt you’ll want to drink the dog’s blood.” He pretended to shudder at the thought.

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob was expected to meet Bella and Edward for the trip and that he knew where to meet them.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: “Why don’t you call Jacob and tell him we’ll be ready for him in an hour or so. He knows where to meet us.”

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc1.description: I discovered that Jacob was not home when Bella called and that Billy would contact a werewolf to pass along the message.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: Jacob wasn’t home, but Billy promised to call around until he could find an available werewolf to pass the news to.

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc2.description: I watched Jacob step warily from the trees human and I saw him with his arms folded across his bare chest and a jacket clutched in one fist.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: I quote: Jacob stepped warily from their shadows; He had his arms folded across his bare chest, a jacket clutched in one fist.

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc2.description: I realized that I had unconsciously expected a smaller, easygoing Jacob and I noticed him seeming bigger and more tense than the Jacob I remembered.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: I quote: Jacob seemed bigger again — no doubt a product of my expectations; I must have unconsciously been hoping to see the smaller Jacob from my memory, the easygoing friend who hadn’t made everything so difficult.

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc2.description: I observed Jacob recoil when Edward reached to touch the map's marked spot and I inferred tension between Jacob and Edward.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: I quote: Edward pulled a map from a side pocket on the pack and offered it to him; We’re here now, Edward said reaching over to touch the right spot; Jacob recoiled from his.

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob offered himself to be kissed for comparison and teased me about experimenting.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: “You could kiss me, for example. I don’t mind if you want to use me to experiment.”

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob is jealous, protective, and believes he loves me as much as or more than Edward.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: “That doesn’t mean that he loves you more than I do.”

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob believes I prefer him when he is a wolf because I can be less guarded around him.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc3.source_text: “Sometimes I think you like me better as a wolf.” “I think it’s easier for you to be near me when I’m not human, because you don’t have to pretend that you’re not attracted to me.”

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob said he was supposed to be the Alpha.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: "Yeah. I was supposed to be the Alpha."

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob initially refused the Alpha role because he did not want any of it or any change and would not take the position when Sam offered it.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: "I didn’t want any of it, Bella. I didn’t want anything to change. I didn’t want to be some legendary chief. I didn’t want to be part of a pack of werewolves, let alone their leader. I wouldn’t take it when Sam offered."

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob later accepted and felt glad to lead because he wanted to ensure the pack was led correctly rather than leave it to someone else.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: "Anyway, I guess I’m glad now. It has to be done, and could I trust someone else to get it right? It’s better to make sure myself."

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob intended to change (transform) to check on what was happening back home because of the storm.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: "I’m going to change," he said. "I want to know what’s going on back home."

tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.description: I noticed Jacob's friendliness wiped clean from his face when Edward arrived, indicating tension between them in that moment.
tw-book3-chapter21_Sc4.source_text: Jacob merely shrugged, all the friendliness wiped clean from his face.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc1.description: I heard Jacob whine and whimpered, producing a high-pitched, grating sound of complaint.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: Jacob whimpered, a high-pitched, grating sound of complaint.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc1.description: I noticed Jacob seemed better equipped for the snow with thicker, longer, shaggy russet fur compared to the others in his pack.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: At least Jacobdid seem to be well equipped for the snow, better even than the others in his pack with his thicker, longer, shaggy russet fur.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc1.description: I heard Jacob answer Edward bluntly and saw him refuse the suggestion to fetch a space heater, which made me view Jacob as independent and unflappable.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: “Better than anything you’ve come up with,” Jacob answered.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc1.description: I watched Jacob slide through the smallest opening of the tent into the arctic air as a few flecks of snow fell to the tent floor.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc1.source_text: Jacob slid through the smallest opening he could manage, while the arctic air flowed in around him, a few flecks of snow falling to the floor of the tent.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob generates a great deal of body heat and claimed to run at 108.9 degrees these days.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: "“Not me,” he said cheerfully. “I run at a toasty one-oh-eight point nine these days. I’ll have you sweating in no time.”"

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob often dresses minimally after transforming, typically wearing only sweats and no shoes or shirt.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: "As usual, when he’d been running around as a wolf, he’d only thrown on the bare essentials — just a pair of sweats, no shirt, no shoes."

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc2.description: I noticed that Jacob is willing to invade my space physically to warm me and that he teases and challenges Edward in the process.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: "Instead, he crawled to my side and started unzipping my sleeping bag."

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc2.description: I became aware that Jacob was not intimidated by Edward’s restraint or warnings and even chuckled during the confrontation.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob provides practical warmth and direct survival advice, even suggesting Bella remove clothes to warm faster.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: "Try to relax," he suggested as another shiver rippled through me violently. "You'll be warm in a minute. Of course, you'd warm up faster if you took your clothes off."

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc3.description: I felt that Jacob exhibits playful confidence and smugness when teasing Edward about jealousy.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: "Don't worry about the bloodsucker," Jacob suggested, and his tone was smug. "He's just jealous."

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc3.description: I recognized that Jacob is comfortable with close physical contact and acts protectively and intimately toward Bella.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: He leaned his head down to press his hot cheek against my numb ear.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.description: I realized that pack members had cropped their hair when they joined the pack and that Jacob's longer hair contrasted with that convention.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: So that was why they’d all cropped their hair in the beginning, when they joined the pack.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob intentionally grew his hair long because he thought I liked it better long.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: "I was growing my hair out because . . . it seemed like you liked it better long."

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.description: I noticed Jacob show tenderness and closeness by shaking his hair so it tickled my cheek and by whispering for me to go to sleep.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: He shook his head so that his unkempt hair — grown out to his chin now — tickled my cheek. "That’s right, honey, go to sleep," Jacob whispered.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob found his long hair convenient that night.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc4.source_text: Turns out it was very convenient tonight, so don’t worry about it.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc5.description: I heard Jacob taunt that I could still change my mind and claim he could do things with me that Edward cannot without killing me.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc5.source_text: “You know, she could still change her mind,” Jacob taunted him. “Consideringall the things I could do with her that you can’t. At least, not without killing her, that is.”

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob believes I am in love with him as well, even if I do not know it.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc5.source_text:
Jacob was defiant. “She’s in love with me, too, you know.”

Jacob sighed. “But shedoesn’t know it.”

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc5.description: I noticed Jacob’s smugness about shared jealousy and the formation of an uncomfortable truce between him and Edward.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc5.source_text:
Jacob’s whisper was suddenly smug. “I knew you were just as crazy jealous as I am.”

“It’s an uncomfortable truce, isn’t it?”

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc5.description: I felt Jacob act protectively toward me by tightening his arms around me as the tent shook.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc5.source_text: The wind ripped around the tent, shaking it like an earthquake. Jacob’s arms tightened around me protectively.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob believed I would not accept his explanation because he said, "I’d tell her all of this, but she’d never believe me."
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc6.source_text: I’d tell her all of this, but she’d never believe me.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc6.description: I felt Jacob's intense jealousy and fear of losing me when he asked, "What is it like? Losing her?" and physically held me.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc6.source_text: "What is it like? Losing her?" "When you thought that you’d lost her forever?" ... Jacob’s arms flexed around me.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc6.description: I noticed that Jacob acknowledged Edward’s motives about protecting me and voiced the idea that Edward left to keep me human.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc6.source_text: But you left because you didn’t want to make her a bloodsucker. You want her to be human.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc7.description: I admitted that I could see Edward does love Bella in his own way and could no longer argue with that fact.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc7.source_text: I can see that you do love her . . . in your way. I can’t argue with that anymore.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc7.description: I revealed that I had a game plan for Bella and asked for a year to try to make her happy and help her heal.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc7.source_text: I had a game plan. give me a year, bl — Edward. I really think I could make her happy.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc7.description: I believed that Bella is stubborn but capable of healing and that she could have a normal life if given time.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc7.source_text: She’s stubborn, no one knows that better than I do, but she’s capable of healing.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc7.description: I expressed contempt for Edward’s vampirism and affirmed my animosity while still engaging him over Bella’s welfare.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc7.source_text: Maybe . . . if you weren’t a disgusting vampire who was planning to suck out the life of the girl I love . . . well, no, not even then.
