tw-book3-chapter22_Sc8.description: I noticed that Jacob openly mocked the vampires as 'leeches' and insisted they are the bad guys.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc8.source_text: You don’t like the leeches being painted as the bad guys?" Jacob mocked. "You know, theyare. Then and now.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc8.description: I noticed that Jacob asked when the truce would end and that he agreed it would last until first light.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc8.source_text: And when doesthis little truce end?" Jacob asked. "First light," they whispered together, and then laughed quietly.

tw-book3-chapter22_Sc8.description: I sensed that Jacob maintained a teasing, confrontational rapport with Edward while still accepting a temporary détente.
tw-book3-chapter22_Sc8.source_text: You could leave, you know — give us a little privacy.

tw-book3-chapter23_Sc1.description: I noticed that Jacob slept curled up against Bella, he snored, and he flinched when he hit the cold tent floor.
tw-book3-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I read: "Jacob was snoring lightly in my ear, his arms still wrapped around me... Jacob fell out, his bare back hitting the icy floor of the tent. 'Hey!' he complained, his eyes flying open. Instinctively, he flinched away from the cold, rolling onto me."

tw-book3-chapter23_Sc1.description: I saw Jacob shift from snarling hostility toward Edward to calming under Bella's touch, revealing both his anger and his capacity to be soothed.
tw-book3-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I read: "Jacob was half-crouched, too, his whole body quivering, while growls rumbled through his clenched teeth... Under my touch, Jacob began to calm himself."

tw-book3-chapter23_Sc1.description: I watched Jacob refuse Bella's plea to stay and I learned that he was going back to Sam to fight the newborn vampires.
tw-book3-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I read: "'Please, Jake? Won't you stay?' 'No.' The word was hard and cold. He shoved out of the tent before I could finish."

tw-book3-chapter23_Sc2.description: I recognized Jacob's howl as a tortured, familiar cry and I felt his sudden absence when he left silently.
tw-book3-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: "The howl tore through my mind... The howl choked off into a peculiar gurgled sob, and then it was quiet again." and "I did not hear his silent escape, but I could feel it"

tw-book3-chapter23_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob was close enough to hear our words and that his reaction was immediate and intense.
I felt that I deeply care about Jacob and I became convinced that I am responsible for his pain.
tw-book3-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: "I’m hurting him. Every time I turn around, I’m hurting him again." and "I’m a hideous person."

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc2.description: I realized that Jacob’s presence and influence were a potent emotional trigger for Bella and that she desperately wanted to forget him in the moment.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "Make me forget him. Make me forget my own name. Fight back!"

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc2.description: I understood that Edward explicitly did not want Bella’s choices to be made as a reaction to Jacob Black and he communicated that preference to her.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "But I’d much rather it wasn’t in reaction to Jacob Black."

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc2.description: I noticed that Bella’s behavior and desperation indicated a shifting belief that she needed to actively distance herself from Jacob’s emotional hold to be with Edward.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "I pulled myself against him and crushed my mouth to his snow-cold lips."

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob assisted Paul in catching and killing a newborn during the conflict.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: I read: "Paul and Jacob got another one"

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc3.description: I understood that Jacob was actively fighting alongside the wolves against the newborn vampires.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc3.source_text: I read: "Sam’s helping her finish him off. Paul and Jacob got another one"

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc5.description: I realized that the werewolves could inflict devastating physical damage when I saw Seth tear Riley's arm away with an earsplitting metallic screech.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc5.source_text: With an earsplitting metallic screech, Riley lost his other arm.

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc5.description: I changed my belief about the werewolf pack's willingness to act violently when I watched Seth launch himself forward like a wrecking ball.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc5.source_text: Seth launched himself forward with the force of a wrecking ball.

tw-book3-chapter24_Sc5.description: I associated Jacob's kind with the pack's brutal loyalty after I saw Seth shake his head and fling Riley's arm into the woods with a broken hissing snicker.
tw-book3-chapter24_Sc5.source_text: Seth shook his head, flinging the arm into the woods. The broken hissing noise that came through Seth’s teeth sounded like snickering.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc1.description: I observed that Jacob was not present at the bonfire scene.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc1.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Edward, Seth

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc2.description: I learned that the wolves as a group were reported to be fine after the confrontation, implying that the wolf pack including Jacob was safe.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc2.source_text: "The others? Alice, Esme? The wolves?" and "All fine. It’s over there, too."

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc2.description: I observed that Jacob himself was not present in the scene and that no direct information about Jacob specifically was provided in this passage.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc3.description: I remembered that I had intended to say something to Jacob but could not complete it during the scene.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: “Hold on. Didn’t you say something before — ?” and “what was I going to say to Jacob? My splintered heart throbbed out a painful, aching beat.”

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc3.description: I felt that my unresolved feelings about Jacob left my heart splintered and in pain.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: “what was I going to say to Jacob? My splintered heart throbbed out a painful, aching beat.”

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc3.description: I became more apprehensive about how a nearby complication involving Alice and Sam might affect Jacob and our situation.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc3.source_text: “About a complication? And Alice, needing to nail down the schedule for Sam. You said it was going to be close. What was going to be close?”

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc4.description: I noticed that Jacob Black was not present in this scene while Seth and Edward were the pack members immediately affected.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "A spasm rocked through Seth's body, and a howl... ripped from his lungs. Edward fell to his knees..."

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc4.description: I noticed Edward called specifically for Sam rather than Jacob, which suggests Sam was the immediate point of contact for this particular emergency.
I began to believe that the wider pack, which could include Jacob, might be involved in this remote crisis because Edward used the pack plural.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: I quote: "This time, the crisis was not here. He was using the pack plural."

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.description: I learned that pack communication had been used to relay the warning, with Alice’s vision passed to Sam and then to Seth.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.source_text: Earlier this morning, Alice saw it and passed it through Sam to Seth.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.description: I observed that a pack member, Seth, reacted with agonized tension and then obeyed orders to return to the forest.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.source_text: Seth was crouched, still tensed in agony, looking as if he meant to launch himself into the forest. 'No!' Edward ordered. 'You gostraight home. Now. As fast as you can!' ... The huge wolf stared into Edward’s agonized eyes for one long second, and then he straightened up and flew into the trees, disappearing like a ghost.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.description: I inferred that the pack (represented by Sam and Seth) is aligned and able to act on information from Alice, which affects how I view their role in the conflict.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc5.source_text: Earlier this morning, Alice saw it and passed it through Sam to Seth.

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob had been injured during the fight with the newborns.
I became convinced that Jacob’s injury was severe when Bella blacked out upon hearing his name.
I realized that Jacob’s condition is central to Bella’s emotional state and that his injury directly affects her consciousness.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc6.source_text: "Of course," I whispered. And then I slipped off the edge I was clinging to inside my head. Everything went black."

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc7.description: I learned that Jacob had suffered extensive trauma with most bones on the right half of his body shattered but that his life was not in danger and he was healing rapidly.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc7.source_text: “Most of the bones on the right half of his body were shattered.” “His life is not in any danger. He was healing at an incredible rate, though his injuries were extensive enough that it will still be a few days before he is back to normal... He won’t have any permanent damage.”

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc7.description: I shifted from panic about Jacob’s fate to relief when I heard multiple people, including Edward and Carlisle, confirm that he would survive and recover.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc7.source_text: “He’s going to live, Bella. Jacob Black is healing as I speak. He’ll be fine.” “His life is not in any danger.”

tw-book3-chapter25_Sc7.description: I felt increased concern and protective feelings for Jacob after learning how severely he had been hurt and that Sam and Paul had intervened to help him.
tw-book3-chapter25_Sc7.source_text: “Sam and Paul got there in time. He was already improving when they took him back to La Push.” “He knocked her out of the way, but he didn’t have time to defend himself.”

tw-book3-chapter26_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob was badly injured, pale and unconscious at first, but was healing quickly so Carlisle said there was no point in plaster.
tw-book3-chapter26_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "He’d had braces everywhere — Carlisle said there was no point in plaster, as fast as he was healing. His face had been pale and drawn, deeply unconscious though he was at the time."

tw-book3-chapter26_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob woke up about a half hour before the doctor left and that the doctors were using trial and error with his pain medication.
tw-book3-chapter26_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "He woke up about a half hour ago, just before the doctor left." "Dr. Fang isn’t sure how much pain medication I need, so he’s going with trial and error."

tw-book3-chapter26_Sc2.description: I noticed that Jacob showed genuine concern for Bella's safety and repeatedly asked if she was okay after he woke.
tw-book3-chapter26_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "How about you?" he asked, sounding really concerned. "Are you okay?"

tw-book3-chapter26_Sc2.description: I perceived that Jacob's appearance shifted from gaunt and fragile to a careful blankness with a mocking smile when he was awake.
tw-book3-chapter26_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "The haggard, gaunt look was gone, but only a careful blankness took its place." "Then, with some effort, he rearranged his expression into a slightly mocking smile."

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc1.description: I had deliberately hidden my breakdown from Jacob and I believed that hiding it was the right choice.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc1.source_text: Yes, I had been right to hide this from Jacob. No one should ever see this.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc1.description: I felt conflicted because I craved Jacob’s arms in that smaller part of myself while I was being comforted by Edward, which increased my guilt.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc1.source_text: Because there was that smaller part of me — smaller, but getting louder and angrier every minute, screaming at the rest of me — that craved a different set of arms. So then there was fresh guilt to season the pain.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc1.description: I became more convinced that I must protect Jacob from seeing my weakness and I reinforced the boundary of what I would reveal to him.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc1.source_text: Yes, I had been right to hide this from Jacob. No one should ever see this.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc2.description: I confirmed that Jacob was physically fine after the confrontation.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc2.source_text: “He’s fine, he’s fine,” I promised, my voice low and husky.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc2.description: I noted that Jacob recovers quickly from physical harm.
My interaction with Jacob involved difficult, unavoidable choices and emotional topics.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc2.source_text: I . . . just had to talk to Jacob about . . . some things that were hard.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc3.description: I acknowledged that I had caused Jacob pain and wanted him to get better and be happy again.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc3.source_text: Each pain I’d caused Jacob, each wound I’d given Edward, stacked up into neat piles that I could not ignore or deny. But I didn’t care if time healed me or not, so long as Jacob could get better. Could be happy again.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc3.description: I understood that my attempts to reconcile parts of myself had hurt Jacob even though he was not present that night.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc3.source_text: And I realized that I’d been wrong all along about the magnets. It had not been Edward and Jacob that I’d been trying to force together, it was the two parts of myself, Edward’s Bella and Jacob’s Bella. But they could not exist together, and I never should have tried.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc4.description: I noted that Jacob Black was not present in the scene and that only Bella and Edward were identified as present.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc4.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc4.description: I implicitly prioritized Edward by reaffirming that I could not live without him, which updates the relational context relative to others not present.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc4.source_text: I know who I can\'t live without.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob Black was a tracked character but was not present during this dress-reveal scene.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc5.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Alice Cullen, Edward Cullen

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc5.description: I concluded that Jacob was not involved in the wedding-dress reveal or immediate preparations in this scene.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc5.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Alice Cullen, Edward Cullen

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc6.description: I worried that Jacob would feel obligated to attend the wedding and that he might be hurt if excluded.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc6.source_text: “I’m not sure if Alice would feel the need to invite . . . a few werewolves. I don’t know if . . . Jake would feel like . . . like he should come. Like that’s the right thing to do, or that I’d get my feelings hurt if he didn’t. He shouldn’t have to go through that.”

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc6.description: I understood that Jacob was considered among the werewolves who might be invited to the wedding by Alice.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc6.source_text: “I’m not sure if Alice would feel the need to invite . . . a few werewolves. I don’t know if . . . Jake would feel like . . . like he should come."

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc7.description: I learned that I came to the very edge of the earth and sky and sea to be alone.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc7.source_text: She knew why I came here — to the very edge of the earth and sky and sea. To be alone.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc7.description: I changed my belief about my control when I realized that controlling my temper had become easy and natural.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc7.source_text: Because I didn’t even have to think about controlling my temper. It was easy now, something I just did, natural. The red haze didn’t wash over my eyes.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc7.description: I updated my relationship feeling toward Leah to one of contempt mixed with guilt for provoking her and relief when she left.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc7.source_text: She scrambled to her feet — pausing only to spit in my direction — and ran for the trees, vibrating like a tuning fork.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc7.description: I learned that I was using a motorcycle accident story and crutches to cover my situation at home.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc7.source_text: I made a face as I pulled my arm through the retarded sling and grabbed my crutches. If only Charlie hadn’t seen me that day and spread the word of my “motorcycle accident.” Stupid props.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc8.description: I learned that I can see and hear packmates through their minds and even see through their eyes.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: So sorry,Embry whispered in my head.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc8.description: I noticed that packmates feel pity and worry for me and continue to follow despite my anger.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: I could feel their worry in my head, try hard as I might to drown it in the sound of the wind and the forest.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc8.description: I learned that Sam can issue telepathic orders to the pack and command them to phase back or wait.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: Let him go.Sam’s thought was soft, but still an order.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc8.description: I decided that remaining in wolf form might be preferable to being human because silence is worth the cost.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: If the silence in my head lasted, I would never go back. I wouldn’t be the first one to choose this form over the other.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc8.description: I hated being seen through the pack's pitying eyes and I resented how that made me feel exposed.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: This was what I hated most — seeing myself through their eyes, worse now that their eyes were full of pity.

tw-book3-chapter27_Sc8.description: I realized that I was trying to let my human identity fade away as I pushed myself faster and farther from the pack.
tw-book3-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: I pushed my legs faster, letting Jacob Black disappear behind me.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob called and asked pointedly whether I was going to school tomorrow before abruptly ending the call.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc4.source_text: “You going to school tomorrow?” "I have to go," he said abruptly.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc4.description: I began to suspect that Jacob's persistence and the timing of his call after three days signaled an unstated urgency or concern.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc4.source_text: What could have changed in the past three days that was so important that Jacob would break his long streak of refusing to answer my phone calls and contact me?

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc4.description: I felt that Jacob's brief desire to hear my voice followed by a sudden departure altered my perception of him as straightforward and introduced an ominous tension.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc4.source_text: “I . . . wanted to hear your voice.” "I have to go," he said abruptly. "I'll talk to you soon, okay?"

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob had been asking whether I was still human as a way to check that the werewolves' treaty remained unbroken and that no Cullens had bitten a human.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: Had Jacob really been asking me if I was still human? Making sure that the werewolves’ treaty was unbroken — that none of the Cullens had dared to bite a human . . . bite, not kill . . . ?

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc5.description: I suspected that Jacob expected some clear answer about my humanity and that his enforcement stance affected how I thought he would treat my situation.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: "I think . . . I think he was checking," I mumbled. "Checking to make sure. That I’m human, I mean."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc5.description: I doubted that Jacob honestly believed I would simply go home to Charlie if I had been bitten, which changed how I interpreted his questioning.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc5.source_text: But did he honestly think I would come home to Charlie if that was the case?

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc7.description: I noticed Jacob insisted that Bella had a right to know and directly challenged Edward about withholding information.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc7.source_text: Why haven’t you told her? “You don’t think Bella has a right to know?” Jacob challenged. “Better frightened than lied to.”

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc7.description: I saw Jacob provoke Edward by recalling painful memories, laughing 'That’s funny' as Edward winced.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc7.source_text: “That’s funny,” Jacob said, laughing as he watched Edward’s face. Jacob grinned, and Edward winced again.

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc7.description: I perceived Jacob’s teasing as a deliberate challenge to Edward’s secrecy and a defense of Bella’s right to information.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc7.source_text: “It’s his own fault if he doesn’t like the things I remember, though.”

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc8.description: I learned that Jacob expressed willingness to try being friends and admitted he might have been wrong about not being able to be friends.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: "I think I might have been wrong before, you know, about not being able to be friends. Maybe we could manage it, on my side of the line. Come see me."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc8.description: I watched Jacob salute the principal, start his motorcycle with a snarling engine, and ride away after being told to remove himself from school property.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: "Jacob said, 'Yes, sir,' and snapped a military salute before he climbed on his bike and kicked it to a start right there on the sidewalk. The engine snarled and then the tires squealed as he spun it sharply around. In a matter of seconds, Jacob raced out of sight."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc8.description: I noticed that Jacob masked his pain with sarcasm and a bitter, mocking grin, indicating emotional hurt beneath bravado.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc8.source_text: "Jacob’s little smirk became a full-blown grin, and I knew he was picturing Charlie showing up to arrest him. This grin was too bitter, too full of mocking to satisfy me."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc9.description: I learned that Paul and the rest of the Quileute pack were involved in the pursuit of Victoria alongside some of the Cullens.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc9.source_text: I read: "And then Paul and the rest of the Quileute pack."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc9.description: I learned that a large Quileute wolf became defensive when Emmett approached what the wolf perceived as the boundary line.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc9.source_text: I read: "The big gray one thought Emmett was over the line, and he got defensive."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc9.description: I imagined that the wolves would have been the most in danger if a fight had broken out and I felt worried for their safety.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc9.source_text: I read: "I imagined the wolves would be in the most danger, but picturing tiny Alice next to one of the huge werewolves,fighting . . . I shuddered."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc10.description: I heard classmates remark on Jacob's size and suggest he might be able to "take Cullen down."
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc10.source_text: "Did you see thesize of that Jacob kid? I think he could take Cullen down."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc10.description: I learned that classmates reported Jacob's friends at La Push are similarly large, reinforcing the perception of physical strength.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc10.source_text: "Have you been down to La Push lately?" Mike asked. "Lauren and I went to the beach a couple of weeks ago, and believe me, Jacob's friends are all just as big as he is."

tw-book3-chapter3_Sc10.description: I noticed that several students were willing to bet on Jacob, indicating they view him as a strong contender in a fight.
tw-book3-chapter3_Sc10.source_text: "Ten on Jacob," Austin said at once. "Jacob," Mike said.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob and Sam were the only ones who initially felt bitter about becoming wolves and that Sam eventually got past that bitterness.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc1.source_text: “Sam and I are the only ones who ever felt really bitter. And Sam got past that a long time ago.”

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc1.description: I learned that the wolves find positive aspects to their change, including speed, freedom, strength, and a sense of family.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc1.source_text: “There are definitely good sides to this — the speed, the freedom, the strength . . . the sense of — ofamily . . . .”

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc1.description: I realized that Jacob perceives himself as having shifted into the role of the 'crybaby' after Sam recovered from bitterness.
I observed that Jacob was protective toward me and offered practical support to prevent me from returning to a situation that might anger Charlie.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc1.source_text: “So don’t go back. I’ll sleep on the couch.”

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob knows detailed history about Sam’s difficult beginnings with phasing and that the pack’s people and rangers searched for him.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: “Sam had it so much harder than the rest of us. Because he was the first, and he was alone... Sam’s mother and Leah Clearwater had the forest rangers searching for him, the police.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.description: I noticed that Jacob oscillated between antagonism and tenderness when he grimly asked if Edward was ready to kill him and later put his arm around me and apologized.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: “Is he ready to kill me?” Jacob asked with a grim smile, unconcerned by my anger... “Sorry,” he said quietly. “I’ll try to behave myself.”

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.description: I found that my irritation softened because my curiosity was pricked by Jacob’s promise to tell the strange story about Sam.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: His words pricked my curiosity in spite of my irritation.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob is willing to tell long, complicated stories about their new life and the strange experiences within the pack.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc2.source_text: “Like I said, it’s a long story. And very . . . strange. There’re so many strange things about this new life. I haven’t had time to tell you the half of it.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: I heard Jacob say that Leah and Sam were high school sweethearts and that Leah was frantic when he disappeared.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: "Yeah. Leah and Sam were high school sweethearts. They started dating when she was just a freshman. She was frantic when he disappeared."

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: I heard Jacob say that Sam came back but wouldn't talk to anyone about where he'd been and that rumors flew that he was up to no good.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: "Sam came back," Jacob said, "but he wouldn't talk to anyone about where he'd been. Rumors flew — that he was up to no good, mostly."

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: I heard Jacob explain that Sam shook Old Quil Ateara's hand and that Old Quil nearly had a stroke because Sam's hand felt burning hot.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: Sam shook his hand. Old Quil just about had a stroke. Sam's hand felt like he'd left it sitting on a hot stovetop.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: I heard Jacob say that Mr. Ateara, Billy, and Harry had seen their grandfathers make the change and that they met with Sam secretly to explain.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: Mr. Ateara, Billy, and Harry had actually seen their grandfathers make the change. When Old Quil told them, they met with Sam secretly and explained.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: I noticed Jacob pronounced the Cullens' name with unconscious bitterness, which revealed his negative feelings toward them.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: "They knew he wouldn’t be the only one affected by the Cullens’ return" — he pronounced the name with unconscious bitterness — "but no one else was old enough."

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.description: I felt Jacob's warm breath and his palm burning my skin as he leaned close, and I entwined my fingers with his to avoid hurting his feelings, which updated my sense of our closeness.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc3.source_text: His palm burned my skin, like he had a fever. He was so close, I could feel his warm breath. I reached up casually, to take his hand away and free my face, but wound my fingers through his so that I wouldn't hurt his feelings.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob says the tribe will resume aging only if they stop phasing for a solid length of time and gain control.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc4.source_text: When we stop phasing for a solid length of time, we age again.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob claims he is already physically older than Bella.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc4.source_text: I’m already older than you, physically at least.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc4.description: I observed Jacob alternate between teasing and gentle behavior as he rolled his eyes and tried to soothe Bella.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob (and those like him) reach full physical maturity very quickly after the gene triggers and that the change can be dramatic from day to day.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc5.source_text: Because we reach full growth inside of a few months when the werewolf gene gets triggered. It's one hell of a growth spurt.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc5.description: I learned that Sam learned what was happening and that life became almost okay for him but that secrecy about the change made things difficult.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc5.source_text: So, you're right. Sam knew what was going on, and everything was almost okay. In most ways, his life was back to, well, not normal. But better.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc5.description: I learned that Sam could not tell Leah about his change because they were not supposed to tell anyone who didn't have to know and that being around her was not really safe.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc5.source_text: Sam couldn't tell Leah. We aren't supposed to tell anyone who doesn't have to know. And it wasn't really safe for him to be around her — but he cheated, just like I did with you.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob admitted he 'cheated' by hiding things and by being with Bella in secret, paralleling Sam's breaches of secrecy and contributing to relationship strain with Leah.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc5.source_text: but he cheated, just like I did with you.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc8.description: I noticed that Jacob was curious and a bit confused about Edward not hearing me.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc8.source_text:
Jacob looked up at me with a curious expression. “But isn’t it like that for you all the time? Havinghim in your head?”
“Yeah.” The smugness faded. “It probably means there’s something wrong with my brain,” I admitted.
“I already knew there was something wrong with your brain,” Jacob muttered.
“Thanks.”

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc8.description: I noticed that Jacob is physically affectionate and comfortable with me because he settled closer, leaned on my arm, and rested his cheek on my head.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc8.source_text: Jacob settled closer to me, so that he was leaning against my arm. He made a little sound of contentment in the back of his throat, and rested his cheek on the top of my head.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc8.description: I learned that Jacob remembered the moronic movie I took him to and the moment Mike Newton puking everywhere.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc8.source_text: He chuckled to himself. “I was remembering that moronic movie you took me to. And Mike Newton puking all over everything.”

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc9.description: I learned that Jacob had seen Sam's memory of the way Bella looked when Sam found her and that the memory haunted both Sam and Jacob.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc9.source_text: I was remembering the way you looked that night Sam found you — I’ve seen it in his head, and it’s like I was there; that memory has always haunted Sam, you know.

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc9.description: I realized that Jacob missed the simplicity of the past and that he valued having a good memory of those times.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc9.source_text: “I miss that,” Jacob said. “The way it used to be so easy . . . uncomplicated. I’m glad I’ve got a good memory.”

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc9.description: I acknowledged that Jacob apologized to Bella and promised not to repeat the teasing, indicating that he respected her boundary.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc9.source_text: “I’m sorry. And . . . okay, I won’t do it again. Promise.”

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.description: I heard Jacob call what Edward is doing a disgusting act and refer to them as "disgusting parasites."
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.source_text: "'Away?' Jacob rolled his eyes. 'That's a nice way to describe what he's doing. Disgusting parasites.'"

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.description: I heard Jacob reluctantly state that he is a werewolf.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.source_text: "'But I am a werewolf,' he said unwillingly."

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.description: I noticed Jacob refused to let go of my hand when I tried to pull free.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.source_text: "'If you can't be nice, I won't come back at all!' I threatened, trying to pull my hand free. He refused to let go."

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.description: I observed Jacob soften, smile, and agree to a simple 'just Bella and Jacob' understanding, showing that his anger had eased.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.source_text: "'If you can really see it that way . . .'" and "'Okay. Just Bella and Jacob. None of those freaky Virgos here.' He smiled at me, the warm, familiar smile that I had missed so much."

tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.description: I realized that Jacob had missed me and that his eyes were free of the angry bitterness for once.
tw-book3-chapter5_Sc10.source_text: "'Me, too,' his smile widened. His eyes were happy and clear, free for once of the angry bitterness."

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob had confided extensive secrets to me which I was trying to force into sense.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: I was thinking about the flood of information Jacob had shared with me, trying to sort it out, to force it all to make sense.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.description: I felt lighter after Jacob smiled and after the secrets were thrashed out, and I believed the situation was improved.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: Despite the overload, I felt lighter. Seeing Jacob smile, having all the secrets thrashed out . . . it didn’t make things perfect, but it made them better.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.description: I believed I was right to have gone to see Jacob because I perceived that Jacob needed me in that moment.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc1.source_text: I was right to have gone. Jacob needed me.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc2.description: I believe that Jacob is not dangerous and I reassured Edward and others of that belief.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc2.source_text: "There's nothing to worry about. Jacob isn't dangerous."

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc2.description: I told Charlie that I had gone to La Push and I learned that Billy had already mentioned my visit to him.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc2.source_text:
“They didn’t need me at work, so I went down to La Push.”

“There wasn’t enough surprise in his face. Billy had already talked to him.”

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc3.description: I declared that Jacob is family.
I called Jacob during my brief window of opportunity to tell him I would be coming over on Saturday.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: I didn’t feel guilty calling Jake — during my brief window of opportunity when Edward took the Volvo home before climbing back in through my window — to let him know I’d be coming over on Saturday again.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc3.description: I intended that Jacob would pick me up if Edward broke my truck again.
tw-book3-chapter6_Sc3.source_text: And if he broke my truck again, then I’d have Jacob pick me up.

tw-book3-chapter6_Sc4.description: I noticed that Jacob Black was not mentioned as present in this scene and therefore had no interaction here.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc3.description: I learned that this scene focuses on Rosalie's upbringing and desires and does not mention Jacob or his life.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc3.source_text: My mother’s job to keep our house — and myself and my two younger brothers — in spotless order.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.description: I noticed Jacob's loud, black motorcycle arrival and I observed him wave urgently for me to run.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.source_text:
the noisy black motorcycle screeched to a stop on the edge of the concrete, the engine still snarling.
Jacob waved to me urgently.
“Run, Bella!” he yelled over the engine’s roar.

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.description: I appreciated Jacob's quick thinking and I recognized him as willing to take risks to help me get away.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: We made it,” he shouted. “Not bad for a prison break, eh?

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.description: I learned from Jacob that the Quileute border creates a safe zone where Alice's predictions cannot reach us.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: “I remembered what you said about the psychic leech not being about to predict what I’m going to do. I’m glad you didn’t think of this — she wouldn’t have let you go to school.”

tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.description: I felt exhilarated and amused by Jacob's laughter and the successful escape after crossing into the safe zone.
tw-book3-chapter7_Sc10.source_text: The bike slowed, and Jacob straightened up and howled with laughter.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc1.description: I recognized that Jacob had engineered my escape and was proud of it.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: Jacob was still full of himself for engineering my escape.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc1.description: I observed Jacob ask if anyone would come looking for me while sounding hopeful.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: Do you think they’ll come looking for you?” he asked, sounding hopeful.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc1.description: I noticed Jacob miss not having everyone know everything all the time and value a quiet, private place inside his head.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: "I forget what it’s like, not having everyone know everything all the time. Having a quiet, private place inside my head."

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc1.description: I felt Jacob reach for my hand and that his gesture reinforced a close, couplelike connection between us.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc1.source_text: Without seeming to think about it, he reached out and took my hand.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob communicated that Quil had imprinted on a toddler and that the imprinting is considered scandalous by others.
I understood from Jacob that imprinting is not like instantaneous romantic love but feels like a gravitational pull that makes the imprinter become whatever the imprinted needs.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: "It’s not like love at first sight, really. It’s more like . . . gravity moves. When you see her, suddenly it’s not the earth holding you here anymore. She does. And nothing matters more than her. And you would do anything for her, be anything for her. . . . You become whatever she needs you to be, whether that’s a protector, or a lover, or a friend, or a brother."

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc2.description: I noticed Jacob defended Quil vehemently and I felt that Jacob accused me of being judgmental.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc2.source_text: "It’s not like that; you’ve got it all wrong," Jacob defended his friend, suddenly vehement. "You’re making judgments," he accused.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob believes imprinting is not something he can control and that he expects he may never find his match.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: I noted: "Never." "It's not supposed to be," he admitted. "But you have to see her — the one that's supposedly meant for you."

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc3.description: I noticed Jacob promise to stop being forward about his feelings and to just be Jacob, which shifted how I perceived his restraint.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: I noted: "Sorry," he apologized. "I won't be like that anymore. I'll just be Jacob."

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc3.description: I observed that Jacob masks his anxiety with deliberate cheer and that he tries to occupy me and protect me while I am vulnerable.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc3.source_text: I noted: "Don't worry about me," he insisted, smiling with deliberate cheer, too brightly. "I know what I'm doing. Just tell me if I'm upsetting you."

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc5.description: I confirmed from Jacob that he asked whether I had been bitten and that I answered yes when he questioned me.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc5.source_text: "You know. When you said it was none of my business . . . if — if he bit you." "Yes," I whispered.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc5.description: I learned from Jacob that the treaty had no geographic limit and that it relied on the Cullens' vow not to harm humans.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc5.source_text: "There wasn't a geographic limit to the treaty, Bella. Our great-grandfathers only agreed to keep the peace because the Cullens swore that they were different, that humans weren't in danger from them."

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc5.description: I believed that if the Cullens broke their vow the treaty would be meaningless and that conflict or war would be inevitable.
I understood that Jacob declared he would no longer recognize the Bella he knew and that our friendship would end.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc5.source_text: "You won't be Bella anymore," he told me. "My friend won't exist."

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc6.description: I observed Jacob erupt suddenly, with a soda can popping in his hand and soda soaking me as a sign of his emotional outburst.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc6.source_text: He was suddenly on his feet, and there was a loudpop as the soda can exploded in his hand. Soda flew everywhere, soaking me, like it was spraying from a hose.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc6.description: I watched Jacob quiver, growl, and blur as if near transformation before he forced himself to calm down.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc6.source_text: The shaking rolled through him, getting faster, until it looked like he was vibrating. His shape blurred. . . . And then Jacob gritted his teeth together, and the growling stopped. He squeezed his eyes tight in concentration; the quivering slowed until only his hands were shaking.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc6.description: I realized Jacob's feelings had turned hostile toward my choice of Edward when he said he would rather I were dead.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc6.source_text: “Anything. Anything else. You’d be better off dead. I’d rather you were.”

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc6.description: I felt hurt and recoiled physically when Jacob's words struck me, as if I had been slapped.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc6.source_text: I recoiled like he’d slapped me. It hurt worse than if he had.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc8.description: I observed that Jacob Black was not present in this scene and that only Bella and Edward were there.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc8.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc8.description: I inferred that Bella's declared lack of interest in staying angry with everyone could include a softened stance toward people like Jacob.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc8.source_text: I didn’t care that I was supposed to be angry with him. I didn’t care that I was supposed to be angry with everyone.

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc9.description: I learned that Jacob was surprised that Bella's change or decision came so soon and that he had not been expecting it.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc9.source_text: “He wasn’t expecting . . . that it was so soon.”

tw-book3-chapter8_Sc9.description: I concluded that Bella now feels threatened and unwelcome because Jacob verbally expressed a preference to see her dead.
tw-book3-chapter8_Sc9.source_text: “He said he’d rather see me dead.” "I don’t think I’m welcome anymore," I whispered.

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob called, apologized, and asked me to be nice and give him a break because he sounded upset.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: He said he didn’t mean it, and that he’s sorry. He wants you to call him. Be nice and give him a break. He sounded upset.

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc1.description: I hardened my stance toward Jacob by deciding not to call him and by mentally accepting silence if he preferred me dead.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: I didn’t want to talk to him. Last I’d heard, they weren’t big on allowing phone calls from the other side. If Jacob preferred me dead, then maybe he should get used to the silence.

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc1.description: I became less forgiving of Jacob in the moment and chose not to engage with him despite his apology.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc1.source_text: I grimaced. Charlie didn’t usually editorialize on my messages. Jacob could just go ahead and be upset. I didn’t want to talk to him.

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob called to apologize profusely and I heard him call the incident the stupidest thing he’d ever said.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: Oh, Bella, I’m so sorry! ... It was the stupidest thing I’ve ever said in my life and I’m sorry.

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob proposed that Bella be safest on the reservation and I heard him urge convincing my 'bloodsucker' of that plan.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: Try to convince your bloodsucker that the safest place for you to be — especially when he leaves — is on the reservation. We’re well able to handle anything.

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob suggested rearranging territorial boundaries to catch anyone who approached Forks and I heard him offer to keep an eye on things until Sam agreed.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: Just rearranging some boundaries, so we can catch anyone who gets too near Forks. ... but until he comes around, I’ll keep an eye on things.

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.description: I learned that Jacob intended to gather the scent of my visitor so we could track him and I heard him say he was going to get that scent.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: Yeah. I’m going to get the scent of your visitor so we can track him if he c

tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.description: I noticed Jacob’s tone shift from ashamed to eager to help and I inferred that he prioritized protecting Bella over lingering anger.
tw-book3-chapter9_Sc3.source_text: He’s not thrilled with me, is he? ... That’s not the problem. There’s . . . well, there’s this other problem that’s slightly more worrisome than a bratty teenage werewolf. . . .

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob was missing and that the town was plastered with HAVE YOU SEEN THIS BOY? posters asking about him.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: The HAVE YOU SEEN THIS BOY? posters were not Jacob’s father’s idea. ... Each one of them, stapled to telephone poles and taped to street signs, was like a fresh slap in the face.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.description: I knew that Jacob lived in La Push on the reservation and that his father Billy refused to put up flyers there and seemed resigned to Jacob's disappearance.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: For Billy’s refusing to put up the flyers in La Push, the reservation on the coast that was Jacob’s home. For his seeming resigned to Jacob’s disappearance, as if there was nothing he could do. For his saying, “Jacob’s grown up now. He’ll come home if he wants to.”

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.description: I recognized Jacob as my best friend and my close emotional tie, which made his disappearance a personal loss for me.
I understood that my father had made my missing friend the focus of an extensive search that included police stations and multiple towns.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc4.source_text: He’d made sure that all the police stations in the state of Washington had the same flyer hanging on the wall, too. His own station had a whole corkboard dedicated to finding Jacob.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob is deliberately avoiding humans and following his wolf instincts.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.source_text: He's trying not to think human, you know. Just going with his instincts.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob's current location is somewhere in northern Canada and that he doesn't pay attention to state lines.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.source_text: Somewhere in northern Canada. I can't tell you which province. He doesn't pay much attention to state lines.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob made his choices and that some pack members hold a negative attitude about my choice.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.source_text: Jacob made his choices, you made yours. Jake doesn't like their attitude about it.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob knows I am worried because he can't hide everything from the pack.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc5.source_text: He can't hide everything from us, hard as he's trying.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc6.description: I learned that Jacob was a runaway who was one of the straws on my father's overburdened back.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc6.source_text: Jacob-the-runaway was just one of the straws on his overburdened back.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc6.description: I understood that Jacob's situation contributed to my father's worry about me as his barely-a-legal-adult daughter.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc6.source_text: My poor dad had so much to deal with right now. Jacob-the-runaway was just one of the straws on his overburdened back. He was almost as worried about me, his barely-a-legal-adult daughter who was about to become a Mrs. in just a few days’ time.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc10.description: I noticed that Jacob was not listed among the people present for this fitting and therefore was not part of the scene.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc10.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Charlie Swan, Alice, Edward Cullen

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.description: I noticed the empty seat where my best friend should be.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.source_text: I didn’t worry about tripping on my train or giggling at the wrong moment or being too young or the staring audience or even the empty seat where my best friend should be.

tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.description: I didn’t care in that moment that the whole town was talking about me or that my best friend was absent because I was with Edward in my happy place.
tw-book4-chapter1_Sc11.source_text: I didn’t care, for the moment, that the whole town was talking about me. I didn’t think about the spectacle I would have to star in much too soon. I didn’t worry... even the empty seat where my best friend should be.

tw-book4-chapter19_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob was present at the scene and was actively trying to keep me conscious and alive.
tw-book4-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: I read 'Jacob? Jacob, still here, still trying to save me.'

tw-book4-chapter19_Sc1.description: I heard Jacob urgently demand that I stay with him and keep my heart beating as he tried to help me through the crisis.
tw-book4-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: I heard 'You stay with me now, Bella! Do you hear me? Stay! You’re not leaving me. Keep your heart beating!'

tw-book4-chapter19_Sc1.description: I remembered that I had promised both Edward and Jacob that I would stay, and that promise motivated me to fight for my life.
tw-book4-chapter19_Sc1.source_text: I remembered 'Hadn’t I promised them both?'

tw-book4-chapter19_Sc2.description: I recognized that Jacob was among those depending on my survival and that thought strengthened my will to live.
tw-book4-chapter19_Sc2.source_text: Edward was depending on me. Jacob. Charlie Alice Rosalie Carlisle Renée Esme… Renesmee.

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc3.description: I feared that Jacob might hate me or have returned to Sam’s pack after my transformation.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: What about Jacob? Was he fine? Did my long-suffering best friend hate me now? Had he gone back to Sam’s pack? Seth and Leah, too?

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc3.description: I became uncertain about my bond with Jacob and worried that my transformation could have driven a wedge between us.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: What about Jacob? Was he fine? Did my long-suffering best friend hate me now?

tw-book4-chapter20_Sc3.description: I recognized that I did not know Jacob's status and that his whereabouts and feelings were unknown to me in that moment.
tw-book4-chapter20_Sc3.source_text: What about Jacob? Was he fine? Did my long-suffering best friend hate me now? Had he gone back to Sam’s pack?

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc1.description: I realized that Jacob was downstairs with Renesmee and that his heart had been beating below.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: Renesmee and Jacob are downstairs. . . . I realized belatedly that it must have been Jacob’s heart I’d heard below.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob does not like Renesmee much.
I understood that Jacob’s proximity could trigger my wild side and that I needed to keep away from his scent.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc1.source_text: I had to keep away from scents that might trigger my wild side. From the people that I loved in particular.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.description: I heard a different, rough, throaty chuckle from the first floor and inferred that Jacob was watching from the house.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: The laughter came from upstairs and down, and I very easily recognized the much different, rough, throaty chuckle from the first floor.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.description: I became aware that Jacob remained hurt by my past actions and that I had hoped for a future reunion when I was more stable.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: I couldn’t imagine what he was thinking now, or what he was still doing here. I’d envisioned our reunion—if he could ever forgive me—taking place far in the future, when I was more stable, and time had healed the wounds I’d inflicted in his heart.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.description: I felt uncertain about confronting Jacob immediately because of my mood swings and Jasper's fears, and I wanted to hunt before dealing with complicated emotions.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc2.source_text: I didn’t turn to look at him now, wary of my mood swings. It wouldn’t be good to let any emotion take too strong a hold on my frame of mind. Jasper’s fears had me on edge, too. I had to hunt before I dealt with anything else.

tw-book4-chapter21_Sc8.description: I believed that if I could resist killing totally human strangers then I might be able to handle the werewolf and the half-vampire child that I loved.
tw-book4-chapter21_Sc8.source_text: If I could resist totally human strangers, wouldn’t I be able to handle the werewolf and a half-vampire child that I loved?

tw-book4-chapter22_Sc2.description: I noticed that Jacob became nervous and that he confronted Edward while pleading about whether I should see the child.
tw-book4-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "It’s nothing you need to worry about this second" and "Are you sure, bloodsucker?"

tw-book4-chapter22_Sc2.description: I realized that Jacob's behavior was protective and anxious regarding Renesmee, as he hurried into the house and then stood between Rosalie and the others while cringing from the proximity.
tw-book4-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "Jacob joined her and then stood in front of her, closer than was normal, There was no sense of comfort in that closeness; both of them seemed to cringe from the proximity"

tw-book4-chapter22_Sc2.description: I inferred that Jacob's physical reaction to me might alter his romantic feelings and open the possibility of a different, friendlier relationship between us.
tw-book4-chapter22_Sc2.source_text: I quote: "Maybe now I could truly be his friend, since I disgusted him enough physically that he couldn't love me the same way as before"

tw-book4-chapter22_Sc3.description: I noticed that Jacob's skin felt almost as warm as Renesmee's and that touching him now felt like touching an open flame to me.
tw-book4-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: His skin, always so warm to me before, felt like an open flame to me now. It was almost the same temperature as Renesmee’s.

tw-book4-chapter22_Sc3.description: I realized that Jacob had an immediate, close connection with Renesmee as he accepted her from Rosalie without protest and interacted with her easily.
tw-book4-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: Renesmee went to Jacob willingly enough, pushing her tiny hand against his cheek and then squirming around to stretch toward me again.

tw-book4-chapter22_Sc3.description: I was surprised to see Jacob's face more serene than I had seen in a long time despite his obvious anxiety, which changed my belief about his emotional state around Renesmee.
tw-book4-chapter22_Sc3.source_text: And yet, despite his obvious anxiety, his face was more serene than I had seen it in a long time.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: I observed that Jacob did not phase to protect himself during the incident and I understood that he had not actively mitigated the situation.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I noticed the line describing Jacob as someone "who wouldn’t even phase to protect himself."

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob was being kept outside with Renesmee and I understood that others wanted me kept away from the baby for safety.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I heard that the group agreed I should be kept away from my baby and I listened to Jacob being described as outside with Renesmee.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: I heard Jacob and Rosalie bickering over whose turn it was to feed Renesmee and I noted their ongoing antagonistic dynamic.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I heard them bickering quietly on the front steps about whose turn it was to feed Renesmee.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.description: I felt that Jacob did not deserve my overreaction and I acknowledged that my anger was disproportionate to his actions.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc1.source_text: I admitted to myself, "I knew that Jacob didn’t deserve my overreaction."

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob’s imprinting on Renesmee made her untouchable under the pack’s rules and ensured the pack would not harm her.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: So Renesmee was untouchable because of the way Jacob now felt about her.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: I recognized that Jacob and I were now defined as family in some way because of his words about belonging in each other’s lives.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: You said we belonged in each other’s lives, right? That we were family.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc2.description: I felt both relief and chagrin about owing Jacob so much and found it difficult to be angry with him despite wanting to be.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc2.source_text: It rankled to realize over and over again how much I owed Jacob when I just wanted to be mad at him.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: I noticed Jacob stood tense with his arms crossed tightly while he watched the measurements.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc3.source_text: I was aware that Jacob’s arms were crossed as tightly over his chest as Edward’s arms were locked around me.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: I perceived Jacob’s anger soften into resigned concern when he sighed and said he guessed that was all he could ask.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc3.source_text: Guess that’s all I can ask.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: I saw Jacob express fondness and a claim of being liked by Renesmee even while looking troubled.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc3.source_text: I told you she likes me, too, Jacob teased from across the room, his eyes on Renesmee.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc3.description: I heard Jacob demand that Carlisle be perfect in his measurements, revealing his urgent protectiveness.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc3.source_text: Be perfect, Doc, Jacob said, making the words almost threatening.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc4.description: I noted that Jacob was not present among the characters in this scene and therefore had no direct actions or statements here.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc4.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen, Renesmee, Jasper, Leah, Rosalie, Carlisle, Emmett, Alice, Esme

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc5.description: I observed that Jacob sat next to Seth in a protective posture and looked bored before falling asleep.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: Jacob sat next to Seth protectively, looking bored. From the way his eyelids drooped, I was sure he’d be unconscious momentarily.

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc5.description: I noticed that Jacob can hold Renesmee very still and that his stillness attracted nearby sparrows when he held her beneath a hemlock.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: like the sparrows that had hopped closer and closer when Jacob had held her, both of them very still beside one of the big hemlocks;

tw-book4-chapter23_Sc5.description: I felt a subtle rivalry with Jacob because Renesmee's unconscious thoughts included my face as often as his, which I tried not to let bother me.
tw-book4-chapter23_Sc5.source_text: I was pleased by how often my face—both of my faces...cropped up in her unconscious thoughts. More than Edward or Rosalie. I was neck and neck with Jacob; I tried not to let that get to me.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc1.description: I noticed that Jacob (and Seth) looked crashed for the night and might have stayed up late.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: then nodded toward Jacob and Seth, who looked like they were crashed for the night; I wonder how long they’d stayed up this time.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc1.description: I learned that Jacob is one of the people who sometimes holds Renesmee when she sleeps.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: “Where does she usually sleep?” Alice shrugged. “In Rose's arms. Or Jacob's. Or Esme's. You get the picture.”

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc1.description: I recognized that Jacob’s presence and enthusiasm matter to me and that Edward wanted Jacob to be awake for the reveal for that reason.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc1.source_text: “I think it might be more fun if Jacob was awake for the big reveal, don’t you agree? So that someone there is able to express the right level of enthusiasm?”

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc2.description: I noticed Jacob Black was not present with us during this portion of the woods journey.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc2.source_text: Alice took off with us on her heels, heading due north.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc4.description: I observed that the low ceiling had exposed beams that someone as tall as Jacob would likely hit his head on.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc4.source_text: The low ceiling had long exposed beams that someone as tall as Jacob would surely knock his head on.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc4.description: I learned that the nursery wasn't finished because of conflicts with angry werewolves.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc4.source_text: “That will be Renesmee’s room,” he said, nodding to an empty room with a pale wooden floor. “They didn’t have time to do much with it, what with the angry werewolves. . . .”

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc4.description: I blamed Jacob in a joking way for making everything perfect after the recent nightmare of events.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc4.source_text: Drat Jacob for making everything perfect this way.

tw-book4-chapter24_Sc5.description: I recognized that Jacob's skin and touch are described as notably hotter compared with Edward's more comfortable warmth.
tw-book4-chapter24_Sc5.source_text: It wasn't the same as touching Jacob’s flame-hot skin, but it was more comfortable.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob knocked on Charlie’s door, took him into the woods, phased in front of him, phased back, got dressed, and then spoke to calm him.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.source_text:
“So I knocked on Charlie’s door this morning and asked him to come for a walk with me. He was confused, but when I told him it was about you and that you were back in town, he followed me out to the woods. I told him you weren’t sick anymore, and that things were a little weird, but good. He was about to take off to see you, but I told him I had to show him something first. And then I phased.”
“Lemme see… I phased back and got dressed, and then after he started breathing again, I said something like, ‘Charlie, you don’t live in the world you thought you lived in. The good news is, nothing has changed—except that now you know. Life’ll go on the same way it always has. You can go right back to pretending that you don’t believe any of this.’”

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.description: I learned that Jacob told Charlie only a limited account, avoided detailed explanations about Bella, and intended to provide a red herring.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.source_text:
“Relax, Bella. I didn’t tell him anything you weren’t planning to tell him.”
“Wasn’t the whole ‘let him make the wrong assumptions’ thing your plan? I think I provided a very nice red herring, if I do say so myself.”

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.description: I heard Jacob express that he thought he had done Bella a favor by managing Charlie’s introduction to the truth.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: “If you’d give this just a minute, you’ll see that I did you a favor here.”

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.description: I heard Jacob describe Charlie as brave for not fainting or vomiting when Jacob phased in front of him.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc4.source_text: “He’s brave. Brave as you are. Didn’t pass out or throw up or anything. I gotta say, I was impressed.”

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob told Charlie we would stick around only if he could tolerate the strange parts about Renesmee.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc5.source_text: And then I told him that if he could deal with that, you all would stick around for a while and he would have a chance to get to know her.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc5.description: I noticed Jacob said he would always love Bella but that he would love her 'the right way' from now on.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc5.source_text: Bella, things are different with us now, but you’ll always be my best friend, and I’ll always love you. But I’ll love you the right way now.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc5.description: I learned that Jacob apologized to Bella for causing her pain about the situation with Charlie.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc5.source_text: I am sorry about it hurting you. I didn’t know it was like that.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc6.description: I saw Jacob take Renesmee into his arms, nod with concern, and gesture with the other wolves to move to the far corner of the room.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc6.source_text: "Take her," I whispered, sliding Renesmee into Jacob's arms. He nodded, concern wrinkling his forehead. He gestured to the others, and they all went to the far corner of the room.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc6.description: I noticed Jacob grin in triumph when Alice involved the wolves and when he was given Renesmee to hold.
I felt calmer when Jacob held Renesmee because I recognized that her presence steadied me.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc6.source_text: "But I need her. She keeps me calm."

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc7.description: I learned that Jacob told Charlie that the intervention was necessary and that Bella was dying, prompting Charlie's initial confrontation.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc7.source_text: Jake told me this was… necessary. That you were dying.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc7.description: I noticed that Jacob greeted Charlie casually and later offered an apologetic glance to me, indicating his awkward, protective stance.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc7.source_text: 'Hey, Charlie,' Jacob greeted him from the corner. 'How’re things?' Jacob shot an apologetic glance at me across the room.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc7.description: I inferred that Jacob had shared informal details about Renesmee with Charlie, including the possibility of a nickname, which shaped Charlie's expectations.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc7.source_text: Jake says you call her Nessie?

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc8.description: I heard Jacob whisper reassurance to Charlie saying it was a need-to-know situation and promising it was okay.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc8.source_text: “Need to know, Charlie. It’s okay. I promise.”

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc8.description: I observed Jacob pat Charlie on the back and lean in to whisper, indicating a protective and mediating role between Charlie and the supernatural secret.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc8.source_text: Jacob got up and came over to pat Charlie on the back. He leaned in to whisper something in Charlie’s ear; only Charlie didn’t know we could all hear.

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc8.description: I saw Jacob’s glowing stare at Renesmee and his confident assurances change the room’s tone toward acceptance.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc8.source_text: "Everything’s going to be great, Charlie. Just try to not believe anything you see."

tw-book4-chapter25_Sc8.description: I heard Jacob point out that Renesmee was special and that he had predicted her uniqueness.
tw-book4-chapter25_Sc8.source_text: Jacob elbowed him. "Told you she was special, didn’t I?"

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: I noted that Jacob was not present in this scene and that the interaction centered on Bella and Charlie at the front door.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc1.source_text: I read 'Characters present: Bella Swan, Charlie' and scene description indicating Jacob was not there.

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc1.description: I believe Jacob's relationship with Bella and Charlie was unchanged by this scene because he was not involved in the visit or conversation.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc1.source_text: I read 'Bella and Charlie stand at the front door after a long, tense day' and no mention of Jacob.

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc2.description: I saw Jacob raiding the fridge during the family's relaxed gathering.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc2.source_text: The group’s human charade has slipped slightly, and the family members are at ease — Alice lounging, Jasper nearby, Carlisle reading, Esme sketching, Rosalie and Emmett building a house of cards, Edward at the piano, and Jacob raiding the fridge.

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc2.description: I noticed Jacob is accepted into the Cullens' informal atmosphere and behaves comfortably among them.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc2.source_text: Inside the house the Cullens and Jacob resume a relaxed, informal atmosphere.

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc2.description: I came to think Jacob is treated more as part of the group than as an outsider given his ease and casual actions in the household.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc2.source_text: Inside the house the Cullens and Jacob resume a relaxed, informal atmosphere.

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc3.description: I observed that Jacob was present at the riverbank with the group during the arm-wrestling incident.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc3.source_text: Characters present: Bella Swan, Emmett, Edward, Alice, Esme, Jacob, Rosalie, Jasper, Carlisle, Esme

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc3.description: I noticed that Jacob did not intervene in the arm-wrestling, suggesting he played an observant or neutral role in this moment.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc3.source_text: The group moves outside to the riverbank where Emmett selects a large granite boulder as an impromptu arm-wrestling surface.

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc4.description: I heard Jacob joke about Bella being 'freaky' in the sunlight.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc4.source_text: I quoted: Jacob jokes about Bella being 'freaky' in the sunlight

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc4.description: I interpreted Jacob's joke as a sign of casual teasing that reflects familiarity and acceptance rather than hostility.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc4.source_text: I quoted: Jacob jokes about Bella being 'freaky' in the sunlight

tw-book4-chapter26_Sc4.description: I sensed Jacob's tone shifted my perception of him toward seeing comfort with Bella's changes instead of rejection.
tw-book4-chapter26_Sc4.source_text: I quoted: Jacob jokes about Bella being 'freaky' in the sunlight

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc1.description: I was surprised to include Jacob and the werewolves in my life, associating them with deep, woodsy colors.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc1.source_text: The werewolves, with their deep, woodsy colors, were not something I’d expected; Jacob, of course, and Seth, too.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc1.description: I learned that Quil and Embry joined Jacob's pack and became part of my fabric of life, and that Sam and Emily were cordial.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc1.source_text: But my old friends Quil and Embry became part of the fabric as they joined Jacob’s pack, and even Sam and Emily were cordial.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc1.description: I noticed that tensions between our families eased, mostly because of Renesmee.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc1.source_text: The tensions between our families eased, mostly due to Renesmee. She was easy to love.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc2.description: I learned that Leah has become Jacob's second-in-command and that she now fills the role of his beta.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc2.source_text: I quote: She was his second-in-command now, his “beta,” as I’d called it once long ago.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc2.description: I heard Jacob explain that he intended to formalize his Alpha role by nailing down the proper formalities for leadership.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc2.source_text: I quote: “I figured as long as I was going to do this Alpha thing for real,” Jacob explained, “I’d better nail down the formalities.”

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc2.description: I noticed that Jacob spends a great deal of time with Renesmee, which contributes to Leah's frequent need to check in with him.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc2.source_text: I quote: The new responsibility made Leah feel the need to check in with him often, and since he was always with Renesmee…

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc5.description: I learned that Carlisle and Edward never had these discussions when Jacob was around because there was one sure way to halt aging that Jacob would not be likely to be excited about.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc5.source_text: They never had these discussions when Jacob was around, because there was one sure way to halt aging, and that wasn’t something Jacob was likely to be excited about.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc5.description: I noticed that Jacob and Renesmee seemed alike in many ways, both described as half-and-half beings, two things at the same time.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc5.source_text: Jacob and Renesmee seemed alike in so many ways, both half-and-half beings, two things at the same time.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc5.description: I felt that it was too dangerous to consider vampire venom as a way to halt aging because werewolf lore insisted that vampire venom was a death sentence rather than a course to immortality and my instincts screamed 'Too dangerous!'
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc5.source_text: Too dangerous! my instincts screamed at me. … all the werewolf lore insisted that vampire venom was a death sentence rather than a course to immortality. . . .

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc7.description: I learned Jacob was determined to come with us to Brazil.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc7.source_text: However, today the argument was about Brazil. Jacob was determined to come with us.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc7.description: I realized Jacob planned a sabbatical from high school and intended to return when things slowed down.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc7.source_text: It’s just a sabbatical. I’ll get back to school when things… slow down.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc7.description: I noticed Jacob made hunting a contest with Renesmee to motivate her, which strengthened their bond.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc7.source_text: Jacob had made it a contest between them, and that made her more willing than anything else.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc7.description: I heard Jacob dismiss pack nannying responsibilities by saying he was not his pack’s nanny.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc7.source_text: I’m not my pack’s nanny. They’ve all got responsibilities in La Push anyway.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.description: I watched Jacob yank his t-shirt off and charge after Renesmee into the forest, already trembling with excitement.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: He yanked his t-shirt off as he charged after her into the forest, already trembling.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.description: I heard Jacob tease Renesmee sarcastically and indulgently that she was stalling and that she was afraid he would catch the biggest one again.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: “Suuuure you’re not thirsty, Nessie,” Jacob answered a little sarcastically, but more indulgently than anything else. “You’re just afraid I’ll catch the biggest one again!”

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.description: I saw Jacob as playful and synchronized with Renesmee and I considered him both a hunter and sometimes childlike in his behavior.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.source_text:
They had the move perfectly synchronized.

Jacob was more a child than Renessee sometimes.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.description: I realized that Jacob had as big a stake in the upcoming events as any of us and I acknowledged that his entire life was at stake.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc8.source_text: He had as big a stake in this as any of us—his entire life was at stake, just like mine.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc9.description: I saw Jacob with his ears flattened and his muzzle streaked with blood from his kill and I heard the growl building in his throat.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc9.source_text: Jacob’s ears flattened as he took in my expression; he crouched forward, baring his teeth —his muzzle was streaked with blood from his kill. His eyes raked the forest. I could hear the growl building in his throat.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc9.description: I heard Jacob's earlier echoing howl that Irina reacted to, linking Irina's anger to Jacob's presence.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc9.source_text: I heard Renesmee’s cry of victory from the forest, heard Jacob’s echoing howl, and saw Irina’s face jerk reflexively to the sound when it echoed to her a few seconds later.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc9.description: I trusted Jacob's protective instincts and I agreed with him that Renesmee should be returned to the safety of the house.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc9.source_text: Jacob huffed impatiently and poked my back with his nose. He must want Renesmee back at the safety of the house, just in case. I agreed with him on that, and we hurried home with Seth and Leah running at our flanks.

tw-book4-chapter27_Sc9.description: I noticed that Jacob called in reinforcements and that big paws followed Carlisle when Edward and Carlisle went after Irina.
tw-book4-chapter27_Sc9.source_text: I supposed I shouldn’t have been shocked. With Renesmee in even a hint of danger, of course Jacob would call in reinforcements.

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc1.description: I realized that Jacob had phased during Irina's visit and that his transformation may have worsened the situation.
tw-book4-chapter28_Sc1.source_text: I wished I’d noticed her earlier, before Jacob had phased.

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc1.description: I accepted that Jacob would accompany us to South America and that his presence was important to the expedition plans.
tw-book4-chapter28_Sc1.source_text: Now that it was accepted that Jacob would come with us, he figured prominently in the plans—

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc1.description: I suspected that our association with Jacob could prevent local people who believed in vampires from talking to any of us about their stories.
tw-book4-chapter28_Sc1.source_text: it was unlikely that the people who believed in vampires would speak to any of us about their stories.

tw-book4-chapter28_Sc2.description: I saw that Irina apparently witnessed a vampire and a werewolf who were best friends, which may be the accusation's core.
