tw-book4-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: I read: "I guess I’ve been wandering back this direction for a while, and maybe it’s because I was headed here. But it wasn’t until this morning that I really started running. I didn’t know if I could make it."

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc2.description: I noticed that Jacob is part of a pack with Sam and others watching nearby and that Sam likely informed Billy of his return.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: I read: "I’m sure Sam’s told him. I’ll go see him when… when the party’s over." "Sam’s out there. And some of the others. Just in case, you know."

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc2.description: I understood that Jacob came to be my friend and to try to make the wedding night perfect for me despite his own pain.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: I read: "I’m just here to be your friend. Your best friend, one last time." "I’m here to . . . To make it perfect."

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc2.description: I noticed Jacob’s physical changes, including a new, shorter haircut and a taller, more imposing stature.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc2.source_text: I read: "Was it possible that he was still growing? He had to be closer to seven feet than to six." "You cut your hair," I noted. "Yeah. Easier, you know."

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc4.description: I remembered telling Edward that he should have left Bella with me and that I had tried to protect her.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc4.source_text: You should have left Bella with me.

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc4.description: I remembered that I did everything I could to keep Bella away from Edward.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc4.source_text: I did everything I could to keep her away from you. Every single thing.

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc4.description: I felt cold and numbed when Edward fell apart and asked me for a favor despite my rage.
tw-book4-chapter14_Sc4.source_text: I felt cold as snow—there was no fire in me.

tw-book4-chapter14_Sc4.description: I reacted with contempt and called Edward a parasite when he pleaded for my help.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: I scouted the perimeter, ran spokes with Seth, and picked up the north half of the circle while looking for signs of the Cullens.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: He was already picking up the north half of the circle. Anything? Nope. Nothing but nothing. I ran a few spokes.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: I learned that Seth looped back toward the main perimeter and that running with Seth was easier than running with Leah.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: Seth looped back toward the main perimeter. It was easier to run with him than it was to do the same with Leah.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: I noticed my feelings were softening toward the vampires and that I was less hostile than I had expected to be.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: There was always an edge to her thoughts. She didn’t want to feel the softening toward the vampires that was going on in my head.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: I realized that Leah’s antagonism shifted away from me and focused more on the Cullens and Bella, making running with her less unbearable.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: But there was no antagonism toward me now at all, just the Cullens and Bella. Running with Leah wasn’t nearly as bad as I’d expected.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.description: I decided I would want to tell the Cullens to leave with Bella for safety but feared they would listen and that Bella would disappear from my life.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc1.source_text: I probably ought to suggest that, but I was afraid they would listen to me. And I didn’t want to have Bella disappear—to never know whether she’d made it or not.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc2.description: I observed that Jacob asserts he will never be part of Bella's family and feels excluded.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: I’ll never be part of your family, Bella.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc2.description: I realized that Jacob mourns a lost possible future in which he might have been part of Bella's family and accepts that that future died long ago.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc2.source_text: I could have been. I would have been good there. But that was just a distant future that died long before it had a chance to live.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob finds Bella's plan to hide her transformation from Charlie and later see him again to be insane and unacceptable.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: I learned that we had been patrolling the eastern mountains when the vampires left and that our patrols changed when the Cullens returned.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc3.source_text: We took a winding path through the eastern mountains. It was a familiar route. We’d run these mountains when the vampires had left a year ago, making it part of our patrol route to better protect the people here. Then we’d pulled back the lines when the Cullens returned.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: I smelled and tracked a heavy, somewhat recent concentration of vampire scent on one particular trail.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc3.source_text: I found a heavy, somewhat recent concentration on one particular trail—all of them coming and going here except for Edward.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: I felt surprised and honored when Leah told me I make a good Alpha and that I am worth following.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc3.source_text: I think you make a good Alpha. Not in the same way Sam does, but in your own way. You’re worth following, Jacob.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: I discovered that Leah wanted to stay with my pack and that Seth also preferred remaining with us.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc3.source_text: I want to stay with you, she told me. I want to stay, too, Seth thought quietly.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc3.description: I decided that I plan to return to being wolf-only after our purpose is finished and that I need to persuade Seth to continue his human responsibilities.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc3.source_text: And, as I’m planning on quitting as soon as I can manage it… maybe that won’t be so often. We’ve got a purpose now, but when… after that’s over, I’m just going to go wolf. Seth, you need a purpose.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc4.description: I felt my hands tremble while Alice stared at them.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: Alice was staring at my hands, watching them tremble.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc4.description: I kept being surprised by each new injury and wondered when I was going to stop being surprised.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: Funny how it kept hitting me, like each new thing was a surprise. When was I going to stop being surprised?

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc4.description: I offered to take Emmett and to help with the ripping part if needed, which showed my willingness to protect Bella and to engage with the Cullens' conflicts.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: I’ll take Emmett,” I offered. “You can help Edward with the ripping part.

tw-book4-chapter15_Sc4.description: I learned that Edward and others besides me were also deeply affected by Bella's injury and that Alice loved Bella too.
tw-book4-chapter15_Sc4.source_text: Edward and I weren’t the only ones who were burning over this. Alice loved Bella, too.

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc4.description: I was ordered to fight Emmett and Jasper alongside Quil and Embry and I recognized that I could not refuse the Alpha’s command.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: You will fight with us tonight. I understand that this is hard for you, so you will concentrate on their fighters—Emmett and Jasper Cullen. Quil and Embry will fight with you.

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc4.description: I admitted that I had been blinded by hate earlier and I realized that killing Carlisle would be murder because Carlisle is good.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: Everything was inside out. This afternoon, I’d been chomping at the bit to attack them. ... Carlisle Cullen. Looking at him without that hate clouding my eyes, I couldn’t deny that killing him was murder. He was good.

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc4.description: I felt crushed under Sam’s authority and I experienced a loss of agency as Sam’s edict compelled me to perform my obligation to the tribe.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: Yes, the Alpha decreed, his double voice blistering with the heat of his authority. There are no loopholes tonight. You, Jacob, are going to fight the Cullens with us. ... You will perform this obligation.

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc4.description: I recognized Seth’s pain and sense of betrayal because Seth had become friendly with the Cullens during the brief alliance yet would still obey Sam.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc4.source_text: For him this was a betrayal—during that one day of alliance, fighting beside Edward Cullen, Seth had truly become the vampire’s friend.

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc5.description: I learned that Sam kept Embry from coming with us because Sam doesn't want the pack to grow and feared Embry might be convinced to leave La Push.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: So Sam’s not going to take any chances on him getting convinced to jump ship. He doesn’t want our pack any bigger than it is now.

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc5.description: I felt uneasy about speaking for the pack when I couldn't hear their thoughts and worried I might have said something inappropriate.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: Was that okay? I asked them. It worried me, speaking for them that way, when I couldn’t hear exactly what they were thinking. I didn’t want to assume anything. I didn’t want to be like Jared that way. Did I say anything you didn’t want me to? Did I not say something I should have?

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc5.description: I discovered that the clothes left on the porch were men's clothes, tan pants and a white button-down, and that they smelled strongly of vampires.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: They were definitely guy’s clothes—tan pants and a white button-down shirt. Neither of them long enough, but they looked like they’d fit around me.

tw-book4-chapter16_Sc5.description: I admitted to myself that having some clothes, even smelly hand-me-downs, made me feel better about being effectively homeless and without possessions.
tw-book4-chapter16_Sc5.source_text: I had to admit, I felt better with some clothes to my name, even stinky ones that didn’t quite fit. It was hard not being able to just jet back home and grab another pair of old sweatpants when I needed them. The homeless thing again—not having anyplace to go back to. No possessions, either, which wasn’t bothering me too bad now, but would probably get annoying soon.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.description: I drove an Aston Martin Vanquish and I felt the car respond almost as if my thoughts were steering it while I accelerated onto the highway.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: I just threw myself into the silky leather seat and cranked the engine while my knees were still crunched up under the steering wheel. The car felt almost airborne as it leaped forward. The car responded to me like my thoughts were steering rather than my hands.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.description: I reached speeds near two hundred on the highway and I saw no police intervention despite the risk.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: If by lucky you meant taking a well-traveled highway at two hundred without so much as seeing one cop, even in the thirty-mile-an-hour speed-trap towns.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.description: I glimpsed members of the wolf pack while I drove, noticing Quil running parallel and I saw Leah peering uneasily from the ferns.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: The only sign of surveillance I came across was just a hint of dark brown fur flitting through the woods, running parallel to me for a few miles on the south side of Forks. Quil, it looked like. ... I caught a fleeting glimpse of Leah’s gray face peering uneasily through the ferns.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.description: I planned originally to total the vampire's car on my way back and I had set out intending confrontation as part of my route.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: The second part of it was totaling the bloodsucker’s car on my way back.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.description: I considered that imprinting could remove my pain and I briefly thought that surrendering choice might be an acceptable price for no longer hurting.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: That would go away, you know, if you imprinted. You wouldn’t have to hurt over her anymore. Seemed like maybe getting your choices taken away from you wasn’t the very worst thing in the world.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.description: I searched a crowded park thoroughly for a potential soul mate and I found nothing that matched what I needed, which made me give up.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: I walked around for what felt like hours. ... Either way, nothing. ... That was when I gave up.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.description: I concluded that La Push still seemed like the strongest candidate region for finding my genetic match and I adjusted my expectations accordingly.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: If Sam was right, the best place to find my genetic match would be in La Push.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.description: I parked across two handicapped spots and I displayed reckless disregard for minor consequences while I processed my emotions.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc1.source_text: I parked across two handicapped spots—just begging for a ticket—and joined the crowd.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc2.description: I learned that Jacob's authority as the true Alpha and Ephraim's heir is required to grant the Cullens an exception to the treaty.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: I’m asking this of the true Alpha, Jacob. I’m asking this of Ephraim’s heir. No. Sam’s authority is assumed. It belongs to you. You’ll never take it from him, but no one can rightfully agree to what I’m asking except for you.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc2.description: I realized that my expectation of having four days was wrong and that my few days had become a few hours, which collapsed my sense of time and options.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: First, counting on Edward’s hatred of the thing so much. Now, I’d realized that I thought of those four days as a sure thing. My few days had become a few hours.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc2.description: I felt a change in how I saw Edward when I recognized that Edward could not hate something that loved Bella and therefore seemed unable to hate me either.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: This was what had changed Edward—that the monster had convinced him of this love. He couldn’t hate what loved Bella. It was probably why he couldn’t hate me, either.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc2.description: I felt overwhelming grief and helplessness as the timeline shortened and as I understood the consequences of the choice Edward asked me to make.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc2.source_text: The endless ocean of grief that waited stretched out before me. I tried to catch my breath. My knees buckled. I had to grab the car to hold myself up.

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc3.description: I experienced that I fought Rosalie to protect Bella, that Rosalie stabbed my left arm with a scalpel, and that I ripped the blade out of my arm.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "As I hit her stone body... I felt the scalpel in her hand stab deep into my left arm."

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc3.description: I performed CPR on Bella, repeatedly blowing air into her mouth and pumping her chest while counting compressions to keep her heart beating.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "CPR?" Edward growled at me, fast and demanding. I quote: "I bent over her head... I pressed mine to hers and blew a lungful of air into it."

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc3.description: I felt my belief shift as I accepted that Edward would immediately prioritize Bella's wish for the baby and act without hesitation even during the crisis.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc3.source_text: I quote: "I guess I should have known that he would always give her what she wanted, no matter how stupid her request might be."

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc4.description: I noticed that Jacob Black is included in the scene's characters-to-track list.
tw-book4-chapter17_Sc4.source_text: Characters to track: Bella Swan, Edward Cullen, Jacob Black

tw-book4-chapter17_Sc4.description: I noticed that Jacob Black is also not listed as present in the scene, which suggests he is off-stage here.
I concluded that Jacob's role in this particular scene is likely peripheral or contextual because the scene content is organized around Bella rather than interactions.

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc1.description: I recounted that I launched myself at Rosalie, subdued her physically, and allowed a scalpel to stab my left arm while stopping her attack.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: I quote: "I launched myself at Rosalie, jumping across the table without bothering to phase. As I hit her stone body, knocking her toward the door, I felt the scalpel in her hand stab deep into my left arm."

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc1.description: I confirmed that I performed CPR and mouth-to-mouth on Bella to get her breathing and that her lips tasted like blood when I breathed into her.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: I quote: "I bent over her head. Her mouth looked clear, so I pressed mine to hers and blew a lungful of air into it. Her lips tasted like blood."

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc1.description: I realized that my previous fantasies about Bella were now unbearable and I could no longer picture her naked after seeing her injured and exposed.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: I quote: "How many times had I imagined her naked? Now I couldn’t look. I was afraid to have these memories in my head."

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc1.description: I discovered that I view Rosalie as a direct physical threat when her thirst surfaces and that Alice silently supported our intervention to save Bella.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc1.source_text: I quote: "No, Rose!" Edward roared... "Then Rosalie lost her focus. I saw the expression on her face shift, saw her lips pull back from her teeth and her black eyes glint with thirst." and "And then Alice was there, yanking her by the throat to get her into the hall."

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: I performed chest compressions and mouth-to-mouth on Bella, counting steadily while I tried to keep her heart beating.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc2.source_text: I read: "My hands were on her chest, doing compressions. I counted in my head, trying to keep the rhythm steady. One. Two. Three. Four."

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: I felt a tiny crunch as Edward’s blow broke my little finger when he knocked my hand aside.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc2.source_text: I read: "There was a tiny crunch as his blow broke my little finger."

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: I realized that the draw I felt toward Bella had vanished and that my longing shifted into a desire to leave the scene forever.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc2.source_text: I read: "So this body had no more draw for me. The senseless need to be near her had vanished. Or maybe moved was the better word. It seemed like I felt the pull from the opposite direction now... the longing to get away from here and never, ever come back."

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc2.description: I snarled at Edward in the doorway and understood anew that our relationship was tense and confrontational in that moment.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc2.source_text: I read: "Edward and I snarled at the same time."

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc3.description: I felt a strong, almost commanding pull and heat urging me to attack Rosalie and destroy the newborn.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: It seemed like the pull had not been leading to the door after all. I could feel it now, encouraging me, tugging me forward. Pushing me to finish this, to cleanse the world of this abomination.

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc3.description: I changed from despair to a hate-fueled determination as strength and red heat returned to me when I heard the creature feeding.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: My strength came back to me as I listened to the sound of the little executioner feeding. Strength and hate and heat—red heat washing through my head, burning but erasing nothing.

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc3.description: I accepted that the newborn was an unnatural aberration as others had warned.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: Sam had been right. The thing was an aberration—its existence went against nature. A black, soulless demon.

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc3.description: I noticed that the newborn had warm brown, milk-chocolate eyes that matched Bella's exactly.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: Warm brown eyes, the color of milk chocolate—the exact same color that Bella’s had been.

tw-book4-chapter18_Sc3.description: I judged that Rosalie was distracted and would try to kill me after I destroyed the creature, so I expected to have to fight her as well.
tw-book4-chapter18_Sc3.source_text: Rosalie would try to kill me when the creature was dead, and I would fight back.
